body.text: sarvadharmasvabhāvasamatāvipañcita-Samādhirājasūtram |
body.translated_text: <s>Samādhirājasūtra</s>, Elaboration on the Equality of the Inherent Nature of All <s>Dharmas</s> |

body.text: 1 Nidānaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: Chapter 1: <s>Nidānaparivarta</s> (The Introductory Chapter) |

body.text:
evaṃ mayā śrutam | ekasmin samaye bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati sma gṛdhrakūṭe parvate mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhaṃ paripūrṇena bhikṣuniyutaśatasahasreṇa aśītyā ca bodhisattvaniyutaiḥ sārdham | sarvairakajātipratibaddhairabhijñābhijñātairdaśadiglokadhātusaṃnipatitairdhāraṇīsūtrāntagatiṃ gataiḥ sarvasattvadharmadānasaṃtoṣakairmahābhijñājñānodāhārakuśalaiḥ sarvapāramitāparamapāramitāprāptaiḥ sarvabodhisattvasamādhisamāpattivyavasthānajñānakuśalaiḥ sarvabuddhastutastobhitapraśastaiḥ sarvabuddhakṣetravyākramaṇakuśalaiḥ sarvamārasaṃtrāsanajñānakuśalaiḥ sarvadharmayathāvajjñānakuśalaiḥ sarvasattvendriyaparāparajñānakuśalaiḥ buddhasarvakarmapūjāsamādānaprajñānakuśalaiḥ sarvalokadharmānupaliptaiḥ kāyavākcittasamalaṃkṛtaiḥ mahāmaitrīmahākaruṇāsaṃnāhasaṃnaddhaiḥ mahāvīryāsaṃkhyeyakalpāparikṣīṇamānasaiḥ mahāsiṃhanādanādibhiḥ sarvaparapravādānabhibhūtaiḥ avaivartikamudrāmudritaiḥ sarvabuddhadharmābhiṣekaprāptaiḥ | tadyathā - meruṇā ca nāma bodhisattvena mahāsattvena | sumeruṇā ca | mahāmeruṇā ca | meruśikhariṃdhareṇa ca | merupradīparājena ca | merukūṭena ca | merudhvajena ca | merugajena ca | meruśikhare saṃghaṭṭanarājena ca | merusvareṇa ca | megharājena ca | dundubhisvareṇa ca | ratnapāṇinā ca | ratnākareṇa ca | ratnaketunā ca | ratnaśikhareṇa ca | ratnasaṃbhavena ca ratnaprabhāsena ca | ratnayaṣṭinā ca | ratnamudrāhastena ca | ratnavyūhena ca | ratnajālinā ca | ratnaprabheṇa ca | ratnadvīpeṇa ca | ratiṃkareṇa ca | dharmavyūhena ca | vyūharājena ca | lakṣaṇasamalaṃkṛtena ca | svaravyūhena ca | svaraviśuddhiprabheṇa ca | ratnakūṭena ca | ratnacūḍena ca | daśaśataraśmikṛtārciṣā jyoti rasena ca | candrabhānunā ca | sahacittotpādadharmacakrapravartinā ca | śubhakanakaviśuddhiprabheṇa ca | satatamabhayaṃdadānena ca nāma bodhisattvena mahāsattvena | ajitabodhisattvapūrvaṃgamaiśca sarvairbhadrakalpikairbodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ | mañjuśrīpūrvaṃgamaiśca ṣaṣṭibhiranupamacittaiḥ | bhadrapālapūrvaṃgamaiśca ṣoḍaśabhiḥ satpuruṣaiḥ | caturmahārājapūrvaṃgamaiśca cāturmahārājakāyikairdevaputraiḥ | peyālam | yāvad brahmapūrvaṃgamaiśca brahmakāyikairdevaputraistadanyaiśca
maheśākhyamaheśākhyairudārodārairdevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyairbhagavān (Vaidya 2) satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito 'rcito 'pacāyitaścatasṛṇāmapi parṣadāṃ sadevalokasya lokasya vandanīyaḥ pūjanīyo namaskaraṇīyaḥ | tatra khalu bhagavānanekaśatasahasrayā parṣadā parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto dharmaṃ deśayati sma ādau kalyāṇaṃ madhye kalyāṇaṃ paryavasāne kalyāṇam | svarthaṃ suvyañjanaṃ kevalaṃ paripūrṇaṃ pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ brahmacaryaṃ saṃprakāśayati sma ||
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) mountain, together with a great assembly of monks — a full hundred thousand <s>niyutas</s> of monks — and together with eighty <s>niyutas</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: all single-birth-bound, endowed with superknowledges, assembled from world-systems in the ten directions, having reached the culmination of <s>dhāraṇī</s>-<s>sūtrāntas</s>, satisfying all beings with the gift of <s>Dharma</s>, skilled in the exercise of great superknowledge and wisdom, having attained the supreme perfection of all <s>pāramitās</s>, skilled in knowledge of the establishment of all <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhis</s> and attainments, praised and lauded by all Buddhas, skilled in traversing all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, skilled in the knowledge that terrifies all <s>māras</s>, skilled in knowing all <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are, skilled in knowing the superior and inferior faculties of all beings, skilled in wisdom concerning the undertaking of worship through all acts of a <s>Buddha</s>, untainted by all worldly <s>dharmas</s>, adorned in body, speech, and mind, armored in the armor of great loving-kindness and great compassion, with minds unwearied through incalculable <s>kalpas</s> of great vigor, roaring the great lion's roar, unconquered by all proponents of other doctrines, sealed with the seal of non-retrogression, having attained the consecration of all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities. Namely: the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Meru</s>, <s>Sumeru</s>, <s>Mahāmeru</s>, <s>Meruśikharindhara</s>, <s>Merupradīparāja</s>, <s>Merukūṭa</s>, <s>Merudhvaja</s>, <s>Merugaja</s>, <s>Meruśikhare-saṃghaṭṭanarāja</s>, <s>Merusvara</s>, <s>Megharāja</s>, <s>Dundubhisvara</s>, <s>Ratnapāṇi</s>, <s>Ratnākara</s>, <s>Ratnaketu</s>, <s>Ratnaśikhara</s>, <s>Ratnasaṃbhava</s>, <s>Ratnaprabhāsa</s>, <s>Ratnayaṣṭi</s>, <s>Ratnamudrāhasta</s>, <s>Ratnavyūha</s>, <s>Ratnajālin</s>, <s>Ratnaprabha</s>, <s>Ratnadvīpa</s>, <s>Ratiṃkara</s>, <s>Dharmavyūha</s>, <s>Vyūharāja</s>, <s>Lakṣaṇasamalaṃkṛta</s>, <s>Svaravyūha</s>, <s>Svaraviśuddhiprabha</s>, <s>Ratnakūṭa</s>, <s>Ratnacūḍa</s>, <s>Daśaśataraśmikṛtārcir-jyotirasa</s>, <s>Candrabhānu</s>, <s>Sahacittotpāda-dharmacakrapravartin</s>, <s>Śubhakanakaviśuddhiprabha</s>, and the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Satatam-abhayaṃdadāna</s>; together with all the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> of the Fortunate <s>Kalpa</s> (<s>Bhadrakalpa</s>), led by <s>Ajita</s>; together with sixty of incomparable mind led by <s>Mañjuśrī</s>; together with sixteen true men led by <s>Bhadrapāla</s>; together with the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> god-sons led by the four Great Kings; in abbreviated form, up to the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> god-sons led by <s>Brahmā</s>; and other <s>Maheśākhya</s> and non-<s>Maheśākhya</s> beings of great and noble [station] — gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, humans and non-humans. The Blessed One (Vaidya 2) was honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped, venerated, and respected, worthy of salutation, worship, and homage by the four assemblies and by the world with its gods. There the Blessed One, surrounded and attended by an assembly of many hundreds of thousands, was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> — excellent in the beginning, excellent in the middle, excellent in the end — proclaiming the holy life with good meaning, good phrasing, complete, fulfilled, pure, and perfectly clear. ||

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena tasminneva parṣatsaṃnipāte candraprabho nāma kumārabhūtaḥ saṃnipatito 'bhūt saṃniṣaṇṇaḥ pūrvajinakṛtādhikāro 'varopitakuśalamūlo jātismaro labdhapratibhāno mahāyānasaṃprasthito mahākaruṇābhiyuktaḥ | atha khalu candraprabhaḥ kumārabhūta utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ prāvṛtya dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat - pṛccheyamahaṃ bhagavantaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ kaṃcideva pradeśam, sacenme bhagavānavakāśaṃ kuryāt pṛṣṭapraśnavyākaraṇāya | evamukte bhagavān candraprabhaṃ kumārabhūtamāmantrayate sma - pṛccha tvaṃ kumārabhūta tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ yad yadeva kāṅkṣasi | ahaṃ tasya tasyaiva praśnasya pṛṣṭasya vyākaraṇena cittamārādhayiṣyāmi | sarvajño 'smi samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ kumāra sarvadarśī sarvadharmabalavaiśāradyavṛṣabhatāmanuprāpto 'nāvaraṇavimokṣajñānasamanvāgataḥ | nāsti kumāra tathāgatasya sarvadharmeṣvajñātaṃ vā adṛṣṭaṃ vā aśrutaṃ vā aviditaṃ vā asākṣātkṛtaṃ vā anabhisaṃbuddhaṃ vā anantāparyanteṣu lokadhātuṣu | nityakṛtaste kumāra avakāśo bhavatu tathāgataṃ praśnaparipṛcchanāya | ahaṃ te tasya tasyaiva praśnasya pṛṣṭasya vyākaraṇena cittamārādhayiṣyāmi ||
body.translated_text: Now at that time, in that very assembly, a prince named <s>Candraprabha</s> (Moon-Radiance) had assembled and was seated — one who had performed service under former <s>Jinas</s>, who had planted roots of merit, who remembered his past lives, who had attained eloquence, who had set out in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, and who was devoted to great compassion. Then <s>Candraprabha</s> the prince, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, and bowing with palms joined toward the Blessed One, said to the Blessed One: "I would ask the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, about a certain matter, if the Blessed One would grant me the opportunity for answering my question." When this was said, the Blessed One addressed <s>Candraprabha</s> the prince: "Ask, O prince, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, whatever you wish. I shall satisfy your mind by answering each and every question. I am omniscient, a Perfectly Awakened One, O prince — all-seeing, having attained the bull-like eminence of all <s>dharma</s>-powers and confidences, endowed with unobstructed liberation-knowledge. There is nothing, O prince, among all <s>dharmas</s> in the boundless and infinite world-systems that is unknown, unseen, unheard, uncomprehended, unrealized, or unawakened to by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. You always have permission, O prince, to question the <s>Tathāgata</s>. I shall satisfy your mind by answering each and every question." ||

body.text: atha khalu candraprabhaḥ kumārabhūtastuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajātastasyāṃ velāyāṃ bhagavantaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Candraprabha</s> the prince, pleased, elated, delighted, joyful, and filled with gladness and happiness, at that moment addressed the Blessed One in verses:

children.text: kathaṃ carantaḥ saṃbuddha lokanātha prabhaṃkara /
children.translated_text: "How should one conduct oneself, O Perfectly Awakened One, O World-Protector, O Light-Maker,

children.text: labhate 'cintiyaṃ jñānaṃ vyākuruṣva hitaṃkara // SRS_1.1 //
children.translated_text: to obtain that inconceivable knowledge? Explain, O Beneficent One! // SRS_1.1 //

children.text: kathaṃ carantu narendra satyavādi naravṛṣabha naradevapūjanīya /
children.translated_text: "How should one conduct oneself, O Lord of Men, O Truth-Speaker, O Bull among Men, O One Worthy of Worship by Men and Gods?

children.text: atuliyu varu labdhamagrayāṇaṃ giravara pṛṣṭa viyākuruṣva nātha // SRS_1.2 //
children.translated_text: Having obtained the incomparable, excellent, foremost vehicle — O Mountain of Speech, explain to me who asks, O Protector! // SRS_1.2 //

children.text: adhyāśayena pṛcchāmi śāṭhyaṃ mama na vidyate /
children.translated_text: "With sincere intention I ask — there is no deception in me;

children.text: sākṣī na kaścidanyo me anyatra puruṣottamāt // SRS_1.3 //
children.translated_text: there is no other witness for me than the Supreme among Men. // SRS_1.3 //

children.text: vipula praṇidhi mahyamasti chandaścariya prajānasi mahya śākyasiṃha /
children.translated_text: "My aspiration is vast — you know my conduct and zeal, O Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>;

children.text: na ca ahaṃ vacanavittako bhaviṣye laghu pratipatti bhaṇāhi me narendra // SRS_1.4 //
children.translated_text: and I shall not be one of mere words — tell me a practice that is swift, O Lord of Men! // SRS_1.4 //

children.text: (Vaidya 3)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 3)

children.text: katarāhārakā dharmā buddhayāne bahuṃkarāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Which <s>dharmas</s> constitute nourishment? Which are most productive in the <s>Buddha</s>-vehicle?

children.text: vyākuruṣva mahāvīra sarvadharmāṇa pāraga // SRS_1.5 //
children.translated_text: Explain, O Great Hero, O one who has gone beyond all <s>dharmas</s>! // SRS_1.5 //

children.text: upakare dharma mama brūhi nātha yatha naru niṣevatu bhoti tīkṣṇaprajñaḥ |
children.translated_text: "Tell me that beneficial <s>Dharma</s>, O Protector, by cultivating which a person becomes one of sharp wisdom,

children.text: apagatabhayabhairavo atrasto na ca parityāgu karoti śīlaskandhāt /
children.translated_text: free from fear and terror, unafraid, and does not abandon the aggregate of morality,

children.text: vyapagatamadarāgadoṣamohaścarati ca cārika sarvaśāntadoṣaḥ // SRS_1.6 //
children.translated_text: free from pride, passion, hatred, and delusion, and conducts himself with all faults pacified. // SRS_1.6 //

children.text: kathaṃ na tyajate śīlaṃ kathaṃ dhyānaṃ na riñcati /
children.translated_text: "How does one not abandon morality? How does one not forsake <s>dhyāna</s>?

children.text: kathaṃ niṣevate 'raṇyaṃ kathaṃ prajñā pravartate // SRS_1.7 //
children.translated_text: How does one resort to the forest? How does wisdom unfold? // SRS_1.7 //

children.text: kathaṃ daśabalaśāsane udāre abhirati vindati śīla rakṣamāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: "How does one find delight in the noble teaching of the Ten-Powered One while guarding morality?

children.text: kathaṃ bhavati acchidru śīlaskandhaḥ kathaṃ ca tuleti svabhāvu saṃskṛtasya // SRS_1.8 //
children.translated_text: How does the aggregate of morality become unbroken? And how does one discern the nature of the conditioned? // SRS_1.8 //

children.text: kathaṃ kāyena vācā pariśuddho bhoti paṇḍitaḥ /
children.translated_text: "How does the wise one become pure in body and speech,

children.text: asaṃkliṣṭena cittena buddhajñānaṃ niṣevate // SRS_1.9 //
children.translated_text: and with an undefiled mind cultivate <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge? // SRS_1.9 //

children.text: kathaṃ bhavati viśuddhakāyakarmā kathaṃ ca vivarjita bhonti vācadoṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: "How does one become one of pure bodily action? And how are faults of speech eliminated?

children.text: kathaṃ bhavati asaṃkliṣṭacittaḥ puruṣavara mama pṛṣṭa vyākuruṣva // SRS_1.10 //
children.translated_text: How does one become one of undefiled mind? O Best of Men, explain to me who asks! // SRS_1.10 //

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃścandraprabhaṃ kumārabhūtametadavocat - ekadharmeṇa kumāra samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattva etān guṇān pratilabhate, kṣipraṃ cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate | katamenaikadharmeṇa? iha kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvasattveṣu samacitto bhavati hitacitto 'pratihatacitto 'viṣamacittaḥ | anena kumāra ekadharmeṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattva etān guṇān pratilabhate kṣipraṃ cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One said to <s>Candraprabha</s> the prince: "O prince, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> endowed with one single <s>dharma</s> obtains these qualities and quickly awakens to the unsurpassed, perfect awakening. With which one <s>dharma</s>? Here, O prince, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> has an equal mind toward all beings — a mind of benefit, an unobstructed mind, an impartial mind. Endowed with this one <s>dharma</s>, O prince, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> obtains these qualities and quickly awakens to the unsurpassed, perfect awakening." ||

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāṃ candraprabhaṃ kumārabhūtaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata - (Vaidya 4)
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that moment, addressed <s>Candraprabha</s> the prince in verses: (Vaidya 4)

children.text: ekadharmaṃ samādāya bodhisattvo ya vartate /
children.translated_text: "A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who undertakes and abides in one <s>dharma</s>

children.text: etān guṇān sa labhate kṣipraṃ bodhiṃ ca budhyate // SRS_1.11 //
children.translated_text: obtains these qualities and quickly awakens to <s>bodhi</s>. // SRS_1.11 //

children.text: na ca kaści pratihanyate 'sya cittam apratihatacittu yo bhoti bodhisattvaḥ /
children.translated_text: "No one obstructs the mind of that <s>Bodhisattva</s> who dwells with an unobstructed mind;

children.text: na ca khilu janayati na pradoṣaṃ labhati yathā parikīrtitān viśeṣān // SRS_1.12 //
children.translated_text: and he does not generate hostility — he obtains the excellences as proclaimed. // SRS_1.12 //

children.text: samaṃ cittaṃ niṣevitvā vipāko darśitaḥ samaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Having cultivated an equal mind, an equal result is shown:

children.text: samāḥ pādatalā bhonti samaścācāragocaraḥ // SRS_1.13 //
children.translated_text: his soles become level, and his conduct and domain become even. // SRS_1.13 //

children.text: samamaviṣamacittu bhāvayitvā apagatadoṣakhilaḥ prahīṇakāṅkṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Having cultivated an even, impartial mind, free from the taint of faults, with doubt abandoned,

children.text: caraṇavaratalāḥ samāsya bhonti paramaprabhāsvara śuddhadarśanīyaḥ // SRS_1.14 //
children.translated_text: the soles of his feet become even — supremely radiant, pure, and beautiful to behold. // SRS_1.14 //

children.text: daśadiśita viroci bodhisattvaḥ sphurati śirīya prabhāya buddhakṣetram /
children.translated_text: "The <s>Bodhisattva</s> shines in the ten directions, illuminating <s>Buddha</s>-fields with the splendor of his radiance;

children.text: yada bhavati sa labdhu śāntabhūmi tada bahusattva sthapeti buddhajñāne // SRS_1.15 //
children.translated_text: when he has attained the stage of peace, then he establishes many beings in <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. // SRS_1.15 //

body.text:
tatra kumāra sarvasattveṣu samacitto bodhisattvo mahāsattvo hitacitto 'pratihatacitto 'viṣamacittaṃ imaṃ sarvadharmasvabhāvasamatāvipañcitaṃ nāma samādhiṃ pratilabhate | katamaśca sa kumāra sarvadharmasvabhāvasamatāvipañcitaṃ nāma samādhiḥ pratilabhate | katamaśca sa kumāra sarvadharmasvabhāvasamatāvipañcito nāma samādhiḥ? body.translated_text: There, O Prince, the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s>, with a mind equal toward all beings, with a mind of beneficence, with an unobstructed mind, with an impartial mind, attains this <s>samādhi</s> called 'Discernment of the Equality of the Inherent Nature of All <s>Dharmas</s>' (<s>sarvadharmasvabhāvasamatāvipañcita</s>). And what, O Prince, is this <s>samādhi</s> called 'Discernment of the Equality of the Inherent Nature of All <s>Dharmas</s>'? Namely: restraint of body; restraint of speech; restraint of mind; purification of <s>karma</s>; transcendence of objects of support; full comprehension of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates); equality of the <s>dhātus</s> (elements); withdrawal from the <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases); abandonment of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving); entry into the direct realization of non-arising; illumination of causes; non-destruction of the fruits of <s>karma</s>; seeing the <s>dharma</s>; cultivation of the path; contemplation of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; sharpness of wisdom; penetration into the truths; knowledge of <s>dharma</s>; knowledge of entry into the analytical knowledges; knowledge of the analysis of syllables and words; transcendence of objects; full comprehension of sounds; attainment of joy; experience of delight in the <s>dharma</s>; uprightness; gentleness; straightness; non-crookedness; absence of frowning; pleasantness; good conduct; friendliness; sweetness; a smiling countenance; being the first to speak; saying 'Come, you are welcome!'; freedom from laziness; respect for teachers; attendance on teachers; contentment with one's station; insatiability for wholesome <s>dharmas</s>; purity of livelihood; not abandoning forest-dwelling; knowledge of the stages of the <s>bhūmis</s>; non-loss of mindfulness; skill in the <s>skandhas</s>; skill in the <s>dhātus</s>; skill in the <s>āyatanas</s>; entry into the direct realization of the higher knowledges; withdrawal from afflictions; uprooting of the latent tendencies and their accompaniments; progress to distinction in knowledge; the outflow of cultivation; skill in recovering from transgressions; suppression of the active afflictions; abandonment of the latent tendencies; (Vaidya 5) transcendence of existence; memory of past births; freedom from doubt; having a mind devoted to <s>dharma</s> regarding the ripening of <s>karma</s>; sharpness of knowledge in seeking learning; thirst for knowledge; awakening through knowledge; the ground of a thoroughbred; a mind like a mountain; immovability; unshakability; knowledge of establishment on the stage of non-retrogression; the outflow of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>; disgust toward evil <s>dharmas</s>; non-occurrence of afflictions; non-abandonment of the training; establishment in <s>samādhi</s>; knowledge of intentions; knowledge of the distinctions of beings' rebirths; knowledge of equality; knowledge of connecting words; abandonment of household life; non-delight in the three realms; a mind that is not withdrawn; non-attachment to <s>dharmas</s>; embracing the true <s>dharma</s>; guarding the <s>dharma</s>; understanding the ripening of <s>karma</s> as a condition; skill in <s>Vinaya</s> (discipline); pacification of disputes; non-quarrelsomeness; non-contentiousness; the ground of patience; undertaking patience; equality of destinies; skill in the investigation of <s>dharma</s>; the mind of going forth; skill in the determination of <s>dharma</s>; knowledge of the analysis of words of <s>dharma</s>; skill in producing words of <s>dharma</s>; knowledge and skill in producing the words that distinguish the meaningful from the meaningless; knowledge of the past; knowledge of the future; knowledge of the present; knowledge of the equality of the three times; knowledge of the purity of the triple sphere; knowledge of the states of the body; knowledge of the states of the mind; guarding the modes of deportment; disturbing the modes of deportment [of others, to awaken them]; discriminating the modes of deportment; graciousness in deportment; knowledge and skill in the beneficial and harmful; speaking what is appropriate; knowledge of the world; generous giving; an open hand; a mind free from grasping; a sense of shame and moral dread; disgust toward unwholesome states of mind; not abandoning the <s>dhūtaguṇas</s> (ascetic qualities); undertaking proper conduct; engaging in pleasant behavior; rising from one's seat and offering it to elders; restraining pride; collecting the mind; knowledge of the arising of thoughts; knowledge of penetrating meaning; knowledge of penetrating wisdom; awakening through knowledge; departure of ignorance; knowledge of entering the mind; knowledge of awakening to the inherent nature of mind; knowledge and skill in providing nourishment [of dharma]; knowledge of all sounds; knowledge of establishing etymological analysis; knowledge of determining meaning; avoidance of the meaningless; contemplation of good persons; association with good persons; avoidance of base persons; accomplishment of the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions), and non-relishing therein; display of the higher knowledges; knowledge of entry into the inherent nature of conventional designations by name; transcendence of conventional designations; weariness with conditioned formations; non-desire for honors; equanimity regarding dishonors; non-interest in gain; non-despondency in non-gain; non-desire for fame; non-aversion to infamy; non-attachment to praise; non-dejection at blame; non-clinging to happiness; non-aversion to suffering; non-appropriation of conditioned formations; non-attachment to true praise; forbearance of false praise; not socializing with householders and renunciants [inappropriately]; avoidance of improper resorts; frequenting proper resorts; perfection of conduct; avoidance of misconduct; not corrupting families; not neglecting the teaching; speaking little; speaking moderately; skill in replies; refutation of opponents; timeliness; avoidance of untimeliness; distrust of ordinary beings; not despising the suffering, and giving wealth to them; not looking down upon the poor; compassion for the immoral; speaking what is beneficial; having a mind of mercy; benefiting through <s>dharma</s>; giving up material possessions; being established in non-accumulation; (Vaidya 6) praising moral conduct; censuring immorality; serving the virtuous without hypocrisy; giving up everything; inviting [others] with sincere intention; acting as one has spoken; constant application; experiencing joy with respect; knowledge of illustrations; skill in former connections; being preceded by wholesome roots; skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>); abandonment of signs; turning away from perceptions; full comprehension of objects; producing discourses (<s>sūtrāntas</s>); skill in <s>Vinaya</s>; determination of the truths; entry into the direct realization of liberation; speaking with definitive statement; not abandoning knowledge and vision as they truly are; speaking without doubt; cultivating emptiness; practicing the signless; observing the inherent nature of the wishless; attaining fearless confidence; illumination through knowledge; firmness in moral conduct; entry into attainments; attainment of wisdom; delight in solitude; self-knowledge; knowledge of what is minor; contentment; clarity of mind; avoidance of [wrong] views; attainment of <s>dhāraṇī</s> (mnemonic retention); entry into knowledge; knowledge of the practice regarding what is possible and impossible; the gateway of reasoning concerning causes; the principle; the path; the practice; the instruction; the admonition; the exhortation; the conduct; conforming patience; the ground of patience; departure of impatience; the ground of knowledge; abandonment of ignorance; establishment in knowledge; the ground of the practitioner of <s>yoga</s>; the domain of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>; association with good persons; avoidance of bad persons; knowledge of penetrating awakening to the inherent nature of all <s>dharmas</s>; the <s>Buddha</s>-stage proclaimed by the <s>Tathāgata</s>; approved by the wise; rejected by the foolish; hard to understand for <s>Śrāvakas</s>; known to <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>; beyond the reach of <s>tīrthikas</s>; embraced by <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; followed by the <s>Daśabalas</s> (Ten-Powered Ones); to be worshipped by gods; to be revered by <s>Brahmā</s>; to be realized by <s>Śakra</s>; to be honored by <s>Nāgas</s>; to be rejoiced in by <s>Yakṣas</s>; to be praised by <s>Kinnaras</s>; to be extolled by <s>Mahoragas</s>; to be cultivated by <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; to be fully mastered by the wise; it is the unsurpassed treasure; giving without material [reward]; medicine for the afflicted; joy of those with peaceful minds; the treasury of knowledge; the inexhaustible [source] of eloquence; the method of the <s>sūtrāntas</s>; the departure from the [five] repositories; the domain of heroes; the full comprehension of the three realms; the lineage of those who go to the far shore; the boat for those in the midst of the flood; the fame of those who desire renown; the praise of <s>Buddhas</s>; the commendation of <s>Tathāgatas</s>; the hymn of the <s>Daśabalas</s>; the virtue of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; the equanimity of the compassionate; the loving-kindness of those who wish to quell hostility; the joy of those whose conduct is peaceful; the encouragement of those of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; the practice of those whose roar is like a lion's; the path to the knowledge of a <s>Buddha</s>; the liberation of all beings; the seal of all <s>dharmas</s>; the sustenance of all knowledge; the garden of all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; the terror of <s>Māra</s>'s army; the knowledge of those going to safety; the purpose of those who have accomplished their aim; the protection of those amidst enemies; the refutation of opponents through the <s>dharma</s>; the treasury of the truths and the confidences; the search for truth by the foolish; the preliminary sign of the eighteen distinctive qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>; the ornament of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>; the outflow of conduct; the adornment of the <s>Buddha</s>'s sons; the delight of those who desire liberation; the joy of the eldest sons; the fulfillment of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge; beyond the reach of all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>; the purification of mind; the purification of body; the accomplishment of the doors of liberation; the non-defilement of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge; the non-arising of passion; (Vaidya 7) the departure of hatred; beyond the reach of delusion; the arising of knowledge; the production of <s>vidyā</s> (wisdom); the abandonment of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance); the satisfaction of those whose essence is liberation; the contentment of those whose essence is <s>samādhi</s>; the eye of those who wish to see; the higher knowledge of those who wish to perform miracles; the spiritual power of those who wish to create manifestations; the <s>dhāraṇī</s> of those who seek the meaning of what they have heard; the non-confusion of mindfulness; the foundation of the <s>Buddhas</s>; the skill in means of the Leaders; subtle, hard to understand for those not devoted [to practice]; unknowable by those not liberated; hard to understand through sound for those who turn away from letters; known by the discerning; understood by the gentle; penetrated by those of few desires; grasped by those of vigorous effort; retained by those possessed of mindfulness; the exhaustion of suffering; the non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s>; the single gateway of instruction for all existences, destinies, rebirths, and sense-bases. This, O Prince, is called the <s>samādhi</s> named 'Discernment of the Equality of the Inherent Nature of All <s>Dharmas</s>'.

body.text: asmin khalu punaḥ sarvadharmaparyāye samādhinirdeśe bhagavatā bhāṣyamāṇe aśīternayutānāṃ devamānuṣikāyāḥ prajāyāḥ pūrvaparikarmakṛtāyā anutpattikeṣu dharmeṣu kṣānteḥ pratilambho 'bhūt | ṣaṇṇavateśca nayutānāmānulomikāyāḥ kṣānteḥ pratilambho 'bhūt | triṇavaternayutānāṃ ghoṣānugāyāḥ kṣānteḥ pratilambho 'bhūt | paripūrṇasya bhikṣuśatasahasrasya anupādāyāsravebhyaścittāni vimuktāni | ṣaṣṭeśca prāṇiśatasahasrāṇāṃ devamānuṣikāyāḥ prajāyā virajo vigatamalaṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣurviśuddham | aśīteśca bhikṣusahasrāṇāmanupādāyāsravebhyaścitāni vimuktāni | pañcabhiścopāsakaśatairanāgāmiphalaṃ prāptam | ṣaṣṭyā copāsikāśataiḥ sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ prāptam | ayaṃ ca trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātuḥ ṣaḍvikāraṃ kampitaḥ prakampitaḥ saṃprakampitaḥ | calitaḥ pracalitaḥ saṃpracalitaḥ | vedhitaḥ pravedhitaḥ saṃpravedhitaḥ | kṣubhitaḥ prakṣubhitaḥ saṃprakṣubhitaḥ | raṇitaḥ praraṇitaḥ saṃpraraṇitaḥ | garjitaḥ pragarjitaḥ saṃpragarjitaḥ | pūrvā digavanamati paścimā digunnamati | paścimā digavanamati pūrvā digunnamati | uttarā digavanamati dakṣiṇā digunnamati | dakṣiṇā digavanamati uttarā digunnamati | antādavanamati madhyādunnamati | antādunnamati madhyādavanamati | aprameyasya cāvabhāsasya loke prādurbhāvo 'bhūt | sarvaśca lokadhātuḥ sadevakaśca samārakaḥ sabrahmakaḥ saśramaṇabrāhmaṇikāḥ prajāstenāvabhāsenāvabhāsitāḥ sphuṭā abhūvan | imau ca candrasūryau evaṃmaharddhikau evaṃmahānubhāvau evaṃmaheśākhyau na bhāsato na tapato na virocataḥ | yā api lokāntarikā andhakāratamisrāḥ, tā api tenāvabhāsena sphuṭā abhūvan | ye 'pi tāsūpapannāḥ sattvāḥ, te 'pyanyonyaṃ saṃjānate sma | evaṃ cāhuḥ - anyo 'pi kila bho ayaṃ sattva ihopapannaḥ | yāvadavīcermahānarakāditi ||
body.translated_text: When this discourse on <s>dharmas</s> — the exposition of <s>samādhi</s> — was being spoken by the Blessed One, eighty <s>nayutas</s> of the divine and human assembly who had performed prior preparation obtained the patient acceptance of the unborn nature of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpattikadharma-kṣānti</s>). Ninety-six <s>nayutas</s> obtained the conforming patience (<s>ānulomikī kṣānti</s>). Thirty-nine <s>nayutas</s> obtained the patience that follows upon hearing (<s>ghoṣānugā kṣānti</s>). A full hundred thousand monks had their minds liberated from the outflows without clinging. For sixty hundred thousand living beings of the divine and human assembly, the dust-free, stainless <s>Dharma</s>-eye was purified with regard to <s>dharmas</s>. Eighty thousand monks had their minds liberated from the outflows without clinging. Five hundred male lay followers attained the fruit of non-returner. Six hundred female lay followers attained the fruit of once-returner. And this trichiliocosmic world-system trembled with six kinds of trembling — it shook, greatly shook, and thoroughly shook; it quaked, greatly quaked, and thoroughly quaked; it vibrated, greatly vibrated, and thoroughly vibrated; it was agitated, greatly agitated, and thoroughly agitated; it resounded, greatly resounded, and thoroughly resounded; it rumbled, greatly rumbled, and thoroughly rumbled. The east dipped down and the west rose up; the west dipped down and the east rose up; the north dipped down and the south rose up; the south dipped down and the north rose up; the edges dipped down and the middle rose up; the edges rose up and the middle dipped down. And an immeasurable radiance appeared in the world. The entire world-system — with its gods, with its <s>Māras</s>, with its <s>Brahmās</s>, and its people including <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — was illuminated and suffused with that radiance. And these moon and sun, so mighty in supernatural power, so great in majesty, so great in sovereignty, did not shine, did not blaze, did not illuminate. Even those interworld spaces of blind darkness were suffused with that radiance. And those beings who were reborn there recognized one another and said: 'Why, there is another being reborn here too!' — and so on down to the great <s>Avīci</s> hell.

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje nidānaparivarto nāma prathamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the first chapter in the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, called the <s>Nidāna</s> (Introduction) chapter.

body.text:
(Vaidya 8)
2 Śālendrarājapūrvayogaparivarto dvitīyaḥ |
body.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 8) Chapter 2: The <s>Śālendrarāja-pūrvayoga</s> (Former Connection with King <s>Śālendrarāja</s>).

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāṃ candraprabhasya kumārabhūtasya etadeva pūrvayogaparivartaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā gāthābhigītena vistareṇa saṃprakāśayati sma -
body.translated_text: Then at that time the Blessed One illuminated in greater detail, in extensive verse, this very chapter on former connection for the prince <s>Candraprabha</s>:

children.text: smarati daśabalāna ṣaṣṭikoṭī purimabhave nivasiṃsu gṛdhrakūṭe /
children.translated_text: 'I remember sixty <s>koṭis</s> of Possessors of the Ten Powers who in former lives dwelt on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak);

children.text: puri mama caramāṇu bodhicaryāmima varaśānta samādhi deśayiṃsu // SRS_2.1 //
children.translated_text: formerly, while I was practicing the conduct of awakening, they taught this supreme, peaceful <s>samādhi</s>.' // SRS_2.1 //

children.text: teṣāṃ paścimako āsīllokanāthaḥ prabhaṃkaraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The last among them was the Lord of the World, <s>Prabhaṃkara</s> (Illuminator);

children.text: śālendrarāja nāmena sa mayā paripṛcchitaḥ // SRS_2.2 //
children.translated_text: he was named <s>Śālendrarāja</s> — and he was questioned by me.' // SRS_2.2 //

children.text: ahaṃ ca kṣatriyo āsaṃ rājaśreṣṭho mahīpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I was a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, the foremost of kings, a lord of the earth;

children.text: maṃma co śata putrāṇāṃ pañcābhūvannanūnakāḥ // SRS_2.3 //
children.translated_text: and I had five hundred sons, not one fewer.' // SRS_2.3 //

children.text: koṭīmayā vihāraṇāṃ tasya buddhasya kāritā /
children.translated_text: 'A <s>koṭi</s> of monasteries were built by me for that <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: candanasya viśiṣṭasya kecidratnamayā abhūta // SRS_2.4 //
children.translated_text: of the finest sandalwood — some were made of jewels.' // SRS_2.4 //

children.text: priyo manāpaśca bahujanasya bhīṣmottaro nāma abhūṣi rājā /
children.translated_text: 'Beloved and pleasing to the multitude, there was a king named <s>Bhīṣmottara</s>;

children.text: akārṣi buddhasya viśiṣṭapūjā aṣṭādaśavarṣasahasrakoṭyaḥ // SRS_2.5 //
children.translated_text: he performed distinguished worship of the <s>Buddha</s> for eighteen thousand <s>koṭis</s> of years.' // SRS_2.5 //

children.text: jinasya tasya dvipadottamasya śālendrarājasya vināyakasya /
children.translated_text: 'Of that <s>Jina</s>, supreme among bipeds, <s>Śālendrarāja</s>, the Guide —

children.text: ṣaṭūsaptativarṣasahasrakoṭiyo āyustadā āsi aninditasya // SRS_2.6 //
children.translated_text: his lifespan then was seventy-six thousand <s>koṭis</s> of years, that blameless one.' // SRS_2.6 //

children.text: niyutāntaśītisahasra śrāvakāṇāṃ traividya ṣaḍabhijña jitendriyāṇām /
children.translated_text: 'Eighty thousand <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, possessing the triple knowledge, the six superknowledges, with senses conquered,

children.text: kṣīṇāsravāṇāntimadehadhāriṇāṃ saṃghastadā āsi narottamasya // SRS_2.7 //
children.translated_text: with outflows destroyed, bearers of their final body — such was the <s>Saṃgha</s> then of that best of men.' // SRS_2.7 //

children.text: (Vaidya 9)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 9)

children.text: bahuprakārā mayi tasya pūjā kṛtā jinasya dvipadottamasya /
children.translated_text: 'Many kinds of worship were performed by me for that <s>Jina</s>, the supreme among bipeds;

children.text: arthāya lokasya sadevakasya imaṃ samādhiṃ pratikāṅtā sadā // SRS_2.8 //
children.translated_text: for the benefit of the world with its gods, I always longed for this <s>samādhi</s>.' // SRS_2.8 //

children.text: saputradāreṇa mi pravrajitvā śālendrarājasya jinasya antike /
children.translated_text: 'Having gone forth with wife and sons in the presence of the <s>Jina</s> <s>Śālendrarāja</s>,

children.text: caturdaśavarṣasahasrakoṭiyo ayaṃ samādhiḥ paripṛcchito mayā // SRS_2.9 //
children.translated_text: for fourteen thousand <s>koṭis</s> of years this <s>samādhi</s> was inquired about by me.' // SRS_2.9 //

children.text: aśīti gāthā niyutā sahasrāṇyanye ca koṭīśata bimbarāṇām /
children.translated_text: 'Eighty <s>nayutas</s> of thousands of verses, and also hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of other sections —

children.text: tasyodgṛhītaḥ sugatasya antikāditaḥ samādheḥ parivarta eṣaḥ // SRS_2.10 //
children.translated_text: that much was memorized from the presence of the <s>Sugata</s>: this is a chapter from that <s>samādhi</s>.' // SRS_2.10 //

children.text: hastā śirā bhārya tathaiva putrā ratnaṃ prabhūtaṃ tatha khādyabhojyam /
children.translated_text: 'Hands, head, wife, and sons, abundant jewels, food, and drink —

children.text: na kiṃci dravyaṃ mi na tyaktapūrvam ima samādhiṃ pratikāṅkṣatā varam // SRS_2.11 //
children.translated_text: there was no possession that I had not given away while longing for this supreme <s>samādhi</s>.' // SRS_2.11 //

children.text: smarāmi buddhāna sahasrakoṭiyo taduttare yattika gaṅgavālukāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I remember thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, and beyond that as many as the sands of the Ganges,

children.text: yehi sthihitvā iha gṛdhrakūṭe ayaṃ samādhirvaru śānta deśitaḥ // SRS_2.12 //
children.translated_text: who, having stood here on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s>, taught this excellent, peaceful <s>samādhi</s>.' // SRS_2.12 //

children.text: sarve ca śākyarṣabhanāmagheyāḥ sarveṣu co rāhula nāma putrāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'All bore the name <s>Śākyarṣabha</s> (Bull of the <s>Śākyas</s>); all had sons named <s>Rāhula</s>;

children.text: ānandanāmā paricārakāśca kapilāhvayāḥ pravrajitāśca sarve // SRS_2.13 //
children.translated_text: their attendants were all named <s>Ānanda</s>, and all had gone forth from [a city called] <s>Kapila</s>.' // SRS_2.13 //

children.text: agreyugaṃ kolitaśāriputrā samanāma sarve ca abhūṣi tāyinaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Their foremost pair were <s>Kolita</s> and <s>Śāriputra</s>; all those Protectors bore the same name;

children.text: samanāmikā co tada lokadhātuḥ sarve 'pi cotpanna kaṣāyakāle // SRS_2.14 //
children.translated_text: and the world-systems too had the same name — and all arose in the age of defilement.' // SRS_2.14 //

children.text: (Vaidya 10)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 10)

children.text: sarve mayā satkṛta te narendrā imāṃ carantena mi bodhicārikām /
children.translated_text: 'All those lords of men were honored by me while practicing this conduct of awakening;

children.text: yāvanti co kāci jināna pūjā sarvā kṛtā etu samādhimeṣatā // SRS_2.15 //
children.translated_text: and whatever worship of the <s>Jinas</s> — all was done desiring this <s>samādhi</s>.' // SRS_2.15 //

children.text: pratipattiya eṣa samādhi labhyate bahuprakārā pratipattiruktā /
children.translated_text: 'Through practice is this <s>samādhi</s> obtained — many kinds of practice have been declared;

children.text: guṇeṣu sarveṣu pratiṣṭhitasya na durlabhastasya samādhireṣaḥ // SRS_2.16 //
children.translated_text: for one established in all virtues, this <s>samādhi</s> is not hard to obtain.' // SRS_2.16 //

children.text: raseṣvagṛdhrasya alolupasya kuleṣvasaktasya anīrṣukasya /
children.translated_text: 'For one not greedy for flavors, not covetous, unattached to families, free from envy,

children.text: matrīvihārasya amatsarasya na durlabhastasya samādhireṣaḥ // SRS_2.17 //
children.translated_text: dwelling in loving-kindness, free from jealousy — this <s>samādhi</s> is not hard to obtain.' // SRS_2.17 //

children.text: satkāralābheṣu anarthikasya ājīvaśuddhasya akiṃcanasya /
children.translated_text: 'For one indifferent to honor and gain, of pure livelihood, possessing nothing,

children.text: viśuddhaśīlasya viśāradasya na durlabhastasya samādhireṣaḥ // SRS_2.18 //
children.translated_text: of pure morality, confident — this <s>samādhi</s> is not hard to obtain.' // SRS_2.18 //

children.text: ārabdhavīryasya atandritasya raṇyādhimuktasya dhute sthitasya /
children.translated_text: 'For one of aroused vigor, unwearied, delighting in solitude, established in ascetic practices,

children.text: nairātmyakṣāntīya pratiṣṭhitasya na durlabhastasya samādhireṣaḥ // SRS_2.19 //
children.translated_text: established in the patient acceptance of selflessness — this <s>samādhi</s> is not hard to obtain.' // SRS_2.19 //

children.text: sudāntacittasya anuddhatasya īryāya caryāya pratiṣṭhitasya /
children.translated_text: 'For one of well-tamed mind, not agitated, established in deportment and conduct,

children.text: tyāgādhimuktasya amatsarasya na durlabhastasya samādhireṣaḥ // SRS_2.20 //
children.translated_text: inclined to generosity, free from jealousy — this <s>samādhi</s> is not hard to obtain.' // SRS_2.20 //

children.text: anuvyañjanalakṣaṇā buddhadharmā ye 'ṣṭādaśā kīrtita nāyakena /
children.translated_text: 'The minor and major marks, the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, and those eighteen [special qualities] proclaimed by the Leader —

children.text: balāviśāradya na tasya durlabhā dhāreti yaḥ śāntamimaṃ samādhim // SRS_2.21 //
children.translated_text: the powers and confidences are not hard to obtain for one who upholds this peaceful <s>samādhi</s>.' // SRS_2.21 //

children.text: (Vaidya 11)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 11)

children.text: buddhena ye cakṣuṣa dṛṣṭa sattvāsta ekakālasmi bhaveyu buddhāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Those beings beheld by the <s>Buddha</s>'s eye in the ten directions — they would all become <s>Buddhas</s> at one time;

children.text: teṣaika ekasya bhaveyurāyuḥ acintiyākalpasahasrakoṭiyaḥ // SRS_2.22 //
children.translated_text: and the lifespan of each one of them would be inconceivable thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>.' // SRS_2.22 //

children.text: teṣaika ekasya śiro bhaveyuḥ sarvu samudreṣu yathaiva vālukāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Each one of them would have as many heads as there are grains of sand in all the oceans;

children.text: yāvanti te sarva śiro bhaveyuḥ śire śire jihva bhaveyu tāttikāḥ // SRS_2.23 //
children.translated_text: and as many as all those heads would be, each head would have that many tongues.' // SRS_2.23 //

children.text: te tasya sarve bhaṇi ānuśaṃsā yo gātha dhāreyya itaḥ samādhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'If all of them were to proclaim the benefits of one who upholds [even] a verse from this <s>samādhi</s>,

children.text: na kiṃcimātraṃ parikīrtitaṃ bhavet kiṃ vā punaryo hi śikṣitva dhāraye // SRS_2.24 //
children.translated_text: not even a fraction would be described — how much more so for one who trains in and upholds [the whole]!' // SRS_2.24 //

children.text: dhūtān samādāya guṇāṃśca vartate spṛhenti devāsurayakṣaguhyakāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'One who adopts the ascetic practices and abides in virtues — gods, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Guhyakas</s> attend him;

children.text: rājāna bhonti anuyātru tasya dhāreti yaḥ śānta samādhi durlabham // SRS_2.25 //
children.translated_text: kings become his retinue — for one who upholds this peaceful, rare <s>samādhi</s>.' // SRS_2.25 //

children.text: parigṛhīto bhavati jinebhirdevāśca nāgāḥ sada ānuyātrāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Protected by the <s>Jinas</s>, with gods and <s>Nāgas</s> always as retinue;

children.text: pratyarthikāstasya śriya no sahanti dhāreti yaḥ śānta samādhi durlabham // SRS_2.26 //
children.translated_text: adversaries cannot withstand his glory — for one who upholds this peaceful, rare <s>samādhi</s>.' // SRS_2.26 //

children.text: anantu tasya pratibhānu bhoti ananta sūtrāntasahasra bhāṣate /
children.translated_text: 'His eloquence becomes infinite; he speaks infinite thousands of <s>sūtras</s>;

children.text: na tasya viṣṭhā nu kadāci bhoti dhāreti yaḥ śāntamimaṃ samādhim // SRS_2.27 //
children.translated_text: he never becomes confused — for one who upholds this peaceful <s>samādhi</s>.' // SRS_2.27 //

children.text: drakṣyanti buddhamamitābhu nāyakaṃ sukhāvatīṃ cāpyatha lokadhātum /
children.translated_text: 'They shall see the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Amitābha</s>, the Leader, and the world-system <s>Sukhāvatī</s> —

children.text: ye paścime kāli mahābhayānake samādhi śrutvā imu dhārayeyuḥ // SRS_2.28 //
children.translated_text: those who, in the last age, the time of great terror, having heard this <s>samādhi</s>, uphold it.' // SRS_2.28 //

children.text: (Vaidya 12)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 12)

children.text: prakāśayitvā imu ānuśaṃsā adhyeṣate śāstu svayaṃ svayaṃbhūḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having proclaimed these benefits, the Self-Arisen Teacher himself entreats:

children.text: parinirvṛtasya mama paścikāle samādhi dhāretha imaṃ viśuddham // SRS_2.29 //
children.translated_text: "After my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, in the final time, uphold this pure <s>samādhi</s>!"' // SRS_2.29 //

children.text: ye keci buddhā daśasu diśāsu atītakāle 'pi ca pratyutpannāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever <s>Buddhas</s> there are in the ten directions, in the past and also in the present —

children.text: sarve jinā atra samādhiśikṣitā budhyanti bodhiṃ virajāmasaṃskṛtām // SRS_2.30 //
children.translated_text: all those <s>Jinas</s> trained in this <s>samādhi</s> and awakened to the dustless, unconditioned awakening.' // SRS_2.30 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje śālendrarāja(pūrvayoga)parivarto nāma dvitīyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter in the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, called the <s>Śālendrarāja-pūrvayoga</s> (Former Connection with <s>Śālendrarāja</s>) chapter.

body.text:
(Vaidya 13)
3 Bhūtaguṇavarṇaprakāśanaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 13) Chapter 3: The <s>Bhūtaguṇavarṇaprakāśana</s> (Illumination of the Description of True Qualities).

body.text:
tatra bhagavān punarapi candraprabhaṃ kumārabhūtamāmantrayate sma - tasmāttarhiṃ kumāra yo bodhisattvo mahāsattva ākāṅkṣati tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya bhūtaṃ buddhaguṇavarṇaṃ saṃprakāśayituṃ no cārthato vā vyañjanato vā paryādānaṃ gantuṃ sarvaṃ ca me vacanaṃ buddhaparigṛhītaṃ niścaritumiti, tena kumāra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sarvasattvānāmarthāya ayaṃ samādhirudgrahītavyaḥ paryavāptavyo dhārayitavyo vācayitavyaḥ pravartayitavyaḥ uddeṣṭavyaḥ svādhyātavyaḥ araṇābhāvanayā bhāvayitavyo bahulīkartavyaḥ parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayitavyaḥ | katame ca te kumāra tathāgatasya bhūtā buddhaguṇāḥ? iha kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'raṇyagato vā vṛkṣamūlagato vā abhyavakāśagato vā śūnyāgāramadhyagato vā evaṃ pratisaṃśikṣate - evaṃ sa bhagavāṃstathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān | niṣyandaḥ sa tathāgataḥ puṇyānām | avipraṇāśaḥ kuśalamūlānām | alaṃkṛtaḥ kṣāntyā | āgamaḥ puṇyanidhānānām | citrito 'nuvyañjanaiḥ | kusumito lakṣaṇaiḥ | pratirūpo gocareṇa | apratikūlo darśanena | abhiratiḥ śraddhādhimuktānām | anabhibhūtaḥ prajñayā | anavamardanīyo balaiḥ | śāstā sarvasattvānām | pitā bodhisattvānām | rājā āryapudgalānām | sārthavāha ādikarmikāṇām | aprameyo jñānena | anantaḥ pratibhānena | viśuddhaḥsvareṇa | āsvādanīyo ghoṣeṇa | asecanako rūpeṇa | apratisamaḥ kāyena | aliptaḥ kāmaiḥ | anupalipto rūpaiḥ | asaṃsṛṣṭa ārūpyaiḥ | vimukto duḥkhebhyaḥ | vipramuktaḥ skandhebhyaḥ | visaṃyukto dhātubhiḥ | saṃvṛta āyatanaiḥ | praticchanno granthaiḥ | vimuktaḥ paridāhaiḥ | parimuktastṛṣṇāyāḥ | oghāduttīrṇaḥ | paripūrṇo jñānena | pratiṣṭhito 'tītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ jñāne | apratiṣṭhito nirvḥṇe | sthito bhūtakoṭyḥm | sthitaḥ sarvasattvollokanīyḥyḥṃ bhūmau | ime te kumḥra tathḥgatasya bhūtḥ buddhaguṇḥḥ | ebhirbuddhaguṇavarṇaiḥ samanvḥgato bodhisattvo mahḥsattva imaṃ samḥdhimḥgamya anḥcchedyena pratibhḥnena tathḥgatasyḥhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya
bhūtaṃ buddhaguṇavarṇaṃ saṃprakḥśayan no cḥrthato no vyañjanataśca paryḥdḥnaṃ gacchati | sarvaṃ cḥsya vacanaṃ buddhaparigṛhītaṃ niścarati ||
body.translated_text: Thereupon the Blessed One again addressed the prince <s>Candraprabha</s>: "Therefore, prince, whatever <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> aspires to proclaim the true praise of the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, and not to reach exhaustion in either meaning or letter, and to utter all my words as encompassed by the <s>Buddha</s> — by that prince, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, for the sake of all beings, this <s>samādhi</s> should be taken up, mastered, retained, recited, circulated, expounded, studied, cultivated through the practice of non-contention (<s>araṇā</s>), made abundant, and extensively proclaimed to others. And what, prince, are the true <s>Buddha</s>-qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s>? Here, prince, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, gone to the forest, or gone to the root of a tree, or in the open air, or in an empty dwelling, trains thus: 'Thus is that Blessed One, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, <s>Sugata</s>, Knower of the World, unsurpassed, Charioteer of persons to be tamed, Teacher of gods and humans, <s>Buddha</s>, Blessed One. That <s>Tathāgata</s> is the outflow of merits. He is the non-loss of wholesome roots. He is adorned with patience. He is the repository of stores of merit. He is variegated with the minor marks. He is blossoming with the major marks. He is fitting in his domain. He is not disagreeable to behold. He is the delight of those with faith and conviction. He is unconquered by wisdom. He is unconquerable by powers. He is the teacher of all beings. He is the father of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. He is the king of noble persons. He is the caravan-leader of beginners. He is immeasurable in knowledge. He is infinite in eloquence. He is pure in voice. He is delightful in speech. He is exquisite in form. He is incomparable in body. He is unstained by desires. He is unsmeared by forms. He is unmixed with the formless. He is freed from sufferings. He is released from the aggregates. He is disjoined from the elements. He is closed off from the sense-bases. He is concealed from the bonds. He is liberated from torments. He is released from craving. He has crossed beyond the flood. He is complete in knowledge. He is established in the knowledge of the <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones of the past, future, and present. He does not abide in <s>nirvāṇa</s>. He is established at the limit of reality. He is established on the ground from which all beings may behold him.' These, prince, are the true <s>Buddha</s>-qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. A <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> endowed with these praises of <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, having entered this <s>samādhi</s>, with unbroken eloquence proclaims the true praise of the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, and does not reach exhaustion in either meaning or letter. And all his words issue forth as encompassed by the <s>Buddha</s>. //

body.text: atha bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses —

children.text: na sukaru jinavarṇa sarvi vaktuṃ bahumapi kalpasahasra bhāṣamāṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: "It is not easy to speak all the praise of the <s>Jina</s>, even if one were to speak for many thousands of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: (Vaidya 14)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya p. 14)

children.text: tatha guṇa samudānitā jinebhiḥ imu varu śānta samādhimeṣamāṇaiḥ // SRS_3.1 //
children.translated_text: such qualities have been accumulated by the <s>Jinas</s> — by those who seek this supreme, peaceful <s>samādhi</s>!" // SRS_3.1 //

children.text: paramasu-abhirūpadarśanīyāḥ kanya alaṃkṛtagātra premaṇīyāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Supremely beautiful and lovely to behold, maidens with adorned limbs, endearing —

children.text: datta puri adīnamānasena imu varu śānta samādhimeṣatā me // SRS_3.2 //
children.translated_text: these were given by me formerly with an undaunted mind — [all] in search of this supreme, peaceful <s>samādhi</s>!" // SRS_3.2 //

children.text: tatha mayi dhanadhānyadāsidāsā tatha maṇimuktisuvarṇarūpyakaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: "Likewise wealth, grain, male and female servants, and jewels, pearls, gold, and silver —

children.text: tyakta mayi adīnamānasena imu varu śānta samādhimeṣatā me // SRS_3.3 //
children.translated_text: these were relinquished by me with an undaunted mind — [all] in search of this supreme, peaceful <s>samādhi</s>!" // SRS_3.3 //

children.text: maṇiratanavicitramuktahārā rucira pu vasana śaṅkhasuvarṇasūtrā /
children.translated_text: "Pearl necklaces variegated with jewels, beautiful garments with threads of conch-shell and gold —

children.text: tyakta mayi purā vināyakeṣu imu varu śānta samādhimeṣatā me // SRS_3.4 //
children.translated_text: these were relinquished by me formerly to the Guides — [all] in search of this supreme, peaceful <s>samādhi</s>!" // SRS_3.4 //

children.text: aparimita ananta kalpakoṭyaḥ paramasugandhika vārṣikāśca /
children.translated_text: "For immeasurable, infinite <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, supremely fragrant <s>vārṣika</s> flowers and others —

children.text: tyakta mayi jināna cetiyeṣu paramaniruttaru cittu saṃjanitvā // SRS_3.5 //
children.translated_text: these were relinquished by me at the shrines of the <s>Jinas</s>, having generated the supreme, unsurpassed mind!" // SRS_3.5 //

children.text: tathariva mayi dattu dharmadānaṃ parṣagatena janitva citrikāram /
children.translated_text: "Likewise the gift of <s>Dharma</s> was given by me, generating wonder in the assembly;

children.text: na ca mama samutpanna jātu cittaṃ siya mama jñātru daditva dharmadānam // SRS_3.6 //
children.translated_text: and never did a thought arise in me: 'May someone know that I have given the gift of <s>Dharma</s>!'" // SRS_3.6 //

children.text: eta guṇa samudānituṃ mi pūrvā vana varu sevita nityamalpaśabdam /
children.translated_text: "These qualities were accumulated by me formerly — I frequented the finest forests, always quiet,

children.text: kṛpabahulu bhavāmi nityakālaṃ sada mama cittu labheya buddhajñānam // SRS_3.7 //
children.translated_text: I was always full of compassion — [with this thought]: 'May my mind always attain <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge!'" // SRS_3.7 //

children.text: na ca mama kvacidāgraho abhūṣi priyataravastuna ātmano 'pi bhoktum /
children.translated_text: "And never did I have attachment anywhere, nor desire to enjoy even the dearest possessions for myself;

children.text: (Vaidya 15)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya p. 15)

children.text: dadami ahu prabhūta deyadharmaṃ sada mama cittu labheya buddhajñānam // SRS_3.8 //
children.translated_text: I give abundantly the things to be given — [with this thought]: 'May my mind always attain <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge!'" // SRS_3.8 //

children.text: akhilamadhurasaṃvibhāgaśīlaḥ smitavadanaḥ śrutidhāri snigdhaghoṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: "With the character of sharing all sweet things completely, with a smiling face, retaining what is heard, with an affectionate voice,

children.text: sumadhuravacanaḥ priyo bahūnāṃ jana mama sarvi atṛpta darśanena // SRS_3.9 //
children.translated_text: speaking supremely sweet words, dear to many — all people are never satiated by the sight of me!" // SRS_3.9 //

children.text: kṣaṇamapi ca na matsarī bhavāmi bhavaniyutena na jātu īrṣyamāsīt /
children.translated_text: "Not even for a moment have I been miserly; for <s>niyutas</s> of existences there was never envy in me;

children.text: sada ahu paritṛpta piṇḍapāte sakala nimantraṇa varjitānyaśeṣā // SRS_3.10 //
children.translated_text: I am always content with alms-food, having completely abandoned all invitations!" // SRS_3.10 //

children.text: bahuśruta śrutadhāri ye bhavanti gātha ito dharaye catuṣpadāṃ pi /
children.translated_text: "Those who are learned and retain what they have heard — whoever retains even a single four-line verse from this —

children.text: te mayi sada satkṛtā abhūvan parama niruttara prema saṃjanitvā // SRS_3.11 //
children.translated_text: they have always been honored by me, having generated supreme, unsurpassed affection!" // SRS_3.11 //

children.text: bahuvidhamananta dānu dattaṃ tathapi ca rakṣitu śīlu dīrgharātram /
children.translated_text: "Manifold, infinite gifts have been given, and morality has been guarded for a long time;

children.text: pūja bahu kṛtā vināyakeṣu imu varu śānta samādhimeṣatā me // SRS_3.12 //
children.translated_text: much worship has been performed to the Guides — [all] in search of this supreme, peaceful <s>samādhi</s>!" // SRS_3.12 //

children.text: pṛthu vividha ananta lokadhātūn maṇiratanaiḥ paripūrya dānu dadyāt /
children.translated_text: "If someone were to fill vast, manifold, infinite world-systems with precious jewels and give them as a gift,

children.text: itu dharayi samādhitaśca gāthām imu tatpuṇya viśiṣyate udāram // SRS_3.13 //
children.translated_text: and [another] were to retain from this <s>samādhi</s> a [single] verse — that merit would be far superior and sublime!" // SRS_3.13 //

children.text: yāvat pṛthu kecidasti puṣpā tathariva gandha manoramā udārāḥ /
children.translated_text: "However many flowers there are, and likewise delightful, sublime fragrances —

children.text: tehi jinu maheyya puṇyakāmā bahumapi kalpa ananta aprameyān // SRS_3.14 //
children.translated_text: with those one might worship the <s>Jina</s>, desiring merit, for many infinite, immeasurable <s>kalpas</s>; // SRS_3.14 //

children.text: yāvat pṛthu kecidasti vādyā tatha bahu bhojana annapānavastrāḥ /
children.translated_text: "and however many musical instruments there are, and likewise abundant food, drink, and garments —

children.text: tehi jinu maheyya puṇyakāmā bahumapi kalpa ananta aprameyān // SRS_3.15 //
children.translated_text: with those one might worship the <s>Jina</s>, desiring merit, for many infinite, immeasurable <s>kalpas</s>; // SRS_3.15 //

children.text: (Vaidya 16)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya p. 16)

children.text: yaśca naru janitva bodhicittam ahu jinu bheṣyu svayaṃbhu dharmarājaḥ /
children.translated_text: "yet if a person, having generated <s>bodhicitta</s>, [says:] 'I shall become a <s>Jina</s>, a Self-Arisen One, a <s>Dharma</s>-king!'

children.text: gāthamimu dhare samāhitaikāṃ tato viśiṣyate puṇyamudāram // SRS_3.16 //
children.translated_text: and retains even a single verse of this [text] with concentration — that sublime merit surpasses [the former]!" // SRS_3.16 //

children.text: yāvata pṛthu gaṅgavālikāḥ syustāvata kalpa bhaṇeya ānuśaṃsā /
children.translated_text: "Even if there were as many <s>Gaṅgā</s>-sand-[grains] as there are in all those vast [rivers], and one were to proclaim the benefits for that many <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: na ca parikṣaya śakyu kīrtyamāne bahutara puṇyasamādhi dhārayitvā // SRS_3.17 //
children.translated_text: even then the merit of retaining this <s>samādhi</s> could not be exhausted when praised — it is far greater!" // SRS_3.17 //

body.text: tasmāttarhi kumāra bodhisattven mahāsattvena udgrahītavyo dhārayitavyo vācayitavyaḥ paryavāptavyaḥ | udgṛhya dhārayitvā vācayitvā paryavāpya araṇābhāvanāyogamanuyuktena ca bhavitavyam | tad bhaviṣyati bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca | atha khalu bhagavāstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Therefore, prince, this [<s>samādhi</s>] should be taken up, retained, recited, and mastered by a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>. Having taken it up, retained it, recited it, and mastered it, one should be devoted to the practice of cultivating non-contention (<s>araṇā</s>). That will be for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of the great multitude, of gods and humans. Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses —

children.text: tasmācchrutveti buddhānāmānuśaṃsān subhadrakān /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, having heard these splendid benefits of the <s>Buddhas</s>,

children.text: kṣipramuddiśathā etaṃ samādhiṃ buddhavarṇitam // SRS_3.18 //
children.translated_text: quickly expound this <s>samādhi</s> praised by the <s>Buddha</s>! // SRS_3.18 //

children.text: trisaptatibuddhakoṭyaḥ pūrvajātiṣu satkṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Seventy-three <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> were honored in former births;

children.text: sarvehi tehi buddhehi idaṃ sūtraṃ prakāśitam // SRS_3.19 //
children.translated_text: by all those <s>Buddhas</s> this <s>sūtra</s> was proclaimed! // SRS_3.19 //

children.text: mahākaruṇajetāramidaṃ sūtraṃ nirucyate /
children.translated_text: "This <s>sūtra</s> is called the conqueror of great compassion;

children.text: bāhuśrutyasmi śikṣitvā buddhadharmā na durlabhāḥ // SRS_3.20 //
children.translated_text: having trained in learning, the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities are not hard to obtain! // SRS_3.20 //

children.text: bheṣyanti paścime kāle nirvṛte lokanāyake /
children.translated_text: "In the latter age, when the Guide of the World has passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: bahu asaṃyatā bhikṣu bāhuśrutye anarthikāḥ // SRS_3.21 //
children.translated_text: there will be many undisciplined monks, uninterested in learning; // SRS_3.21 //

children.text: śīlasya varṇaṃ vakṣyanti śīlena ca anarthikāḥ /
children.translated_text: "they will speak the praise of morality, yet have no interest in morality;

children.text: samādhivarṇaṃ vakṣyanti samādhiya anarthikāḥ // SRS_3.22 //
children.translated_text: they will speak the praise of <s>samādhi</s>, yet have no interest in <s>samādhi</s>; // SRS_3.22 //

children.text: prajñāya varṇaṃ vakṣyanti prajñāya ca anarthikāḥ /
children.translated_text: "they will speak the praise of wisdom, yet have no interest in wisdom;

children.text: vimuktyā bahu bhāṣante vimuktyā ca anarthikāḥ // SRS_3.23 //
children.translated_text: they will speak much about liberation, yet have no interest in liberation! // SRS_3.23 //

children.text: candanasya yathā kaścid bhāṣate puruṣo guṇān /
children.translated_text: "Just as a certain man speaks the virtues of sandalwood:

children.text: īdṛśaṃ candanaṃ nāma gandhajātaṃ manoramam // SRS_3.24 //
children.translated_text: "Such is sandalwood — a fragrant substance, delightful!" // SRS_3.24 //

children.text: athānyaḥ puruṣaḥ kaścidevaṃ pṛccheta taṃ naram /
children.translated_text: "And another man might ask that person:

children.text: gṛhīta candanaṃ kiṃcid yasya vaṇa prabhāṣase // SRS_3.25 //
children.translated_text: "Have you obtained any sandalwood, whose qualities you proclaim?" // SRS_3.25 //

children.text: (Vaidya 17)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya p. 17)

children.text: sa naraṃ taṃ pratibrūyād gandhavarṇaṃ bravīmyaham /
children.translated_text: "That man would reply: "I speak the praise of fragrance;

children.text: jīvikāṃ yena kalpemi taṃ ca gandhaṃ na vedmyaham // SRS_3.26 //
children.translated_text: I earn my livelihood by it — but I myself do not know that fragrance!" // SRS_3.26 //

children.text: evaṃ yoge 'pyayuktānāṃ śīlavarṇena jīvikā /
children.translated_text: "Thus, for those who are not yoked to practice, their livelihood will come from praising morality —

children.text: paścime bheṣyate kāle śīlaṃ caiṣāṃ na bheṣyate // SRS_3.27 //
children.translated_text: this will be in the latter age — yet they themselves will have no morality! // SRS_3.27 //

children.text: evaṃ yoge 'pyayuktānāṃ samādhivarṇena jīvikā /
children.translated_text: "Thus, for those who are not yoked to practice, their livelihood will come from praising <s>samādhi</s> —

children.text: paścime bheṣyate kāle samādhiścaiṣāṃ na bheṣyate // SRS_3.28 //
children.translated_text: this will be in the latter age — yet they themselves will have no <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_3.28 //

children.text: evaṃ yoge 'pyayuktānāṃ prajñāvarṇana jīvikā /
children.translated_text: "Thus, for those who are not yoked to practice, their livelihood will come from describing wisdom —

children.text: bheṣyate paścime kāle prajñā caiṣāṃ na bheṣyate // SRS_3.29 //
children.translated_text: this will be in the latter age — yet they themselves will have no wisdom! // SRS_3.29 //

children.text: evaṃ yoge 'pyayuktānāṃ vimuktivarṇena jīvikā /
children.translated_text: "Thus, for those who are not yoked to practice, their livelihood will come from praising liberation —

children.text: bheṣyate paścime kāle vimuktiścaiṣāṃ na bheṣyate // SRS_3.30 //
children.translated_text: this will be in the latter age — yet they themselves will have no liberation! // SRS_3.30 //

children.text: yatha puruṣu daridru kaścideva sace paribhūtu bhavenmahājanasya /
children.translated_text: "Just as a certain poor man, if he were despised by the multitude,

children.text: sa ca labhati nidhānu paścakāle dhanapati bhūtva janāna satkareyyā // SRS_3.31 //
children.translated_text: were to find a treasure afterward — having become wealthy, he would be honored by the people; // SRS_3.31 //

children.text: evamimu na samādhi yāva labdho na ca bahumato bhavatīha bodhisattvaḥ /
children.translated_text: "so too, as long as this <s>samādhi</s> is not obtained, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is not much esteemed here,

children.text: marumanujakumbhāṇḍarākṣasā no yatha puruṣu daridru arthahīnaḥ // SRS_3.32 //
children.translated_text: among <s>Māras</s>, humans, <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, and <s>Rākṣasas</s> — like a poor man without wealth; // SRS_3.32 //

children.text: yada punariya labdha bhoti bhūmī atuliyu dharmanidhānu paṇḍitena /
children.translated_text: "but when this ground has been obtained, [like] an incomparable treasury of <s>Dharma</s>, by the wise one,

children.text: maru manuja spṛhaṃ janenti tatra sa ca dhanu deti niruttaraṃ prajānām // SRS_3.33 //
children.translated_text: <s>Māras</s> and humans generate longing for him, and he gives the unsurpassed wealth to beings!" // SRS_3.33 //

children.text: tasma imi śruṇitva ānuśaṃsāṃ paramapraṇītayaḥ kīrtitā jinena /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, having heard these benefits — supreme and sublime, proclaimed by the <s>Jina</s> —

children.text: sarva jahiya jñātralābhasaukhyamimu varamuddiśathā samādhi śāntam // SRS_3.34 //
children.translated_text: abandoning all enjoyments of kinsmen and possessions, expound this supreme, peaceful <s>samādhi</s>!" // SRS_3.34 //

children.text: ye keci buddhā diśatā sunirvṛtā anāgatā ye 'pi ca pratyutpannāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Whatever <s>Buddhas</s> have passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s> in the [ten] directions, and those yet to come, and those of the present —

children.text: sarve ca śikṣitva iha samādhau bodhiṃ vibuddhā atulāmacintiyām // SRS_3.35 //
children.translated_text: all of them, having trained in this <s>samādhi</s>, awakened to the incomparable, inconceivable <s>bodhi</s>!" // SRS_3.35 //

children.text: (Vaidya 18)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya p. 18)

children.text: candraprabhaḥ kumāru hṛṣṭacittaḥ puratu jinasya sthihitva vāca bhāṣī /
children.translated_text: The prince <s>Candraprabha</s>, with joyful mind, standing before the <s>Jina</s>, spoke these words:

children.text: ahu puruṣavarasya nirvṛtasya sukisari kāli idaṃ dhariṣye sūtram // SRS_3.36 //
children.translated_text: "I, in the hard times after the supreme man has passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>, shall retain this <s>sūtra</s>! // SRS_3.36 //

children.text: kāya ahu tyajitva jīvitaṃ ca tathapi ca saukhya yadasti loke /
children.translated_text: "Having renounced body and life, and likewise whatever happiness there is in the world,

children.text: tatra ahu mahābhaye 'pi kāle imu varu śānta samādhi dhārayiṣye // SRS_3.37 //
children.translated_text: even in times of great danger, I shall retain this supreme, peaceful <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_3.37 //

children.text: mahakaruṇa janitva sattvakāye sudukhita sattva anātha prāpta dṛṣṭvā /
children.translated_text: "Having generated great compassion for the community of beings, seeing suffering, unprotected beings who have arrived [at my door],

children.text: teṣvahamupasaṃharitva maitrīmimu vara śānta samādhi deśayiṣye // SRS_3.38 //
children.translated_text: directing loving-kindness toward them, I shall teach this supreme, peaceful <s>samādhi</s>!" // SRS_3.38 //

children.text: pañcaśata anūna tasmin kāle ya utthita tatra samādhidhārakāṇām /
children.translated_text: "At that time, no fewer than five hundred arose there as holders of this <s>samādhi</s>;

children.text: pūrvaṃgama kumāra teṣa āsīdiha varasūtraparigrahe udāre // SRS_3.39 //
children.translated_text: the prince was their leader in the reception of this supreme, sublime <s>sūtra</s>." // SRS_3.39 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje bhūtaguṇavarṇaprakāśanaparivarto nāma tṛtīyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter of the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, named "The Exposition of the True Praise of the <s>Buddha</s>-Qualities." //

body.text:
(Vaidya 19)
4 Buddhānusmṛtiparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Vaidya p. 19) Chapter 4: The Chapter on the Recollection of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>Buddhānusmṛtiparivarta</s>).

body.text: atha khalu candraprabhaḥ kumārabhūto bhagavantametadavocat - samādhiḥ samādhiriti bhagavannucyate | katamasyaitaddharmasyādhivacanaṃ samādhiriti? evamukte bhagavāṃścandraprabhaṃ kumārabhūtametadavocat - samādhiḥ samādhiriti kumāra ucyate yaduta cittanidhyāptiḥ | anupapattiḥ | apratisaṃdhiḥ | pratisaṃdhijñānam | apahṛtabhāratā | tathāgatajñānam | buddhavṛṣabhitā | rāgacikitsā | doṣavyupaśamaḥ | mohasya prahāṇam | yuktayogitā | ayuktavivarjanatā | akuśaladharmacchandaḥ | saṃsārānmokṣakāmatā | adhyāśayapratipattiḥ | jāgarikāyā āsevanam | prahāṇasyānutsargaḥ | ārakṣā śukladharmāṇām | upapattiṣvaviśvāsaḥ | anabhisaṃskāraḥ | karmaṇāmādhyātmikānāmāyatanānāmamanasikāraḥ | bāhyānāmāyatanānāmasamudācāraḥ | ātmano 'nutkarṣaṇam | pareṣāmapaṃsanatā | kuśaleṣvanadhyavasānam | pṛthagjaneṣvaviśvāsaḥ | śīlasya niṣyandaḥ | durāsadatā | mahaujaskatā | ātmajñānam | acapalatā | īryāpathasaṃpadavasthānam | avyāpādaḥ | apāruṣyam | pareṣvanutpīḍā | mitrāṇāmanurakṣaṇā | guhyamantrāṇāmārakṣaṇā | avihiṃsā | śīlavatāmanutpīḍanā | ślakṣṇavacanatā | sarvatraidhātuke aniḥśritatā | sarvadharmeṣu śūnyatā | ānulomikī kṣāntiḥ | sarvajñajñāne tīvracchandatā samādhiḥ samādhiriti kumāra ucyate | yā eveṣvevaṃrūpeṣu dharmeṣu pratipattirapratipattiḥ, ayaṃ sa kumāra ucyate samādhiriti ||
body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Candraprabha</s> the prince said this to the Blessed One: '<s>Samādhi</s>, <s>samādhi</s> — thus, O Blessed One, it is spoken. Of which <s>dharma</s> is this a designation — <s>samādhi</s>?' Thus addressed, the Blessed One said this to <s>Candraprabha</s> the prince: '<s>Samādhi</s>, <s>samādhi</s> — thus, O prince, it is said, namely: resolution of mind; non-arising; non-reconnection; knowledge of reconnection; having cast off the burden; <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge; bull-like eminence of the <s>Buddha</s>; treatment of passion; pacification of faults; abandonment of delusion; proper engagement; avoidance of improper engagement; non-desire for unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>; desire for liberation from <s>saṃsāra</s>; practice with superior intention; cultivation of wakefulness; non-relinquishment of exertion; guarding of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>; distrust in future rebirths; non-fabrication; non-attention to internal sense-bases in regard to actions; non-engagement with external sense-bases; not elevating oneself; not disparaging others; non-complacency in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>; distrust in ordinary people; the outflow of morality; being unapproachable [by evil]; being of great energy; self-knowledge; steadiness; abiding in the accomplishment of deportment; non-malice; non-harshness; non-oppression of others; protecting friends; guarding secret counsels; non-violence; non-oppression of the virtuous; speaking gently; non-reliance on the entire triple realm; emptiness in all <s>dharmas</s>; conformity-patience (<s>ānulomikī kṣānti</s>); intense zeal for omniscient knowledge. <s>Samādhi</s>, <s>samādhi</s> — thus, O prince, it is called. That which is the practice and non-practice in these kinds of <s>dharmas</s> — that, O prince, is called <s>samādhi</s>.' ||

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then indeed the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: apāvṛtaṃ me amṛtasya dvāram ācakṣito dharmasvabhāvu yādṛśaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The door of the deathless has been opened by me; the inherent nature of <s>dharma</s> has been declared, such as it is;

children.text: nidarśitā me upapatti yādṛśī prakāśitā nirvṛti sānuśaṃsā // SRS_4.1 //
children.translated_text: the manner of rebirth has been shown by me, such as it is; cessation has been illuminated, along with its benefits. // SRS_4.1 //

children.text: vivarjanīyāḥ sada pāpamitrāḥ kalyāṇamitrāśca niṣevitavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Evil friends must always be avoided, and good friends must be cultivated;

children.text: vaneṣu vastavya gaṇān jahitvā maitraṃ ca cittaṃ sada bhāvanīyam // SRS_4.2 //
children.translated_text: one should dwell in forests, having abandoned crowds, and a mind of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) should always be developed. // SRS_4.2 //

body.text:
śuddhaṃ ca śīlaṃ sada rakṣitavyaṃ dhūteṣu puṣṭiḥ sada vinditavyā /
tyāgaśca prajñā ca niṣevitavyā | na durlabho eṣa samādhi bheṣyati // SRS_4.3 //
body.translated_text: Pure morality (<s>śīla</s>) should always be guarded; strength should always be found in ascetic practices (<s>dhūtas</s>); renunciation and wisdom should be cultivated — this <s>samādhi</s> will not be hard to obtain. // SRS_4.3 //

children.text: (Vaidya 20)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 20)

children.text: tato labhitvā ima śāntabhūmi yasyāmabhūmiḥ pṛthu śrāvakāṇām /
children.translated_text: Having then obtained this stage of peace, in which there is no stage for common <s>Śrāvakas</s>,

children.text: pratyakṣabhūtā sugatasya dharma pratilapsyathā buddhaguṇānacintiyān // SRS_4.4 //
children.translated_text: with the <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>Sugata</s> becoming directly manifest, you will obtain the inconceivable qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>. // SRS_4.4 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā narān bhājanabuddhimantān tān bodhicittasmi samādahetha /
children.translated_text: Seeing people who are vessels of intelligence, establish them in the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>);

children.text: anuttare jñāni pratiṣṭhapitvā na durlabho eṣa samādhirājaḥ // SRS_4.5 //
children.translated_text: having established them in unsurpassed knowledge — this King of <s>Samādhi</s> (<s>Samādhirāja</s>) will not be hard to obtain. // SRS_4.5 //

children.text: yasyārthi īrṣā puna saṃjaneyyā āhāri niṣyandiha pratyavekṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: If envy should arise for one seeking [this <s>samādhi</s>], let one examine the procurement, the outflow,

children.text: paryeṣṭitaśco paribhogataśca na durlabho eṣa samādhi bheṣyate // SRS_4.6 //
children.translated_text: the searching, and the consumption — this <s>samādhi</s> will not be hard to obtain. // SRS_4.6 //

children.text: samādhirājo yadi vaiṣa śūnyato viśuddhaśīlānayu mūrdhni tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: This King of <s>Samādhi</s>, being empty, stands at the crown of those of pure morality;

children.text: svabhāvato dharma sadā samāhitā bālā na jānanti ayuktayogāḥ // SRS_4.7 //
children.translated_text: <s>dharmas</s> are always concentrated by their very nature — fools who are improperly engaged do not know this. // SRS_4.7 //

children.text: yeṣāmayaṃ śānta samādhiriṣṭo na teṣa jātu bhayabuddhi tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: In those for whom this peaceful <s>samādhi</s> is cherished, no thought of fear ever arises;

children.text: sadānupaśyanti narāṇamuttamamimāṃ niṣevitva praśāntabhūmim // SRS_4.8 //
children.translated_text: they always behold the highest of men, having cultivated this stage of supreme peace. // SRS_4.8 //

children.text: ākārato yaḥ smarate tathāgatān sa bhoti śāntendriyu śāntamānasaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who recollects the <s>Tathāgatas</s> through their form — he becomes one of tranquil senses and tranquil mind,

children.text: abhrāntacittaḥ satataṃ samāhitaḥ śrutena jñānena ca sāgaropamaḥ // SRS_4.9 //
children.translated_text: of unconfused thought, constantly concentrated, like an ocean in learning and knowledge. // SRS_4.9 //

children.text: asmin samādhau hi pratiṣṭhihittvā yaścaṃkrame caṃkrami bodhisattvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having established himself in this <s>samādhi</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who practices walking meditation —

children.text: sa paśyati buddhasahasrakoṭiyastaduttare yāttika gaṅgavālukāḥ // SRS_4.10 //
children.translated_text: he sees thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, and beyond that, as many as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. // SRS_4.10 //

children.text: unmādu gaccheya narasya cittaṃ yo buddhadharmāṇa pramāṇu gṛhṇīyāt /
children.translated_text: A man's mind would go to madness if he were to try to measure the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>;

children.text: (Vaidya 21)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 21)

children.text: naivāpramāṇasya pramāṇamasti acintiyā sarvaguṇehi nāyakāḥ // SRS_4.11 //
children.translated_text: for there is no measure of the immeasurable — the Leaders are inconceivable in all their qualities. // SRS_4.11 //

children.text: na so 'sti sattvo daśasu diśāsu yo lokanāthena samaḥ kutottari /
children.translated_text: There is no being in the ten directions who is equal to the Lord of the World, much less superior;

children.text: sarve hi sarvajñaguṇarupetamākāṅkṣatha lapsyatha buddhajñānam // SRS_4.12 //
children.translated_text: all who aspire to the qualities of omniscience shall obtain <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. // SRS_4.12 //

children.text: suvarṇavarṇena samucchrayeṇa samantaprāsādiku lokanāthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Golden-colored in his stature, all-pleasing, the Lord of the World —

children.text: yasyātra ālambani cittu vartate samāhitaḥ socyati bodhisattvaḥ // SRS_4.13 //
children.translated_text: he in whose mind attention to this [form as] support dwells, concentrated — he is called a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. // SRS_4.13 //

children.text: asaṃskṛtaṃ saṃskṛtu jñātva vijño nimittasaṃjñāya vibhāvitāya /
