children.translated_text: The wise one, having known the conditioned and the unconditioned, having developed [beyond] the perception of signs,

children.text: so ānimitte bhavati pratiṣṭhitaḥ prajānatī śūnyaka sarvadharmān // SRS_4.14 //
children.translated_text: becomes established in the signless, knowing all <s>dharmas</s> as empty. // SRS_4.14 //

children.text: yo dharmakāye bhavati pratiṣṭhito abhāva jānāti sa sarvabhāvān /
children.translated_text: He who is established in the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (Dharma-body) knows all phenomena as non-existent;

children.text: abhāvasaṃjñāya vibhāvitāya na rūpakāyena jinendra paśyati // SRS_4.15 //
children.translated_text: having developed the perception of non-existence, he does not see the Lord of Conquerors (<s>Jinendra</s>) through the form-body. // SRS_4.15 //

children.text: ārocayāmi prativedayāmi vo yathā yathā bahu ca vitarkayennaraḥ /
children.translated_text: I declare and proclaim to you: in whatever way and however much a man thinks discursively,

children.text: tathā tathā bhavati tannimittacittastehi vitarkehi tanniśritehi // SRS_4.16 //
children.translated_text: in that same way his mind takes on the signs of those very thoughts, dependent upon them. // SRS_4.16 //

children.text: evaṃ munīndraṃ smarato narasya ākārato jñānato aprameyataḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, for a man recollecting the Lord of Sages through form, through knowledge, through immeasurability,

children.text: anusmṛtiṃ bhāvayataḥ sadā ca tannimnacittaṃ bhavatī tatproṇam // SRS_4.17 //
children.translated_text: always cultivating mindfulness — his mind becomes inclined and bent toward that. // SRS_4.17 //

children.text: sa caṃkramastho na niṣadyamāśrita ākāṅkṣate puruṣavarasya jñānam /
children.translated_text: Standing in walking meditation, not relying on sitting, he aspires to the knowledge of the Best of Men;

children.text: ākāṅkṣamāṇaḥ praṇigheti bodhaye bhaviṣyahaṃ loki niruttaro jinaḥ // SRS_4.18 //
children.translated_text: aspiring, he makes a resolution for awakening: "I shall become in the world the unsurpassed Conqueror (<s>Jina</s>)." // SRS_4.18 //

children.text: (Vaidya 22)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 22)

children.text: sa buddha saṃjānati buddha paśyate buddhāna co dharmata pratyavekṣate /
children.translated_text: He recognizes the <s>Buddha</s>, he sees the <s>Buddha</s>, and he examines the <s>Buddhas</s>' true nature (<s>dharmatā</s>);

children.text: iha samādhismi pratiṣṭhihitvā namasyate buddha mahānubhāvān // SRS_4.19 //
children.translated_text: having established himself in this <s>samādhi</s>, he pays homage to the <s>Buddhas</s> of great power. // SRS_4.19 //

body.text:
kāyena vācā ca prasanna mānasā buddhāna varṇaṃ bhaṇatī abhīkṣṇam /
tathāhi so bhāvitacittasaṃtatī | rātriṃdivaṃ paśyati lokanāthān // SRS_4.20 //
body.translated_text: With body, speech, and serene mind, he constantly proclaims the praises of the <s>Buddhas</s>; for he, of cultivated mind-stream, day and night sees the Lords of the World. // SRS_4.20 //

children.text: yadāpi so bhoti gilāna āturaḥ pravartate vedana māraṇāntikā /
children.translated_text: Even when he is sick and afflicted, when terminal feelings arise,

children.text: na buddhamārabhya smṛtiḥ pramuṣyate na vedanābhiranusaṃharīyati // SRS_4.21 //
children.translated_text: his mindfulness regarding the <s>Buddha</s> is not lost, nor is he overwhelmed by those feelings. // SRS_4.21 //

children.text: tathā hi tena vicinitva jñātā anāgatā āgata dharmaśūnyatā /
children.translated_text: For thus he has investigated and known the emptiness of <s>dharmas</s> — future and past;

children.text: so tādṛśe dharmanaye pratiṣṭhito na khidyate citta carantu cārikām // SRS_4.22 //
children.translated_text: established in such a <s>dharma</s>-method, his mind does not despair, even while wandering its course. // SRS_4.22 //

children.text: tasmācchruṇitvā imu ānuśaṃsā janetha chandamatulāya bodhaye /
children.translated_text: Therefore, having heard these benefits, generate zeal for incomparable awakening!

children.text: mā paścakāle paritāpu bheṣyata sudurlabhaṃ sugatavarāṇa darśanam // SRS_4.23 //
children.translated_text: Lest you be filled with regret in later times — for the sight of the supreme <s>Sugatas</s> is exceedingly rare. // SRS_4.23 //

children.text: ahaṃ ca bhāṣeya praṇīta dharmaṃ yūyaṃ ca śrutvāna samācarethāḥ /
children.translated_text: I would speak the sublime <s>Dharma</s>, and you, having heard, should practice it;

children.text: bhaiṣajya vastrāṃ ca gṛhītva āturo 'panetu vyādhiṃ na prabhoti ātmanaḥ // SRS_4.24 //
children.translated_text: [for] a sick person who has obtained medicine and bandages but cannot remove his own illness [has not benefited]. // SRS_4.24 //

children.text: tasmādvidhijñena vicakṣaṇena imaṃ samādhiṃ pratikāṅkṣatā sadā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, by one who knows the method, who is discerning, always aspiring to this <s>samādhi</s>,

children.text: śīlaṃ śrutaṃ tyāgu niṣevitavyaṃ na durlabho eṣa samādhi bheṣyati // SRS_4.25 //
children.translated_text: morality, learning, and renunciation should be cultivated — this <s>samādhi</s> will not be hard to obtain.' // SRS_4.25 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje buddhānusmṛtiparivarto nāma caturthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: // Thus [ends] the fourth chapter of the glorious <s>Samādhirāja</s>, entitled 'The Chapter on the Recollection of the <s>Buddha</s>' (<s>Buddhānusmṛtiparivarta</s>). //

body.text:
(Vaidya 23)
5 Ghoṣadattaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 23) Chapter 5: <s>Ghoṣadattaparivarta</s> (The Chapter on <s>Ghoṣadatta</s>). |

body.text:
tatra bhagavāṃścandraprabhaṃ kumārabhūtamāmantrayate sma - bhūtapūrvaṃ kumāra atīte 'dhvanyasaṃkhyeye kalpe asaṃkhyeyatare vipule 'prameye 'cintye 'parimāṇe yadāsīt tena kālena tena samayena bhagavān ghoṣadatto nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loke udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān | tena kālena tena samayena tasya bhagavato ghoṣadattasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya aśītiḥ śrāvakakoṭyaḥ prathamasannipāto 'bhūt sarveṣāmarhatām | dvitīyaḥ śrāvakasannipātaḥ saptatikoṭyo 'rhatāmabhūt | tṛtīyaḥ sannipātaḥ ṣaṣṭiḥ śrāvakakoṭyo 'rhatāmabhūt | tena khalu punaḥ samayena tasya bhagavato ghoṣadattasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya catvāriṃśadvarṣasahasrāṇyāyuḥpramāṇamabhūt | ayaṃ ca jambudvīpa ṛddhaḥ sphītaśca kṣemaśca subhikṣaśca ramaṇīyaśca bahujanākīrṇamanuṣyaścābhūt | tena khalu punaḥ samayena asmin jambudvīpe dvau rājānāvabhūtām | dṛḍhabalaśca nāma mahābalaśca nāma | tatraiko rājā ardhaṃ jambudvīpaṃ paribhuṅkte, dvitīyo 'pyardhaṃ paribhuṅkte ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ramaṇīyaṃ ca bahujanākīrṇamanuṣyaṃ ca || tena kālena tena samayena rājño mahābalasya vijite bhagavān ghoṣadattastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha utpanno 'bhūt | iti hi kumāra rājñā mahābalena sa ghoṣadattastathāgataḥ paripūrṇaṃ varṣasahasraṃ nimantrito 'bhūt sārdhaṃ bodhisattvasaṃghena bhikṣusaṃghena ca kalpikena paribhogeṇānavadyena cīvarapiṇḍapātraśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāreṇa | tena ca kumāra kālena tena samayena tasya bhagavato ghoṣadattasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya bodhisattvasaṃghasya saśrāvakasaṃghasya cotsado lābhasatkāraśloko 'bhūt | śrāddhāśca brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo bhagavato ghoṣadattasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya sabodhisattvasaṃghasya cotsadaṃ lābhasatkāramakārṣuḥ | te ca śrāddhā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo bhagavato ghoṣadattasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya lābhasatkārāyodyuktā abhūvan lokāmiṣapūjāyai yaduta rājña eva ca mahābalasyānuśikṣamāṇarūpam | iti hi
kumāra tasya bhagavato ghoṣadattasya etadabhūt - parihīyante bateme sattvāḥ śīlapoṣadhasamādānatastathāgatānāmupasaṃkramaṇatastathāgataparyupāsanato brahmacaryāvāsataḥ pravrajyopasaṃpannabhikṣubhāvataśca | ta ete sattvāstadanantaraṃ sukhagurukāḥ | tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi tadanantaraṃ sukhamidaṃ yaduta lokāmiṣapūjā | ta ete satvā dṛṣṭadharmagurukāśca saṃparāyagurukāśca nātyantaniṣṭhāḥ kuśalamūlāya | tatreyaṃ kumāra katamā duṣṭadharmagurukatā? yaduta pañcakāmaguṇābhiprāyatā | (Vaidya 24) tatra kumāra katamā sāṃparāyikagurukatā? yaduta svargalokādhyālambanatā | katamā cātyantaniṣṭhakuśalamūlagurukatā? yadutātyantaviśuddhiḥ | atyantavimuktiḥ | atyantayogakṣematā | atyantabrahmacaryāvāsaḥ | atyantaparyavasānam | atyantakuśalamūlaniṣṭhā | atyantaparinirvāṇam | yannavahameteṣāṃ sattvānāṃ tathā tathā dharmaṃ deśayeyaṃ yadamī sattvā yathānuttarayā dharmapūjayā dharmapratipattyā ca tathāgataṃ pūjayeyuḥ ||
body.translated_text: There the Blessed One addressed <s>Candraprabha</s> the prince: 'Once upon a time, O prince, in the past, in an innumerable <s>kalpa</s> — more innumerable still, vast, immeasurable, inconceivable, beyond reckoning — at that time, at that period, a Blessed One named <s>Ghoṣadatta</s> arose in the world as a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, <s>Sugata</s>, Knower of the World, unsurpassed, Charioteer of men to be tamed, Teacher of gods and humans, <s>Buddha</s>, Blessed One. At that time, the first assembly of that Blessed One <s>Ghoṣadatta</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, consisted of eighty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, all <s>Arhats</s>. The second assembly of <s>Śrāvakas</s> consisted of seventy <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Arhats</s>. The third assembly consisted of sixty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Śrāvaka</s> <s>Arhats</s>. At that time, the lifespan of that Blessed One <s>Ghoṣadatta</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, was forty thousand years. And this <s>Jambudvīpa</s> was prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, delightful, and teeming with many people. At that time, in this <s>Jambudvīpa</s> there were two kings — one named <s>Dṛḍhabala</s> (Firm Strength) and one named <s>Mahābala</s> (Great Strength). One king ruled over half of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, and the second also ruled over half — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, delightful, and teeming with many people. At that time, in the realm of King <s>Mahābala</s>, the Blessed One <s>Ghoṣadatta</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, had appeared. Thus, O prince, by King <s>Mahābala</s>, that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ghoṣadatta</s> was invited for a full thousand years, together with the assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and the assembly of monks, with proper and blameless requisites — robes, alms-food, beds, seats, and medicine for the sick. At that time, O prince, the Blessed One <s>Ghoṣadatta</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, together with his assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and <s>Śrāvakas</s>, had abundant gain, honor, and renown. Faithful <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders rendered abundant gain and honor to the Blessed One <s>Ghoṣadatta</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, together with his assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Those faithful <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders were zealous in offering gain and honor to the Blessed One <s>Ghoṣadatta</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, through worldly material worship, following the example of King <s>Mahābala</s> himself. Thus, O prince, this thought arose in the Blessed One <s>Ghoṣadatta</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One: "Alas, these beings are declining in the undertaking of moral precepts and observances, in approaching <s>Tathāgatas</s>, in attending upon <s>Tathāgatas</s>, in dwelling in the holy life, and in the state of monks who have gone forth and received ordination. These beings give priority to immediate pleasure. For what reason? Because this immediate pleasure is worldly material worship. These beings, giving priority to the present life and to future lives, are not ultimately devoted to the root of wholesome merit. What then, O prince, is prioritizing the unwholesome <s>dharma</s>? Namely, inclination toward the five strands of sensual pleasure. (Vaidya 24) And what, O prince, is prioritizing the next life? Namely, fixing one's mind on the world of heaven. And what is prioritizing the ultimate wholesome root? Namely: absolute purity, absolute liberation, absolute security from bondage (<s>yogakṣema</s>), absolute dwelling in the holy life (<s>brahmacaryā</s>), absolute culmination, absolute devotion to wholesome roots, absolute <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. What if I were to teach the <s>Dharma</s> to these beings in such a way that these beings would worship the <s>Tathāgata</s> through the unsurpassed worship of <s>Dharma</s> and through the practice of <s>Dharma</s>!"'

body.text: atha khalu kumāra ghoṣadattastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhastasyāṃ velāyāṃ rājño mahābalasya teṣāṃ ca brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāṃ saṃvejanābhiprāya imā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then, O prince, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ghoṣadatta</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, at that moment spoke these verses with the intention of stirring a sense of urgency in King <s>Mahābala</s> and those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders:

children.text: dānapradānena anyonya sevatāṃ teṣānyamanyasmi na bhoti gauravam /
children.translated_text: "When people serve each other through the giving of gifts, there is no [true] reverence toward one another in that;

children.text: nā tādṛśīṃ sevana varṇayanti buddhā vidū yeṣa prahīṇa vāsanā // SRS_5.1 //
children.translated_text: the Buddhas, the wise ones free from latent tendencies, do not praise such service. // SRS_5.1 //

children.text: te tādṛśā bhonti narāḥ susevitā ye dharma deśenti hitāya prāṇinām /
children.translated_text: "Those are truly well-served who teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the benefit of living beings;

children.text: teṣānyamanyasmi abhedya prema yanmārakoṭībhiraśakyu bhinditum // SRS_5.2 //
children.translated_text: the unbreakable affection between them and one another cannot be split even by <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Māras</s>. // SRS_5.2 //

children.text: lokāmiṣeṇo nara sevatāṃ nṛṇāṃ sarveṣaṃ sāṃdṛṣṭika bhoti arthaḥ /
children.translated_text: "When men serve one another with worldly bait, the benefit for all of them is merely visible [in this life];

children.text: nirāmiṣaṃ dharma niṣevatāṃ hi mahānta artho bhavatī narāṇām // SRS_5.3 //
children.translated_text: but for those who serve the <s>Dharma</s> without material bait, the benefit for men becomes great. // SRS_5.3 //

children.text: nirāmiṣaṃ cittu upasthapitvā nirāmiṣaṃ dharma prakāśayitvā /
children.translated_text: "Having established the mind without material bait, having proclaimed the <s>Dharma</s> without material bait —

children.text: nirāmiṣaṃ yeṣa bhaveta prema te tādṛśāḥ kṣipra bhavanti buddhāḥ // SRS_5.4 //
children.translated_text: those whose affection is without material bait, such ones quickly become <s>Buddhas</s>. // SRS_5.4 //

children.text: na jātu kāmān pratisevamānaḥ putreṣu dāreṣu janitva tṛṣṇām /
children.translated_text: "Never will one who indulges in sense-pleasures, having generated craving for sons and wives,

children.text: gṛhaṃ ca sevantu jugupsanīyamanuttarāṃ prāpsyati so 'grabodhim // SRS_5.5 //
children.translated_text: while resorting to the loathsome household life, attain the unsurpassed, supreme awakening. // SRS_5.5 //

children.text: ye kāma varjenti yathāgnikarṣūṃ putreṣu dāreṣu jahitva tṛṣṇām /
children.translated_text: "Those who abandon sense-pleasures as [one avoids] a pit of fire, having forsaken craving for sons and wives,

children.text: (Vaidya 25)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 25)

children.text: uttrastu gehādabhiniṣkramanti na durlabhā teṣviyamagrabodhiḥ // SRS_5.6 //
children.translated_text: who, alarmed, go forth from the household — for them this supreme awakening is not hard to obtain. // SRS_5.6 //

children.text: na kaści buddhaḥ purimeṇa āsī anāgate bheṣyati vāvatiṣṭhate /
children.translated_text: "There was no <s>Buddha</s> in the past, nor will there be in the future, nor does one exist at present,

children.text: yehi sthitairevamagāramadhye prāptā iyamuttama agrabodhiḥ // SRS_5.7 //
children.translated_text: who, while remaining in the household life, attained this unsurpassed, supreme awakening. // SRS_5.7 //

children.text: prahāya rājyaṃ yatha kheṭapiṇḍaṃ vaseta raṇyeṣu vivekakāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Having abandoned the kingdom like a lump of spit, one should dwell in the forests, longing for solitude;

children.text: kleśān prahāya pratihatya māraṃ buddhyanti bodhiṃ virajāmasaṃskṛtām // SRS_5.8 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned the <s>kleśas</s> and defeated <s>Māra</s>, they awaken to the dustless, unconditioned awakening. // SRS_5.8 //

children.text: yo buddhavīrān yatha gaṅgavālukā upasthiheyyā bahukalpakoṭiyaḥ /
children.translated_text: "One who would attend upon heroic <s>Buddhas</s> as numerous as the sands of the Ganges for many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> —

children.text: yaśco gṛhātaḥ parikhinnamānaso 'bhiniṣkrameyyā ayu tatra uttamaḥ // SRS_5.9 //
children.translated_text: yet he who, with a weary mind, goes forth from the household — his [merit] is superior to that. // SRS_5.9 //

children.text: annehi pānehi ca cīvarehi puṣpehi gandhehi vilepanehi /
children.translated_text: "With food, drink, robes, flowers, incense, and ointments —

children.text: nopasthitā bhonti narottamā jinā yatha pravrajitvā cariyāṇa dharmam // SRS_5.10 //
children.translated_text: the supreme ones, the <s>Jinas</s>, are not so well served as by going forth and practicing the <s>Dharma</s>. // SRS_5.10 //

children.text: yaścaiva bodhiṃ pratikāṅkṣamāṇaḥ sattvārtha nirviṇṇu kusaṃskṛtātaḥ /
children.translated_text: "And one who, aspiring to awakening, disgusted with the ill-composed [conditioned existence], for the benefit of beings,

children.text: raṇyāmukhaḥ sapta padāni prakrame ayaṃ tataḥ puṇyaviśiṣṭa bhoti // SRS_5.11 //
children.translated_text: takes seven steps facing the forest — this one becomes more distinguished in merit than that [other]. // SRS_5.11 //

body.text:
aśrauṣīt khalu punaḥ kumāra rājā mahābalo bhagavatā ghoṣadattena tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena imāmevaṃrūpāṃ pravartitāṃ naiṣkramyapratisaṃyuktāṃ kathām | śrutvā ca vimṛśati - yathāhaṃ bhagavato bhāṣitasyārthamājānāmi, na bhagavān dānapāramitāṃ varṇayati, na śīlapāramitāṃ varṇayati | atyantaniṣṭhāṃ saṃvarṇayati | atyantaviśuddhim | atyantabrahmacaryāvāsam | atyantanirvāṇaṃ saṃvarṇayati | tasyaitadabhūt - nedaṃ sukaramagāramadhyāvasatā anuttaradharmapratipattiṃ saṃpādayitum, arthaṃ vā anuprāptum | parihīṇo 'smyanuttarāyā dharmapratipattitaḥ | yannvahaṃ keśaśmaśrūṇyavatārya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇi paridhāya samyageva śraddhayā agārādanagārikāṃ pravrajeyam | iti hi (Vaidya 26) kumāra rājā mahābalaḥ sārdhamaśītyā brāhmaṇagṛhapatiśatasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto yena bhagavān ghoṣadatto nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhastenopasaṃkrāmat | upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya ekānte 'sthāt | atha khalu kumāra bhagavān ghoṣadatto rājño mahābalasya adhyāśayaṃ viditvā imaṃ sarvadharmasvabhāvasamatāvipañcitaṃ samādhiṃ deśayate | atha khalu kumāra rājā mahābala imaṃ samādhiṃ śrutvā tuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ keśaśmaśraṇyavatārya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇi paridhāya samyageva śraddhayā agārādanagārikāṃ pravrajito 'bhūt | sa tathā pravrajitaḥ sannimaṃ samādhimudgṛhītavān | udgṛhya paryavāpya dhārayitvā vācayiotvā bhāvanāyogamanuyukto vyahārṣīt | sa tenaiva kuśalamūlena daśakalpakoṭyo na jātu durgativinipātamagamat, viṃśatiṃ ca buddhakoṭīrārāgayāmāsa | teṣāṃ ca tathāgatānāmantikādimaṃ samādhimaśrauṣīt | śrutvā tebhyo buddhebhyastenodgṛhītaḥ paryavāpto dhārito vācito bhāvanāyogamanuyukto vyahārṣīt | sa tataḥ paścāt tenaiva kuśalamūlena daśānāṃ kalpakoṭīnāmatyayena paripūrṇena kalpaśatasahasreṇa anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddho 'bhūt | so 'prameyāṇāṃ sattvānāmarthaṃ kṛtvā paścād buddhaparinirvāṇena parinirvṛto 'bhūt | tatra kumāra yānyaśītiprāṇiśatasahasrāṇi rājñā mahābalena sārdhaṃ bhagavantaṃ ghoṣadattaṃ tathāgatamupasaṃkrāntāni, te 'pi sarve imaṃ samādhiṃ
śrutvā tuṣṭā udagrā āttamanasaḥ pramuditāḥ
prītisaumanasyajātāḥ keśaśmaśrūṇyavatārya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇi paridhāya samyageva śraddhayā agārādanagārikāṃ pravrajitā abhūvan | te 'pi tathā pravrajitā imaṃ samādhimudgṛhya paryavāpya dhārayitvā vācayitvā bhāvanāyogamanuyuktā vihṛtya tenaiva kuśalamūlena viṃśatikalpakoṭyo na jātu durgativinipātamagaman | sarvatra ca kalpe kalpe buddhakoṭīrbuddhakoṭīrārāgayāmāsa | sarveṣāṃ ca teṣāṃ tathāgatānāmantike imaṃ samādhiṃ śrutvodgṛhya paryavāpya dhārayitvā vācayitvā bhāvanāyogamanuyuktā vihṛtya tenaiva pūrvakreṇa kuśalamūlena viṃśatīnāṃ kalpakoṭīnāmatyayena tataḥ paścāt paripūrṇadaśabhiḥ kalpasahasrairanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhā dṛḍhaśūranāmānastathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā loke utpannā abhuvan | te 'pyaprameyānasaṃkhyeyān sattvān paripācya teṣāṃ cārthaṃ kṛtvā buddhaparinirvṛtā abhūvan | tadanenāpi te kumāra paryāyeṇa evaṃ veditavyaṃ yathāyaṃ samādhirbahukaro bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmanuttarasya sarvajñajñānasyāharaṇāya saṃvartata iti || atha khalu bhagavāṃścandraprabhasya kumārabhūtasya tasyāṃ velāyāmetadeva pūrvayogaparivartaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā gāthābhigītena vistareṇa saṃprakāśayati sma -
body.translated_text: Then, O prince, King <s>Mahābala</s> heard this very discourse connected with renunciation, spoken by the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ghoṣadatta</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One. Having heard it, he reflected: "As I understand the meaning of the Blessed One's words, the Blessed One does not praise the perfection of generosity, nor does he praise the perfection of morality. He praises the ultimate goal — ultimate purity, the ultimate dwelling in the holy life, ultimate <s>nirvāṇa</s>." This thought arose in him: "It is not easy for one dwelling in a household to accomplish the practice of the unsurpassed <s>Dharma</s> or to attain its meaning. I am deprived of the unsurpassed <s>Dharma</s>-practice! Let me shave off my hair and beard, put on the saffron robes, and with proper faith go forth from the household to homelessness." Thus, O (Vaidya 26) prince, King <s>Mahābala</s>, surrounded and attended by eighty hundred-thousands of <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders, approached the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ghoṣadatta</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One. Having approached, he bowed his head at the Blessed One's feet, circumambulated him three times, and stood to one side. Then, O prince, the Blessed One <s>Ghoṣadatta</s>, knowing King <s>Mahābala</s>'s disposition, taught this <s>samādhi</s> — the Elaboration on the Equality of the Inherent Nature of All <s>Dharmas</s>. Then, O prince, King <s>Mahābala</s>, having heard this <s>samādhi</s>, pleased and elated and delighted, shaved off his hair and beard, put on the saffron robes, and with proper faith went forth from the household to homelessness. Having thus gone forth, he took up this <s>samādhi</s>. Having taken it up, mastered it, retained it, recited it, and devoted himself to the practice of meditation, he flourished. By that very root of merit, for ten <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> he never fell into an evil destiny or lower realm, and he pleased twenty <s>koṭis</s> of Buddhas. In the presence of those <s>Tathāgatas</s> he heard this <s>samādhi</s>. Having heard it, he took it up from those Buddhas, mastered it, retained it, recited it, and devoted himself to the practice of meditation. Thereafter, by that very root of merit, after the passage of ten <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> and a full hundred thousand <s>kalpas</s>, he fully awakened to the unsurpassed, perfect awakening. Having accomplished the welfare of immeasurable beings, he afterward passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. And, O prince, those eighty hundred-thousands of living beings who had approached the Blessed One <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ghoṣadatta</s> together with King <s>Mahābala</s> — they too, having heard this <s>samādhi</s>, pleased and elated and delighted, filled with joy and gladness, shaved off their hair and beards, put on the saffron robes, and with proper faith went forth from the household to homelessness. Having thus gone forth, they took up this <s>samādhi</s>, mastered it, retained it, recited it, and devoted themselves to the practice of meditation. By that very root of merit, for twenty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> they never fell into an evil destiny or lower realm. And in every <s>kalpa</s> they pleased <s>koṭis</s> upon <s>koṭis</s> of Buddhas. In the presence of all those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, having heard this <s>samādhi</s>, taken it up, mastered it, retained it, recited it, and devoted themselves to the practice of meditation, by that same former root of merit, after the passage of twenty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> and thereafter a full ten thousand <s>kalpas</s>, they fully awakened to the unsurpassed, perfect awakening — <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones arose in the world bearing the name <s>Dṛḍhaśūra</s> ("Firm Hero"). They too, having ripened immeasurable and incalculable beings and accomplished their welfare, passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. By this account too, O prince, it should be understood that this <s>samādhi</s> is of great service to <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, conducing to the attainment of unsurpassed omniscient knowledge." || Then the Blessed One, at that time, illuminated this very chapter on former connections (<s>pūrvayogaparivarta</s>) to <s>Candraprabha</s> the prince in still greater detail through verses:

children.text: smarāmyahaṃ pūrvamatītamadhvani acintiye kalpi narāṇa uttamaḥ /
children.translated_text: "I remember, in the past, on the bygone path, in an inconceivable <s>kalpa</s>, a supreme one among men —

children.text: (Vaidya 27)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 27)

children.text: utpannu lokārthakaro maharṣi nāmena so ucyati ghoṣadattaḥ // SRS_5.12 //
children.translated_text: a great <s>Ṛṣi</s> arose for the benefit of the world, called by the name <s>Ghoṣadatta</s>. // SRS_5.12 //

children.text: aśīti koṭyaḥ paripūrṇa tasya prathamo gaṇo āsi ya śrāvakāṇām /
children.translated_text: "His first assembly of <s>Śrāvakas</s> was a full eighty <s>koṭis</s>;

children.text: dvitīya cāsīt paripūrṇa saptatistṛtīya co ṣaṣṭyarahantakoṭiyaḥ // SRS_5.13 //
children.translated_text: the second was a full seventy, and the third was sixty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Arhats</s>. // SRS_5.13 //

children.text: sarve ca kṣīṇāsrava niṣkileśāḥ sarve ca ṛddhībalapāramiṃ gatāḥ /
children.translated_text: "All had destroyed their <s>āsravas</s> (defilements), all were free from <s>kleśas</s>, all had reached the perfection of <s>ṛddhi</s>-power;

children.text: varṣaṃ sahasrā duvi viśaṃ cāyuḥ kṣetraṃ ca āsīt pariśuddha śobhanam // SRS_5.14 //
children.translated_text: their lifespan was twenty-two thousand years, and the field was pure and beautiful. // SRS_5.14 //

children.text: abhiṣekaprāptā parahita aprameyā vaśitehi bhūmihi ca supratiṣṭhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Immeasurable [<s>Bodhisattvas</s>], having received consecration, devoted to the welfare of others, well-established on the stages and in the sovereign powers —

children.text: āsanna te drumavari bodhi bodhituṃ ye bodhisatvāsta abhūṣi tāyinaḥ // SRS_5.15 //
children.translated_text: those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who were near the excellent tree of awakening, ready to awaken — they were the Protectors. // SRS_5.15 //

children.text: iha jambudvīpasmi abhūṣi rājā dṛḍhabalo nāma mahābalaśca /
children.translated_text: "Here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> there was a king named <s>Dṛḍhabala</s> (Firm-Strength) and <s>Mahābala</s> (Great-Strength);

children.text: upārdhu rājyasya tadeku bhuñjate dvitīya cādhasya abhūṣi rājā // SRS_5.16 //
children.translated_text: one enjoyed the upper half of the kingdom, and the other was king of the lower [half]. // SRS_5.16 //

children.text: mahābalasyo vijitasmi buddho utpanna so devamanuṣyapūjitaḥ /
children.translated_text: "In <s>Mahābala</s>'s domain the <s>Buddha</s> arose, honored by gods and men;

children.text: labhitva rājā sugatasmi śraddhām upasthihī varṣasahasra pūrṇam // SRS_5.17 //
children.translated_text: the king, having gained faith in the <s>Sugata</s>, served him for a full thousand years. // SRS_5.17 //

children.text: tasyānuśikṣī bahu anyasattvāḥ kurvanti satkāra tathāgatasya /
children.translated_text: "Following his example, many other beings also made offerings to the <s>Tathāgata</s>;

children.text: lokāmiṣeṇaiva hi dharmapūjayā saśrāvakasya atulo 'bhū utsadaḥ // SRS_5.18 //
children.translated_text: with worldly bait indeed, as <s>Dharma</s>-worship — together with his <s>Śrāvakas</s>, incomparable was the increase. // SRS_5.18 //

children.text: abhūṣi cittaṃ puruṣottamasya deśiṣya dharmamimi dharmakāmāḥ /
children.translated_text: "The thought arose in the Supreme Person: 'I shall teach the <s>Dharma</s> — these are lovers of <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: yannūna sarve prajahitva kāmāniha pravrajeyurmama śāsanasmin // SRS_5.19 //
children.translated_text: would that all of them, abandoning sense-pleasures, go forth in my teaching!' // SRS_5.19 //

children.text: (Vaidya 28)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 28)

children.text: sa bhāṣate gātha narāṇamuttamaḥ saṃlekhidharmaṃ sugatāna śikṣām /
children.translated_text: "The Supreme among Men spoke verses — the austere <s>Dharma</s>, the training of the <s>Sugatas</s>,

children.text: gṛhavāsadoṣāṃśca anantaduḥkhān pratipatti dharmeṣviha dharmapūjā // SRS_5.20 //
children.translated_text: the faults of household life and its endless sufferings — practice of the <s>Dharma</s> here is true <s>Dharma</s>-worship. // SRS_5.20 //

children.text: śruṇitva gāthāṃ tada rājapārthivo eko vicinteti rahogato nṛpaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Having heard the verses, the sovereign king reflected alone in solitude:

children.text: na śakya gehasmi sthihitva sarve pratipadyitumuttadharmapūjā // SRS_5.21 //
children.translated_text: 'It is not possible, while remaining in a household, to accomplish the supreme <s>Dharma</s>-worship in its entirety.' // SRS_5.21 //

children.text: sa rājya tyaktvā yatha kheṭapiṇḍaṃ prāṇisahasrebhiraśītibhiḥ saha /
children.translated_text: "Having abandoned the kingdom like a lump of spit, together with eighty thousands of beings,

children.text: upasaṃkramī tasya jinasya antikaṃ vanditva pādau purataḥ sthito 'bhūt // SRS_5.22 //
children.translated_text: he approached that <s>Jina</s>, bowed at his feet, and stood before him. // SRS_5.22 //

children.text: teṣāṃ jino āśayu jānamāno deśetimaṃ śānta samādhi durdṛśam /
children.translated_text: "The <s>Jina</s>, knowing their dispositions, taught this peaceful, hard-to-see <s>samādhi</s>;

children.text: te prītiprāmodyasukhena prīṇitāstuṣṭā udagrāstada pravrajiṃsu // SRS_5.23 //
children.translated_text: filled with the happiness of joy and gladness, pleased and elated, they then went forth. // SRS_5.23 //

children.text: te pravrajitvāna imaṃ samādhiṃ dhāritva vācitva paryāpuṇitva /
children.translated_text: "Having gone forth, they retained, recited, and mastered this <s>samādhi</s>;

children.text: na jātu gacche vinipātadurgatiṃ kalpāna koṭyaḥ paripūrṇa viṃśatim // SRS_5.24 //
children.translated_text: they never went to an evil destiny or lower realm for a full twenty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>. // SRS_5.24 //

children.text: te tena sarve kuśalena karmaṇā adrākṣu buddhāna sahasrakoṭiyaḥ /
children.translated_text: "By that wholesome deed, they all beheld thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of Buddhas;

children.text: sarveṣu co teṣu jinānuśāsane te pravrajitvemu samādhi bhāvayī // SRS_5.25 //
children.translated_text: and in the teaching of all those <s>Jinas</s>, having gone forth, they cultivated this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_5.25 //

children.text: te paścime kāli abhūṣi buddhā dṛḍhaśūranāmāna anantavīryāḥ /
children.translated_text: "In the final time, they became Buddhas bearing the name <s>Dṛḍhaśūra</s> (Firm Hero), of infinite vigor;

children.text: kṛtvā ca arthaṃ bahuprāṇikoṭināṃ te paścikālesmi śikhīva nirvṛtāḥ // SRS_5.26 //
children.translated_text: having accomplished the welfare of many <s>koṭis</s> of living beings, they were extinguished in the final time like a flame. // SRS_5.26 //

children.text: (Vaidya 29)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 29)

children.text: mahābalo rājā ya āsi pūrvaṃ sa jñānaśūro abhu buddha loke /
children.translated_text: "King <s>Mahābala</s> who existed formerly — he became the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Jñānaśūra</s> (Wisdom-Hero) in the world;

children.text: tadā bahu prāṇisahasrakoṭiyaḥ sthapetva bodhāya sa paści nirvṛtaḥ // SRS_5.27 //
children.translated_text: having then established many thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of beings in awakening, he was afterward extinguished. // SRS_5.27 //

children.text: tasmācchruṇitvā imu paścikāle dhāreya sūtramimu buddhavarṇitam /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, having heard this in the final time, retain this <s>sūtra</s> praised by the <s>Buddha</s>;

children.text: dhāretvimamīdṛśa dharmakoṣaṃ bhaviṣyathā kṣipra narāṇamuttamāḥ // SRS_5.28 //
children.translated_text: having retained such a treasury of <s>Dharma</s>, you shall quickly become supreme among men! // SRS_5.28 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje ghoṣadattaparivarto nāma pañcamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, called the <s>Ghoṣadattaparivarta</s> (Chapter on <s>Ghoṣadatta</s>). ||

body.text:
(Vaidya 30)
6 Samādhiparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 30) Chapter 6: <s>Samādhiparivarta</s> (The Chapter on <s>Samādhi</s>). |

body.text: tatra bhagavān punarapi candraprabhaṃ kumārabhūtamāmantrayate sma - tasmāttarhi kumāra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena imaṃ samādhimākāṅkṣatā kṣipraṃ cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhukāmena samādhiparikarma karaṇīyam | tatra kumāra katamat samādhiparikarma? iha kumāra bodhisattvo mahākaruṇāsaṃprasthitena cittena tiṣṭhatāṃ vā tathāgatānāṃ parinirvṛtānāṃ vā pūjākarmaṇe udyukto bhavati, yaduta cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākābhistūryatālāvacarairvaijayantībhiḥ tacca kuśalamūlaṃ samādhipratilambhāya pariṇamayati | sa na kaṃciddharmamākāṅkṣaṃstathāgataṃ pūjayati na rūpaṃ na kāmān na bhogān na svargān na parivārān | api tu khalu punardharmacittako bhavati | sa ākāṅkṣan dharmakāyato 'pi tathāgataṃ nopalabhate, kimaṅga punā rūpakāyata upalapsyate | tasmāttarhi kumāra eṣāṃ sā tathāgatānā pūjā yaduta tathāgatasyādarśanamātmanaścānupalabdhiḥ karmavipākasya cāpratikāṅkṣamāṇatā | anayā kumāra trimaṇḍalapariśuddhayā pūjayā tathāgataṃ pūjayitvā bodhisattvo mahāsattva imaṃ samādhiṃ pratilabhate kṣipraṃ cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate ||
body.translated_text: There the Blessed One again addressed <s>Candraprabha</s>, the prince: 'Therefore, O Prince, the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> who desires this <s>samādhi</s> and who wishes to swiftly, fully awaken to the supreme, perfect <s>saṃbodhi</s> (enlightenment) should undertake the preparatory practice of <s>samādhi</s>. And what, O Prince, is the preparatory practice of <s>samādhi</s>? Here, O Prince, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with a mind established in great compassion, is devoted to the worship of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, whether they abide or have passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — namely with robes, alms-food, bedding, medicines for the sick and requisites, with flowers, incense, fragrance, garlands, unguents, powders, garments, parasols, banners, pennants, and musical instruments and cymbals and victory-banners — and he dedicates that wholesome root toward the attainment of <s>samādhi</s>. He worships the <s>Tathāgata</s> not desiring any <s>dharma</s> — not form, not sensual pleasures, not enjoyments, not heavens, not retinue. Rather, he becomes one whose mind is set on the <s>dharma</s>. He who seeks [thus] does not apprehend the <s>Tathāgata</s> even from the <s>Dharmakāya</s> — how much less would he apprehend [him] from the form-body? Therefore, O Prince, this is the worship of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>: namely, the non-seeing of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the non-apprehension of self, and the non-expectation of the ripening of <s>karma</s>. With this worship purified in the triple sphere, O Prince, having worshipped the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> attains this <s>samādhi</s> and swiftly, fully awakens to the supreme, perfect <s>saṃbodhi</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāṃ candraprabhasya kumārabhūtasya etadeva samādhiparikarmanirdeśaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā gāthābhigītena vistareṇa saṃprakāśamati sma -
body.translated_text: Then at that time the Blessed One further illuminated for <s>Candraprabha</s>, the prince, this very instruction on the preparatory practice of <s>samādhi</s>, in greater detail, with verses in song:

children.text: anantajñānasya daditva gandhān anantagandho bhavatī narāṇām /
children.translated_text: 'Having given fragrances to the one of infinite knowledge, one becomes of infinite fragrance among humans;

children.text: na kalpakoṭīya vrajanti durgatiṃ durgandhiyaṃ teṣu na jātu bhoti // SRS_6.1 //
children.translated_text: they do not go to a lower rebirth for <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, and foul odor never arises among them. // SRS_6.1 //

children.text: te kalpakoṭyaścaramāṇu cārikāṃ pūjitva buddhāna sahasrakoṭiyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s> they practice the conduct, having worshipped thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>;

children.text: te jñānagandhena samudgatena bhavanti buddhā varaśīlagandhikāḥ // SRS_6.2 //
children.translated_text: through the fragrance of knowledge that has arisen, they become <s>Buddhas</s>, fragrant with supreme virtue. // SRS_6.2 //

children.text: sacet punarjānati vāsti sattvo yo gandha detī tatha yasya dīyate /
children.translated_text: 'If moreover he knows: "There is a being who gives fragrance, and one to whom it is given" —

children.text: etena cittena dadāti gandhameṣāsya kṣāntirmṛdu ānulomikī // SRS_6.3 //
children.translated_text: with this mind he gives fragrance — [yet] this is his gentle, conforming patience. // SRS_6.3 //

children.text: (Vaidya 31)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 31)

children.text: tasyaitaṃ kṣāntimadhimātra sevataḥ sacennaraḥ kākaṇicchedyu chidyate /
children.translated_text: 'Cultivating this patience to the utmost, even if the man be cut to bits,

children.text: kalpāna koṭyo yatha gaṅgavālikā na tasya cittaṃ bhavati vivartiyam // SRS_6.4 //
children.translated_text: for <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s> like the sands of the Ganges, his mind does not become retrogressive. // SRS_6.4 //

children.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ vucyati kṣānti nāma kathaṃ puno vucyati ānulomikī /
children.translated_text: 'For what reason is it called "patience"? And how moreover is it called "conforming"?

children.text: avivartiko vucyati kena hetunā kathaṃ puno vucyati bodhisattvaḥ // SRS_6.5 //
children.translated_text: For what cause is one called "non-retrogressive"? And how moreover is one called a "<s>Bodhisattva</s>"? // SRS_6.5 //

children.text: kṣāntyasmi dharme prakṛtau nirātmake nairātmyasaṃjñasya kileśu nāsti /
children.translated_text: '"I am patient with this <s>dharma</s> that is by nature selfless" — for one with the perception of selflessness, indeed there are no [afflictions];

children.text: khaṃ yādṛśaṃ jānati sarvadharmāstasmādiha syā kva tu kṣānti nāma // SRS_6.6 //
children.translated_text: he knows all <s>dharmas</s> to be like space — therefore, where here could there be anything called "patience"? // SRS_6.6 //

children.text: ānulomi sarveṣa jināna śikṣato na cāsti dharmaścarate vicakṣaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Conforming to the training of all the <s>Jinas</s>, the discerning one practices though there is no <s>dharma</s> [to practice];

children.text: na buddhadharmeṣu janeti saṃśayāniyaṃ sa kṣāntirbhavatānulomikī // SRS_6.7 //
children.translated_text: he does not generate doubt regarding the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> — this is the patience called "conforming". // SRS_6.7 //

children.text: evaṃ carantasya ya loki mārāste buddharūpeṇa bhaṇeyya vācā /
children.translated_text: 'For one thus practicing in the world, the <s>Māras</s> would speak to him in the guise of a <s>Buddha</s>:

children.text: sudurlabhā bodhi bhavāhi śrāvakā na gṛhṇotī vākyu na co vivartate // SRS_6.8 //
children.translated_text: "<s>Bodhi</s> is hard to obtain — become a <s>Śrāvaka</s>!" He neither grasps that word nor turns back. // SRS_6.8 //

children.text: bodheti sattvān viṣamātu dṛṣṭito na eṣa mārgo amṛtasya prāptaye /
children.translated_text: 'He awakens beings from wrong views: "This is not the path for attaining the deathless!"

children.text: kumārga varṇitva pathe sthapeti taṃ kāraṇamucyati bodhisattvaḥ // SRS_6.9 //
children.translated_text: Having described the wrong path, he establishes them on the [right] path — for this reason he is called a "<s>Bodhisattva</s>". // SRS_6.9 //

children.text: kṣamiṣyanūlomapathe sthitasya nairātmyasaṅgāya vibodhitasya /
children.translated_text: 'For one established on the patient, conforming path, awakened to non-attachment to selflessness —

children.text: svapnāntare 'pyasya na jātu bhoti asti naro pudgala jīva sattvaḥ // SRS_6.10 //
children.translated_text: even in a dream there never arises for him [the notion]: "There is a man, a person, a being, a creature." // SRS_6.10 //

children.text: (Vaidya 32)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 32)

children.text: sace mārakoṭyo yatha gaṅgavālukāste buddharūpeṇa upāgamitvā /
children.translated_text: 'If <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Māras</s>, like the sands of the Ganges, were to approach him in the guise of <s>Buddhas</s>

children.text: bhaṇeyurabhyantarakāyu jīvo te maṃ vade nāsti na yūya buddhā // SRS_6.11 //
children.translated_text: and say: "There is an inner body, a being" — let them tell me "there is not" — you are not <s>Buddhas</s>! // SRS_6.11 //

children.text: jñānena jānāmyahu skandhaśūnyakaṃ jñātvā ca kleśehi na saṃvasāmi /
children.translated_text: '"Through knowledge I know the aggregates to be empty; and knowing, I do not dwell with afflictions;

children.text: vyāhāramātreṇa ca vyoharāmi parinirvṛto lokamimaṃ carāmi // SRS_6.12 //
children.translated_text: I speak merely through conventional expression; I have attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, yet I move through this world." // SRS_6.12 //

children.text: yathā hi putra puruṣasya jātu kṛtaṃsi nāmā ayameva nāma /
children.translated_text: 'Just as when a son is born to a man, a name is given: "This one is such-and-such by name" —

children.text: nāmaṃ na tasyo diśatā sulabhyate tathāsya nāmaṃ na kutaścidāgatam // SRS_6.13 //
children.translated_text: yet that name cannot be found in any direction — so too his name has not come from anywhere. // SRS_6.13 //

children.text: tathaiva nāmaṃ kṛtu bodhisattvo na cāsya nāmaṃ diśatā sulabhyate /
children.translated_text: 'Likewise, the name "<s>Bodhisattva</s>" is created, yet that name cannot be found in any direction;

children.text: paryeṣamāṇo ayu bodhisattvo jānāti yo eṣa sa bodhisattvaḥ // SRS_6.14 //
children.translated_text: one who, seeking, [understands] this "<s>Bodhisattva</s>" — he who knows this is a [true] <s>Bodhisattva</s>. // SRS_6.14 //

children.text: samudramadhye 'pi jvaleta agni rna bodhisattvasya satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Even if fire were to blaze in the midst of the ocean, still there is no <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the composite self) for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>;

children.text: yato 'sya bodhāya utpannu cittamatrāntare tasya na jīvadṛṣṭiḥ // SRS_6.15 //
children.translated_text: from the moment his mind is aroused toward <s>bodhi</s>, from that very instant there is no belief in a self for him. // SRS_6.15 //

children.text: na hyatra jāto na mṛto ca kaścidutpanna sattvo manujo naro vā /
children.translated_text: 'For here no one is born, nor does anyone die; no being, human, or person has arisen;

children.text: māyopamā dharma svabhāvaśūnyā na śakyate jānitu tīrthikehi // SRS_6.16 //
children.translated_text: <s>dharmas</s> are like an illusion, empty of inherent nature — they cannot be understood by <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers). // SRS_6.16 //

children.text: na cāpi āhāravimūrchitehi lubdhehi gṛddhehi ca pātracīvare /
children.translated_text: 'Nor by those intoxicated with food, nor by the greedy, nor by those covetous of alms-bowl and robes;

children.text: na coddhatehi napi connatehi śakyā iyaṃ jānitu buddhabodhiḥ // SRS_6.17 //
children.translated_text: nor by the agitated, nor by the conceited — this <s>Buddha-bodhi</s> cannot be known [by them]. // SRS_6.17 //

children.text: (Vaidya 33)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 33)

children.text: na styānamiddhābhihataiḥ kusīdaiḥ stabdhehi mānīhi anātrapehi /
children.translated_text: 'Not by those afflicted with sloth and torpor, the lazy, the rigid, the proud, the shameless;

children.text: yeṣāṃ na buddhasmi prasādu asti na śakyate hī varabodhi jānitum // SRS_6.18 //
children.translated_text: those who have no faith in the <s>Buddha</s> — the supreme <s>bodhi</s> indeed cannot be known [by them]. // SRS_6.18 //

children.text: na bhinnavṛttehi pṛthagjanehi yeṣāṃ na dharmasmi prasādu asti /
children.translated_text: 'Not by those ordinary beings whose conduct is broken, who have no faith in the <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: sabrahmacārīṣu ca nāsti gauravaṃ na śakyate hī varabodhi buddhitum // SRS_6.19 //
children.translated_text: and who have no respect for fellow practitioners of the holy life — the supreme <s>bodhi</s> indeed cannot be understood [by them]. // SRS_6.19 //

children.text: abhinnavṛttā hirimanta lajjino yeṣāṃ sti buddhe api dharme prema /
children.translated_text: 'Those whose conduct is unbroken, who possess shame and moral dread, who have love for both the <s>Buddha</s> and the <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: sabrahmacārīṣu ca tīvragauravaṃ te prāpuṇantī varabodhimuttamām // SRS_6.20 //
children.translated_text: and intense respect for fellow practitioners of the holy life — they attain the supreme, excellent <s>bodhi</s>. // SRS_6.20 //

children.text: smṛterupasthāna iha yeṣa gocaraḥ prāmodya prīti śayanamupastṛtam /
children.translated_text: 'Those whose domain is the foundations of mindfulness, whose bed is spread with joy and delight,

children.text: dhyānāni cāhāru samādhi pāniyaṃ budhyanti te 'pi varabodhimuttamām // SRS_6.21 //
children.translated_text: whose food is the <s>dhyānas</s> and whose drink is <s>samādhi</s> — they too awaken to the supreme, excellent <s>bodhi</s>. // SRS_6.21 //

children.text: nairātmyasaṃjñā ca divāvihāro anusmṛtiścaṃkramaśūnyabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The perception of selflessness is their daytime abiding; mindfulness, walking meditation, and the contemplation of emptiness [are theirs];

children.text: bodhyaṅgapuṣpā surabhī manoramā te yujyamānā varabodhi prāpayī // SRS_6.22 //
children.translated_text: the fragrant, delightful flowers of the factors of awakening — those engaged [in these] attain the supreme <s>bodhi</s>. // SRS_6.22 //

children.text: yā bodhisattvāna carī vidūnāmabhūmiranyasya janasya tatra /
children.translated_text: 'That which is the conduct of wise <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is beyond the reach of other beings there —

children.text: pratyekabuddhāna ca śrāvakāṇa ca ko vātra vijño na janeya chandam // SRS_6.23 //
children.translated_text: of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> and <s>Śrāvakas</s> — what wise person would not generate the aspiration [for it]? // SRS_6.23 //

children.text: sacenmamā āyu bhaveta ettakaṃ kalpāna koṭyo yatha gaṅgavālukāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'If my lifespan were to be this long — <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s> like the sands of the Ganges —

children.text: ekasya romasya bhaṇeya varṇaṃ bauddhena jñānena paryantu nāsti // SRS_6.24 //
children.translated_text: and I were to describe the qualities of a single hair-pore, through <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge there would be no end. // SRS_6.24 //

children.text: (Vaidya 34)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 34)

children.text: tasmācchuṇitvā imu ānuśaṃsāmanābhibhūtena jinena deśitām /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, having heard these benefits taught by the <s>Jina</s>, the unconquered one,

children.text: imaṃ samādhiṃ laghu uddiśeyā na durlabhā bheṣyati agrabodhiḥ // SRS_6.25 //
children.translated_text: one should quickly teach this <s>samādhi</s> — the supreme <s>bodhi</s> will not be hard to obtain.' // SRS_6.25 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje samādhiparivarto nāma ṣaṣṭhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth chapter in the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, called the chapter on <s>Samādhi</s> (<s>Samādhiparivarta</s>).

body.text:
(Vaidya 35)
7 Trikṣāntyavatāraparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 35) Chapter 7: The <s>Trikṣāntyavatāraparivarta</s> (Chapter on Entry into the Three Patiences).

body.text: tatra bhagavān punarapi candraprabhaṃ kumārabhūtamāmantrayate sma - tasmātarhi kumāra bodhisattvena mahāsattvenemaṃ samādhimākāṅkṣatā kṣipraṃ cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhukāmena trikṣāntijñānakuśalena bhavitavyam | tena prathamā kṣāntiḥ prajñātavyā | dvitīyā kṣāntiḥ prajñātavyā | tṛtīyā kṣāntiḥ prajñātavyā | trikṣāntiviśeṣakuśalena bhavitavyaṃ trikṣāntijñānaviśeṣakuśalena ca | tat kasya hetoḥ? tathāhi kumāra yadā bodhisattvo mahāsattvastrikṣāntiviśeṣakuśalo bhavati trikṣāntijñānaviśeṣakuśalaśca bhavati, tadāyaṃ kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ kṣipraṃ samādhiṃ pratilabhate, kṣipraṃ cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate | tasmāttarhi kumāra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena kṣipraṃ cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhukāmenāyaṃ trikṣāntyavatāro dharmaparyāya udgrahītavyaḥ | udgṛhya na parebhyo vistareṇa saṃprakāśayitavyaḥ | tad bhaviṣyati bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ceti ||
body.translated_text: There the Blessed One again addressed <s>Candraprabha</s>, the prince: 'Therefore, O Prince, the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> who desires this <s>samādhi</s> and who wishes to swiftly, fully awaken to the supreme, perfect <s>saṃbodhi</s> should become skilled in the knowledge of the three patiences. He should know the first patience. He should know the second patience. He should know the third patience. He should become skilled in the distinction of the three patiences and skilled in the distinction of the knowledge of the three patiences. For what reason? Because, O Prince, when the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> becomes skilled in the distinction of the three patiences and skilled in the distinction of the knowledge of the three patiences, then, O Prince, the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> swiftly attains the <s>samādhi</s> and swiftly, fully awakens to the supreme, perfect <s>saṃbodhi</s>. Therefore, O Prince, the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> who wishes to swiftly, fully awaken to the supreme, perfect <s>saṃbodhi</s> should take up this <s>dharma</s>-discourse on Entry into the Three Patiences. Having taken it up, he should illuminate it in detail for others. That will be for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of the great mass of people, of gods and humans.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃścandraprabhasya kumārabhūtasyemaṃ trikṣāntyavatāraṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ gāthābhigītena vistareṇa saṃprakāśayati sma -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One illuminated for <s>Candraprabha</s>, the prince, this <s>dharma</s>-discourse on Entry into the Three Patiences in detail, with verses in song:

children.text: na kenacit sārdhaṃ karoti vigrahaṃ na bhāṣate vācamanarthasaṃhitām /
children.translated_text: 'He does not engage in quarrel with anyone; he does not speak words devoid of meaning;

children.text: arthe ca dharme ca sadā pratiṣṭhitaḥ prathamāya kṣāntīya sada nirdiśīyati // SRS_7.1 //
children.translated_text: always established in meaning and <s>dharma</s> — this is taught as belonging to the first patience. // SRS_7.1 //

children.text: māyopamān jānati sarvadharmān na cāpi so bhoti nimittagocaraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He knows all <s>dharmas</s> to be like an illusion, nor does he become one whose domain is signs;

children.text: na hīyate jñānavivṛddhabhūmeḥ prathamāya kṣāntīya ime viśeṣāḥ // SRS_7.2 //
children.translated_text: he does not decline from the stage of growth in knowledge — these are the distinctions of the first patience. // SRS_7.2 //

children.text: sa sarvasūtrāntanayeṣu kovidaḥ subhāṣite 'sminnadhimuktipaṇḍitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He is skilled in the methods of all <s>sūtrāntas</s>, wise in conviction regarding this well-spoken [teaching],

children.text: anantajñānī sugatāna jñāne prathamāya kṣāntīya ime viśeṣāḥ // SRS_7.3 //
children.translated_text: of infinite knowledge regarding the knowledge of the <s>Sugatas</s> — these are the distinctions of the first patience. // SRS_7.3 //

children.text: yaḥ kaści dharmaṃ śṛṇute subhāṣitaṃ buddhāna co bhāṣita tanna kāṅkṣati /
children.translated_text: 'Whoever hears the well-spoken <s>dharma</s> — that spoken by the <s>Buddhas</s>, he does not doubt;

children.text: adhimucyate sarvajināna dharmatāṃ prathamāya kṣāntīya ime viśeṣāḥ // SRS_7.4 //
children.translated_text: he has conviction in the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of all the <s>Jinas</s> — these are the distinctions of the first patience. // SRS_7.4 //

children.text: (Vaidya 36)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 36)

children.text: nītārthasūtrāntaviśeṣa jānati yathopadiṣṭā sugatena śūnyatā /
children.translated_text: 'He understands the distinction of <s>sūtrāntas</s> of definitive meaning; emptiness as taught by the <s>Sugata</s>;

children.text: yāsmin punaḥ pudgala sattva pūruṣo neyārthatāṃ jānati sarvadharmān // SRS_7.5 //
children.translated_text: and that wherein there is mention of person, being, or man — he knows all <s>dharmas</s> to be of provisional meaning. // SRS_7.5 //

children.text: ye asmi loke pṛthu anyatīrthā na tasya teṣu pratihanyate manaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Those many other <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers) in this world — his mind is not obstructed by them;

children.text: kāruṇyameteṣu upasthapeti prathamāya kṣāntīya ime viśeṣāḥ // SRS_7.6 //
children.translated_text: he establishes compassion toward them — these are the distinctions of the first patience. // SRS_7.6 //

children.text: ābhāsamāgacchati tasya dhāraṇī tasmiṃśca ābhāsi na jātu kāṅkṣati /
children.translated_text: '<s>Dhāraṇī</s> (mnemonic retention) comes to him as illumination, and regarding that illumination he never doubts;

children.text: satyānuparivartini vāca bhāṣate prathamāya kṣāntīya ime viśeṣāḥ // SRS_7.7 //
children.translated_text: he speaks words that conform to truth — these are the distinctions of the first patience. // SRS_7.7 //

children.text: caturṇa dhātūna siyānyathātvaṃ vāyvambutejaḥpṛthivīya cāpi /
children.translated_text: 'Even if there were an alteration of the four elements — wind, water, fire, and earth —

children.text: na co vivarteta sa buddhabodheḥ prathamāya kṣāntīya ime viśeṣāḥ // SRS_7.8 //
children.translated_text: he would not turn back from <s>Buddha-bodhi</s> — these are the distinctions of the first patience. // SRS_7.8 //

children.text: ye śilpasthānā pṛthu asti loke sarveṣu so śikṣitu bodhisattvaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever arts and crafts exist widely in the world — in all of them the <s>Bodhisattva</s> trains;

children.text: na cātmana uttari kiṃci paśyati prathamāya kṣāntīya ime viśeṣāḥ // SRS_7.9 //
children.translated_text: yet he does not see anything as superior to himself — these are the distinctions of the first patience. // SRS_7.9 //

children.text: akampiyaḥ samathabalena bhoti śelopamo bhoti vipaśyanāya /
children.translated_text: 'He becomes unshakable through the power of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding); like a mountain he becomes through <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight);

children.text: na kṣobhituṃ śakyu sa sarvasattvairdvitīyāya kṣāntīya sa nirdiśīyati // SRS_7.10 //
children.translated_text: he cannot be disturbed by all beings — this is taught as belonging to the second patience. // SRS_7.10 //

children.text: samāhitastiṣṭhati bhāṣate ca samāhitaścaṃkramate niṣīdati /
children.translated_text: 'Absorbed, he stands; absorbed, he speaks; absorbed, he walks; absorbed, he sits;

children.text: samādhiye pāramitāgato vidu dvitīyāya kṣāntīya ime viśeṣāḥ // SRS_7.11 //
children.translated_text: the wise one has gone to the perfection of <s>samādhi</s> — these are the distinctions of the second patience. // SRS_7.11 //

children.text: (Vaidya 37)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 37)

children.text: samāhito labhati abhijña pañca kṣetraśataṃ gacchati dharmadeśakaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Absorbed, he attains the five <s>abhijñās</s> (higher knowledges); the <s>dharma</s>-teacher travels to a hundred <s>kṣetras</s> (Buddha-fields);

children.text: no cāpi so ṛddhibalāttu hīyate dvitīyāya kṣāntīya ime viśeṣāḥ // SRS_7.12 //
children.translated_text: nor does he decline from the power of spiritual attainment — these are the distinctions of the second patience. // SRS_7.12 //

children.text: sa tādṛśaṃ śānta samādhimeṣate samāhitasya na sa asti sattvaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He seeks such a peaceful <s>samādhi</s> — for one absorbed, there is no being

children.text: yastasya cittasya pramāṇu gṛhṇīyā dvitīyāya kṣāntīya ime viśeṣāḥ // SRS_7.13 //
children.translated_text: who could take the measure of his mind — these are the distinctions of the second patience. // SRS_7.13 //

children.text: ye lokadhātuṣviha keci sattvāste buddhajñānena bhaṇeyu dharmān /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever beings there are in the world-realms here — they would speak the <s>dharmas</s> with <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge —'

children.text: udgṛhṇato sarva yato hi bhāṣiutaṃ dvitīyāya kṣāntīya ime viśeṣāḥ // SRS_7.14 //
children.translated_text: who memorizes all that has been spoken — these are the distinctions of the second patience.' // SRS_7.14 //

children.text: purimottarā dakṣiṇapaścimāsu heṣṭhe tathordhvaṃ vidiśāsu caiva /
children.translated_text: 'In the east, north, south, west, below, above, and in the intermediate directions —

children.text: sarvatra so paśyati lokanāthān tṛtīyāya kṣāntīya sa nirdiśīyati // SRS_7.15 //
children.translated_text: everywhere he sees the Lords of the World: this is declared for the third patience.' // SRS_7.15 //

children.text: suvarṇavarṇena samucchrayeṇa acintiyāṃ nirmita nirmiṇitvā /
children.translated_text: 'With a golden-colored body of lofty stature, having created inconceivable magical emanations,

children.text: deśeti dharmaṃ bahuprāṇikoṭināṃ tṛtīyāya kṣāntīya ime viśeṣāḥ // SRS_7.16 //
children.translated_text: he teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to many <s>koṭis</s> of beings — these are the distinctions of the third patience.' // SRS_7.16 //

children.text: ya jambudvīpa iha buddhakṣetre sarvatra so dṛśyati bodhisattvaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Throughout this <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, in this <s>Buddha</s>-field, that <s>Bodhisattva</s> is seen everywhere;

children.text: jñātaśca bhotī sasurāsure jage tṛtīyāya kṣāntīya ime viśeṣāḥ // SRS_7.17 //
children.translated_text: and he becomes known in the world of gods and <s>Asuras</s> — these are the distinctions of the third patience.' // SRS_7.17 //

children.text: buddhāna ācāru tathaiva gocarā īryāpatho yādṛśa nāyakānām /
children.translated_text: 'The conduct and range of <s>Buddhas</s>, the deportment of the Leaders —

children.text: sarvatra so śikṣitu bhoti paṇḍitastṛtīyāya kṣāntīya ime viśeṣāḥ // SRS_7.18 //
children.translated_text: everywhere that wise one trains in them: these are the distinctions of the third patience.' // SRS_7.18 //

children.text: ye lokadhātuṣviha keci sattvāste bodhisattvasya bhaṇeyu varṇam /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever beings in these world-systems were to praise that <s>Bodhisattva</s>,

children.text: (Vaidya 38)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 38)

children.text: sace 'sya tasmin nānunīyate mano na śikṣito ucyati buddhajñāne // SRS_7.19 //
children.translated_text: if his mind is not swayed by that — he is not [yet] said to be trained in <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge.' // SRS_7.19 //

children.text: ye lokadhātuiṣviha keci sattvāste bodhisattvasya bhaṇeyu varṇam /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever beings in these world-systems were to praise that <s>Bodhisattva</s>,

children.text: sace 'sya teṣu pratihanyate mano na śikṣito 'dyāpi sa buddhajñāne // SRS_7.20 //
children.translated_text: if his mind is repelled by them — he is not yet trained in <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge.' // SRS_7.20 //

children.text: arthena labdhena na bhoti sūmano na cāpyanarthena sa bhoti durmanāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He is not elated when gain comes, nor is he dejected by loss;

children.text: śailopame citti sadā pratiṣṭhito ayaṃ viśeṣastṛtīyāya kṣāntiyāḥ // SRS_7.21 //
children.translated_text: always established in a mind [firm] like a mountain — this is the distinction of the third patience.' // SRS_7.21 //

children.text: ghoṣānugāmī iya kṣāntiruktā cintāmayī bhāvanānulomikī /
children.translated_text: 'That which follows upon hearing is called the patience that follows sound (<s>ghoṣānugāmī</s>); that born of reflection is the conforming [patience] of cultivation;

children.text: śrutaṃmayā sā anutpattikā yā śikṣā ca atrāpyayu bodhimārgaḥ // SRS_7.22 //
children.translated_text: that which I have heard is the patience of the unborn (<s>anutpattikī</s>); and training herein is the path of awakening.' // SRS_7.22 //

children.text: tisro 'pi kṣāntīya sadā niruttarāḥ sa bodhisattvena bhavanti labdhāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'When all three supreme and unsurpassed patiences have been obtained by a <s>Bodhisattva</s>,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tatastaṃ sugatā narottamā viyākaronti virajāya bodhaye // SRS_7.23 //
children.translated_text: then the <s>Sugatas</s>, the best of men, having seen him, predict him for the dustless awakening.' // SRS_7.23 //

children.text: tato 'sya taṃ vyākaraṇaṃ śruṇitvā prakampitā medinī ṣaḍvikāram /
children.translated_text: 'Then, upon hearing that prediction, the earth trembles with six kinds of trembling;

children.text: ābhāya kṣetraṃ bhavate prabhāsvaraṃ puṣpāṇi ca varṣiṣu devakoṭyaḥ // SRS_7.24 //
children.translated_text: the field becomes radiant with splendor, and <s>koṭis</s> of gods shower flowers.' // SRS_7.24 //

children.text: tasyo ca taṃ vyākaraṇaṃ śruṇitvā sattvāna koṭī niyutā acintiyā /
children.translated_text: 'And upon hearing that prediction of his, inconceivable <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of beings

children.text: utpādayī citta varāgrabodhaye vayaṃ pi bheṣyāma jina āryacetikāḥ // SRS_7.25 //
children.translated_text: generate the thought of supreme awakening: "We too shall become <s>Jinas</s>, worthy of noble homage!"' // SRS_7.25 //

children.text: kṣāntyā imāstisra niruttarā yadā saṃbodhisattvena bhavanti labdhāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'When these three supreme and unsurpassed patiences have been obtained by a <s>Bodhisattva</s>,

children.text: na cāpi so jāyati nāpi mrīyate na cāpi sa cyavati nopapadyate // SRS_7.26 //
children.translated_text: he is neither born nor does he die; he neither passes away nor is he reborn.' // SRS_7.26 //

children.text: (Vaidya 39)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 39)

children.text: yadā imā kṣānti trayo niruttarā saṃbodhisattvena bhavanti labdhāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'When these three supreme and unsurpassed patiences have been obtained by a <s>Bodhisattva</s>,

children.text: na paśyateḥ jāyati yaśca mrīyate sthitadharmatāṃ paśyati sarvadharmān // SRS_7.27 //
children.translated_text: he does not see anyone being born or dying — he sees all <s>dharmas</s> as abiding in their true nature.' // SRS_7.27 //

children.text: tathāhi teno vitatheti jñātā māyopamā dharma svabhāvaśūnyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For he has known them as false — <s>dharmas</s> are like illusions, empty by their own nature;

children.text: na śūnyatā jāyati no ca mrīyate svabhāvaśūnyā imi sarvadharmāḥ // SRS_7.28 //
children.translated_text: emptiness is neither born nor does it die — all these <s>dharmas</s> are empty by their own nature.' // SRS_7.28 //

children.text: yadāttyasau satkṛtu bhoti kenacid upasthito mānitu pūjito 'rcitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'When he is honored, attended, respected, worshipped, and venerated by anyone,

children.text: na tasya tasminnanunīyate mano jānāti so dharmasvabhāvaśūnyatām // SRS_7.29 //
children.translated_text: his mind is not swayed by that — he knows the own-nature emptiness of <s>dharmas</s>.' // SRS_7.29 //

children.text: ākruṣṭa sattvehi prahāratarjito na teṣu krodhaṃ kurute na mānam /
children.translated_text: 'Abused, beaten, and threatened by beings, he generates neither anger nor pride toward them;

children.text: maitrīṃ ca teṣu dṛḍha saṃjaneti tathaiva sattvāna pramocanāya // SRS_7.30 //
children.translated_text: rather, he generates firm loving-kindness toward them, for the liberation of those very beings.' // SRS_7.30 //

children.text: loṣṭehi daṇḍehi ca tāḍyamānaḥ pratighātu teṣu na karoti paṇḍitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Struck with clods and sticks, that wise one generates no hostility toward them;

children.text: nairātmyakṣāntīya pratiṣṭhitasya na vidyate krodhakhilaṃ na mānaḥ // SRS_7.31 //
children.translated_text: for one established in the patience of selflessness, there exists neither anger, irritation, nor pride.' // SRS_7.31 //

children.text: tathāhi teno vitatheti jñātā māyopamā dharma svabhāvaśūnyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For he has known them as false — <s>dharmas</s> are like illusions, empty by their own nature;

children.text: sa tādṛśe dharmanaye pratiṣṭhitaḥ susatkṛto bhoti sadevaloke // SRS_7.32 //
children.translated_text: established in such a <s>Dharma</s>-method, he is well-honored in the world with its gods.' // SRS_7.32 //

children.text: yadāpi sattvāḥ pragṛhītaśastrāśchindeyu tasyo pṛthu aṅgamaṅgam /
children.translated_text: 'Even when beings, weapons in hand, were to cut his limbs and members one by one,

children.text: na tasya teṣu pratihanyate mano na cāpi maitrī karuṇā tu hīyate // SRS_7.33 //
children.translated_text: his mind would not be repelled by them, nor would his loving-kindness or compassion diminish.' // SRS_7.33 //

children.text: evaṃ ca so tatra janeti cittaṃ chindanti te hi pṛthu aṅgamaṅgam /
children.translated_text: 'Thus he generates the thought: "They are cutting my limbs and members one by one;

children.text: (Vaidya 40)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 40)

children.text: tathā na mahyaṃ śiva śānti nirvṛtī yāvanna sthāpye imi agrabodhaye // SRS_7.34 //
children.translated_text: even so there is no peace, calm, or bliss for me until I have established these [beings] in the supreme awakening."' // SRS_7.34 //

children.text: etādṛśe kṣāntibale niruttare nairātmyakṣāntīsamatāvihāriṇām /
children.translated_text: 'In such supreme power of patience, for those who dwell in the equanimity of the patience of selflessness,

children.text: saṃbodhisattvāna mahāyaśānāṃ kalpāna koṭyaḥ satataṃ subhāvitāḥ // SRS_7.35 //
children.translated_text: for those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of great renown, <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> are constantly well-cultivated.' // SRS_7.35 //

children.text: tatottare yāttika gaṅgavālikā na tāva bodhī bhavatīha sparśitā /
children.translated_text: 'And beyond that, for as many [kalpas] as the sands of the Ganges, awakening is not yet touched;

children.text: ye buddhajñānena na karoti kāryaṃ kiṃ vā punarjñāna tathāgatānām // SRS_7.36 //
children.translated_text: what then of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge not being accomplished — how much more so the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>!' // SRS_7.36 //

children.text: kṣapetu varṇaṃ sukaraṃ na teṣāṃ prabhāṣatā kalpaśatānyacintiyā /
children.translated_text: 'Their virtues cannot easily be exhausted even by one speaking for inconceivable hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> —

children.text: anantakīrtena mahāyaśānāṃ nairātmyakṣāntīya pratiṣṭhitānām // SRS_7.37 //
children.translated_text: those of infinite renown and great fame, established in the patience of selflessness.' // SRS_7.37 //

children.text: tasmāddhi yo icchati bodhi buddhituṃ taṃ jñānaskandhaṃ pravaraṃ niruttaram /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, whoever wishes to know the awakening — that supreme, unsurpassed aggregate of knowledge —

children.text: sa kṣānti bhāvetu jinena varṇitāṃ na durlabhā bodhi varā bhaviṣyati // SRS_7.38 //
children.translated_text: let him cultivate the patience praised by the <s>Jina</s>; the supreme awakening shall not be hard to obtain.' // SRS_7.38 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje trikṣāntyavatāraparivarto nāma saptamaḥ || 7 ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh chapter in the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, called the <s>Tri-kṣānty-avatāra</s> (Entrance into the Three Patiences) chapter.

body.text:
(Vaidya 41)
8 Abhāvasamudgataparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 41) Chapter 8: The <s>Abhāvasamudgata</s> (Arisen from Non-existence).

body.text: tatra punarapi bhagavān candraprabhaṃ kumārabhūtamāmantrayate sma - bhūtapūrvaṃ kumāra atīte 'dhvani asaṃkhyeyaiḥ kalpairasaṃkhyeyatarairvipularaiprameyairacintyairaparimāṇairyadāsīt | tena kālena tena samayena abhāvasamudgato nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loke udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān | tat kiṃ manyase kumāra kena kāraṇena sa tathāgato 'bhāvasamudgata ityucyate? sa khalu punaḥ kumāra tathāgato jātamātra evoparyantarīkṣe saptatālamātraṃ vaihāyasamabhyudgamya sapta padāni prakramitvā imāmevaṃrūpāṃ vācamabhāṣata - abhāvasamudgatāḥ sarvadharmāḥ, abhāvasamudgatāḥ sarvadharmā iti | tena ca kumāra śabdena trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātuḥ svareṇābhivijñapto 'bhūt | tatra bhaumān devānupādāya yāvad brahmalokaṃ paraṃparayā śabdamudīrayāmāsuḥ ghoṣamanuśrāvayāmāsuḥ - abhāvasamudgato batāyaṃ tathāgato bhaviṣyati, yo jātamātra evoparyantarīkṣe saptatālamātramabhyudgamya sapta padāni prakramitvā abhāvaśabdamudīrayati | iti hyabhāvasamudgato 'bhāvasamudgata iti tasya tathāgatasya nāmadheyamudapādi | tasya ca bhagavato bodhiprāptasya sarvavṛkṣapatrebhyaḥ sarvatṛṇagulmauṣadhivanaspatibhyaḥ sarvaśailaśikharebhyaścābhāvasamudgataśabdo niścarati | yāvati ca tatra lokadhātau śabdaprajñaptiḥ sarvato 'bhāvasamudgatavijñaptiśabdo niścarati | tena ca kumāra kālena tena samayena tasya bhagavato 'bhāvasamudgatasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya pravacane mahākaruṇācintī nāma rājakumāro 'bhūdabhirūpaḥ prāsādiko darśanīyaḥ paramaśubhavarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgataḥ | atha khalu kumāra sa mahākaruṇācintī nāma rājakumāro yena bhagavān abhāvasamudgatastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhastenosaṃkrāmat | upasaṃkramya tasya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya ekānte 'sthāt ||
body.translated_text: Then again the Blessed One addressed the prince <s>Candraprabha</s>: 'Formerly, O prince, in a past age, incalculable <s>kalpas</s> ago — incalculable, vast, immeasurable, inconceivable, boundless — at that time, at that moment, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Abhāvasamudgata</s> (Arisen from Non-existence), an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One, appeared in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed charioteer of beings to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. What do you think, prince — for what reason is that <s>Tathāgata</s> called <s>Abhāvasamudgata</s>? That <s>Tathāgata</s>, prince, at the very moment of his birth, rose up into the sky to the height of seven palm trees, took seven steps, and uttered these words: "All <s>dharmas</s> are arisen from non-existence! All <s>dharmas</s> are arisen from non-existence!" And by that sound, prince, the trichiliocosmic world-system was pervaded. Then, from the earth-gods upward to the <s>Brahma</s>-world, [the deities] passed along the sound and proclaimed the cry: "This <s>Tathāgata</s> shall indeed be <s>Abhāvasamudgata</s>, who at the very moment of birth, rising into the sky to the height of seven palm trees, taking seven steps, utters the word <s>abhāva</s> (non-existence)!" Thus the name <s>Abhāvasamudgata</s> arose for that <s>Tathāgata</s>. And when that Blessed One had attained awakening, from all tree-leaves, from all grasses, shrubs, herbs, and forest trees, from all mountain-peaks, the sound <s>abhāvasamudgata</s> issued forth. And whatever verbal designation existed in that world-system, from everywhere the proclamation-sound of <s>abhāvasamudgata</s> issued forth. At that time, prince, under the dispensation of the Blessed One <s>Abhāvasamudgata</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, there was a prince named <s>Mahākaruṇācintī</s> (Inconceivable Great Compassion) — handsome, pleasing, beautiful, endowed with supreme excellent complexion. Then, prince, that prince <s>Mahākaruṇācintī</s> approached the Blessed One <s>Abhāvasamudgata</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One. Having approached, he bowed his head at the Blessed One's feet, circumambulated the Blessed One three times, and stood to one side.'

body.text: atha khalu kumāra sa bhagavān abhāvasamudgatastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho mahākaruṇācintino rājakumārasyādhyāśayaṃ viditvā imaṃ samādhiṃ deśayāmāsa | atha khalu kumāra sa mahākaruṇācintī rājakumāraḥ imaṃ samādhiṃ śrutvā tuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajātaḥ prasīdati sma | prasannacittaśca keśaśmaśrūṇyavatārya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇi paridhāya samyageva śraddhayā agārādanagārikāṃ pravrajito 'bhūt | sa pravrajitaḥ sannimaṃ samādhimudgṛhītavān | udgṛhya paryavāpya dhārayitvā vācayitvā bhāvanāyogamanuyukto vyahārṣīt | sa tainaiva kuśalamūlena (Vaidya 42) viṃśatikalpakoṭyo na jātu durgativinipātamagamat | viṃśatīnāṃ kalpānāmatyayena anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddho 'bhūt | suvicintitārtho nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi | sarveṣu ca teṣu kalpeṣu viśatiṃ ca buddhakoṭīrārāgayāmāsa | paśya kumāra yathāyaṃ samādhirbahukaro bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmanuttarasya buddhajñānasya paripūraṇāya saṃvartate ||
body.translated_text: 'Then, prince, the Blessed One <s>Abhāvasamudgata</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, knowing the inner disposition of the prince <s>Mahākaruṇācintī</s>, taught him this <s>samādhi</s>. Then, prince, the prince <s>Mahākaruṇācintī</s>, having heard this <s>samādhi</s>, became delighted, elated, joyful, filled with joy and happiness, and was filled with serene faith. With serene mind, having shaved off his hair and beard, having put on saffron robes, with perfect faith he went forth from the household life into homelessness. Having gone forth, he memorized this <s>samādhi</s>. Having memorized, comprehended, retained, and recited it, he devoted himself to the practice of cultivation. By that very root of merit, (<s>Vaidya</s> 42) for twenty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> he never went to an evil destiny. At the end of twenty <s>kalpas</s>, he fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect and complete awakening. A <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Suvicitārthra</s> (Well-Considered Meaning), an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One, appeared in the world. And in all those <s>kalpas</s> he encountered twenty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>. See, prince, how this <s>samādhi</s> is of great benefit to <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, conducive to the fulfillment of unsurpassed <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge!'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: smarāmyahaṃ pūrvamatītamadhvani acintiye kalpi narāṇamuttamaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I remember in the past, in a bygone age, in inconceivable <s>kalpas</s>, the best of men —

children.text: utpannu lokārthakaro maharṣirnāmnā hi so 'bhāvasamudgato 'bhūt // SRS_8.1 //
children.translated_text: a great sage, benefactor of the world, arose; his name was <s>Abhāvasamudgata</s>.' // SRS_8.1 //

children.text: sa jātamātro gagane sthihitvā sarveṣa dharmāṇa abhāvu deśayī /
children.translated_text: 'At the very moment of birth, standing in the sky, he taught the non-existence of all <s>dharmas</s>;

children.text: tadānurūpaṃ kṛtu nāmadheyaṃ śabdena sarvaṃ trisahasra vijñapī // SRS_8.2 //
children.translated_text: a name was given corresponding to that — by that sound the entire trichiliocosm was made aware.' // SRS_8.2 //

children.text: devāpi sarve pramumoca śabdaṃ abhāvu nāmneti jino bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: 'All the gods too uttered the cry: "The <s>Jina</s> shall be named <s>Abhāva</s> —

children.text: yo jātamātraḥ pada sapta prakramannabhāvu dharmāṇa bravīti nāyakaḥ // SRS_8.3 //
children.translated_text: the Leader who, at the moment of birth, taking seven steps, declares the non-existence of <s>dharmas</s>."' // SRS_8.3 //

children.text: buddho yadā bheṣyati dharmarājaḥ sarveṣa dharmāṇa prakāśako muniḥ /
children.translated_text: 'When he became a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Dharma</s>-king, the Sage who illuminates all <s>dharmas</s>,

children.text: tṛṇavṛkṣagulmauṣadhiśailaparvate abhāvu dharmāṇa ravo bhaviṣyati // SRS_8.4 //
children.translated_text: from grasses, trees, shrubs, herbs, mountain-peaks — the sound of the non-existence of <s>dharmas</s> issued forth.' // SRS_8.4 //

children.text: yāvanti śabdāstahi lokadhātau sarve hyabhāvā na hi kaści bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever sounds there were in that world-system — all were non-existence, for nothing has [inherent] existence;

children.text: tāvanti kho tasya tathāgatasya svaru niścarī lokavināyakasya // SRS_8.5 //
children.translated_text: that many were the sounds that issued forth of that <s>Tathāgata</s>, the Guide of the World.' // SRS_8.5 //

children.text: tasmiṃśca kāle abhu rājaputraḥ karuṇāvicintī sada nāmadheyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'At that time there was a prince, always named <s>Karuṇāvicintī</s> (Inconceivable Compassion),

children.text: abhirūpa prāsādika darśanīya upāgamī tasya jinasya antikam // SRS_8.6 //
children.translated_text: handsome, pleasing, beautiful — he approached the presence of that <s>Jina</s>.' // SRS_8.6 //

children.text: (Vaidya 43)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 43)

children.text: vanditva pādau munipuṃgavasya pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtya ca gauraveṇa /
children.translated_text: 'Having bowed at the feet of the foremost sage, having circumambulated with reverence,

children.text: prasannacitto niṣasāda tatra śravaṇāya dharmaṃ virajamanuttaram // SRS_8.7 //
children.translated_text: with a serene mind he sat down there, to hear the dustless, unsurpassed <s>Dharma</s>.' // SRS_8.7 //

children.text: sa co jino āśayu jñātva dhīraḥ prakāśayāmāsa samādhimetam /
children.translated_text: 'That steadfast <s>Jina</s>, knowing his disposition, proclaimed this <s>samādhi</s>;

children.text: śrutvā ca so imu virajaṃ samādhiṃ laghu pravrajī jinavaraśāsane 'smin // SRS_8.8 //
children.translated_text: having heard this dustless <s>samādhi</s>, he quickly went forth in the dispensation of that best of <s>Jinas</s>.' // SRS_8.8 //

children.text: sa pravrajitvāna imaṃ samādhiṃ dhāritva vācitva paryāpuṇitvā /
children.translated_text: 'Having gone forth and upheld, recited, and mastered this <s>samādhi</s>,

children.text: kalpāna koṭyaḥ paripūrṇa viṃśatiṃ na jātu gacche vinipātabhūmim // SRS_8.9 //
children.translated_text: for a full twenty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> he never went to a realm of downfall.' // SRS_8.9 //
