children.text: sa tena caivaṃ kuśalena karmaṇā ārāgayī viṃśati buddhakoṭyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'By that very wholesome deed, he encountered twenty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>;

children.text: teṣāṃ ca sarveṣu jināna antikādimaṃ varaṃ śānta samādhi bhāvayī // SRS_8.10 //
children.translated_text: and in the presence of all those <s>Jinas</s> he cultivated this supreme, peaceful <s>samādhi</s>.' // SRS_8.10 //

children.text: sa paścikāle abhu buddha loke sucintitārtho sadanāmadheyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In the final time, he became a <s>Buddha</s> in the world, always bearing the name <s>Suvicintitārtha</s>;

children.text: kṛtvā ca arthaṃ bahuprāṇakoṭināṃ sa paścakālasmi śikhīva nirvṛtaḥ // SRS_8.11 //
children.translated_text: having accomplished the welfare of many <s>koṭis</s> of beings, in the final time he was extinguished like a [sacrificial] flame.' // SRS_8.11 //

children.text: tasmāddhi ya icchati bodhi buddhituṃ sattvāṃśca uttarāyituṃ bhavārṇavāt /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, whoever aspires to awaken to <s>bodhi</s> and to ferry beings across the ocean of existence,

children.text: dhāreta sūtramimu buddhavarṇitaṃ na durlabhā bheṣyati so 'grabodhiḥ // SRS_8.12 //
children.translated_text: let him retain this <s>sūtra</s> praised by the <s>Buddha</s> — the supreme awakening will not be difficult for him!" // SRS_8.12 //

body.text: iti śrī samādhirāje abhāvasamudgataparivarto nāmāṣṭamaḥ || 8 ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth chapter of the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, named "The Chapter on Arising from Non-Existence" (<s>Abhāvasamudgataparivarta</s>). // 8 //

body.text:
(Vaidya 44)
9 Gambhīradharmakṣāntiparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Vaidya p. 44) Chapter 9: The Chapter on Patient Acceptance of Profound <s>Dharmas</s> (<s>Gambhīradharmakṣāntiparivarta</s>).

body.text:
tatra bhagavān punarapi candraprabhaṃ kumārabhūtamāmantrayate sma - tasmāttarhi kumāra bodhisattvena mahāsattvenemaṃ samādhimākāṅkṣatā kṣipraṃ cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhukāmena gambhīradharmakṣāntikuśalena bhavitavyam | kathaṃ ca kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvo gambhīradharmakṣāntikuśalo bhavati? iha kumāra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena māyopamāḥ sarvadharmā yathābhūtataḥ prajñātavyāḥ | svapnopamā marīcyupamāḥ pratiśrutkopamāḥ pratibhāsopamā udakacandropamā nirmitopamāḥ pratibimbopamā ākāśopamāḥ sarvadharmāḥ prajñātavyāḥ | yadā ca kumāra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena māyopamāḥ sarvadharmāḥ parijñātā bhavanti, svapnopamā marīcyupamāḥ pratiśrutkopamāḥ pratibhāsopamā udakacandropamā nirmitopamāḥ pratibimbopamā ākāśopamāḥ sarvadharmāḥ parijñātā bhavanti yathābhūtataḥ tadāyaṃ kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvo gambhīradharmakṣāntikuśala ityucyate | sa gambhīrayā dharmakṣāntyā samanvāgato rañjanīyeṣu dharmeṣu na rajyate, doṣaṇīyeṣu dharmeṣu na duṣyate, mohanīyeṣu dharmeṣu na muhyate | tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi - sa taṃ dharmaṃ na samanupaśyati, taṃ dharmaṃ nopalabhate | yo rajyeta, yatra vā rajyeta,
yena vā rajyeta | yo duṣyeta, yatra vā duṣyeta, yena vā duṣyeta | yo muhyeta, yatra vā muhyeta, yena vā muhyeta | sa taṃ dharmaṃ na samanupaśyati, taṃ dharma nopalabhate | taṃ dharmamasamanupaśyannanupalabhamāno 'rakto 'duṣṭo 'mūḍho 'viparyastacittaḥ samāhita ityucyate | niṣprapañcaḥ...... | tīrṇaḥ pāragataḥ...... | sthalagataḥ...... | kṣemaprāptaḥ | arūpaprāptaḥ | śīlavān | jñānavān | prajñāvān | puṇyavān | ṛddhimān...... | smṛtimān...... | matimān...... | gatimān | hrīmān ...... | dhṛtimān | cāritravān | dhūtaguṇasaṃlekhavān | anaṅganaḥ | niṣkiṃcanaḥ | arhan | kṣīṇāsravaḥ | niṣkleśo vaśībhūtaḥ suvimuktacittaḥ suvimuktaprajñaḥ ājāneyo mahānāgaḥ kṛtakṛtyaḥ kṛtakaraṇīyo 'pahṛtabhāro 'nuprāptasvakārthaḥ parikṣīṇabhavasaṃyojanaḥ samyagājñāsuvimuktacittaḥ sarvacetovaśiparamapāramitāprāptaḥ śramaṇaḥ | brāhmaṇaḥ snātakaḥ | pāragaḥ vedakaḥ śrotriyaḥ | buddhaputraḥ | śākyaputraḥ | marditakaṇṭakaḥ | utkṣiptaparikhaḥ | udīrṇaparikhaḥ | ākṣiptaśalyaḥ | nirjaraḥ | bhikṣuḥ | apariveṣṭanaḥ | puruṣaḥ | satpuruṣaḥ | uttamapuruṣaḥ | mahāpuruṣaḥ | puruṣasiṃhaḥ | puruṣanāgaḥ | puruṣājāneyaḥ | puruṣadhaureyaḥ puruṣaśūraḥ | puruṣavīraḥ | puruṣapuṣpaḥ | puruṣapadmaḥ | puruṣapuṇḍarīkaḥ | puruṣadamakaḥ | puruṣacandraḥ | akāpuruṣaḥ | puruṣānupaliptaḥ ityucyate | atha khalu bhagavāstasyāṃ velāyamimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Thereupon the Blessed One again addressed the prince <s>Candraprabha</s>: "Therefore, prince, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> who aspires to this <s>samādhi</s> and wishes quickly to awaken to the unsurpassed, perfect awakening should be skilled in the patient acceptance of profound <s>dharmas</s>. And how, prince, does a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> become skilled in the patient acceptance of profound <s>dharmas</s>? Here, prince, all <s>dharmas</s> should be understood by the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> as they truly are — as like an illusion. All <s>dharmas</s> should be understood as like a dream, like a mirage, like an echo, like a reflection, like the moon in water, like a magical creation, like a mirror-image, like space. And when, prince, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> has fully comprehended all <s>dharmas</s> as like an illusion, like a dream, like a mirage, like an echo, like a reflection, like the moon in water, like a magical creation, like a mirror-image, like space — as they truly are — then, prince, this <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> is called 'skilled in the patient acceptance of profound <s>dharmas</s>.' Endowed with this profound patient acceptance of <s>dharmas</s>, he is not attracted to attractive <s>dharmas</s>, he is not repelled by repelling <s>dharmas</s>, he is not confused by confusing <s>dharmas</s>. Why? Because he does not perceive that <s>dharma</s>, he does not apprehend that <s>dharma</s> — neither that which would be attracted, nor that toward which attraction would arise, nor that by which one would be attracted; neither that which would be repelled, nor that toward which repulsion would arise, nor that by which one would be repelled; neither that which would be confused, nor that toward which confusion would arise, nor that by which one would be confused. He does not perceive that <s>dharma</s>, he does not apprehend that <s>dharma</s>. Not perceiving and not apprehending that <s>dharma</s>, he is called 'unattracted, unrepelled, unconfused, with undistorted mind, concentrated.' [He is called] 'free from conceptual proliferation ...' 'one who has crossed over, gone to the other shore ...' 'one who has reached dry ground ...' 'one who has reached safety.' 'One who has reached the formless.' 'One possessing morality.' 'One possessing knowledge.' 'One possessing wisdom.' 'One possessing merit.' 'One possessing supernatural power ...' 'One possessing mindfulness ...' 'One possessing intelligence ...' 'One possessing [right] course.' 'One possessing moral shame ...' 'One possessing fortitude.' 'One possessing [right] conduct.' 'One endowed with the purificatory qualities (<s>dhūtaguṇa</s>).' 'Stainless.' 'Possessing nothing.' '<s>Arhat</s>.' 'One whose defilements are exhausted.' 'Free from <s>kleśas</s>, self-mastered, with well-liberated mind, with well-liberated wisdom, a thoroughbred, a great <s>Nāga</s>, one who has done what was to be done, one who has accomplished what was to be accomplished, one who has laid down the burden, one who has attained his own goal, one whose fetters to existence are exhausted, one whose mind is well-liberated through right knowledge, one who has attained the supreme perfection of mastery over all [states of] mind.' 'An ascetic.' 'A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.' 'A bathed one.' 'One who has gone beyond.' 'A knower of the <s>Vedas</s>.' 'A learned one.' 'A son of the <s>Buddha</s>.' 'A son of the <s>Śākya</s>.' 'One who has crushed the thorns.' 'One who has raised the drawbridge.' 'One who has lifted the moat.' 'One who has extracted the dart.' 'One free from decay.' 'A monk.' 'One who is unwrapped.' 'A person.' 'A true person.' 'A supreme person.' 'A great person.' 'A lion among persons.' 'An elephant among persons.' 'A thoroughbred among persons.' 'A foremost bearer among persons.' 'A hero among persons.' 'A valiant one among persons.' 'A flower among persons.' 'A lotus among persons.' 'A white lotus among persons.' 'A tamer of persons.' 'A moon among persons.' 'Not a base person.' 'An unstained person' — thus he is called. Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses —

children.text: yada lokadhātu na vivarta bhoti ākāśu bhoti ayu sarvalokaḥ /
children.translated_text: "When a world-system has not yet evolved, there is space — that is the entire world;

children.text: (Vaidya 45)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya p. 45)

children.text: yathaiva taṃ pūrvu tathaiva paścāt tathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān // SRS_9.1 //
children.translated_text: as it was before, so it is afterward — know all <s>dharmas</s> to be like that!" // SRS_9.1 //

children.text: idaṃ jagad yāva ca kiṃci vartate adhastameti abhūdāpaskandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: "This world, whatever exists here, sinks below — the water-element has vanished;

children.text: yathaiva taṃ heṣṭhe tathaiva ūrdhvaṃ tathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān // SRS_9.2 //
children.translated_text: as it is below, so it is above — know all <s>dharmas</s> to be like that!" // SRS_9.2 //

children.text: yathāntarīkṣasmi na kiṃcidabhraṃ kṣaṇena co dṛśyati abhramaṇḍalam /
children.translated_text: "Just as in the sky there are no clouds, yet in an instant a mass of clouds is seen —

children.text: pūrvāntu jānīya kutaḥ prasūtaṃ tathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān // SRS_9.3 //
children.translated_text: one should know from whence its prior [state] arose — know all <s>dharmas</s> to be like that!" // SRS_9.3 //

children.text: tathāgatasyo yatha nirvṛtasya manasi karontaḥ pratibimbu dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: "Just as when people make a mental [image] of the <s>Tathāgata</s> who has passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>, a reflection is seen,

children.text: yathaiva taṃ pūrvu tathaiva paścāt tathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān // SRS_9.4 //
children.translated_text: as it was before, so it is afterward — know all <s>dharmas</s> to be like that!" // SRS_9.4 //

children.text: yathaiva phenasya mahāntu piṇḍamoghena ucchettu naro nirīkṣate /
children.translated_text: "Just as a man examines a great mass of foam on a river and [tries to] grasp it,

children.text: nirīkṣya so tatra na sārasaṃdarśī tathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān // SRS_9.5 //
children.translated_text: and upon examining, finds no substance in it — know all <s>dharmas</s> to be like that!" // SRS_9.5 //

children.text: deve yathā varṣati sthūlabinduke pṛthak pṛthag budbuda saṃbhavanti /
children.translated_text: "When the sky rains thick drops, individual bubbles arise —

children.text: utpannabhagnā na hi santi budbudāstathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān // SRS_9.6 //
children.translated_text: arisen and burst, the bubbles do not [truly] exist — know all <s>dharmas</s> to be like that!" // SRS_9.6 //

children.text: yathaiva grāmāntari lekhadarśanāt kriyāḥ pravartanti pṛthak śubhāśubhāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Just as from seeing written characters in a town, various actions — good and bad — proceed,

children.text: na lekhasaṃkrānti girāya vidyate tathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān // SRS_9.7 //
children.translated_text: yet no transference from the writing to the speech is found — know all <s>dharmas</s> to be like that!" // SRS_9.7 //

children.text: yathā naro mānamadena mohito bhramanti saṃjānatimāṃ vasuṃdharām /
children.translated_text: "Just as a man, confused by pride and intoxication, imagines this earth to be moving,

children.text: na co mahīyā calitaṃ na kampitaṃ tathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān // SRS_9.8 //
children.translated_text: yet the earth has not moved nor trembled — know all <s>dharmas</s> to be like that!" // SRS_9.8 //

children.text: (Vaidya 46)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya p. 46)

children.text: ādarśapṛṣṭhe tatha tailapātre nirīkṣate nāri mukhaṃ svalaṃkṛtam /
children.translated_text: "On the surface of a mirror, or in a vessel of oil, a woman sees her own well-adorned face;

children.text: sā tatra rāgaṃ janayitva bālā pradhāvitā kāma gaveṣamāṇā // SRS_9.9 //
children.translated_text: that foolish one, generating desire there, rushes forth seeking pleasure. // SRS_9.9 //

children.text: mukhasya saṃkrānti yadā na vidyate bimbe mukhaṃ naiva kadāci labhyate /
children.translated_text: "When no transference of the face exists, and no face is ever found in the image —

children.text: yathā sa mūḍhā janayeta rāgaṃ tathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān // SRS_9.10 //
children.translated_text: just as that deluded one generates desire, know all <s>dharmas</s> to be like that!" // SRS_9.10 //

children.text: yathaiva gandharvapuraṃ marīcikā yathaiva māyā supinaṃ yathaiva /
children.translated_text: "Just as a <s>Gandharva</s>-city, just as a mirage, just as an illusion, just as a dream —

children.text: svabhāvaśūnyā tu nimittabhāvanā tathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān // SRS_9.11 //
children.translated_text: empty of own-nature, yet [arising through] cultivation of signs — know all <s>dharmas</s> to be like that!" // SRS_9.11 //

children.text: yathaiva candrasya nabhe viśuddhe hrade prasanne pratibimba dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: "Just as in the pure sky, the reflection of the moon is seen in a clear pond —

children.text: śaśisya saṃkrānti jale na vidyate tallakṣaṇān jānatha sarvadharmān // SRS_9.12 //
children.translated_text: no transference of the moon into the water is found — know all <s>dharmas</s> to have that characteristic!" // SRS_9.12 //

children.text: yathā naraḥ śailavanāntare sthito bhaṇeyya gāyeyya haseyya rodaye /
children.translated_text: "Just as a man standing amidst mountains and forests might speak, sing, laugh, or weep,

children.text: pratiśrutkā śrūyati no ca dṛśyate tathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān // SRS_9.13 //
children.translated_text: an echo is heard but not seen — know all <s>dharmas</s> to be like that!" // SRS_9.13 //

children.text: gīte ca vādye ca tathaiva rodite pratiśrutkā jāyati taṃ pratītya /
children.translated_text: "In singing, playing music, and likewise weeping, an echo arises dependent on those [sounds];

children.text: girāya ghoṣo na kadāci vidyate tathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān // SRS_9.14 //
children.translated_text: yet no sound is ever found in the speech [itself] — know all <s>dharmas</s> to be like that!" // SRS_9.14 //

children.text: yathaiva kāmān supinanta seviya pratibuddhasattvaḥ puruṣo na paśyati /
children.translated_text: "Just as one who has enjoyed pleasures in a dream, upon awakening, does not see them —

children.text: sa bāla kāmeṣvatikāmalobhī tathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān // SRS_9.15 //
children.translated_text: that fool, excessively greedy for pleasures — know all <s>dharmas</s> to be like that!" // SRS_9.15 //

children.text: rūpān yathā nirmiṇi māyakāro hastīrathānaśvarathān vicitrān /
children.translated_text: "Just as a magician creates various forms — elephants, chariots, horses, and wagons —

children.text: (Vaidya 47)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya p. 47)

children.text: na cātra kaścid ratha tatra dṛśate tathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān // SRS_9.16 //
children.translated_text: yet no chariot is actually seen there — know all <s>dharmas</s> to be like that!" // SRS_9.16 //

children.text: yathā kumārī supināntarasmin sā putra jātaṃ ca mṛtaṃ ca paśyati /
children.translated_text: "Just as in a dream a maiden sees a son born and [then] dead —

children.text: jāte 'tituṣṭā mṛte daurmanaḥsthitā tathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān // SRS_9.17 //
children.translated_text: overjoyed at the birth, sorrowful at the death — know all <s>dharmas</s> to be like that!" // SRS_9.17 //

children.text: yathā mṛtāṃ mātaramātmajaṃ vā svapne tu vai roditi uccaśabdam /
children.translated_text: "Just as in a dream one weeps aloud for a dead mother or child —

children.text: na tasya mātā mriyate na putrastathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān // SRS_9.18 //
children.translated_text: yet neither his mother nor his son has died — know all <s>dharmas</s> to be like that!" // SRS_9.18 //

children.text: yathaiva rātrau jala candra dṛśyate acchasmi vārismi anāvilasmi /
children.translated_text: "Just as at night the moon is seen in clear, limpid, undisturbed water —

children.text: agrāhya tuccho jala candraśūnya tathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān // SRS_9.19 //
children.translated_text: ungraspable, insubstantial, the water is devoid of the moon — know all <s>dharmas</s> to be like that!" // SRS_9.19 //

children.text: yathaiva grīṣmāṇa madhyāhnakāle tṛṣābhitaptaḥ puruṣo vrajeta /
children.translated_text: "Just as in summer at midday, a man tormented by thirst walks along

children.text: marīcikāṃ paśyati toyarāśiṃ tathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān // SRS_9.20 //
children.translated_text: and sees a mirage as a mass of water — know all <s>dharmas</s> to be like that!" // SRS_9.20 //

children.text: marīcikāyāmudakaṃ na vidyate sa mūḍha sattvaḥ pibituṃ tadicchati /
children.translated_text: "In a mirage no water is found, yet that deluded being wishes to drink it;

children.text: abhūtavāriṃ pibituṃ na śakyate tathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān // SRS_9.21 //
children.translated_text: the water that does not exist cannot be drunk — know all <s>dharmas</s> to be like that!" // SRS_9.21 //

children.text: yathaiva ārdraṃ kadalīya skandhaṃ sārārthikaḥ puruṣu vipāṭayeta /
children.translated_text: "Just as a man seeking substance splits open the moist trunk of a plantain tree —

children.text: bahirvā adhyātma na sāramasti tathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān // SRS_9.22 //
children.translated_text: neither outside nor within is there any substance — know all <s>dharmas</s> to be like that!" // SRS_9.22 //

children.text: na cakṣuṃ pramāṇaṃ na śrotra ghrāṇaṃ na jihva pramāṇaṃ na kāyacittam /
children.translated_text: "The eye is not a valid measure, nor are the ear and nose; the tongue is not a valid measure, nor body and mind.

children.text: pramāṇa yadyeta bhaveyurindriyā kasyāryamārgeṇa bhaveta kāryam // SRS_9.23 //
children.translated_text: If these sense-faculties were valid measures, what need would anyone have of the noble path? // SRS_9.23 //

children.text: (Vaidya 48)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya p. 48)

children.text: yasmādime indriya apramāṇā jaḍāḥ svabhāvena avyākṛtāśva /
children.translated_text: "Since these faculties are not valid measures — inert by nature and indeterminate —

children.text: tasmād ya nirvāṇapathaiva arthikaḥ sa āryamārgeṇa karotu kāryam // SRS_9.24 //
children.translated_text: therefore, whoever seeks the path to <s>nirvāṇa</s> should accomplish [his goal] through the noble path!" // SRS_9.24 //

children.text: pūrvāntu kāyasya avekṣamāṇo naivātra kāyo napi kāyasaṃjñā /
children.translated_text: "Examining the prior [nature] of the body, one finds neither body nor the concept of body there;

children.text: na yatra kāyo napi kāyasaṃjñā asaṃskṛtaṃ gotramidaṃ pravucyati // SRS_9.25 //
children.translated_text: where there is no body and no concept of body — that lineage is called the unconditioned!" // SRS_9.25 //

children.text: nivṛtti dharmāṇa na asti dharmā yeneti nāsti na te jātu asti /
children.translated_text: "Cessation does not apply to <s>dharmas</s>, nor do those <s>dharmas</s> have 'existence' — by what they would have 'non-existence,' they never have 'existence';

children.text: astīti nāstīti ca kalpanāvatāmevaṃ carantāna na duḥkha śāmyati // SRS_9.26 //
children.translated_text: for those who are engrossed in the conceptualizations of 'it exists' and 'it does not exist' — their suffering does not cease!" // SRS_9.26 //

children.text: astīti nāstīti ubhe 'pi antā śuddhī aśuddhīti ime 'pi antā /
children.translated_text: "'It exists' and 'it does not exist' — both are extremes; 'pure' and 'impure' — these too are extremes;

children.text: tasmādubhe anta vivarjayitvā madhye 'pi sthānaṃ na karoti paṇḍitaḥ // SRS_9.27 //
children.translated_text: therefore, having abandoned both extremes, the wise one does not take a stand even in the middle!" // SRS_9.27 //

children.text: astīti nāstīti vivāda eṣa śuddhī aśuddhīti ayaṃ vivādaḥ /
children.translated_text: "'It exists' and 'it does not exist' — this is a dispute; 'pure' and 'impure' — this is a dispute;

children.text: vivādaprāptāna na duḥkha śāmyati avivādaprāptāna duḥkhaṃ nirudhyate // SRS_9.28 //
children.translated_text: for those who have arrived at disputation, suffering does not cease; for those who have arrived at non-disputation, suffering is extinguished!" // SRS_9.28 //

children.text: smṛterupasthānakathāṃ kathitvā manyanti bālā vaya kāyasākṣī /
children.translated_text: "Having spoken a discourse on the foundations of mindfulness, the foolish think: 'We are direct witnesses of the body';

children.text: na kāyasākṣisya ca asti manyanā prahīṇa tasyo pṛthu sarva manyanā // SRS_9.29 //
children.translated_text: but there is no conceit in one who directly witnesses the body — all his manifold conceits have been abandoned!" // SRS_9.29 //

children.text: caturṣu dhyāneṣu kathāṃ kathitvā vadanti bālā vayaṃ dhyānagocarāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Having spoken a discourse on the four <s>dhyānas</s>, the foolish say: 'We are ones whose domain is <s>dhyāna</s>';

children.text: na kleśadhyāyi na ca asti manyanā viditva jñānena madaḥ prahīyate // SRS_9.30 //
children.translated_text: there is no conceit in one who meditates on <s>kleśas</s> [i.e. their cessation] — having understood through knowledge, pride is abandoned!" // SRS_9.30 //

children.text: caturṣu sattveṣu kathāṃ kathitvā vadanti bālā vaya satyadarśinaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Having spoken a discourse on the four truths, the foolish say: 'We are seers of truth';

children.text: (Vaidya 49)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya p. 49)

children.text: na satyadarśisya ca kāci manyanā amanyanā satya jinena deśitā // SRS_9.31 //
children.translated_text: but there is no conceit in a seer of truth — non-conceit is the truth taught by the <s>Jina</s>!" // SRS_9.31 //

children.text: rakṣeta śīlaṃ na ca tena manye śruṇeyya dharmaṃ na ca tena manye /
children.translated_text: "One should guard morality, yet not be conceited thereby; one should hear the <s>Dharma</s>, yet not be conceited thereby;

children.text: yanaiva so manyati alpaprajño tanmūlakaṃ duḥkha vivardhate 'sya // SRS_9.32 //
children.translated_text: for that very thing on which one of little wisdom is conceited — from that root, suffering increases for him!" // SRS_9.32 //

children.text: duḥkhasya mūlaṃ madu saṃnidarśitaṃ sarvajñinā lokavināyakena /
children.translated_text: "The root of suffering has been shown to be pride by the Omniscient One, the Guide of the World;

children.text: madena mattāna duḥkhaṃ pravardhate amanyamānāna dukhaṃ nirudhyate // SRS_9.33 //
children.translated_text: for those intoxicated by pride, suffering increases; for those free from conceit, suffering ceases!" // SRS_9.33 //

children.text: kiyadbahūn dharma paryāpuṇeyyā śīlaṃ na rakṣeta śrutena mattaḥ /
children.translated_text: "What use is it to learn many <s>Dharma</s>-discourses if one does not guard morality, being intoxicated by learning?

children.text: na bāhuśrutyena sa śakyu tāyituṃ duḥśīla yena vrajamāna durgatim // SRS_9.34 //
children.translated_text: He cannot be saved by his learning — the immoral one who proceeds toward an evil rebirth!" // SRS_9.34 //

children.text: sacet punaḥ śīlamadena matto na bāhuśrutyasmi karoti yogam /
children.translated_text: "But if one is intoxicated by the pride of morality and does not apply himself to learning,

children.text: kṣayetva so śīlaphalamaśeṣaṃ puno 'pi sa pratyanubhoti duḥkham // SRS_9.35 //
children.translated_text: the fruit of his morality will be entirely exhausted — and he will again experience suffering!" // SRS_9.35 //

children.text: kiṃcāpi bhāveyya samādhi loke na co vibhāveyya sa ātmasaṃjñām /
children.translated_text: "Even if one cultivates <s>samādhi</s> in this world, yet does not penetrate the perception of self,

children.text: punaḥ prakupyanti kileśu tasya yathodrakasyeha samādhibhāvanā // SRS_9.36 //
children.translated_text: the <s>kleśas</s> will arise in him again — like the <s>samādhi</s>-cultivation of <s>Udraka</s> here!" // SRS_9.36 //

children.text: nairātmyadharmān yadi pratyavekṣate tān pratyavekṣya yadi bhāvayeta /
children.translated_text: "If one examines <s>dharmas</s> of selflessness, and having examined, cultivates them —

children.text: sa hetu nirvāṇaphalasya prāptaye yo anyaheturna sa bhoti śāntaye // SRS_9.37 //
children.translated_text: That is the cause for attaining the fruit of <s>nirvāṇa</s> — any other cause does not lead to peace. // SRS_9.37 //

children.text: yathā naraścauragaṇairupadrutaḥ palāyitumicchati jīvitārthikaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Just as a man beset by a band of thieves, desiring to flee for his life,

children.text: na tasya pādāḥ prabhavanti gacchituṃ gṛhītva caurehi sa tatra hanyate // SRS_9.38 //
children.translated_text: whose feet are unable to carry him away — seized by the thieves, he is slain on the spot. // SRS_9.38 //

children.text: (Vaidya 50)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 50)

children.text: evaṃ naraḥ śīlavihīna mūḍhaḥ palāyitumicchati saṃskṛtātaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Even so, the deluded man devoid of morality, wishing to escape from the conditioned,

children.text: sa śīlahīno na prabhoti gacchituṃ jarāya vyādhyā maraṇena hanyate // SRS_9.39 //
children.translated_text: bereft of morality he is unable to proceed — he is destroyed by old age, disease, and death. // SRS_9.39 //

children.text: yathaiva caurāṇa bahū sahasro nānāmukhehi prakaroti pāpam /
children.translated_text: "Just as thousands of thieves commit evil through many different approaches,

children.text: evaṃ kileśā vividhairmukhebhiryathaiva cauro hani śuklapākṣam // SRS_9.40 //
children.translated_text: even so the <s>kleśas</s> [attack] through various means, just as a thief destroys the bright fortnight. // SRS_9.40 //

children.text: yena sunidhyāptu nirātmaskandhā ākruṣṭhu paribhāṣṭu na śaṅku bhoti /
children.translated_text: "One who has well contemplated the selfless <s>skandhas</s>, who feels no anxiety when abused or reviled —

children.text: sa kleśamārasya vaśaṃ na gacchate yaḥ śūnyatāṃ jānati so na kupyate // SRS_9.41 //
children.translated_text: he does not fall under the power of <s>Māra</s> of the <s>kleśas</s>; he who knows emptiness does not become angry. // SRS_9.41 //

children.text: bahū jano bhāṣati skandhaśūnyatāṃ na ca prajānāti yathā nirātmakāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Many people speak of the emptiness of the <s>skandhas</s>, yet do not truly comprehend how they are selfless;

children.text: te aprajānanta parehi coditāḥ krodhābhibhūtāḥ paruṣaṃ vadanti // SRS_9.42 //
children.translated_text: not understanding, when provoked by others, overcome by anger they speak harshly. // SRS_9.42 //

children.text: yathā naro āturu kāyaduḥkhito bahūhi varṣehi na jātu mucyate /
children.translated_text: "Just as a man who is ill, suffering in body, for many years finds no release —

children.text: sa dīrghagailānyadukhena pīḍitaḥ paryeṣate vaidyu cikitsanārthikaḥ // SRS_9.43 //
children.translated_text: afflicted by the pain of long illness, he searches for a physician, desiring treatment. // SRS_9.43 //

children.text: punaḥ punastena gaveṣatā ca āsādito vaidya vidū vicakṣaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Searching again and again, he finds a skilled and discerning physician;

children.text: kāruṇyatāṃ tena upasthapetvā prayuktu bhaiṣajyamidaṃ niṣevyatām // SRS_9.44 //
children.translated_text: that [physician], having established compassion, applies [the medicine]: 'This remedy should be taken.' // SRS_9.44 //

children.text: gṛhītva bhaiṣajya pṛthuṃ varāṃ varāṃ na sevate āturu yena mucyate /
children.translated_text: "Having received the abundant, excellent medicine, the sick man does not take it — [the medicine] by which he would be freed;

children.text: na vaidyadoṣo na ca bhaiṣajānāṃ tasyaiva doṣo bhavi āturasya // SRS_9.45 //
children.translated_text: it is not the physician's fault, nor the fault of the medicine — it is the fault of that sick man himself. // SRS_9.45 //

children.text: evamiha śāsani pravrajitvā paryāpuṇitvā bala dhyāna indriyān /
children.translated_text: "Even so, having gone forth in this teaching, having learned the powers, <s>dhyānas</s>, and faculties,

children.text: na bhāvanāyāmabhiyukta bhonti ayuktayogīna kuto 'sti nirvṛtiḥ // SRS_9.46 //
children.translated_text: they do not devote themselves to meditation practice — for the unyoked practitioner, how can there be liberation? // SRS_9.46 //

children.text: (Vaidya 51)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 51)

children.text: svabhāvaśūnyāḥ sada sarvadharmā vastuṃ vibhāventi jināna putrāḥ /
children.translated_text: "All <s>dharmas</s> are always empty by nature — the sons of the <s>Jinas</s> perceive their true nature;

children.text: sarveṇa sarvaṃ bhava sarvaśūnyaṃ prādeśikī śūnyatā tīrthikānām // SRS_9.47 //
children.translated_text: existence in its entirety is empty through and through — the emptiness of the <s>tīrthikas</s> is merely partial. // SRS_9.47 //

children.text: na vijña bālehi karonti vigrahaṃ satkṛtya bālān parivarjayanti /
children.translated_text: "The wise do not quarrel with fools — respecting fools, they avoid them;

children.text: mamāntike enti praduṣṭacittā na bāladharmehi karoti saṃstavam // SRS_9.48 //
children.translated_text: 'They come to me with hostile minds' — [the wise one] does not praise the qualities of fools. // SRS_9.48 //

children.text: na vijña bālāna karoti sevanāṃ viditva bālāna svabhāvasaṃtatim /
children.translated_text: "The wise do not associate with fools, knowing the inherent nature of fools' continuum;

children.text: kiyacciraṃ bālu susevito 'pi puno 'pi te bhonti amitrasaṃnibhāḥ // SRS_9.49 //
children.translated_text: however long a fool is well served, they again become like enemies. // SRS_9.49 //

children.text: na vijña bāleṣviha viśvasanti vijñāya bālāna svabhāvadharmatām /
children.translated_text: "The wise do not trust in fools, knowing the natural <s>dharmatā</s> (lawfulness) of fools;

children.text: svabhāvabhinna prakṛtīya bālā na cāsti mitraṃ hi pṛthagjanānām // SRS_9.50 //
children.translated_text: fools are by nature divided in character — there is no true friendship among ordinary people. // SRS_9.50 //

children.text: sahadharmikeno vacanena uktāḥ krodhaṃ ca doṣaṃ ca apratyayaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: "When admonished with words in accordance with <s>Dharma</s>, they display anger, hostility, and distrust —

children.text: prāviṣkaronti imi bāladharmān imamarthu vijñāya na viśvasanti // SRS_9.51 //
children.translated_text: these are the qualities of fools; knowing this fact, [the wise] do not trust them. // SRS_9.51 //

children.text: bālā hi bālehi samaṃ samenti yathā amedhyena amedhyu sārdham /
children.translated_text: "Fools indeed gather together with fools, as filth [mixes] with filth;

children.text: vijñāḥ punarvijñajanena sārdhaṃ samenti sarpiryatha sarpimaṇḍaiḥ // SRS_9.52 //
children.translated_text: but the wise gather with the wise, as clarified butter [mixes] with cream. // SRS_9.52 //

children.text: saṃsāradoṣāṇa apratyavekṣaṇāt karmāṇa vipākamanotarantaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Not examining the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s>, not entering into [reflection on] the ripening of <s>karma</s>,

children.text: buddhāna co vākyamaśraddadhānāste cchedyabhedyasmi caranti bālāḥ // SRS_9.53 //
children.translated_text: not having faith in the words of Buddhas — such fools walk in that which is to be cut and split. // SRS_9.53 //

children.text: sudurlabhaṃ labhya manuṣyalābhaṃ na śilpasthāneṣu bhavanti kovidāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Having obtained the hard-to-obtain human birth, they are not skilled in any craft or occupation;

children.text: (Vaidya 52)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 52)

children.text: daridrabhūtāna dhanaṃ na vidyate ajīvamānāstada pravrajanti // SRS_9.54 //
children.translated_text: reduced to poverty, without wealth, unable to make a living — then they go forth. // SRS_9.54 //

children.text: te pravrajitvā iha buddhaśāsane adhyuṣitā bhontiha pātracīvare /
children.translated_text: "Having gone forth here in the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching, they become attached to bowl and robe;

children.text: te pāpamitrehi parigṛhītāstāṃ nācarante sugatāna śikṣām // SRS_9.55 //
children.translated_text: seized by evil friends, they do not practice the training of the <s>Sugatas</s>. // SRS_9.55 //

children.text: te ātmanaḥ śīlamapaśyamānāścittavyavasthāṃ na labhanti bālāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Not seeing morality in themselves, those fools do not attain stability of mind;

children.text: rātriṃdivaṃ bhonti ayuktayogā na te jugupsanti ca pāpakarmataḥ // SRS_9.56 //
children.translated_text: day and night they remain unyoked in practice — they feel no shame at their evil deeds. // SRS_9.56 //

children.text: kāyena cittena asaṃyatānāṃ na kiṃci vācāya sa jalpitavyam /
children.translated_text: "For those unrestrained in body and mind, nothing should be said about their speech;

children.text: sadā gaveṣanti parasya doṣān aparāddhu kiṃ kena vā codayiṣye // SRS_9.57 //
children.translated_text: they always search for the faults of others — 'Who has committed an offense? With what shall I charge them?' // SRS_9.57 //

children.text: āhāri adhyuṣita bhonti bālā na cāsti mātrajñatu bhojanasmin /
children.translated_text: "Fools become attached to food — they have no sense of moderation in eating;

children.text: buddhasya puṇyehi labhitva bhojanaṃ tasyaiva bālā akṛtajña bhonti // SRS_9.58 //
children.translated_text: obtaining food through the merit of the <s>Buddha</s>, those fools are ungrateful to him. // SRS_9.58 //

children.text: te bhojanaṃ svādurasaṃ praṇītaṃ labdhvā ca bhuñjanti ayuktayogāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Having obtained delicious, refined food of excellent flavor, the unyoked ones consume it;

children.text: teṣāṃ sa āhāru vadhāya bhoti yatha hastipotāna bisā adhautakāḥ // SRS_9.59 //
children.translated_text: that food becomes their destruction — like unwashed lotus roots for young elephants. // SRS_9.59 //

children.text: kiṃ cāpi vidvān matimān vicakṣaṇo bhuñjīta āhāru śuci praṇītam /
children.translated_text: "Though a learned, wise, and discerning one may also eat pure, refined food,

children.text: na caiva adhyuṣita tatra bhoti agṛghnu so bhuñjati yuktayogī // SRS_9.60 //
children.translated_text: he does not become attached to it — without grasping, he eats as one yoked in practice. // SRS_9.60 //

children.text: kiṃ cāpi vidvān matimān vicakṣaṇo ābhāṣate bālu kuto hi svāgatam /
children.translated_text: "Though a learned, wise, and discerning one may address a fool saying 'Welcome!' —

children.text: (Vaidya 53)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 53)

children.text: tatha saṃgṛhītvā priyavadyatāya kāruṇyatāṃ tatra upasthapeti // SRS_9.61 //
children.translated_text: having thus embraced [the fool] with pleasant speech, he establishes compassion there. // SRS_9.61 //

children.text: yo bhoti bālāna hitānukampī tasyaiva bālā vyasanena tuṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: "He who is compassionate and caring toward fools — those very fools are pleased by his misfortune;

children.text: etena doṣeṇa jahitva bālān mṛgovadeko viharedaraṇye // SRS_9.62 //
children.translated_text: because of this fault, having abandoned fools, one should dwell alone in the forest like a deer. // SRS_9.62 //

children.text: ima īdṛśān doṣa viditva paṇḍito na jātu bālehi karoti saṃgatim /
children.translated_text: "Having understood such faults as these, a wise one never associates with fools:

children.text: vihīnaprajñānupasevato me svargāttu hāniḥ kuta bodhi lapsye // SRS_9.63 //
children.translated_text: 'If I associate with those of inferior wisdom, I shall lose even heaven — how then shall I attain awakening?' // SRS_9.63 //

children.text: maitrīvihārī ca bhavanti paṇḍitāḥ karuṇāvihārī muditāvihārī /
children.translated_text: "The wise ones dwell in loving-kindness, dwell in compassion, dwell in sympathetic joy,

children.text: upekṣakāḥ sarvabhaveṣu nityaṃ samādhi bhāvetva spṛśanti bodhim // SRS_9.64 //
children.translated_text: and in equanimity toward all existences always — having cultivated <s>samādhi</s>, they touch awakening. // SRS_9.64 //

children.text: te bodhi buddhitva śivāmaśokāṃ viditva sattvān janavyādhipīḍitān /
children.translated_text: "Having awakened to that auspicious, sorrowless awakening, knowing beings afflicted by the disease of worldly life,

children.text: kāruṇyatāṃ tatra upasthapetvā kathāṃ kathenti paramārthayuktām // SRS_9.65 //
children.translated_text: having established compassion toward them, they speak discourses connected with the ultimate truth. // SRS_9.65 //

children.text: ye tāṃ vijānanti jināna dharmatāmanābhilapyaṃ sugatāna satyam /
children.translated_text: "Those who understand the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of the <s>Jinas</s> — the inexpressible truth of the <s>Sugatas</s> —

children.text: te dharma śrutvā ima evarūpāṃ lapsyanti kṣānti ariyāṃ nirāmiṣām // SRS_9.66 //
children.translated_text: they, having heard such a <s>Dharma</s> as this, will obtain the noble patient acceptance, free from material bait. // SRS_9.66 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje gambhīradharmakṣāntiparivarto nāma navamaḥ || 9 ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth chapter in the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, called the <s>Gambhīradharmakṣāntiparivarta</s> (Chapter on Patient Acceptance of the Profound <s>Dharma</s>). || 9 ||

body.text:
(Vaidya 54)
10 Purapraveśaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 54) Chapter 10: <s>Purapraveśaparivarta</s> (The Chapter on Entering the City). |

body.text: tatra bhagavān punarapi candraprabhaṃ kumārabhūtamāmantrayate sma - tasmāttarhi kumāra pratipattisāro bhaviṣyāmītyevaṃ tvayā kumāra sadā śikṣitavyam | tat kasya hetoḥ? pratipattisārasya hi kumāra bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya na durlabhā bhavatyanuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ, kiṃ punarayaṃ samādhiḥ | atha khalu candraprabhaḥ kumārabhūta utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat - āścaryaṃ bhagavan yāvat subhāṣitā ceyaṃ bhagavatā bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmavavādānuśāsanī sarvabodhisattvaśikṣā deśitā svākhyātā suprajñaptā | sarvatathāgatagocaro 'yaṃ bhagavan yatra abhūmiḥ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ kaḥ punarvādo 'nyatīrthikānām? pratipattisārāśca vayaṃ bhagavan bhaviṣyāmaḥ anapekṣāḥ kāyajīvite ca bhūtvā tathāgatasyānu śikṣiṣyāmahe | tat kasya hetoḥ? śikḥitukāmāśca vayaṃ bhagavaṃstathāgatasya, abhisaṃboddhukāmā vayaṃ bhagavannanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim | arthikā vayaṃ bhagavan anuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ | vidhvaṃsayitukāmāśca vayaṃ bhagavan māraṃ pāpīyāṃsam | mocayitukāmā vayaṃ bhagavan sarvasattvān sarvabhayebhyaḥ sarvaduḥkhebhyaḥ | adhivāsayatu me bhagavān śvastane mama gṛhe bhaktaṃ bhoktuṃ sārdhaṃ bodhisattvagaṇena sārdhaṃ bhikḥusaṃghena cānukampāmupādāya | adhivāsayati sma bhagavāṃścandraprabhasya kumārabhūtasya tūḥṇīṃbhāvena śvastane gṛhe bhaktaṃ bhoktuṃ sārdhaṃ bodhisattvagaṇena bhikḥusaṃghena cānukampāmupādāya | atha khalu candraprabhaḥ kumārabhūto bhagavatastūḥṇīṃbhāvenādhivāsanaṃ viditvā utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakḥiṇīkṛtya bhagavato 'ntikāt prākrāmat ||
body.translated_text: There the Blessed One again addressed <s>Candraprabha</s> the prince: "Therefore, O prince, 'I shall be one for whom practice is essential' — thus should you always train, O prince. Why? For a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> for whom practice is essential, the unsurpassed, perfect awakening is not hard to obtain — how much less this <s>samādhi</s>!" Then <s>Candraprabha</s> the prince, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, and bowing with palms joined toward the Blessed One, said to the Blessed One: "It is wonderful, Blessed One, how well spoken is this instruction and admonishment for <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> by the Blessed One — the entire training of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> has been taught, well proclaimed, well established! This, Blessed One, is the domain of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, wherein all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> have no footing — what need to speak of other sectarians? We shall be, O Blessed One, those for whom practice is essential! Without regard for body or life, we shall train in accordance with the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Why? Because we wish to train under the <s>Tathāgata</s>, O Blessed One; we wish to fully awaken, O Blessed One, to the unsurpassed, perfect awakening; we desire, O Blessed One, the unsurpassed, perfect awakening; we wish to destroy, O Blessed One, <s>Māra</s> the Evil One; we wish to liberate, O Blessed One, all beings from all fears and all sufferings! May the Blessed One consent to take his meal tomorrow at my house, together with the assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and together with the <s>Saṅgha</s> of monks, out of compassion!" The Blessed One consented through silence to take his meal the next day at the house of <s>Candraprabha</s> the prince, together with the assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and the <s>Saṅgha</s> of monks, out of compassion. Then <s>Candraprabha</s> the prince, knowing the Blessed One's consent through his silence, rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, bowed his head at the Blessed One's feet, circumambulated the Blessed One three times, and departed from the Blessed One's presence. ||

body.text:
atha khalu candaprabhaḥ kumārabhūto yena rājagṛhaṃ mahānagaraṃ yena ca svakaṃ niveśanaṃ tenopasamakrāmat | upasaṃkramya candraprabhaḥ svagṛhaṃ prāviśat | praviśya ca tāmeva rātriṃ prabhūtaṃ praṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ svādanīyamabhisaṃskārayati sma | śatarasaṃ ca bhojanaṃ saṃpādya tasyā eva rātryā atyayena rājagṛhaṃ mahānagaraṃ susiktaṃ susaṃmṛṣṭaṃ muktakusumābhikīrṇaṃ gandhaghaṭikānirghūpitamucchritacchatradhvajapatākaṃ (Vaidya 55) dhūpanadhūpitaṃ vitānavitatamavasaktapaṭṭadāmakalāpaṃ sarathyāntarāpaṇamapagatapāṣāṇaḥarkarakaṭhallaṃ vicitrapuṣpābhikīrṇaṃ candanacūrṇābhikīrṇaṃ gavākṣatoraṇaniryūhapañjarajālārdhacandrasamalaṃkṛtaṃ candanānuliptamakārṣīt | sarvāvantaṃ nagaramutpalakumudapadmapuṇḍarīkābhyavakīrṇamakārṣīt | svaṃ ca gṛhaṃ sarvālaṃkāravyūhitamakārṣīt | atha khalu candraprabhaḥ kumārabhūta imānevaṃrupān nagaravyūhān gṛhavyūhān bhojanavyūhān samalaṃkṛtya rājagṛhānmahānagarānniṣkramya yena gṛdhrakūṭaparvato yena bhagavāṃstenopasamakrāmat | upasaṃkramya bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya ekānte 'sthāt | ekānte sthitaḥ candraprabhaḥ kumārabhūto bhagavataḥ kālamārocayāmāsa - kālo bhagavan, kālaḥ sugata, siddhaṃ bhaktaṃ yasyedānīṃ kālaṃ manyase | atha khalu bhagavān utthāyāsanāt kalyameva nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhaṃ paripūrṇena bhikṣuśatasahasreṇa saṃbahulaiśca bodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto 'nekaiśca devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyaśatasahasraiḥ pūjyamāno 'bhiṣṭūyamāno mahatā buddhānubhāvena mahatā buddhaprātihāryeṇa mahatā buddheryāpathena raśmikoṭiniyutaśatasahasrairniścaradbhirnānātūryaśatasahasraiḥ puṣpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaraiḥ pravarṣadbhiryena rājagṛhaṃ mahānagaraṃ tenopasaṃkrāmati sma | candraprabhasya kumārabhūtasya niveśane prakṣiptaśca bhagavatā dakṣiṇaścakraratnasamalaṃkṛtaḥ aparimitakuśalasaṃcitapādaratna indrakīle, atha tāvadeva tasmin mahānagare anekāni āścaryādbhutāni prātihāryāṇi saṃdṛśyante sma | iyamatra dharmatā
| tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Candraprabha</s> the prince approached the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> and his own residence. Having approached, <s>Candraprabha</s> entered his home. Having entered, that very night he prepared abundant, refined food and drink of all kinds, both hard and soft. Having prepared a meal of a hundred flavors, at the passing of that night, he had the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> well sprinkled, well swept, strewn with scattered flowers, perfumed with incense-pots, with raised parasols, banners, and pennants, (Vaidya 55) fumigated with incense, spread with canopies, hung with strips of cloth and garland-clusters, with all streets and markets cleared of stones, gravel, and potsherds, strewn with varied flowers, sprinkled with sandalwood powder, adorned with windows, arches, balconies, lattices, and half-moons, and anointed with sandalwood. He had the entire city strewn with <s>utpalas</s>, <s>kumudas</s>, lotuses, and white lotuses. He had his own house adorned with every ornament. Then <s>Candraprabha</s> the prince, having thus adorned the city, the house, and the food, went forth from the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> and approached <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> mountain where the Blessed One was. Having approached, he circumambulated the Blessed One three times and stood to one side. Standing to one side, <s>Candraprabha</s> the prince announced the time to the Blessed One: "It is time, Blessed One; it is time, <s>Sugata</s>; the meal is ready — may you now consider it the proper time." Then the Blessed One, rising from his seat in the early morning, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, surrounded and attended by the great assembly of monks — a full hundred thousand monks — and by numerous <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, and being worshipped and praised by many hundreds of thousands of gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, humans and non-humans, with the great majesty of a <s>Buddha</s>, with the great miracle of a <s>Buddha</s>, with the great deportment of a <s>Buddha</s>, with hundreds of thousands of <s>niyutas</s> and <s>koṭis</s> of rays emanating, with hundreds of thousands of various musical instruments, and raining down flowers, incense, garlands, unguents, powders, and robes — he approached the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>. The Blessed One placed his right foot, adorned with the <s>cakra</s>-mark, the jewel of his sole accumulated through immeasurable merit, on the threshold of <s>Candraprabha</s> the prince's residence — and at that very moment, in that great city, many wonderful and marvelous miracles became visible. This is the natural order of things here. Here the following was said:

children.text: puravara praviśanti nāyakasmin caraṇavaru sthapitaśca indrakīle /
children.translated_text: "When the Leader enters the excellent city, and his supreme foot is placed upon the threshold — /

children.text: calati vasumatī śirīya tasya pramudita bhonti purottamasmi sattvāḥ // SRS_10.1 //
children.translated_text: the earth trembles by his splendor, and beings in the best of cities become delighted. // SRS_10.1 //

children.text: ye naraḥ kṣudhitāḥ pipāsitā vā na bhavati teṣa jighatsa tasmi kāle /
children.translated_text: 'Those men who are hungry or thirsty — their hunger ceases to exist at that time;

children.text: apagata bhavatī kṣughā pipāsā yada jinu nikṣipatīndrakīli pādam // SRS_10.2 //
children.translated_text: hunger and thirst depart when the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) sets down his <s>Indrakīla</s> (Indra-pillar) foot. // SRS_10.2 //

children.text: tatha puna nara ye bhavanti andhāḥ śrotravihīna anātha alpapuṇyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And those men who are blind, deprived of hearing, helpless, of little merit —

children.text: sarvi pratilabhanti cakṣu śrotraṃ yada jinu nikṣipatīndrakīli pādam // SRS_10.3 //
children.translated_text: all of them regain their eyes and ears when the <s>Jina</s> sets down his <s>Indrakīla</s> foot. // SRS_10.3 //

children.text: yamaviṣaye ye keci bhonti pretāḥ suduḥkhita kheṭasiṃghāṇakabhojanāśāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) there are in <s>Yama</s>'s domain, greatly suffering, hoping for food of phlegm and mucus —

children.text: sarvi sukhita bhonti ābhaspṛṣṭā yada jinu nikṣipatīndrakīli pādam // SRS_10.4 //
children.translated_text: all become happy, touched by radiance, when the <s>Jina</s> sets down his <s>Indrakīla</s> foot. // SRS_10.4 //

children.text: (Vaidya 56)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 56)

children.text: śailaśikharaśṛṅgaparvatāśca tatha varapādapaśālakarṇikārāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Mountain peaks, crests, and ranges, and likewise excellent <s>Śāla</s> trees and <s>Karṇikāra</s> trees —

children.text: sarvi abhinamanti yena buddho yada jinu nikṣipatīndrakīli pādam // SRS_10.5 //
children.translated_text: all bow toward the <s>Buddha</s> when the <s>Jina</s> sets down his <s>Indrakīla</s> foot. // SRS_10.5 //

children.text: sanagaranigamā sasāgarāntā pracali vasuṃdhari ṣaḍvikāra sarvā /
children.translated_text: 'With its cities and towns, bounded by oceans, the entire earth trembles in six ways;

children.text: na bhavati viheṭha kasyapi ceha yada jinu nikṣipatīndrakīli pādam // SRS_10.6 //
children.translated_text: yet there is no harm to anyone here when the <s>Jina</s> sets down his <s>Indrakīla</s> foot. // SRS_10.6 //

children.text: marumanujakumbhāṇḍarākṣasāśca nabhaḥsthita tuṣṭa udagracittāḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Māras</s>, humans, <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, and <s>Rākṣasas</s>, stationed in the sky, delighted, with uplifted minds,

children.text: chatra dhariya ca lokanāyakasya paramaprīṇita janetva bodhichandam // SRS_10.7 //
children.translated_text: hold parasols over the Leader of the World, supremely gladdened, generating the aspiration for <s>bodhi</s>. // SRS_10.7 //

children.text: śrūyati ca manojña vādyaśabdastūryasahasra aghaṭṭitā raṇanti /
children.translated_text: 'Delightful musical sounds are heard; thousands of instruments resound untouched;

children.text: pramuditāstada bhonti sarvasattvā yada jinu nikṣipatīndrakīli pādam // SRS_10.8 //
children.translated_text: all beings become joyful at that time when the <s>Jina</s> sets down his <s>Indrakīla</s> foot. // SRS_10.8 //

children.text: vṛkṣaśatasahasra onamanti sarvi prapuṣpita bhonti tasmi kāle /
children.translated_text: 'Hundreds of thousands of trees bow down; all are in full blossom at that time;

children.text: devaśatasahasra antarīkṣe pūja karonti amānuṣī jinasya // SRS_10.9 //
children.translated_text: hundreds of thousands of gods in the sky offer superhuman worship to the <s>Jina</s>. // SRS_10.9 //

children.text: ṛṣabhagaṇa tadā nadanti hṛṣṭā hayadviradādhipatī pravṛddhakāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Herds of bulls then bellow joyfully; horses and great elephants grow in stature;

children.text: mṛgapatayo nadanti siṃhanādaṃ yada jinu nikṣipatīndrakīli pādam // SRS_10.10 //
children.translated_text: lions roar their lion's roar when the <s>Jina</s> sets down his <s>Indrakīla</s> foot. // SRS_10.10 //

children.text: mahīpataya ye keci bhūmipālā diśividiśāsu ca āgatā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever sovereigns and earth-protectors there are, coming from the directions and intermediate directions —

children.text: dharaṇitali patanti hṛṣṭacittā dṛṣṭu jinasya śirīmimamevarūpām // SRS_10.11 //
children.translated_text: they fall upon the ground with joyful hearts, seeing such splendor of the <s>Jina</s>. // SRS_10.11 //

children.text: anye abhiṣṭuvanti lokanātham apari kṣipanti jinasya puṣpavṛṣṭim /
children.translated_text: 'Others praise the Lord of the World; others shower the <s>Jina</s> with a rain of flowers;

children.text: (Vaidya 57)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 57)

children.text: apari daśanakhāñjaliṃ karitvā aho jinu kāruṇiko bhaṇanti vācam // SRS_10.12 //
children.translated_text: others, making a ten-fingered <s>añjali</s> (gesture of reverence), utter the words: "Oh, the <s>Jina</s> is compassionate!" // SRS_10.12 //

children.text: keci vara kṣipanti muktahārān bahuvidha ābharaṇān janetva prītim /
children.translated_text: 'Some throw excellent pearl necklaces, and various ornaments, generating joy;

children.text: cīvara ratanān kṣipanti anye atuliyu agru jinatva bodhicittam // SRS_10.13 //
children.translated_text: others throw robes and jewels, with incomparable zeal, having generated the <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening). // SRS_10.13 //

children.text: keci vara kṣipanti hemajālaṃ apari punarmukhaphullakaṃ kṣipanti /
children.translated_text: 'Some throw excellent golden nets; others in turn throw face-garlands;

children.text: keci vara kṣipanti hemaniṣkāṃstatha apare parihārakān kṣipanti // SRS_10.14 //
children.translated_text: some throw excellent gold coins; others in turn throw armlets. // SRS_10.14 //

children.text: kaṭakavara kṣipanti keci tatra apari keyūra kṣipanti ratnacitrān /
children.translated_text: 'Some there throw excellent bracelets; others throw arm-bands studded with jewels;

children.text: ambara kusumān kṣipanti anye citta janetva 'siyāṃ vayaṃ pi buddhāḥ' // SRS_10.15 //
children.translated_text: others throw cloth garments and flowers, generating the thought: "May we too become <s>Buddhas</s>!" // SRS_10.15 //

children.text: apari naraḥ kṣipanti hemacitrāṃstatha maṇisūtravarān prasannacittāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Others throw [ornaments] bright with gold, and excellent jeweled garlands, with serene minds;

children.text: keci ca ratanajālakaṃ kṣipanti dvāri yadā sthitu bhoti lokanāthaḥ // SRS_10.16 //
children.translated_text: some throw jeweled nets — when the Lord of the World stands at the gate. // SRS_10.16 //

children.text: paramaduḥkhita ye bhavanti sattvā bahuvidhupadruvu śokaśalya prāptāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Those beings who are greatly suffering, afflicted by many kinds of distress, pierced by the arrow of grief —

children.text: sarvi sukhasamarpitā bhavanti puruṣavarasya śirīya nāyakasya // SRS_10.17 //
children.translated_text: all become endowed with happiness, through the splendor of the Leader, the Bull among Men. // SRS_10.17 //

children.text: parabhṛtaśukasārikāmayūrāstathapi ca sārasacāṣahaṃsakrauñcāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Cuckoos, parrots, <s>sārikā</s> birds, peacocks, likewise <s>sārasa</s> cranes, <s>cāṣa</s> birds, geese, and <s>krauñca</s> herons —

children.text: sarvi dvijagaṇā nabhe sthihitvā paramamanojñarutāni vyāharanti // SRS_10.18 //
children.translated_text: all flocks of birds, standing in the sky, utter the most delightful sounds. // SRS_10.18 //

children.text: pramudita tada bhonti pakṣisaṃghā madhuramanojñarutaṃ pramuñcamānāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The flocks of birds then become joyful, releasing sweet and delightful sounds;

children.text: rāgu tatha samenti doṣamohaṃ ye ca śṛṇanti manojña pakṣiśabdān // SRS_10.19 //
children.translated_text: passion is calmed, likewise hatred and delusion, for those who hear the delightful sounds of the birds. // SRS_10.19 //

children.text: (Vaidya 58)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 58)

children.text: śruṇiya rañjanīya sattvakoṭyaḥ sarvi ca labhanti kṣāntimānulomām /
children.translated_text: 'Hearing and being delighted, <s>koṭīs</s> of beings all attain the conforming patience;

children.text: tāṃśca sugata vyākaroti sarvān bhaviṣyatha yūya jinā anāgatāśca // SRS_10.20 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>Sugata</s> gives predictions to all of them: "You shall be <s>Jinas</s> in the future!" // SRS_10.20 //

children.text: na bhavati kileśu tasmi kāle sarvi sagaurava bhonti dharmarāje /
children.translated_text: 'There are no afflictions at that time; all have reverence for the <s>Dharma</s>-king;

children.text: apagatabhayadoṣamohajālāḥ praṇipatitāḥ sugatamabhiṣṭuvantaḥ // SRS_10.21 //
children.translated_text: free from the net of fear, fault, and delusion, they bow down and praise the <s>Sugata</s>. // SRS_10.21 //

children.text: paśyiya tada rūpa nāyakasya spṛha janayanti varasmi buddhajñāne /
children.translated_text: 'Seeing then the form of the Leader, they generate aspiration for the supreme <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge:

children.text: kada vaya labhe jñānamevarūpam āśayu jñātva jino 'sya vyākaroti // SRS_10.22 //
children.translated_text: "When shall we obtain such knowledge?" Knowing their intention, the <s>Jina</s> gives them predictions. // SRS_10.22 //

children.text: raśmi śatasahasra niścaranti ekaikataḥ sugatasya romakūpāt /
children.translated_text: 'Hundreds of thousands of rays issue forth from each and every hair-pore of the <s>Sugata</s>;

children.text: taduttari yatha gaṅgavālikā vā na pi ca nimittu gṛhītu śakyu tāsām // SRS_10.23 //
children.translated_text: and beyond that, as many as the sands of the Ganges — yet the signs of those [rays] cannot be grasped. // SRS_10.23 //

children.text: sūryaprabha na bhāntiṃ tasmi kāle na pi maṇi nāgni na sarvadevatānām /
children.translated_text: 'The sun's radiance does not shine at that time, nor jewels, nor fire, nor [the light] of all the gods;

children.text: sarvi prabha na bhānti tasmi kāle yada praviśanta puraṃ vibhāti buddhaḥ // SRS_10.24 //
children.translated_text: all radiances do not shine at that time — when the <s>Buddha</s>, entering the city, illuminates all. // SRS_10.24 //

children.text: padmaśatasahasra prādurbhūtā dharaṇitu koṭisahasrapatra śuddhāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Hundreds of thousands of lotuses appear from the ground, with pure <s>koṭī</s>-thousand petals,

children.text: yatra daśabalaḥ sthapeti pādaṃ mārga gataḥ sugato mahāgaṇena // SRS_10.25 //
children.translated_text: wherever the <s>Daśabala</s> (Ten-Powered One) places his foot — the <s>Sugata</s> gone along the road with a great retinue. // SRS_10.25 //

children.text: aśuci kalimalā na bhonti tasmi kāle nagaravaraṃ praviśanti nāyakasmin /
children.translated_text: 'Impurity, dirt, and stain do not exist at that time when the Leader enters the excellent city;

children.text: nagaru surabhi sarvi dhūpanena gandha manojña pravāyate samantāt // SRS_10.26 //
children.translated_text: the city becomes fragrant throughout with incense; a delightful fragrance wafts everywhere. // SRS_10.26 //

children.text: vīthi nagari tada bhoti sarvā apagataloṣṭakaṭhalla sikta gandhaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The streets of the city are then all cleared of rubble and gravel, sprinkled with fragrances;

children.text: (Vaidya 59)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 59)

children.text: puṇya daśalabasya evarūpā vividha vikīrṇa bhavanti muktapuṣpāḥ // SRS_10.27 //
children.translated_text: such is the merit of the <s>Daśabala</s> — various loose flowers are scattered about. // SRS_10.27 //

children.text: yakṣa śatasahasra raudracittāḥ kanakanibhaṃ dvipadendru dṛṣṭva buddham /
children.translated_text: 'Hundreds of thousands of <s>Yakṣas</s> of fierce disposition, seeing the <s>Buddha</s>, the lord of bipeds, golden in hue,

children.text: janayi vipulu nāyakasmi premaṃ śaraṇamupeti ca buddhadharmasaṃghān // SRS_10.28 //
children.translated_text: generate vast love for the Leader and take refuge in the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>. // SRS_10.28 //

children.text: ye ca devaśatasahasra koṭiyo vā upagata sarvi narendradarśanāya /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of gods come to see the Lord of Men,

children.text: varṣati sugatasya puṣpavarṣaṃ gaganatale ca sthihanti muktapuṣpāḥ // SRS_10.29 //
children.translated_text: they rain a shower of flowers upon the <s>Sugata</s>, and stand in the sky with loose flowers. // SRS_10.29 //

children.text: ye manuja kṣipī jinasya puṣpaṃ gaganatale bhavatīti puṣpachatram /
children.translated_text: 'Those humans who throw flowers at the <s>Jina</s> — in the sky they become a canopy of flowers;

children.text: ye puna kusumān kṣipanti devā dharaṇitale stṛta bhonti divyapuṣpāḥ // SRS_10.30 //
children.translated_text: and those gods who throw blossoms — divine flowers are strewn upon the earth. // SRS_10.30 //

children.text: na bhavati kadāci dṛṣṭva tṛptī devamanuṣyakubhāṇḍarākṣasānām /
children.translated_text: 'There is never satiety in seeing [him] for gods, humans, <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, and <s>Rākṣasas</s>;

children.text: yada daśabalu dṛṣṭva lokanāthaṃ pramudita bhonti udagrakalyacittāḥ // SRS_10.31 //
children.translated_text: when they see the <s>Daśabala</s>, the Lord of the World, they become joyful, elated, and of good disposition. // SRS_10.31 //

children.text: na manasi tada bhonti divyapuṣpā na ca puna vismayu jāyate ca tatra /
children.translated_text: 'The divine flowers are not noticed at that time, nor does wonder arise there;

children.text: yada puruṣavarasya kāyu dṛṣṭvā tuṣṭa bhavanti udagra sarvasattvāḥ // SRS_10.32 //
children.translated_text: when they have seen the body of the Bull among Men, all beings become content and elated. // SRS_10.32 //

children.text: brahma daśabalasya dakṣiṇeno tatha puna vāmatu śakra devarājā /
children.translated_text: '<s>Brahmā</s> stands at the <s>Daśabala</s>'s right side, and <s>Śakra</s>, the King of Gods, at his left;

children.text: gaganatalagatā analpa devakoṭyaḥ puruṣavarasya janenti citrikāram // SRS_10.33 //
children.translated_text: gone to the sky, innumerable <s>koṭīs</s> of gods create marvelous displays for the Bull among Men. // SRS_10.33 //

children.text: parivṛta jinu devadānavehi marumanujāna śiriṃ grasitva sarvām /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Jina</s>, surrounded by gods and <s>Dānavas</s>, absorbing all the splendor of <s>Māras</s> and humans,

children.text: dharaṇi kramatalehi citrayanto praviśi puraṃ bhagavānnimantraṇāya // SRS_10.34 //
children.translated_text: adorning the earth with [his] foot-steps, the Blessed One enters the city upon invitation. // SRS_10.34 //

children.text: (Vaidya 60)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 60)

children.text: kusumita anuvyañjanehi kāye yatha gaganaṃ paripūrṇa tārakehi /
children.translated_text: 'With a body blossoming with the minor marks, like the sky filled with stars,

children.text: pratapati sthitu rājamārgi buddhaścandro nabhaḥstha yathaiva pūrṇimāsyām // SRS_10.35 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Buddha</s>, standing on the royal road, blazes like the full moon in the sky. // SRS_10.35 //

children.text: maṇiratanu yathā viśuddhu śreṣṭhaṃ vyapagatadoṣamalaṃ prabhāsamānam /
children.translated_text: 'Like an excellent jewel-body, pure, free from fault and stain, radiant,

children.text: diśi vidiśi pramuñci ābha śuddhāṃ tatha jinu bhāsati sarvalokadhātum // SRS_10.36 //
children.translated_text: releasing pure radiance in all directions — so the <s>Jina</s> illuminates all world-realms. // SRS_10.36 //

children.text: parivṛtu jinu devadānavehi praviśati rājagṛhaṃ narāṇa śreṣṭhaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Jina</s>, surrounded by gods and <s>Dānavas</s>, enters <s>Rājagṛha</s>, the foremost among men;

children.text: dharaṇi kramatalehi citrayanto praviśati candraprabhasya gehi buddhaḥ // SRS_10.37 //
children.translated_text: adorning the earth with [his] foot-steps, the <s>Buddha</s> enters the house of <s>Candraprabha</s>. // SRS_10.37 //

children.text: puruvaru samalaṃkṛtaṃ samantād bahu dhvaja koṭisahasra ucchitātra /
children.translated_text: 'The excellent city, adorned all around, with many thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of banners raised;

children.text: gandhavaravilipta sarvabhūmī sumanaḥprakīrṇa tathaiva vārṣikāram // SRS_10.38 //
children.translated_text: the entire ground anointed with the finest fragrance, strewn with flowers, likewise a shower of rain. // SRS_10.38 //

children.text: yada sugatu kathāṃ katheti nātho vīthigato manujān kṛpāyamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'When the <s>Sugata</s>, the Lord, speaks his discourse while going along the street, having compassion on the people,

children.text: nirmitu jinu tatra nirmiṇitvā vitarati teṣu praṇīta buddhadharmān // SRS_10.39 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Jina</s> creates emanations there, and distributes to them the excellent <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. // SRS_10.39 //

children.text: daśaniyuta jināna nirmitāna kanakanibhā abhirūpa darśanīyā /
children.translated_text: 'Ten <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Jina</s>-emanations, golden in hue, beautiful, pleasing to behold —

children.text: parivṛtu jinu buddhu nirmitehi vitarati śūnyata śānta buddhabodhim // SRS_10.40 //
children.translated_text: surrounded by <s>Buddha</s>-emanations, the <s>Jina</s> distributes the peaceful, empty <s>Buddha-bodhi</s>. // SRS_10.40 //

children.text: prāṇiśatasahasra taṃ śruṇitvā praṇidadhi cittu varāgrabuddhajñāne /
children.translated_text: 'Hundreds of thousands of beings, hearing that, direct their minds to the supreme, excellent <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge:

children.text: kada vaya labhi jñānamevarūpaṃ āśayu jñātva jino 'sya vyākaroti // SRS_10.41 //
children.translated_text: "When shall we obtain such knowledge?" Knowing their intention, the <s>Jina</s> gives them predictions. // SRS_10.41 //

children.text: keci spṛha janenti tatra kāle parama acintiya labdha tehi lābhāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Some generate aspiration at that time — supreme, inconceivable are the gains obtained by them

children.text: (Vaidya 61)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 61)

children.text: yehi jinu nimantrito narendro na ca paryanta sa teṣu dakṣiṇāyāḥ // SRS_10.42 //
children.translated_text: who have invited the <s>Jina</s>, the Lord of Men — and there is no limit to their merit-offerings. // SRS_10.42 //

children.text: keci punarupapādayi sucittaṃ śvo vaya kāruṇikaṃ nimantrayāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Some then generate the good thought: "Tomorrow we shall invite the Compassionate One,

children.text: hitakaramanukampakaṃ prajānāṃ yasya sudurlabhu darśanaṃ bhaveṣu // SRS_10.43 //
children.translated_text: the benefactor and sympathizer of beings, whose sight is rare to obtain in [any] existence." // SRS_10.43 //

children.text: keci sthita niryūhakhoṭake hi subhagu vibhūṣitagātra premaṇīyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Some, standing in balconies and turrets, with beautiful, adorned, lovable forms,

children.text: divya daśabalasya muktapuṣpāṇyavakirate 'gru janitva bodhicittam // SRS_10.44 //
children.translated_text: scatter divine loose flowers upon the <s>Daśabala</s>, generating supreme zeal and the <s>bodhicitta</s>. // SRS_10.44 //

children.text: surucira vara campakasya mālāṃ tatha atimuktaka gandhavarṣikāṃ ca /
children.translated_text: 'Garlands of the finest <s>campaka</s> flowers, likewise <s>atimuktaka</s> and fragrant rain-flowers,

children.text: apari puna kṣipanti paṭṭadāmān parama niruttaru cittu saṃjanitvā // SRS_10.45 //
children.translated_text: others in turn throw silk streamers, having generated the supreme, unsurpassed thought. // SRS_10.45 //

children.text: keci sthita gṛhe gṛhītapuṣpāḥ paramavibhūṣitakāyu cīvarehi /
children.translated_text: 'Some, standing in their houses, holding flowers, with bodies supremely adorned with garments,

children.text: puṣpa vividhu gṛhītva paṭṭadāmān pravarṣi yena jino mahānubhāvaḥ // SRS_10.46 //
children.translated_text: holding various flowers and silk streamers, [throw them] in the direction of the <s>Jina</s> of great power. // SRS_10.46 //

children.text: padumakumudotpalān kṣipanti keci apari kṣipanti viśiṣṭa hemapuṣpān /
children.translated_text: 'They throw <s>padma</s> lotuses, water lilies, and <s>utpalas</s>; some throw distinguished golden flowers;

children.text: maṇiratana kṣipanti keci tasmin apari kṣipanti ca cūrṇa candanasya // SRS_10.47 //
children.translated_text: some throw jewels and gems at him; others throw sandalwood powder. // SRS_10.47 //

children.text: aparimita bhavanti accharīyā atuliya ye na ca śakyu kīrtanāya /
children.translated_text: 'Immeasurable are the wonders, incomparable, which cannot be narrated —

children.text: puravaru praviśanti nāyakasmin bahujanakoṭya sthihiṃsu buddhajñāne // SRS_10.48 //
children.translated_text: when the Leader enters the excellent city, many <s>koṭīs</s> of people become established in <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. // SRS_10.48 //

children.text: abṛha atapāśca dṛṣṭasattyāḥ sudṛśa sudarśana ye ca anya devāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Abṛha</s> (Cloudless), <s>Atapa</s> (Torridless), <s>Dṛṣṭasattya</s> (Clear-Seeing), <s>Sudṛśa</s> (Beautiful-Seeing), <s>Sudarśana</s> (Good-Seeing), and whatever other gods there are,

children.text: tatha punarakaniṣṭha vītarāgā upagata sarvi narendradarśanāya // SRS_10.49 //
children.translated_text: likewise the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> (Highest) gods, free from passion — all have come to see the Lord of Men. // SRS_10.49 //

children.text: (Vaidya 62)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 62)

children.text: tatha śubhamarutāśca aprameyā aparimita śubhā udagracittāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Likewise immeasurable <s>Śubhamarutā</s> (Fair-Breeze) gods, immeasurable <s>Śubhā</s> (Beautiful) gods with elated minds,

children.text: śubhakṛtsna niyutāśca aprameyā upagata paśyitu nāyakaṃ maharṣim // SRS_10.50 //
children.translated_text: immeasurable <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> (All-Beautiful) gods — they have come to see the Leader, the Great Seer. // SRS_10.50 //

children.text: aparimitu tathāpramāṇaābhā tatha puna deva parītta ābha ye ca /
children.translated_text: 'Immeasurable <s>Apramāṇābha</s> (Infinite Radiance) gods, likewise <s>Parīttābha</s> (Limited Radiance) gods,

children.text: bahu niyuta ābhasvarāṇa tasmin upagata paśyitu te 'pi lokanātham // SRS_10.51 //
children.translated_text: many <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Ābhāsvara</s> (Radiant) gods therein — they too have come to see the Lord of the World. // SRS_10.51 //

children.text: bahava śatasahasra pāriṣadyāstatha puna brahmapurohitāḥ prasannāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Many hundreds of thousands of <s>Brahma</s>'s retinue, likewise the serene <s>Brahmapurohitas</s> (Ministers of <s>Brahma</s>),

children.text: bahuśata puna brahmakāyikānāṃ upagata nāyakadarśanāya sarve // SRS_10.52 //
children.translated_text: many hundreds of <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods — all have come to see the Leader. // SRS_10.52 //

children.text: tatha puna paranirmitāpi devāstatha nirmāṇaratiśca śuddhasattvāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Likewise the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods of pure nature,

children.text: pramudita tuṣitātha yāmadevā upagata sarvi namasyamāna buddham // SRS_10.53 //
children.translated_text: the joyful <s>Tuṣita</s> gods and the <s>Yāma</s> gods — all have come, paying homage to the <s>Buddha</s>. // SRS_10.53 //

children.text: tridaśa apu ca śakra devarājā apsarakoṭiśataiḥ sahāgato 'tra /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Trāyatriṃśa</s> (Thirty-three) gods together with <s>Śakra</s>, the King of Gods, accompanied here by hundreds of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Apsarases</s>,

children.text: kusumavarṣa saṃpravarṣamāṇo upagata buddhamunīndradarśanāya // SRS_10.54 //
children.translated_text: showering showers of flowers, have come to see the <s>Buddha</s>, the Lord of Sages. // SRS_10.54 //

children.text: caturi caturdiśāsu lokapālā vaiśravaṇo dhṛtarāṣṭra nāgarājā /
children.translated_text: 'The four World-Protectors of the four directions — <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, the <s>Nāga</s> King,

children.text: virūḍhaku virūpākṣu hṛṣṭacittā upagata sarvi narendra te stuvantā // SRS_10.55 //
children.translated_text: <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, and <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, with joyful hearts — all have come, praising the Lord of Men. // SRS_10.55 //

children.text: ailavila balavanta yakṣarājā parivṛta yakṣaśatehi premajātaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Ailavila</s> (Eḷavila), the powerful <s>Yakṣa</s>-king, surrounded by hundreds of <s>Yakṣas</s>, filled with love,

children.text: gaganatali sthihitva hṛṣṭacittaḥ kṣipati aneka vicitra puṣpavarṣam // SRS_10.56 //
children.translated_text: standing in the sky with a joyful mind, showered manifold and various flower-rains.' // SRS_10.56 //

children.text: apari punarananta māladhārī vividha vicitra gṛhītva mālyagandhān /
children.translated_text: 'And others — infinite garland-bearers, having taken various and diverse garlands and perfumes,

children.text: (Vaidya 63)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 63)

children.text: sarvi saparivāra hṛṣṭacittāḥ puruṣavarasya karonti tatra pūjām // SRS_10.57 //
children.translated_text: all with retinues and joyful minds — performed worship there of the best of men.' // SRS_10.57 //

children.text: bahava śata karoṭapāṇi yakṣā api ca subhūṣi teṣa yakṣakanyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Many hundreds of <s>Yakṣas</s> with bowls in hand, and also their beautifully adorned <s>Yakṣa</s>-maidens,

children.text: sumadhura sumanojña yakṣavādyaistūryaśatehi karonti buddhapūjām // SRS_10.58 //
children.translated_text: with sweet and delightful <s>Yakṣa</s> music — with hundreds of instruments they performed worship of the <s>Buddha</s>.' // SRS_10.58 //

children.text: lalitamadhuragītavāditasmin sukuśalaiḥ saha kinnarīsahasraiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'With graceful, sweet songs and music, together with thousands of skilful <s>Kinnarī</s>-maidens,

children.text: druma upagata gandhamādanāto jinavaru pūjitu kinnarāṇa rājñā // SRS_10.59 //
children.translated_text: coming from the tree on <s>Gandhamādana</s> — the best of <s>Jinas</s> was worshipped by the king of the <s>Kinnaras</s>.' // SRS_10.59 //

children.text: śaṃbara bala vemacitra rāhu dānavakanya sahasrapārivārāḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Śaṃbara</s>, <s>Bala</s>, <s>Vemacitra</s>, <s>Rāhu</s>, with thousands of <s>Dānava</s>-maidens as retinue,

children.text: asuragaṇa maharddhikāśca anye upagata te ratanāni varṣamāṇāḥ // SRS_10.60 //
children.translated_text: and other hosts of mighty <s>Asuras</s> — they approached, showering jewels.' // SRS_10.60 //

children.text: śataniyuta ananta rākṣasānāṃ rākṣasakoṭiśatairupāsyamānāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Hundreds of <s>nayutas</s> of infinite <s>Rākṣasas</s>, attended by hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: pṛthu vividha vicitra muktapuṣpān puruṣavarasya kṣipanti gauraveṇa ||61 ||
children.translated_text: showered manifold, various, and excellent flowers upon the best of men with reverence.' // SRS_10.61 //

children.text: tathapi ca anavataptu nāgarājā paramasuśikṣitāśca nāgakanyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And likewise <s>Anavatapta</s>, the <s>Nāga</s>-king, with supremely well-trained <s>Nāga</s>-maidens,

children.text: tūryaśatasahasra nādayantyo upagata pūjana tatra lokanātham // SRS_10.62 //
children.translated_text: sounding hundreds of thousands of instruments — they approached to worship the Lord of the World.' // SRS_10.62 //

children.text: pañcaśata anavataptu putrā vipulu anuttaru jñāna prārthayantaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Anavatapta</s>'s five hundred sons, aspiring to vast, unsurpassed knowledge,

children.text: svajanaparivṛtā udagra bhūtvā upagata pūjayituṃ svayaṃ svayaṃbhūm // SRS_10.63 //
children.translated_text: surrounded by their own people, elated, approached to worship the Self-Arisen One himself.' // SRS_10.63 //

children.text: tathapi ca apalālu nāgarājā puruṣavarasya kṛtāñjaliḥ praṇamya /
children.translated_text: 'And likewise <s>Apalāla</s>, the <s>Nāga</s>-king, with palms joined, bowing to the best of men,

children.text: (Vaidya 64)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 64)

children.text: vara rucira gṛhītva nāgapuṣpān sthita gagane munirāja satkarontaḥ // SRS_10.64 //
children.translated_text: having taken excellent and beautiful <s>Nāga</s>-flowers, standing in the sky, honoring the King of Sages.' // SRS_10.64 //

children.text: tathapi ca mucilinda nāgarājā prītamanāḥ parituṣṭa harṣajātaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And likewise <s>Mucilinda</s>, the <s>Nāga</s>-king, with a delighted mind, satisfied, filled with joy,

children.text: vividha ratnamauktikaṃ gṛhītvā upagami nāyaku abhikirantu tatra // SRS_10.65 //
children.translated_text: having taken various jewels and pearls, approached to scatter them upon the Leader there.' // SRS_10.65 //

children.text: tathapi ca kāliko 'pi nāgarājā upagatu mukhu tathāgatasya hṛṣṭacittaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And likewise <s>Kālika</s>, the <s>Nāga</s>-king, with joyful mind, approached the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>,

children.text: vara rūcira gṛhītva ratnadāmān puruṣavarasya pūja karitva śreṣṭhām // SRS_10.66 //
children.translated_text: having taken excellent and beautiful jewel-garlands, performing the supreme worship of the best of men.' // SRS_10.66 //

children.text: so 'pi parama gauravaṃ janitvā anusmaramāṇu guṇāṃstathāgatasya /
children.translated_text: 'He too, having generated supreme reverence, recollecting the virtues of the <s>Tathāgata</s>,

children.text: svajanaparivṛtaḥ sanāgasaṃgho bahuvidhu bhāṣati varṇa nāyakasya // SRS_10.67 //
children.translated_text: surrounded by his own people and the assembly of <s>Nāgas</s>, declared the praises of the Leader in manifold ways.' // SRS_10.67 //

children.text: nandu tathā upanandu nāgarājā tatha punastakṣaka kṛṣṇagautamau ca /
children.translated_text: '<s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s>, <s>Nāga</s>-kings, and also <s>Takṣaka</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, and <s>Gautama</s> —

children.text: upagata jinu te namasyamānāḥ praṇipatitāḥ sugatasya pādayorhi // SRS_10.68 //
children.translated_text: they approached the <s>Jina</s>, bowing in salutation, prostrate at the <s>Sugata</s>'s feet.' // SRS_10.68 //

children.text: upagata elapatru nāgarājā parivṛta nāgaśatehi rocamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Elapatra</s>, the <s>Nāga</s>-king, approached, surrounded by hundreds of <s>Nāgas</s>, radiant,

children.text: munivara jinu kāśyapaṃ smaranto svaka upapatti apaśyi akṣaṇeṣu // SRS_10.69 //
children.translated_text: remembering the <s>Jina</s>, the sage <s>Kāśyapa</s>, he saw his own rebirth in the unfavorable states:' // SRS_10.69 //

children.text: aho ahu puri āsi kāṅkṣaprāpto mayi puri cchinnu parittamelapatram /
children.translated_text: '"Alas! Formerly I was one who had attained doubt; a small <s>elapatra</s>-leaf was destroyed by me formerly;

children.text: so ahu upapannu akṣaṇasmin na sukaru dharma vijānituṃ jinasya // SRS_10.70 //
children.translated_text: I was reborn in this unfavorable state — it is not easy to understand the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Jina</s>.' // SRS_10.70 //

children.text: kṣipra ahu jahitva nāgayoniṃ parama jugupsitametu jantukāyam /
children.translated_text: '"Let me quickly abandon the <s>Nāga</s>-birth, this supremely loathsome creature-body,

children.text: (Vaidya 65)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 65)

children.text: dharmamahu vijāni śāntibhāvaṃ puruṣavareṇa ya jñātu bodhimaṇḍe // SRS_10.71 //
children.translated_text: and may I understand the <s>Dharma</s>, the state of peace, that which was known by the best of men at the seat of awakening!"' // SRS_10.71 //

children.text: sāgara ahirājacakravartī parivṛtu nāgatrikoṭisahasraiḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Sāgara</s>, the <s>Cakravartin</s> among serpent-kings, surrounded by three thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Nāgas</s>,

children.text: varuṇa manasvī gṛhītva muktāhārān upagatu te bhagavantu pūjanāya // SRS_10.72 //
children.translated_text: <s>Varuṇa</s>, and <s>Manasvī</s>, having taken pearl-necklaces — they approached to worship the Blessed One.' // SRS_10.72 //

children.text: kṣipta śila jinasya tatra yeno gaganasthitena gṛhītva tasmi kāle /
children.translated_text: 'The stone that was thrown at the <s>Jina</s> — it was caught in mid-air at that time;

children.text: rājagṛhi sa kimpilo 'pi yakṣaḥ purataḥ sthitaḥ sugatasya gauraveṇa // SRS_10.73 //
children.translated_text: in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, that <s>Yakṣa</s> <s>Kimpila</s> too stood before the <s>Sugata</s> with reverence.' // SRS_10.73 //

children.text: alakavatī samagra rājadhānī śūnya abhūṣi na tatra kaści yakṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Alakavatī</s>, the entire capital, became empty — not a single <s>Yakṣa</s> remained there;
