children.translated_text: 'Many <s>nayuta</s>-hundreds, thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> — gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, and <s>Yakṣas</s> stationed throughout the sky —

children.text: sarviṃ spṛha janenti nāyakasmin bhagavatu vāca śruṇitva arthayuktām // SRS_14.26 //
children.translated_text: all generate aspiration toward the Leader, having heard the Blessed One's words endowed with meaning. // SRS_14.26 //

children.text: snigdhamṛdumanojñakālayuktāṃ sumadhura vāca praṇīta premaṇīyām /
children.translated_text: 'Affectionate, gentle, delightful, and timely, exceedingly sweet, refined, and lovable —

children.text: aparimitasvarāṅgasaṃprayuktāṃ hitakara mokṣakarīṃ bahujanasya // SRS_14.27 //
children.translated_text: endowed with infinite vocal qualities — beneficial, liberating for many beings! // SRS_14.27 //

children.text: turiyaśatasahasra aprameyā sumadhura yukta bhaveyurekakāle /
children.translated_text: 'If immeasurable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of musical instruments, exceedingly sweet, were to play at one time,

children.text: (Vaidya 86)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 86)

children.text: divyasvara viśiṣṭa premaṇīyā abhibhavati sugatasya ekavācā // SRS_14.28 //
children.translated_text: with divine sounds, distinguished, and lovable — a single word of the <s>Sugata</s> surpasses them all! // SRS_14.28 //

children.text: dvijagaṇakalaviṅkamañjudhoṣāḥ surucira premaṇīyāḥ sugītaśabdāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Bird-flocks, <s>kalaviṅkas</s>, with lovely voices, most beautiful, lovable, well-sung sounds;

children.text: śaṅkhapaṭahabherivīṇaśabdāḥ kalamapi na labhantiḥ buddhaśabde // SRS_14.29 //
children.translated_text: conch-shells, kettledrums, drums, and <s>vīṇā</s> sounds — not even a fraction do they equal of the <s>Buddha</s>'s voice! // SRS_14.29 //

children.text: parabhṛtaśukaśārikāṇa śabdāstatha punaḥ krauñcamayūrakinnarāṇām /
children.translated_text: 'The sounds of cuckoos, parrots, and <s>sārikā</s> birds, likewise of <s>krauñca</s> herons, peacocks, and <s>Kinnaras</s>,

children.text: ruta ravita ya keci premaṇīyāḥ kalamapi buddhasvarasya nānubhonti // SRS_14.30 //
children.translated_text: whatever cries and calls are lovable — not even a fraction do they compare to the <s>Buddha</s>'s voice! // SRS_14.30 //

children.text: priya madhura manojña premaṇīyāḥ sumadhura śāntagirā praśaṃsanīyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Dear, sweet, delightful, lovable, exceedingly sweet, with peaceful words, praiseworthy —

children.text: sarvi gira prayukta ekakāle giravara harṣaṇiyāstathāgatasya // SRS_14.31 //
children.translated_text: all words uttered at one time — the excellent words of the <s>Tathāgata</s> are cause for rejoicing! // SRS_14.31 //

children.text: suramanujanarendradānavānāṃ sakalabhave tribhave ya asti sattvāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Of gods, humans, lords of men, and <s>Dānavas</s>, whatever beings exist in the entire threefold existence —

children.text: yā prabhā abhavat prabhākarāṇāṃ abhibhavati sugatasya ekaraśmiḥ // SRS_14.32 //
children.translated_text: whatever radiance there was of all luminaries — a single ray of the <s>Sugata</s> surpasses them all! // SRS_14.32 //

children.text: kusumitu sugatasya ātmabhāvaḥ parivṛtu vicitru sarvalakṣaṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Sugata</s>'s body blossoms, surrounded and adorned by all the marks;

children.text: puṇyaśatanirvṛtu accha śuddhaḥ pratapati sarvajage jinasya kāyaḥ // SRS_14.33 //
children.translated_text: produced by hundreds of merits, clear and pure — the <s>Jina</s>'s body blazes throughout the entire world! // SRS_14.33 //

children.text: śaṅkhāna śabda paṇavasughoṣakāṇāṃ bherīṇa śabda tathapi ca kimpalānām /
children.translated_text: 'The sounds of conch-shells, <s>paṇava</s> drums, sweet-sounding drums, kettledrums, and also <s>kimpala</s> instruments —

children.text: sarve ca śabda sumadhura premaṇīyā buddhasya śabde śatima kalāṃ na bhonti // SRS_14.34 //
children.translated_text: all those sweet, lovable sounds do not equal a hundredth fraction of the <s>Buddha</s>'s voice! // SRS_14.34 //

children.text: tūryāṇa koṭiniyutasahasraśabdā āsvādanīya sumadhura divyakalpāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The sounds of <s>koṭī-nayuta</s> thousands of instruments, delectable, exceedingly sweet, divine-like,

children.text: prāmodanīya marugaṇa apsarāṇāṃ buddhasya śabde śatima kalāṃ na bhonti // SRS_14.35 //
children.translated_text: gladdening the hosts of <s>Marus</s> (gods) and <s>Apsarases</s> — they do not equal a hundredth fraction of the <s>Buddha</s>'s voice! // SRS_14.35 //

children.text: (Vaidya 87)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 87)

children.text: krauñcā mayūra parabhṛta cakravākā haṃsāḥ kuṇālā bahuvidhapakṣisaṃghāḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Krauñca</s> herons, peacocks, cuckoos, <s>cakravāka</s> birds, geese, <s>kuṇāla</s> birds, and various flocks of birds —

children.text: ye te saśabdāḥ sumadhura ekakāle buddhasya śabde śatima kalāṃ na bhonti // SRS_14.36 //
children.translated_text: all those sweet-sounding ones together at one time do not equal a hundredth fraction of the <s>Buddha</s>'s voice! // SRS_14.36 //

children.text: nāgāna yakṣāṇa asuramahoragāṇāṃ devendrabrahmamarupatīnāṃ ca śabdāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The sounds of <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the lords of the <s>Marus</s> —

children.text: yāvanta śabdāstribhave manojña kāntā buddhasvarasya kalamapi te na bhonti // SRS_14.37 //
children.translated_text: all the delightful, lovely sounds in the three realms do not equal even a fraction of the <s>Buddha</s>'s voice! // SRS_14.37 //

children.text: yā brahmaṇo vā marupatinaśca ābhā prabhāsvarāṇāṃ maṇiratanāna ābhāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever radiance of <s>Brahmā</s> or of the lords of the <s>Marus</s>, the radiance of the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> (Radiant) [gods], of jewels and gems —

children.text: sarvā ya ābhā vividhamanekarūpāḥ sarvāsta ekā abhibhavi buddharaśmiḥ // SRS_14.38 //
children.translated_text: all radiances of various manifold kinds — a single ray of the <s>Buddha</s> surpasses all of them! // SRS_14.38 //

children.text: kāyena śuddho vacasā manena caiva jñānena śuddhastribhavi anopaliptaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Pure in body, pure in speech and mind, pure in knowledge, unstained in the three realms of existence —

children.text: guṇasārarāśi guṇaratano narendraḥ sarvaguṇehi asamasamaḥ svayaṃbhūḥ // SRS_14.39 //
children.translated_text: a mass of the essence of virtues, a jewel of virtues, O Lord of Men — equal to the unequaled in all virtues, O Self-Arisen One! // SRS_14.39 //

children.text: evaṃ stavitvā daśabala satyavādiṃ vācaṃ prabhāṣi muditamanaḥ kumāraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Thus having praised the <s>Daśabala</s>, the speaker of truth, the prince spoke with a joyful mind:

children.text: pūjitva buddhamatuliyamaprameyaṃ buddho bhaveya yatha iva śākyasiṃhaḥ // SRS_14.40 //
children.translated_text: "Having worshipped the incomparable, immeasurable <s>Buddha</s>, may I become a <s>Buddha</s> just like the Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>!" // SRS_14.40 //

children.text: tasyo viditvā sugatu viśiṣṭa caryāmasaṅgajñānī smitamakaronnarendraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Knowing his distinguished conduct, the <s>Sugata</s>, of unattached knowledge, the Lord of Men, displayed a smile;

children.text: maitreyu pṛcchī daśabalajyeṣṭhaputraṃ kasyārthi etaṃ smitu kṛtu nāyakena // SRS_14.41 //
children.translated_text: <s>Maitreya</s> asked the eldest son of the <s>Daśabala</s>: "For whose sake has this smile been produced by the Leader?" // SRS_14.41 //

children.text: ākampitābhūdvasumati ṣaḍvikāraṃ devāśca nāga gaganasthitā udagrāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The earth trembled in six ways; gods and <s>Nāgas</s>, stationed in the sky, elated,

children.text: prekṣanti buddhaṃ pramudita hṛṣṭacittāstaṃ vyākarohi sugata anābhibhūtaḥ // SRS_14.42 //
children.translated_text: beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, joyful and glad-hearted — "Reveal him, O <s>Sugata</s>, O unconquered one!" // SRS_14.42 //

children.text: abhūmirasmi bhagavatu śrāvakāṇāṃ yatra pravṛttaṃ puruṣavarasya jñānam /
children.translated_text: '"This is beyond the reach of the Blessed One's <s>Śrāvakas</s> — where the knowledge of the Bull among Men operates;

children.text: suviśuddhajñāninnanupamaprajñabhūmi akhilā te smitu kṛtu jina kasya arthe // SRS_14.43 //
children.translated_text: of supremely purified knowledge, on the incomparable ground of wisdom — O <s>Jina</s>, completely, for whose sake did you produce the smile?" // SRS_14.43 //

children.text: (Vaidya 88)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 88)

children.text: pṛcchami daśabalaṃ vināyakaṃ śākyasiṃha dvipadānamuttamam /
children.translated_text: 'I ask the <s>Daśabala</s>, the Guide, the Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>, the supreme among bipeds —'

children.text: jñānapāramiṃ gataṃ prabhākaraṃ rāgadveṣakhilamohasādakam // SRS_14.44 //
children.translated_text: who has gone to the perfection of knowledge, the Illuminator, [in whom] passion, hatred, rigidity, delusion, and obstructions [are destroyed].' // SRS_14.44 //

children.text: kalpakoṭi carito 'si nāyako gaṅgavālukasamāstatottaram /
children.translated_text: 'For <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> you have practiced, O Leader — as many as the sands of the Ganges and beyond;

children.text: eṣamāṇu varabodhimuttamāṃ kasya arthi smitu etu darśitam // SRS_14.45 //
children.translated_text: seeking the supreme, unsurpassed awakening — for whose sake have you displayed this smile?' // SRS_14.45 //

children.text: hastapāda parikṛtta śāstunā putradāra priyajñāti bāndhavān /
children.translated_text: 'Hands and feet were cut off by the Teacher; sons, wives, beloved kinsmen, and relatives [were given up];

children.text: eṣamāṇu varajñānamuttamaṃ ko nu hetu smitadarśane mune // SRS_14.46 //
children.translated_text: seeking the supreme, unsurpassed knowledge — what is the reason for displaying the smile, O Sage?' // SRS_14.46 //

children.text: aśvahastirathapattiyo tvayā dāsadāsimaṇiratna rūpyakam /
children.translated_text: 'Horses, elephants, chariots, and infantry, slaves, maids, gems, jewels, and silver —

children.text: naiva dravyaratanaṃ ca labhyate yanna tyaktu caratā ti cārikām // SRS_14.47 //
children.translated_text: there is no possession or treasure that was not given up while practicing this conduct!' // SRS_14.47 //

children.text: jñānu śreṣṭhu tribhave 'tivartate sarvasattvacariyāṃ prajānase /
children.translated_text: 'Your supreme knowledge transcends the three realms; you know the conduct of all beings;

children.text: dhātucittu adhimuktikovidā kasya arthi smitu etu darśitam // SRS_14.48 //
children.translated_text: skilled in [knowing] elements, minds, and dispositions — for whose sake have you displayed this smile?' // SRS_14.48 //

children.text: kena pūjita narāṇamuttamāḥ kasya vārtha vipulo bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: 'By whom was the best of men worshipped? For whom will there be vast benefit?

children.text: ko ca asya cariyāya grāhakaḥ kasya arthi smitu darśitaṃ mune // SRS_14.49 //
children.translated_text: And who is the practitioner of his conduct? For whose sake have you displayed the smile, O Sage?' // SRS_14.49 //

children.text: ṣaḍvikāra pṛthivī prakampitā padmakoṭya dharaṇītu utthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The earth trembled with six kinds of trembling; <s>koṭis</s> of lotuses arose from the ground,

children.text: koṭipatraparamā prabhāsvarā hemavarṇarucirā manoramā // SRS_14.50 //
children.translated_text: with <s>koṭis</s> of petals, supremely radiant, golden-colored, beautiful, and delightful.' // SRS_14.50 //

children.text: yatrime sthita jinasya aurasā bodhisattva paramā maharddhikāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Those who stand here — the <s>Jina</s>'s own sons, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> supreme and mighty,

children.text: dharmabhāṇaka bahū samāgatāsteṣa kāruṇika pṛcchi nāyakam // SRS_14.51 //
children.translated_text: and many <s>Dharma</s>-preachers who have assembled — the compassionate ones ask the Leader on their behalf.' // SRS_14.51 //

children.text: (Vaidya 89)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 89)

children.text: bheriśaṅkhatuṇavāḥ sughoṣakāstūrya koṭiniyutāḥ pravāditāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Drums, conches, flutes, and sweet-sounding instruments — <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of musical instruments were played;

children.text: teṣa śabda gaganasmi śrūyate yādṛśaḥ sugataghoṣa acintiyaḥ // SRS_14.52 //
children.translated_text: their sound is heard in the sky — such as the inconceivable sound of the <s>Sugata</s>.' // SRS_14.52 //

children.text: haṃsakrauñcakalaviṅkakokilāḥ pakṣisaṃgha bahukāḥ samāgatāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Geese, cranes, <s>kalaviṅkas</s>, cuckoos — great flocks of birds have assembled;

children.text: muñci ghoṣa paramaṃ prabhāsvaraṃ buddhaghoṣakala nānubhonti te // SRS_14.53 //
children.translated_text: they utter a supreme, radiant cry — yet they cannot match the melodious tone of the <s>Buddha</s>'s voice.' // SRS_14.53 //

children.text: kena dāna dama saṃyamaḥ pure kalpakoṭi bahukā niṣevitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'By whom were generosity, restraint, and self-control formerly practiced for many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>?

children.text: kena pūjita narāṇa uttamā kasya arthi smitu etu darśitam // SRS_14.54 //
children.translated_text: By whom was the best of men worshipped? For whose sake have you displayed this smile?' // SRS_14.54 //

children.text: kena pūrvi dvipadendru pṛcchito gauravaṃ paramu saṃjanitvana /
children.translated_text: 'By whom was the supreme among bipeds formerly questioned with supreme reverence?

children.text: buddhabodhi kathameṣa labhyate kasya arthi smitu etu darśitam // SRS_14.55 //
children.translated_text: How is <s>Buddha</s>-awakening to be obtained? For whose sake have you displayed this smile?' // SRS_14.55 //

children.text: yāttikā daśabalā atītakāḥ pratyutpanna sugatā anāgatāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'As many Possessors of the Ten Powers as have passed, and the <s>Sugatas</s> present and yet to come —

children.text: sarva jānasi narāṇamuttamo tena pṛcchami prajāya kāraṇāt // SRS_14.56 //
children.translated_text: you, the best of men, know them all; therefore I ask for the sake of the people.' // SRS_14.56 //

children.text: cittasaṃtati prajāya jānate sarvi prāṇina anantagocarāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'You know the mind-continuity of beings; all living beings are your infinite range;

children.text: yasya yādṛśu narasya āśayastena pṛcchami narāṇamuttamam // SRS_14.57 //
children.translated_text: whatever is the disposition of whatever person — therefore I ask the best of men.' // SRS_14.57 //

children.text: ye caranti cariyāmanuttamāṃ hetuyuktivinayasmi kovidāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Those who practice the unsurpassed conduct, skilled in reasoning, logic, and discipline —

children.text: buddhajñāna kathametu labhyate etadarthi dvipadendru pṛcchiham // SRS_14.58 //
children.translated_text: how is <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge to be obtained? For this purpose I ask the supreme among bipeds.' // SRS_14.58 //

children.text: ye hi dharma sukhumāḥ sudurdṛśāḥ śūnya śānta atulā acintiyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Those subtle <s>dharmas</s> that are hard to see — empty, peaceful, incomparable, inconceivable,

children.text: bhāvitā daśabalāna gocarāsteṣa artha ahu pṛcchi nāyakam // SRS_14.59 //
children.translated_text: cultivated as the range of the Possessors of the Ten Powers — for their meaning I ask the Leader.' // SRS_14.59 //

children.text: (Vaidya 90)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 90)

children.text: yeṣa maitri karuṇā subhāvitā sarvaprāṇiṣu jage acintiyā /
children.translated_text: 'Those whose loving-kindness and compassion are well-cultivated, inconceivable toward all beings in the world,

children.text: sattvasaṃjña na ca yeṣa vartate teṣa arthi dvipadendru pṛcchiyām // SRS_14.60 //
children.translated_text: yet in whom the perception of "being" does not operate — for their sake I ask the supreme among bipeds.' // SRS_14.60 //

children.text: yeṣa jñānamatulamacintiyaṃ teṣa grāhya na kadāci vidyate /
children.translated_text: 'Those whose knowledge is incomparable and inconceivable, for whom there is never anything to be grasped,

children.text: cittagocariya pāramiṃ gatā teṣa arthi ahu nātha pṛcchami // SRS_14.61 //
children.translated_text: who have gone to the perfection of the range of mind — for their sake I ask you, O Protector.' // SRS_14.61 //

children.text: śīlajñānaguṇapāramiṃ gatā tryadhvajñānamatulaṃ bhivartate /
children.translated_text: 'Gone to the perfection of morality, knowledge, and virtues, with incomparable knowledge of the three times,

children.text: naiva tubhya skhalitūpalabhyate kasya arthi smitu etu darśitam // SRS_14.62 //
children.translated_text: in whom no stumbling whatsoever is found — for whose sake have you displayed this smile?' // SRS_14.62 //

children.text: śāriputra aniruddha kolitā ye ca anya sugatasya śrāvakāḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Kolita</s> (Maudgalyāyana), and whatever other <s>Śrāvakas</s> of the <s>Sugata</s> —

children.text: naiva teṣa iha jñānu vartate buddhagocaru ayaṃ nirūttaraḥ // SRS_14.63 //
children.translated_text: even their knowledge does not operate here; this range of the <s>Buddha</s> is unsurpassed.' // SRS_14.63 //

children.text: sarvadharmavaśipāramiṃ gatāḥ sarvaśikṣacariyāya udgatāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Those who have gone to the perfection of mastery over all <s>dharmas</s>, who have risen in the practice of all trainings —

children.text: saṃjanetva karuṇāṃ vināyakā muñca ghoṣa paramārthakovidā // SRS_14.64 //
children.translated_text: having generated compassion, O Guide, utter the voice, O one skilled in the ultimate meaning!' // SRS_14.64 //

children.text: ye 'pi pūrva bahukalpakoṭiyo eva cinti dvipadendru pṛcchitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Those who formerly, for many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, thus reflected and questioned the supreme among bipeds,

children.text: bhaṣyamagru śaraṇaṃ parāyaṇaṃ teṣa adya phala brūhi nāyakā // SRS_14.65 //
children.translated_text: spoken of as foremost, as refuge, as support — declare the fruit of those today, O Leader!' // SRS_14.65 //

children.text: yakṣarākṣasakumbhāṇḍaguhyakāḥ prekṣamāṇa dvipadānamuttamam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, and <s>Guhyakas</s>, gazing upon the best of men,

children.text: sarvi prāñjalisthitāḥ sagauravāḥ śrotu vyākaraṇamagrapudgalān // SRS_14.66 //
children.translated_text: all stand with palms joined and reverence, to hear the prediction of the foremost persons.' // SRS_14.66 //

children.text: (Vaidya 91)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 91)

children.text: bodhisattva bahavo 'dya āgatā ṛddhimanta bahukṣetrakoṭibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Many <s>Bodhisattvas</s> have come today, possessing supernatural powers, from many <s>koṭis</s> of fields;

children.text: jeṣṭhaputra sugatasya aurasāḥ sarvi prāñjalisthitāḥ sagauravāḥ // SRS_14.67 //
children.translated_text: the eldest sons, the <s>Sugata</s>'s own — all stand with palms joined and reverence.' // SRS_14.67 //

children.text: gandhahasti purimādiśā gato 'kṣobhyakṣetra diśi lokaviśrutaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Gandhahasti</s> has come from the eastern direction, renowned in the field of <s>Akṣobhya</s>;

children.text: bodhisattvanayutaiḥ puraskṛtaḥ śākyasiṃhu dvipadendru pṛcchanā // SRS_14.68 //
children.translated_text: preceded by <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, [they ask] the Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>, the supreme among bipeds.' // SRS_14.68 //

children.text: sukhāvatīya varalokadhātuto mahāsthāma prāpta avalokiteśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'From <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, the excellent world-system, <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s> and <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>;

children.text: bodhisattvanayutaiḥ puraskṛtaḥ śākyasiṃhu dvipadendru pṛcchanā // SRS_14.69 //
children.translated_text: preceded by <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, [they ask] the Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>, the supreme among bipeds.' // SRS_14.69 //

children.text: yena pūrva bahukalpakoṭiyo aprameya sugatā upasthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He who formerly, for many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, attended immeasurable <s>Sugatas</s>,

children.text: sāgarāṇa sakalā ca vālikā eṣatā parama jñānamuttamam // SRS_14.70 //
children.translated_text: [for as many kalpas as] all the sands of the oceans — seeking the supreme, unsurpassed knowledge;' // SRS_14.70 //

children.text: sarvabuddhastuta saṃpraśaṃsitaḥ sarvadharmaguṇapāramiṃ gataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Praised and commended by all <s>Buddhas</s>, gone to the perfection of all <s>Dharma</s>-qualities,

children.text: sarvalokadiśatāsu viśruto mañjughoṣa sthitu prāñjalīkṛtaḥ // SRS_14.71 //
children.translated_text: renowned in all directions of all worlds — <s>Mañjughoṣa</s> stands with palms joined.' // SRS_14.71 //

children.text: buddhakṣetraniyutaiścaritvanā sudurlabhamīdṛśakāna darśanam /
children.translated_text: 'Having traveled through <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Buddha</s>-fields — the sight of such ones is extremely rare;

children.text: buddhaputraguṇavat suśikṣitāḥ sarvi prāñjalisthitāḥ sagauravāḥ // SRS_14.72 //
children.translated_text: <s>Buddha</s>-sons, endowed with virtues, well-trained — all stand with palms joined and reverence.' // SRS_14.72 //

children.text: nāsti anya iha kaści bhājanaṃ evarūpi yatha eta sūratāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'There is no other vessel here for [<s>Dharma</s>] of such a kind as these heroes;

children.text: dharmakoṣadhara sarvaśāstunāṃ snigdhabhāva gira muñca nāyakā // SRS_14.73 //
children.translated_text: they hold the <s>Dharma</s>-treasury of all Teachers — utter the voice of tender affection, O Leader!' // SRS_14.73 //

children.text: na hyakāraṇaka jinā vināyakā darśayanti smitamagrapudgalāḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Jinas</s>, Guides, foremost persons do not display a smile without reason;

children.text: muñca ghoṣavara dundubhisvara kasya arthi smitu etu darśitam // SRS_14.74 //
children.translated_text: utter the supreme voice-sound like a drum — for whose sake have you displayed this smile?' // SRS_14.74 //

children.text: (Vaidya 92)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 92)

children.text: haṃsakokilamayūrasārasā meghanāda vṛṣabhāḥ pragarjitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The cries of geese, cuckoos, peacocks, and <s>sārasas</s>, the thunder of clouds, and the roar of bulls,

children.text: divyavādyamadhurāḥ pravāditā vyākarohi gira sattvamocanī // SRS_14.75 //
children.translated_text: divine music sweetly played — speak words that liberate beings!' // SRS_14.75 //

children.text: maitrasaṃjanani premavardhanī jñānadarśani avidyariñcanī /
children.translated_text: '[Words] that generate loving-kindness, that increase love, that reveal knowledge and dispel ignorance,

children.text: arthatīraṇi prajñāvivardhanī kalpakoṭiniyutā viśodhanī // SRS_14.73 //
children.translated_text: that establish meaning, that increase wisdom, that purify for <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>;' // SRS_14.76 //

children.text: viniścitabhāvavibhāvitaduḥkhanirodhapadārthanidarśanī /
children.translated_text: 'That demonstrate the meaning of the cessation of suffering through definitive understanding,

children.text: sarvakutīrthakavādadhvaṃsanī śūnya nisattva nijīva vibhāvani // SRS_14.77 //
children.translated_text: that destroy the doctrines of all wrong paths, that illuminate emptiness, no-self, and no-soul.' // SRS_14.77 //

children.text: puṇyasahasraśatehi alaṃkṛtaḥ buddhasahasraśatehi caritviha /
children.translated_text: 'Adorned by hundreds of thousands of merits, having practiced with hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>,

children.text: devasahasraśatehi susaṃstutaḥ brahmasahasraśatehi namaskṛtaḥ // SRS_14.78 //
children.translated_text: praised by hundreds of thousands of gods, saluted by hundreds of thousands of <s>Brahmās</s>;' // SRS_14.78 //

children.text: rākṣasayakṣakumbhāṇḍaprasādani nāgasuparṇamahoragamocani /
children.translated_text: 'Generating faith in <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>; liberating <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Suparṇas</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s>;

children.text: nityamasaktaprayuktaudīraṇi karmaphalehi śubhehi samudgataḥ // SRS_14.79 //
children.translated_text: always unattached, diligent in utterance — arisen through pure fruits of <s>karma</s>.' // SRS_14.79 //

children.text: ye ca keci jināḥ parinirvṛtā ye ca anāgata ye ca avasthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever <s>Jinas</s> have passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, those yet to come, and those now established —

children.text: sarvi prajānasi saṅgu na te 'stīti sarvaguṇehi samudgata nāyaka // SRS_14.80 //
children.translated_text: you know them all, and there is no attachment in you — O Leader, arisen from all virtues!' // SRS_14.80 //

children.text: bhūtadharā sasamudraparvata sarvi mahī ṣaḍvikāra prakampitā /
children.translated_text: 'The entire earth with its oceans and mountains trembled with six kinds of trembling;

children.text: devagaṇā nabhi puṣpa kṣipanti ca divyu pravāyati gandhu manoramu // SRS_14.81 //
children.translated_text: hosts of gods scatter flowers from the sky, and a divine, delightful fragrance wafts.' // SRS_14.81 //

children.text: hatarāgadoṣatimirā nikhilā pariśuddhaśīla pariśuddhamanāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Free from passion, hatred, and the darkness of all defilements, of pure morality, of pure mind,

children.text: (Vaidya 93)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 93)

children.text: praśānta śūnya animittaratā narasiṃhanādu nada kāruṇikā // SRS_14.82 //
children.translated_text: peaceful, delighting in emptiness and the signless — the compassionate one roars the roar of a man-lion!' // SRS_14.82 //

children.text: pratibhānavanta suviśālayaśā susamāptaprajña tathajñāna jinā /
children.translated_text: 'Eloquent, of vast renown, of perfected wisdom and knowledge, O <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: tava loki nāsti samu kāruṇikā bhaṇa kasyu arthi smitu darśayase // SRS_14.83 //
children.translated_text: in the world there is none equal to you, O Compassionate One — tell us, for whose sake do you display the smile?' // SRS_14.83 //

children.text: kalaviṅkakokilamayūraravāstatha jīvaṃjīvaṃ jīvakamanojñarutāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The cries of <s>kalaviṅkas</s>, cuckoos, peacocks, <s>sārasas</s>, <s>jīvaṃjīvas</s>, and <s>jīvakas</s> — delightful sounds on earth in a single instant —

children.text: rañjanīya śabdu bhuvi ekakṣaṇe kala tena bhonti sugatasya svare // SRS_14.84 //
children.translated_text: are but a fraction of the <s>Sugata</s>'s voice.' // SRS_14.84 //

children.text: bheryo mṛdaṅgapaṇavāśca tathā śaṅkha saveṇu tathā vallariyo /
children.translated_text: 'Drums, <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>, <s>paṇavas</s>, conches, flutes, and <s>vallaris</s> —

children.text: tūryāsahasra siya ekaravāḥ kala nānubhonti sugatasya rute // SRS_14.85 //
children.translated_text: even if thousands of instruments sounded as one — they would be but a fraction of the <s>Sugata</s>'s voice.' // SRS_14.85 //

children.text: tūryasahasra vara divyarutā rañjanīya gīta siya apsarasām /
children.translated_text: 'Thousands of supreme, divine instrumental melodies, the delightful songs of <s>Apsarases</s>,

children.text: sugīti śabdarati saṃjane kala na bhonti sugatasya rute // SRS_14.86 //
children.translated_text: the joy of beautiful songs and sounds — they are but a fraction of the <s>Sugata</s>'s voice.' // SRS_14.86 //

children.text: ekasvarā tu tava lokahitā nānādhimukti svaru niścarati /
children.translated_text: 'Yet your single voice benefits the world — sounds issue forth [suited to] various dispositions;

children.text: ekaiku manyi mama bhāṣi jino brūhi smitaṃ ti kṛtu kasya kṛte // SRS_14.87 //
children.translated_text: each one thinks: "The <s>Jina</s> speaks to me" — tell us, for whose sake have you displayed the smile?' // SRS_14.87 //

children.text: devāna śabda tatha nāgarutā ye cāpi kinnararutā madhurāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The sounds of gods, the voices of <s>Nāgas</s>, the sweet sounds of <s>Kinnaras</s> —

children.text: praśamenti kleśa na kadācidapi buddhasvarāstu sada kleśanudāḥ // SRS_14.88 //
children.translated_text: they never pacify afflictions; but the <s>Buddha</s>'s voice always dispels afflictions.' // SRS_14.88 //

children.text: prītiṃ janeti na ca rāgaratiṃ maitrīṃ janeti na ca doṣamatim /
children.translated_text: 'It generates joy but not delight in passion; it generates loving-kindness but not a mind of hatred;

children.text: prajñāṃ janeti na ca moharatiṃ buddhāna sarva malanāśi svaraḥ // SRS_14.89 //
children.translated_text: it generates wisdom but not delight in delusion — the voice of all <s>Buddhas</s> destroys all defilements.' // SRS_14.89 //

children.text: na bahi ca śabdu pariṣātu prajā sarveṣa chindati sa kāṅkṣaśatān /
children.translated_text: 'His sound does not go beyond the assembly — it cuts hundreds of doubts for all;

children.text: (Vaidya 94)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 94)

children.text: na ca onato na hi ca aunnamato samasaukhyadarśana svaro muninaḥ // SRS_14.90 //
children.translated_text: it is neither lowered nor raised — the Sage's voice shows equal happiness [to all].' // SRS_14.90 //

children.text: bhajyādiyaṃ mahī saśailaraṇā kṣīyate sāgarajalaṃ ca tathā /
children.translated_text: 'This earth with its mountains and forests might break; the ocean's water might be exhausted;

children.text: candro 'tha sūryu dharaṇīṃ prapated giramanyathā na puna bhāṣi jinaḥ // SRS_14.91 //
children.translated_text: the moon and sun might fall to earth — but the <s>Jina</s> never speaks otherwise [than truth].' // SRS_14.91 //

children.text: sarvāṅgavākya pariśuddhagirā siṃhasvarā madhuramañjagirā /
children.translated_text: 'With speech purified in every limb and word, with a lion's voice, with sweet and pleasing speech,

children.text: brahmasvarā sugata kāruṇikā bhaṇa kasya arthi smitu darśayase // SRS_14.92 //
children.translated_text: with <s>Brahmā</s>'s voice, O compassionate <s>Sugata</s> — tell us, for whose sake do you display the smile?' // SRS_14.92 //

children.text: yāvanta sattva iha sarva jage sarveṣa citta carate kuśalaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'However many beings there are in all the world — you are skilled in the minds and conduct of them all;

children.text: ye atītanāgata ye sāṃpratikā bhaṇa kasya arthi smitu darśayase // SRS_14.93 //
children.translated_text: those of the past, future, and present — tell us, for whose sake do you display the smile?' // SRS_14.93 //

children.text: yāvanta kecijjina kāruṇikā jñānasmi sarvi vaśi pāramiṃ gatāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'However many <s>Jinas</s> there are, compassionate, gone to the perfection of mastery in knowledge —

children.text: na ca te jinā vimalacandramukhā nāhaitukaṃ smita sada darśayase // SRS_14.94 //
children.translated_text: those <s>Jinas</s> of stainless moon-like faces never display a smile without a cause.' // SRS_14.94 //

children.text: api kalpakoṭi bhaṇi apratimā yatha gaṅgavālika bhaṇeyya guṇān /
children.translated_text: 'Even if one were to speak for incomparable <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> — as many as the sands of the Ganges — praising the virtues,

children.text: na ca śakyu kīrtitu pramāṇu guṇe bhaṇa kasya arthi smitu darśayase // SRS_14.95 //
children.translated_text: it would not be possible to fully describe the measure of the virtues — tell us, for whose sake have you displayed this smile?' // SRS_14.95 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje smitasaṃdarśanaparivartaścaturdaśaḥ || 14 ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourteenth chapter of the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, called the <s>Smitasaṃdarśana</s> (Displaying the Smile) chapter.

body.text:
(Vaidya 95)
15 Smitavyākaraṇaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 95) Chapter 15: The <s>Smitavyākaraṇa</s> (Prediction through the Smile).

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāṃ maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamābhiḥ sārūpyābhirgāthābhiḥ pratyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, replied to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> with these fitting verses:

children.text: candraprabho eṣa kumārabhūtaḥ saṃstutya buddhamatulīya prītiyā /
children.translated_text: 'This <s>Candraprabha</s>, the prince, having praised the <s>Buddha</s> with incomparable joy,

children.text: bhāṣitva buddhāna viśiṣṭa varṇaṃ praśaṃsanīyaḥ sada kāli bheṣyati // SRS_15.1 //
children.translated_text: having spoken the distinguished praises of the <s>Buddhas</s> — shall always be praiseworthy in the [future] age.' // SRS_15.1 //

children.text: ihaiva co rājagṛhasmi pūrvaṃ dṛṣṭvaiva buddhāna sahasrakoṭayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Right here in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, formerly, having seen thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>,

children.text: sarveṣa cānena jināna antike ayaṃ varaḥ śāntasamādhi pṛcchitaḥ // SRS_15.2 //
children.translated_text: in the presence of all those <s>Jinas</s>, he asked about this supreme, peaceful <s>samādhi</s>.' // SRS_15.2 //

children.text: sarvatra co eṣa mamāsi putro imāṃ caranto varabodhicārikām /
children.translated_text: 'Everywhere he was my son, practicing this supreme conduct of awakening;

children.text: sarvatra cāsīt pratibhānavantaḥ sarvatra cāsīt sada brahmacārī // SRS_15.3 //
children.translated_text: everywhere he was eloquent; everywhere he was always a <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate practitioner).' // SRS_15.3 //

children.text: sa paścime kāli mahābhayānake tvameva sākṣī ajitā mamātra /
children.translated_text: 'In the final, dreadful age — you yourself are my witness, O <s>Ajita</s> (Maitreya) —

children.text: sthihitva śuddhe sada brahmacarye vaistārikaṃ eṣa samādhi kāhite // SRS_15.4 //
children.translated_text: established always in pure celibate conduct, he shall teach this <s>samādhi</s> extensively.' // SRS_15.4 //

children.text: samādhimeṣantu idaṃ praṇītaṃ etena mārgeṇa sa bodhi lapsyate /
children.translated_text: 'Through this <s>samādhi</s>, this excellent [practice], by this very path he shall attain awakening;

children.text: parigṛhīto bahubuddhakoṭibhiḥ pūjāṃ varāṃ kāhiti nāyakānām // SRS_15.5 //
children.translated_text: protected by many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, he shall perform supreme worship of the Leaders.' // SRS_15.5 //

children.text: jñāne sthihitvā ahu vyākaromi candraprabhasyācaritaṃ viśiṣṭam /
children.translated_text: 'Standing in knowledge, I declare — the distinguished conduct of <s>Candraprabha</s>:

children.text: na paścakāle 'sya bhave 'ntarāyo na brahmacaryasya na jīvitasya // SRS_15.6 //
children.translated_text: In the future time, there shall be no obstacle for him — neither to his holy life nor to his life. // SRS_15.6 //

children.text: haste yathā āmalakāni pañca prajānāti buddhasahasrakoṭayaḥ /
children.translated_text: As five myrobalans in the palm of one's hand — he knows thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>;

children.text: (Vaidya 96)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 96)

children.text: taduttare yāttika gaṅgavālikā anāgatā yeṣviya pūjanā hoti // SRS_15.7 //
children.translated_text: and beyond those, as many as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> — the future ones whom he shall worship. // SRS_15.7 //

children.text: devāna nāgāna aśītikoṭayaḥ yakṣāṇa co koṭisahasra saptatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Eighty <s>koṭis</s> of gods and <s>Nāgas</s>, and seventy thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Yakṣas</s> —

children.text: autsukyameṣanti ya paścakāle pūjāṃ karontā dvipadottamānām // SRS_15.8 //
children.translated_text: they come eagerly in future times, worshipping the best of two-footed beings. // SRS_15.8 //

children.text: sa pūja kṛtvā dvipadāna uttamān samudācari jñānamimaṃ niruttaram /
children.translated_text: Having worshipped the best of two-footed beings, he practiced this unsurpassed knowledge;

children.text: sa paścime cocchrayi lokanātho vimalaprabho nāma jino bhaviṣyati // SRS_15.9 //
children.translated_text: in the final [time] he shall rise as Lord of the World — he shall become the Conqueror named <s>Vimalaprabha</s> (Stainless Radiance). // SRS_15.9 //

children.text: idaṃ svakaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ śrutitvā prītisphuṭo āsi kumārabhūtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard this, his own prediction, the prince was bursting with joy;

children.text: candraprabho udgata sapta tāla udānudāneti nabhe sthihitvā // SRS_15.10 //
children.translated_text: <s>Candraprabha</s> rose up seven palm-tree heights, and standing in the sky, uttered exclamations of joy: // SRS_15.10 //

children.text: aho jinā uttamadharmadeśakā vimuktijñānādhipatībale sthitā /
children.translated_text: 'Ah, the Conquerors, supreme <s>Dharma</s>-teachers, established in the power of sovereign liberation-knowledge!

children.text: suniścite uttamajñāni tiṣṭhasi anābhibhūto 'si parapravādibhiḥ // SRS_15.11 //
children.translated_text: You stand firmly in the supreme knowledge, unconquered by proponents of other doctrines! // SRS_15.11 //

children.text: vivarjitā saṅga vimukti sparśitā vibhāvitaṃ vastu bhave na sajjasi /
children.translated_text: Attachment abandoned, liberation touched, true reality cultivated — you are not stuck in existence;

children.text: prapañca sarve sakalā na bhonti te asaṅgajñānaṃ tribhave 'bhivartate // SRS_15.12 //
children.translated_text: all conceptual proliferations (<s>prapañca</s>) whatsoever do not exist for you — unattached knowledge turns in the triple world! // SRS_15.12 //

children.text: sarvaprapañcebhiranopaliptā dṛṣṭiḥ prapañcāḥ sakalāḥ prahīṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: Unstained by all conceptual proliferations, with all views and proliferations abandoned,

children.text: subhāviate mārga niketu nāsti anābhibhūtā aviruddha kenacita // SRS_15.13 //
children.translated_text: the path is well-cultivated, there is no abode — unconquered, unopposed by anyone! // SRS_15.13 //

children.text: niketu traidhātuki nāsti tubhyaṃ oghāśca granthāśca prahīṇa sarve /
children.translated_text: For you there is no abode in the triple realm; all floods (<s>oghas</s>) and bonds (<s>granthas</s>) are abandoned;

children.text: tṛṣṇālatābandhana sarvi chinnā bhava prahīṇo bhavasaṃghi nāsti // SRS_15.14 //
children.translated_text: all the bonds of the creeper of craving are cut — existence is abandoned, attachment to existence is no more! // SRS_15.14 //

children.text: (Vaidya 97)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 97)

children.text: svabhāvu dharmāṇamabhāvu jānase anābhilapyā gira saṃprabhāṣase /
children.translated_text: You know the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s> as non-existent; you speak words that are inexpressible;

children.text: siṃhena vā kroṣṭuka tīrtha nāśitā ye te viparyāsasthitā avidvasu // SRS_15.15 //
children.translated_text: as by a lion the fords of the jackals are destroyed — so too those who dwell in perversions, the ignorant! // SRS_15.15 //

children.text: nidhāna śreṣṭhaṃ mayi labdhamadya dharmaṃ nidhānaṃ sugatena deśitam /
children.translated_text: The supreme treasure has been obtained by me today — the <s>Dharma</s>-treasure taught by the <s>Sugata</s>;

children.text: prahīṇa sarvā vinipātu durgati kāṅkṣā na mehāsti bhaviṣya nāyakaḥ // SRS_15.16 //
children.translated_text: all downfall and bad destinations are abandoned — there is no doubt left; I shall become a Leader! // SRS_15.16 //

children.text: mūrdhasmi pāṇiṃ pratisthāpayitvā suvarṇavarṇaṃ ruciraṃ prabhāsvaram /
children.translated_text: Having placed upon my head a hand — golden-colored, beautiful, and radiant —

children.text: abhiṣiñca bodhāya nararṣabhastaṃ sadevakaṃ loka sthapetva sākṣiṇam // SRS_15.17 //
children.translated_text: consecrate him for awakening, O Bull among Men — making the world with its gods the witness!' // SRS_15.17 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje smitavyākaraṇaparivarto nāma pañcadaśaḥ || 15 ||
body.translated_text: // Thus [ends] the fifteenth chapter of the glorious <s>Samādhirāja</s>, entitled 'The Chapter on the Smile and Prediction' (<s>Smitavyākaraṇaparivarta</s>). // 15 //

body.text:
(Vaidya 98)
16 Pūrvayogaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 98) Chapter 16: <s>Pūrvayogaparivarta</s> (The Chapter on Former Connection). |

children.text: smarāmi pūrvaṃ caramāṇu cārikāṃ siṃhadhvajasya sugatasya śāsane /
children.translated_text: 'I remember of old, while following the course under the teaching of the <s>Sugata</s> <s>Siṃhadhvaja</s> (Lion-Banner) —

children.text: abhūṣi bhikṣu vidu dharmabhāṇako nāmena so ucyati brahmadattaḥ // SRS_16.1 //
children.translated_text: there was a learned monk, a <s>Dharma</s>-reciter, called by name <s>Brahmadatta</s>. // SRS_16.1 //

children.text: ahaṃ tadāsīnmati rājaputro ābādhiko bāḍha gilāna duḥkhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: I was then a prince, severely afflicted, ill, and suffering;

children.text: mahyaṃ ca si ācariyo abhūṣi yo brahmadattastada dharmabhāṇakaḥ // SRS_16.2 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Brahmadatta</s>, that <s>Dharma</s>-reciter, was my teacher. // SRS_16.2 //

children.text: pañcottarā vaidyaśatā anūnakā vyādhiṃ cikitsanti udyuktamānasāḥ /
children.translated_text: Five hundred and five physicians, no fewer, strove with earnest minds to treat my illness;

children.text: vyādhiṃ na śaknanti mama cikitsituṃ sarve mama jñātaya āsi duḥkhitāḥ // SRS_16.3 //
children.translated_text: yet they were unable to cure my illness — all my kinsmen were distressed. // SRS_16.3 //

children.text: śrutvā ca gailānyu sa mahya bhikṣu gilānapṛccho mama antikāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing of my illness, that monk, visiting the sick, came to my presence;

children.text: kṛpāṃ janetvā mama brahmadatto imaṃ samādhiṃ varu tatra deśayī // SRS_16.4 //
children.translated_text: generating compassion for me, <s>Brahmadatta</s> taught this excellent <s>samādhi</s> there. // SRS_16.4 //

children.text: tasya mamā etu samādhi śrutvā utpanna prīti ariyā nirāmiṣā /
children.translated_text: Having heard this <s>samādhi</s> from him, noble, immaterial joy arose in me;

children.text: svabhāvu dharmāṇa prajānamāno ucchvāsi vyādhī tuhu tasmi kāle // SRS_16.5 //
children.translated_text: knowing the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s>, I was relieved of my illness at that very time. // SRS_16.5 //

children.text: dīpaṃkaraḥ so caramāṇu cārikāmabhūṣi bhikṣurvidu dharmabhāṇakaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who was following that course as a learned monk, a <s>Dharma</s>-reciter — he was <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>;

children.text: ahaṃ ca āsīnmatirājaputraḥ samādhijñānena hu vyādhi mocitaḥ // SRS_16.6 //
children.translated_text: and I was the prince, freed from illness through the knowledge of <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_16.6 //

children.text: tasmāt kumārā bahu paścakāle anusmaranto imu pārihāṇim /
children.translated_text: Therefore, O prince, in the future age, remembering this decline,

children.text: sahesi bālāna durukta vākyaṃ dhārentu vācentu imaṃ samādhim // SRS_16.7 //
children.translated_text: endure the harsh words of fools — retain and recite this <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_16.7 //

children.text: (Vaidya 99)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 99)

children.text: bheṣyanti bhikṣu bahu paścakāle lubdhāśca duṣṭāśca asaṃyatāśca /
children.translated_text: There will be many monks in the future age — greedy, corrupt, and undisciplined;

children.text: pāpeccha adhyoṣita pātracīvare pratikṣipiṣyanti imaṃ samādhim // SRS_16.8 //
children.translated_text: of evil wishes, attached to robes and bowls — they will reject this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_16.8 //

children.text: īrṣyālukā uddhata prākaṭendriyāḥ kuleṣu cādhyoṣita lābhakāmāḥ /
children.translated_text: Envious, restless, with unguarded senses, attached to families and desirous of gain,

children.text: prāyogike saṃstavi nitya saṃśritāḥ pratikṣipiṣyanti imaṃ samādhim // SRS_16.9 //
children.translated_text: always relying on elaborate practices and praise — they will reject this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_16.9 //

children.text: hastāṃśca pādāṃśca tatha vidyamānā hāsye ca lāsye ca sadā prayuktāḥ /
children.translated_text: Gesticulating with hands and feet, always engaged in laughter and dancing,

children.text: parasparaṃ kaṇṭhita śliṣyamāṇā grāmeṣu caryāpathi anyu bheṣyati // SRS_16.10 //
children.translated_text: embracing one another neck to neck — their deportment in the villages will be different [from what it should be]. // SRS_16.10 //

children.text: ayuktayogānimi bhonti lakṣaṇāḥ parakumārīṣu ca nitya dhyoṣitāḥ /
children.translated_text: These are the marks of improper engagement — always dwelling with other men's daughters;

children.text: rūpeṇa raktā grathitā bhavanti hiṇḍanti grāmānnigamāṃśca rāṣṭrān // SRS_16.11 //
children.translated_text: attached to beauty, entangled, they wander through villages, towns, and kingdoms. // SRS_16.11 //

children.text: te khādyapeyasmi sadā prayuktā nāṭye ya gīte ca tathaiva vādite /
children.translated_text: They are always engaged in food and drink, in drama, song, and music;

children.text: krayavikraye co sada bhonti utsukāḥ pāne 'pi cādhyoṣita naṣṭalajjāḥ // SRS_16.12 //
children.translated_text: always zealous in buying and selling, addicted even to drinking, having lost all shame. // SRS_16.12 //

children.text: lekhāna piṣyanti ayuktayogāḥ śīlaṃ tatheryāpathu chorayitvā /
children.translated_text: They paint pictures, improperly engaged, having abandoned morality and proper deportment;

children.text: maryāda bhinditva gṛhībhi sārdhaṃ te bhinnavṛttā vitathapratiṣṭhitāḥ // SRS_16.13 //
children.translated_text: breaking boundaries, together with laypeople — they are of broken conduct, established in falsehood. // SRS_16.13 //

children.text: ye karma buddhehi sadā vivarjitāstulamānakūṭe ca sadā prayuktāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those actions always rejected by the <s>Buddhas</s> — engaged in false weights and measures —

children.text: tatkarma kṛtvāna kiliṣṭapāpakān apāyu yāsyanti nihīnakarmāḥ // SRS_16.14 //
children.translated_text: having done such actions, defiled and sinful, those of base deeds will go to the lower realms. // SRS_16.14 //

children.text: prabhūtavittaṃ maṇihemaśaṃkhaṃ gṛhāṃśca jñātīṃśca vihāya pravraji /
children.translated_text: Having abundant wealth — gems, gold, conches — having abandoned homes and relatives to go forth,

children.text: (Vaidya 100)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 100)

children.text: te pravrajitvāniha buddhaśāsane pāpāni karmāṇi sadācaranti // SRS_16.15 //
children.translated_text: having gone forth in the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching, they always perform evil deeds. // SRS_16.15 //

children.text: dhane ca dhānye ca te sārasaṃjñino dhenūśca gāvaḥ śakaṭāni sajjayī /
children.translated_text: Thinking wealth, grain, cows, oxen, and carts are essential —

children.text: kimartha tehi ima keśa choritā śikṣāya yeṣāṃ pratipatti nāsti // SRS_16.16 //
children.translated_text: for what purpose did they shave their heads, when they have no practice of the training? // SRS_16.16 //

children.text: mayā ca pūrve cariyāṃ caritvā suduṣkaraṃ kalpasahasra cīrṇam /
children.translated_text: By me in former times, having practiced extremely difficult conduct for thousands of <s>kalpas</s> —

children.text: ayaṃ ca me śānta samādhireṣito yatteṣa śrutvā tada hāsyu bheṣyati // SRS_16.17 //
children.translated_text: this peaceful <s>samādhi</s> is my cherished [teaching]; yet when they hear it, they will laugh! // SRS_16.17 //

children.text: ciraṃ mṛṣāvādi abrahmacāriṇo apāyanimnāḥ sada kāmalābhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Long-time liars, unchaste, inclined toward the lower realms, always desirous of gain —

children.text: te brahmacārīṇa dhvajaṃ gṛhītvā duḥśīla vakṣyanti na eṣa dharmaḥ // SRS_16.18 //
children.translated_text: having grasped the banner of the celibate, those of broken morality will say: "This is not the <s>Dharma</s>!" // SRS_16.18 //

children.text: bhedāya sthāsyanti ca te parasparaṃ ayuktibhirlābha gaveṣamāṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: They will stand for schism against each other, seeking gain with improper means;

children.text: avarṇa bhāṣitva ta anyamanyaṃ cyutā gamipyanti apāyabhūmim // SRS_16.19 //
children.translated_text: speaking disparagingly of one another, fallen, they will go to the realm of the lower destinies. // SRS_16.19 //

children.text: śataḥsahasreṣu sudurlabhāste kṣāntībalaṃ yeṣu tadā bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: Among hundreds of thousands, exceedingly rare will be those who at that time possess the power of patience;

children.text: ato bahū ye kalahasmi utsukāḥ prapañca kāhinti jahitva kṣāntim // SRS_16.20 //
children.translated_text: far more numerous will be those eager for quarrel, creating proliferations, having abandoned patience. // SRS_16.20 //

children.text: vakṣyanti vācā vaya bodhisattvāḥ śabdo 'pi teṣāṃ vraji deśadeśe /
children.translated_text: They will say in words: "We are <s>Bodhisattvas</s>" — and their reputation will travel from place to place;

children.text: abhūtaśabdena madena mattā vipannaśīlāna kuto 'sti bodhiḥ // SRS_16.21 //
children.translated_text: intoxicated by pride with false reputation — how can there be awakening for those of broken morality? // SRS_16.21 //

children.text: na me śrutaṃ nāpi kadāci dṛṣṭamadhyāśayo yasya viśuddha nāsti /
children.translated_text: I have neither heard nor ever seen that one whose intention is not pure,

children.text: imeṣu dharmeṣu ca nāsti kṣāntiḥ sa lapsyate bodhi kṣipitva dharmān // SRS_16.22 //
children.translated_text: who has no patience in these <s>dharmas</s>, will obtain awakening while rejecting the <s>Dharma</s>. // SRS_16.22 //

children.text: (Vaidya 101)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 101)

children.text: bhītāśca trastāśca gṛhaṃ tyajanti te pravraji dṛḍhatarā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Frightened and terrified, they leave their homes; having gone forth, they become more stubborn;

children.text: viśeṣakāmā vilayaṃ prayānti kṣipitva yānaṃ puruṣottamānām // SRS_16.23 //
children.translated_text: desiring distinction, they go to ruin, having cast away the vehicle of the Supreme among Men. // SRS_16.23 //

children.text: nihīnaprajñā guṇaviprahīnā vakṣyanti doṣaṃ sada agrayāne /
children.translated_text: Of base wisdom, devoid of qualities, they constantly find fault with the supreme vehicle;

children.text: yasmai ca te taccharaṇaṃ prapannāstatraiva ye doṣaśatān vadanti // SRS_16.24 //
children.translated_text: and to the very refuge they have taken — there they speak hundreds of faults. // SRS_16.24 //

children.text: ājīvakā ye bahu pravrajitvā anarthikāḥ sarvasubuddhabodhaye /
children.translated_text: Those who go forth as livelihood-seekers, uninterested in the awakening of all <s>Buddhas</s> —

children.text: te ātmadṛṣṭīya sthihitva bālā uttrasta bheṣyanti śruṇitva śūnyatām // SRS_16.25 //
children.translated_text: those fools, standing in the view of self, will be terrified when they hear of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>). // SRS_16.25 //

children.text: vihāru kṛtvāna ta anyamanyaṃ vyāpādadoṣāṃśca khilaṃ janetvā /
children.translated_text: Making monasteries against one another, generating ill-will, hatred, and obduracy,

children.text: abhyākhya datvā ca paraspareṇa lapsyanti prāmodya karitva pāpakam // SRS_16.26 //
children.translated_text: giving false charges against each other — they will rejoice, having done evil. // SRS_16.26 //

children.text: yaḥ śīlavanto guṇavantu bheṣyati maitrīvihārī sada kṣāntikovidaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who is moral, endowed with qualities, always dwelling in loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), skilled in patience,

children.text: susaṃvṛto mārdavasūrataśca paribhūta so bheṣyati tasmi kāle // SRS_16.27 //
children.translated_text: well-restrained, gentle, and heroic — he will be despised at that time. // SRS_16.27 //

children.text: yo kho punarbheṣyati duṣṭacittaḥ sudāruṇo raudrātihīnakarmā /
children.translated_text: But he who is of corrupt mind, exceedingly cruel, of terrible and base deeds,

children.text: adharmacārī kalahe rataśca sa pūjito bheṣyati tasmi kāle // SRS_16.28 //
children.translated_text: acting unrighteously, delighting in quarrels — he will be honored at that time. // SRS_16.28 //

children.text: ārocayāmi prativedayāmi sacet kumārā mama śraddha gacchasi /
children.translated_text: I declare and proclaim: if, O prince, you place faith in me,

children.text: imāṃ smaritvā sugatānuśāsanīṃ mā jātu viśvastu bhavesi teṣām // SRS_16.29 //
children.translated_text: remembering this teaching of the <s>Sugata</s>, never trust those [corrupt monks]. // SRS_16.29 //

children.text: te tīvrarāgāstatha tīvradoṣāste tīvramohāḥ sada mānamattāḥ /
children.translated_text: They are of intense passion, of intense hatred, of intense delusion, always intoxicated with pride;

children.text: (Vaidya 102)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 102)

children.text: adāntakāyāśca adāntavācaḥ adāntacittāśca apāyanimnāḥ // SRS_16.30 //
children.translated_text: of untamed body, untamed speech, untamed mind — inclined toward the lower realms. // SRS_16.30 //

children.text: ahaṃ ca bhāṣeyya guṇāna varṇān na co guṇān bhikṣu samācareyyā /
children.translated_text: Even if I were to proclaim the praise of qualities, yet monks would not practice those qualities;

children.text: na ghoṣamātreṇa ca bodhi labhyate pratipattisārāṇa na bodhi durlabhā // SRS_16.31 //
children.translated_text: awakening is not obtained by mere sound — for those whose essence is practice, awakening is not hard to obtain.' // SRS_16.31 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje pūrvayogaparivarto nāma ṣoḍaśaḥ || 16 ||
body.translated_text: // Thus [ends] the sixteenth chapter of the glorious <s>Samādhirāja</s>, entitled 'The Chapter on Former Connection' (<s>Pūrvayogaparivarta</s>). // 16 //

body.text:
(Vaidya 103)
17 Bahubuddhanirhārasamādhimukhaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 103) Chapter 17: <s>Bahubuddhanirhārasamādhimukhaparivarta</s> (The Chapter on the <s>Samādhi</s>-Gateway of the Accomplishment of Many <s>Buddhas</s>). |

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstāṃ mahatīṃ sāgaropamāṃ parṣadaṃ dharmakathayā saṃdarśya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya samādāpya utthāyāsanāt prākrāmat | yena ca gṛdhrakūṭaparvatarājastenaiva upasamakrāmat | upasaṃkramya ca prajñapta evāsane nyaṣīdat | bhikṣusaṃghaparivṛto devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyanamaskṛtaḥ sāgaropamāyāṃ parṣadi dhama saṃdeśayati sma | atha khalu candraprabhaḥ kumārabhūto bhagavantaṃ nirgataṃ viditvā aśītyā prāṇikoṭīśataiḥ sārdhaṃ sarvairdevabhūtairanyalokadhātvāgataiśca saṃbahulairbodhisattvamahāsattvaniyutaiḥ sārdhaṃ puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanaṃ gṛhītvā tūryaśatairvādyamānaiśchatradhvajaghaṇṭāpatākābhiratyucchritābhiḥ mahāmālyābhinirhāramādāya bhagavataḥ pūjākarmaṇe yena gṛdhrakūṭaparvato yena ca bhagavāṃstenopajagāma | upetya ca bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya taiḥ puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanaistūryatālāvacaraiḥ pravādyamānairmahatīṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā ekānte nyaṣīdat sagauravaḥ sapratīśo dharmaparipṛcchāyai ||
body.translated_text: Then indeed the Blessed One, having instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened that great ocean-like assembly with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, rose from his seat and departed. He approached the <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) mountain-king. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Surrounded by the assembly of monks, saluted by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, humans, and non-humans, he was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to that ocean-like assembly. Then <s>Candraprabha</s> the prince, having learned that the Blessed One had departed, together with eighty hundred <s>koṭis</s> of beings — all divine beings and those who had come from other world-systems — and together with a great many <s>niyutas</s> of <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, carrying flowers, incense, fragrances, garlands, and unguents, with hundreds of musical instruments being played, with very high parasols, banners, bells, and pennants, bearing a great garland-array, came for the worship of the Blessed One to the <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> mountain and to the Blessed One. Having arrived, he bowed his head at the Blessed One's feet, circumambulated the Blessed One three times, and having performed a great worship with those flowers, incense, fragrances, garlands, unguents, musical instruments, and cymbals being played, sat down to one side, respectful and attentive, for the purpose of asking about the <s>Dharma</s>. ||

body.text:
atha khalu candraprabhaḥ kumārabhūto bhagavantametadavocat - pṛccheyamahaṃ bhagavantaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ kaṃcideva pradeśaṃ sacenme bhagavānavakāśaṃ kuryāt pṛṣṭapraśnavyākaraṇāya | evamukte bhagavāṃścandraprabhaṃ kumārabhūtametadavocat - pṛccha tvaṃ kumāra tathāgatamarhataṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ yad yadevākāṅkṣasi | nityakṛtaste kumāra tathāgatenāvakāśaḥ | evamukte candraprabhaḥ kumārabhūto bhagavantametadavocat - katibhirbhagavan dharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvaḥ imaṃ sarvadharmasvabhāvasamatāvipañcitaṃ samādhiṃ pratilabhate? evamukte bhagavāṃścandraprabhaṃ kumārabhūtametadavocat - caturbhiḥ kumāra dharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvaḥ imaṃ sarvadharmasvabhāvasamatāvipañcitaṃ samādhiṃ pratilabhate | katamaiścaturbhiḥ? iha kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sūrato bhavati suvisaṃvāso dānto dāntabhūmimanuprāptaḥ | sa parairākruṣṭo vā paribhāṣito vā duruktānāṃ durbhāṣitānāṃ vacanapathānāṃ kṣamo bhavatyadhivāsanajātīyaḥ karmadarśī nihatamāno dharmakāmaḥ | anena kumāra prathamena dharmeṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ imaḥ samādhiṃ pratilabhate | punaraparaṃ kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ śīlavān bhavati | pariśuddhaśīlaḥ (Vaidya 104) akhaṇḍaśīlaḥ acchidraśīlaḥ aśabalaśīlaḥ akalmaṣaśīlaḥ acyutaśīlaḥ anāvilaśīlaḥ agarhitaśīlaḥ abhyudgataśīlaḥ aniśritaśīlaḥ aparāmṛṣṭaśīlaḥ anupalambhaśīlaḥ āryapraśastaśīlo vijñapraśastaśīlaḥ | anena kumāra dvitīyena dharmeṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ ima samādhiṃ pratilabhate | punaraparaṃ kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvastraidhātuke uttrastacitto bhavati saṃtrastacitto nirviṇṇacitto niḥsaraṇacittaḥ | anarthikaḥ anabhirataḥ anadhyavasitaḥ anabhiṣaktaḥ | sarvatraidhātuke udvignamānasaḥ | anyatra traidhātukāt sattvāni mocayiṣyāmīti vyāyamate | samudāgacchatyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | anena kumāra tṛtīyena dharmeṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattva imaṃ samādhiṃ pratilabhate | punaraparaṃ kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ śrāddho bhavati | atṛpto bhavati dharmaparyeṣṭyām | bahuśruto bhavati | viśārado bhavati | dharmakāmaśca dharmagurukaḥ | na lābhasatkāraślokaguruko
na jñānagurukaḥ | yathāśrutāṃśca dharmān yathāparyavāptān parebhyaśca vistareṇa deśayati saṃprakāśayati hitavastupūrvagamena cittena na jñātralābhakāmanayā | api tu khalu punaḥ kimitīme sattvā imān dharmān śrutvā avinivartanīyā bhaveyuranuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheriti | anena kumāra caturthena dharmeṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ imaṃ samādhiṃ pratilabhate ||
body.translated_text: Then the prince <s>Candraprabha</s> said to the Blessed One: "I would ask the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, about a certain point, if the Blessed One would grant me the opportunity to answer my question." When this was said, the Blessed One said to the prince <s>Candraprabha</s>: "Ask the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, whatever you wish, prince. The <s>Tathāgata</s> always grants you the opportunity." When this was said, the prince <s>Candraprabha</s> said to the Blessed One: "By how many <s>dharmas</s>, Blessed One, does a <s>Bodhisattva</s> endowed [with them] attain this <s>samādhi</s> which is the detailed exposition of the equality of the own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s>?" When this was said, the Blessed One said to the prince <s>Candraprabha</s>: "By four <s>dharmas</s>, prince, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> endowed [with them] attains this <s>samādhi</s> which is the detailed exposition of the equality of the own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s>. Which four? Here, prince, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> is gentle, easy to live with, tamed, and has attained the ground of the tamed. When reviled or abused by others, he is patient with harsh and ill-spoken words, being of a forbearing nature, seeing [the results of] <s>karma</s>, with pride abandoned, loving the <s>Dharma</s>. By this first <s>dharma</s>, prince, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> endowed [with it] attains this <s>samādhi</s>. Furthermore, prince, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> is morally virtuous — of purified morality, (Vaidya p. 104) unbroken morality, unperforated morality, unspotted morality, unstained morality, unfallen morality, untroubled morality, unblamable morality, lofty morality, unsupported morality, ungrasped morality, non-apprehending morality, morality praised by the noble ones, morality praised by the wise. By this second <s>dharma</s>, prince, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> endowed [with it] attains this <s>samādhi</s>. Furthermore, prince, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> has a mind that is alarmed, frightened, wearied, and seeking escape regarding the three realms. He has no interest in, no delight in, no resolve toward, no attachment to [the three realms]. His mind is distressed regarding the entire three realms. [Yet thinking:] 'I will liberate beings from beyond the three realms!' — he strives. He progresses toward the unsurpassed, perfect awakening. By this third <s>dharma</s>, prince, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> endowed [with it] attains this <s>samādhi</s>. Furthermore, prince, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> is faithful. He is insatiable in the quest for <s>Dharma</s>. He is learned. He is confident. He loves the <s>Dharma</s> and reveres the <s>Dharma</s>. He does not revere gain, honor, and fame, nor does he revere [mere] knowledge. And whatever <s>dharmas</s> he has heard and mastered, he teaches and proclaims them extensively to others, with a mind preceded by benevolence, not with the intention of gaining followers and profit. Rather [he thinks:] 'How may these beings, having heard these <s>dharmas</s>, become irreversible from the unsurpassed, perfect awakening?' By this fourth <s>dharma</s>, prince, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> endowed [with it] attains this <s>samādhi</s>." //

body.text: ebhiḥ kumāra caturbhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattva imaṃ sarvadharmasvabhāvasamatāvipañcitaṃ samādhiṃ pratilabhate kṣipraṃ cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhibhabhisaṃbudhyate | tadanenāpi te kumāra paryāyeṇaivaṃ veditavyaṃ yathāyaṃ samādhirbahubuddhadeśito bahubuddhavarṇito bahubuddhasaṃprakāśito bahubuddhapravicitaḥ | bahūnāṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmantikānmayā pravrajitvā ayaṃ kumāra sarvadharmasvabhāvasamatāvipañcitaḥ samādhirvistareṇa śruta udgṛhītaḥ pṛṣṭo dhārito vācitaḥ pravartito 'raṇabhāvanayā bhāvito bahulīkṛtaḥ parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśitaḥ | atha khalu bhagavānimameva bahubuddhanirhārasamādhimukhaṃ pūrvayogakathānirdeśaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā tasyāṃ velāyāṃ candraprabhasya kumārabhūtasya vistareṇa gāthābhigītena saṃprakāśayati sma -
body.translated_text: "By these four <s>dharmas</s>, prince, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> endowed [with them] attains this <s>samādhi</s> which is the detailed exposition of the equality of the own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s>, and quickly awakens to the unsurpassed, perfect awakening. By this method too, prince, you should understand how this <s>samādhi</s> has been taught by many <s>Buddhas</s>, praised by many <s>Buddhas</s>, proclaimed by many <s>Buddhas</s>, and investigated by many <s>Buddhas</s>. Having gone forth in the presence of many <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones, I, prince, have heard this <s>samādhi</s> which is the detailed exposition of the equality of the own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s> extensively, taken it up, asked about it, retained it, recited it, circulated it, cultivated it through the practice of non-contention, made it abundant, and proclaimed it extensively to others." Then the Blessed One, for the purpose of further illuminating this gateway of <s>samādhi</s> brought forth by many <s>Buddhas</s> — this exposition of the story of former practices — at that time proclaimed it in greater detail to the prince <s>Candraprabha</s> in verses and song —

children.text: smarāmi kalpe 'tuliyāprameye yadā jino āsi svarāṅgaghoṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: "I remember in an incomparable, immeasurable <s>kalpa</s>, when a <s>Jina</s> named <s>Svarāṅgaghoṣa</s> existed;

children.text: svarāṅgaghoṣasya tathāgatasya varṣaṃ śatā ṣaṣṭi abhūṣi āyuḥ // SRS_17.1 //
children.translated_text: the lifespan of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Svarāṅgaghoṣa</s> was one hundred and sixty years. // SRS_17.1 //

children.text: tasyānu buddho parimeṇa āsīt jñāneśvaro nāma narāṇamuttamaḥ /
children.translated_text: "After him, the next <s>Buddha</s> was named <s>Jñāneśvara</s>, the supreme among men;

children.text: jñāneśvarasya dvipadottamasya varṣaṃ sahasrā daśa dvau ca āyuḥ // SRS_17.2 //
children.translated_text: the lifespan of <s>Jñāneśvara</s>, the best of bipeds, was twelve thousand years. // SRS_17.2 //

children.text: jñāneśvarasyāpi pareṇa buddho tejeśvaro nāma jino abhūṣi /
children.translated_text: "And after <s>Jñāneśvara</s>, the <s>Jina</s> named <s>Tejeśvara</s> arose;

children.text: (Vaidya 105)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya p. 105)

children.text: tejeśvarasya dvipadottamasya ṣaṭsaptatī varṣasahasra āyuḥ // SRS_17.3 //
children.translated_text: the lifespan of <s>Tejeśvara</s>, the best of bipeds, was seventy-six thousand years. // SRS_17.3 //

children.text: tejeśvarasyoparatena buddho matīśvaro nāma jino abhūṣi /
children.translated_text: "And after <s>Tejeśvara</s>'s passing, the <s>Jina</s> named <s>Matīśvara</s> arose;

children.text: matīśvarasya dvipadottamasya varṣāṇa koṭī paripūrṇa āyuḥ // SRS_17.4 //
children.translated_text: the lifespan of <s>Matīśvara</s>, the best of bipeds, was a full <s>koṭi</s> of years. // SRS_17.4 //

children.text: matīśvarasyoparatena buddho brahmeśvaro nāma jino abhūṣi /
children.translated_text: "And after <s>Matīśvara</s>'s passing, the <s>Jina</s> named <s>Brahmeśvara</s> arose;

children.text: brahmeśvarasya dvipadottamasya caturdaśo varṣasahasra āyuḥ // SRS_17.5 //
children.translated_text: the lifespan of <s>Brahmeśvara</s>, the best of bipeds, was fourteen thousand years. // SRS_17.5 //

children.text: brahmeśvarasyoparatena buddho agnīśvaro nāma jino abhūṣi /
children.translated_text: "And after <s>Brahmeśvara</s>'s passing, the <s>Jina</s> named <s>Agnīśvara</s> arose;

children.text: agnīśvarasya dvipadottamasya ṣaṣṭistadā varṣasahasra āyuḥ // SRS_17.6 //
children.translated_text: the lifespan of <s>Agnīśvara</s>, the best of bipeds, was then sixty thousand years. // SRS_17.6 //

children.text: agnīśvarasyoparatena buddho brahmānano nāma jino abhūṣi /
children.translated_text: "And after <s>Agnīśvara</s>'s passing, the <s>Jina</s> named <s>Brahmānana</s> arose;

children.text: brahmānanasya dvipadottamasya rātriṃdivā sapta abhūṣi āyuḥ // SRS_17.7 //
children.translated_text: the lifespan of <s>Brahmānana</s>, the best of bipeds, was [only] seven days and nights. // SRS_17.7 //

children.text: brahmānanasyoparatena buddho gaṇeśvaro nāma jino abhūṣi /
children.translated_text: "And after <s>Brahmānana</s>'s passing, the <s>Jina</s> named <s>Gaṇeśvara</s> arose;

children.text: gaṇeśvarasya dvipadottamasya ṣaḍvarṣakoṭyaḥ paripūrṇa āyuḥ // SRS_17.8 //
children.translated_text: the lifespan of <s>Gaṇeśvara</s>, the best of bipeds, was a full six <s>koṭis</s> of years. // SRS_17.8 //

children.text: gaṇeśvarasyoparatena buddho ghoṣeśvaro nāma jino abhūṣi /
children.translated_text: "And after <s>Gaṇeśvara</s>'s passing, the <s>Jina</s> named <s>Ghoṣeśvara</s> arose;

children.text: ghoṣeśvarasya dvipadottamasya navavarṣakoṭyaḥ paripūrṇa āyuḥ // SRS_17.9 //
children.translated_text: the lifespan of <s>Ghoṣeśvara</s>, the best of bipeds, was a full nine <s>koṭis</s> of years. // SRS_17.9 //

children.text: ghoṣeśvarasyoparatena buddho ghoṣānano nāma jino abhūṣi /
children.translated_text: "And after <s>Ghoṣeśvara</s>'s passing, the <s>Jina</s> named <s>Ghoṣānana</s> arose;

children.text: ghoṣānanasya dvipadottamasya daśavarṣakoṭyaḥ paripūrṇa āyuḥ // SRS_17.10 //
children.translated_text: the lifespan of <s>Ghoṣānana</s>, the best of bipeds, was a full ten <s>koṭis</s> of years. // SRS_17.10 //

children.text: (Vaidya 106)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya p. 106)

children.text: ghoṣānanasyoparatena buddhaścandrānano nāma jino abhūṣi /
children.translated_text: "And after <s>Ghoṣānana</s>'s passing, the <s>Jina</s> named <s>Candrānana</s> arose;

children.text: candrānanasya dvipadottamasya rātriṃdivā eka abhūṣi āyuḥ // SRS_17.11 //
children.translated_text: the lifespan of <s>Candrānana</s>, the best of bipeds, was [only] one day and night. // SRS_17.11 //

children.text: candrānanasyoparatena buddhaḥ sūryānano nāma jino abhūṣi /
children.translated_text: "And after <s>Candrānana</s>'s passing, the <s>Jina</s> named <s>Sūryānana</s> arose;

children.text: sūryānanasya dvipadottamasya aṣṭādaśo varṣasahasra āyuḥ // SRS_17.12 //
children.translated_text: the lifespan of <s>Sūryānana</s>, the best of bipeds, was eighteen thousand years. // SRS_17.12 //

children.text: sūryānanasyoparatena buddho brahmānano nāma jino abhūṣi /
children.translated_text: "And after <s>Sūryānana</s>'s passing, the <s>Jina</s> named <s>Brahmānana</s> arose;

children.text: brahmānanasya dvipadottamasya triviṃśati varṣasahasra āyuḥ // SRS_17.13 //
children.translated_text: the lifespan of <s>Brahmānana</s>, the best of bipeds, was twenty-three thousand years. // SRS_17.13 //

children.text: brahmānanasyoparatena buddho brahmaśravo nāma jino abhūṣi /
children.translated_text: "And after <s>Brahmānana</s>'s passing, the <s>Jina</s> named <s>Brahmaśravas</s> arose;

children.text: brahmaśravasya dvipadottamasya aṣṭādaśo varṣasahasra āyuḥ // SRS_17.14 //
children.translated_text: the lifespan of <s>Brahmaśravas</s>, the best of bipeds, was eighteen thousand years. // SRS_17.14 //

children.text: ekasmi kalpasmi ime upannā duve śate lokavināyakānām /
children.translated_text: "In a single <s>kalpa</s>, two hundred guides of the world arose;

children.text: śruṇohi nāmāniha kīrtayiṣye anābhibhūtān tathāgatānām // SRS_17.15 //
children.translated_text: hear! I shall now proclaim the names of those unconquered <s>Tathāgatas</s>! // SRS_17.15 //

children.text: anantaghoṣaśca vighuṣṭaghoṣo vighuṣṭatejaśca vighuḥṭaśabdaḥ /
children.translated_text: "<s>Anantaghoṣa</s>, <s>Vighuṣṭaghoṣa</s>, <s>Vighuṣṭateja</s>, <s>Vighuṣṭaśabda</s>,

children.text: svarāvighuṣṭaśca svarārcitaśca svarāṅgaśūraśca svarāṅgaśabdaḥ // SRS_17.16 //
children.translated_text: <s>Svarāvighuṣṭa</s>, <s>Svarārcita</s>, <s>Svarāṅgaśūra</s>, and <s>Svarāṅgaśabda</s>; // SRS_17.16 //

children.text: jñānābalo jñānaviśeṣagaśca jñānābhibhūrjñānasamudgataśca /
children.translated_text: "<s>Jñānābala</s>, <s>Jñānaviśeṣaga</s>, <s>Jñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Jñānasamudgata</s>,

children.text: jñānārcimān jñānaabhyudgataśca vighuṣṭajñānastatha jñānaśūraḥ // SRS_17.17 //
children.translated_text: <s>Jñānārcimān</s>, <s>Jñānābhyudgata</s>, <s>Vighuṣṭajñāna</s>, and <s>Jñānaśūra</s>; // SRS_17.17 //

children.text: brahmābalo brahmavasuḥ subrahma brahmā ca devastatha brahmaghoṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: "<s>Brahmābala</s>, <s>Brahmavasu</s>, <s>Subrahma</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Brahma-deva</s>, and <s>Brahmaghoṣa</s>,

children.text: (Vaidya 107)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya p. 107)

children.text: brahmeśvaro brahmanarendranetre brahmasvarāṅgaḥ svarabrahmadattaḥ // SRS_17.18 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmeśvara</s>, <s>Brahmanarendra-netra</s>, <s>Brahmasvarāṅga</s>, and <s>Svarabrahma-datta</s>; // SRS_17.18 //

body.text:
tejobalastejavatiḥ sutejāḥ tejeśvarastejasamudrataśca /
tejovibhustejaviniścitaśca | tejasvarendraḥ suvighuṣṭatejāḥ // SRS_17.19 //
body.translated_text: "<s>Tejobala</s>, <s>Tejavatī</s>, <s>Suteja</s>, <s>Tejeśvara</s>, <s>Tejasamudrata</s>, <s>Tejovibhu</s>, <s>Tejaviniścita</s>, <s>Tejasvarendra</s>, and <s>Suvighuṣṭateja</s>; // SRS_17.19 //

children.text: bhīṣmo balo bhīṣmamatiḥ subhīṣmo bhīṣmānano bhīṣmasamudrataśca /
children.translated_text: "<s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Bala</s>, <s>Bhīṣmamati</s>, <s>Subhīṣma</s>, <s>Bhīṣmānana</s>, <s>Bhīṣmasamudrata</s>,

children.text: bhīṣmārci rbhīṣmottaru rbhīṣmaghoṣā ete jinā lokavināyakā 'bhūt // SRS_17.20 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bhīṣmārci</s>, <s>Bhīṣmottara</s>, <s>Bhīṣmaghoṣa</s> — these were the <s>Jinas</s>, guides of the world! // SRS_17.20 //

children.text: gambhīraghoṣaḥ śiridhāraṇaśca viśuddhaghoṣeśvaru śuddhaghoṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: "<s>Gambhīraghoṣa</s>, <s>Śiridhāraṇa</s>, <s>Viśuddhaghoṣeśvara</s>, <s>Śuddhaghoṣa</s>,

children.text: anantaghoṣaḥ suvimuktaghoṣo māro balo māravitrāsanaśca // SRS_17.21 //
children.translated_text: <s>Anantaghoṣa</s>, <s>Suvimuktaghoṣa</s>, <s>Mārabala</s>, and <s>Māravitrāsana</s>; // SRS_17.21 //

children.text: sunetra śuddhānanu netraśuddho viśuddhanetraśca anantanetraḥ /
children.translated_text: "<s>Sunetra</s>, <s>Śuddhānanu</s>, <s>Netraśuddha</s>, <s>Viśuddhanetra</s>, <s>Anantanetra</s>,

children.text: samantanetraśca vighuṣṭanetro netrābhibhūrnetra aninditaśca // SRS_17.22 //
children.translated_text: <s>Samantanetra</s>, <s>Vighuṣṭanetra</s>, <s>Netrābhibhū</s>, and <s>Netra-anindita</s>; // SRS_17.22 //

children.text: dāntottaro dānta sudāntacittaḥ sudānta śāntedriya śāntamānasaḥ /
children.translated_text: "<s>Dāntottara</s>, <s>Dānta</s>, <s>Sudāntacitta</s>, <s>Sudānta</s>, <s>Śāntendriya</s>, <s>Śāntamānasa</s>,

children.text: śāntottaraḥ śāntaśirī praśāntaḥ śāntīya pāraṃgatu śāntiśūraḥ // SRS_17.23 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śāntottara</s>, <s>Śāntaśirī</s>, <s>Praśānta</s>, and <s>Śāntiśūra</s> — one who has gone to the far shore of peace! // SRS_17.23 //

children.text: sthitottaraḥ śānta sudāntacittaḥ sudāntaśāntendriyu śāntamānasaḥ /
children.translated_text: "<s>Sthitottara</s>, <s>Śānta</s>, <s>Sudāntacitta</s>, <s>Sudāntaśāntendriya</s>, <s>Śāntamānasa</s>,

children.text: śāntottaraḥ śāntaśriyā jvalantaḥ śāntapraśānteśvaru śāntiśūraḥ // SRS_17.24 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śāntottara</s>, blazing with the glory of peace, <s>Śāntapraśānteśvara</s>, and <s>Śāntiśūra</s>; // SRS_17.24 //

children.text: gaṇendra gaṇamukhyu gaṇeśvaraśca gaṇābhibhūrgaṇivara śuddhajñānī /
children.translated_text: "<s>Gaṇendra</s>, <s>Gaṇamukhya</s>, <s>Gaṇeśvara</s>, <s>Gaṇābhibhū</s>, <s>Gaṇivara</s>, <s>Śuddhajñānī</s>,

children.text: mahāgaṇendraśca gaṇendraśūro anyo puno gaṇivara pramocakaḥ // SRS_17.25 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mahāgaṇendra</s>, <s>Gaṇendraśūra</s>, and another <s>Gaṇivara</s> the Liberator; // SRS_17.25 //

children.text: dharmadhvajaśco tatha dharmaketuḥ dharmottaro dharmasvabhāva udgataḥ /
children.translated_text: "<s>Dharmadhvaja</s>, <s>Dharmaketu</s>, <s>Dharmottara</s>, <s>Dharmasvabhāva-udgata</s>,

children.text: (Vaidya 108)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya p. 108)

children.text: dharmabalaścaiva sudharmaśūraḥ svabhāvadharmottaraniścitaśca // SRS_17.26 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dharmabala</s>, <s>Sudharmaśūra</s>, and <s>Svabhāvadharmottara-niścita</s>. // SRS_17.26 //

children.text: svabhāvadharmottaraniścitasya aśītikoṭyaḥ sahanāmadheyāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Under <s>Svabhāvadharmottara-niścita</s> there were eighty <s>koṭis</s> [of Buddhas] bearing the same designation;

children.text: dvitīyakalpasmi utpanna nāyakā ete mayā pūjita bodhikāraṇāt // SRS_17.27 //
children.translated_text: in a second <s>kalpa</s>, these guides arose — all worshipped by me for the sake of awakening! // SRS_17.27 //

children.text: svabhāvadharmottaraniścitasya yo nāmadheyaṃ śṛṇute jinasya /
children.translated_text: "Whoever hears the name of the <s>Jina</s> <s>Svabhāvadharmottara-niścita</s>,

children.text: śrutvā ca dhāreti vighuṣṭa nāma sa kṣiprametaṃ labhate samādhim // SRS_17.28 //
children.translated_text: and having heard, retains that proclaimed name — he will quickly attain this <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_17.28 //

children.text: eteṣa buddhān pareṇa anyo acintiye aparimitasmi kalpe /
children.translated_text: "After those <s>Buddhas</s>, in another inconceivable, immeasurable <s>kalpa</s>,

children.text: abhūṣi buddho naradevapūjitaḥ sa nāmadheyena narendraghoṣaḥ // SRS_17.29 //
children.translated_text: a <s>Buddha</s> arose, honored by gods and men — named <s>Narendraghoṣa</s>. // SRS_17.29 //

children.text: narendraghoṣasya tathāgatasya ṣaṭsaptatī varṣasahasramāyuḥ /
children.translated_text: "The lifespan of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Narendraghoṣa</s> was seventy-six thousand years;

children.text: trayaśca koṭīśata śrāvakāṇāṃ yaḥ sannipātaḥ prathamo abhūṣi // SRS_17.30 //
children.translated_text: the first assembly of <s>Śrāvakas</s> numbered three hundred <s>koṭis</s>. // SRS_17.30 //

children.text: ṣaḍabhijña traividya jitendriyāṇāṃ mahānubhāvāna maharddhikānām /
children.translated_text: "[They were] possessors of the six superknowledges, the threefold knowledge, with conquered senses,

children.text: kṣīṇāsravāṇāntimadehadhāriṇāṃ saṃghastadā āsi prabhākarasya // SRS_17.31 //
children.translated_text: of great might and great supernatural power, with defilements exhausted, bearers of their final body — such was the <s>Saṃgha</s> of <s>Prabhākara</s> at that time. // SRS_17.31 //

children.text: aśīti koṭīniyutā sahasrā yo bodhisattvāna gaṇo abhūṣi /
children.translated_text: "There were eighty <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in that assembly —

children.text: gambhīrabuddhīna viśāradānāṃ mahānubhāvāna maharddhikānām // SRS_17.32 //
children.translated_text: of profound intellect, confident, of great might, and great supernatural power; // SRS_17.32 //

children.text: abhijñaprāptāḥ pratibhānavanto gatigatāḥ sarvita śunyatāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: "having attained the superknowledges, eloquent, having gone the full course of emptiness;

children.text: ṛddhīya gacchanti te kṣetrakoṭiyo tatottare yāttika gaṅgavālukāḥ // SRS_17.33 //
children.translated_text: by supernatural power they travel to <s>koṭis</s> of fields — beyond that, as many as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>! // SRS_17.33 //

children.text: (Vaidya 109)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya p. 109)

children.text: pṛcchitva praśnaṃ dvipadānanuttamān punenti tasyaiva jinasya antike /
children.translated_text: "Having asked questions of the supreme among bipeds, they return to the presence of that very <s>Jina</s>;

children.text: sūtrāntanirhāraniruktikovidā ālokabhūtā vicaranti medinīm // SRS_17.34 //
children.translated_text: skilled in the elucidation and etymology of <s>sūtras</s>, they walk the earth as beacons of light! // SRS_17.34 //

children.text: sattvānamarthāya caranti cārikāṃ mahānubhāvāḥ sugatasya putrāḥ /
children.translated_text: "For the sake of beings they wander on their journey — these sons of the <s>Sugata</s> of great might;

children.text: na kāmahetoḥ prakaronti pāpaṃ devā pi teṣāṃ spṛha saṃjanenti // SRS_17.35 //
children.translated_text: they do not commit evil for the sake of pleasure — even gods generate longing for them!" // SRS_17.35 //

children.text: anarthikā bhavagatiṣu na niśritāḥ samāhitā dhyānavihāragocarāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Desiring nothing in the courses of existence, unattached, concentrated, dwelling in the domain of <s>dhyāna</s>,

children.text: viniścitārthāśca viśāradāśca nirāmagandhāḥ sada brahmacāriṇaḥ // SRS_17.36 //
