children.translated_text: seventy-six <s>koṭis</s> of beings who heard this <s>sūtra</s>;' // SRS_18.48 //

children.text: te 'pi vyākṛta buddhena drakṣyante lokanāyakān /
children.translated_text: 'they too were predicted by the <s>Buddha</s> — they shall see Lords of the World

children.text: yathā vāluka gaṅgāyāścaranto bodhicārikām // SRS_18.49 //
children.translated_text: as many as the sands of the Ganges while practicing the conduct of awakening.' // SRS_18.49 //

children.text: sarveṣāṃ pūja kāhinti buddhajñānagaveṣakāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'They shall perform worship of all [those Buddhas], seekers of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge;

children.text: tatra tatra śruṇiṣyanti idaṃ sūtraṃ niruttaram // SRS_18.50 //
children.translated_text: and everywhere they shall hear this unsurpassed <s>sūtra</s>.' // SRS_18.50 //

children.text: aśītyā kalyakoṭībhi bheṣyante lokanāyakāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In eighty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, they shall become Lords of the World —

children.text: sarve ekatra kalpe 'smiṃ hitaiṣī anukampakāḥ // SRS_18.51 //
children.translated_text: all in this very <s>kalpa</s>, benevolent and compassionate.' // SRS_18.51 //

children.text: maitreyasya ca buddhasya pūjāṃ kṛtvā niruttarām /
children.translated_text: 'Having performed unsurpassed worship of the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Maitreya</s>,

children.text: saddharma śreṣṭhaṃ dhāritvā gamiṣyanti sukhāvatīm // SRS_18.52 //
children.translated_text: and having upheld the supreme true <s>Dharma</s>, they shall go to <s>Sukhāvatī</s>.' // SRS_18.52 //

children.text: yatrāsau virajo buddho amitāyustathāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Where that dustless <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Amitāyus</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, [dwells] —

children.text: tasya pūjāṃ kariṣyanti agrabodhīya kāraṇāt // SRS_18.53 //
children.translated_text: they shall perform worship of him for the sake of supreme awakening.' // SRS_18.53 //

children.text: trisaptatirasaṃkhyeyā kalpā ye ca anāgatāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For seventy-three incalculable <s>kalpas</s> yet to come,

children.text: na durgatiṃ gamiṣyanti śrutvedaṃ sūtramuttamam // SRS_18.54 //
children.translated_text: they shall not go to an evil destiny, having heard this supreme <s>sūtra</s>.' // SRS_18.54 //

children.text: ye kecit paścime kāle śroṣyante sūtramuttamam /
children.translated_text: 'Whoever in the final age shall hear this supreme <s>sūtra</s>,

children.text: aśrupātaṃ ca kāhinti sarvaistaiḥ satkṛto hyaham // SRS_18.55 //
children.translated_text: and shall shed tears [of faith] — by all of them I am honored!' // SRS_18.55 //

children.text: ārocayāmi sarveṣāṃ yāvantaḥ purataḥ sthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I declare to all who stand before me:

children.text: parindāmi imāṃ bodhiṃ yā me kṛchreṇa sparśitā // SRS_18.56 //
children.translated_text: I entrust this awakening that was attained by me with difficulty.' // SRS_18.56 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje samādhyanuparindanā nāma parivarto 'ṣṭādaśaḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus ends the eighteenth chapter of the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, called the <s>Samādhy-anuparindanā</s> (Entrusting the <s>Samādhi</s>).

body.text:
(Vaidya 132)
19 Acintyabuddhadharmanirdeśaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 132) Chapter 19: The <s>Acintyabuddhadharmanirdeśa</s> (Teaching of Inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>Dharmas</s>).

body.text: tasmāttarhi kumāra bodhisattvena mahāsattvenemaṃ samādhimākāṅkṣatā acintyabuddhadharmanirdeśakuśalena bhavitavyam | acintyabuddhadharmaparipṛcchakajātikena bhavitavyam | acintyabuddhadharmādhimuktikena bhavitavyam | acintyabuddhadharmaparyeṣaṇākuśalena bhavitavyam | acintyāṃśca buddhadharmān śrutvā nottrasitavyaṃ na saṃtrasitavyaṃ na saṃtrāsamāpattavyam | evamukte candraprabhaḥ kumārabhūto bhagavantametadavocat - yathā kathaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ acintyabuddhadharmanirdeśakuśalo bhavati, acintyabuddhadharmaparipṛcchākuśalaśca, acintyabuddhadharmādhimuktaśca? acintyabuddhadharmaparyeṣaṇākuśalaśca bhavati, acintyāṃśca buddhadharmān śratvā nottrasyati na saṃtrasyati na saṃtrāsamāpadyate?
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, prince, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> who longs for this <s>samādhi</s> should be skilled in the teaching of inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. He should be of a nature that inquires into inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. He should have faith in inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. He should be skilled in seeking out inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. And having heard the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, he should not be frightened, not terrified, not overcome by terror.' When this was said, the prince <s>Candraprabha</s> said to the Blessed One: 'How, Blessed One, does a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> become skilled in the teaching of inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, skilled in inquiring into inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, one who has faith in inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, skilled in seeking inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, and — having heard inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> — is neither frightened, nor terrified, nor overcome by terror?'

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena pañcaśikho nāma gandharvaputraḥ pañcabhistūryaśataiḥ sārdhaṃ gaganatalādavatīrya bhagavataḥ purataḥ sthito 'bhūdupasthānaparicaryāyai | atha khalu pañcaśikhasya gandharvaputrasyaitadabhavat - yannvahaṃ yathaivaḥ devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāṃ śakrasya ca devānāmindrasya sudharmāyāṃ devasabhāyāmupasthānaparicaryāṃ karomi, saṃgītiṃ saṃprayojayāmi, tathaivādya devātidevasyāpi tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya pūjāyai saṃgītiṃ saṃprayojayeyam ||
body.translated_text: At that time, a <s>Gandharva</s>-son named <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, together with five hundred musical instruments, descended from the sky and stood before the Blessed One for service and attendance. Then this occurred to the <s>Gandharva</s>-son <s>Pañcaśikha</s>: 'Just as I perform service and attendance for the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods and <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, in the <s>Sudharmā</s> assembly hall, and put on a musical concert, so today let me put on a musical concert for the worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, who is the God above gods.'

body.text: atha khalu pañcaśikho gandharvaputrastaiḥ pañcabhistūryaśataistaiśca pañcamātrairgandharvaputraśataiḥ sārdhamekasvarasaṃgītisaṃprayuktābhistūryasaṃgītibhirvaidūryadaṇḍāṃ vīṇāmādāya bhagavataḥ purato vādayāmāsa | atha khalu bhagavata etadabhūt - yannvahaṃ tathārūpamṛddhyabhisaṃskāramabhisaṃskuryāṃ yathārūpeṇa ṛddhyabhisaṃskāreṇābhisaṃskṛtena candraprabhaḥ kumārabhūto 'cintyabuddhadharmanidhyaptikauśalyamadhigacchet, sarvadharmasvabhāvasamatāvipañcitācca samādherna calet | pañcaśikhasya ca gandharvaputrasya tantrīsvaragītisvarakauśalyamupadiśeyam ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Gandharva</s>-son <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, with those five hundred instruments and together with those five hundred <s>Gandharva</s>-sons, with instrumental music combined in a single harmony, taking up a <s>vīṇā</s> (lute) with a lapis-lazuli handle, played before the Blessed One. Then this occurred to the Blessed One: 'Let me create such a supernatural transformation by which the prince <s>Candraprabha</s> may gain skill in the contemplation of inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> and not waver from the <s>samādhi</s> that elaborates the equality of the own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s>; and by which I may also teach the <s>Gandharva</s>-son <s>Pañcaśikha</s> skill in the sounds of string-music and song.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstathārūpamṛddhyabhisaṃskāramabhisaṃskaroti sma, yattebhyaḥ pañcabhyastūryaśatebhyaḥ saṃprayuktebhyaḥ pravāditebhyo yathānakumpopasaṃhṛtaḥ śabdo niścarati dharmapratisaṃyuktaḥ | imāśca buddhadharmanidhyaptigāthā niścaranti buddhānubhāvena -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One created such a supernatural transformation that from those five hundred instruments, when combined and played, a sound issued forth as though drawn from a kettledrum — connected with the <s>Dharma</s>. And these verses on the contemplation of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> issued forth by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>:

children.text: ekahi vālapathe bahubuddhā yāttika vālika gaṅganadīye /
children.translated_text: 'On a single hair-tip, as many <s>Buddhas</s> as there are grains of sand in the river Ganges;

children.text: (Vaidya 133)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 133)

children.text: kṣetraṃ tāttika teṣa jinānāṃ te ca vilakṣaṇa te visabhāgāḥ // SRS_19.1 //
children.translated_text: as many are the fields of those <s>Jinas</s> — and they are varied, they are dissimilar.' // SRS_19.1 //

children.text: pañcagatīgata bālapathasmin nairayikā pi ca tiryagatāśca /
children.translated_text: 'On this hair-tip, beings gone to the five destinies — hell-beings and those in animal births,

children.text: te yamalaukika devamanuṣyā nāpi ca saṃkaru no ca upīḍo // SRS_19.2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s>-worldlings, gods, and humans — and yet there is no crowding, no oppression.' // SRS_19.2 //

children.text: tatra pade sasarāḥ sasamudrāḥ sarva nadī tatha utsa taḍāgāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In that [point], the deserts and oceans, all rivers, springs, and ponds —

children.text: no pi ca saṃkaru no ca upīḍo evamacintiyu dharma jinānām // SRS_19.3 //
children.translated_text: there is no crowding, no oppression; such are the inconceivable <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>Jinas</s>.' // SRS_19.3 //

children.text: tatra pade 'pi ca parvata neke cakravāla api meru sumeru /
children.translated_text: 'In that [point] there are also many mountains — <s>Cakravāla</s>, <s>Meru</s>, <s>Sumeru</s>,

children.text: ye mucilinda mahāmucilinda vindhyatha gṛdhrakūṭo himavāṃśca // SRS_19.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mucilinda</s>, <s>Mahāmucilinda</s>, <s>Vindhya</s>, <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s>, and <s>Himavat</s>.' // SRS_19.4 //

children.text: tatra pade nirayāśca sughorāstapana pratāpana ānabhiramyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In that [point] are also terrifying hells — <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Anabhiramya</s> (Joyless);

children.text: tatra ca ye niraye upapannā vedana te pi dukhāṃ anubhonti // SRS_19.5 //
children.translated_text: and those reborn in those hells experience painful feelings.' // SRS_19.5 //

children.text: tatra pade 'pi ca devavimānā dvādaśayojana te ramaṇīyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In that [point] are also divine palaces, twelve <s>yojanas</s> [in extent], delightful;

children.text: teṣu bahū marutān sahasrā divyaratīṣu sukhānyanubhonti // SRS_19.6 //
children.translated_text: in them, many thousands of <s>Maruts</s> (gods) experience happiness in divine pleasures.' // SRS_19.6 //

children.text: tatra pade ca buddhāna utpādo śāsanu lokavidūna jvaleti /
children.translated_text: 'In that [point], <s>Buddhas</s> arise, and the teaching of the Knowers of the World blazes forth;

children.text: taṃ ca na paśyati jñānavihīno yena na śodhita carya viśuddhā // SRS_19.7 //
children.translated_text: but one devoid of knowledge does not see it — one who has not purified the pure conduct.' // SRS_19.7 //

children.text: tatra pade 'pi ca dharma niruddho nirvṛtu nāyaku śrūyati śabdaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In that [point] the <s>Dharma</s> has also ceased, and the Leader is heard to have attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>;

children.text: tatra pade 'pi ca keci śṛṇonti tiṣṭhati nāyaku bhāṣati dharmam // SRS_19.8 //
children.translated_text: yet in that very [point], some hear: "The Leader abides, teaching the <s>Dharma</s>."' // SRS_19.8 //

children.text: tatra pade 'pi ca keṣacidāyurvarṣa acintiya vartati saṃjñā /
children.translated_text: 'In that [point], for some, the perception exists of a lifespan of inconceivable years;

children.text: (Vaidya 134)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 134)

children.text: tatra pade 'pi vā kālu karonti no ciru jīvati śrūyati śabdaḥ // SRS_19.9 //
children.translated_text: and in that very [point], for some, death occurs — the sound is heard: "He does not live long."' // SRS_19.9 //

children.text: tatra pade 'pi ca keṣaci saṃjñā dṛṣṭu tathāgatu pūjitu buddho /
children.translated_text: 'In that [point], for some the perception exists: "The <s>Tathāgata</s> has been seen, the <s>Buddha</s> worshipped" —

children.text: toṣitu mānasu saṃjñagraheṇa no pi ca pūjitu no ca upanno // SRS_19.10 //
children.translated_text: the mind is pleased through the grasping of perception; yet [in truth] he was not worshipped, nor did he arise.' // SRS_19.10 //

children.text: svasmi gṛhe supineva manuṣyo kāmaguṇeṣu ratīranubhūya /
children.translated_text: 'Like a man in his own house in a dream, experiencing pleasures in the objects of desire —

children.text: sa pratibuddhu na paśyati kāmāṃstacca prajānati so supino ti // SRS_19.11 //
children.translated_text: when awakened, he does not see those desires, and he knows: "That was a dream."' // SRS_19.11 //

children.text: yat tatha dṛṣṭu śruta mata jñātaṃ sarvamidaṃ vitathaṃ supino vā /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever is seen, heard, felt, or known — all this is false, like a dream;

children.text: yastu bhaveta samādhiya lābhī so imu jānati dharmasvabhāvān // SRS_19.12 //
children.translated_text: whoever attains this <s>samādhi</s>, he knows the own-nature of these <s>dharmas</s>.' // SRS_19.12 //

children.text: sūsukhitāḥ sada te nara loke yeṣa priyāpriyu nāsti kahiṃcit /
children.translated_text: 'Supremely happy always are those men in the world for whom there is no pleasant or unpleasant anywhere;

children.text: ye vanakandarake 'bhiramanti śrāmaṇakaṃ susukhaṃ anubhonti // SRS_19.13 //
children.translated_text: who delight in forests and mountain-caves — they experience the supreme happiness of the ascetic life.' // SRS_19.13 //

children.text: yeṣa mamāpi tu nāsti kahiṃcid yeṣa parigrahu sarvaśu nāsti /
children.translated_text: 'Those for whom there is no "mine" anywhere, who have no possessions whatsoever —

children.text: khaṅgasamā vicarantimu loke te gagane pavaneva vrajanti // SRS_19.14 //
children.translated_text: like rhinoceroses they wander in this world; like wind in the sky, they move.' // SRS_19.14 //

children.text: bhāvitu mārga pravartitu jñānaṃ śūnyaka dharma nirātmanu sarve /
children.translated_text: 'The path is cultivated, knowledge set in motion — all <s>dharmas</s> are empty, without self;

children.text: yena vibhāvita bhontimi dharmāstasya bhavet pratibhānamanantam // SRS_19.15 //
children.translated_text: for whom these <s>dharmas</s> are thus illuminated, his eloquence becomes infinite.' // SRS_19.15 //

children.text: sūsukhitā bata te nara kole yeṣa na sajjati mānasu loke /
children.translated_text: 'Supremely happy indeed are those men in the world whose minds are not attached to the world;

children.text: vāyusamaṃ sada teṣviha cittaṃ no ca priyāpriyu vidyati saṅgo // SRS_19.16 //
children.translated_text: their minds are always like the wind herein — there exists no attachment to pleasant or unpleasant.' // SRS_19.16 //

children.text: (Vaidya 135)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 135)

children.text: apriyu ye dukhitehi nivāso ye hi priyā dukhi tehi viyogo /
children.translated_text: 'The unpleasant is dwelling with those who cause suffering; the pleasant is separation from those who bring sorrow;

children.text: anta ubhe api eti jahitvā te sukhitā nara ye rata dharme // SRS_19.17 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned both these extremes — happy are those people who delight in <s>Dharma</s>!' // SRS_19.17 //

children.text: ye anunīyati śrutvimi dharmān sa pratihanyati śrutva adharmam /
children.translated_text: 'One who is swayed upon hearing these <s>dharmas</s>, and one who is repelled upon hearing non-<s>dharma</s> —

children.text: so madamānahato viparīto mānavaśena dukhi anubhoti // SRS_19.18 //
children.translated_text: struck by intoxication and pride, confused, through the power of pride he experiences suffering.' // SRS_19.18 //

children.text: ye samatāya pratiṣṭhita bhonti nityamanunnata nāvanatāśca /
children.translated_text: 'Those who are established in equanimity, always neither elated nor downcast,

children.text: ye priyato 'priyataśca sumuktāste sada muktamanā viharanti // SRS_19.19 //
children.translated_text: who are freed from both the pleasant and unpleasant — they always dwell with liberated minds.' // SRS_19.19 //

children.text: śīle pratiṣṭhitu sūpariśuddhe dhyāne pratiṣṭhitu nityamacintye /
children.translated_text: 'Established in morality supremely pure, established in <s>dhyāna</s> always and inconceivable,

children.text: ye vanakandari śānti ramante teṣa na vidyati vīmati jātu // SRS_19.20 //
children.translated_text: who delight in the peace of forests and caves — for them there never exists doubt.' // SRS_19.20 //

children.text: ye ca punarvitathe pratipannāḥ kāmaguṇeṣu ratāḥ sada bālāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'But those who follow the false [path], always fools delighting in objects of desire —

children.text: gṛdhru yathā kuṇapeṣvadhimuktā nityavaśānugatā namucisya // SRS_19.21 //
children.translated_text: like vultures attached to corpses, they are always under the control of <s>Namuci</s> (<s>Māra</s>).' // SRS_19.21 //

body.text: asmin khalu punargāthābhinirhāre bhāṣyamāṇe candraprabhaḥ kumārabhūtaḥ acintyeṣu buddhadharmeṣu gambhīranidhyaptinirdeśakauśalyamanuprāptaḥ, sūtrāntanirhārāvabhāsaṃ ca pratilabdhavān | pañcaśikhasya ca gandharvaputrasya ghoṣānugāyāḥ kṣānteḥ pratilambho 'bhūt | aprameyāṇāṃ ca sattvānāṃ devamānuṣikāyāḥ prajāyā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpannāni | aprameyāṇāṃ ca sattvānāmarthaḥ kṛto 'bhūta ||
body.translated_text: When this presentation of verses was being spoken, the prince <s>Candraprabha</s> attained skill in the teaching of profound contemplation of inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, and obtained the illumination of <s>sūtra</s> elucidation. And the <s>Gandharva</s>-son <s>Pañcaśikha</s> obtained the patience that follows upon hearing (<s>ghoṣānugā kṣānti</s>). And immeasurable beings of the divine and human assembly generated the thought of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening. And the welfare of immeasurable beings was accomplished.

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje acintyabuddhadharmanirdeśaparivarto nāmonaviṃśatitamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the nineteenth chapter of the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, called the <s>Acintyabuddhadharmanirdeśa</s> (Teaching of Inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>Dharmas</s>).

body.text:
(Vaidya 136)
20 Indraketudhvajarājaparivartaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 136) Chapter 20: The <s>Indraketudhvajarāja</s> (King <s>Indraketudhvaja</s>).

body.text: tatra khalu bhagavāṃścandraprabhaṃ kumārabhūtamāmantrayate sma - tasmāttarhi kumāra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sarvakuśalamūlaśikṣāguṇadharmaniśritena bhavitavyam | asaṃsargabahulena ca bhavitavyam, pāpamitraparivarjakena kalyāṇamitrasaṃniśritena paripṛcchakajātīyena dharmaparyeṣṭyāmatṛptena prāmodyabahulena dharmārthikena dharmakāmena dharmaratena dharmaparigrāhakeṇa dharmānudharmapratipannena | śāstṛsaṃjñā anena sarvabodhisattveṣūtpādayitavyā | yasya cāntikādimaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śṛṇoti, tena tasyāntike prītigauravaṃ śāstṛsaṃjñā cotpāditavyā| yaḥ kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattva imān dharmān samādāya vartate, sa kṣipramanācchedyapratibhāvaniryāto bhavati | acintyabuddhadharmādhimuktaśca bhavati | gambhīreṣu ca dharmeṣu nidhyaptiṃ gacchati | ālokabhūtaśca bhavati sadevakasya lokasya kāṅkṣāvimativicikitsāndhakāravidhamanatayā ||
body.translated_text: There the Blessed One addressed <s>Candraprabha</s> the prince: "Therefore, O prince, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> should rely upon all roots of merit, trainings, qualities, and <s>dharmas</s>. He should be one who dwells mostly in non-association, one who avoids evil friends, one who relies on good friends, one whose nature is to inquire, one insatiable in the quest for <s>Dharma</s>, one abounding in gladness, one who desires <s>Dharma</s>, one who loves <s>Dharma</s>, one who delights in <s>Dharma</s>, one who embraces <s>Dharma</s>, one who practices in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>. He should generate the perception of 'teacher' toward all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. And toward the one from whom he hears this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, he should generate affectionate respect and the perception of 'teacher.' The <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, O prince, who undertakes and abides in these <s>dharmas</s>, quickly becomes one whose eloquence is unbreakable. He becomes one with conviction in the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. He attains contemplative insight into the profound <s>dharmas</s>. And he becomes a light to the world with its gods, by dispelling the darkness of doubt, uncertainty, and perplexity." ||

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that moment, spoke these verses:

children.text: abhyatīta bahukalpakoṭiyo aprameya atulā acintiyāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> have passed — immeasurable, incomparable, inconceivable —

children.text: yad abhūṣi dvipadānamuttamo indraketudhvajarāja nāyakaḥ // SRS_20.1 //
children.translated_text: since there arose the Supreme among Bipeds, the Leader named <s>Indraketudhvajarāja</s>. // SRS_20.1 //

children.text: so samādhimimu śāntu deśayi yatra nāsti naru jīva pudgalaḥ /
children.translated_text: "He taught this peaceful <s>samādhi</s> wherein there is no person, no living being, no individual;

children.text: māya budbuda marīci vidyutā sarva dharma dakacandrasaṃnibhāḥ // SRS_20.2 //
children.translated_text: all <s>dharmas</s> are like illusion, bubbles, a mirage, lightning — resembling a water-moon. // SRS_20.2 //

children.text: nāsti sattva manujo ca labhyate kālu kṛtva paraloki gacchi yo /
children.translated_text: "There is no being, and no person can be found — [no being] who, having died, goes to another world;

children.text: no ca karma kṛtu vipraṇaśyate kṛṣṇa śukla phala deti tādṛśam // SRS_20.3 //
children.translated_text: yet <s>karma</s> once done does not perish — black and white, it gives its corresponding fruit. // SRS_20.3 //

children.text: eṣa yukti nayadvāra bhadrakaṃ sūkṣma durdṛśu jināna gocarā /
children.translated_text: "This is the method, the auspicious gateway of reasoning, subtle, hard to see, the domain of the <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: yatra akṣarapadaṃ na labhyate buddhabodhi bhagavān prajānati // SRS_20.4 //
children.translated_text: wherein no syllable or word is found — the Blessed One comprehends <s>Buddha</s>-awakening. // SRS_20.4 //

children.text: (Vaidya 137)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 137)

children.text: dhāraṇī vipulajñānasaṃcayā sūtrakoṭiniyutāna āgatā /
children.translated_text: "<s>Dhāraṇī</s>, the accumulation of vast knowledge, the source of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of <s>sūtras</s>,

children.text: buddhakoṭiniyutāna gocarastaṃ samādhi bhagavān prabhāṣate // SRS_20.5 //
children.translated_text: the domain of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of Buddhas — the Blessed One proclaims that <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_20.5 //

children.text: āturāṇamaya vyādhimocako bodhisattvasamudānitaṃ dhanam /
children.translated_text: "The liberator from disease and affliction of the sick — the treasure gathered by <s>Bodhisattvas</s>,

children.text: sarvabuddhastuta saṃprakāśito devakoṭiniyutehi pūjitaḥ // SRS_20.6 //
children.translated_text: praised and proclaimed by all Buddhas, worshipped by <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of gods. // SRS_20.6 //

children.text: sarva bālajana bhūtacodanā tīrthikehi parivarjitaḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: "The reproof of all foolish people and beings, always avoided by <s>tīrthikas</s>,

children.text: śreṣṭha śīladhanu buddhavarṇitaṃ vidyuteva gagane na lipyate // SRS_20.7 //
children.translated_text: the supreme treasury of morality praised by the <s>Buddha</s> — like lightning in the sky, it is untainted. // SRS_20.7 //

children.text: yehi pūjita jināna koṭiyo dānaśīlacaritā vicakṣaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Those who have worshipped <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Jinas</s>, discerning ones who have practiced generosity and morality,

children.text: pāpamitra puri yehi varjitā teṣa paitṛkadhanaṃ niruttaram // SRS_20.8 //
children.translated_text: those who have previously avoided evil friends — for them it is the unsurpassed ancestral treasure. // SRS_20.8 //

children.text: tatra bhikṣu sthitu dharmabhāṇako brahmacāri sugatasya aurasaḥ /
children.translated_text: "A monk standing there [as] a <s>Dharma</s>-preacher, a celibate, a true son of the <s>Sugata</s> —

children.text: śrutva dharmamimamānulomikaṃ citta pādesi ya lokanāyakaḥ // SRS_20.9 //
children.translated_text: having heard this <s>Dharma</s> in conformity, he produces the mind [of awakening] that the World-Leader [taught]. // SRS_20.9 //

children.text: indraketudhvajarāju nāyako adhyabhāṣi abhu dharmabhāṇakam /
children.translated_text: "The Leader <s>Indraketudhvajarāja</s> addressed that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher:

children.text: bhikṣubhāva paramaṃ ti duṣkaraṃ cittupāda vara agrabodhaye // SRS_20.10 //
children.translated_text: "'The state of a monk is supremely difficult — [especially] the arising of the thought for the supreme awakening. // SRS_20.10 //

children.text: śīlu rakṣa maṇiratnasaṃnibhaṃ mitra seva sada ānulomikam /
children.translated_text: "'Guard morality like a jewel-gem; always serve a concordant [good] friend;

children.text: pāpamitra na kadāci sevato buddhajñānamacireṇa lapsyase // SRS_20.11 //
children.translated_text: never serving evil friends — you will quickly attain <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge!' // SRS_20.11 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje indraketudhvajarājaparivarto nāma viṃśatitamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twentieth chapter in the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, called the <s>Indraketudhvajarājaparivarta</s>. ||

body.text:
(Vaidya 138)
21 Pūrvayogaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 138) Chapter 21: <s>Pūrvayogaparivarta</s> (The Chapter on Former Connections). |

children.text: āsi pūrvamiha jambusāhvaye apramatta duvi śreṣṭhidārakau /
children.translated_text: "Formerly here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, two diligent merchant's sons,

children.text: pravrajitva sugatasya śāsane khaṅgabhūta vanaṣaṇḍamāśritau // SRS_21.1 //
children.translated_text: having gone forth in the <s>Sugata</s>'s teaching, like rhinoceroses, they resorted to a forest grove. // SRS_21.1 //

children.text: ṛddhimanta caturdhyānalābhinau kāvyaśāstrakuśalau suśikṣitau /
children.translated_text: "Possessing <s>ṛddhi</s>, having attained the four <s>dhyānas</s>, skilled in poetry and <s>śāstras</s>, well-trained,

children.text: antarikṣapadabhūmikovidau te asakta gagane vrajanti ca // SRS_21.2 //
children.translated_text: expert in the paths of sky and earth, unattached — they traveled through the sky. // SRS_21.2 //

children.text: te ca tatra vanaṣaṇḍi śītale nānapuṣpabharite manorame /
children.translated_text: "And there in that cool forest grove, filled with various flowers, delightful,

children.text: nānapakṣidvijasaṃghasevite anyamanya katha saṃprayojite // SRS_21.3 //
children.translated_text: frequented by various flocks of birds, they engaged each other in conversation. // SRS_21.3 //

children.text: tena rāja mṛgayā aṭantake śabda śrutva vanu taṃ upāgamī /
children.translated_text: "A king, wandering there on a hunt, heard the sound and approached that forest;

children.text: dṛṣṭva pārthiva tatha dharmabhāṇakau teṣu prema paramaṃ upasthahi // SRS_21.4 //
children.translated_text: seeing the sovereign and those two <s>Dharma</s>-preachers, supreme affection arose in him toward them. // SRS_21.4 //

children.text: tehi sārdhu katha ānulomikīṃ kṛtva rāju purato niṣīdi so /
children.translated_text: "Having had a concordant conversation with them, the king sat before them;

children.text: tasya rājña balakāya nantako ṣaṣṭhikoṭiniyutānyupāgamī // SRS_21.5 //
children.translated_text: his military retinue — sixty <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> — also approached. // SRS_21.5 //

children.text: ekameku teṣu dharmabhāṇako rājamabravī śṛṇohi kṣatriyā /
children.translated_text: "Each one of those <s>Dharma</s>-preachers addressed the king: 'Listen, O <s>Kṣatriya</s>!

children.text: buddhapādu paramaṃ sudurlabho apramattu sada bhohi pārthiva // SRS_21.6 //
children.translated_text: The presence of a <s>Buddha</s> is supremely hard to obtain — always be vigilant, O sovereign! // SRS_21.6 //

children.text: āyu gacchati sadānavasthitaṃ girinadīya salileva śīghragam /
children.translated_text: "'Life passes, always unstable — flowing swiftly like the water of a mountain river;

children.text: vyādhiśokajarapīḍitasya te nāsti trāṇu yatha karma bhadrakam // SRS_21.7 //
children.translated_text: for you who are afflicted by disease, grief, and old age, there is no protection other than wholesome <s>karma</s>. // SRS_21.7 //

children.text: (Vaidya 139)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 139)

children.text: dharmapālu bhava rājakuñjarā rakṣimaṃ daśabalāna śāsanam /
children.translated_text: "'Be a protector of <s>Dharma</s>, O elephant among kings! Guard this teaching of the Ten-Powered One!

children.text: kṣīṇa kāli parame sudāruṇe dharmapakṣi sthihi rājakuñjara // SRS_21.8 //
children.translated_text: In the terrible final age of decline, stand in the faction of <s>Dharma</s>, O elephant among kings! // SRS_21.8 //

children.text: eva te bahuprakāra paṇḍitā ovadanti tada taṃ narādhipam /
children.translated_text: "Thus those wise ones instructed that lord of men in many ways;

children.text: sārdhu ṣaṣṭaniyutehi pārthivo bodhicittamudapādayattadā // SRS_21.9 //
children.translated_text: together with sixty <s>niyutas</s>, that sovereign then generated the thought of awakening. // SRS_21.9 //

children.text: śrutva dharma tada rājakuñjaraḥ sūratānakhilāna bhāṣato /
children.translated_text: "Having heard the <s>Dharma</s>, that elephant among kings — as the gentle, guileless ones spoke —

children.text: prītijāta sumanā udagrako vandya pāda śirasāya prakramī // SRS_21.10 //
children.translated_text: filled with joy, glad, and elated, bowed his head at their feet and departed. // SRS_21.10 //

children.text: tasya rājña bahavo 'nyabhikṣavo lābhakāma praviśintu tat kulam /
children.translated_text: "To that king, [came] many other monks who desired gain and entered that [royal] family;

children.text: teṣa dṛṣṭa cariyā na tādṛśī teṣu rāja na tathā sagauravam // SRS_21.11 //
children.translated_text: seeing that their conduct was not of that [high] kind, the king did not show the same respect toward them. // SRS_21.11 //

children.text: tacca śāsanamatītaśāstukaṃ paścimaṃ ca tada varṣu vartate /
children.translated_text: "And that teaching belonged to a past Teacher; in its final period the rains [of Dharma] still fell;

children.text: jambudvīpi suparittabhājanā prādurbhūta bahavo asaṃyatāḥ // SRS_21.12 //
children.translated_text: in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, [there being] but a small vessel [for the Dharma], many unrestrained ones had appeared. // SRS_21.12 //

children.text: utka lubdha bahu tatra bhikṣavo lābhakāma upalambhadṛṣṭikāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Greedy, covetous, many monks were there, desiring gain, of the view that grasps at [real] existence;

children.text: vipranaṣṭa sugatasya śāsanād grāhayiṃsu bahulaṃ tadā nṛpam // SRS_21.13 //
children.translated_text: lost from the <s>Sugata</s>'s teaching, they misled the king excessively. // SRS_21.13 //

children.text: ghātayeti ubhi dharmabhāṇakau ye ucchedu pravadanti tīrthikāḥ /
children.translated_text: "'Have those two <s>Dharma</s>-preachers killed! They proclaim annihilationism like <s>tīrthikas</s>!

children.text: dīrghacārika samādapenti te nirvṛtīya na te kiṃci darśikā // SRS_21.14 //
children.translated_text: They urge upon [you] long wanderings — they show nothing [leading to] liberation.' // SRS_21.14 //

children.text: karma naśyati vipāku naśyati skandha nāstīti vadanti kuhakāḥ /
children.translated_text: "'<s>Karma</s> perishes, its fruition perishes, the <s>skandhas</s> do not exist!' — thus speak those deceivers;

children.text: (Vaidya 140)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 140)

children.text: tāṃ kṣipāhi viṣayātu pārthiva evameva ciru dharma sthāsyati // SRS_21.15 //
children.translated_text: 'Banish those two from your domain, O sovereign — thus the <s>Dharma</s> will long endure!' // SRS_21.15 //

children.text: śrutva teṣa vacanaṃ tadantaraṃ kāṅkṣa prāptu bhuta rājakuñjaraḥ /
children.translated_text: "Having heard their words, the elephant among kings thereupon fell into doubt;

children.text: ghātayiṣyi amu dharmabhāṇakau mā upekṣitu anartha bheṣyati // SRS_21.16 //
children.translated_text: 'I shall have those two <s>Dharma</s>-preachers killed — do not disregard [this], or harm will follow!' // SRS_21.16 //

children.text: tasya rājña anubaddha devatā pūrvajāti sahacīrṇu cārikā /
children.translated_text: "A deity, bound to that king — one who had practiced together with him in former lives,

children.text: dīrgharā hitakāma paṇḍitā sā avoci tada rājapārthivam // SRS_21.17 //
children.translated_text: wise, long-sighted, desiring his welfare — she spoke to that sovereign king: // SRS_21.17 //

children.text: cittupāda ma janehi īdṛśaṃ pāpamitravacanena kṣatriyā /
children.translated_text: "'Do not generate such a thought! [Deceived] by the words of evil friends, O <s>Kṣatriya</s>,

children.text: mā tva bhikṣu duvi dharmabhāṇakau pāpamitravacanena ghātaya // SRS_21.18 //
children.translated_text: do not have those two monk <s>Dharma</s>-preachers killed through the words of evil friends! // SRS_21.18 //

children.text: na tva kiṃci smarasī narādhipa yatti tehi vanaṣaṇḍi bhāṣitam |
children.translated_text: "'Do you not remember anything, O lord of men — what they spoke in that forest grove?

children.text: kṣīṇakāli parame sudāruṇe dharmapakṣi sthihi rājakuñjara /
children.translated_text: In the terrible final age of decline, stand in the faction of <s>Dharma</s>, O elephant among kings! // [SRS_21.19]

children.text: rāja bhūtavacanena coditaḥ so na riñjati jināna śāsanam // SRS_21.19 //
children.translated_text: "The king, admonished with true words, did not abandon the <s>Jinas</s>' teaching. // SRS_21.19 //

children.text: tasya rājña tada bhrāta dāruṇaḥ prātisīmiku sa tehi grāhitaḥ |
children.translated_text: "But then the king's cruel brother — he was seized by those [evil monks]:"

children.text: eṣa deva tava bhrāta pāpako jīvitena na jātu nandate /
children.translated_text: "'Your Majesty, this brother of yours is wicked — he never delights in life [as it is];

children.text: tau ca bhikṣu duvi ghora vaidyakā te vrajanti gaganena vidyayā // SRS_21.20 //
children.translated_text: and those two monks are terrible sorcerers — they travel through the sky by magic!' // SRS_21.20 //

children.text: te sma śrutva tava mūlamāgatā sarvi bhūta tava vijñapematha /
children.translated_text: "'Having heard that, they came to your root [palace] — all of us inform your majesty;

children.text: kṣipra ghātaya ghora vaidyakā mā ti paści anutāpu bheṣyati // SRS_21.21 //
children.translated_text: quickly have those terrible sorcerers killed — lest afterward there be regret!' // SRS_21.21 //

children.text: saṃnahitva tada rājakuñjaro pāpamitravacanena prasthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Then that elephant among kings, armored, set forth at the words of evil friends;

children.text: (Vaidya 141)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 141)

children.text: sarvasainyaparivārito nṛpo yatra bhikṣu vani taṃ upāgato // SRS_21.22 //
children.translated_text: the king, surrounded by all his forces, went to where the monks were in the forest. // SRS_21.22 //

children.text: jñātva ghoramatidāruṇaṃ nṛpaṃ nāga yakṣa vani tatra ye sthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Knowing the terrible and exceedingly cruel king, the <s>nāgas</s> and <s>yakṣas</s> who dwelt in that forest —

children.text: iṣṭavarṣa tada tatra pātita tena rāja sahasenayā hato // SRS_21.23 //
children.translated_text: at that time they caused a hail of stones to fall; by that the king together with his army was slain. // SRS_21.23 //

children.text: pāpamitravacanena paśyathā kālu kṛtva tada rāja dāruṇam /
children.translated_text: "See [the result of] the words of evil friends! That cruel king, having thus made his time [of death],

children.text: yena krodhu kṛtu dharmabhāṇake so avīci gatu ṣaṣṭijātiyo // SRS_21.24 //
children.translated_text: because he generated anger toward the <s>Dharma</s>-preachers — he went to <s>Avīci</s> for sixty lifetimes! // SRS_21.24 //

children.text: te 'pi bhikṣu bahavopalambhikā yehi grāhitu rāja kṣatriyo /
children.translated_text: "And those many monks who grasped at [real] existence, by whom the <s>Kṣatriya</s> king was misled —

children.text: jātikoṭiśata apyacintiyo vedayiṃsu narakeṣu vedanām // SRS_21.25 //
children.translated_text: for hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of lifetimes, inconceivable, they experienced suffering in the hells. // SRS_21.25 //

children.text: devatā yāya rāju codito yāya rakṣita dharmabhāṇakau /
children.translated_text: "The deity by whom the king was admonished, by whom the <s>Dharma</s>-preachers were protected —

children.text: tāya buddha yatha gaṅgavālikā dṛṣṭva pūjita carantu cārikām // SRS_21.26 //
children.translated_text: she saw and worshipped Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, practicing the [Bodhisattva] conduct. // SRS_21.26 //

children.text: ṣaṣṭikoṭiniyutā anūnakā yehi dharma śrutu sārdhu rājinā /
children.translated_text: "The sixty <s>koṭi-niyutas</s>, not one fewer, who heard the <s>Dharma</s> together with the king,

children.text: yehi bodhivaracittu pāditaṃ buddha bhūyi pṛthulokadhātuṣu // SRS_21.27 //
children.translated_text: who generated the supreme thought of awakening — they became Buddhas in vast world-systems. // SRS_21.27 //

children.text: teṣu āyu bahukalpakoṭiyo teṣa jñānamatulamacintiyam /
children.translated_text: "Their lifespans were many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>; their knowledge was incomparable and inconceivable;

children.text: tehi sarvimu samādhi bhadrakaṃ deśayitva dvipadendu nirvṛtā // SRS_21.28 //
children.translated_text: they all taught this excellent, auspicious <s>samādhi</s> and, as lords among bipeds, were extinguished. // SRS_21.28 //

children.text: etu śrutva vacanaṃ niruttaraṃ śīlabrahmaguṇajñānasaṃcayam /
children.translated_text: "Having heard this unsurpassed teaching — the accumulation of morality, holiness, qualities, and knowledge —

children.text: apramatta bhavathā atandritā buddhajñānamacireṇa lapsyathā // SRS_21.29 //
children.translated_text: be vigilant, be unwearied! You shall quickly attain <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge! // SRS_21.29 //

body.text:
(Vaidya 142)
drakṣyathā daśadiśe tathāgatān śāntacitta kṛpamaitralocanān | sarvalokaśaraṇaṃ parāyaṇaṃ dharmavarṣu jagi utsṛjiṣyathā || 30 ||
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 142) "You shall see the <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the ten directions — peaceful-minded, with eyes of compassion and loving-kindness; the refuge and final resort of all the world — and you shall release the rain of <s>Dharma</s> upon the world!" // 30 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje pūrvayogaparivarto nāma ekaviṃśatitamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-first chapter in the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, called the <s>Pūrvayogaparivarta</s> (Chapter on Former Connections). ||

body.text:
(Vaidya 143)
22 Tathāgatakāyanirdeśaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 143) Chapter 22: <s>Tathāgatakāyanirdeśaparivarta</s> (The Chapter on the Exposition of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s Body). |

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃścandraprabhaṃ kumārabhūtamāmantrayate sma - tasmāt tarhi kumāra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena kāye 'nadhyavasitena jīvite nirapekṣeṇa bhavitavyam | tat kasya hetoḥ? kāyajīvitādhyavasānahetorhi kumāra akuśaladharmābhisaṃskāro bhavati | tasmāttarhi kumāra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena na rūpakāyatastathāgataḥ prajñātavyaḥ | tat kasya hetoḥ? dharmakāyā hi buddhā bhagavanto dharmakāyaprabhāvitāśca na rūpakāyaprabhāvitāḥ | tasmāttarhi kumāra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena tathāgatakāyaṃ prārthayitukāmena tathāgatakāyaṃ jñātukāmena ayaṃ samādhirudgrahītavyaḥ paryavāptavyo dhārayitavyo vācayitavyaḥ pravartitavyaḥ uddeṣṭavyaḥ svādhyātavyo vācayitavyo bhāvanāyogamanuyuktena bhavitavyam parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayitavyaḥ | tatra kumāra tathāgatasya kāyaḥ śatapuṇyanirjātayā buddhyānekārthanirdeśo dharmanirjātaḥ ānimittaḥ sarvanimittāpagato gambhīraḥ apramāṇaḥ apramāṇadharmaḥ ānimittasvabhāvaḥ sarvanimittavibhāvitaḥ | acalo 'pratiṣṭhito 'tyantākāśasvabhāvo 'dṛśyaścakṣuḥpathasamatikrānto dharmakāyaḥ prajñātavyaḥ | acintyaḥ cittabhūmivigataḥ sukhaduḥkhāviprakampyaḥ sarvaprapañcasamatikrānto 'nirdeśyo 'niketo buddhajñānaṃ prārthayitukāmānāṃ ghoṣapathasamatikrāntaḥ sasāro rāgasamatikrāntaḥ abhedyo doṣapathasamatikrānto dṛḍho mohapathasamatikrānto nirdiṣṭaḥ | śūnyatānirdeśena ajāto jātisamatikrāntaḥ anāsravaḥ vipākasamatikrāntaḥ nityo vyāhāreṇa | vyavahāraśca śūnyaḥ nirviśeṣo nirvāṇena, nirvṛtaḥ śabdena, śānto ghoṣeṇa, sāmānyaḥ saṃketena, saṃketaḥ paramārthena, paramārtho bhūtavacanena | śītalo niṣparidānaḥ animittaḥ amanyitaḥ aninditaḥ aprapañcitaḥ - alpaśabdo nirdeśena | aparyanto varṇanirdeśena, mahābhijñāparikarmanirjātaḥ asmṛtitaḥ avidūre mahābhijñāparikarmanirdeśena | ayamucyate kumāra tathāgatakāya iti ||
body.translated_text: Then indeed the Blessed One addressed <s>Candraprabha</s> the prince: 'Therefore, O prince, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> should not be attached to the body and should be indifferent to life. For what reason? Because, O prince, attachment to body and life gives rise to the fabrication of unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>. Therefore, O prince, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> should not conceive the <s>Tathāgata</s> through the form-body (<s>rūpakāya</s>). For what reason? Because the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, are <s>Dharmakāya</s> (Dharma-body) — empowered by the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, not empowered by the form-body. Therefore, O prince, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> who wishes to seek the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body, who wishes to know the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body, should take up this <s>samādhi</s>, master it, retain it, recite it, propagate it, expound it, study it, teach it to others, be devoted to its cultivation, and explain it to others in detail. Therein, O prince, the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body — born from the hundredfold merit of wisdom, indicating many meanings, born from the <s>Dharma</s>, signless, beyond all signs, profound, immeasurable, of immeasurable <s>dharmas</s>, of signless essential nature, cultivated beyond all signs — unmoving, without foundation, of the essential nature of absolute space, invisible, beyond the path of the eye — should be known as the <s>Dharmakāya</s>. Inconceivable, beyond the ground of thought, unshaken by pleasure and suffering, transcending all conceptual proliferation (<s>prapañca</s>), inexpressible, without abode — for those who wish to seek <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, it transcends the path of sound. Pervading, it transcends the path of passion. Indestructible, it transcends the path of hatred. Firm, it transcends the path of delusion. As taught: through the teaching of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), unborn, it transcends birth. Free from outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>), it transcends ripening. Permanent by verbal designation — yet designation is empty. Non-different from <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Ceased by name. Peaceful by sound. Conventional by agreement. Agreement is ultimate truth. Ultimate truth is factual speech. Cool, without remainder, signless, unconceived, unreproached, without proliferation — of little expression by designation. Boundless by the teaching of appearances. Born from the preparation of great superknowledge. Not far from mindfulness, through the teaching of the preparation of great superknowledge. This, O prince, is called the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body.' ||

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then indeed the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: ya icche lokanāthasya kāyaṃ jānitumīdṛśam /
children.translated_text: 'He who wishes to know such a body of the Lord of the World —

children.text: imaṃ samādhiṃ bhāvitvā kāyaṃ buddhasya jñāsyati // SRS_22.1 //
children.translated_text: having cultivated this <s>samādhi</s>, he will know the body of the <s>Buddha</s>. // SRS_22.1 //

children.text: (Vaidya 144)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 144)

children.text: puṇyanirjātu buddhasya kāyaḥ śuddhaḥ prabhāsvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Born from merit, the <s>Buddha</s>'s body is pure and radiant;

children.text: sameti so 'ntarīkṣeṇa nānātvaṃ nāsya labhyate // SRS_22.2 //
children.translated_text: it accords with the sky — no duality is found in it. // SRS_22.2 //

children.text: yādṛśā bodhirbuddhasya lakṣaṇāni ca tādṛśāḥ /
children.translated_text: Such as is the <s>Buddha</s>'s awakening, such are his marks;

children.text: yādṛśā lakṣaṇāstasya kāyastasya hi tādṛśaḥ // SRS_22.3 //
children.translated_text: such as are his marks, such indeed is his body. // SRS_22.3 //

children.text: saṃbodhilakṣaṇaḥ kāyo buddhakṣetraṃ hi tādṛśam /
children.translated_text: The body bears the marks of awakening; such too is the <s>Buddha</s>-field;

children.text: balā vimokṣā dhyānāni sarve te 'pyekalakṣaṇāḥ // SRS_22.4 //
children.translated_text: the powers, liberations, and <s>dhyānas</s> — all these too are of one mark. // SRS_22.4 //

children.text: evaṃ saṃbhavu buddhānāṃ lokanāthāna īdṛśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Such is the arising of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Lords of the World;

children.text: na jātu kenacicchakyaṃ paśyituṃ māṃsacakṣuṣā // SRS_22.5 //
children.translated_text: it can never be seen by anyone with the fleshly eye. // SRS_22.5 //

children.text: bahū evaṃ pravakṣyanti dṛṣṭo me lokanāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Many will say thus: "The Leader of the World has been seen by me —

children.text: suvarṇavarṇaḥ kāyena sarvalokaṃ prabhāsati // SRS_22.6 //
children.translated_text: golden-colored in body, he illuminates the entire world." // SRS_22.6 //

children.text: adhiṣṭhānena buddhānāmanubhāvādvikurvitaiḥ /
children.translated_text: By the sovereign power of the <s>Buddhas</s>, through their miraculous transformations,

children.text: yenāsau dṛśyate kāyo lakṣaṇehi vicitritaḥ // SRS_22.7 //
children.translated_text: that body is seen, adorned with marks. // SRS_22.7 //

children.text: ārohapariṇāhena kāyo buddhasya darśitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>'s body has been displayed in height and breadth;

children.text: na ca pramāṇaṃ kāyasya labdhaṃ tena acintiyaḥ // SRS_22.8 //
children.translated_text: yet no measure of that body has been found — [therefore] it is inconceivable. // SRS_22.8 //

children.text: yadi pramāṇaṃ labhyeta kāyo buddhasya ettakaḥ /
children.translated_text: If a measure could be found — the <s>Buddha</s>'s body being of such-and-such size —

children.text: nirviśeṣo bhavecchāstā devaiśca manujairapi // SRS_22.9 //
children.translated_text: the Teacher would be no different from gods and humans. // SRS_22.9 //

children.text: samāhitasya cittasya vipāko 'pi tallakṣaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: The fruit of the concentrated mind also bears that mark;

children.text: tallakṣaṇaṃ nāmarūpaṃ śuddhaṃ bhoti prabhāsvaram // SRS_22.10 //
children.translated_text: name-and-form of that mark becomes pure and radiant. // SRS_22.10 //

children.text: na caiṣa kenacijjātu samādhiḥ śāntu bhāvitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Never has this peaceful <s>samādhi</s> been cultivated by anyone

children.text: yatheha lokanāthena kalpakoṭyo niṣevitaḥ // SRS_22.11 //
children.translated_text: as it was practiced by this Lord of the World for <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>. // SRS_22.11 //

children.text: bahubhiḥ śukladharmaiśca samādhirjanito 'pyayam /
children.translated_text: By many wholesome <s>dharmas</s> this <s>samādhi</s> was generated;

children.text: samādherasya vaipulyāt kāyo mahyaṃ na dṛśyate // SRS_22.12 //
children.translated_text: because of the vastness of this <s>samādhi</s>, my body cannot be seen. // SRS_22.12 //

children.text: yasya vo yādṛśaṃ cittaṃ nāmarūpaṃ pi tādṛśam /
children.translated_text: Whatever your mind is like, such is your name-and-form;

children.text: niḥsvabhāvasya cittasya nāmarūpaṃ vilakṣaṇam // SRS_22.13 //
children.translated_text: of a mind without own-nature, the name-and-form is markless. // SRS_22.13 //

children.text: yasya codārasaṃjñādi nāmarūpasmi vartate /
children.translated_text: For one in whom a lofty perception operates regarding name-and-form,

children.text: visabhāgāya saṃjñāya udāraṃ cittu jāyate // SRS_22.14 //
children.translated_text: through a contrary perception, a lofty mind arises. // SRS_22.14 //

children.text: yasya co mṛdukī saṃjñā nāmarūpasmi vartate /
children.translated_text: For one in whom a subtle perception operates regarding name-and-form,

children.text: agṛdhraṃ nāmarūpasmi cittaṃ bhoti prabhāsvaram // SRS_22.15 //
children.translated_text: the mind, free from grasping at name-and-form, becomes radiant. // SRS_22.15 //

children.text: smarāmī pūrvajātīṣu asaṃkhyeyeṣu saptasu /
children.translated_text: I remember in former births, in seven innumerable [<s>kalpas</s>] —

children.text: tisro me pāpikāḥ saṃjñā naivotpannāḥ kadācana // SRS_22.16 //
children.translated_text: three evil perceptions never arose in me. // SRS_22.16 //

children.text: (Vaidya 145)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 145)

children.text: anāsravaṃ ca me cittaṃ kalpakoṭyo hyacintiyāḥ /
children.translated_text: My mind was free from outflows for inconceivable <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: karomi cārthaṃ sattvānāṃ na ca me kāyu dṛśyate // SRS_22.17 //
children.translated_text: I accomplish the welfare of beings, yet my body is not seen. // SRS_22.17 //

children.text: yathā ca yasya bhāvehi vimuktaṃ bhoti mānasam /
children.translated_text: When one's mind is liberated from [certain] phenomena,

children.text: na tasya tehi bhāvehi bhūyo bhoti samāgamaḥ // SRS_22.18 //
children.translated_text: there is no further coming-together with those phenomena for that one. // SRS_22.18 //

children.text: vimuktaṃ mama vijñānaṃ sarvabhāvehi sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: My consciousness is liberated from all phenomena in every way;

children.text: svabhāvo jñātu cittasya bhūyo jñānaṃ pravartate // SRS_22.19 //
children.translated_text: having known the own-nature of the mind, knowledge turns further. // SRS_22.19 //

children.text: kṣetrakoṭīsahasrāṇi gacchanti mama nirmitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of fields are traversed by my emanations;

children.text: kurvanti cārthaṃ sattvānāṃ yatra kāyo na labhyate // SRS_22.20 //
children.translated_text: they accomplish the welfare of beings, where [the true] body is not found. // SRS_22.20 //

children.text: alakṣaṇo nirnimitto yathaiva gaganaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: Without marks, without signs, just as space —

children.text: kāyo nirabhilāpyo me durvijñeyo nidarśitaḥ // SRS_22.21 //
children.translated_text: my body is inexpressible, hard to know — thus it has been shown. // SRS_22.21 //

children.text: dharmakāyo mahāvīro dharmeṇa kāya nirjito /
children.translated_text: The Great Hero is the <s>Dharmakāya</s>; the body was accomplished through the <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: na jātu rūpakāyeṇa śakyaṃ prajñāpituṃ jino // SRS_22.22 //
children.translated_text: the Conqueror can never be designated through the form-body. // SRS_22.22 //

children.text: kathānirdeśu yasyaitaṃ śrutvā prītirbhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: For one in whom joy will arise upon hearing this teaching and instruction,

children.text: na tasya māraḥ pāpīyānavatāraṃ labhiṣyati // SRS_22.23 //
children.translated_text: <s>Māra</s>, the Evil One, will not find an opening. // SRS_22.23 //

children.text: śrutvā ca dharmaṃ gambhīraṃ yasya trāso na bheṣyati /
children.translated_text: And one for whom no terror will arise upon hearing the profound <s>Dharma</s> —

children.text: na cāsau jīvitārthāya buddhabodhiṃ pratikṣipet // SRS_22.24 //
children.translated_text: he will not reject <s>Buddha</s>-awakening for the sake of life. // SRS_22.24 //

children.text: bhūtakoṭīsahasrāṇāṃ bhūtanirdeśa jñāsyati /
children.translated_text: He will know the true teaching of thousands of limits of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>);

children.text: ālokabhūto lokānāṃ yena yena gamiṣyati // SRS_22.25 //
children.translated_text: he will become a light to the worlds, wherever he goes.' // SRS_22.25 //

body.text: tatra kumāra tathāgatasya kāyo nimittakarmaṇāpi na sukaraṃ jñātum | nīlo vā nīlavarṇo vā nīlanidarśano vā nīlanirbhāso vā | pīto vā pītavarṇo vā pītanidarśano vā pītanirbhāso vā | lohito vā lohitavarṇo vā lohitanidarśano vā lohitanirbhāso vā | avadāto vā avadātavarṇo vā avadātanidarśano vā avadātanirbhāso vā | mañjiṣṭho vā mañjiṣṭhavarṇo vā mañjiṣṭhanidarśano vā mañjiṣṭhanirbhāso vā | sphaṭiko vā sphaṭikavarṇo vā sphaṭikanidarśano vā sphaṭikanirbhāso vā | āgneyo vā agnivarṇo vā agninidarśano vā agninirbhāso vā | sarpirmaṇḍopamo vā sarpirvarṇo vā sarpirnidarśano vā sarpirnirbhāso vā | sauvarṇo vā suvarṇavarṇo vā suvarṇanidarśano vā suvarṇanirbhāso vā | vaidūryo vā vaidūryavarṇo vā vaidūryanidarśano vā vaidūryanirbhāso vā | vidyudvā vā vidyudvarṇo vā vidyunnidarśano vā vidyunnirbhāso vā | brahmo vā brahmavarṇo vā brahmanidarśano vā brahmanirbhāso vā | devo vā devavarṇo vā devanidarśano vā devanirbhāso vā | iti hi kumāra tathāgatasya kāyaḥ śuddhaḥ sarvanimittairapyacintyaḥ apyacintyanirdeśo rūpakāyapariniṣpattyā | na sukaraṃ sadevakenāpi lokena kāyasya pramāṇamudgrahītumanyatra sarvākārairacintyaḥ aprameyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, O prince, the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body is not easy to know even through sign-activity: blue or blue-colored, blue in appearance or blue in radiance; yellow or yellow-colored, yellow in appearance or yellow in radiance; red or red-colored, red in appearance or red in radiance; white or white-colored, white in appearance or white in radiance; madder-red or madder-colored, madder in appearance or madder in radiance; crystal or crystal-colored, crystal in appearance or crystal in radiance; fiery or fire-colored, fire in appearance or fire in radiance; like clarified butter or butter-colored, butter in appearance or butter in radiance; golden or gold-colored, gold in appearance or gold in radiance; <s>vaidūrya</s> or <s>vaidūrya</s>-colored, <s>vaidūrya</s> in appearance or <s>vaidūrya</s> in radiance; lightning or lightning-colored, lightning in appearance or lightning in radiance; <s>Brahmā</s>-like or <s>Brahmā</s>-colored, <s>Brahmā</s> in appearance or <s>Brahmā</s> in radiance; divine or divine-colored, divine in appearance or divine in radiance. Thus, O prince, the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body is pure, inconceivable even through all signs — of inconceivable teaching through the accomplishment of the form-body. It is not easy, even for the world with its gods, to grasp the measure of that body — rather, it is in all respects inconceivable, immeasurable.' ||

body.text:
atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
(Vaidya 146)
body.translated_text: Then indeed the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses: (Vaidya 146)

children.text: yadrajo lokadhātūṣu pāṃsusaṃjñānidarśanam |
children.translated_text: 'Whatever dust there is in the world-systems — designated as particles —

children.text: utsahradataḍāgeṣu samudreṣu ca yajjalam /
children.translated_text: and whatever water there is in springs, ponds, lakes, and oceans —

children.text: na teṣāṃ labhyate anto ettakā paramāṇavaḥ // SRS_22.26 //
children.translated_text: no end is found of those; such are the atoms. // SRS_22.26 //

children.text: samudrādvālakoṭībhirmātuṃ śakyaṃ jalaṃ bhavet |
children.translated_text: It might be possible to measure the water of the ocean with the tips of hairs;

children.text: na tulyā lokanāthena upamā saṃprakāśitā /
children.translated_text: but no comparison has been shown that is equal to the Lord of the World;

children.text: jalabindavo 'prameyāstathaiva paramāṇavaḥ // SRS_22.27 //
children.translated_text: the drops of water are immeasurable, and likewise the atoms. // SRS_22.27 //

children.text: paśmāmyekasya sattvasya tato bahutarānaham /
children.translated_text: I see the [aspirations] of a single being; then I see those of far more —

children.text: adhimukticittotpādo naikakāle prajānitum // SRS_22.28 //
children.translated_text: the arising of the mind of aspiration is not to be known at a single time. // SRS_22.28 //

children.text: ye mayā ātmabhāvasya bhūtavarṇā nidarśitāḥ /
children.translated_text: The true descriptions of my own being that I have shown —

children.text: sarvasattvādhimuktāstāneteṣāmupamākṣamāḥ // SRS_22.29 //
children.translated_text: they are fitting comparisons for the aspirations of all beings. // SRS_22.29 //

children.text: nimittakarmaṇā caiva varṇanirbhāsa īdṛśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Through sign-activity, such color and radiance

children.text: śakyaṃ jānituṃ buddhasya viśeṣo hīdṛśo mama // SRS_22.30 //
children.translated_text: can be known of the <s>Buddha</s> — such is my distinction. // SRS_22.30 //

children.text: nimittāpagatā buddhā dharmakāyaprabhāvitāḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddhas</s> are beyond signs, empowered by the <s>Dharmakāya</s>;

children.text: gambhīrāścāprameyāśca tena buddhā acintiyāḥ // SRS_22.31 //
children.translated_text: they are profound and immeasurable — therefore the <s>Buddhas</s> are inconceivable. // SRS_22.31 //

children.text: acintiyasya buddhasya buddhakāyo 'pyacintiyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Of the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Buddha</s>'s body too is inconceivable;

children.text: acintiyā hi te kāyā dharmakāyaprabhāvitāḥ // SRS_22.32 //
children.translated_text: inconceivable indeed are those bodies, empowered by the <s>Dharmakāya</s>. // SRS_22.32 //

children.text: cittenāpi na buddhānāṃ kāyaścintayituṃ kṣamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even by the mind, the body of the <s>Buddhas</s> cannot be conceived;

children.text: tathā hi tasya kāyasya pramāṇaṃ nopalabhyate // SRS_22.33 //
children.translated_text: for no measure of that body can be found. // SRS_22.33 //

children.text: aprameyā hi te dharmāḥ kalpakoṭyo niṣevitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Immeasurable indeed are those <s>dharmas</s>, practiced for <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: teno acintiyaḥ kāyo nirvṛto me prabhāsvaraḥ // SRS_22.34 //
children.translated_text: therefore my body is inconceivable — ceased, radiant. // SRS_22.34 //

children.text: agrāhyaḥ sarvasattvehi na pramāṇehi gṛhyate /
children.translated_text: Ungraspable by all beings, it is not grasped by any measure;

children.text: tathā hi kāyo buddhasya apramāṇo hyacintiyaḥ // SRS_22.35 //
children.translated_text: for the <s>Buddha</s>'s body is immeasurable and inconceivable. // SRS_22.35 //

children.text: apramāṇehi dharmehi pramāṇaṃ tatra kalpitam /
children.translated_text: By immeasurable <s>dharmas</s>, a measure is imagined therein;

children.text: akalpitehi dharmehi buddho 'pyevamakalpitaḥ // SRS_22.36 //
children.translated_text: by unimagined <s>dharmas</s>, the <s>Buddha</s> too is thus unimagined. // SRS_22.36 //

children.text: pramāṇaṃ kalpamākhyāto apramāṇamakalpitam /
children.translated_text: Measure is called a construction; the immeasurable is unconstructed;

children.text: akalpyaḥ kalpāpagatastena buddho acintiyaḥ // SRS_22.37 //
children.translated_text: the unconstructable, beyond construction — therefore the <s>Buddha</s> is inconceivable. // SRS_22.37 //

children.text: apramāṇaṃ yathākāśaṃ mātuṃ śakyaṃ na kenacit /
children.translated_text: Just as space is immeasurable and cannot be measured by anyone,

children.text: tathaiva kāyu buddhasya ākāśasamasādṛśaḥ // SRS_22.38 //
children.translated_text: even so is the <s>Buddha</s>'s body — like space itself. // SRS_22.38 //

children.text: ye kāyamevaṃ jānanti buddhānāṃ te jinātmajāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who know the body of the <s>Buddhas</s> thus — they are the sons of the Conquerors;

children.text: te 'pi buddhā bhaviṣyanti lokanāthā acintiyāḥ // SRS_22.39 //
children.translated_text: they too will become <s>Buddhas</s>, Lords of the World, inconceivable.' // SRS_22.39 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje tathāgatakāyanirdeśaparivarto nāma dvāviṃśatitamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: // Thus [ends] the twenty-second chapter of the glorious <s>Samādhirāja</s>, entitled 'The Chapter on the Teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s Body' (<s>Tathāgatakāyanirdeśaparivarta</s>). //

body.text:
(Vaidya 147)
23 Tathāgatācintyanirdeśaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 147) Chapter 23: <s>Tathāgatācintyanirdeśaparivarta</s> (The Chapter on the Teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s Inconceivability). |

body.text: tasmāttarhi kumāra yo bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ ākāṅkṣet kimityahaṃ catasraḥ pratisaṃvidaḥ sākṣātkuryāmiti | katamāścatasraḥ? yaduta arthapratisaṃvidaṃ dharmapratisaṃvidaṃ niruktipratisaṃvidaṃ pratibhānapratisaṃvidam | imāścatasraḥ pratisaṃvidaḥ sākṣātkuryāmiti, tena kumāra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena ayaṃ samādhirudgrahītavyaḥ partavāptavyo dhārayitavyo vācayitavyaḥ pravartayitavyaḥ uddeṣṭavyaḥ svādhyātavyo bhāvayitavyaḥ, parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayitavyaḥ | bhāvanāyogamanuyuktena ca bhavitavyam | tatra kumāra katamā dharmapratisaṃvidaḥ? imāḥ kumāra bodhisattvo dharmapratisaṃvida evaṃ pratisaṃśikṣate - yāvanto vā rūpavyāhārāstāvantastathāgatasya varṇavyāhārāḥ | evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ | yāvantaḥ kumāra vijñānavyāhārāstāvantastathāgatasya varṇavyāhārāḥ | iti hi kumāra aprameyā acintyā asaṃkhyeyāḥ atulyāmāpyāparimāṇāstathāgatasya rūpavarṇavyāhārāḥ | iti hi kumāra aparyantā anantā rūpavyāhārāḥ | evamacintyāstathāgatasya varṇavyāhārāḥ | evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ | iti hi anantā aparyantā acintyā vijñānavyāhārāḥ | evamacintyāstathāgatasya varṇavyāhārāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, O Prince, the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> who desires [this, thinking]: 'How may I directly realize the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>)?' — and what are these four? Namely: analytical knowledge of meaning (<s>arthapratisaṃvid</s>), analytical knowledge of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmapratisaṃvid</s>), analytical knowledge of etymology (<s>niruktipratisaṃvid</s>), and analytical knowledge of eloquence (<s>pratibhānapratisaṃvid</s>) — 'May I directly realize these four analytical knowledges!' — that <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s>, O Prince, should take up this <s>samādhi</s>, master it, retain it, recite it, transmit it, expound it, study it, and cultivate it, and should illuminate it in detail for others. And he should be devoted to the practice of cultivation. Now, O Prince, what is the analytical knowledge of <s>dharma</s>? Here, O Prince, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> trains in the analytical knowledge of <s>dharma</s> thus: 'As many as the designations of form (<s>rūpa</s>), so many are the designations of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s qualities. Likewise for feeling, perception, and formations. As many as the designations of consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), O Prince, so many are the designations of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s qualities.' Thus, O Prince, immeasurable, inconceivable, incalculable, incomparable, and boundless are the designations of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s form-qualities. Thus, O Prince, the designations of form are endless, infinite. Likewise inconceivable are the designations of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s qualities. Likewise for feeling, perception, and formations. Thus the designations of consciousness are infinite, endless, inconceivable. Likewise inconceivable are the designations of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s qualities.

body.text: iti hi kumāra aprameyā asaṃkhyeyāḥ saṃskṛte doṣāḥ | aprameyā asaṃkhyeyā nirvāṇe anuśaṃsāḥ | asaṃkhyeyāstathāgatasya varṇāḥ | iti hi kumāra yāvanti nirvāṇanāmāni tāvantastathāgatasya varṇāḥ | iti hi kumāra asaṃkhyeyāni nirvāṇanāmāni | asaṃkhyeyāstathāgatasya varṇāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus, O Prince, immeasurable and incalculable are the faults in the conditioned. Immeasurable and incalculable are the benefits of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Incalculable are the qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Thus, O Prince, as many as the names of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, so many are the qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Thus, O Prince, incalculable are the names of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Incalculable are the qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text:
catvāra ime kumāra tathāgatasya varṇavyāhārā acintyā acintyavyāhārāḥ | katame catvāraḥ ?yaduta acintyaḥ saṃskāravyāhāraḥ | acintyaḥ svaravyāhāraḥ | acintyaḥ saṃkleśavyāhāra | acintyo vyavadānavyāhāraḥ | ime kumāra catvārastathāgatasya varṇavyāhārā acintyā acintyavyāhārāḥ | catvāra ime kumāra tathāgatasya varṇavyāhārā acintyā acintyanirdeśāḥ | te na sukaraṃ paryantaniṣṭhāsthānena nirdeṣṭum | katame catvāraḥ? eṣa eva catuṣkaḥ | evaṃ vistareṇa nirdeṣṭavyam | yaduta catvāro bodhisattvānāṃ nayāḥ | catasro yuktayaḥ | catvāro dvārāḥ | catvāra nirdeśāḥ | catvāro ghoṣāḥ | catvāro vacanapathāḥ | catvāro vyāhārāḥ | catvāri saṃghābhāṣyāṇi | catasro nāmanidhyaptayaḥ | catasro manujanidhyaptayaḥ | catvāri prativacanāni | catvāri dvārāṇi | catvāryakṣarāṇi | catvāro 'vatārāḥ | catvāraḥ padāḥ | catvāri nirhārapadāni | catvāraḥ sūtrāntapadāḥ | catvāraścaryāpathāḥ | catvāro 'cintyapathāḥ | catvāraḥ tulyapathāḥ | catvāro 'nantapathāḥ | catvāro 'paryantapathāḥ | catvāro 'saṃkhyeyapathāḥ | catvāro 'prameyapathāḥ | catvāro 'parimāṇapathāḥ |(Vaidya 148) catvḥri jñḥnḥni | catvḥro jñḥnasaṃcayḥḥ | catvḥri jñḥnagotrḥṇi | catvḥri pratibhḥnḥni | catvḥraḥ pratibhḥnasaṃcayḥḥ | catvḥri pratibhḥnagotrḥṇi | catvḥraḥ sūtrḥntasaṃcayḥḥ | catvḥri pratibhḥnakaraṇḥni | catvḥraḥ sūtrḥntanirhḥrḥḥ | catvḥri bḥhuśrutyagotrḥṇi | catvḥri buddhadhanḥni | catasro bodhisattvaśikṣḥḥ | catvḥro bodhisattvagocarḥḥ | catvḥri bodhisattvakarmḥṇi | catvḥri bodhisattvapratibhḥnḥni | catasro mḥrgabhḥvanḥḥ | catvḥri kleśaprahḥṇḥni | catvḥryapḥyajahanḥni | catvḥryajñḥnavidhamanḥni | catvḥryavidyḥprahḥṇḥni | catvḥri duḥkhopaśamanḥni | catvḥri daurmanasyaprahḥṇḥni | catvḥryupḥyasaṃjananḥni | catvḥri dṛṣṭiprahḥṇḥni | catvḥryupapannaparijñḥnḥni | catvḥryḥtmadṛṣṭiprahḥṇḥni | catvḥri sattvadṛṣṭiprahḥṇḥni | catvḥri jīvadṛṣṭiprahḥṇḥni | catvḥri pudgaladṛṣṭiprahḥṇḥni | catvḥri bhavadṛṣṭiprahḥṇḥni | catvḥri vastuprahḥṇḥni | catvḥryupalambhadṛṣṭiprahḥṇḥni | te na sukaraṃ
paryantasthḥnena nirdeṣṭam ||
body.translated_text: There are, O Prince, four inconceivable designations of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s qualities, four inconceivable expressions. What are the four? Namely: inconceivable is the designation of conditioned formations; inconceivable is the designation of sounds; inconceivable is the designation of defilement; inconceivable is the designation of purification. These, O Prince, are the four inconceivable designations of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s qualities, four inconceivable expressions. There are, O Prince, four inconceivable designations of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s qualities, four inconceivable expositions. They cannot easily be expounded to their final limit. What are the four? The same four. They should be expounded in detail thus: namely, four methods of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; four reasonings; four gateways; four expositions; four sounds; four speech-paths; four expressions; four congregational statements; four ascertainments of names; four ascertainments of persons; four replies; four entrances; four syllables; four entries; four words; four derivation-words; four <s>sūtrānta</s>-words; four conduct-paths; four inconceivable paths; four equal paths; four infinite paths; four limitless paths; four incalculable paths; four immeasurable paths; four inestimable paths; (Vaidya 148) four knowledges; four accumulations of knowledge; four families of knowledge; four types of eloquence; four accumulations of eloquence; four families of eloquence; four accumulations of <s>sūtrāntas</s>; four instruments of eloquence; four derivations of <s>sūtrāntas</s>; four families of great learning; four <s>Buddha</s>-treasures; four trainings of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; four domains of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; four actions of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; four types of <s>Bodhisattva</s> eloquence; four path-cultivations; four abandonments of afflictions; four abandonments of lower rebirths; four dispersals of ignorance; four abandonments of <s>avidyā</s> (nescience); four calming of sufferings; four abandonments of dejection; four generations of skillful means; four abandonments of views; four comprehensions of rebirth; four abandonments of the view of self; four abandonments of the view of beings; four abandonments of the view of a life-principle; four abandonments of the view of a person; four abandonments of the view of existence; four abandonments of objects; four abandonments of the view of apprehension. They cannot easily be expounded to their final limit.

body.text: catasro dhāraṇyaḥ | katamāścatasraḥ? yaduta anantaḥ sarvasaṃskāraparibhāṣāvyāhāraḥ | tatra yajjñānamiyaṃ prathamā dhāraṇī | anantaḥ svaraparibhāṣāvyāhāraḥ | tatra yajjñānamiyaṃ dvitīyā dhāraṇī | anantaḥ saṃkleśaparibhāṣāvyāhāraḥ | tatra yajjñānamiyaṃ tṛtīyā dhāraṇī | ananto vyavadānaguṇānuśaṃsāvyāhāraḥ | tatra yajjñānamiyaṃ caturthī dhāraṇī | imāścatasro dhāraṇyaḥ | iti hi yā kumāra dhāraṇī tajjñānam, sa dharmaḥ | iti hi dharmajñānena dharmapratisaṃvit ||
body.translated_text: There are four <s>dhāraṇīs</s> (mnemonic retentions). What are the four? Namely: infinite is the designation of the paraphrase of all conditioned formations; the knowledge therein is the first <s>dhāraṇī</s>. Infinite is the designation of the paraphrase of sounds; the knowledge therein is the second <s>dhāraṇī</s>. Infinite is the designation of the paraphrase of defilement; the knowledge therein is the third <s>dhāraṇī</s>. Infinite is the designation of the benefits of purification-qualities; the knowledge therein is the fourth <s>dhāraṇī</s>. These are the four <s>dhāraṇīs</s>. Thus, O Prince, the <s>dhāraṇī</s> is that knowledge; that is the <s>dharma</s>. Thus, through the knowledge of <s>dharma</s>, there is the analytical knowledge of <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: dharmajñāne yo 'rthaḥ, iyamucyate arthapratisaṃvit | dharmajñāne yacchandaḥ, iyamucyate niruktipratisaṃvit | dharmajñāne yā vyavahāradeśanā ācakṣaṇā prajñapanā prakāśanā prasthāpanā vicaraṇā vibhajanā uttānīkaraṇatā asaktavacanatā anelāmūkavacanatā anavalīnavacanatā, iyamucyate pratibhānapratisaṃvit ||
body.translated_text: The meaning that is in the knowledge of <s>dharma</s> — this is called the analytical knowledge of meaning. The linguistic intention that is in the knowledge of <s>dharma</s> — this is called the analytical knowledge of etymology. The teaching of conventions in the knowledge of <s>dharma</s> — the explaining, describing, designating, illuminating, setting forth, investigating, analyzing, making clear, unobstructed speech, non-stammering speech, unhesitating speech — this is called the analytical knowledge of eloquence.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One at that time spoke these verses:

children.text: yāttakaṃ jñānu buddhasya rūpaprajñapti tāttikā /
children.translated_text: 'As great as the <s>Buddha</s>'s knowledge, so great is the designation of form;

children.text: yāvatī rūpaprajñapti rūpavyāhāra tāttakā // SRS_23.1 //
children.translated_text: as great as the designation of form, so great is the expression of form. // SRS_23.1 //

children.text: yāvanto rūpavyāhārāḥ śīlanāmāni tāttakāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'As many as the expressions of form, so many are the names of moral conduct;

children.text: yāvanti śīlanāmāni buddhanāmāni tāttakāḥ // SRS_23.2 //
children.translated_text: as many as the names of moral conduct, so many are the names of a <s>Buddha</s>. // SRS_23.2 //

children.text: yāttakā buddhanāmāni sattvanāmāni tāttakāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'As many as the names of a <s>Buddha</s>, so many are the names of beings;

children.text: ettakānyekasattvasya ahaṃ nāmāni jānami // SRS_23.3 //
children.translated_text: that many names of a single being do I know! // SRS_23.3 //

children.text: anantā nāmavyāhārā ye me pūrvaṃ prakāśitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Infinite are the name-expressions that were formerly illuminated by me;

children.text: śīlanāmā buddhanāmā sattvanāmā ca te samāḥ // SRS_23.4 //
children.translated_text: the names of moral conduct, the names of a <s>Buddha</s>, and the names of beings — they are all equal. // SRS_23.4 //

children.text: yāttakāḥ saṃskṛte doṣā nirvāṇe tāttakā guṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'As many as the faults in the conditioned, so many are the virtues in <s>nirvāṇa</s>;

children.text: buddhasya tāttakā varṇā aupamyā me prakāśitāḥ // SRS_23.5 //
children.translated_text: so many are the qualities of a <s>Buddha</s> — illustrated by me through similes. // SRS_23.5 //

children.text: yāttakāḥ sarvasattvānāṃ cittotpādā nidarśitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'As many as the mental arisings of all beings that have been shown,

children.text: tāttakā lokanāthasya ekaromāta raśmayaḥ // SRS_23.6 //
children.translated_text: so many are the rays from a single hair-pore of the Lord of the World! // SRS_23.6 //

children.text: (Vaidya 149)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 149)

children.text: nāmāśca adhimuktiśca sarvasattvāna yāttikāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The names and the aspirations of all beings — as many as they are,

children.text: tato bhūyo narendrasya svarāṅgavarṇa bhāṣitāḥ // SRS_23.7 //
children.translated_text: even more than that have the vocal qualities of the Lord of Men been spoken! // SRS_23.7 //

children.text: ye nāmāḥ sarvasattvānāmekasattvasya darśitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The names of all beings that have been shown for a single being —

children.text: ekasattvasya te nāmāḥ sarvasattvāna darśitāḥ // SRS_23.8 //
children.translated_text: the names of a single being have been shown as the names of all beings. // SRS_23.8 //

children.text: pratisaṃvidānāmottāra ayaṃ buddhena deśitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This explication of the analytical knowledges has been taught by the <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: anantanāmanirdeśā bodhisattvāna kāraṇāt // SRS_23.9 //
children.translated_text: with infinite expositions of names, for the sake of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. // SRS_23.9 //

children.text: ya icchet kathaṃ bhāṣeyyā sūtrakoṭīranantikāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He who would wish to speak infinite <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>sūtras</s> —

children.text: idaṃ sūtraṃ pravartitvā anolīnaḥ prakāśayet // SRS_23.10 //
children.translated_text: having set this <s>sūtra</s> in motion, let him illuminate [them] undaunted! // SRS_23.10 //

children.text: asaktaḥ pariṣanmadhye sūtrakoṭīḥ prabhāṣate /
children.translated_text: 'Unattached, in the midst of the assembly, he speaks <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>sūtras</s>;

children.text: yathākāśamaparyantamevaṃ dharmaṃ sa bhāṣate // SRS_23.11 //
children.translated_text: just as space is without limit — so does he speak the <s>dharma</s>. // SRS_23.11 //

children.text: emeva bodhisattvānāṃ śuddhasattvāna tāyinām /
children.translated_text: 'Thus for those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, pure beings, protectors —

children.text: idaṃ sūtraṃ samudgṛhya bhavanti jñānasaṃpadaḥ // SRS_23.12 //
children.translated_text: having taken up this <s>sūtra</s>, they attain the perfection of knowledge. // SRS_23.12 //

children.text: yathā yathā prakāśenti śraddadhanto imaṃ nayam /
children.translated_text: 'The more they illuminate [it], having faith in this method,

children.text: tathāsya vardhate jñānaṃ himavanteva pādapāḥ // SRS_23.13 //
children.translated_text: the more their knowledge grows — like trees on the <s>Himavat</s> (Himālaya)!' // SRS_23.13 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje tathāgatācintyanirdeśaparivartastrayoviṃśatitamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-third chapter in the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, the chapter called 'Exposition of the Inconceivable [Qualities] of the <s>Tathāgata</s>' (<s>Tathāgatācintyanirdeśaparivarta</s>).

body.text:
(Vaidya 150)
24 Pratisaṃvidavatāraparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 150) Chapter 24: The <s>Pratisaṃvidavatāraparivarta</s> (Chapter on Entry into the Analytical Knowledges).

body.text: tatra kumāra kathaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvo dharmapratisaṃvidi caran dharmeṣu dharmānupaśyī samudāgacchatyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau? iha kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvo dharmeṣu dharmānupaśyī nānyatra rūpeṇa bodhiṃ samanupaśyati | nānyatra rūpādvodhāya carati | nānyatra rūpeṇa bodhiṃ paryeṣate | nānyatra rūpeṇa bodhāya samudāgacchati | nānyatra rūpeṇa sattvāni bodhāya samādāpayati | nānyatra rūpeṇa tathāgataṃ paśyati | rūpasyāvināśasvabhāvaḥ tathāgata iti tathāgataṃ paśyati | anyad rūpamanyo rūpasvabhāva iti naivaṃ paśyati | anyo rūpasvabhāvo 'nyastathāgata iti naivaṃ paśyati | yaśca rūpasvabhāvo yaśca tathāgata ityadvayeyaṃ dharmatā | evaṃ paśyan bodhisattvo mahāsattvaścarati dharmapratisaṃvidi | evaṃ nānyatra vedanāyā nānyatra saṃjñāyā nānyatra saṃskārebhyo nānyatra vijñānena bodhiṃ samanupaśyati | nānyatra vijñānādbodhāya carati | nānyatra vijñānena bodhiṃ paryeṣate | nānyatra vijñānena bodhāya samudāgacchati | nānyatra vijñānena sattvāni bodhāya samādāpayati | nānyatra vijñānena tathāgataṃ paśyati | vijñānasyāvināśasvabhāvastathāgata iti tathāgataṃ paśyati | anyadvijñānamanyo vijñānasvabhāva iti naivaṃ paśyati | anyo vijñānasvabhāvo 'nyastathāgata iti naivaṃ paśyati | yaśca vijñānasvabhāvo yaśca tathāgata ityadvayeyaṃ dharmatā | evaṃ paśyan bodhisattvo mahāsattvaścarati dharmapratisaṃvidi ||
body.translated_text: Now, O Prince, how does the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s>, practicing in the analytical knowledge of <s>dharma</s>, contemplating <s>dharmas</s> among <s>dharmas</s>, attain unsurpassed, perfect <s>saṃbodhi</s>? Here, O Prince, the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s>, contemplating <s>dharmas</s> among <s>dharmas</s>, does not perceive <s>bodhi</s> apart from form. He does not practice for <s>bodhi</s> apart from form. He does not seek <s>bodhi</s> apart from form. He does not attain <s>bodhi</s> apart from form. He does not encourage beings toward <s>bodhi</s> apart from form. He does not see the <s>Tathāgata</s> apart from form. He sees the <s>Tathāgata</s> as: 'The indestructible own-nature of form is the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' He does not see it thus: 'Form is one thing, the own-nature of form is another.' He does not see it thus: 'The own-nature of form is one thing, the <s>Tathāgata</s> is another.' That which is the own-nature of form and that which is the <s>Tathāgata</s> — this <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) is non-dual. Seeing thus, the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> practices the analytical knowledge of <s>dharma</s>. Likewise, he does not perceive <s>bodhi</s> apart from feeling, apart from perception, apart from formations, apart from consciousness. He does not practice for <s>bodhi</s> apart from consciousness. He does not seek <s>bodhi</s> apart from consciousness. He does not attain <s>bodhi</s> apart from consciousness. He does not encourage beings toward <s>bodhi</s> apart from consciousness. He does not see the <s>Tathāgata</s> apart from consciousness. He sees the <s>Tathāgata</s> as: 'The indestructible own-nature of consciousness is the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' He does not see it thus: 'Consciousness is one thing, the own-nature of consciousness is another.' He does not see it thus: 'The own-nature of consciousness is one thing, the <s>Tathāgata</s> is another.'
