That which is the own-nature of consciousness and that which is the <s>Tathāgata</s> — this <s>dharmatā</s> is non-dual. Seeing thus, the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> practices the analytical knowledge of <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One at that time spoke these verses:

children.text: rūpeṇa darśitā bodhī bodhaye rūpa darśitam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Bodhi</s> has been shown through form; form has been shown for the sake of <s>bodhi</s>;

children.text: visabhāgena śabdena uttaro dharma deśitaḥ // SRS_24.1 //
children.translated_text: through a dissimilar sound, the superior <s>dharma</s> has been taught. // SRS_24.1 //

children.text: śabdena uttaraṃ rūpaṃ gambhīraṃ ca svabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Through sound, the superior form [is shown], profound by its own nature;

children.text: samaṃ rūpaṃ ca bodhiśca nānātvaṃ nāsya labhyate // SRS_24.2 //
children.translated_text: form and <s>bodhi</s> are equal — no difference in them can be found. // SRS_24.2 //

children.text: yathā nirvāṇa gambhīraṃ śabdenāsaṃprakāśitam /
children.translated_text: 'Just as <s>nirvāṇa</s> is profound, not illuminated by sound,

children.text: labhyate na ca nirvāṇaṃ sa ca śabdo na labhyate // SRS_24.3 //
children.translated_text: and <s>nirvāṇa</s> cannot be found — that sound too cannot be found. // SRS_24.3 //

children.text: śabdaścāpyatha nirvāṇamubhayaṃ tanna labhyate /
children.translated_text: 'Sound and also <s>nirvāṇa</s> — both of them cannot be found;

children.text: evaṃ śūnyeṣu dharmeṣu nirvāṇaṃ saṃprakāśitam // SRS_24.4 //
children.translated_text: thus, in empty <s>dharmas</s>, <s>nirvāṇa</s> has been illuminated. // SRS_24.4 //

children.text: nirvāṇaṃ nirvṛtī vuttā nirvāṇaṃ ca na labhyate /
children.translated_text: '<s>Nirvāṇa</s> has been called cessation; yet <s>nirvāṇa</s> cannot be found;

children.text: apravṛttyaiva dharmāṇāṃ yathā paścāttathā purā // SRS_24.5 //
children.translated_text: by the very non-occurrence of <s>dharmas</s> — as it is afterward, so it is before. // SRS_24.5 //

children.text: sarvadharmāḥ svabhāvena nirvāṇasamasādṛśāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'All <s>dharmas</s> by their own nature are equal to and similar to <s>nirvāṇa</s>;

children.text: jñātā naiṣkramyasārehi ye yuktā buddhaśāsane // SRS_24.6 //
children.translated_text: this is known by those whose essence is renunciation, who are devoted to the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching. // SRS_24.6 //

children.text: (Vaidya 151)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 151)

children.text: paśyitvā kāyu buddhasya vakṣyante dṛṣṭu nāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having seen the body of the <s>Buddha</s>, they will say: "The Leader has been seen!"

children.text: na cāhaṃ rūpakāyena paśyituṃ śakya kenacit // SRS_24.7 //
children.translated_text: But I cannot be seen through the form-body by anyone. // SRS_24.7 //

children.text: jñātaḥ svabhāvo rūpasya yādṛśaṃ rūpalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: 'The own-nature of form has been known — such is the characteristic of form;

children.text: rūpasvabhāvamājñāya kāyo mama nideśitaḥ // SRS_24.8 //
children.translated_text: having understood the own-nature of form, my body has been pointed out. // SRS_24.8 //

children.text: evaṃ pañcāna skandhānāṃ jñānaṃ me dharmalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: 'Thus my knowledge of the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) is the characteristic of <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: jñātvā svabhāvaṃ dharmāṇāṃ dharmakāye pratiṣṭhitaḥ // SRS_24.9 //
children.translated_text: having known the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s>, one is established in the <s>Dharmakāya</s>. // SRS_24.9 //

children.text: deśemi dharma sattvānāṃ dharmakāye 'pyaniḥsṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I teach the <s>dharma</s> for beings, yet I have not departed from the <s>Dharmakāya</s> —'

children.text: na ca dharmata buddhānāṃ śakyaṃ vācāya bhāṣitum // SRS_24.10 //
children.translated_text: nor can the <s>dharmatā</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> be expressed in words.' // SRS_24.10 //

children.text: imaṃ nayamajānanto buddhaśabdaṃ śruṇitva te /
children.translated_text: 'Not knowing this method, having heard the word "<s>Buddha</s>,"

children.text: ghoṣamātreṇa vakṣyanti dṛṣṭo me naranāyakaḥ // SRS_24.11 //
children.translated_text: they will say by mere sound: "The Leader of men has been seen by me."' // SRS_24.11 //

children.text: sarvasaṃjñāprahīṇasya bhavasaṃjñā vigacchati /
children.translated_text: 'For one who has abandoned all perceptions, the perception of existence vanishes;

children.text: na jātu śabdasaṃjñasya bhavate śāstṛdarśanam // SRS_24.12 //
children.translated_text: for one who has the perception of [mere] sound, there is never a seeing of the Teacher.' // SRS_24.12 //

children.text: yaḥ śūnyatāṃ prajānāti īdṛśaṃ rūpalakṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: 'One who understands emptiness — such is the characteristic of form;

children.text: na cānyā śūnyatā uktā anyā rūpasvabhāvatā /
children.translated_text: emptiness is not said to be other [than form], nor is the own-nature of form [other than emptiness];

children.text: yastu rūpaṃ prajānāti sa prajānāti śunyatām // SRS_24.13 //
children.translated_text: one who understands form, understands emptiness.' // SRS_24.13 //

children.text: yaḥ śūnyatāṃ prajānāti īdṛśaṃ rūpalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: 'One who understands emptiness — such is the characteristic of form —

children.text: na cāsau mārakoṭībhirbhūyaḥ śakya parājitum // SRS_24.14 //
children.translated_text: he cannot again be defeated by <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Māras</s>.' // SRS_24.14 //

children.text: prajānāti hi yo rūpaṃ sa prajānāti śūnyatām /
children.translated_text: 'One who understands form, understands emptiness;

children.text: ya śūnyatāṃ prajānāti sa prajānāti nirvṛtim // SRS_24.15 //
children.translated_text: one who understands emptiness, understands <s>nirvāṇa</s>.' // SRS_24.15 //

children.text: imāṃ gatimajānantaḥ pranaṣṭā aupalambhikāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Not knowing this path, those who grasp at [real] existence are lost;

children.text: abhāve bhāvasaṃjñeyo bhāve cābhāvasaṃjñinaḥ // SRS_24.16 //
children.translated_text: they have the perception of existence in non-existence, and the perception of non-existence in existence.' // SRS_24.16 //

children.text: vañcitā jñātralābhena pranaṣṭā mama śāsanāt /
children.translated_text: 'Deceived by gaining relatives [and followers], they are lost from my teaching;

children.text: phalasaṃjñā avasthāne riktāḥ śrāmaṇakāddhanāt // SRS_24.17 //
children.translated_text: having the perception of fruit in [mere] position — they are empty of the wealth of the ascetic life.' // SRS_24.17 //

children.text: kusīdā hīnavīryāśca śīlaskandhe asaṃsthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Lazy, of feeble vigor, not established in the aggregate of morality —

children.text: paryupthitāśca vakṣyanti na etad buddhaśāsanam // SRS_24.18 //
children.translated_text: overwhelmed [by defilements], they will say: "This is not the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching!"' // SRS_24.18 //

children.text: kecidevaṃ pravakṣyanti vayaṃ bodhāya prasthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Some will declare thus: "We have set out for awakening!" —

children.text: adāntā avinītāśca parasparamagauravāḥ // SRS_24.19 //
children.translated_text: yet [they are] untamed, undisciplined, without mutual respect.' // SRS_24.19 //

children.text: śabdakāmā bhaviṣyanti dharme caivānavasthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'They will desire fame and will not be established in <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: evaṃ sā bheṣyate icchā jñātralābhagaveṣaṇe // SRS_24.20 //
children.translated_text: thus their desire will be [directed] toward seeking relatives and gain.' // SRS_24.20 //

children.text: lābhakāmā bhaviṣyanti saṃnipāte hi cintakāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'They will desire gain, scheming in assemblies,

children.text: madapramādābhibhūtā lābhasatkāra arthikāḥ // SRS_24.21 //
children.translated_text: overcome by intoxication and heedlessness, desiring gain and honor.' // SRS_24.21 //

children.text: (Vaidya 152)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 152)

children.text: niḥsṛtā lābhasatkāre jñātralābhagaveṣiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Gone forth [yet] seeking gain and honor, seekers of relatives and profit,

children.text: stūpān vihārān kāhenti kulastrīṣvadhimūrcchitāḥ // SRS_24.22 //
children.translated_text: they will build <s>stūpas</s> and monasteries — infatuated with women of good families.' // SRS_24.22 //

children.text: niḥsṛtāścopalambhasmin kāmatṛṣṇāsu niḥsṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Gone forth yet caught in grasping, gone forth yet caught in sensual craving —

children.text: gṛhikarma kariṣyanti mārasya viṣaye sthitāḥ // SRS_24.23 //
children.translated_text: they will do the work of householders, stationed in <s>Māra</s>'s domain.' // SRS_24.23 //

children.text: gṛhiṇāṃ deśayiṣyanti kāmā agniśikhopamāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'They will teach householders: "Desires are like the tip of a flame!" —

children.text: praviśya ca gṛhāṃsteṣāṃ dūṣayiṣyanti tān kulān // SRS_24.24 //
children.translated_text: yet entering those households, they will corrupt those families.' // SRS_24.24 //

children.text: gṛhiṇaśca bhaviṣyanti teṣu śāstārasaṃjñinaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And the householders will regard them as teachers;

children.text: teṣāṃ ca vipravustānāṃ putradārāṇi dūṣayi // SRS_24.25 //
children.translated_text: and in their absence, those [monks] will corrupt their wives and children.' // SRS_24.25 //

children.text: ye teṣāmannapānena kariṣyanti anugraham /
children.translated_text: 'Those who help them with food and drink —

children.text: teṣāṃ tatputradāreṣu bhāryāsaṃjñā bhaviṣyati // SRS_24.26 //
children.translated_text: toward their wives and children, the perception of "wife" will arise [in those monks].' // SRS_24.26 //

children.text: gṛhiṇo na svadāreṣu bhaviṣyantyadhimūrcchitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The householders will not be as infatuated with their own wives

children.text: yathā te pravrajitvā hi paradāreṣu mūrcchitāḥ // SRS_24.27 //
children.translated_text: as those [monks], having gone forth, are infatuated with others' wives.' // SRS_24.27 //

children.text: śikṣāvadātavastrāṇaṃ gṛhīṇaṃ yā mi darśitā /
children.translated_text: 'The training I taught for lay followers in white garments —

children.text: sā śikṣā teṣāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ tasmin kāle na bheṣyati // SRS_24.28 //
children.translated_text: that training will not exist for those monks at that time.' // SRS_24.28 //

children.text: bherīśaṅkhamṛdaṅgehi pūjāṃ kāhenti te mama /
children.translated_text: 'With drums, conches, and <s>mṛdaṅgas</s> they will perform worship of me —

children.text: yā ca sā uttamā pūjā pratipattirna bheṣyati // SRS_24.29 //
children.translated_text: but that supreme worship which is [actual] practice will not exist.' // SRS_24.29 //

children.text: te ātmanā suduḥśīlā dṛṣṭvā śīlapratiṣṭhitān /
children.translated_text: 'They themselves, of poor morality, seeing those established in morality,

children.text: anyonyamevaṃ vakṣyanti ete 'pi yādṛśā vayam // SRS_24.30 //
children.translated_text: will say to one another: "Those are no different from us."' // SRS_24.30 //

children.text: śrutvā śīlasya te varṇaṃ duḥśīlāḥ pāpagocarāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having heard the praise of morality, those of poor morality and evil conduct —

children.text: paryutthitāśca vakṣyanti naivaitadbuddhabhāṣitam // SRS_24.31 //
children.translated_text: overwhelmed, they will say: "This is not spoken by the <s>Buddha</s>!"' // SRS_24.31 //

children.text: na ca hrī bheṣyate teṣāṃ naṣṭaṃ śrāmaṇakaṃ dhanam /
children.translated_text: 'They will have no shame; the wealth of the ascetic life is lost;

children.text: coditābhūtavācāya buddhabodhiṃ pratikṣiti // SRS_24.32 //
children.translated_text: urged on by false speech, they will reject <s>Buddha</s>-awakening.' // SRS_24.32 //

children.text: teṣāṃ vyāpannacittānāmutsṛṣṭvā buddhaśāsanam /
children.translated_text: 'For those of corrupted minds, having abandoned the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching,

children.text: dharmaṃ pratikṣipitvā ca vāso 'vīcau bhaviṣyati // SRS_24.33 //
children.translated_text: and having rejected the <s>Dharma</s> — their dwelling will be in <s>Avīci</s>.' // SRS_24.33 //

children.text: na me śrutaṃ ca dṛṣṭaṃ vā yeṣāmetādṛśī carī /
children.translated_text: '"Neither heard nor seen by me is one whose conduct is like this,

children.text: te buddhajñānaṃ lapsyante bāladharmapratiṣṭhitāḥ // SRS_24.34 //
children.translated_text: yet they will attain <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge" — those established in the <s>dharma</s> of fools!' // SRS_24.34 //

children.text: yā teṣāṃ kuhanā tatra śāṭhiyaṃ vākkiyaṃ tadā /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever deception is among them there, whatever fraud and quarreling at that time —

children.text: jānāmi tadahaṃ sarvaṃ jñānaṃ me 'tra pravartate // SRS_24.35 //
children.translated_text: I know all of that; my knowledge operates there.' // SRS_24.35 //

children.text: sacet kalpaṃ prabhāṣeyaṃ yatteṣāṃ skhalitaṃ pṛthu /
children.translated_text: 'Even if I were to speak for a <s>kalpa</s> about their manifold failings —

children.text: bodhisattvapratijñānāṃ kiṃcinmātraṃ prakīrtitam // SRS_24.36 //
children.translated_text: of those who claim the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vow — only a small portion would be described.' // SRS_24.36 //

children.text: nāsti pāpamakartavyaṃ kumārā teṣa bheṣyati /
children.translated_text: 'There is no evil that they, O prince, will not commit;

children.text: mā tehi saṃstavaṃ sārdhaṃ kuryāstvaṃ kāli paścime // SRS_24.37 //
children.translated_text: do not engage in intimacy with them in the final age.' // SRS_24.37 //

children.text: (Vaidya 153)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 153)

children.text: ālapet saṃlapeyyāsi kuryāsī teṣu gauravam /
children.translated_text: 'You should address them, speak with them, show them respect;

children.text: anolīnaḥ satkareyyāsi agrabodhīya kāraṇāt // SRS_24.38 //
children.translated_text: without being withdrawn, you should honor them — for the sake of supreme awakening.' // SRS_24.38 //

children.text: varṣāgraṃ paripṛcchitvā yaste vṛddhataro bhavet /
children.translated_text: 'Having inquired about seniority in rains [years of ordination], whoever is more senior —

children.text: kuryā hi gauravaṃ tatra śirasā pādavandanam // SRS_24.39 //
children.translated_text: you should show reverence there, bowing at their feet with your head.' // SRS_24.39 //

children.text: na teṣāṃ skhalitaṃ paśyedvodhimaṇḍa vipaśyatām /
children.translated_text: 'Do not look at their failings while keeping the seat of awakening in view;

children.text: pratighātaṃ na janayet maitracittaḥ sadā bhavet // SRS_24.40 //
children.translated_text: do not generate hostility — always be of a mind of loving-kindness.' // SRS_24.40 //

children.text: yadyeṣāṃ skhalitaṃ paśyeddoṣāṃsteṣāṃ na kīrtayet /
children.translated_text: 'Even if you see their failings, do not proclaim their faults;

children.text: yādṛśaṃ kāhitī karma lapsyate tādṛśaṃ phalam // SRS_24.41 //
children.translated_text: whatever <s>karma</s> one performs, one will receive a corresponding fruit.' // SRS_24.41 //

children.text: smitena mukhacandreṇa vṛddheṣu navakeṣu ca /
children.translated_text: 'With a smiling moon-face, toward seniors and juniors alike,

children.text: pūrvābhāṣī bhavennityaṃ hatamānaśca sūrataḥ // SRS_24.42 //
children.translated_text: always be the first to speak — with pride destroyed, a hero.' // SRS_24.42 //

children.text: cīvaraiḥ piṇḍapātaiśca kuryāsteṣāmanugraham /
children.translated_text: 'With robes and alms-food, help them;

children.text: evaṃ cittaṃ pradadhyāstvaṃ sarve bheṣyanti nāyakāḥ // SRS_24.43 //
children.translated_text: thus generate the thought: "All shall become Leaders."' // SRS_24.43 //

children.text: adhyeṣyeyuryadi tvāṃ te dharmadānasya kāraṇāt /
children.translated_text: 'If they should request you for the gift of <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: prathamaṃ vācaṃ bhāṣeyyā nāhaṃ vaipulyaśikṣitaḥ // SRS_24.44 //
children.translated_text: first speak these words: "I am not trained in the extensive [teachings]."' // SRS_24.44 //

children.text: evaṃ tvaṃ vāca bhāṣeyyā āyuṣmān vijña paṇḍitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Thus you should speak: "The venerable one is wise and learned;

children.text: kathaṃ mahātmanāṃ śakyaṃ purato bhāṣituṃ mayā // SRS_24.45 //
children.translated_text: how could I speak before great-souled ones?"' // SRS_24.45 //

children.text: sahasaiṣāṃ na jalpeta tulayitvā ca bhājanam /
children.translated_text: 'Do not speak suddenly to them; rather, assess whether [they are] a [fit] vessel;

children.text: yadi bhājanaṃ vijānīyā anadhīṣṭo 'pi deśayet // SRS_24.46 //
children.translated_text: if you know [them to be] a vessel, teach even without being invited.' // SRS_24.46 //

children.text: yadi duḥśīla paśyesi pariṣāyāṃ bahusthitān /
children.translated_text: 'If you see many of poor morality established in the assembly,

children.text: saṃlekhaṃ mā prabhāṣestvāṃ varṇaṃ dānasya kīrtayeḥ // SRS_24.47 //
children.translated_text: do not speak of austerity — rather, proclaim the praise of generosity.' // SRS_24.47 //

children.text: bhaveyuryadi vālpecchāḥ śuddhāḥ śīle pratiṣṭhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'If they should be of few desires, pure, established in morality,

children.text: maitraṃ cittaṃ janitvā tvaṃ kuryāḥ saṃlekhikīṃ kathām // SRS_24.48 //
children.translated_text: having generated a mind of loving-kindness, give a discourse on austerity.' // SRS_24.48 //

children.text: parīttā yadi pāpecchā śīlavanto bahū bhavet /
children.translated_text: 'If those of evil desires are few and the moral are many,

children.text: labdhapakṣastadā bhūtvā varṇaṃ śīlasya kīrtayet // SRS_24.49 //
children.translated_text: then, having gained support, proclaim the praise of morality.' // SRS_24.49 //

children.text: pūrvaṃ pariṣadaṃ jñātvā yadi śuddhā bhavettadā /
children.translated_text: 'First know the assembly — if it is pure,

children.text: yāvantaḥ kuśalā dharmāḥ sarvāṃstebhyaḥ prakāśayet // SRS_24.50 //
children.translated_text: then illumine for them all the wholesome <s>dharmas</s>.' // SRS_24.50 //

children.text: dānaṃ śīlaṃ tathā kṣāntiṃ vīryaṃ dhyānaṃ śrutaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: 'Generosity, morality, patience, vigor, <s>dhyāna</s>, and learning,

children.text: saṃtuṣṭyalpecchasaṃlekhān varṇayet kīrtayet sadā // SRS_24.51 //
children.translated_text: contentment, few desires, austerity — always praise and proclaim [these].' // SRS_24.51 //

children.text: araṇyavāsaṃ dhyānasukhaṃ gaṇavāsavivarjanam /
children.translated_text: 'Forest-dwelling, the happiness of meditation, avoidance of group-living —

children.text: eteṣāṃ varṇa bhāṣeta evaṃ hi dhārayet sukham // SRS_24.52 //
children.translated_text: speak the praise of these; thus one will uphold [the teaching] with happiness.' // SRS_24.52 //

children.text: araṇyavāsa no riñcenna śīlaparamo bhavet /
children.translated_text: 'Do not abandon forest-dwelling; do not be one whose highest [concern] is morality [alone];

children.text: pratisaṃlānu seveta na dānaparamo bhavet // SRS_24.53 //
children.translated_text: practice seclusion; do not be one whose highest [concern] is generosity [alone].' // SRS_24.53 //

children.text: (Vaidya 154)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 154)

children.text: śīlaskandhe sthihitvā ca bāhuśrutyamupārjayet /
children.translated_text: 'Established in the aggregate of morality, acquire learning;

children.text: imaṃ samādhimeṣantaḥ pūjayecchāstṛdhātavaḥ // SRS_24.54 //
children.translated_text: seeking this <s>samādhi</s>, worship the relics of the Teacher.' // SRS_24.54 //

children.text: chatrairdhvajaiḥ patākābhirgandhamālyavilepanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'With parasols, banners, pennants, perfumes, garlands, and ointments,

children.text: kārayet pūja buddhasya samādhiṃ śāntameṣatā // SRS_24.55 //
children.translated_text: perform worship of the <s>Buddha</s>, seeking the peaceful <s>samādhi</s>.' // SRS_24.55 //

children.text: rañjanīyehi tūryehi saṃgītiṃ saṃprayojayet /
children.translated_text: 'With delightful instruments, put on musical concerts;

children.text: pūjayeddhātuṃ buddhasya anolīno atandritaḥ // SRS_24.56 //
children.translated_text: worship the <s>Buddha</s>-relics, without being withdrawn, without weariness.' // SRS_24.56 //

children.text: yāvanti gandhamālyāni dhūpanaṃ cūrṇa cailikam /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever perfumes and garlands, incense, powders, and cloth [there are] —

children.text: sarvaistaiḥ pūjayennāthaṃ buddhajñānasya kāraṇāt // SRS_24.57 //
children.translated_text: with all of these, worship the Protector for the sake of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge.' // SRS_24.57 //

children.text: yāvatī kācit pūjāsti aprameyā acintiyā /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever worship there is — immeasurable, inconceivable —

children.text: kuryāstāḥ sarvabuddhānāṃ samādhiṃ śāntameṣatāḥ // SRS_24.58 //
children.translated_text: perform all of it for all <s>Buddhas</s>, seeking the peaceful <s>samādhi</s>.' // SRS_24.58 //

children.text: pratyaṃśaṃ sarvasattvebhyaḥ samaṃ dadyādaniśritaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Give equally to all beings, in each share, without attachment,

children.text: asaṅgajñānameṣanto buddhajñānamanuttaram // SRS_24.59 //
children.translated_text: seeking the unobstructed knowledge, the unsurpassed <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge.' // SRS_24.59 //

children.text: mayāpi pūrvabuddhānāṃ kṛtā pūjā acintiyā /
children.translated_text: 'By me too, inconceivable worship was performed for former <s>Buddhas</s>,

children.text: aniśritena bhūtvainaṃ samādhiṃ śāntameṣatā // SRS_24.60 //
children.translated_text: being without attachment, seeking this peaceful <s>samādhi</s>.' // SRS_24.60 //

children.text: durlabhotpādu buddhānāṃ durlabho mānuṣo bhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Rare is the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>; rare is human birth;

children.text: durlabhā śāsane śraddhā pravrajyā upasaṃpadā // SRS_24.61 //
children.translated_text: rare is faith in the teaching; [rare are] going forth and full ordination.' // SRS_24.61 //

children.text: yena ārāgitaḥ śāstā cittaṃ bodhāya nāmitam /
children.translated_text: '[You] by whom the Teacher has been pleased and the mind inclined toward awakening —

children.text: mā cala tvaṃ pratijñāyāstiṣṭha ca pratipattiṣu // SRS_24.62 //
children.translated_text: do not waver from your vow; stand firm in practice!' // SRS_24.62 //

children.text: ya idaṃ dhārayet sūtraṃ kṣayakāle upasthite /
children.translated_text: 'Whoever upholds this <s>sūtra</s> when the time of decline is at hand,

children.text: pratibhānaṃ labhet kṣipraṃ pravṛttaṃ yadi dhārayet // SRS_24.63 //
children.translated_text: shall quickly obtain eloquence — if he upholds [it] while it is [still] current.' // SRS_24.63 //

children.text: ekagāthāṃ pi dhāritvā puṇyaskandho acintiyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Even by upholding a single verse, the aggregate of merit is inconceivable;

children.text: kiṃ vā punaḥ sarvasūtraṃ dhārayed yaḥ śrutārthikaḥ // SRS_24.64 //
children.translated_text: how much more so for one who upholds the entire <s>sūtra</s>, desiring learning!' // SRS_24.64 //

children.text: sarvasattvān bodhiprāptān pūjayed yo hyatandritaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'One who would worship all beings who have attained awakening, unwearied,

children.text: yaḥ kuryād gauraveṇāsau kalpasattvopamān sadā // SRS_24.65 //
children.translated_text: who would honor them with reverence, always, for as many <s>kalpas</s> as there are beings —' // SRS_24.65 //

children.text: itaḥ samādhito yaśca gāthāmekāṃ pi dhārayet /
children.translated_text: 'and one who would uphold even a single verse from this <s>samādhi</s> —

children.text: sarvaṃ purimakaṃ puṇyaṃ kalāṃ nopaiti ṣoḍaśīm // SRS_24.66 //
children.translated_text: all that former merit does not reach a sixteenth part [of the latter].' // SRS_24.66 //

children.text: acintiyānānuśaṃsān buddhajñānena jānami /
children.translated_text: 'Inconceivable are the benefits — I know them by <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge;

children.text: imaṃ samādhiṃ śrutveha yaḥ kāṅkṣāṃ na kariṣyati // SRS_24.67 //
children.translated_text: whoever, hearing this <s>samādhi</s> here, will not generate doubt [shall attain them].' // SRS_24.67 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje pratisaṃvidavatāraparivarto nāma caturviṃśatitamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter of the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, called the <s>Pratisaṃvidavatāra</s> (Entrance into Analytical Knowledge).

body.text:
(Vaidya 155)
25 Anumodanāparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 155) Chapter 25: The <s>Anumodanā</s> (Rejoicing).

body.text: tatra bhagavān punareva candraprabhaṃ kumārabhūtamāmantrayate sma - tasmāttarhiṃ kumāra bodhisattvena mahāsattvenopāyakuśalena bhavitavyam | kathaṃ ca kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattva upāyakuśalo bhavati? iha kumāra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sarvasattvānāmantike jñātisaṃjñā utpādayitavyā | sarvasattvānāmantike jñāticittamupasthāpya yaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ kuśalamūlapuṇyaskandhastat sarvamanumodayitavyam | trirātryāstridivasasya sarvasattvānāṃ kuśalamūlapuṇyaskandhamanumodya sarvajñatārambaṇena cittotpādena teṣāmeva sarvasattvānāṃ niryātayitavyam | anena kuśalamūlena bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ kṣipramimaṃ samādhiṃ pratilabhate,kṣipraṃ cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate ||
body.translated_text: There the Blessed One again addressed the prince <s>Candraprabha</s>: 'Therefore, prince, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> should be skilled in means. And how, prince, is a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> skilled in means? Here, prince, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> should generate the perception of kinship toward all beings. Having established the thought of kinship toward all beings, he should rejoice in whatever aggregate of merit and roots of merit belongs to all beings. Three times at night and three times during the day, having rejoiced in the aggregate of merit and roots of merit of all beings, with a generation of mind aimed at omniscience, he should transfer [that merit] to those very beings. By this root of merit, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> quickly attains this <s>samādhi</s> and quickly awakens to unsurpassed, perfect and complete awakening.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: sarve mama jñātaya eti sattvāḥ yasteṣamastī pṛthu puṇyaskandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: '"All beings are my kinsmen" — whatever vast aggregate of merit is theirs,

children.text: rātrestrirevaṃ divasasya ca trīranumodamī emu janitva cittam // SRS_25.1 //
children.translated_text: three times at night and three times during the day, I rejoice, generating this thought.' // SRS_25.1 //

children.text: anumodamī ye suviśuddhaśīlā ye jīvitārthe na karonti pāpam /
children.translated_text: 'I rejoice in those of supremely pure morality, who do no evil for the sake of their lives;

children.text: adhimuktisaṃpanna ya bodhisattvā anumodamī teṣa ya kiṃci puṇyam // SRS_25.2 //
children.translated_text: those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> endowed with faith — I rejoice in whatever merit is theirs.' // SRS_25.2 //

children.text: anumodamī yeṣa prasādu buddhe dharme prasādo 'sti tathaiva saṃghe /
children.translated_text: 'I rejoice in those who have faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, who have faith likewise in <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Saṃgha</s>;

children.text: anumodamī ye sugatasya pūjāṃ kurvanti bodhiṃ pratikāṅkṣamāṇāḥ // SRS_25.3 //
children.translated_text: I rejoice in those who perform worship of the <s>Sugata</s>, longing for awakening.' // SRS_25.3 //

children.text: anumodamī yeṣa na ātmadṛṣṭirna bhāvadṛṣṭirna ca jīvadṛṣṭiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I rejoice in those who have no self-view, no view of [inherent] existence, no view of a living being;

children.text: (Vaidya 156)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 156)

children.text: anumodamī yeṣa na pāpadṛṣṭirye śūnyatāṃ dṛṣṭva janenti tuṣṭim // SRS_25.4 //
children.translated_text: I rejoice in those who have no wrong view, who generate joy upon seeing emptiness.' // SRS_25.4 //

children.text: anumodamī ye sugatasya śāsane labhanti pravrajyopasaṃpadaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: 'I rejoice in those who in the <s>Sugata</s>'s teaching obtain going forth and full ordination,

children.text: alpeccha saṃtuṣṭa vane vasanti praśāntacāritra ye dhyānagocarāḥ // SRS_25.5 //
children.translated_text: of few desires, content, dwelling in forests, of peaceful conduct, whose range is <s>dhyāna</s>.' // SRS_25.5 //

children.text: anumodamī ekaka ye 'dvitīyā vane vasantī sada khaḍgabhūtāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I rejoice in those who are alone, without a second, dwelling in forests, always like rhinoceroses,

children.text: ājīvaśuddhāḥ sada alpakṛtyā ye jñātrahetorna na karenti kūhanām // SRS_25.6 //
children.translated_text: of pure livelihood, always with few concerns, who do not practice deceit for the sake of gaining relatives.' // SRS_25.6 //

children.text: anumodamī yeṣa na saṃstavo 'sti na cāpi īrṣyā na kuleṣu tṛṣṇā /
children.translated_text: 'I rejoice in those who have no intimacy, no envy, no craving for families —

children.text: uttrasti traidhātuki nityakālam anopaliptā vicaranti loke // SRS_25.7 //
children.translated_text: alarmed at the three realms at all times, they conduct themselves in the world untainted. // SRS_25.7 //

children.text: anumodamī yeṣa prapañcu nāsti nirviṇṇa sarvāsu bhavopapattiṣu /
children.translated_text: "I rejoice in those who have no conceptual elaboration, who are disgusted with all rebirths in existence,

children.text: avigṛhītā upaśāntacittā na durlabhasteṣa samādhireṣaḥ // SRS_25.8 //
children.translated_text: who are free from grasping, of pacified mind — for them this <s>samādhi</s> is not hard to obtain. // SRS_25.8 //

children.text: anumodamī ye gaṇadoṣa dṛṣṭvā sarvān vivādān parivarjayitvā /
children.translated_text: "I rejoice in those who, seeing the faults of groups, having avoided all disputes,

children.text: sevantyaraṇyaṃ vanamūlamāśritā vimuktisārāḥ sugatasya putrāḥ // SRS_25.9 //
children.translated_text: resort to the forest, dwelling at the foot of trees — sons of the <s>Sugata</s> for whom liberation is essential. // SRS_25.9 //

children.text: anumodamī ye viharantyaraṇye nātmānamutkarṣi parānna paṃsaye /
children.translated_text: "I rejoice in those who dwell in the forest, who do not exalt themselves nor disparage others;

children.text: anumodamī yeṣa pramādu nāsti ye apramattā ima buddhaśāsane // SRS_25.10 //
children.translated_text: I rejoice in those who have no heedlessness — who are vigilant in this <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching. // SRS_25.10 //

children.text: yāvanta dharmāḥ pṛthu bodhipākṣikāḥ sarveṣa mūlaṃ hyayamapramādaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Whatever <s>dharmas</s> there are that are conducive to awakening in their various aspects — the root of them all is this heedlessness [absence, i.e., vigilance];

children.text: ye buddhaputrāḥ sada apramattā na durlabhasteṣa ayaṃ samādhiḥ // SRS_25.11 //
children.translated_text: for those sons of the <s>Buddha</s> who are always vigilant, this <s>samādhi</s> is not hard to obtain. // SRS_25.11 //

children.text: nidhānalābhaḥ sugatāna śāsanaṃ pravrajyalābho dvitīyaṃ nidhānam /
children.translated_text: "The <s>Sugatas</s>' teaching is [like] finding a treasury; going forth is the second treasury;

children.text: (Vaidya 157)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 157)

children.text: śraddhāya lābhastṛtīyaṃ nidhānamayaṃ samādhiścaturthaṃ nidhānam // SRS_25.12 //
children.translated_text: obtaining faith is the third treasury; and this <s>samādhi</s> is the fourth treasury. // SRS_25.12 //

children.text: śratvā imaṃ śūnyata buddhagocaraṃ tasyāpratikṣepu nidhānalambhaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Having heard this emptiness, the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s>, and not rejecting it — that is finding a treasury;

children.text: anantu pratibhānu nidhānalambho yā dhāraṇī tat paramaṃ nidhānam // SRS_25.13 //
children.translated_text: infinite eloquence is finding a treasury; <s>dhāraṇī</s> — that is the supreme treasury. // SRS_25.13 //

children.text: yāvanti dharmāḥ kuśalāḥ prakīrtitāḥ śīlaṃ śrutaṃ tyāgu tathaiva kṣāntiḥ /
children.translated_text: "Whatever wholesome <s>dharmas</s> have been proclaimed — morality, learning, generosity, likewise patience —

children.text: sarveṣa mūlaṃ hyayamapramādo nidhānalambhaḥ sugatena deśitaḥ // SRS_25.14 //
children.translated_text: the root of them all is this vigilance — [thus] finding a treasury has been taught by the <s>Sugata</s>. // SRS_25.14 //

children.text: ye apramattā iha buddhaśāsane samyak ca yeṣāṃ praṇidhānamasti /
children.translated_text: "Those who are vigilant here in the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching, and who have proper aspiration —

children.text: na durlabhasteṣa ayaṃ samādhirāsannabhūtā iha buddhaśāsane // SRS_25.15 //
children.translated_text: for them this <s>samādhi</s> is not hard to obtain; they are near to the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching. // SRS_25.15 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje anumodanāparivarto nāma pañcaviṃśatitamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter in the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, called the <s>Anumodanāparivarta</s> (Chapter on Rejoicing). ||

body.text:
(Vaidya 158)
26 Dānānuśaṃsāparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 158) Chapter 26: <s>Dānānuśaṃsāparivarta</s> (Chapter on the Benefits of Generosity). |

body.text: tasmāttarhi kumāra apramatto bhaviṣyāmītyevaṃ tvayā kumāra śikṣitavyam, apramattasya hi kumāra bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya na durlabhā bhavatyanuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ, kimaṅga punarayaṃ samādhiḥ | kathaṃ ca kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ apramatto bhavati? iha kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ pariśuddhaśīlo bhavati | iha kumāra pariśuddhaśīlo bodhisattvaḥ apramatto bhavati | iha kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ pariśuddhaśīlo bhavati | iha kumāra pariśuddhaśīlo bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ avirahito bhavati sarvajñatācittena ṣaṭsu pāramitāsu | tasyeme ānuśaṃsā bhavanti | tān śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru | bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te | deśeme kumāra anuśaṃsā dānādhimuktasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya | katame daśa? yaduta mātsaryakleśo 'sya nigṛhīto bhavati | tyāgānubṛṃhitaṃ cāsya cittaṃ sadā bhavati | bahujanasādhāraṇebhyaśca bhogebhyaḥ sāramādadāti | mahābhogeṣu ca kuleṣūpapadyate | jātamātrasya cāsya tyāgacittamāmukhībhavati | priyaśca bhavati catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāmū | viśāradaścāsaṃkucitaḥ parṣadamavagāhate | digvidikṣu cāsyodāro varṇakīrtiśabdaśloko loke 'bhyudgacchati | mṛdutaruṇahastapādaśca bhavati samacaraṇatalapratiṣṭhitaḥ | avirahitaśca bhavati kalyāṇamitrairyāvadbodhimaṇḍaniṣadanāt | ime kumāra daśānuśaṃsā dānādhimuktasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya ||
body.translated_text: "Therefore, O prince, 'I shall be vigilant' — thus should you train, O prince. For a vigilant <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, O prince, the unsurpassed, perfect awakening is not hard to obtain — how much less this <s>samādhi</s>! And how, O prince, does a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> become vigilant? Here, O prince, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> is of purified morality. Here, O prince, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of purified morality becomes vigilant. Here, O prince, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> is of purified morality. Here, O prince, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> of purified morality is never separated from the thought of omniscience in the six <s>pāramitās</s>. For him there are these benefits. Listen well and attend carefully; I shall speak to you. These, O prince, are the ten benefits for a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> devoted to generosity. What ten? Namely: the defilement of avarice is restrained in him; his mind is always nourished by renunciation; he takes the essence from possessions shared with many people; he is reborn in families of great wealth; the moment he is born, the thought of renunciation becomes foremost in him; he becomes dear to the four assemblies; he enters the assembly confident and without hesitation; in the directions and intermediate directions, his noble fame, glory, and renown arise in the world; he becomes soft and tender in hands and feet, established on level soles; and he is never separated from good friends until he sits at the seat of awakening. These, O prince, are the ten benefits for a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> devoted to generosity." ||

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Here the following was said:

children.text: nigṛhītaṃ si mātsaryaṃ tyāgacittaṃ ca bṛṃhitam /
children.translated_text: "Avarice is restrained, and the thought of renunciation is nourished;

children.text: ādattasāro bhavati samṛddhe jāyate kule // SRS_26.1 //
children.translated_text: he becomes one who takes the essence, and is born in prosperous families. // SRS_26.1 //

children.text: jātamātrasya cittaṃ si tyāga eva pravartate /
children.translated_text: "The moment he is born, his mind is directed toward renunciation;

children.text: priyo bhavati sattvānāṃ gṛhapravrajitāna ca // SRS_26.2 //
children.translated_text: he becomes dear to beings — both householders and renunciants. // SRS_26.2 //

children.text: viśāradaśca parṣatsu ama rūpa saṃkramet /
children.translated_text: "Confident in assemblies, whatever form he may assume,

children.text: bhavatyudāraśabdo 'sya grāmeṣu nagareṣu ca // SRS_26.3 //
children.translated_text: his fame becomes noble — in villages and cities. // SRS_26.3 //

children.text: mṛdū hastau ca pādau ca bhaviṣyanti na durlabhāḥ /
children.translated_text: "His hands and feet will become soft — not hard to obtain;

children.text: kalyāṇamitrāṃllabhate buddhāṃśca śrāvakānapi // SRS_26.4 //
children.translated_text: he obtains good friends — Buddhas and <s>Śrāvakas</s> as well. // SRS_26.4 //

children.text: mātsaryacittaṃ si na jātu bhoti tyāgeṣu citta ramate 'sya nityam /
children.translated_text: "The thought of avarice never arises in him; his mind always delights in renunciation;

children.text: priyaśca bhoti bahusattvakoṭināṃ amatsarisyā imi ānuśaṃsāḥ // SRS_26.5 //
children.translated_text: and he is dear to many <s>koṭis</s> of beings — these are the benefits of being without avarice. // SRS_26.5 //

children.text: (Vaidya 159)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 159)

children.text: mahādhane cāpi kule sa jāyate jātasya tyāge ramate mano 'sya /
children.translated_text: "He is born in a family of great wealth; once born, his mind delights in generosity;

children.text: ādattasāraśca karoti kālamamatsarisyā imi ānuśaṃsāḥ // SRS_26.6 //
children.translated_text: he takes the essence and makes good use of his time — these are the benefits of being without avarice. // SRS_26.6 //

children.text: viśāradaśco pariṣāṃ vigāhate udāraśabdo 'sya diśāsu yāti /
children.translated_text: "He enters assemblies confidently; his noble fame travels in all directions;

children.text: mṛdu hastapādo 'sya sadaiva jāyate amatsarisyā imi ānuśaṃsāḥ // SRS_26.7 //
children.translated_text: his hands and feet are always born soft — these are the benefits of being without avarice. // SRS_26.7 //

children.text: kalyāṇamitrāsya na bhonti durlabhā buddhāṃśca yo paśyati śrāvakāṃśca /
children.translated_text: "Good friends are not hard for him to find; he sees Buddhas and <s>Śrāvakas</s>;

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca tān pūjayate prasanno amatsarisyā imi ānuśaṃsāḥ // SRS_26.8 //
children.translated_text: and seeing them, he worships them with faith — these are the benefits of being without avarice. // SRS_26.8 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje dānānuśaṃsāparivarto nāma ṣaḍaviṃśatitamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter in the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, called the <s>Dānānuśaṃsāparivarta</s> (Chapter on the Benefits of Generosity). ||

body.text:
(Vaidya 160)
27 Śīlanirdeśaparivartaḥ |
daśeme kumāra anuśaṃsāḥ pariśuddhaśīlasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya | katame daśa? yaduta jñānaṃ ca pariśodhayati paripūrayati | buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmanuśikṣate | agarhito bhavati paṇḍitānām | pratijñāto na calati | pratipattau tiṣṭhati | saṃsārāt palāyate | nirvāṇamarpayati | niṣparyutthāno viharati | samādhiṃ pratilabhate | adaridraśca bhavati | ime kumāra daśānuśaṃsāḥ pariśuddhaśīlasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya ||
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 160) Chapter 27: <s>Śīlanirdeśaparivarta</s> (Chapter on the Exposition of Morality). | "These, O prince, are the ten benefits for a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> of purified morality. What ten? Namely: he purifies and fulfills knowledge; he trains in accordance with the Blessed Buddhas; he is blameless among the wise; he does not waver from his resolve; he stands firm in practice; he flees from <s>saṃsāra</s>; he delivers [beings] to <s>nirvāṇa</s>; he dwells without mental affliction; he attains <s>samādhi</s>; and he is not impoverished. These, O prince, are the ten benefits for a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> of purified morality." ||

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Here the following was said:

children.text: jñānaṃ ca paripūreti buddhānāmanuśikṣate /
children.translated_text: "He fulfills knowledge and trains in accordance with the Buddhas;

children.text: agarhitaḥ paṇḍitānāṃ bhoti nityaṃ viśāradaḥ // SRS_27.1 //
children.translated_text: blameless among the wise, he is always confident. // SRS_27.1 //

children.text: pratijñāto na calati pratipattau ca tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: "He does not waver from his resolve; he stands firm in practice;

children.text: arpeti yena nirvāṇaṃ saṃsārātaḥ palāyate // SRS_27.2 //
children.translated_text: he delivers [beings] to <s>nirvāṇa</s>; he flees from <s>saṃsāra</s>. // SRS_27.2 //

children.text: niṣparyutthito viharati samādhiṃ labhate laghu /
children.translated_text: "He dwells without mental affliction; he quickly obtains <s>samādhi</s>;

children.text: adaridraśca bhavati śīlaskandhe pratiṣṭhitaḥ // SRS_27.3 //
children.translated_text: and he is not impoverished — established in the aggregate of morality. // SRS_27.3 //

children.text: jñānaṃ ca tasyo paripūrṇu bhoti anuśikṣate cāti tathāgatānām /
children.translated_text: "His knowledge becomes fulfilled; he trains in accordance with the <s>Tathāgatas</s>;

children.text: na cāsya nindāṃ prakaronti paṇḍitāḥ tathā hi tasyo pariśuddha śīlam // SRS_27.4 //
children.translated_text: and the wise do not criticize him — for his morality is pure. // SRS_27.4 //

children.text: pratijñāto 'sau na calāti paṇḍitaḥ tathā hi śūraḥ pratipattiye sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: "That wise one does not waver from his resolve; for that hero stands firm in practice;

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca saṃsāramanekadoṣaṃ palāyate nirvṛti yena yāti // SRS_27.5 //
children.translated_text: and seeing <s>saṃsāra</s> with its many faults, he flees — and goes where <s>nirvāṇa</s> leads. // SRS_27.5 //

children.text: paryutthitaṃ cittu na bhoti tasya tathā hyasau śīlabale pratiṣṭhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Affliction does not arise in his mind, for he is established in the power of morality;

children.text: kṣipraṃ samādhiṃ labhate niraṅgaṇaṃ pariśuddhaśīlasyimi ānuśaṃsāḥ // SRS_27.6 //
children.translated_text: he quickly attains <s>samādhi</s> free from stain — these are the benefits of one of purified morality. // SRS_27.6 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje śīlanirdeśaparivarto nāma saptaviṃśatimaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter in the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, called the <s>Śīlanirdeśaparivarta</s> (Chapter on the Exposition of Morality). ||

body.text:
(Vaidya 161)
28 Daśānuśaṃsāparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 161) Chapter 28: <s>Daśānuśaṃsāparivarta</s> (Chapter on the Ten Benefits). |

body.text: daśeme kumāra ānuśaṃsāḥ kṣāntipratiṣṭhitasya maitrīvihāriṇo bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya | katame daśa?agninā na dahyate | śastreṇa na hanyate | viṣamasya na kramate | udakena na mriyate | devatāścainaṃ rakṣanti | lakṣaṇālaṃkṛtaṃ ca kāyaṃ pratilabhate | sarvadurgatidvārāṇi cāsya pithitāni bhavanti | brahmaloke cāsyopapattirbhavati | sukhena cāsya rātriṃdivāni vrajanti | prītisukhaṃ cāsya kāyaṃ na vijahāti | ime kumāra daśānuśaṃsāḥ kṣāntipratiṣṭhitasya maitrīvihāriṇo bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya ||
body.translated_text: "These, O prince, are the ten benefits for a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> established in patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) and dwelling in loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>). What ten? Namely: he is not burned by fire; he is not slain by weapons; poison does not spread in him; he does not die by water; deities protect him; he obtains a body adorned with the [thirty-two] marks; all gates to evil destinies are shut for him; he is reborn in the <s>Brahma</s>-world; his days and nights pass in happiness; and joy and bliss do not leave his body. These, O prince, are the ten benefits for a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> established in patience and dwelling in loving-kindness." ||

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Here the following was said:

children.text: agninā dahyate nāsau śastreṇa na ca hanyate /
children.translated_text: "He is not burned by fire, nor is he slain by weapons;

children.text: viṣaṃ na kramate kāye udake mriyate na saḥ // SRS_28.1 //
children.translated_text: poison does not spread in his body; he does not die in water. // SRS_28.1 //

children.text: rakṣanti devatāścainaṃ dvātriṃśad bhonti lakṣaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Deities protect him; the thirty-two marks appear;

children.text: durgatiḥ pithitā cāsya kṣāntiye anuśaṃsime // SRS_28.2 //
children.translated_text: the gates to evil destinies are shut for him — these are the benefits of patience. // SRS_28.2 //

children.text: brahmatvaṃ atha śakratvaṃ bhoti cāsya na durlabham /
children.translated_text: "The state of <s>Brahmā</s> and also of <s>Śakra</s> — these are not hard for him to obtain;

children.text: sukhaṃ viharate nityaṃ priti bhonti acintiyā // SRS_28.3 //
children.translated_text: he always dwells in happiness; his joy is inconceivable. // SRS_28.3 //

children.text: no agniśastreṇa sa jātu hanyate viṣeṇa vā vārigato na mriyate /
children.translated_text: "He is never slain by fire or weapons, nor does he die from poison or water;

children.text: rakṣanti devāstatha nāga yakṣā maitrīvihāriṣyimi ānuśaṃsāḥ // SRS_28.4 //
children.translated_text: gods, <s>nāgas</s>, and <s>yakṣas</s> protect him — these are the benefits of dwelling in loving-kindness. // SRS_28.4 //

children.text: dvātriṃśa kāye 'sya bhavanti lakṣaṇā no cāsya bhūyo vinipātu bhoti /
children.translated_text: "Thirty-two marks appear on his body; he never again falls to a lower realm;

children.text: cyutaśca sa brahmapuropapadyate kṣāntisthitasyo imi ānuśaṃsāḥ // SRS_28.5 //
children.translated_text: and passing away, he is reborn in the <s>Brahma</s>-city — these are the benefits of one established in patience. // SRS_28.5 //

children.text: sukhena rātriṃdiva tasya yānti prītisphuṭaḥ kāyu tadāsya bhoti /
children.translated_text: "His days and nights pass in happiness; his body is suffused with joy;

children.text: sa kṣāntisauratyabale pratiṣṭhitaḥ prasannacittaḥ sada bhoti paṇḍitaḥ // SRS_28.6 //
children.translated_text: established in the power of patience and gentleness, that wise one always has a serene mind. // SRS_28.6 //

body.text: daśeme kumāra ānuśaṃsā ārabdhavīryasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya | katame daśa? yaduta durāsadaśca bhavati | buddhaparigrahaṃ ca pratilabhate | devatāparigṛhītaśca bhavati | śrutvā cāsya dharmā na parihīyante | aśratapūrvāṃśca dharmān pratilabhate | samādhigotraṃ ca pratilabhate | alpābādhaśca bhavati | āhāraścāsya samyak pariṇāmayati | padmopamaśca bhavati na musalopamaḥ | ibhe kumāra daśānuśaṃsā ārabdhavīryasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya ||
body.translated_text: "These, O prince, are the ten benefits for a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> of aroused vigor. What ten? Namely: he becomes hard to assail; he obtains the <s>Buddha</s>'s embrace; he is sustained by deities; the <s>dharmas</s> he has heard are not lost to him; he obtains <s>dharmas</s> previously unheard; he attains the lineage of <s>samādhi</s>; he has few illnesses; his food digests properly; he becomes like a lotus, not like a pestle; these, O prince, are the ten benefits for a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> of aroused vigor." ||

body.text:
(Vaidya 162)
tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 162) Here the following was said:

children.text: durāsadaḥ sadā bhoti paridāho na vidyate /
children.translated_text: "He is always hard to assail; there is no torment [for him];

children.text: rakṣanti devatāścainaṃ kṣipraṃ buddhān sa paśyati // SRS_28.7 //
children.translated_text: deities protect him; he quickly sees Buddhas. // SRS_28.7 //

children.text: śrutaṃ na hīyate tasya aśrataṃ bhoti āmukham /
children.translated_text: "What he has heard is never lost; the unheard becomes accessible to him;

children.text: praṇidhiṃ paripūreti vīryavante ime guṇāḥ // SRS_28.8 //
children.translated_text: he fulfills his aspiration — these are the qualities of the vigorous one. // SRS_28.8 //

children.text: samādhigotraṃ labhate vyādhiścāsya na jāyate /
children.translated_text: "He attains the lineage of <s>samādhi</s>; illness does not arise in him;

children.text: sukhaṃ cāsyānnapānāni pacyante na viṣīdati // SRS_28.9 //
children.translated_text: his food and drink are digested happily — he does not become dejected. // SRS_28.9 //

children.text: utpalaṃ varimadhye va so 'nupūrveṇa vardhate /
children.translated_text: "Like a lotus in the midst of water, he gradually grows;

children.text: evaṃ śuklehi dharmehi bodhisattvo vivardhate // SRS_28.10 //
children.translated_text: even so, through wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> grows. // SRS_28.10 //

children.text: avandhyāścāsya gacchanti rātrayo divasāni ca /
children.translated_text: "His nights and days pass fruitfully;

children.text: bhaviṣyati mṛtyukāle phalametasya cedṛśam // SRS_28.11 //
children.translated_text: at the time of death, such will be his fruit. // SRS_28.11 //

children.text: ārabdhavīryeṇa tathāgatena kalpairanaikaiḥ samudāgatena /
children.translated_text: "By the <s>Tathāgata</s> of aroused vigor, who has accumulated [merit] through countless <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: ye bodhisattvā viriyeṇupetāsteṣānuśaṃsā imi saṃprakāśitāḥ // SRS_28.12 //
children.translated_text: these benefits have been proclaimed for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> endowed with vigor. // SRS_28.12 //

children.text: ārabdhavīryo bhavatī durāsadaḥ parigṛhīto bhavatī jinehi /
children.translated_text: "One of aroused vigor becomes hard to assail; he is embraced by the <s>Jinas</s>;

children.text: devā pi tasya spṛha saṃjanenti nacireṇa so lapsyati buddhabodhim // SRS_28.13 //
children.translated_text: even the gods generate longing toward him — he will quickly attain <s>Buddha</s>-awakening. // SRS_28.13 //

children.text: śrataṃ ca tasyo na kadāci hīyate anye pṛthū cāpi labhanti dharmāḥ /
children.translated_text: "What he has heard is never lost; and he also obtains many other vast <s>dharmas</s>;

children.text: pratibhānu tasyo adhimātru vardhate ārabdhavīryasya ime 'nuśaṃsāḥ // SRS_28.14 //
children.translated_text: his eloquence grows exceedingly — these are the benefits of one of aroused vigor. // SRS_28.14 //

children.text: samādhigotraṃ ca laghuṃ dhigacchati ābādhu tasyo na kadāci bhoti /
children.translated_text: "He quickly attains the lineage of <s>samādhi</s>; illness never arises in him;

children.text: yathaiva so bhojanu tatra bhuñjate sukhena tasyo pariṇāmu gacchati // SRS_28.15 //
children.translated_text: whatever food he eats there, it is digested happily. // SRS_28.15 //

children.text: rātriṃdivaṃ bhavati śuklapakṣo ārabdhavīryasya atandritasya /
children.translated_text: "Day and night are always on the bright side for one of aroused vigor, unwearied;

children.text: bodhī pi tasyo nacireṇa bheṣyate tathā hyasau vīryabalairupetaḥ // SRS_28.16 //
children.translated_text: his awakening too will not be long in coming — for he is endowed with the power of vigor. // SRS_28.16 //

body.text:
(Vaidya 163)
daśeme kumāra ānuśaṃsā dhyānādhimuktasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya | katame daśa? yaduta ācāre tiṣṭhati | gocare carati | niṣparidāho viharati | guptendriyo bhavati | prītimanubhavati | viviktaḥ kāmaiḥ | atṛpto dhyānaiḥ | mukto māraviṣayāt | pratiṣṭhito buddhaviṣaye | vimuktiṃ paripācayati | ime kumāra daśānuśaṃsā dhyānādhimuktasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya ||
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 163) 'These, O prince, are the ten benefits for a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> who is inclined toward <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). Which ten? Namely: he abides in [proper] conduct; he moves in [proper] domain; he dwells free from distress; he is one of guarded senses; he experiences joy; he is secluded from sensual desires; he is unsatiated with <s>dhyānas</s>; he is freed from <s>Māra</s>'s domain; he is established in the <s>Buddha</s>'s domain; he brings liberation to maturity. These, O prince, are the ten benefits for a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> who is inclined toward <s>dhyāna</s>.' ||

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Concerning this, it was said:

children.text: nāsau bhoti anācāro ācāre saṃpratiṣṭhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He is not one of misconduct — he is established in [proper] conduct;

children.text: gocare carate yogī varjeti ca agocaram // SRS_28.17 //
children.translated_text: the practitioner (<s>yogī</s>) moves in [proper] domain and avoids what is not his domain. // SRS_28.17 //

children.text: niṣparidāhyavihārī guptendriya susaṃvṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Dwelling free from distress, with guarded senses, well-restrained,

children.text: anubhavati saṃprītiṃ dhyānadhyāyisya gocaraḥ // SRS_28.18 //
children.translated_text: he experiences joy — the domain of one who meditates on <s>dhyāna</s>. // SRS_28.18 //

children.text: viraktaḥ kāmatṛṣṇāyā dhyānasaukhyaṃ niṣevate /
children.translated_text: Detached from the craving for sensual pleasures, he resorts to the bliss of <s>dhyāna</s>;

children.text: mukto 'sau māraviṣayād buddhagocari saṃsthitaḥ // SRS_28.19 //
children.translated_text: freed from <s>Māra</s>'s domain, he is established in the <s>Buddha</s>'s domain. // SRS_28.19 //

children.text: yogino hi viśeṣo 'yaṃ yadeko ramate vane /
children.translated_text: This is the distinction of the practitioner — that he delights alone in the forest;

children.text: vimuktiṃ paripāceti taṃ bhoti daśamaṃ padam // SRS_28.20 //
children.translated_text: he brings liberation to maturity — that is the tenth stage. // SRS_28.20 //

children.text: ācāri so tiṣṭhati bodhisattvaḥ sarvānanācāru vivarjayitvā /
children.translated_text: That <s>Bodhisattva</s> abides in [proper] conduct, having avoided all misconduct;

children.text: agocaraṃ varjiya gocare sthitaḥ samādhiyukte imi ānuśaṃsāḥ // SRS_28.21 //
children.translated_text: avoiding what is not his domain, established in [proper] domain — these are the benefits of one devoted to <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_28.21 //

children.text: paridāhu tasyo na kadāci bhoti āryaṃ spṛśitveha sukhaṃ nirāmiṣam /
children.translated_text: Distress never arises in him, having touched the noble, immaterial happiness;

children.text: kāyena cittena ca bhoti śītalaḥ samādhiyukte imi ānuśaṃsāḥ // SRS_28.22 //
children.translated_text: he is cool in body and in mind — these are the benefits of one devoted to <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_28.22 //

children.text: viharatyaraṇyāyataneṣu gupto vikṣepu tasyo na kadāci bhoti /
children.translated_text: He dwells guarded in the forest retreats; distraction never arises in him;

children.text: prītiṃ ca tasmillaṃbhate nirāmiṣaṃ tathā hi kāyena viviktu bhoti // SRS_28.23 //
children.translated_text: and he obtains immaterial joy therein — for thus he is secluded in body. // SRS_28.23 //

children.text: alipta kāmehi asaṃkiliṣṭo tathā hi māraviṣayāttu muktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Unstained by sensual desires, undefiled, and thus freed from <s>Māra</s>'s domain,

children.text: tathāgatānāṃ viṣaye pratiṣṭhito vimukti tasyo paripāku gacchati // SRS_28.24 //
children.translated_text: established in the domain of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> — his liberation comes to maturity.' // SRS_28.24 //

body.text: daśeme kumāra ānuśaṃsāḥ prajñācaritasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya | katame daśa? yaduta sarvasvaparityāgo bhavati na ca dānena śuddhiṃ manyate | akhaṇḍaśīlaśca bhavati na ca śīlamāśritaḥ |(Vaidya 164) kṣāntibalasupratiṣṭhitaśca bhavati na ca sattvasaṃjñāsaṃpratiṣṭhitaḥ | ārabdhavīryaśca bhavati kāyacittaviviktaḥ | dhyānadhyāyī ca bhavati apratiṣṭhitadhyāyī | durdharṣaśca bhavati māraiḥ, aprakampyaśca bhavati sarvaparapravādibhiḥ | lavdhālokaśca bhavati sarvasaṃskāragatyām | adhimātrā cāsya sarvasattveṣu mahākaruṇā samatikrāmati | na ca śrāvakapratyekabhūmeḥ spṛhayati | buddhadhyānasamādhisamāpattīravatarati | ime kumāra daśānuśaṃsāḥ prajñācaritasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya ||
body.translated_text: 'These, O prince, are the ten benefits for a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> who practices with wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). Which ten? Namely: he relinquishes all possessions yet does not consider purification to come through giving; he is of unbroken morality (<s>śīla</s>) yet does not rely on morality; (Vaidya 164) he is firmly established in the power of patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) yet is not established in the perception of a being; he is of aroused vigor yet is secluded in body and mind; he meditates on <s>dhyāna</s> yet meditates without foundation; he is invincible by <s>Māras</s> and unshakable by all proponents of other doctrines; he has obtained light regarding the course of all conditioned formations; his great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) toward all beings surpasses [all]; he does not aspire to the stage of <s>Śrāvakas</s> or <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>; he enters into the <s>dhyānas</s>, <s>samādhis</s>, and attainments of the <s>Buddha</s>. These, O prince, are the ten benefits for a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> who practices with wisdom.' ||

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Concerning this, it was said:

children.text: sarvasvaṃ tyajate dhīraḥ śuddhiṃ tena na manyate /
children.translated_text: 'The wise one relinquishes all possessions — he does not consider purification to come thereby;

children.text: akhaṇḍaṃ rakṣate śīlaṃ niśrayo 'sya na vidyate // SRS_28.25 //
children.translated_text: he guards unbroken morality — no reliance is found for him [therein]. // SRS_28.25 //

children.text: kṣāntiṃ bhāveti sa prājñaḥ sattvasaṃjñā vivartitā /
children.translated_text: That wise one cultivates patience — the perception of a being is turned away;

children.text: ārabdhavīryo bhavati kāyacittaviviktataḥ // SRS_28.26 //
children.translated_text: he is of aroused vigor, secluded in body and mind. // SRS_28.26 //

children.text: dhyānadhyāyī ca so bhoti apratiṣṭho aniśritaḥ /
children.translated_text: He meditates on <s>dhyāna</s> yet is without foundation and without reliance;

children.text: durdharṣo bhoti mārehi prajñāvanta ime guṇāḥ // SRS_28.27 //
children.translated_text: he is invincible by <s>Māras</s> — these are the qualities of one endowed with wisdom. // SRS_28.27 //

children.text: akampiyo ca so bhoti sarvaiḥ parapravādibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: He is unshakable by all proponents of other doctrines;

children.text: labdhālokaśca saṃsāre prajñāyā īdṛśā guṇāḥ // SRS_28.28 //
children.translated_text: he has obtained light in <s>saṃsāra</s> — such are the qualities of wisdom. // SRS_28.28 //

children.text: mahākṛpāṃ sa labhate sarvasattvāna antike /
children.translated_text: He obtains great compassion toward all beings;

children.text: śrāvakapratyekajñāne na spṛheti kadācana // SRS_28.29 //
children.translated_text: he never aspires to the knowledge of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. // SRS_28.29 //

body.text:
sarvasvatyāgena na śuddhi manyate akhaṇḍaśīlo na ca śīlaniśritaḥ /
bhāveti kṣāntī na ca sattvasaṃjñā | prajñādhimukte imi ānuśaṃsāḥ // SRS_28.30 //
body.translated_text: Through relinquishing all, he does not consider purification [thereby]; of unbroken morality, yet not relying on morality; he cultivates patience without the perception of a being — these are the benefits of one inclined toward wisdom. // SRS_28.30 //

children.text: ārabdhavīryo bhavatī vimukto aniśrito dhyāyati apratiṣṭhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Of aroused vigor, he is liberated — without reliance he meditates, without foundation;

children.text: durdharṣu māreṇa sa bhoti paṇḍito prajñādhimukte imi ānuśaṃsāḥ // SRS_28.31 //
children.translated_text: invincible by <s>Māra</s>, that wise one — these are the benefits of one inclined toward wisdom. // SRS_28.31 //

children.text: akampiyo bhoti parapravādibhiḥ sa labdhagādho bhavatīha saṃskṛte /
children.translated_text: Unshakable by proponents of other doctrines, he obtains depth here in the conditioned;

children.text: adhimātra sattveṣu kṛpāṃ janeti prajñādhimukte imi ānuśaṃsāḥ // SRS_28.32 //
children.translated_text: he generates surpassing compassion toward beings — these are the benefits of one inclined toward wisdom. // SRS_28.32 //

children.text: pratyekabuddheṣu ca śrāvakeṣu co na tasya jātu spṛha teṣu jāyate /
children.translated_text: Toward <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> and <s>Śrāvakas</s>, no aspiration for their [stage] ever arises in him;

children.text: (Vaidya 165)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 165)

children.text: tathā hyasau buddhaguṇāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ prajñādhimukte imi ānuśaṃsāḥ // SRS_28.33 //
children.translated_text: for he is established in the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities — these are the benefits of one inclined toward wisdom.' // SRS_28.33 //

body.text: daśeme kumāra ānuśaṃsā bahuśrutasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya | katame daśa? yaduta saṃkleśaṃ na karoti | vyāpādaṃ na janayati | kāṅkṣāṃ vivṛṇoti | dṛṣṭimṛjvīkaroti | utpathaṃ ca varjayati | mārge pratiṣṭhate | amṛtadvāre tiṣṭhati | āsannasthāyī bhavati bodhaye | ālokabhūto bhavati sattvānām | durgatibhyo na bibheti | ime kumāra daśānuśaṃsā bahuśrutasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya ||
body.translated_text: 'These, O prince, are the ten benefits for a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> of great learning (<s>bahuśruta</s>). Which ten? Namely: he does not become defiled; he does not generate ill-will; he removes doubt; he straightens wrong views; he avoids the wrong path; he is established on the path; he stands at the door of the deathless; he is close to awakening; he becomes a light for beings; he does not fear the lower realms. These, O prince, are the ten benefits for a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> of great learning.' ||

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Concerning this, it was said:

children.text: anuśaṃsā daśaivaite bāhuśratye prakāśitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'These ten benefits of great learning have been proclaimed

children.text: tathāgatena buddhena yathābhūtaṃ prajānatā // SRS_28.34 //
children.translated_text: by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Buddha</s>, who knows things as they truly are. // SRS_28.34 //

children.text: saṃkleśaṃ vyavadānaṃ ca ubhau pakṣau sa jānati /
children.translated_text: He knows both sides — defilement and purification;

children.text: saṃkleśaṃ pariavarjitvā vyodāne mārgi tiṣṭhati // SRS_28.35 //
children.translated_text: having avoided defilement, he stands on the path of purification. // SRS_28.35 //

children.text: kāṅkṣāṃ vivarati jñānī dṛṣṭīmṛjvīkaroti ca /
children.translated_text: The wise one removes doubt and straightens wrong views;

children.text: mārga utpatha varjeti ṛjuke mārgi tiṣṭhati // SRS_28.36 //
children.translated_text: he avoids the wrong path and stands on the straight path. // SRS_28.36 //

children.text: tiṣṭhate cāmṛtadvāre āsanno bhoti bodhaye /
children.translated_text: He stands at the door of the deathless; he is close to awakening;

children.text: ālokabhūtaḥ sattvānāṃ durgatibhyo na bhīyati // SRS_28.37 //
children.translated_text: he is a light for beings; he does not fear the lower realms. // SRS_28.37 //

children.text: jānāti dharmaṃ pṛthu sāṃkileśikaṃ vyavadānapakṣaṃ pi tathaiva jānati /
children.translated_text: He knows the <s>dharma</s> broadly — that which pertains to defilement; the purification side he likewise knows;

children.text: sa saṃkileśaṃ parivarjayitvā vyodāni saṃśikṣati dharmi uttame // SRS_28.38 //
children.translated_text: having avoided defilement, he trains in purification, in the supreme <s>Dharma</s>. // SRS_28.38 //

children.text: kāṅkṣāṃ ca so vivarati sarvaprāṇināṃ dṛṣṭī ca tasyo bhavati sadojjvakā /
children.translated_text: He removes the doubt of all living beings; his views are always upright;

children.text: sa utpathaṃ mārgu vivarjayitvā saṃtiṣṭhate ṛjuki pathe sadā śive // SRS_28.39 //
children.translated_text: having avoided the wrong path, he always stands on the straight, auspicious path. // SRS_28.39 //

children.text: amṛtasya dvāre bhavatī sadā sthito āsanna bhotī vipulāya bodhaye /
children.translated_text: He always stands at the door of the deathless; he is close to the vast awakening;

children.text: ālokabhūtaḥ pṛthu sarvaprāṇināṃ na cāpyasau bhāyati durgatibhyaḥ // SRS_28.40 //
children.translated_text: he is a light broadly for all living beings; and he does not fear the lower realms.' // SRS_28.40 //

body.text: daśeme kumāra ānuśaṃsā dharmadānagurukasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya parebhyo dharmadānaṃ dadataḥ | katame daśa? yaduta akriyāṃ vivarjayati || kriyāmavatarati | satpuruṣadharme pratiṣṭhate | buddhakṣetraṃ pariśodhayati | bodhimaṇḍamarpayati | vastuṃ parityajati | kleśānnigṛhvāti | sarvasattvebhyaḥ pratyaṃśaṃ (Vaidya 166) dadāti | tadārambaṇāṃ ca maitrīṃ bhāvayati | dṛṣṭadhārmikaṃ ca sukhaṃ pratilabhate | ime kumāra daśānuśaṃsā dharmadānagurukasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya parebhyo dharmadānaṃ dadataḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'These, O prince, are the ten benefits for a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> who values the gift of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmadāna</s>) and gives the gift of <s>Dharma</s> to others. Which ten? Namely: he avoids non-action; he enters into action; he is established in the <s>dharma</s> of good people; he purifies the <s>Buddha</s>-field; he ascends the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>); he relinquishes substance; he restrains the afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>); he gives a portion to all beings; (Vaidya 166) he cultivates loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) with that as its support; and he obtains happiness in this very life. These, O prince, are the ten benefits for a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> who values the gift of <s>Dharma</s> and gives the gift of <s>Dharma</s> to others.' ||

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Concerning this, it was said:

children.text: yo hi dānaṃ dādātyagraṃ dharmadānamamatsarī /
children.translated_text: 'He who gives the supreme gift — the gift of <s>Dharma</s> — without miserliness,

children.text: daśa tasyānuśaṃsā vai lokanāthena bhāṣitāḥ // SRS_28.41 //
children.translated_text: ten benefits for him have been proclaimed by the Lord of the World. // SRS_28.41 //

children.text: akriyāṃ sarvi varjeti kriyāmotarate viduḥ /
children.translated_text: He avoids all non-action; the wise one enters into action;

children.text: satpuruṣa dharmapratipannastyāgacittaṃ niṣevate // SRS_28.42 //
children.translated_text: practicing the <s>dharma</s> of good people, he resorts to the mind of renunciation. // SRS_28.42 //

children.text: buddhakṣetraṃ ca śodheti kṣetraṃ bhoti syanuttaram /
children.translated_text: He purifies the <s>Buddha</s>-field — his field becomes unsurpassed;

children.text: bodhimaṇḍaṃ samārūḍho dharmadānasyidaṃ phalam // SRS_28.43 //
children.translated_text: having ascended the seat of awakening — this is the fruit of the gift of <s>Dharma</s>. // SRS_28.43 //

children.text: tyajate sarvavastūni śikṣate dharmarājinaḥ /
children.translated_text: He relinquishes all possessions; he trains after the <s>Dharma</s>-kings;

children.text: kileśā nigṛhītāsya bodhistasya na durlabhā // SRS_28.44 //
children.translated_text: his afflictions are restrained — awakening is not hard for him to obtain. // SRS_28.44 //

children.text: sarvasattvāna pratyaṃśaṃ maitracittaḥ prayacchati /
children.translated_text: With a mind of loving-kindness, he gives a share to all beings;

children.text: anīrṣukaśca so bhoti saukhyaṃ bhoti syamānuṣam // SRS_28.45 //
children.translated_text: he becomes free from envy — his happiness becomes superhuman. // SRS_28.45 //

children.text: vivarjitā akriyā paṇḍitena kriyāya so nitya viduḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Non-action has been avoided by the wise one; always established in action, the learned one;

children.text: mahātmadharmeṣu sadā pratiṣṭhito yo dharmadānaṃ sada deti paṇḍitaḥ // SRS_28.46 //
children.translated_text: always established in the <s>dharmas</s> of great souls — the wise one who constantly gives the gift of <s>Dharma</s>. // SRS_28.46 //

children.text: kṣetraṃ ca tasya sada bhoti śuddhaṃ dharmā vivardhantimi bodhipākṣikāḥ /
children.translated_text: His field is always pure; the <s>dharmas</s> conducive to awakening increase;

children.text: āsanna bhoti sada bodhimaṇḍe dharmaṃ daditvā imi ānuśaṃsāḥ // SRS_28.47 //
children.translated_text: he is always close to the seat of awakening — having given the <s>Dharma</s>, these are the benefits. // SRS_28.47 //

children.text: kleśā na santī parityakta vastūn vastuṃ parijñātu svalakṣaṇena /
children.translated_text: Afflictions do not exist [for him], having relinquished possessions; having fully known substance through its own-characteristic,

children.text: vimukta sarvehi parigrahehi na tasya saṅgo bhavatī kadācit // SRS_28.48 //
children.translated_text: liberated from all acquisitions — attachment never arises for him. // SRS_28.48 //

children.text: upasthitaṃ cittu vicakṣaṇasya sarve 'pi sattvā sukhino bhavantu /
children.translated_text: The mind of the discerning one is present [with the thought]: "May all beings be happy!"

children.text: sa maitracitto bhavatī anīrṣyuko dṛṣṭeva dharme 'sya sukhaṃ analpakam // SRS_28.49 //
children.translated_text: He becomes one of loving mind, free from envy — his happiness in this very life is not small.' // SRS_28.49 //

body.text: daśeme kumāra ānuśaṃsāḥ śūnyatāvihāriṇo bodhisatvasya mahāsattvasya | katame daśa? yaduta buddhavihāreṇa viharati | aniśrito dhyāyati | upapattiṃ na prārthayati | śīlaṃ na parāmṛśati | (Vaidya 167) āryānnāpavadati | aviruddho viharati | vastu nopalabhate | viviktaśca bhavati | buddhānnābhyākhyāyati | saddharmaṃ dhārayati | ime kumāra daśānuśaṃsāḥ śūnyatāvihāriṇo bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya ||
body.translated_text: 'These, O prince, are the ten benefits for a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> who dwells in emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>). Which ten? Namely: he dwells with the dwelling of a <s>Buddha</s>; he meditates without reliance; he does not aspire to [future] rebirth; he does not grasp at morality; (Vaidya 167) he does not reproach the noble ones (<s>āryas</s>); he dwells without conflict; he does not apprehend substance; he is secluded; he does not slander the <s>Buddhas</s>; he retains the true <s>Dharma</s>. These, O prince, are the ten benefits for a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> who dwells in emptiness.' ||

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Concerning this, it was said:

children.text: yo vihāro narendrāṇāṃ sarvabuddhāna gocaraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'That dwelling which is the domain of all <s>Buddhas</s>, of the Lords of Men —

children.text: teno viharate yogī yatra jīvo na labhyate // SRS_28.50 //
children.translated_text: the practitioner dwells therein, where no living being is found. // SRS_28.50 //

children.text: aniśritaḥ sarvaloke āryaṃ dhyānaṃ na riñcati /
children.translated_text: Without reliance on all the world, he does not abandon the noble <s>dhyāna</s>;

children.text: upapattiṃ na prārtheti dṛṣṭvā dharmasvabhāvatām // SRS_28.51 //
children.translated_text: he does not aspire to rebirth, having seen the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s>. // SRS_28.51 //

children.text: aparāmṛṣṭaśīlasya bhavecchīlamaniśritam /
children.translated_text: For one who does not grasp at morality, his morality is without reliance;

children.text: na so 'pavadate kiṃcidanyamāryaṃ anāsravam // SRS_28.52 //
children.translated_text: he does not reproach in the slightest another who is noble and free from outflows. // SRS_28.52 //

children.text: aviruddho viharati vivādo 'sya na vidyate /
children.translated_text: He dwells without conflict; dispute does not exist for him;

children.text: vastuṃ nopalabhed yogī vivikto viharī sadā // SRS_28.53 //
children.translated_text: the practitioner does not apprehend substance — he always dwells in seclusion. // SRS_28.53 //

children.text: abhyākhyāti na so buddhamapi jīvitakāraṇāt /
children.translated_text: He does not slander the <s>Buddha</s>, even for the sake of his life;

children.text: niśritaḥ śūnyadharmeṣu kāyasākṣī viśāradaḥ // SRS_28.54 //
children.translated_text: relying on the <s>dharmas</s> of emptiness, a bodily witness, confident — // SRS_28.54 //

children.text: sarveṣāṃ lokanāthānāṃ buddhabodhimacintiyām /
children.translated_text: the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-awakening of all the Lords of the World —

children.text: dharmaṃ dhāreti satkṛtya buddhadharmānna kāṅkṣati // SRS_28.55 //
children.translated_text: he retains the <s>Dharma</s> with reverence and does not doubt the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. // SRS_28.55 //

children.text: ye te vihārāḥ puruṣarṣabhāṇāṃ yasminnabhūmiḥ pṛthutīrthikānām /
children.translated_text: Those dwellings of the Bulls among Men, wherein there is no ground for common non-Buddhist teachers —

children.text: viharatyasau tairiha bodhisattvo yasminna sattvo na jīvu na pudgalaḥ // SRS_28.56 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Bodhisattva</s> dwells therein, where there is no being, no living soul, no person. // SRS_28.56 //

children.text: na niśrayastasya kadāci vidyate aniśritaḥ sevate dhyānasaukhyam /
children.translated_text: No reliance is ever found for him; without reliance he resorts to the bliss of <s>dhyāna</s>;

children.text: nirātma niḥsattva viditva dharmānupapattisaṃjñāsya na jātu bhoti // SRS_28.57 //
children.translated_text: having known <s>dharmas</s> as selfless and without a being — the perception of rebirth never arises for him. // SRS_28.57 //

children.text: svabhāvu dharmāṇa prajānataśca śīle 'pi tasyeha na kaści niśrayaḥ /
children.translated_text: For one who knows the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s>, even in morality there is no reliance for him;

children.text: śīlena no manyati jātu śuddhiṃ prasādamāryeṣu karoti nityam // SRS_28.58 //
children.translated_text: he never considers purification through morality alone — he always generates faith in the noble ones. // SRS_28.58 //

children.text: virodhu tasyo na kadāci bhoti vibhāvitāḥ sarvasvabhāvaśūnyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Conflict never arises for him — all own-natures are cultivated as empty;

children.text: na cāpi so 'bhyākhyāti nāyakānāṃ saddharma dhāritva tathāgatānām // SRS_28.59 //
children.translated_text: and he does not slander the Leaders — retaining the true <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.' // SRS_28.59 //

body.text:
(Vaidya 168)
daśeme kumāra ānuśaṃsāḥ pratisaṃlayanābhiyuktasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya | katame daśa ?yaduta anāvilacitto bhavati | apramatto viharati | buddhamanusmarati | caryāṃ śraddadhāti | jñāne na kāṅkṣati | kṛtajño bhavati | buddhānāṃ dharmaṃ na pratikṣipati | susaṃvṛto viharati | dāntabhūmimanuprāpnoti| pratisaṃvidaḥ sākṣātkaroti | ime kumāra daśānuśaṃsāḥ pratisaṃlayanābhiyuktasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya ||
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 168) These, O Prince, are the ten benefits for a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> devoted to meditative seclusion (<s>pratisaṃlayana</s>). What are the ten? Namely: his mind becomes unclouded; he dwells diligently; he recollects the <s>Buddha</s>; he has faith in the conduct; he does not doubt in knowledge; he is grateful; he does not reject the <s>dharma</s> of the <s>Buddhas</s>; he dwells well-restrained; he attains the stage of self-mastery; and he directly realizes the analytical knowledges. These, O Prince, are the ten benefits for a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> devoted to meditative seclusion.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: On this, it is said:

children.text: cittamanāvilaṃ bhoti pramādāḥ sarvi varjitāḥ /
children.translated_text: The mind becomes unclouded, all heedlessness is abandoned;

children.text: apramatto viharati pratisaṃlānagocaram // SRS_28.60 //
children.translated_text: he dwells diligent, ranging in meditative seclusion. // SRS_28.60 //

children.text: śrutvā ca lokanāthānāṃ caryāṃ buddhāna śraddadhe /
children.translated_text: Having heard the conduct of the Lords of the World, he has faith in the <s>Buddhas</s>;

children.text: jñāne na kāṅkṣate yogī buddhajñāne acintiye // SRS_28.61 //
children.translated_text: the <s>yogī</s> does not doubt in knowledge — in the inconceivable knowledge of the <s>Buddha</s>. // SRS_28.61 //

children.text: kṛtajño bhoti buddhānāṃ buddhadharmānna kāṅkṣati /
children.translated_text: He becomes grateful toward the <s>Buddhas</s>, he does not doubt the <s>Buddha-dharma</s>;

children.text: susaṃvṛto viharati dāntabhūmipratiṣṭhitaḥ // SRS_28.62 //
children.translated_text: he dwells well-restrained, established in the stage of self-mastery. // SRS_28.62 //

children.text: pratisaṃvidaḥ sa labhate ya eko ramate sadā /
children.translated_text: He obtains the analytical knowledges, he who always delights in solitude,

children.text: jahitvā lābhasatkāraṃ pratisaṃlānagocaraḥ // SRS_28.63 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned gain and honor, ranging in meditative seclusion. // SRS_28.63 //

children.text: cittaṃ ca tasyo bhavati anāvilaṃ sarve pramādāḥ parivarjitāsya /
children.translated_text: And his mind becomes unclouded, all heedlessness abandoned;

children.text: sadāpramatto bhavatī mahātmā samādhiyuktasya ime 'nuśaṃsāḥ // SRS_28.64 //
children.translated_text: the great being is always diligent — these are the benefits for one devoted to <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_28.64 //

children.text: smaritva buddhān dvipadānamuttamān śraddhāti teṣāṃ cariyāmanuttarām /
children.translated_text: Recollecting the <s>Buddhas</s>, the supreme among bipeds, he has faith in their unsurpassed conduct;

children.text: na kāṅkṣati jñānu tathāgatānāṃ samādhiyukte imi ānuśaṃsāḥ // SRS_28.65 //
children.translated_text: he does not doubt the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> — these are the benefits for one devoted to <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_28.65 //

children.text: buddhāna so bhoti sadā kṛtajño na jīvitārthaṃ sa kṣipeta dharmam /
children.translated_text: He is always grateful toward the <s>Buddhas</s>, he would not reject the <s>dharma</s> even for the sake of his life;

children.text: susaṃvṛto viharati nityakālaṃ samādhiyukte imi ānuśaṃsāḥ // SRS_28.66 //
children.translated_text: he dwells well-restrained at all times — these are the benefits for one devoted to <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_28.66 //

children.text: sa dāntabhūmīmanuprāpta bhoti pratisaṃvidaḥ sākṣikaroti kṣipram /
children.translated_text: He attains the stage of self-mastery, he quickly realizes the analytical knowledges directly;

children.text: anācchedyavākya pratibhānavāṃśca sūtrāntakoṭiniyutāna bhāṣate // SRS_28.67 //
children.translated_text: with unbroken speech and ready wit, he expounds <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of <s>sūtras</s>. // SRS_28.67 //

children.text: sa buddhabodhiṃ parigṛhṇate laghum ārakṣate śāsanu nāyakasya /
