children.translated_text: He swiftly embraces the awakening of a <s>Buddha</s>, he guards the teaching of the Guide;

children.text: (Vaidya 169)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 169)

children.text: nihanitva so sarvaparapravādinaḥ karoti vaistārika buddhabodhim // SRS_28.68 //
children.translated_text: having defeated all opposing disputants, he makes the awakening of the <s>Buddha</s> widely known. // SRS_28.68 //

children.text: itaścyavitvāna sa bodhisattvaḥ sukhāvatīṃ gacchati lokadhātum /
children.translated_text: Having departed from here, that <s>Bodhisattva</s> goes to the <s>Sukhāvatī</s> world-realm;

children.text: anutpādadharmeṣu ca kṣānti lapsyate amitāyuṣo dharmavarāgru śrutvā // SRS_28.69 //
children.translated_text: and he will attain patient acceptance of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s>, having heard the supreme excellent <s>dharma</s> of <s>Amitāyus</s>. // SRS_28.69 //

body.text: daśeme kumāra ānuśaṃsā araṇyavāsagurukasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya | katame daśa? yaduta alpakṛtyo viharati | gaṇaṃ varjayati | vivādo 'sya na bhavati | avyāvadhyo bhavati | āsravāna vardhayati | adhikaraṇaṃ na karoti | upaśāntaścarati | susaṃvṛtaśva viharati | mokṣānukūlā cāsya cittasaṃtatirbhavati | kṣipraṃ ca vimuktiṃ sākṣātkaroti | ime kumāra daśānuśaṃsā araṇyavāsagurukasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya ||
body.translated_text: These, O Prince, are the ten benefits for a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> who values dwelling in the forest. What are the ten? Namely: he dwells with few duties; he avoids assemblies; he has no disputes; he is unobstructed; he does not increase the <s>āsravas</s> (defilements); he does not engage in disputes; he walks peacefully; he dwells well-restrained; his mind-stream becomes favorable to liberation; and he quickly realizes liberation directly. These, O Prince, are the ten benefits for a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> who values dwelling in the forest.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: On this, it is said:

children.text: alpakṛtyaḥ sadā bhoti gaṇaṃ varjeti dūrataḥ /
children.translated_text: He is always of few duties, he avoids assemblies from afar;

children.text: vivādo na bhavatyasya vaneṣvekavihāriṇaḥ // SRS_28.70 //
children.translated_text: no dispute arises for him — for the one who dwells alone in the forests. // SRS_28.70 //

children.text: avyāvadhyena cittena āsravānna vivardhayet /
children.translated_text: With an unobstructed mind, he does not increase the <s>āsravas</s>;

children.text: nāsyādhikaraṇaṃ bhoti guṇāste 'raṇyavāsinaḥ // SRS_28.71 //
children.translated_text: no disputes arise for him — these are the virtues of the forest-dweller. // SRS_28.71 //

children.text: upaśāntaḥ sa carate manovākkāyasaṃvṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: He walks peacefully, restrained in mind, speech, and body;

children.text: mokṣānukūlo bhavati vimuktiṃ kṣipra sparśati // SRS_28.72 //
children.translated_text: he becomes favorable to liberation, he quickly touches liberation. // SRS_28.72 //

children.text: bhavati satatamalpakṛtyu yogī pṛthugaṇadoṣeṇa vivarjayitvā /
children.translated_text: The <s>yogī</s> is always of few duties, having abandoned the faults of large assemblies;

children.text: na vivadati kadāci mukta yogī imi guṇa tasya bhavatyaraṇyavāse // SRS_28.73 //
children.translated_text: the liberated <s>yogī</s> never quarrels — these virtues are his in forest dwelling. // SRS_28.73 //

children.text: yada bhavati nirviṇṇu saṃskṛte 'sau na bhavati tasya spṛhā kahiṃci loke /
children.translated_text: When he becomes weary of the conditioned, he has no craving anywhere in the world;

children.text: na ca bhavati vivṛddhirāsravāṇāṃ vani vasato 'sya bhavanti ānuśaṃsāḥ // SRS_28.74 //
children.translated_text: nor is there growth of the <s>āsravas</s> — for him dwelling in the forest, these are the benefits. // SRS_28.74 //

children.text: adhikaraṇu na jātu cāsya bhoti upaśāntarato vivekacārī /
children.translated_text: No disputes ever arise for him; delighting in peace, walking in solitude,

children.text: vacasi manasi kāye saṃvṛtasyo bahu guṇa tasya bhavantyaraṇyavāse // SRS_28.75 //
children.translated_text: restrained in speech, mind, and body — many virtues are his in forest dwelling. // SRS_28.75 //

children.text: (Vaidya 170)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 170)

children.text: bhavati ca anukūla tasya mokṣo laghu pratipadyati so vimukti śāntam /
children.translated_text: And liberation becomes favorable for him; he swiftly attains peaceful liberation;

children.text: vani vasati vimukti sevato 'syā imi guṇa bhonti araṇyavāsi sarve // SRS_28.76 //
children.translated_text: dwelling in the forest, devoted to liberation — all these virtues belong to the forest-dweller. // SRS_28.76 //

body.text: daśeme kumāra ānuśaṃsāḥ piṇḍacārikasya dhūtaguṇasaṃlekhapratiṣṭhitasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya | katame daśa? yaduta jñātrakāmatāsya na bhavati | yaśaskāmatāsya na bhavati | lābhasatkārakāmatāsya na bhavati | āryavaṃśapratiṣṭhitaśca bhavati | kuhanalapanatāsya na bhavati | ātmānaṃ notkarṣayati | parānna paṃsayati | anunayapratighaprahīṇaḥ paragṛhe carati | nirāmiṣaṃ ca dharmadānaṃ dadāti | dhūtaguṇasaṃlekhapratiṣṭhitasya cāsya grāhyā dharmadeśanā bhavati | ime kumāra daśānuśaṃsāḥ piṇḍapātikasya dhūpaguṇasaṃlekhapratiṣṭhitasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya ||
body.translated_text: These, O Prince, are the ten benefits for a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> who practices alms-round (<s>piṇḍacārika</s>) and is established in the ascetic qualities (<s>dhūtaguṇa</s>) and austerity. What are the ten? Namely: he has no desire for relatives; he has no desire for fame; he has no desire for gain and honor; he is established in the noble lineage (<s>āryavaṃśa</s>); he has no hypocrisy or flattery; he does not exalt himself; he does not disparage others; free from attachment and aversion, he moves among others' houses; he gives the gift of <s>dharma</s> without material gain; and his <s>dharma</s>-teaching, being established in the ascetic qualities and austerity, becomes authoritative. These, O Prince, are the ten benefits for a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> who practices alms-collection and is established in the ascetic qualities and austerity.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: On this, it is said:

children.text: na jñātrakāmo bhavati yaśo nāpyabhinandate /
children.translated_text: He has no desire for relatives, nor does he delight in fame;

children.text: lābhālābhe samacitto yo dhūteṣu pratiṣṭhitaḥ // SRS_28.77 //
children.translated_text: equal-minded toward gain and non-gain — one who is established in the ascetic practices. // SRS_28.77 //

children.text: notsṛjatyāryavaṃśaṃ ca kuhanā lapanā na ca /
children.translated_text: He does not abandon the noble lineage, and has neither hypocrisy nor flattery;

children.text: utkarṣeti na cātmānaṃ parān paṃsayate na ca // SRS_28.78 //
children.translated_text: he does not exalt himself, nor does he disparage others. // SRS_28.78 //

children.text: pratighānunayau cāsya dharmaṃ deśī nirāmiṣam /
children.translated_text: Free from aversion and attachment, he teaches the <s>dharma</s> without material gain;

children.text: grāhyaṃ si vacanaṃ bhoti piṇḍapāte guṇā amī // SRS_28.79 //
children.translated_text: his words become authoritative — these are the virtues of the alms-round. // SRS_28.79 //

children.text: na mārgate jñātra yaśo na lābhaṃ caturāryavaṃśe bhavati pratiṣṭhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: He does not seek relatives, fame, or gain; he is established in the four noble lineages;

children.text: akuhako alapaku bhoti paṇḍito dhūtādhimuktasya imīdṛśā guṇāḥ // SRS_28.80 //
children.translated_text: without hypocrisy, without flattery, the wise one — such are the virtues of one devoted to ascetic practices. // SRS_28.80 //

children.text: nātmānamutkarṣi parānna paṃsī puruṣaṃ pi ukto na kadāci kupyate /
children.translated_text: He does not exalt himself, he does not disparage others; even when rebuked, he never becomes angry;

children.text: varṇaṃ pi śrutvā janaye na harṣaṃ yaḥ piṇḍapātena bhaveta tuṣṭaḥ // SRS_28.81 //
children.translated_text: even hearing praise, he does not generate elation — one who is content with alms-food. // SRS_28.81 //

children.text: nirāmiṣaṃ deti ca dharmadānaṃ na lābhasatkāra gaveṣate 'sau /
children.translated_text: He gives the gift of <s>dharma</s> without material gain, he does not seek gain and honor;

children.text: grāhyā ca tasya bhavate 'sya bhāṣitaṃ dhūtādhimuktasya ime 'nuśaṃsāḥ // SRS_28.82 //
children.translated_text: and his speech becomes authoritative — these are the benefits of one devoted to ascetic practices. // SRS_28.82 //

body.text: iti hi kumāra evaṃrūpeṣu dhūtaguṇeṣu pratiṣṭhito bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'raṇye viharan buddhanidhānaṃ pratilabhate | dharmanidhānaṃ pratilabhate | jñānanidhānaṃ pratilabhate | pūrvāntāparāntapratyutpannajñānanidhānaṃ (Vaidya 171) pratilabhate | kathaṃ ca kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvo buddhanidhānaṃ pratilabhate?imāḥ kumāra vivekacārī bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ pañcābhijñāḥ pratilabhate | sa divyena cakṣuṣā viśuddhenātikrāntamānuṣyakeṇa pūrvasyāṃ diśi aprameyānasaṃkhyeyān buddhān bhagavataḥ paśyati | evaṃ dakṣiṇasyāṃ paścimāyāmuttarasyāṃ diśi aprameyānasaṃkhyeyān buddhān bhagavataḥ paśyati | so 'virahito bhavati buddhadarśanena | evaṃ hi kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvo buddhanidhānaṃ pratilabhate | kathaṃ ca kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvo dharmanidhānaṃ pratilabhate? yaṃ ca te buddhā bhagavanto dharmaṃ deśayanti, taṃ sa bodhisattvo mahāsattvo divyena śrotradhātunā sarvaṃ śṛṇoti | so 'virahito bhavati dharmaśravaṇena | evaṃ hi kumāra bodhisattvo dharmanidhānaṃ pratilabhate | kathaṃ ca kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvo jñānanidhānaṃ pratilabhate? yena jñānena sarvadharmānārādhayati | ārādhayitvā avipramuṣitasmṛtiḥ sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati | tasya ca yo 'rthaḥ sa prajānāti | evaṃ hi kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvo jñānanidhānaṃ pratilabhate | kathaṃ ca kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ pūrvāntāparāntapratyutpannajñānanidhānaṃ pratilabhate? so 'bhijñayā atītānāgatapratyutpannasattvacittacaritajñānamavatarati | evaṃ hi kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ pūrvāntāparāntapratyutpannajñānanidhānaṃ pratilabhate | saṃkṣiptena kumāra evaṃguṇadharmapratiṣṭhito bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvabuddhadharmān pratilabhate yatrābhūmiḥ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānām, kaḥ punarvādaḥ sarvaparapravādinām ||
body.translated_text: Thus, O Prince, a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> established in such ascetic qualities, dwelling in the forest, obtains the treasure of the <s>Buddha</s>. He obtains the treasure of <s>dharma</s>. He obtains the treasure of knowledge. He obtains the treasure of knowledge of the past, future, and present. And how, O Prince, does the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> obtain the treasure of the <s>Buddha</s>? Here, O Prince, a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> who walks in solitude attains the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>). With the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, he sees in the eastern direction immeasurable and incalculable <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones. Likewise in the southern, western, and northern directions he sees immeasurable and incalculable <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones. He is never separated from the sight of the <s>Buddha</s>. Thus, O Prince, the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> obtains the treasure of the <s>Buddha</s>. And how, O Prince, does the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> obtain the treasure of <s>dharma</s>? Whatever <s>dharma</s> those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, teach — the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> hears all of it with the divine ear-element. He is never separated from hearing the <s>dharma</s>. Thus, O Prince, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> obtains the treasure of <s>dharma</s>. And how, O Prince, does the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> obtain the treasure of knowledge? Through that knowledge by which he masters all <s>dharmas</s>, and having mastered them, with unfailing mindfulness he teaches the <s>dharma</s> to beings, and he understands its meaning. Thus, O Prince, the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> obtains the treasure of knowledge. And how, O Prince, does the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> obtain the treasure of knowledge of the past, future, and present? Through superknowledge he enters into the knowledge of the mental conduct of beings of the past, future, and present. Thus, O Prince, the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> obtains the treasure of knowledge of the past, future, and present. In brief, O Prince, a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> established in such qualities and <s>dharmas</s> obtains all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> — a stage inaccessible to all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, how much more so to all opposing disputants!

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: On this, it is said:

children.text: buddhanidhānaṃ ca dharmanidhānaṃ jñānanidhānaṃ ca pūrvāntanidhānam /
children.translated_text: The treasure of the <s>Buddha</s>, the treasure of <s>dharma</s>, the treasure of knowledge, and the treasure of the past —

children.text: pañca abhijñāḥ sa kṣipraṃ labhati yo vidu raṇṇi sadā sthitu bhoti // SRS_28.83 //
children.translated_text: he quickly attains the five superknowledges, the wise one who always abides in the forest. // SRS_28.83 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje daśānuśaṃsāparivarto nāma aṣṭāviṃśatitamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-eighth chapter in the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, the chapter called "The Ten Benefits" (<s>Daśānuśaṃsāparivarta</s>).

body.text:
(Vaidya 172)
29 Tejaguṇarājaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 172) Chapter 29: The <s>Tejaguṇarājaparivarta</s> (Chapter on King <s>Tejaguṇa</s>).

body.text: tatra bhagavān punarapi candraprabhaṃ kumārabhūtamāmantrayate sma - tasmāttarhi kumāra divyāni cakravartirājyaiśvaryasukhānyapahāya pravrajiṣyāmītyevaṃ tvayā kumāra sadā śikṣitavyam | pravrajitena kumāra dhūtaguṇasaṃlekhapratiṣṭhitena vivekacāriṇā kṣāntisauratyasaṃpannena bhavitavyam | sadā ca ārabdhavīryeṇa te kumāra ādīptaśiraścailopamena ayaṃ sarvadharmasvabhāvasamatāvipañcitaḥ samādhiḥ śrotavya udgrahītavyaḥ paryavāptavyaḥ pravartayitavyo dhārayitavyo vācayitavyaḥ uddeṣṭavyaḥ svādhyātavyo 'raṇābhāvanayā bhāvayitavyo bahulīkartavyaḥ, parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayitavyaḥ | khaṅgaviṣāṇabhūtena advitīyena ca te kumāra araṇyaniṣeviṇā sadā bhavitavyam | ātmaparityāgenāpi te kumāra sarvasattvānāmarthaḥ sadā karaṇīya iti ||
body.translated_text: There the Blessed One again addressed Prince <s>Candraprabha</s>: "Therefore, O Prince, [you should train thus]: 'I shall renounce the divine pleasures, sovereignty, and enjoyments of a <s>Cakravartin</s> king and go forth!' — thus, O Prince, you should always train. Having gone forth, O Prince, one established in ascetic qualities and austerity, walking in solitude, should be endowed with <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) and <s>sauratya</s> (gentleness). And always, O Prince, with aroused vigor, as if your head and turban were on fire, this <s>samādhi</s> that elaborates the equality of the own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s> should be heard, grasped, mastered, set in motion, retained, recited, expounded, studied, cultivated through meditation on non-contention, practiced extensively, and fully elucidated to others in detail. Like a rhinoceros horn, alone and without a companion, O Prince, you should always dwell in the forest. Even at the cost of sacrificing yourself, O Prince, you should always act for the benefit of all beings."

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyā velāyāmetamevārthamudbhāvayaṃścandraprabhasya kumārabhūtasyemaṃ pūrvayogakathāparivartaṃ gāthābhigītena vistareṇa saṃprakāśayati sma -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, bringing forth this very meaning, fully elucidated to Prince <s>Candraprabha</s> this chapter on the story of past connections (<s>pūrvayoga</s>), extensively in verses:

children.text: smaramī atīta bahukalpaśatā yada āsi nāyaku anantayaśāḥ /
children.translated_text: "I recall hundreds of past <s>kalpas</s>, when there was a Guide of infinite fame,

children.text: naradevanāgagaṇapūjaniyo nāmena tejaguṇi rāja jino // SRS_29.1 //
children.translated_text: worshipped by hosts of gods, humans, and <s>Nāgas</s>, the Conqueror named King <s>Tejaguṇi</s>. // SRS_29.1 //

children.text: daśa bhikṣukoṭi ṣaḍabhijñaruhāḥ pratisaṃvidāna vaśipāragatāḥ /
children.translated_text: Ten <s>koṭīs</s> of monks, possessing the six superknowledges,

children.text: dhūtavṛtta saṃlekhita śāntamanāḥ iti tasya tena samayena gaṇāḥ // SRS_29.2 //
children.translated_text: who had reached mastery of the analytical knowledges, of ascetic conduct and austerity, with peaceful minds — such was his assembly at that time. // SRS_29.2 //

children.text: ṣaṭsaptatī nagara koṭiśatāḥ pañcāśayojanapramāṇa samāḥ /
children.translated_text: Seventy-six hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of cities, each fifty <s>yojanas</s> in extent,

children.text: ratanāna saptana viśiṣṭavarā iha jambudvīpi tada kāli abhūt // SRS_29.3 //
children.translated_text: excellent and adorned with seven kinds of jewels — such existed in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> at that time. // SRS_29.3 //

children.text: tada kāli te puravarā sakalāḥ pratimaṇḍitā bahu udyānaśataiḥ /
children.translated_text: At that time, all those excellent cities were adorned with hundreds of gardens;

children.text: udyāna sarvi ghanameghanibhāḥ phalapuṣpamaṇḍita tarunicitāḥ // SRS_29.4 //
children.translated_text: all the gardens were like dense clouds, filled with fruits and flowers and young trees. // SRS_29.4 //

children.text: phalavṛkṣajāti vividhā rucirāḥ lakucāmrajambupanasairnicitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Various kinds of beautiful fruit trees — filled with <s>lakuca</s>, mango, <s>jambu</s>, and jackfruit;

children.text: (Vaidya 173)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 173)

children.text: karṇikāracampakapunnāgaśataiḥ pratimaṇḍitāsta udyānavarāḥ // SRS_29.5 //
children.translated_text: adorned with hundreds of <s>karṇikāra</s>, <s>campaka</s>, and <s>punnāga</s> trees — those excellent gardens. // SRS_29.5 //

children.text: nyagrodha sarvi dvijasaṃgharutāḥ kalaviṅkakokilamayūraśataiḥ /
children.translated_text: All the <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan) trees resounded with flocks of birds — hundreds of <s>kalaviṅka</s> cuckoos, and peacocks,

children.text: śukajīvaṃjīvakakuṇālarutā bahupakṣisaṃgharuta kāli tadā // SRS_29.6 //
children.translated_text: the sounds of parrots, <s>jīvaṃjīvaka</s> birds, and <s>kuṇāla</s> birds — the sounds of many flocks of birds at that time! // SRS_29.6 //

children.text: dhṛtarāṣṭrarājahaṃsopanibhā bhṛṅgakuṇālā varaghoṣarutāḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> geese, royal geese, <s>bhṛṅga</s> birds, and <s>kuṇāla</s> birds with excellent, resonant calls,

children.text: citrāṅgaraktamahāvarṇaprabhāḥ sumanojñaśabda madhurā muditāḥ // SRS_29.7 //
children.translated_text: with dappled, red, and great-colored splendor, their sounds most delightful, sweet, and joyful! // SRS_29.7 //

children.text: iti pakṣi samāgata kāli tadā kalaviṅkamayūravihaṅgarutaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Thus birds gathered at that time — with the sounds of <s>kalaviṅka</s> birds, peacocks, and other birds;

children.text: parapuṣṭa śārika vicitra dvijā bahupakṣighoṣaruta nānavidhāḥ // SRS_29.8 //
children.translated_text: cuckoos, <s>sārikā</s> birds, and variegated winged ones — many kinds of bird-sounds of many sorts! // SRS_29.8 //

children.text: tehi niṣevita udyānaśatā mucilindavārṣika aśokaśataiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Frequented by them were hundreds of gardens, with <s>mucilinda</s>, <s>vārṣika</s>, and hundreds of <s>aśoka</s> trees,

children.text: atimuktakātha javapuṣpapatraiḥ padmotpalaiḥ kumudapuṇḍarikaiḥ // SRS_29.9 //
children.translated_text: with <s>atimuktaka</s> vines, barley-flowers, and leaves, with lotuses, <s>utpalas</s>, water-lilies, and white lotuses. // SRS_29.9 //

children.text: padumaiḥ sahasraśatapatracitā imi puṣpa puṣkariṇiśobhakarāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Lotuses with hundred-thousand petals, adorned — these flowers beautifying the lotus-ponds;

children.text: pratimaṇḍitāḥ surabhigandhavarāḥ śobhanti puṣkariṇiyo rucirāḥ // SRS_29.10 //
children.translated_text: adorned with the finest, fragrant scents, the beautiful lotus-ponds shone! // SRS_29.10 //

children.text: tahi kāli rāja iha jambudhvaje dṛḍhadattu āsi manujādhipatiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'At that time, in this <s>Jambudhvaja</s> (Rose-Apple Banner), there was a king named <s>Dṛḍhadatta</s> (Firm Gift), the lord of men;

children.text: putrāṇa tasya abhu pañcaśatāḥ prāsādikāḥ paramadarśanikāḥ // SRS_29.11 //
children.translated_text: he had five hundred sons, gracious and supremely handsome. // SRS_29.11 //

children.text: tahi kāli rājyu śivu kṣema abhūt anupadrutaṃ suramaṇīya śivam /
children.translated_text: 'At that time the kingdom was auspicious, secure, free from affliction, divinely beautiful, and blessed;

children.text: ayu jambudvīpa kusumairnicito nirviṃśeṣa devabhavanehi samam // SRS_29.12 //
children.translated_text: this <s>Jambudvīpa</s> was strewn with flowers, equal to divine abodes without distinction. // SRS_29.12 //

children.text: (Vaidya 174)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 174)

children.text: tahi kāli so daśabalo anidho jinu bhāṣate imu samādhivaram /
children.translated_text: 'At that time, that unshakable <s>Daśabala</s>, the <s>Jina</s>, spoke this supreme <s>samādhi</s>:

children.text: svapnopamā bhavagatī sakalā na va kaści jāyati na co mriyate // SRS_29.13 //
children.translated_text: "All states of existence are like a dream; no one is truly born, nor does anyone die. // SRS_29.13 //

children.text: na sattva labhyati na jīvu naro imi dharma phenakadalīsadṛśāḥ /
children.translated_text: '"No being is found, no self, no person — these <s>dharmas</s> are like foam and a plantain tree,

children.text: māyopamā gaganavidyusamā dakacandrasaṃnibha marīcisamāḥ // SRS_29.14 //
children.translated_text: like an illusion, like lightning in the sky, like a reflection of the moon in water, like a mirage! // SRS_29.14 //

children.text: na ca asmi loki mṛtu kaści naro paraloki saṃkramati gacchati vā /
children.translated_text: '"No person dies in this world, nor transmigrates or goes to another world;

children.text: na ca karma naśyati kadāci kṛtaṃ phalameti kṛṣṇa śubha saṃsarato // SRS_29.15 //
children.translated_text: yet <s>karma</s> once done is never destroyed — dark and bright fruits ripen for the one who transmigrates. // SRS_29.15 //

children.text: na ca śāśvataṃ na ca ucchedu puno na ca karmasaṃcayu na cāpi sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: '"It is neither eternal nor is there annihilation; there is no accumulation of <s>karma</s> nor any fixed state;

children.text: na ca so 'pi kṛtva punaraspṛśatī na ca anyu kṛtva puna vedayate // SRS_29.16 //
children.translated_text: the one who does [the deed] does not [himself] experience it again, nor does another do it and another experience [its fruit]. // SRS_29.16 //

children.text: na ca saṃkramo na ca punāgamanaṃ na ca sarvamasti na ca nāsti punaḥ /
children.translated_text: '"There is no transmigration, nor again any coming; not everything exists, nor does it not-exist;

children.text: na ca dṛṣṭisthānu gatiśuddhiriho na ca sattvacaru na praśāntagatī // SRS_29.17 //
children.translated_text: purity of destination is not through standing in a view; there is no path of beings, nor is there a tranquil destination. // SRS_29.17 //

children.text: anupādu śāntu animittapadaṃ sugatāna gocaru jināna guṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: '"Non-arising, peaceful, the signless state — the domain of the <s>Sugatas</s>, the qualities of the <s>Jinas</s>;

children.text: bala dhāraṇī daśabalāna balaṃ buddhāniyaṃ vṛṣabhitā paramā // SRS_29.18 //
children.translated_text: powers, <s>dhāraṇīs</s>, the strength of the <s>Daśabalas</s> — this is the supreme bull-like quality of the <s>Buddhas</s>! // SRS_29.18 //

children.text: varaśukladharma guṇasaṃnicayo guṇajñānadhāraṇibalaṃ paramam /
children.translated_text: '"The excellent, bright <s>dharma</s>, an accumulation of virtues; the supreme power of virtue, knowledge, and <s>dhāraṇī</s>;

children.text: ṛddhivikurvaṇāvidhiḥ paramā varapañcābhijñā pratilābhanayaḥ // SRS_29.19 //
children.translated_text: the supreme method of spiritual powers and transformations; the method of attaining the five excellent <s>abhijñās</s> (higher knowledges)! // SRS_29.19 //

children.text: na ca sa prajānatīha svabhāvu kvaci agatāgatī nipuṇadharmagatī /
children.translated_text: '"But he does not know own-nature as being anywhere — the subtle <s>dharma</s>-course of non-coming and non-going;

children.text: (Vaidya 175)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 175)

children.text: na ca dharmadhātu vrajatīha kvaci evaṃ gatī agati dharmagatī // SRS_29.20 //
children.translated_text: nor does the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of dharma) go anywhere here — thus the course of <s>dharma</s> is going and non-going! // SRS_29.20 //

children.text: na ca ghoṣasaṃcayu svabhāvagatī gatiyo svabhāvu na kahiṃci sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: '"No accumulation of sound, the course of own-nature — the own-nature of destinations is not fixed anywhere;

children.text: asthitā aniśritā svabhāvagatī jinagocaro viraju śāntapadam // SRS_29.21 //
children.translated_text: unfixed, unsupported, the course of own-nature — the domain of the <s>Jinas</s>, the dustless, peaceful state! // SRS_29.21 //

children.text: śāntapraśānta upaśāntagatī na ca sā gatī kvacana saṃsthihatī /
children.translated_text: '"Peaceful, tranquil, the course of calm — yet that course is not established anywhere;

children.text: bhāvu svabhāvu nugatāḥ satataṃ nipuṇaṃ sudurdṛśu padaṃ acalam // SRS_29.22 //
children.translated_text: always following the own-nature of existence — subtle, hard to see, the state is unmoving! // SRS_29.22 //

children.text: na ca sā calā hi svayameva sthitā asthitā anāgata svabhāvu sthitā /
children.translated_text: '"Yet it is not moving, for it stands by itself; unfixed, uncome, established in own-nature;

children.text: na ca śakya bhāṣitu svabhāvu sthitī śūnyā ca sā acalu dharmasthitī // SRS_29.23 //
children.translated_text: the standing in own-nature cannot be expressed — it is empty, and that <s>dharma</s>-standing is unmoving! // SRS_29.23 //

children.text: ghoṣaśca ukta na ca ghoṣagatī ghoṣasvabhāvagati dharmagatī /
children.translated_text: '"Sound has been spoken, yet there is no course of sound; the <s>dharma</s>-course is the course of the own-nature of sound;

children.text: na ca ghoṣasaṃcayu sthitī ca kvaci evaṃsvabhāvu gati dharmagatī // SRS_29.24 //
children.translated_text: nor is there any standing of the accumulation of sound anywhere — such is the own-nature course, the <s>dharma</s>-course! // SRS_29.24 //

children.text: gatiśabda uktu na ca sattvagatī dharmasvabhāva nipuṇārthagatī /
children.translated_text: '"The word 'destination' is spoken, yet there is no destination of beings; the course of the subtle meaning of <s>dharma</s>'s own-nature;

children.text: ghoṣo 'pi coktu na ca sattvagatī na ca ghoṣu labhyati na sattvagatiḥ // SRS_29.25 //
children.translated_text: sound too has been spoken, yet there is no destination of beings — neither sound is found nor the destination of beings! // SRS_29.25 //

children.text: na ca ananta nānta na ca madhyagatiḥ naivāsti nāsti na ca deśagatī /
children.translated_text: '"Neither infinite, nor with an end, nor a middle course; neither existing nor non-existing, nor a particular destination;

children.text: jñātā ca yādṛśa svabhāvagatī iya deśanā jinavarāṇa samā // SRS_29.26 //
children.translated_text: when the course of own-nature is known as it truly is — this teaching is equal to that of the supreme <s>Jinas</s>! // SRS_29.26 //

children.text: virajaṃ viśuddhi paramārthapadaṃ śānta praśānta arajaṃ virajam /
children.translated_text: '"Dustless, pure, the state of ultimate reality; peaceful, tranquil, dustless, stainless;

children.text: na ca kalpa manyana praśāntapadaṃ jinu bhāṣate paramakāruṇiko // SRS_29.27 //
children.translated_text: not to be conceived or imagined, the peaceful state — the <s>Jina</s>, supremely compassionate, speaks it! // SRS_29.27 //

children.text: (Vaidya 176)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 176)

children.text: na pi cāsti akṣarapracāra iho vipulā gatirvipulā arthagatī /
children.translated_text: '"Nor is there here the operation of syllables; vast is the course, vast the course of meaning;

children.text: buddhehi sevita jinehi stutā avabhāsa dharmanaya sūkṣmagatī // SRS_29.28 //
children.translated_text: cultivated by <s>Buddhas</s>, praised by <s>Jinas</s> — the illumination of the subtle course of the <s>dharma</s>-method! // SRS_29.28 //

children.text: dharmanidhāna virajaṃ vipulaṃ yatra sthitā apratimā sugatā /
children.translated_text: '"The treasury of <s>dharma</s>, dustless and vast, wherein the incomparable <s>Sugatas</s> abide;

children.text: deśenti dharmaratanaṃ virajaṃ paramārthaśūnya nipuṇārthagatī // SRS_29.29 //
children.translated_text: they teach the dustless jewel of <s>dharma</s> — the course of subtle meaning, empty in ultimate reality!" // SRS_29.29 //

children.text: aśrauṣi rāja dṛḍhadattu tadā dvipadendra bhāṣati samādhimimam /
children.translated_text: 'King <s>Dṛḍhadatta</s> heard it at that time — the Lord of Bipeds spoke this <s>samādhi</s>;

children.text: so 'śītikoṭinayutehi tadā upasaṃkramī tada jinu kāruṇikam // SRS_29.30 //
children.translated_text: with eighty <s>koṭī-nayutas</s> then, he approached the compassionate <s>Jina</s>. // SRS_29.30 //

children.text: balavantu gauravu janetva jine vanditva pādu manujādhipatiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The powerful lord of men, having generated reverence for the <s>Jina</s>, having bowed at his feet,

children.text: purataḥ sthito daśabalasya tadā kṛtāñjalirdaśanakhaḥ pramuditaḥ // SRS_29.31 //
children.translated_text: stood before the <s>Daśabala</s>, with ten-fingered <s>añjali</s>, joyful. // SRS_29.31 //

children.text: tasyo viditva pariśuddha carīṃ jina indriyeṣu vaśi pāragataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Knowing his pure conduct, the <s>Jina</s>, master of the faculties, gone to the far shore,

children.text: adhumuktikovidu naraḥ pravaro imu tasya deśayi samādhivaram // SRS_29.32 //
children.translated_text: skilled in discerning dispositions, that supreme man — he taught him this excellent <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.32 //

children.text: yada tena rājña paramārtha śruto utpanna prīti ariyā vipulā /
children.translated_text: 'When that king heard the ultimate truth, noble, vast joy arose in him;

children.text: ujjhitva dvīpa sakalāṃścaturo vijahitva kāma abhiniṣkrami so // SRS_29.33 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned all four continents, having renounced sensual pleasures, he went forth! // SRS_29.33 //

children.text: yada rāja pravraji jahitva mahīṃ bodhāya arthiku bhaviṣyajinaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'When the king went forth, having abandoned the earth, desiring awakening, a future <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: sarve manuṣya iha jambudhvaje vijahitva kāmaratī pravrajitā // SRS_29.34 //
children.translated_text: all humans in this <s>Jambudhvaja</s>, having abandoned delight in sensual pleasures, went forth too! // SRS_29.34 //

children.text: vipulo gaṇo daśabalasya tadā bahu bhikṣu bhikṣuṇi prayuktamanāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The retinue of the <s>Daśabala</s> was vast — many monks and nuns, with devoted minds;

children.text: (Vaidya 177)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 177)

children.text: akṛṣṭā anupta tada oṣadhayo prādurbhūtā marutparicarāḥ // SRS_29.35 //
children.translated_text: unplowed and unsown, plants sprang forth then, tended by the wind! // SRS_29.35 //

children.text: kāṣāya tricīvara prādurbhūtā samacchinna susīvita te 'nupamāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Saffron triple-robes appeared spontaneously — well-cut, well-sewn, incomparable;

children.text: amalā virajāśca suvarṇacittā buddhasya guṇocita puṇyabalāḥ // SRS_29.36 //
children.translated_text: stainless, dustless, golden-minded — befitting the <s>Buddha</s>'s qualities, the power of merit! // SRS_29.36 //

children.text: paśyo kumāra sa hi rājavaro vijahitva sarva mahi pravrajitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'See, O Prince, that excellent king, having abandoned everything, went forth!

children.text: bheṣyanti sattva kṣayakāli bahu aparīttabhogā na tyajanti gṛhān // SRS_29.37 //
children.translated_text: But there will be many beings in the age of decline, of no small enjoyments, who will not abandon their homes! // SRS_29.37 //

children.text: tāḍana bandhana kudaṇḍa bahu ākrośa tarjanamaniṣṭadukham /
children.translated_text: 'Much beating, binding, cruel punishment, abuse, threats, and unwished-for suffering —

children.text: sahiṣyanti rājakula pīḍa bahu suparīttabhoga na ca bhaktu gṛhe // SRS_29.38 //
children.translated_text: they will endure much oppression from royal households, with very little food and no sustenance at home! // SRS_29.38 //

children.text: aparītta āyu na ca asti dhanaṃ sumahān pramādu na ca puṇyabalam /
children.translated_text: 'Little is their lifespan, and there is no wealth; great is their heedlessness, and there is no merit-power;

children.text: na ca śilpasthānakuśalā abudhā dāridriyaṃ ca na ca vittu gṛhe // SRS_29.39 //
children.translated_text: unskilled in arts and crafts, ignorant — poverty, and no possessions at home! // SRS_29.39 //

children.text: paradāragṛddha aviśuddhamanā īrṣyālukāḥ paramasāhasikāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Greedy for others' wives, of impure minds, jealous, supremely violent;

children.text: saṃkliṣṭadharma na ca vṛttu sthitā vakṣyanti buddha bhaviṣyām vayam // SRS_29.40 //
children.translated_text: defiled in <s>dharma</s>, not established in conduct — they will say: "We shall become <s>Buddhas</s>!" // SRS_29.40 //

children.text: utkocavañcanaka sāhasikā ahamāḍhyu dharma dhanadāsmi jage /
children.translated_text: 'Bribe-takers, deceivers, violent ones: "I am wealthy! I am a <s>dharma</s>-giver in the world!"

children.text: upaghātakāḥ kuhaka naikṛtikā vakṣyanti buddha bhaviṣyāma vayam // SRS_29.41 //
children.translated_text: Harmers, hypocrites, the treacherous — they will say: "We shall become <s>Buddhas</s>!" // SRS_29.41 //

children.text: vadhabandhupadravi parasya ratāḥ duḥśīla dāruṇa praduṣṭamanāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Delighting in killing, binding, and harassing others; immoral, cruel, of corrupt minds;

children.text: akṛtajña bhedaka vihiṃsasthitā vakṣyanti haṃ te bhaṇa bodhicarim // SRS_29.42 //
children.translated_text: ungrateful, schismatics, devoted to violence — they will say: "Come, tell us the conduct of awakening!" // SRS_29.42 //

children.text: yasyaiva tena śruta bodhicarī tasyaiva madhyi pratighaṃ janayī /
children.translated_text: 'The very one from whom he heard the conduct of awakening — toward that very one he generates enmity;

children.text: (Vaidya 178)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 178)

children.text: śrutvā ca budhaṃ skhalitamekapadaṃ tasyaiva bhāṣati avarṇaśatān // SRS_29.43 //
children.translated_text: and having heard one stumbled word from a wise one, he speaks a hundred calumnies about that very one! // SRS_29.43 //

children.text: tadimāṃ kumāra mama śrutva giraṃ mā tehi saṃstavu karohi tadā /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, O Prince, having heard my words, do not associate with them at that time;

children.text: supināntare 'pi aviśvasta siyā yadi icchase spṛśitu bodhicarīm // SRS_29.44 //
children.translated_text: even in a dream, do not trust [them] — if you wish to touch the conduct of awakening! // SRS_29.44 //

children.text: dhūtavṛtta saṃlikhita naikaguṇān parikīrtayantu bahukalpaśatān /
children.translated_text: 'They will proclaim for hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> many qualities of those who practice ascetic practices, though only nominally;

children.text: bhaṇatī guṇānna ca guṇeṣu sthito na sa budhyate paramabodhigirām // SRS_29.45 //
children.translated_text: they speak of virtues but are not established in virtues — they do not awaken to the supreme word of awakening! // SRS_29.45 //

children.text: bhavathā sadāpi akhilā madhurā sada śuddhaśīla suprasannamanāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Be always kind and sweet; always of pure conduct and serene mind;

children.text: pariśuddhaśīla bhavathā satataṃ nacireṇa lapsyatha samādhivaram // SRS_29.46 //
children.translated_text: be of purified conduct constantly — before long you shall obtain this supreme <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_29.46 //

children.text: na karotha māna na janetha khilaṃ pariśuddhamānasa sadā bhavathā /
children.translated_text: 'Do not make pride; do not generate rigidity; always be of purified mind;

children.text: mada māna mrakṣa vijahitva tataḥ pratilapsyathā imu samādhivaram // SRS_29.47 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned intoxication, pride, and hypocrisy — you shall obtain this supreme <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_29.47 //

children.text: guṇato anusmari jinaṃ satataṃ varakāñcanacchaviprabhāsakaram /
children.translated_text: 'Remember the <s>Jina</s> constantly by his virtues — the one who produces the radiance of excellent golden complexion;

children.text: gaganaṃ ca rātriya nakṣatrasphuṭaṃ tatha kāyu lakṣaṇasphuṭo munino // SRS_29.48 //
children.translated_text: and as the sky at night is bright with stars, so the body of the Sage is bright with the [thirty-two] marks! // SRS_29.48 //

children.text: dhvajacchatravitānapatākavarāṃ cūrṇānulepanaṃ gṛhītva bahūn /
children.translated_text: 'Taking many banners, parasols, canopies, pennants, powders, and unguents,

children.text: pūjāṃ karotha sugatasya sadā nacireṇa lapsyatha samādhivaram // SRS_29.49 //
children.translated_text: always perform worship of the <s>Sugata</s> — before long you shall obtain this supreme <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_29.49 //

children.text: vara gandhamālyakusumā rucirāṃ vāditra tūrya pragṛhīta bahu /
children.translated_text: 'Taking many excellent, fragrant garlands, lovely flowers, musical instruments, and other offerings,

children.text: (Vaidya 179)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 179)

children.text: jinastūpi pūja prakarotha sadā nacireṇa lapsyatha samādhivaram // SRS_29.50 //
children.translated_text: always perform worship at the <s>Jina</s>'s <s>stūpa</s> — before long you shall obtain this supreme <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_29.50 //

children.text: paṇavaiḥ sughoṣakamṛdaṅgaśataiḥ paṭahairvipañcivaraveṇuravaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'With <s>paṇavas</s>, sweet-sounding <s>mṛdaṅga</s> drums by the hundreds, with kettledrums, <s>vipañcī</s> (lutes), and the sounds of excellent flutes,

children.text: madhurasvarairviṃvidhavādyagaṇaiḥ pūjetha nāyaku prasannamanāḥ // SRS_29.51 //
children.translated_text: with sweet-voiced, various musical ensembles — worship the Leader with a serene mind! // SRS_29.51 //

children.text: kāretha buddhapratimāṃ rucirāṃ ratanāmayīṃ suparikarmakṛtām /
children.translated_text: 'Have a beautiful image of the <s>Buddha</s> made — made of jewels, well-crafted,

children.text: prāsādikāṃ paramasudarśanīyāṃ nacireṇa lapsyatha samādhivaram // SRS_29.52 //
children.translated_text: gracious, supremely beautiful to behold — before long you shall obtain this supreme <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_29.52 //

children.text: vanaṣaṇḍa sevatha vivikta sadā vijahitva grāmanagareṣu ratim /
children.translated_text: 'Always resort to secluded forest groves; having abandoned delight in villages and cities,

children.text: advitīya khaṅgasama bhotha sadā nacireṇa lapsyatha samādhivaram // SRS_29.53 //
children.translated_text: always be solitary like a rhinoceros — before long you shall obtain this supreme <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_29.53 //

children.text: ahu dharmasvāmi mama yūyu sutā anuśikṣathā mama samādhicarim /
children.translated_text: 'I am the Lord of <s>Dharma</s>; you are my sons — train in my <s>samādhi</s>-practice!

children.text: ahu so abhūṣi diśatā suviśruto dṛḍhadattu nāma manujādhipatiḥ // SRS_29.54 //
children.translated_text: I was that renowned one in those directions — King <s>Dṛḍhadatta</s>, lord of men! // SRS_29.54 //

children.text: maya buddha pūjita ananta pure maya śīlu rakṣitu viśuddhamanāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I worshipped <s>Buddhas</s> immeasurably in the past; I guarded moral conduct with a purified mind;

children.text: maya gauravaṃ daśabaleṣu kṛtaṃ imu śāntameṣata samādhivaram // SRS_29.55 //
children.translated_text: I showed reverence to the <s>Daśabalas</s> — [thus] I sought this peaceful, supreme <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_29.55 //

children.text: maya putra dāra parityakta pure śirahastapādanayanāgravarāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I abandoned sons and wife in the past, and excellent heads, hands, feet, and eyes —

children.text: na ca līnacittata kadāci kṛtā imu śāntameṣata samādhivaram // SRS_29.56 //
children.translated_text: yet my mind never became discouraged — [thus] I sought this peaceful, supreme <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_29.56 //

children.text: (Vaidya 180)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 180)

children.text: dhanadhānya dāsa bahudāsiśatā ratanā prabhūta parityakta mayā /
children.translated_text: 'Wealth, grain, male servants, and hundreds of female servants, abundant jewels — all were given up by me;

children.text: saṃtarpitā pi bahuyācanakā imu śāntameṣata samādhivaram // SRS_29.57 //
children.translated_text: many petitioners too were satisfied — [thus] I sought this peaceful, supreme <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_29.57 //

children.text: maya mukti sphāṭika suvarṇa bahu vaidūrya śaṅkha śila tyakta pure /
children.translated_text: 'I gave up much crystal, gold, <s>vaidūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), conch-shells, and stones in the past;

children.text: maṇi śuddharūpiya pravāla ghanā imu śāntameṣata samādhivaram // SRS_29.58 //
children.translated_text: gems, pure silver, and solid coral — [thus] I sought this peaceful, supreme <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_29.58 //

children.text: maya tyakta ābharaṇa nānavidhā varamuktahāra tatha sīhanukāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I gave up various ornaments, excellent pearl necklaces, and lion-shaped [ornaments];

children.text: ratanāna jālika viśiṣṭa pṛthu imu śāntameṣata samādhivaram // SRS_29.59 //
children.translated_text: many distinguished jeweled nets — [thus] I sought this peaceful, supreme <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_29.59 //

children.text: maya vastrakoṭya paramā sukhumāḥ pariśuddha kāśikadukūlavarāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I gave up supreme, fine garments by the <s>koṭī</s>, pure <s>Kāśika</s> silks, excellent;

children.text: bahuhemacitra parityakta pare imu śāntameṣata samādhivaram // SRS_29.60 //
children.translated_text: many gold-embroidered [robes] given to others — [thus] I sought this peaceful, supreme <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_29.60 //

children.text: maya hasti aśva ratha nānavidhāḥ parityakta svapriyasuto mahilāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I gave up elephants, horses, and various chariots, [even] my beloved sons and wives;

children.text: na ca daurmanasyata kadāci kṛtā imu śāntameṣata samādhivaram // SRS_29.61 //
children.translated_text: yet my mind never became dejected — [thus] I sought this peaceful, supreme <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_29.61 //

children.text: maya dṛṣṭva pūrvi sudaridra narāḥ paryeṣṭiduḥkhita ca kṛcchragatāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having seen in the past the greatly poor, those suffering in their search and fallen into hardship,

children.text: maya te dhanena adaridra kṛtāḥ imu śāntameṣata samādhivaram // SRS_29.62 //
children.translated_text: I made them free from poverty with wealth — [thus] I sought this peaceful, supreme <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_29.62 //

children.text: hastī rathāśvarathakā nayutāḥ pracchannaratanamaṇijālacitāḥ /
children.translated_text: "<s>Nayutas</s> of elephants, horse-chariots, covered with nets of jewels and gems,

children.text: dattā mayā yācanakāna purā imu śāntameṣata samādhivaram // SRS_29.63 //
children.translated_text: were given by me formerly to supplicants — [all to] seek this peaceful, supreme <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.63 //

children.text: udyāna koṭinayutā bahavaḥ samalaṃkaritva maya datta purā /
children.translated_text: "Many <s>koṭi-nayutas</s> of gardens, having adorned them, I gave formerly;

children.text: (Vaidya 181)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 181)

children.text: harṣetva mānasu janitva kṛpāṃ imu śāntameṣata samādhivaram // SRS_29.64 //
children.translated_text: gladden your minds, having generated compassion — seek this peaceful, supreme <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_29.64 //

children.text: grāmātha rāṣṭranagarā nigamāḥ samalaṃkaritva maya datta purā /
children.translated_text: "Villages, kingdoms, cities, and towns — having adorned them, I gave formerly;

children.text: datvā ca prītimanubhomi sadā imu śāntameṣata samādhivaram // SRS_29.65 //
children.translated_text: and having given, I always experience joy — [all to] seek this peaceful, supreme <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.65 //

children.text: ratanāna rāśaya sumerusamāstatha cīvarābharaṇakāśca bahu /
children.translated_text: "Heaps of jewels equal to <s>Sumeru</s>, and also many robes and ornaments —

children.text: ye datta pūrvi maya yācanake imu śāntameṣata samādhivaram // SRS_29.66 //
children.translated_text: those were given by me formerly to supplicants — [all to] seek this peaceful, supreme <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.66 //

children.text: sudaridra sattva kṛta āḍhya mayā parikṛcchraprāpta paritrāta bahu /
children.translated_text: "I made the very poor wealthy; I rescued many who had reached dire straits;

children.text: bahuduḥkhapadruta sukhī mi kṛtā imu śāntameṣata samādhivaram // SRS_29.67 //
children.translated_text: many afflicted by great suffering I made happy — [all to] seek this peaceful, supreme <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.67 //

children.text: yada āsi īścaru mahīya ahaṃ dukhitāṃ ca paśyami bahuṃ janatām /
children.translated_text: "When I was lord of the earth and saw the great multitude of suffering people,

children.text: utsṛṣṭa teṣu maya rājyamabhūt kṛpa saṃjanetva sukhito ca yathā // SRS_29.68 //
children.translated_text: I relinquished my kingdom to them, having generated compassion — so that they might be happy. // SRS_29.68 //

children.text: ye me kumāra kṛta āścariyā kṛta duṣkarāṇi bahu kalpaśatā /
children.translated_text: "The wonders I performed, O prince, the difficult deeds done through hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> —

children.text: na ca te maya kṣapaṇa śakya siyā kalpāna koṭinayutā bhaṇataḥ // SRS_29.69 //
children.translated_text: those could not be exhausted by me even speaking for <s>koṭi-nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>. // SRS_29.69 //

body.text: unmattacittabhūmi gacchi narā | aśraddadhanta sugatasya carim /

children.text: kṛta ye mi duṣkara tadāścariyā imu śāntameṣata samādhivaram // SRS_29.70 //
children.translated_text: the difficult deeds I did are indeed wondrous — [all to] seek this peaceful, supreme <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.70 //

body.translated_text: "Men of deranged minds would go to the extreme, not believing in the <s>Sugata</s>'s career;

children.text: ārocayāmi ca kumāra idaṃ śraddadhanta me avitathaṃ vacanam /
children.translated_text: "And I declare this to you, O prince — have faith in my truthful word;

children.text: na hi vāca bhāṣati mṛṣāṃ sugataḥ sada satyavādi jinu kāruṇikaḥ // SRS_29.71 //
children.translated_text: for the <s>Sugata</s> never speaks a false word — the <s>Jina</s> is always truthful, compassionate. // SRS_29.71 //

children.text: (Vaidya 182)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 182)

children.text: anye ime 'pi ca prakāra bahū caratā śodhita ya kalpaśatāḥ /
children.translated_text: "And these are other practices of many kinds, purified through hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> of conduct:

children.text: kathamahaṃ labhitvimu samādhivaraṃ moceya sattvaniyutāṃ dukhitām // SRS_29.72 //
children.translated_text: 'How may I, having obtained this supreme <s>samādhi</s>, liberate <s>nayutas</s> of suffering beings!' // SRS_29.72 //

children.text: yasmin kṣaṇe ayu samādhi mayā pratilabdha bhūta mahājñānapathaḥ /
children.translated_text: "The moment I obtained this <s>samādhi</s>, the true path of great knowledge,

children.text: so 'haṃ labhitvimu samādhivaraṃ paśyāmi buddhanayutān subahūn // SRS_29.73 //
children.translated_text: having obtained this supreme <s>samādhi</s>, I see very many <s>nayutas</s> of Buddhas. // SRS_29.73 //

children.text: ṛddhī ananta pratilabdha mayā sa vikurvamāṇu vraji kṣetraśatān /
children.translated_text: "I obtained infinite <s>ṛddhi</s>; transforming myself, I traveled to hundreds of fields;

children.text: gatvā ca pṛcchi ahu kāruṇikān praśnāna koṭiniyutāna bahum // SRS_29.74 //
children.translated_text: having gone, I asked those Compassionate Ones many <s>koṭi-nayutas</s> of questions. // SRS_29.74 //

children.text: yaścaiva bhāṣi mama te sugatā praśnāna koṭiniyutāna tadā /
children.translated_text: "And whatever those <s>Sugatas</s> spoke to me — <s>koṭi-nayutas</s> of questions at that time —

children.text: gṛhṇitva sarvamahu dhārayamī na ca bhraśyate ekapadaṃ pi mamā // SRS_29.75 //
children.translated_text: grasping it all, I retain it; not even a single word is lost to me. // SRS_29.75 //

children.text: taṃ co śruṇitva ahu bhūtanayaṃ praśnāna koṭinayutāna bahum /
children.translated_text: "And having heard that true method — many <s>koṭi-nayutas</s> of questions —

children.text: deśitva taṃ viraja śāntapadaṃ sthāpemi sattva bahu jñānapathe // SRS_29.76 //
children.translated_text: having taught that dustless, peaceful state, I establish many beings on the path of knowledge. // SRS_29.76 //

children.text: asmin samādhiya sthihitva mayā śikṣitva bhūtanaya kalpaśatān /
children.translated_text: "Established in this <s>samādhi</s>, having trained in the true method for hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: bahusattvakoṭinayutāni purā ye sthāpitā viraji mārgavare // SRS_29.77 //
children.translated_text: many <s>koṭi-nayutas</s> of beings were formerly established by me on the dustless, supreme path. // SRS_29.77 //

children.text: yehī na dṛṣṭa purimā sugatā bhāṣantakā imu nayaṃ virajam /
children.translated_text: "Those who have not seen former <s>Sugatas</s> speaking this dustless method —

children.text: tehī na śakyamiha śraddadhituṃ paramārthaśūnyata samādhivaram // SRS_29.78 //
children.translated_text: they cannot have faith in this supreme <s>samādhi</s> of ultimate emptiness. // SRS_29.78 //

children.text: ye śrāddha paṇḍita vidhijña narā gambhīrabhūtanayalabdhanayāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Those who are faithful, wise, knowledgeable of method, who have attained the profound true method —

children.text: (Vaidya 183)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 183)

children.text: te nā trasanti na ca saṃtrasiṣū śrutvā ca bhonti sada āttamanāḥ // SRS_29.79 //
children.translated_text: they are not frightened, nor will they be terrified; having heard it, they are always delighted. // SRS_29.79 //

children.text: te te dharenti varabodhi samā te te hi putra anujāta mamā /
children.translated_text: "They retain the supreme, equal awakening; they are indeed my true-born sons;

children.text: te te hyudumbarakusumasamāsteṣārtha haṃ caritu kalpaśatān // SRS_29.80 //
children.translated_text: they are like <s>udumbara</s> flowers — for their sake I have practiced for hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>. // SRS_29.80 //

children.text: na pi tasya asti vinipātabhayaṃ aṣṭākṣaṇā vigata tasya sadā /
children.translated_text: "There is no fear of a lower realm for him; the eight inopportune states are always gone for him;

children.text: drakṣyanti buddhanayutān subahūn imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.81 //
children.translated_text: he will see very many <s>nayutas</s> of Buddhas — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.81 //

children.text: yatha maitrako jinu anantayaśāḥ sattvāna bheṣyi bahu arthakaraḥ /
children.translated_text: "Just as <s>Maitreya</s>, the <s>Jina</s> of infinite fame, will be of great benefit to beings —

children.text: tatha vyākaromyahamanantamatiṃ hastasmi yasya susamādhivaram // SRS_29.82 //
children.translated_text: so do I predict infinite wisdom for one in whose hand is the supreme <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.82 //

children.text: smṛtimān sa bhoti matimān jñānodgataḥ śrutidharo bhavati /
children.translated_text: "He becomes mindful, intelligent, of arisen knowledge, a retainer of what he has heard;

children.text: pratibhānu tasya bhavati vipulaṃ imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.83 //
children.translated_text: his eloquence becomes vast — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.83 //

children.text: devānāṃ ca sa bhavati pūjaniyo marutāṃ ca sada namasyanīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: "He becomes worthy of worship by gods, and always worthy of homage by the wind-gods (<s>Maruts</s>);

children.text: abhirakṣitaḥ satata devagaṇaiḥ imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayati // SRS_29.84 //
children.translated_text: constantly protected by hosts of deities — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.84 //

children.text: na ca so 'gnimadhye mriyate na jale na ca tasya śastra kramate na viṣam /
children.translated_text: "He does not die in the midst of fire or water; weapons do not prevail over him, nor poison;

children.text: na ca vairiṇāṃ gamaniyo bhavatī imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.85 //
children.translated_text: he becomes inaccessible to enemies — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.85 //

children.text: vanakandare vasatu tasya sadā marutā karonti vara pāricarim /
children.translated_text: "When he dwells always in forest caves, the wind-gods perform excellent service for him;

children.text: upasthāyakāśca bahu yakṣaśatā imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.86 //
children.translated_text: many hundreds of <s>yakṣas</s> attend him — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.86 //

children.text: (Vaidya 184)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 184)

children.text: jñānena sāgarasamo bhavatī na sajjate guṇa bhaṇantu muneḥ /
children.translated_text: "He becomes ocean-like in knowledge; the qualities of the Sage are declared without clinging;

children.text: bhūtāṃśca buddhaguṇa kīrtayate imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.87 //
children.translated_text: he proclaims the true <s>Buddha</s>-qualities — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.87 //

children.text: nānto na cāsya paryantu śrute na pramāṇu labhyati yathā gagane /
children.translated_text: "There is no end or limit to his learning; no measure of it is found, as with space;

children.text: jñānolkadhāri timiraṃ harati imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.88 //
children.translated_text: bearing the torch of knowledge, he dispels darkness — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.88 //

children.text: snigdhaṃ suyukta sada muñca girāṃ parṣatsu bhāṣati supremaṇiyām /
children.translated_text: "He always utters affectionate, well-measured speech; in assemblies he speaks most lovingly;

children.text: siṃho yathā sa vinadaṃ bhaṇatī imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.89 //
children.translated_text: like a lion, he roars as he speaks — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.89 //

children.text: vaidyo bhiṣaku samu so bhavatī gati lenu trāṇa śaraṇaṃ bahūnām /
children.translated_text: "He becomes like a physician and healer — a refuge, shelter, and protector for many;

children.text: ālokabhūtu jagi so bhavati imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.90 //
children.translated_text: he becomes a light to the world — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.90 //

children.text: na ca tasya maithuni mano ramate śamathe rataḥ spṛśati dhyānasukham /
children.translated_text: "His mind does not delight in sexual intercourse; delighting in calm, he touches the bliss of <s>dhyāna</s>;

children.text: śāntāṃ sa bhāṣati praśānta giram imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.91 //
children.translated_text: he speaks peaceful, tranquil speech — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.91 //

children.text: na ca tasya mānasu nimittarataṃ sarve vibhāvita nimitta pṛthu /
children.translated_text: "His mind does not delight in signs; he has discerned all the various signs;

children.text: satataṃ samāhitu vidū bhavatī imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.92 //
children.translated_text: always concentrated, a wise one — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.92 //

children.text: cakṣuśca so labhati aprākṛtakaṃ yeno sa paśyati anantajinān /
children.translated_text: "He obtains an extraordinary eye, by which he sees infinite <s>Jinas</s>;

children.text: so 'nantacakṣurbhavati vṛṣabho imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.93 //
children.translated_text: that bull becomes one of infinite vision — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.93 //

children.text: krauñcasvaro madhurayuktagiro kalaviṅkadundubhisvaro bhavatī /
children.translated_text: "His voice is like a <s>krauñca</s> crane, sweetly modulated, like a <s>kalaviṅka</s> bird, like a drum;

children.text: saṃgītiyuktasvaru mañjugiro imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.94 //
children.translated_text: his voice is harmonious and melodious, his speech pleasant — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.94 //

children.text: (Vaidya 185)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 185)

children.text: meghābhigarjitasvaro bhavatī haṃsasvaro ravati mañjugiraḥ /
children.translated_text: "His voice becomes like a thundercloud; like a swan he resounds with pleasant speech;

children.text: pañcasvarāṅgaśatayuktasvaro imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.95 //
children.translated_text: his voice is endowed with hundreds of the five vocal qualities — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.95 //

children.text: bahukalpakoṭinayutā vividhā madhurasvarāṅgasuprayuktasvarāḥ /
children.translated_text: "For many <s>koṭi-nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, with diverse sweet voices well-modulated —

children.text: acintiyā sa gira niścaratī imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.96 //
children.translated_text: inconceivable speech issues from him — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.96 //

children.text: na ca bhojane bhavati gṛdhnumanā na pātracīvararato bhavatī /
children.translated_text: "His mind has no greed for food; he does not delight in bowl and robe;

children.text: alpecchu saṃtuṣṭa susaṃlikhito imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.97 //
children.translated_text: of few desires, content, well-disciplined — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.97 //

children.text: na ca ātma utkarṣaku so bhavatī na parasya bhāṣati avarṇu kvacit /
children.translated_text: "He does not exalt himself; he never speaks ill of another;

children.text: dhyāne rataḥ sukhumacittu sadā imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.98 //
children.translated_text: delighting in <s>dhyāna</s>, of subtle mind always — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.98 //

children.text: ātmānuprekṣī satataṃ bhavatī na parasya skhalitemeṣati ca /
children.translated_text: "He always examines himself; he does not seek out another's stumbling;

children.text: aviruddhu sarvi jagi so bhavatī imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.99 //
children.translated_text: he is in harmony with all in the world — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.99 //

children.text: akiliṣṭacittu pariśuddhacarī aśaṭho avañcaku sadā bhavatī /
children.translated_text: "Of undefiled mind, of purified conduct, without deceit or guile always;

children.text: sadamārdavaḥ sada vimokṣarato imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.100 //
children.translated_text: always gentle, always delighting in liberation — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.100 //

children.text: tyāgādhimukta satataṃ bhavatī mātsaryacittu na ca tasya ratam /
children.translated_text: "He is always devoted to renunciation; the thought of avarice has no hold on him;

children.text: śīlenupetu satataṃ bhavatī imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.101 //
children.translated_text: he is always endowed with morality — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.101 //

children.text: abhirūpa darśaniyu premaṇiyo varakāñcanacchavi prabhāsakaraḥ /
children.translated_text: "Handsome, pleasing to behold, inspiring love, with the complexion of excellent gold, radiating splendor —

children.text: (Vaidya 186)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 186)

children.text: dvātriṃśallakṣaṇadharo bhavatī imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.102 //
children.translated_text: he becomes a bearer of the thirty-two marks — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.102 //

children.text: prāsādikaśca sada so bhavatī abhilakṣito bahujanasya priyo /
children.translated_text: "He is always gracious, distinguished, dear to many people;

children.text: prekṣanta tṛpti na labhanti narā imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.103 //
children.translated_text: those who behold him find no satiety — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.103 //

children.text: devāsya nāga tatha yakṣagaṇāstuṣṭā udagrāḥ sada āttamanāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Gods, <s>nāgas</s>, and <s>yakṣa</s>-hosts — pleased, elated, and delighted —

children.text: bhāṣanti varṇa praviśitva kulānimu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.104 //
children.translated_text: speak his praise, entering [his] families — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.104 //

body.text:
brahmā ca śakra vaśavarti vahu upasthānu tasya prakaronti sadā /
na ca tasya unnata mano bhavatī | imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.105 //
body.translated_text: "<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, and many <s>Vaśavartins</s> always serve him; yet his mind does not become proud — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.105 //

children.text: na ca tasya durgatibhayaṃ bhavatī na pi cākṣaṇā na vinipātabhayam /
children.translated_text: "There is no fear of evil destinies for him, nor of inopportune states, nor fear of lower realms;

children.text: parimuktu sarvavinipātabhayādimu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.106 //
children.translated_text: released from all fear of lower rebirths — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.106 //

children.text: na ca tasya kāṅkṣa vimatirbhavatī vara buddhadharma śruṇiyā nipuṇān /
children.translated_text: "There is no doubt or uncertainty in him when hearing subtle, excellent <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>;

children.text: gambhīrajñānānugato bhavatī imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.107 //
children.translated_text: he becomes one who has entered profound knowledge — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.107 //

children.text: yaṃ yaṃ pi dharmaṃ śruṇatī sukhumaṃ sarvatra bhoti vaśi pāragataḥ /
children.translated_text: "Whatever subtle <s>dharma</s> he hears, he becomes a master everywhere, having gone beyond;

children.text: balavantu hetunipuṇo bhavatī imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.108 //
children.translated_text: he becomes powerful, skilled in causes — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.108 //

children.text: evaṃ prabhāṣita jinena girā ahu tena bhomi paricīrṇa sadā /
children.translated_text: "Thus proclaimed by the <s>Jina</s>'s voice: 'I have always been served by him' —

children.text: labhate ca dhāraṇi viśiṣṭa varāmimu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.109 //
children.translated_text: and he obtains distinguished, supreme <s>dhāraṇī</s> — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.109 //

children.text: kālakriyāṃ ca sa karoti yadā amitābhu tasya purataḥ sthihatī /
children.translated_text: "And when he dies, <s>Amitābha</s> stands before him,

children.text: (Vaidya 187)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 187)

children.text: bhikṣugaṇena saha kāruṇiko imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.110 //
children.translated_text: together with the assembly of monks, the Compassionate One — for the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.110 //

children.text: lābhī ca dhāraṇiya so bhavatī dharmanidhāna vaśipāragataḥ /
children.translated_text: "He becomes a possessor of <s>dhāraṇī</s>, a master of the <s>Dharma</s>-treasury, having gone beyond to mastery;

children.text: pratibhānavānanācchedyagiro ya imaṃ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.111 //
children.translated_text: possessing eloquence, of unbreakable speech — one who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.111 //

children.text: yenaiva so vrajati dharmadharo ālokabhūta bhavatī jagataḥ /
children.translated_text: "Wherever that <s>Dharma</s>-bearer goes, he becomes a light to the world;

children.text: sipraśāntacara suviśuddhamanā imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.112 //
children.translated_text: of very peaceful conduct, of perfectly purified mind — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.112 //

children.text: vara dharmakośa vividhaṃ nipuṇaṃ so dharmakāya vaśi pāragataḥ /
children.translated_text: "The excellent, varied, subtle treasury of <s>Dharma</s> — he is a master of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, having gone beyond to mastery;

children.text: so saṃśayaṃ chinatti sarvajage imu yaḥ samādhi naru dhārayatī // SRS_29.113 //
children.translated_text: he cuts the doubts of all in the world — the person who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_29.113 //

children.text: sarve 'pi sattva siya kāruṇikā bhagavān bhavāntakaraṇe sugataḥ /
children.translated_text: "Even if all beings were compassionate like the Blessed <s>Sugata</s> who puts an end to existence,

children.text: tān satkareyyā bahu kalpaśatān yatha gaṅgavāluka tathottari vā // SRS_29.114 //
children.translated_text: and one were to honor them for many hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> — as many as the sands of the Ganges, or more — // SRS_29.114 //

children.text: yaścaiva paści kṣayakāli imaṃ śrutvā samādhimiha kaści naraḥ /
children.translated_text: "yet whoever in the final age of decline, having heard this <s>samādhi</s>,

children.text: anumodamīti bhaṇataikagiraṃ kala puṇyaskandha na sa pūrva bhavet // SRS_29.115 //
children.translated_text: says even a single word 'I rejoice!' — his heap of merit would be even greater than the former. // SRS_29.115 //

children.text: yasyo kumāra iya śāntagatī paramārthaśūnyata samādhivaro /
children.translated_text: "O prince, for him in whom this peaceful path — the supreme <s>samādhi</s> of ultimate emptiness —

children.text: prāvartu bhoti tatha pustagataḥ so dharmabhāṇaku sthitaḥ sumatiḥ // SRS_29.116 //
children.translated_text: circulates, even in written book form — that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher, wise, is established. // SRS_29.116 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje tejaguṇarājaparivarto nāmonatriṃśatitamaḥ || 29 ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-ninth chapter in the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, called the <s>Tejaguṇarājaparivarta</s> (Chapter on King <s>Tejaguṇa</s>). || 29 ||

body.text:
(Vaidya 188)
30 Anuśaṃsāparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 188) Chapter 30: <s>Anuśaṃsāparivarta</s> (Chapter on Benefits). |

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān punareva candraprabhaṃ kumārabhūtamāmantrayate sma - tasmāttarhi kumāra ya ākāṅkṣed bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ - kimityahaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ rutamadhigaccheyamindriyāṇāṃ ca parāparajñatāṃ vijñāya dharmaṃ deśayeyamiti,tena kumāra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena ayaṃ sarvadharmasvabhāvasamatāvipañcitaḥ samādhiḥ śrotavya udgrahītavyaḥ paryavāptavyo dhārayitavyo vācayitavyaḥ araṇābhāvanayā bhāvayitavyo bahulīkartavyaḥ parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayitavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One again addressed the prince <s>Candraprabha</s>: 'Therefore, prince, if a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> should wish: "How may I comprehend the voices of all beings and, having known the superiority and inferiority of their faculties, teach the <s>Dharma</s>?" — then, prince, that <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> should hear, grasp, master, retain, recite, cultivate through meditation on non-contention, practice extensively, and illuminate in detail to others this <s>samādhi</s> that elaborates the equality of the own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: aparimita atīta nāyakāstena dṛṣṭāḥ puratu katha prayuktā pṛcchitā lokanāthāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Immeasurable Leaders of the past were seen by him; before them he was engaged in questioning, having questioned those Lords of the World;

children.text: pravara kuśalamūle tiṣṭhato bodhisattvo imu virajasamādhiṃ dhārayan mokṣakāmaḥ // SRS_30.1 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Bodhisattva</s> standing in the foremost roots of merit, upholding this dustless <s>samādhi</s>, desiring liberation.' // SRS_30.1 //

children.text: labhati sukha praṇītaṃ divyamānuṣyakaṃ co
children.translated_text: 'He obtains happiness — excellent, divine and human;

children.text: labhati paramapūjāṃ divyamānuṣyakāṃ so /
children.translated_text: he obtains supreme worship — divine and human;

children.text: labhati sukha praṇītaṃ dhyānasaukhyāryasaukhyam
children.translated_text: he obtains excellent happiness — the bliss of <s>dhyāna</s>, noble bliss —

children.text: imu viraja samādhiṃ dhārayan mokṣakāmaḥ // SRS_30.2 //
children.translated_text: upholding this dustless <s>samādhi</s>, desiring liberation.' // SRS_30.2 //

children.text: varṇu śruṇiya udāraṃ harṣu tasyo na bhoti
children.translated_text: 'Hearing lofty praise, no elation arises in him;

children.text: na pi ca punaravarṇe maṅkubhāvaṃ nigacchet /
children.translated_text: nor again upon [hearing] blame does he fall into dejection;

children.text: śailopamu akampeyyo aṣṭabhirlokadharmair
children.translated_text: like a mountain, unshakeable by the eight worldly <s>dharmas</s> —

children.text: imu viraja samādhiṃ dhārayan mokṣakāmaḥ // SRS_30.3 //
children.translated_text: upholding this dustless <s>samādhi</s>, desiring liberation.' // SRS_30.3 //

children.text: akhilamadhuravāṇī ślakṣṇavācā suyuktā apagatabhrukuṭiśco pūrvaālāpi bhoti /
children.translated_text: 'Of entirely sweet speech, of smooth and well-ordered words, with furrowed brows gone, he is always the first to speak;

children.text: satatasmitamukhaśco śikṣito nāyakānām imu virajasamādhiṃ dhārayan mokṣakāmaḥ // SRS_30.4 //
children.translated_text: always with a smiling face, trained [in the way] of the Leaders — upholding this dustless <s>samādhi</s>, desiring liberation.' // SRS_30.4 //

children.text: bhavati sa sukhavāsaḥ sūrataḥ snigdhacitto bhavati sada sudānto dāntabhūmisthitaśca /
children.translated_text: 'He becomes one of pleasant dwelling, a hero, of tender mind; always well-tamed, established on the ground of the tamed;

children.text: sumadhura priyavāṇī snigdhasatyābhidhāyī imu virajasamādhiṃ dhārayan bodhikāmaḥ // SRS_30.5 //
children.translated_text: of sweet and pleasing speech, speaking with tender truth — upholding this dustless <s>samādhi</s>, desiring awakening.' // SRS_30.5 //

children.text: na ca sa katha karotī vaigrahīṃ no vivādān apagatakhila doṣā varjitāstena śeṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He never engages in contentious talk, nor disputes; rigidity, faults — all are abandoned by him, and the rest [of defilements];

children.text: (Vaidya 189)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 189)

children.text: pramuditu sada bhotī sūrato mārdavaśca imu viraja samādhiṃ dhārayan bodhikāmaḥ // SRS_30.6 //
children.translated_text: always joyful, a hero, and gentle — upholding this dustless <s>samādhi</s>, desiring awakening.' // SRS_30.6 //

children.text: bhavati ca sada vidvāṃstyāgi nityābhiyuktaḥ sudukhita jana dṛṣṭvā teṣamannaṃ dadāti /
children.translated_text: 'He is always learned, a renouncer, constantly devoted; seeing people in great suffering, he gives them food;

children.text: priyataru parityaktuṃ bhoti nityaṃ sudātā imu virajasamādhiṃ dhārayan bodhikāmaḥ // SRS_30.7 //
children.translated_text: one for whom it is dearer to give away, always a supreme giver — upholding this dustless <s>samādhi</s>, desiring awakening.' // SRS_30.7 //

children.text: devaśatasahasrāṇa spṛhāṃ ye saṃjanentī nāga asura yakṣā nityupasthāyakāsya /
children.translated_text: 'Hundreds of thousands of gods generate longing [for him]; <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s> are his constant attendants;

children.text: vani pavani vasante rakṣa tasyā karontī imu viraja samādhiṃ yo naro dhārayati // SRS_30.8 //
children.translated_text: in forests and winds, while he dwells, they provide protection — for the man who upholds this dustless <s>samādhi</s>.' // SRS_30.8 //

children.text: bhaṇi vacanamasaktaṃ brahmadhoṣasvaro 'sau haṃsaravitaghoṣaḥ kinnarodgītaghoṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He speaks unattached words, with a voice like <s>Brahmā</s>'s, with the melody of a swan, with the song of a <s>Kinnara</s>;

children.text: pañcaśatasvarāṅgo harṣaṇīyasvaraśco bhavati naditaśabdo ghuṣṭaśabdaḥ suśabdaḥ // SRS_30.9 //
children.translated_text: endowed with five hundred vocal qualities, with a delightful voice — his sound resounds, proclaimed, well-sounding.' // SRS_30.9 //

children.text: yāvatatu pṛthu kṣatrāṇa naraḥ kaścideva sūkṣma raja kareyyā śakya te lakṣaṇāya /
children.translated_text: 'If any man could make fine dust-particles of all the vast <s>Kṣatriya</s>-lands, countable by characteristic —

children.text: tatu bahutaru tasyo ye svarā niścarantī imu viraja samādhiṃ yo naro dhārayāti // SRS_30.10 //
children.translated_text: more numerous than that are the vocal qualities that issue from him — the man who upholds this dustless <s>samādhi</s>.' // SRS_30.10 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje 'nuśaṃsāparivarto nāma triṃśatitamaḥ || 30 ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the thirtieth chapter of the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, called the <s>Anuśaṃsā</s> (Benefits) chapter.

body.text:
(Vaidya 190)
31 Sarvadharmasvabhāvanirdeśaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 190) Chapter 31: The <s>Sarvadharmasvabhāvanirdeśa</s> (Teaching on the Own-Nature of All <s>Dharmas</s>).

body.text: tatra bhagavān punarapi candraprabhaṃ kumārabhūtamāmantrayate sma - tasmāttarhi kumāra ya ākāṅkṣed bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ kimityahaṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ svabhāvaṃ kathaṃ jānīyāmiti,tena kumāra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena ayaṃ sarvadharmasvabhāvasamatāvipañcitaḥ samādhiḥ śrotavya udgrahītavyaḥ paryavāptavyo dhārayitavyo vācayitavya uddeṣṭavyaḥ svādhyātavyaḥ araṇābhāvanayā bhāvayitavyo bahulīkartavyaḥ parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayitavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: There the Blessed One again addressed the prince <s>Candraprabha</s>: 'Therefore, prince, if a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> should wish: "How may I know the own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s>?" — then, prince, that <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> should hear, grasp, master, retain, recite, expound, study, cultivate through meditation on non-contention, practice extensively, and illuminate in detail to others this <s>samādhi</s> that elaborates the equality of the own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: tasyo rāgu na jātu kupyate na ca doṣo tasyo moha na jātu kupyate vṛṣabhisya /
children.translated_text: 'Passion never arises in him, nor hatred, nor delusion ever arises in that bull [among men];

children.text: teno sarvi kileśa cchoritānavaśeṣā yo 'sau dharmasvabhāvu jānatī supraśāntam // SRS_31.1 //
children.translated_text: for by him all afflictions have been abandoned without remainder — he who knows the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s>, supremely peaceful.' // SRS_31.1 //

children.text: so 'sau śikṣa na jātu oṣirī sugatānāṃ so 'sau śūru na jātu istriyāṇāṃ vaśameti /
children.translated_text: 'He never abandons the training of the <s>Sugatas</s>; that hero never falls under the power of women;

children.text: so 'sau śāsani prīti vindate sugatānāṃ yo 'sau dharmasvabhāvu jānatī supraśāntam // SRS_31.2 //
children.translated_text: he finds delight in the teaching of the <s>Sugatas</s> — he who knows the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s>, supremely peaceful.' // SRS_31.2 //

children.text: so 'sau jñānavidhijña paṇḍito matimāṃśca so 'sau buddha ananta paśyatī aparyantāṃ /
children.translated_text: 'He is a wise knower of the methods of knowledge, intelligent; he sees <s>Buddhas</s> infinite, boundless;

children.text: so 'sau dhāraṇijñānu jānatī aparyantaṃ yo 'sau dharmasvabhāvu jānatī nayayuktim // SRS_31.3 //
children.translated_text: he knows the knowledge of <s>dhāraṇī</s>, boundless — he who knows the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s>, the method.' // SRS_31.3 //

children.text: so 'sau neha cireṇa bheṣyati dvipadendraḥ so 'sau vaidyu bhiṣaku bheṣyate sukhadātā /
children.translated_text: 'He shall not be long in becoming the supreme among bipeds; he shall become a physician, a healer, a giver of happiness;

children.text: so 'sau uddhari śalya sarvaśo dukhitānāṃ yo 'sau dharmasvabhāvu jānatī supraśāntam // SRS_31.4 //
children.translated_text: he shall extract the darts completely from those in suffering — he who knows the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s>, supremely peaceful.' // SRS_31.4 //

children.text: so 'sau āturu jñātva duḥkhitānimi sattvān so 'sau bherī sadā parāhanī amṛtasya /
children.translated_text: 'Having known these beings to be afflicted and suffering, he always beats the drum of the deathless;

children.text: so 'sau bheṣyati nāyako jino nacireṇa yo 'sau dharmasvabhāvu jānatī supraśāntam // SRS_31.5 //
children.translated_text: he shall become a Leader, a <s>Jina</s>, before long — he who knows the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s>, supremely peaceful.' // SRS_31.5 //

children.text: (Vaidya 191)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 191)

children.text: so 'sau bhaiṣajyanayeṣu kovido varavaidyo ādiṃ jānati sarvavyādhināṃ yatra muktiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He is skilled in the methods of medicine, a supreme physician; he knows the beginning of all diseases, where liberation [lies];

children.text: so 'sau bhūtanayaśikṣito matimanto śikṣitvā bahusattva mocayī pṛthu naṣṭān // SRS_31.6 //
children.translated_text: that intelligent one, trained in the method of truth — having trained, he shall liberate many beings who are widely lost.' // SRS_31.6 //

children.text: so 'sau śūnyanayeṣu kovido matiśūraḥ so 'sau loki asaktu bhuñjati sada piṇḍam /
children.translated_text: 'He is skilled in the methods of emptiness, a hero of intellect; unattached in the world, he always eats alms-food;

children.text: so 'sau bodhivarāya sthāpayi bahusattvān yo 'sau dharmasvabhāvu jānatī supraśāntam // SRS_31.7 //
children.translated_text: he establishes many beings in the supreme awakening — he who knows the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s>, supremely peaceful.' // SRS_31.7 //

children.text: so 'sau kṣāntibalena udgato naracandraḥ so 'sau loṣṭakadaṇḍatāḍito na ca kupyī /
children.translated_text: 'He has risen through the power of patience, that moon among men; struck with clods and sticks, he is never angry;

children.text: so 'sau chidyatu aṅgamaṅgaśo na ca kṣubhye yo 'sau dharmasvabhāvu jānatī supraśāntam // SRS_31.8 //
children.translated_text: even when his limbs are cut piece by piece, he is not agitated — he who knows the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s>, supremely peaceful.' // SRS_31.8 //

children.text: so 'sau kṣāntibale pratiṣṭhito balavanto so 'sau kṣāntiya vastu tādṛśo supraśāntaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He is established in the power of patience, that powerful one; his essence in patience is such — supremely peaceful;

children.text: so 'sau kṣāntibalena manyate matiśūro yo 'sau dharmasvabhāvu jānatī supraśāntam // SRS_31.9 //
