children.translated_text: he is considered a hero of intellect through the power of patience — he who knows the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s>, supremely peaceful.' // SRS_31.9 //

children.text: so 'sau vastu na jātu manyate ahu cchinnā teno sarvi bhavā vibhāvitāḥ sada śūnyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He never considers things as [truly] cut off; by him all existences are illuminated as always empty;

children.text: tasyo saṃjñā prahīṇa sarvaśo nikhileno yo 'sau dharmasvabhāvu jānatī supraśāntam // SRS_31.10 //
children.translated_text: all his perceptions have been abandoned completely without remainder — he who knows the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s>, supremely peaceful.' // SRS_31.10 //

children.text: te te dharmasvabhāvu deśayī supraṇītaṃ te te bodhi spṛśī anuttarāṃ nacireṇa /
children.translated_text: 'Those who teach the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s> supremely excellently — those who touch the unsurpassed awakening before long —

children.text: yeṣāṃ dharmasvabhāvu gocaraḥ sunidhyapto teṣāṃ datta ananta dakṣiṇā aparyantā // SRS_31.11 //
children.translated_text: those whose range is the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s>, well-contemplated — to them is given an infinite, boundless offering.' // SRS_31.11 //

children.text: so 'sau bhāṣati sūtrakoṭiyo aparyantā yatha gaṅganadīya vālikāstatu bhūyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He speaks <s>koṭis</s> of <s>sūtras</s>, boundless — more than the sands of the river Ganges;

children.text: no cāsyu pratibhānu chidyate varṇamāne yo 'sau dharmasvabhāvu jānatī supraśāntam // SRS_31.12 //
children.translated_text: yet his eloquence is not exhausted in proclaiming — he who knows the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s>, supremely peaceful.' // SRS_31.12 //

body.text: so 'sau kalpasahasrakoṭiśo nayutāni jñāneno sada bhoti udgato yatha meruḥ /
body.translated_text: 'For thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> and <s>nayutas</s>, he is always risen through knowledge like <s>Meru</s>;

body.text: (Vaidya 192)

children.text: dharma tasya kṣayo na vidyate bhaṇamāne yo 'sau dharmasvabhāvu jānatī supraśāntam // SRS_31.13 //
children.translated_text: his <s>Dharma</s> is never exhausted in proclaiming — he who knows the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s>, supremely peaceful.' // SRS_31.13 //

body.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 192)

children.text: vistīrṇaṃ vipulaṃ acintiyaṃ pratibhānaṃ bhotī bodhivarāṃ gaveṣataḥ sada tasyo /
children.translated_text: 'Vast, extensive, inconceivable is the eloquence that always belongs to him, seeking the supreme awakening;

children.text: nityaṃ bhāṣati sūtrakoṭiyo aparyantā yo 'sau dharmasvabhāvu jānatī supraśāntam // SRS_31.14 //
children.translated_text: he constantly speaks boundless <s>koṭis</s> of <s>sūtras</s> — he who knows the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s>, supremely peaceful.' // SRS_31.14 //

children.text: yaṃ caite dvipadottamā jinā bhaṇi dharmaṃ sarvaṃ taṃ ca śruṇitva gṛhṇatī paripūrṇam /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever <s>Dharma</s> those <s>Jinas</s>, the supreme among bipeds, have spoken — he hears all of it and grasps it completely;

children.text: no vā ekapade 'pi vidyate vimatisyo yo 'sau sarvi abhāva jānatī imi dharmān // SRS_31.15 //
children.translated_text: nor is there doubt in even a single word — he who knows all these <s>dharmas</s> as non-existent.' // SRS_31.15 //

children.text: so 'sau bhoti viśiṣṭa tyāgavān sada kālaṃ bhotī dānapatiḥ sukhaṃdado dukhitānām /
children.translated_text: 'He is always distinguished in generosity; he becomes a lord of giving, a giver of happiness to the suffering;

children.text: dṛṣṭā duḥkhita sattva tarpayī ratanehī yo 'sau dharmasvabhāvu jānatī sada śūnyam // SRS_31.16 //
children.translated_text: seeing suffering beings, he satisfies them with jewels — he who knows the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s> as always empty.' // SRS_31.16 //

children.text: sau 'sau jambudhvaje bhaviṣyatī sada rājā sattvānāṃ sada saukhya kāhitī aparyantam /
children.translated_text: 'He shall always be a king in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>; he shall always produce boundless happiness for beings;

children.text: maitrāye samupetu prāṇīnāṃ sada kāle yo 'sau dharmasvabhāvu jānatī sada śūnyam // SRS_31.17 //
children.translated_text: endowed with loving-kindness toward beings at all times — he who knows the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s> as always empty.' // SRS_31.17 //

children.text: putrān dhītara dāsadāsiyo tyajya dhīro hastau pāda śirāṃsi sa tyajī tatha rājyam /
children.translated_text: 'Giving up sons, daughters, slaves and servant-girls, that steadfast one gives away his hands, feet, and head, and his kingdom too;

children.text: no cālīyati tasya mānasaṃ vṛṣabhisyo yo 'sau dharmasvabhāvu jānatī sada śūnyam // SRS_31.18 //
children.translated_text: yet the mind of that bull [among men] is never diminished — he who knows the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s> as always empty.' // SRS_31.18 //

children.text: aṅgāṅgaṃ puna tasya chidyatī yadi kāyo no tasya pratihanyate manaḥ supine 'pi /
children.translated_text: 'Even when his limbs are cut piece by piece — even his body — his mind is not repelled, not even in a dream;

children.text: teno pūjita bhonti nāyakā dvipadendrā yo 'sau dharmasvabhāvu jānatī sada śūnyam // SRS_31.19 //
children.translated_text: by him the Leaders, the supreme among bipeds, are worshipped — he who knows the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s> as always empty.' // SRS_31.19 //

children.text: teno pūjita sarvi nāyakā ya atītāstatha pūjita ye anāgatā dvipadendrāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'By him all the Leaders of the past are worshipped; and those of the future, the supreme among bipeds;

children.text: tehī satkṛta sarvi nāyakā sthita ye co yo 'sau dharmasvabhāvu jānatī sada śūnyam // SRS_31.20 //
children.translated_text: by them all established Leaders are honored — he who knows the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s> as always empty.' // SRS_31.20 //

children.text: (Vaidya 193)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 193)

children.text: so 'sau kośa dhareti paṇḍitaḥ sugatānāṃ so 'sau dhāraṇiye pratiṣṭhitaḥ paramāyām /
children.translated_text: 'That wise one holds the treasury of the <s>Sugatas</s>; he is established in the supreme <s>dhāraṇī</s>;

children.text: so 'sau bheṣyati lokanāyako naciareṇa yacchutvā imu sūtraṃ dhārayet kṣayakāle // SRS_31.21 //
children.translated_text: he shall become a Lord of the World before long — whoever, having heard this <s>sūtra</s>, upholds it in the age of decline.' // SRS_31.21 //

children.text: so 'ndho naiva kadāci bheṣyatī vidu jātu no co aṅgavihīnu bheṣyatī bahukalpān /
children.translated_text: 'He shall never become blind, nor ever lacking a limb, that wise one, for many <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: teno akṣaṇa aṣṭa varjitā imi nityaṃ yeno sūtramidaṃ prabhāṣitaṃ apramuṣṭam // SRS_31.22 //
children.translated_text: the eight unfavorable conditions are always avoided by him — by whom this <s>sūtra</s> has been proclaimed without forgetting.' // SRS_31.22 //

children.text: nāsau durgatiṣu gamiṣyati puna jātu nityaṃ lakṣaṇadhāri bheṣyatī abhirūpaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He shall never go to the evil destinies again; always bearing the [supreme] marks, he shall be of beautiful form;

children.text: pacco tasya abhijña bhāvitā imi nityaṃ purataḥ so sugatāna sthāsyatī sada śūraḥ // SRS_31.23 //
children.translated_text: the five superknowledges are always cultivated by him — he shall always stand before the <s>Sugatas</s>, that hero.' // SRS_31.23 //

children.text: bahukān nirmita nirmiṇitvāna ayu jñānī preṣatī bahukṣetrakoṭiṣu vinayārtham /
children.translated_text: 'Having created many emanations, the knowledgeable one sends them to many <s>koṭis</s> of fields for the purpose of discipline;

children.text: yehi dṛṣṭa bhavanti nirmitā bahu buddhāḥ tehī bodhivarāya sthāpitā bahu sattvāḥ // SRS_31.24 //
children.translated_text: those by whom those emanations are seen [as] many <s>Buddhas</s> — by them many beings are established in the supreme awakening.' // SRS_31.24 //

children.text: smṛtimantaḥ gatimantaḥ prajñāvān dhṛtimāṃśca sthāmnā vīryabalena so sadā samupetaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Mindful, intelligent, wise, steadfast, and always endowed with strength, vigor, and power;

children.text: dharmapāramiprāpta bheṣyati mahatejā yaḥ śrutvā imu sūtra dhārayet kṣayakāle // SRS_31.25 //
children.translated_text: he shall become one who has reached the perfection of <s>Dharma</s>, of great splendor — whoever, having heard this <s>sūtra</s>, upholds it in the age of decline.' // SRS_31.25 //

children.text: raśmikoṭisahasra niścarī sada teṣāṃ vyomāḥ sarvi karonti maṇḍalāḥ suriyāṇām /
children.translated_text: 'Thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of rays always issue from them; they make the entire sky into discs like suns;

children.text: yehī bhāvita bhonti śūnyakā imi dharmāste te śūra bhavanti nāyakā nacireṇa // SRS_31.26 //
children.translated_text: those by whom these <s>dharmas</s> [of] emptiness are cultivated — those heroes shall become Leaders before long.' // SRS_31.26 //

children.text: eṣo gocaru śāntu bhāvito maya pūrvaṃ bahukalpāna sahasra koṭiyo niyutāni /
children.translated_text: 'This peaceful range was cultivated by me formerly, for thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: (Vaidya 194)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 194)

children.text: vīryaṃ me na kadāci sahasita iha mārge yadahaṃ dīpaṃkareṇa vyākṛto jinabhūmī // SRS_31.27 //
children.translated_text: my vigor was never relaxed on this path — since I was predicted by <s>Dīpaṃkara</s> for the stage of a <s>Jina</s>.' // SRS_31.27 //

children.text: yūyaṃ pī mama caryā śikṣathā iha sūtre gambhīrā paramārtha deśitā iya netrī /
children.translated_text: 'You too should train in my conduct, in this <s>sūtra</s>; profound, ultimate meaning is taught — this is the guide;

children.text: yatrāmī bahu naṣṭa tīrthikā viparitā kṣiptvā bodhimapāyi bhairave prapatanti // SRS_31.28 //
children.translated_text: where these many lost <s>tīrthikas</s>, confused, having rejected awakening, fall into the fearsome [abyss].' // SRS_31.28 //

children.text: bahukalpāna sahasrakoṭiyo nayutāni veditvā amu tatra vedanā kaṭu tībrāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, having experienced bitter, intense feelings there,

children.text: bahukalpā nayutānamatyayāt punareva hetuḥ so amṛtasya prāptaye bhaviṣyate // SRS_31.29 //
children.translated_text: after the passing of many <s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, even that [experience] becomes a cause for attaining the deathless.' // SRS_31.29 //

children.text: ye te paścimi kāli bhairave sugatasyo rakṣanti imu sūtramīdṛśaṃ praśāntam /
children.translated_text: Those who in the latter terrifying age guard this peaceful <s>sūtra</s> of the <s>Sugata</s>,

children.text: teṣāṃ bodhi varā na durlabhā iya śreṣṭhā te te paścimi kāli vyākṛta dhari dharmān // SRS_31.30 //
children.translated_text: for them the supreme <s>bodhi</s> is not hard to obtain — those excellent ones in the latter age are prophesied as bearers of the <s>dharma</s>. // SRS_31.30 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje sarvadharmasvabhāvanirdeśaparivarto nāmaikatriṃśatitamaḥ || 31 ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the thirty-first chapter in the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, the chapter called "Exposition of the Own-Nature of All Dharmas" (<s>Sarvadharmasvabhāvanirdeśaparivarta</s>).

body.text:
(Vaidya 195)
32 Sūtradhāraṇānuśaṃsāparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 195) Chapter 32: The <s>Sūtradhāraṇānuśaṃsāparivarta</s> (Chapter on the Benefits of Retaining the Sūtra).

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān punareva candraprabhaṃ kumārabhūtamāmantrayate sma - tasmāttarhi kumāra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena mahābhijñāparikarma dhārayitukāmenāyaṃ samādhirdhārayitavyaḥ udgrahītavyaḥ paryavāptavyo dhārayitavyo vācayitavyaḥ pravartayitavyaḥ uddeṣṭavyaḥ svādhyātavyo bhāvayitavyaḥ, parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayitavya | katamacca tat kumāra sarvadharmāṇāmabhijñāparikarma? yaduta sarvadharmāṇāmaparigrahaḥ aparāmarśaḥ śīlaskandhasyāmanyanā samādhiskandhasya apracāraḥ prajñāskandhasya vivekadarśanaṃ vimuktiskandhasya yathābhūtadarśanaṃ vimuktijñānadarśanaskandhasya svabhāvaśūnyatādarśanaṃ sarvadharmāṇām | yayābhijñayā samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvasamādhivikurvitāni vikurvan sarvasattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati | idamucyate kumāra mahābhijñāparikarmeti ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One again addressed Prince <s>Candraprabha</s>: "Therefore, O Prince, a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> wishing to perform the preparation for the great superknowledges (<s>mahābhijñāparikarma</s>) should retain this <s>samādhi</s> — he should grasp it, master it, retain it, recite it, set it in motion, expound it, study it, cultivate it, and fully elucidate it to others in detail. And what, O Prince, is the preparation for the superknowledge of all <s>dharmas</s>? Namely: the non-grasping of all <s>dharmas</s>, non-adherence, the non-conceit regarding the aggregate of moral conduct, the non-proliferation of the aggregate of <s>samādhi</s>, the seeing of seclusion in the aggregate of wisdom, the seeing of things as they truly are in the aggregate of liberation, and the seeing of the emptiness of own-nature in the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation regarding all <s>dharmas</s>. Endowed with this superknowledge, the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s>, performing all the transformations of <s>samādhi</s>, teaches the <s>dharma</s> to all beings. This, O Prince, is called the preparation for the great superknowledge."

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One at that time spoke these verses:

children.text: mahābhijñāparikarma avivādena deśitam /
children.translated_text: "The preparation for the great superknowledge has been taught through non-contention;

children.text: vivāde yastu carati sodgṛhṇan na vimucyate // SRS_32.1 //
children.translated_text: one who engages in contention, grasping at it, is not liberated. // SRS_32.1 //

children.text: abhijñā tasya sā prajñā bauddhaṃ jñānamacintiyam /
children.translated_text: That superknowledge is wisdom — the inconceivable knowledge of the <s>Buddha</s>;

children.text: udgrahe yaḥ sthito bhoti jñānaṃ tasya na vidyate // SRS_32.2 //
children.translated_text: one who remains fixed on grasping has no [true] knowledge. // SRS_32.2 //

children.text: bahavo 'cintiyā dharmā ye śabdena prakāśitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Many inconceivable <s>dharmas</s> have been illuminated through words;

children.text: yastatra niviśecchabde saṃghābhāṣyaṃ na jānati // SRS_32.3 //
children.translated_text: one who clings to words therein does not understand the meaning spoken for the <s>Saṃgha</s>. // SRS_32.3 //

children.text: saṃghābhāṣyamajānānaḥ kiṃ saṃghāya tu bhāṣitam /
children.translated_text: Not understanding what was spoken for the <s>Saṃgha</s> — what has been said for the assembly?

children.text: adharmaṃ bhāṣate dharmaṃ dharmatāyāmaśikṣitaḥ // SRS_32.4 //
children.translated_text: He speaks non-<s>dharma</s> as <s>dharma</s>, untrained in <s>dharmatā</s> (the true nature of things). // SRS_32.4 //

children.text: lokadhātusahasreṣu ye mayā sūtra bhāṣitāḥ /
children.translated_text: In thousands of world-realms, the <s>sūtras</s> spoken by me,

children.text: nānāvyañjana ekārthā na śakyaṃ parikīrtitum // SRS_32.5 //
children.translated_text: with varied expressions but a single meaning — they cannot be fully proclaimed. // SRS_32.5 //

children.text: ekaṃ padārthaṃ cintetvā sarve te bhonti bhāvitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having contemplated a single meaning, all those are cultivated;

children.text: yāvantaḥ sarvabuddhehi bahu dharmāḥ prakāśitāḥ // SRS_32.6 //
children.translated_text: as many as the <s>dharmas</s> illuminated by all the <s>Buddhas</s>. // SRS_32.6 //

children.text: nairātmyaṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ ye narā arthakovidāḥ /
children.translated_text: The selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s> — those who are skilled in this meaning,

children.text: asmin pade tu śikṣitvā buddhadharmā na durlabhāḥ // SRS_32.7 //
children.translated_text: having trained in this point, the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> are not hard to obtain. // SRS_32.7 //

children.text: sarvadharmā buddhadharmā dharmatāyāṃ ya śikṣitāḥ /
children.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s> are <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> for those trained in <s>dharmatā</s>;

children.text: ye dharmatāṃ prajānanti na virodhenti dharmatām // SRS_32.8 //
children.translated_text: those who understand <s>dharmatā</s> do not oppose <s>dharmatā</s>. // SRS_32.8 //

children.text: (Vaidya 196)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 196)

children.text: sarvā vāg buddhavāgeva sarvaśabdo hyavastukaḥ /
children.translated_text: All speech is indeed <s>Buddha</s>-speech; all words are without substance;

children.text: diśo daśa gaveṣitvā buddhavāg naiva labhyate // SRS_32.9 //
children.translated_text: having searched the ten directions, <s>Buddha</s>-speech cannot be found. // SRS_32.9 //

children.text: eṣā vācā buddhavācā gaveṣitvā diśo daśa /
children.translated_text: This speech is <s>Buddha</s>-speech — having searched the ten directions,

children.text: na labhyate 'nuttaraiṣā na labdhā na ca lapsyate // SRS_32.10 //
children.translated_text: it cannot be found; this unsurpassed [speech] has not been obtained and will not be obtained. // SRS_32.10 //

children.text: anuttarā buddhavācā buddhavācā niruttarā /
children.translated_text: Unsurpassed is <s>Buddha</s>-speech, <s>Buddha</s>-speech is without reply;

children.text: aṇurna lapsyate 'treti tenokteyamanuttarā // SRS_32.11 //
children.translated_text: not even an atom can be obtained herein — therefore it is called unsurpassed. // SRS_32.11 //

children.text: aṇu notpadyate dharmo aṇuśabdena deśitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Not even an atom of <s>dharma</s> arises; the atom has been taught through words;

children.text: aṇumātro na co labdho loke śabdena deśitaḥ // SRS_32.12 //
children.translated_text: not even an atom has been obtained — taught in the world through words. // SRS_32.12 //

children.text: alabdhirlabdhadharmāṇāṃ labdhau labdhirna vidyate /
children.translated_text: Non-attainment is the <s>dharma</s> of those who have attained; in attainment, no attainment exists;

children.text: ya evaṃ dharma jānanti budhyante bodhimuttamām // SRS_32.13 //
children.translated_text: those who know <s>dharma</s> thus awaken to the supreme <s>bodhi</s>. // SRS_32.13 //

children.text: te buddhānuttarāṃ bodhiṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartayī /
children.translated_text: They [realize] the unsurpassed <s>bodhi</s> of the <s>Buddhas</s> and turn the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of Dharma);

children.text: dharmacakraṃ pravartitvā buddhadharmān prakāśayī // SRS_32.14 //
children.translated_text: having turned the <s>Dharmacakra</s>, they illuminate the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. // SRS_32.14 //

children.text: bodhisattvāśca budhyante buddhajñānamanuttaram /
children.translated_text: And the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> awaken to the unsurpassed knowledge of the <s>Buddha</s>;

children.text: tena buddhā iti proktā buddhajñānā prabodhanāt // SRS_32.15 //
children.translated_text: therefore they are called <s>Buddhas</s> — from awakening to <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. // SRS_32.15 //

children.text: abhāvo apraṇihitamānimittaṃ ca śūnyatā /
children.translated_text: Non-existence, wishlessness, signlessness, and emptiness —

children.text: ebhirvimokṣadvārehirdvāraṃ buddhaḥ prakāśayī // SRS_32.16 //
children.translated_text: through these doors of liberation, the <s>Buddha</s> has illuminated the door. // SRS_32.16 //

children.text: cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ ca ghrāṇaṃ ca jihvā kāyo manastathā /
children.translated_text: Eye, ear, nose,

children.text: ete śūnyāḥ svabhāvena saṃbuddhaiḥ saṃprakāśitāḥ // SRS_32.17 //
children.translated_text: tongue, body, and mind likewise — these are empty by their own nature, as proclaimed by the fully Awakened Ones. // SRS_32.17 //

children.text: etādṛśānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ svabhāvaṃ yaḥ prajānati /
children.translated_text: One who understands the own-nature of such <s>dharmas</s>,

children.text: nāsau vivādaṃ kurute jñātvā dharmāṇa lakṣaṇam // SRS_32.18 //
children.translated_text: he does not engage in dispute, having known the characteristic of <s>dharmas</s>. // SRS_32.18 //

children.text: eṣa gocaru śūrāṇāṃ bodhisattvāna tāyinām /
children.translated_text: This is the domain of the heroes, the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, the protectors;

children.text: na te kadācit kāṅkṣanti jānante dharmaśūnyatām // SRS_32.19 //
children.translated_text: they never doubt — they know the emptiness of <s>dharmas</s>. // SRS_32.19 //

children.text: dharmasvabhāvaṃ jānāti buddhastenocyate hi saḥ /
children.translated_text: He knows the own-nature of <s>dharma</s> — therefore he is called a <s>Buddha</s>;

children.text: bodhaye vinayī sattvānaprameyānacintiyān // SRS_32.20 //
children.translated_text: for the sake of awakening, he disciplines immeasurable, inconceivable beings. // SRS_32.20 //

children.text: satkṛto buddhaśabdena śīlaśabdena so kṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: He is honored with the word "<s>Buddha</s>," he is made [worthy] with the word "moral conduct";

children.text: śīlaśabdo buddhaśabda ubhau tāvekalakṣaṇau // SRS_32.21 //
children.translated_text: the word "moral conduct" and the word "<s>Buddha</s>" — both have a single characteristic. // SRS_32.21 //

children.text: yāvantaḥ kīrtitāḥ śabdā hīna utkṛṣṭamadhyamāḥ /
children.translated_text: As many words as have been proclaimed — inferior, superior, and middling —

children.text: samāhitaikaśabdena buddhaśabdena deśitāḥ // SRS_32.22 //
children.translated_text: they are all taught as a single concentrated word, the word "<s>Buddha</s>." // SRS_32.22 //

children.text: na buddhadharmā deśasthā na pradeśastha kīrtitāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> do not abide in a region, nor are they proclaimed as located in a place;

children.text: na cotpannā niruddhā va ekatvena pṛthak tathā // SRS_32.23 //
children.translated_text: they are neither arisen nor ceased, neither one nor separate. // SRS_32.23 //

children.text: (Vaidya 197)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 197)

children.text: na te navāḥ purāṇā vā na teṣāmasti manyanā /
children.translated_text: They are neither new nor old, they have no conceit;

children.text: na ca nīlā na pītā va nāvadatā na lohitāḥ // SRS_32.24 //
children.translated_text: they are neither blue nor yellow, neither white nor red. // SRS_32.24 //

children.text: anābhilāpyā agrāhyā evaṃ ghoṣeṇa deśitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Inexpressible and ungraspable — thus they have been taught through sound;

children.text: na ca ghoṣasya sā bhūmiḥ prātihāryaṃ muneridam // SRS_32.25 //
children.translated_text: yet that is not the domain of sound — this is the miracle of the Sage. // SRS_32.25 //

children.text: anāsravā hi te dharmā- nena ucyanti hi /
children.translated_text: For those <s>dharmas</s> are without defilements — therefore they are so called;

children.text: stṛtā aparyāpannā daśadiśe eṣā buddhāna deśanā // SRS_32.26 //
children.translated_text: spread out, unbounded, in the ten directions — this is the teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s>. // SRS_32.26 //

children.text: parinirvṛtasya buddhasya dṛśyate buddhavigrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: Of the <s>Buddha</s> who has entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, the <s>Buddha</s>-form is seen;

children.text: tatsthānaṃ manasīkurvan prātihāryaṃ sa paśyati // SRS_32.27 //
children.translated_text: attending to that place with the mind, one sees the miracle. // SRS_32.27 //

children.text: na cāsau labhyate sattvo nirvṛtiryena sparśitā /
children.translated_text: No being can be found by whom <s>nirvāṇa</s> has been touched;

children.text: evaṃ ca diśito dharmo bahavaḥ sattva mocitāḥ // SRS_32.28 //
children.translated_text: yet the <s>dharma</s> has been taught thus, and many beings have been liberated. // SRS_32.28 //

children.text: yathā candraśca sūryaśca kāṃsapātrīya dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: Just as the moon and sun are seen in a bronze vessel,

children.text: na ca yāti svakaṃ bimbamevaṃ dharmāṇa lakṣaṇam // SRS_32.29 //
children.translated_text: yet their own reflection does not go [into it] — such is the characteristic of <s>dharmas</s>. // SRS_32.29 //

children.text: pratibhāsopamā dharmā yairhi jñātā svabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Dharmas</s> are like reflections — by those who have known them by their own nature,

children.text: naiva te rūpakāyena paśyante buddhavigraham // SRS_32.30 //
children.translated_text: they do not see the <s>Buddha</s>-form through the form-body. // SRS_32.30 //

children.text: avigraho hyayaṃ dharmo vigraho nātra kaścana /
children.translated_text: This <s>dharma</s> is without form (<s>avigraha</s>); there is no form whatsoever herein;

children.text: avigrahaśca yo dharma eṣa buddhasya vigrahaḥ // SRS_32.31 //
children.translated_text: and that <s>dharma</s> which is formless — that is the <s>Buddha</s>'s form. // SRS_32.31 //

children.text: dharmakāyena paśyanti ye te paśyanti nāyakam /
children.translated_text: Those who see through the <s>Dharmakāya</s> — they see the Guide;

children.text: dharmakāyā hi saṃbuddhā etat saṃbuddhadarśanam // SRS_32.32 //
children.translated_text: for the fully Awakened Ones are the <s>Dharmakāya</s> — this is the seeing of the <s>Buddha</s>. // SRS_32.32 //

children.text: pratītya pratinirdiṣṭā aprati pratideśitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Dependently designated, they have been taught as without designation;

children.text: imāṃ gatiṃ vijānīta śrāmaṇyena hi ye 'rthikāḥ // SRS_32.33 //
children.translated_text: know this path, you who are intent on the <s>śramaṇa</s>-life! // SRS_32.33 //

children.text: aprāpti prāpti nirdiṣṭā sattvānāṃ jñātva āśayam /
children.translated_text: Non-attainment has been taught as attainment, knowing the dispositions of beings;

children.text: yo saṃdhābhāṣyottarate na so kena vihanyate // SRS_32.34 //
children.translated_text: one who comprehends the intentional meaning — by what can he be obstructed? // SRS_32.34 //

children.text: yasya bhoti mayā prāptamaprāptaṃ tena cocyate /
children.translated_text: He for whom there is "I have attained" — by that very [thought] it is called unattained;

children.text: yena śrāmaṇyamaprāptaṃ tena śramaṇa ucyate // SRS_32.35 //
children.translated_text: he by whom the <s>śramaṇa</s>-life is unattained — he is called a <s>śramaṇa</s>. // SRS_32.35 //

children.text: kathaṃ gambhīrime dharmā vakṣyante ye na śikṣitāḥ /
children.translated_text: How profound are these <s>dharmas</s>! They cannot be spoken by those who are untrained;

children.text: te ca gambhīranāmena na śakyaṃ parikīrtitum // SRS_32.36 //
children.translated_text: and they cannot be fully proclaimed by the name "profound." // SRS_32.36 //

children.text: avastukāḥ pañca skandhā abhūtvā eta utthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: The five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) are without substance; without having existed, they have arisen;

children.text: nātra utthāpyako hyasti yasya skandhāḥ samutthitāḥ // SRS_32.37 //
children.translated_text: yet no one can be found here who causes the <s>skandhas</s> to arise. // SRS_32.37 //

children.text: yallakṣaṇāḥ pañca skandhāḥ sarvadharmāstallakṣaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever is the characteristic of the five <s>skandhas</s> — that is the characteristic of all <s>dharmas</s>;

children.text: tallakṣaṇāste nirdiṣṭā lakṣaṇaṃ ca na vidyate // SRS_32.38 //
children.translated_text: they have been taught as having that characteristic, yet no characteristic can be found. // SRS_32.38 //

children.text: (Vaidya 198)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 198)

children.text: yathāntarīkṣaṃ gaganamevaṃ dharmāṇa lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Like the sky and space — such is the characteristic of <s>dharmas</s>,

children.text: pūrvāntamaparāntaṃ ca pratyutpannaṃ ca paśyantaḥ // SRS_32.39 //
children.translated_text: seeing the past, the future, and the present. // SRS_32.39 //

children.text: agrāhyaṃ gaganaṃ proktaṃ grāhyamatra na labhyate /
children.translated_text: Space has been called ungraspable; nothing graspable can be found therein;

children.text: eṣa svabhāvo dharmāṇāmagrāhyo gaganopamaḥ // SRS_32.40 //
children.translated_text: this is the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s> — ungraspable, like space. // SRS_32.40 //

children.text: evaṃ ca deśitā dharmā na śrāvako vipaśyati /
children.translated_text: Though <s>dharmas</s> have been taught thus, the <s>Śrāvaka</s> does not see [them clearly];

children.text: yaśco na paśyatī dharmaṃ tasya dharmā acintiyāḥ // SRS_32.41 //
children.translated_text: and for one who does not see the <s>dharma</s>, the <s>dharmas</s> are inconceivable. // SRS_32.41 //

children.text: asvabhāvā ime dharmāḥ svabhāvaiṣāṃ na labhyate /
children.translated_text: These <s>dharmas</s> are without own-nature; their own-nature cannot be found;

children.text: yogināṃ gocaro hyeṣa ye yuktā buddhabodhaye // SRS_32.42 //
children.translated_text: this is the domain of <s>yogīs</s> — those who are devoted to the awakening of the <s>Buddha</s>. // SRS_32.42 //

children.text: ya evaṃ jānāti dharmān sa na dharmeṣu sajjate /
children.translated_text: One who knows <s>dharmas</s> thus does not cling to <s>dharmas</s>;

children.text: asajjamāno dharmeṣu dharmasaṃjñā prabodhayī // SRS_32.43 //
children.translated_text: not clinging to <s>dharmas</s>, he awakens [to] the perception of <s>dharma</s>. // SRS_32.43 //

children.text: vibhāvitāḥ sarvadharmā bodhisattvena tāyinā /
children.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s> have been thoroughly analyzed by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the protector;

children.text: dharmasaṃjñā vibhāvitvā buddhadharmānna manyate // SRS_32.44 //
children.translated_text: having analyzed the perception of <s>dharma</s>, he does not conceive of the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. // SRS_32.44 //

children.text: amanyamānā hi sā koṭī kalpetvā koṭi vyāhṛtā /
children.translated_text: That limit which is free from conceit — having imagined a limit, it was declared;

children.text: ya evaṃ koṭiṃ jānāti kalpakoṭiṃ na manyate // SRS_32.45 //
children.translated_text: one who knows the limit thus does not conceive of a <s>koṭī</s> (limit) of <s>kalpas</s>. // SRS_32.45 //

children.text: purimāṃ koṭi kalpitvā bālaḥ saṃsāri saṃsari /
children.translated_text: Having imagined a prior limit, the fool wanders in <s>saṃsāra</s>;

children.text: na cāsya labhyate sthānaṃ gaveṣitvā diśo daśa // SRS_32.46 //
children.translated_text: yet his [original] place cannot be found, even searching the ten directions. // SRS_32.46 //

children.text: śūnyaṃ jñātvā ca saṃsāraṃ bodhisattvo na sajjate /
children.translated_text: Having known <s>saṃsāra</s> to be empty, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not cling;

children.text: caranti caiva bodhyarthaṃ caristeṣāṃ na labhyate // SRS_32.47 //
children.translated_text: they walk for the sake of awakening, yet their walking cannot be found. // SRS_32.47 //

children.text: śakunānāṃ yathākāśe padaṃ teṣāṃ na labhyate /
children.translated_text: Just as the tracks of birds in the sky cannot be found,

children.text: evaṃsvabhāvā sā bodhirbodhisattvaiśca budhyate // SRS_32.48 //
children.translated_text: such is the nature of that <s>bodhi</s> — and it is awakened to by the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. // SRS_32.48 //

children.text: yathā māyāṃ vidarśeti māyākāraḥ suśikṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a well-trained magician displays an illusion —

children.text: nānāprakārarūpāṇi na ca rūpopalabhyate // SRS_32.49 //
children.translated_text: forms of various kinds — yet no form can be found, // SRS_32.49 //

children.text: alabdhilabdhirno manye labdhe labdhirna vidyate /
children.translated_text: [so] the attainment of non-attainment is not conceived by me; in attainment, no attainment exists;

children.text: māyopamaṃ ca tajjñānaṃ na māyāyāṃ ca tat sthitam // SRS_32.50 //
children.translated_text: and that knowledge is like an illusion, yet it does not abide in the illusion. // SRS_32.50 //

children.text: evaṃ śūnyeṣu dharmeṣu bālabuddhiṃ vikalpayet /
children.translated_text: Thus in empty <s>dharmas</s>, those of childish intellect construct distinctions;

children.text: vikalpe caramāṇānāṃ gatayaḥ ṣaṭa parāyaṇam // SRS_32.51 //
children.translated_text: for those who move about in conceptual proliferation, the six destinies are their final resort. // SRS_32.51 //

children.text: jātijaropagāḥ sattvā jātisteṣāṃ na kṣīyate /
children.translated_text: Beings are subject to birth and old age; their births do not diminish;

children.text: jātimaraṇaskandhānāṃ duḥkhaṃ teṣāmanantakam // SRS_32.52 //
children.translated_text: for the <s>skandhas</s> of birth and death, their suffering is without end. // SRS_32.52 //

children.text: duḥkho jātisaṃsāro bālabuddhīhi kalpitaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃsāra</s> with its birth and suffering is constructed by those of childish intellect;

children.text: kalpāsteṣāṃ na kṣīyante kalpakoṭyaśca saṃsarī // SRS_32.53 //
children.translated_text: their constructions do not diminish, and they wander through <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>. // SRS_32.53 //

children.text: (Vaidya 199)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 199)

children.text: ayuktāḥ saṃprayuktāśca karmayogasmi te sthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Unyoked [from wisdom] yet conjoined [with defilements], they abide in the bondage of <s>karma</s>;

children.text: karmaṇaste na mucyate karmopādāni ye ratāḥ // SRS_32.54 //
children.translated_text: they are not freed from <s>karma</s> — those who delight in appropriating <s>karma</s>. // SRS_32.54 //

children.text: karmaughe vahatāṃ teṣāṃ karma na kṣīyate sadā /
children.translated_text: Carried along in the flood of <s>karma</s>, their <s>karma</s> never diminishes;

children.text: punaḥ punaśca mrīyante mārapakṣe sthitāḥ sadā // SRS_32.55 //
children.translated_text: again and again they die, always standing in <s>Māra</s>'s camp. // SRS_32.55 //

children.text: mārābhibhūtā duṣprajñāḥ saṃkliṣṭena hi karmaṇā /
children.translated_text: Overpowered by <s>Māra</s>, of faulty wisdom, through defiled <s>karma</s>,

children.text: anubhonti jātimaraṇaṃ tatratatropapattiṣu // SRS_32.56 //
children.translated_text: they experience birth and death in various rebirths. // SRS_32.56 //

children.text: maraṇaṃ te nigacchanti andhā bālāḥ pṛthagjanāḥ /
children.translated_text: They meet death — blind fools, ordinary beings;

children.text: hanyante ca vihanyante gatiścaiṣāṃ na bhadrikā // SRS_32.57 //
children.translated_text: they are struck and destroyed, and their destiny is not auspicious. // SRS_32.57 //

children.text: parasparaṃ ca ghātenti śastrebhirbālabuddhayaḥ /
children.translated_text: They slay each other with weapons, those of childish intellect;

children.text: evaṃ prayujyamānānāṃ duḥkhaṃ teṣāṃ pravardhate // SRS_32.58 //
children.translated_text: thus engaged, their suffering increases. // SRS_32.58 //

children.text: putrā mahyaṃ dhanaṃ mahyaṃ bālabuddhīhi kalpitam /
children.translated_text: "Sons are mine, wealth is mine" — thus constructed by those of childish intellect;

children.text: asataṃ karma kalpitvā saṃsāro bhūyu vardhate // SRS_32.59 //
children.translated_text: having constructed unreal <s>karma</s>, <s>saṃsāra</s> increases further. // SRS_32.59 //

children.text: saṃsāraṃ vardhayantaste saṃsaranti pṛthagjanāḥ /
children.translated_text: Increasing <s>saṃsāra</s>, the ordinary beings wander;

children.text: pṛthak pṛthak ca gacchanti tena coktāḥ pṛthagjanāḥ // SRS_32.60 //
children.translated_text: they go each their separate way — therefore they are called "ordinary beings" (<s>pṛthagjanāḥ</s>). // SRS_32.60 //

children.text: pṛthudharmā pravakṣyanti ujjhitvā buddhaśāsanam /
children.translated_text: They will proclaim inferior <s>dharmas</s>, having abandoned the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching;

children.text: na te mokṣaṃ labhiṣyanti mārasya vaśamāgatāḥ // SRS_32.61 //
children.translated_text: they will not obtain liberation, having come under <s>Māra</s>'s power. // SRS_32.61 //

children.text: kāmanāṃ kāraṇaṃ bālāḥ striyaṃ sevanti pūtikām /
children.translated_text: Fools, for the sake of sensual pleasures, resort to foul women;

children.text: pūtikāṃ gati gacchanti patante tena durgatim // SRS_32.62 //
children.translated_text: they go to a foul destiny — thereby they fall into misfortune. // SRS_32.62 //

children.text: kāmānna buddhā varṇenti nāpi strīṇāṃ niṣevaṇam /
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddhas</s> do not praise sensual pleasures, nor resorting to women;

children.text: mahābhayo 'hipāśo 'yamistripāśaḥ sudāruṇaḥ // SRS_32.63 //
children.translated_text: this snare of women is a great terror, a serpent's noose, extremely terrible. // SRS_32.63 //

children.text: vivarjayanti taṃ dhīrāścaṇḍamāśīviṣaṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: The wise ones avoid it, as one avoids a fierce poisonous serpent;

children.text: na viśvasanti istrīṇāṃ naiṣa mārgo hi bodhaye // SRS_32.64 //
children.translated_text: they do not trust women — for this is not the path to awakening. // SRS_32.64 //

children.text: bhāventi bodhimārgaṃ ca sarvabuddhairniṣevitam /
children.translated_text: They cultivate the path to awakening practiced by all <s>Buddhas</s>;

children.text: bhāvayitvā ca taṃ mārgaṃ bhonti buddhā anuttarāḥ // SRS_32.65 //
children.translated_text: and having cultivated that path, they become unsurpassed <s>Buddhas</s>. // SRS_32.65 //

children.text: anuttarāśca te yuktā bhonti lokasya cetiyāḥ /
children.translated_text: And those unsurpassed ones, properly engaged, become reliquaries (<s>caityas</s>) for the world;

children.text: anuttareṇa jñānena buddhā bhonti anuttarāḥ // SRS_32.66 //
children.translated_text: through unsurpassed knowledge, the <s>Buddhas</s> become unsurpassed. // SRS_32.66 //

children.text: poṣadhaṃ ca niṣevanti śīlaskandhe samādapī /
children.translated_text: They practice the <s>poṣadha</s> (observance day) and cause others to undertake the aggregate of morality;

children.text: samādapenti bodhāya sattvakoṭīracintiyāḥ // SRS_32.67 //
children.translated_text: they establish for awakening inconceivable <s>koṭis</s> of beings. // SRS_32.67 //

children.text: kurvanti te 'rthaṃ sattvānāmaprameyacintiyam /
children.translated_text: They accomplish the welfare of beings — immeasurable and inconceivable;

children.text: te te śūrā mahāprajñā tāḍentyamṛtadundubhim // SRS_32.68 //
children.translated_text: those heroes, of great wisdom, strike the drum of the deathless. // SRS_32.68 //

children.text: (Vaidya 200)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 200)

children.text: kampenti mārabhavanaṃ cālenti mārakāyikān /
children.translated_text: They shake <s>Māra</s>'s abode and agitate the <s>Mārakāyika</s> [gods];

children.text: samādapenti bodhāya mārakoṭīracintiyāḥ // SRS_32.69 //
children.translated_text: they establish for awakening inconceivable <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Māras</s>. // SRS_32.69 //

children.text: paravādīnnigṛhṇanti nirjinanti ca tīrthikān /
children.translated_text: They subdue proponents of other doctrines and conquer <s>tīrthikas</s>;

children.text: kampenti vasudhāṃ sarvāṃ sasamudrāṃ saparvatām // SRS_32.70 //
children.translated_text: they shake the entire earth with its oceans and mountains. // SRS_32.70 //

children.text: vikurvamāṇā kāyebhiranekarddhivikurvitaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Performing transformations with their bodies, through manifold miraculous displays,

children.text: nidarśenti mahāprajñāḥ prātihāryānacintiyān // SRS_32.71 //
children.translated_text: those of great wisdom show inconceivable miracles. // SRS_32.71 //

children.text: kṣetrakoṭī prakampenti yathā gaṅgāya vālikā /
children.translated_text: They cause <s>koṭis</s> of fields to tremble — as many as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>;

children.text: parājinitvā te mārā bodhiṃ budhyantyanuttarām // SRS_32.72 //
children.translated_text: having defeated the <s>Māras</s>, they awaken to the unsurpassed awakening. // SRS_32.72 //

children.text: nirmiṇvanti ca te vṛkṣān ratanaiḥ suvicitritān /
children.translated_text: They create trees beautifully adorned with jewels,

children.text: phalapuṣpehi saṃyuktān gandhavantān manoramān // SRS_32.73 //
children.translated_text: endowed with fruits and flowers, fragrant and delightful. // SRS_32.73 //

children.text: prāsādāṃśca vimānāni kūṭāgārān saharṣikān /
children.translated_text: Palaces, mansions, and upper-storied pavilions with terraces —

children.text: nirmiṇvanti ca te śūrāḥ puṣkariṇyo manoramāḥ // SRS_32.74 //
children.translated_text: those heroes create delightful lotus-pools. // SRS_32.74 //

children.text: aṣṭāṅgajalasaṃpannāḥ svacchāḥ śītā anāvilāḥ /
children.translated_text: Endowed with water possessing eight qualities — clear, cool, and undefiled;

children.text: pibanti ye tato vāri tisrastṛṣṇā jahanti te // SRS_32.75 //
children.translated_text: those who drink water from them abandon the three cravings. // SRS_32.75 //

children.text: avivartyāśca te bhonti pītvā vāri niruttaram /
children.translated_text: They become non-retrogressing, having drunk the unsurpassed water;

children.text: anuttareṇa jñānena bhonti buddhā anuttarāḥ // SRS_32.76 //
children.translated_text: through unsurpassed knowledge, they become unsurpassed <s>Buddhas</s>. // SRS_32.76 //

children.text: anuttarāṃ gatiṃ śāntāṃ gacchantīti vijānatha /
children.translated_text: Know that they go to the unsurpassed, peaceful destination;

children.text: imāṃ gatimajānantaḥ pranaṣṭāḥ sarvatīrthikāḥ // SRS_32.77 //
children.translated_text: not knowing this destination, all the <s>tīrthikas</s> are lost. // SRS_32.77 //

children.text: te ca tadgatikāḥ sattvā ye teṣāṃ bhonti niśritāḥ /
children.translated_text: And those beings who go to that destination, who rely upon them [the <s>tīrthikas</s>] —

children.text: patiṣyanti mahāghorāmavīcimaparāyaṇāḥ // SRS_32.78 //
children.translated_text: they will fall into the greatly terrible <s>Avīci</s> [hell], without refuge. // SRS_32.78 //

children.text: yāstatra vedanā ghorā na śakyāstāḥ prakīrtitum /
children.translated_text: The terrible feelings there cannot be proclaimed;

children.text: ahaṃ ca tāḥ prajānāmi bodhisattvāśca tāyinaḥ // SRS_32.79 //
children.translated_text: I know them, and the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, the protectors, [know them too]. // SRS_32.79 //

children.text: ye ceha dharme kāṅkṣanti evaṃ gambhīri durdṛśe /
children.translated_text: Those who doubt this <s>Dharma</s>, so profound and hard to see —

children.text: abhūmistatra bālānāmupalambhasmi ye sthitāḥ // SRS_32.80 //
children.translated_text: there is no ground there for fools who stand in apprehension. // SRS_32.80 //

children.text: nirmiṇvanti viyūhāṃste naikarūpanidarśanān /
children.translated_text: They create arrays showing manifold forms,

children.text: yena te sarvi gacchanti buddhakṣetrānanuttarān // SRS_32.81 //
children.translated_text: by which all of them go to unsurpassed <s>Buddha</s>-fields. // SRS_32.81 //

children.text: yāvantyo buddhakṣetreṣu rūpanirhārasaṃpadaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever accomplishments of form-manifestation exist in the <s>Buddha</s>-fields —

children.text: sarvāstā iha darśenti bodhisattvā maharddhikāḥ // SRS_32.82 //
children.translated_text: all those are displayed here by those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of great miraculous power. // SRS_32.82 //

children.text: mahādharmeṇa saṃnaddhā mahāvīrā mahābalāḥ /
children.translated_text: Armored with the great <s>Dharma</s>, great heroes of great strength,

children.text: mahāśūnyārthavajreṇa prahārāṇi dadanti te // SRS_32.83 //
children.translated_text: they deliver blows with the <s>vajra</s> of the meaning of great emptiness. // SRS_32.83 //

children.text: raśmikoṭisahasrāṇi yathā gaṅgāya vālikā /
children.translated_text: Thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of rays — as many as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> —

children.text: kāyato niścarantyeṣāṃ yebhirlokaḥ prabhāsate // SRS_32.84 //
children.translated_text: issue from their bodies, by which the world is illuminated. // SRS_32.84 //

children.text: (Vaidya 201)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 201)

children.text: na te strīṣvabhirajyante na ca teṣāṃ virāgatā /
children.translated_text: They are not attached to women, nor do they have aversion;

children.text: vibhāvitaiteṣāṃ saṃjñā istrisaṃjñā svabhāvataḥ // SRS_32.85 //
children.translated_text: their perception is cultivated — the perception of 'woman' is [understood] in its own-nature. // SRS_32.85 //

children.text: aśūnyā buddhakṣetrāste yeṣu śūrā bhavanti te /
children.translated_text: Those <s>Buddha</s>-fields are not empty where those heroes exist;

children.text: kiṃ teṣāṃ māru pāpīyānantarāyaṃ kariṣyati // SRS_32.86 //
children.translated_text: what obstacle can <s>Māra</s>, the Evil One, create for them? // SRS_32.86 //

children.text: dṛṣṭīkṛteṣu ye sthitvā bahu buddhā virāgitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who stand in views born of [wrong] actions have turned away from many <s>Buddhas</s>;

children.text: vyāpādena upastabdhā icchālobhapratisthitāḥ // SRS_32.87 //
children.translated_text: supported by ill-will, established in desire and greed — // SRS_32.87 //

children.text: sarvasaṃjñā vibhāvitvā saṃjñāvaivartiye sthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: having cultivated all perceptions, they stand in the non-retrogression of perception;

children.text: ya evaṃ jñāsyate jñānaṃ buddhajñānamacintiyam // SRS_32.88 //
children.translated_text: he who thus knows knowledge — the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge — // SRS_32.88 //

children.text: pūrvāntamaparāntaṃ ca pratyutpannaṃ ca paśyati /
children.translated_text: he sees the past, the future, and the present;

children.text: evaṃ ca deśitā dharmā na cātra kiṃci deśitam // SRS_32.89 //
children.translated_text: and thus <s>dharmas</s> are taught, yet nothing whatsoever is taught herein. // SRS_32.89 //

children.text: na ca jñānena jānāti na cājñānena sīdati /
children.translated_text: He does not know through knowledge, nor does he decline through ignorance;

children.text: jñānājñāne vikalpetvā buddhajñāneti vuccati // SRS_32.90 //
children.translated_text: having discriminated knowledge and ignorance — [that] is called <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. // SRS_32.90 //

children.text: vijñaptivākyasaṃketaṃ bodhisattvaḥ prajānati /
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> understands the conventions of informative speech;

children.text: karoti arthaṃ sattvānāmaprameyacintiyam // SRS_32.91 //
children.translated_text: he accomplishes the welfare of beings — immeasurable and inconceivable. // SRS_32.91 //

children.text: saṃjñā saṃjānanārthena udgraheṇa nidarśitā /
children.translated_text: Perception, by the meaning of perceiving, has been shown through grasping;

children.text: anudgrahaśca sā saṃjñā viviktārthena deśitā // SRS_32.92 //
children.translated_text: and that non-grasping perception has been taught with the meaning of seclusion. // SRS_32.92 //

children.text: yacco viviktaṃ sā saṃjñā yā viviktā sa deśanā /
children.translated_text: That which is secluded — that is perception; that which is secluded — that is the teaching;

children.text: saṃjñāsvabhāvo jñātaśca evaṃ saṃjñā na bheṣyati // SRS_32.93 //
children.translated_text: the own-nature of perception is known — thus perception will not arise. // SRS_32.93 //

children.text: prahāsyāma imāṃ saṃjñāṃ yasya saṃjñā pravartate /
children.translated_text: "We shall abandon this perception" — for one in whom perception operates,

children.text: saṃjñā prapañce carati na sa saṃjñātu mucyate // SRS_32.94 //
children.translated_text: perception moves in conceptual proliferation — he is not freed from perception. // SRS_32.94 //

children.text: kasyeyaṃ saṃjñā utpannā kena saṃjñā utpāditā /
children.translated_text: Whose is this perception that has arisen? By whom was perception produced?

children.text: kena sā sparśitā saṃjñā kena saṃjñā nirodhitā // SRS_32.95 //
children.translated_text: By whom was that perception touched? By whom was perception ceased? // SRS_32.95 //

children.text: dharmo na labdho buddhena yasya saṃjñā utpadyate /
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> did not find a <s>dharma</s> for which perception arises;

children.text: iha cintetha taṃ arthaṃ tataḥ saṃjñā na bheṣyati // SRS_32.96 //
children.translated_text: reflect on this meaning here — then perception will not arise. // SRS_32.96 //

children.text: kadā saṃjñā anutpannā kasya saṃjñā virudhyate /
children.translated_text: When was perception unarisen? Whose perception is it that ceases?

children.text: vimokṣa ciatacārasya kathaṃ tatra utpadyate // SRS_32.97 //
children.translated_text: How does liberation arise for one whose mind has ceased to wander? // SRS_32.97 //

children.text: yadā vimokṣaṃ spṛśati sarva cintā acintiyā /
children.translated_text: When one touches liberation, all thinking becomes inconceivable;

children.text: acintiyā yadā cintā tadā bhoti acintiyaḥ // SRS_32.98 //
children.translated_text: when thinking becomes inconceivable, then one becomes inconceivable. // SRS_32.98 //

children.text: cintābhūmau sthihitvāna pūrvameva vicintitā /
children.translated_text: Having formerly stood on the ground of thinking, one had thought;

children.text: sarvacintāṃ jahitvāna tato bheṣyatyacintiyaḥ // SRS_32.99 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned all thinking, then one becomes inconceivable. // SRS_32.99 //

children.text: (Vaidya 202)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 202)

children.text: śukladharmavipāko 'yamasaṃskāreṇa paśyati /
children.translated_text: This fruit of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> — he sees without fabrication;

children.text: ekakṣaṇena jānāti sarvasattvavicintitam // SRS_32.100 //
children.translated_text: in a single instant he knows the thoughts of all beings. // SRS_32.100 //

children.text: yathā sattvāstathā cintā yathā cintā tathā jināḥ /
children.translated_text: As are beings, so is thinking; as is thinking, so are the Conquerors;

children.text: acintiyena buddhena iyaṃ cintā prakāśitā // SRS_32.101 //
children.translated_text: by the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>, this [nature of] thinking has been illuminated. // SRS_32.101 //

children.text: yo raho eku cinteti kadā cintā na bheṣyati /
children.translated_text: One who thinks alone in solitude, "When will thinking cease?" —

children.text: na cintāṃ cintayantasya sarvacintā vigacchati // SRS_32.102 //
children.translated_text: for one not thinking about thinking, all thinking vanishes. // SRS_32.102 //

children.text: cyute mṛte kālagate yasya cintā pravartate /
children.translated_text: For one in whom thinking operates regarding the fallen, the dead, the departed —

children.text: cintānusāri vijñānaṃ nāsā cintāntamucyate // SRS_32.103 //
children.translated_text: consciousness follows thinking — this is not called the end of thinking. // SRS_32.103 //

children.text: ye sthitā istrisaṃjñāyāṃ rāgasteṣāṃ pravartate /
children.translated_text: Those who stand in the perception of 'woman' — passion operates for them;

children.text: vibhāvitāyāṃ saṃjñāyāṃ na rāgeṇopalipyate // SRS_32.104 //
children.translated_text: when perception is cultivated [as empty], one is not stained by passion. // SRS_32.104 //

children.text: iyaṃ cintā mahācintā dharmacintā niruttarā /
children.translated_text: This thinking is great thinking — the supreme <s>Dharma</s>-thinking;

children.text: anayā dharmacintāya bhūtacintā pravartate // SRS_32.105 //
children.translated_text: through this <s>Dharma</s>-thinking, true thinking operates. // SRS_32.105 //

children.text: bahu acintiyā cintā dīrgharātraṃ vicintitā /
children.translated_text: Much inconceivable thinking has been thought for a long time;

children.text: na ca cintākṣayo jātaścintayitvā ayoniśaḥ // SRS_32.106 //
children.translated_text: yet the exhaustion of thinking has not occurred through thinking improperly. // SRS_32.106 //

children.text: yo 'sau cintayate nāma kṣaye jñānaṃ na vidyate /
children.translated_text: For that which is called 'thinking' — knowledge of its exhaustion is not found;

children.text: na kṣayo bhūmijñānasya kṣayasyo eṣa dharmatā // SRS_32.107 //
children.translated_text: there is no exhaustion of the knowledge of the ground — this is the nature of exhaustion. // SRS_32.107 //

children.text: ghoṣo vākpatha vijñaptiḥ kṣayaśabdena deśitā /
children.translated_text: Sound, the path of speech, information — taught through the word 'exhaustion';

children.text: nirviśeṣāśca te dharmā yathā jñānaṃ tathā kṣayaḥ // SRS_32.108 //
children.translated_text: yet those <s>dharmas</s> are non-different — as is knowledge, so is exhaustion. // SRS_32.108 //

children.text: anutpannāniruddhāśca animittā alakṣaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: Unarisen, unceased, signless, without marks —

children.text: kalpakoṭiṃ pi bhāṣitvā animittena deśitāḥ // SRS_32.109 //
children.translated_text: even if spoken of for <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, they are taught as signless. // SRS_32.109 //

children.text: sarvabhāvān vibhāvitvā abhāve ye pratiṣṭhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having cultivated all phenomena, those established in non-existence —

children.text: na cānyo darśito bhāvo nābhāvo 'nyo nidarśitaḥ // SRS_32.110 //
children.translated_text: no other existence has been shown, nor has another non-existence been demonstrated. // SRS_32.110 //

children.text: vijñaptā bhāvaśabdena abhāvasya prakāśanā /
children.translated_text: The expression through the word 'existence' is the illumination of non-existence;

children.text: na cāsau sarvabuddhehi abhāvaḥ śakyu paśyitum // SRS_32.111 //
children.translated_text: yet that non-existence cannot be seen even by all the <s>Buddhas</s>. // SRS_32.111 //

children.text: yo bhāvaḥ sarvabhāvānāmabhāva eṣa darśitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The [true] nature of all phenomena — their non-existence has been shown;

children.text: evaṃ bhāvān vijānitvā abhāvo bhoti darśitaḥ // SRS_32.112 //
children.translated_text: having known phenomena thus, non-existence is shown. // SRS_32.112 //

children.text: nāsau sparśayituṃ śakyamabhāvo jātu kenacit /
children.translated_text: That non-existence can never be touched by anyone;

children.text: sparśanāttu abhāvasya nirvṛti eṣa deśitā // SRS_32.113 //
children.translated_text: yet from the touching of non-existence, this cessation (<s>nirvṛti</s>) has been taught. // SRS_32.113 //

children.text: ahaṃ buddho bhavelloke yasyaiṣā ho matirbhavet /
children.translated_text: "I shall become a <s>Buddha</s> in the world" — for one in whom such a thought arises,

children.text: na jātu bhavatṛṣṇārto bodhiṃ budhyeta paṇḍitaḥ // SRS_32.114 //
children.translated_text: tormented by craving for existence, the wise one never awakens to <s>bodhi</s>. // SRS_32.114 //

children.text: na kaṃci dharmaṃ prārtheti bodhisattvaḥ samāhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The concentrated <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not seek any <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: niṣkiṃcanā nirābhogā eṣā bodhīti ucyate // SRS_32.115 //
children.translated_text: possessionless, effortless — this is called awakening (<s>bodhi</s>). // SRS_32.115 //

children.text: (Vaidya 203)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 203)

children.text: bahū evaṃ pravakṣyanti vayaṃ bodhāya prasthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Many will say thus: "We have set out for awakening" —

children.text: imāṃ gatimajānanto dūre te buddhabodhaye // SRS_32.116 //
children.translated_text: not knowing this path, they are far from <s>Buddha</s>-awakening. // SRS_32.116 //

children.text: śabdena deśitā dharmāḥ sarve saṃskāra śūnyakāḥ /
children.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s> taught by sound are conditioned and empty;

children.text: yaśva svabhāvaḥ śabdasya gambhīraḥ sūkṣma durdṛśaḥ // SRS_32.117 //
children.translated_text: and the own-nature of sound itself — profound, subtle, hard to see. // SRS_32.117 //

children.text: mahābhijñāya nirdeśa idaṃ sūtraṃ pravuccati /
children.translated_text: A teaching of great superknowledge — this <s>sūtra</s> is proclaimed;

children.text: arthāya bodhisattvānāṃ sarvabuddhehi deśitam // SRS_32.118 //
children.translated_text: taught by all <s>Buddhas</s> for the benefit of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. // SRS_32.118 //

children.text: pratipakṣā hatāsteṣāṃ yāvantaḥ sāṃkileśikāḥ /
children.translated_text: The opponents of defilement have been destroyed for them —

children.text: pratiṣṭhitā abhijñāsu ṛddhisteṣāṃ subhāvitā // SRS_32.119 //
children.translated_text: established in the superknowledges, their miraculous powers are well-cultivated. // SRS_32.119 //

children.text: sthitāḥ praṇidhijñānasmiṃstacca jñānaṃ vibhāvitam /
children.translated_text: Standing in the knowledge of their vows, that knowledge is cultivated;

children.text: atṛptirlabdhajñānasya aprameyā acintiyā // SRS_32.120 //
children.translated_text: the unsatisfied thirst of one who has obtained knowledge is immeasurable and inconceivable. // SRS_32.120 //

children.text: na teṣāmabhisaṃskāraḥ samādhī riddhikāraṇam /
children.translated_text: There is no fabrication for them — <s>samādhi</s> as the cause of their miraculous power;

children.text: vipāka eṣa śūrāṇāṃ nityakālaṃ samāhitaḥ // SRS_32.121 //
children.translated_text: this is the fruit of those heroes — constantly concentrated. // SRS_32.121 //

children.text: vipākajāye ṛddhīye gacchantī kṣetrakoṭyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Through their fruit-born miraculous power, they traverse <s>koṭis</s> of fields;

children.text: paśyanti lokapradyotān yathā gaṅgāya vālikā // SRS_32.122 //
children.translated_text: they see the illuminators of the world — as many as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. // SRS_32.122 //

children.text: upapattiścyutisteṣāṃ yathā cittasya vartate /
children.translated_text: Their rebirth and death operate as their mind wills;

children.text: cittasya vaśitāṃ prāptāḥ kāyasteṣāṃ prabhāsvaraḥ // SRS_32.123 //
children.translated_text: having attained mastery of the mind, their body is radiant. // SRS_32.123 //

children.text: bhāvanāmayi ṛddhīye ye sthitā buddhaśrāvakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those <s>Buddha</s>-<s>Śrāvakas</s> who stand in the miraculous power born of cultivation —

children.text: tebhiḥ saṃskāraṛddhīye kalāṃ nāyānti ṣoḍaśīm // SRS_32.124 //
children.translated_text: they do not approach even a sixteenth fraction of the miraculous power of fabrication. // SRS_32.124 //

children.text: na teṣāṃ sarvadevebhirāśayaḥ śakyu jānitum /
children.translated_text: Their intention cannot be known by all gods,

children.text: anyatra lokanāthebhyo ye vā teṣāṃ same sthitāḥ // SRS_32.125 //
children.translated_text: except by the Lords of the World, or those who stand equal to them. // SRS_32.125 //

children.text: na teṣāmasti khālityaṃ na caiva palitaṃ śire /
children.translated_text: For them there is no baldness, nor greying of the hair on the head;

children.text: audārikā jarā nāsti na duḥkhamaraṇaṃ tathā // SRS_32.126 //
children.translated_text: there is no gross old age, nor suffering and death. // SRS_32.126 //

children.text: saṃśayo vimatirnāsti kāṅkṣā teṣāṃ na vidyate /
children.translated_text: Doubt and uncertainty do not exist; perplexity is not found in them;

children.text: rātriṃdivaṃ gaveṣanti sūtrakoṭīśatāni te // SRS_32.127 //
children.translated_text: day and night they seek hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>sūtras</s>. // SRS_32.127 //

children.text: prahīṇānuśayāsteṣāṃ yāvantaḥ sāṃkileśikāḥ /
children.translated_text: Their latent tendencies of defilement are all abandoned;

children.text: samacittāḥ sadā bhonti sarvasattvāna te 'ntike // SRS_32.128 //
children.translated_text: they are always of equal mind toward all beings. // SRS_32.128 //

children.text: samādhikoṭiniyutāṃ nirdiśanti daśaddiśe /
children.translated_text: They teach <s>niyutas</s> of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>samādhis</s> in the ten directions;

children.text: praśnakoṭīsahasrāṇi vyākurvan hyanavasthitāḥ // SRS_32.129 //
children.translated_text: they answer thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of questions, without hesitation. // SRS_32.129 //

children.text: strīsaṃjñā puruṣasaṃjñā ca sarvasaṃjñā vibhāvitāḥ /
children.translated_text: The perception of woman, the perception of man — all perceptions are cultivated [as empty];

children.text: sthitā abhāvasaṃjñāyāṃ deśenti bhūtaniścayam // SRS_32.130 //
children.translated_text: standing in the perception of non-existence, they teach the ascertainment of reality. // SRS_32.130 //

children.text: pariśuddhena jñānena yathāvaddharmadeśakāḥ /
children.translated_text: With purified knowledge, they teach the <s>Dharma</s> as it truly is;

children.text: dharmasaṃgītyābhiyuktāḥ samādhijñānagocarāḥ // SRS_32.131 //
children.translated_text: devoted to <s>Dharma</s>-assemblies, their domain is <s>samādhi</s>-knowledge. // SRS_32.131 //

children.text: (Vaidya 204)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 204)

children.text: yāpi dhyānacaristeṣāṃ nāsau bhāvapratiṣṭhitā /
children.translated_text: Even their practice of <s>dhyāna</s> is not established in [any] phenomenon;

children.text: avandhyaṃ vacanaṃ teṣāmavandhyā dharmadeśanā // SRS_32.132 //
children.translated_text: their speech is never barren; their <s>Dharma</s>-teaching is never barren. // SRS_32.132 //

children.text: sulabdhaṃ tena mānuṣyaṃ prahīṇāḥ sarvi akṣaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: Well-gained is their human birth; all inauspicious moments are abandoned;

children.text: kṛtajñāḥ sarvabuddhānāṃ yeṣāṃ sūtramidaṃ priyam // SRS_32.133 //
children.translated_text: grateful to all <s>Buddhas</s> — those for whom this <s>sūtra</s> is dear. // SRS_32.133 //

children.text: kalpā acintiyāstehi ye saṃsārāttu choritāḥ /
children.translated_text: Inconceivable <s>kalpas</s> are stolen away from <s>saṃsāra</s> by those

children.text: yairitaḥ sūtraśreṣṭhāto dhṛtā gāthā catuṣpadā // SRS_32.134 //
children.translated_text: who have retained a single four-line verse from this supreme <s>sūtra</s>. // SRS_32.134 //

children.text: dṛṣṭāste sarvabuddhehi taiste buddhāśca satkṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: They have been seen by all <s>Buddhas</s>, and they have honored those <s>Buddhas</s>;

children.text: kṣipraṃ ca bodhiṃ prāpsyanti teṣāṃ sūtramidaṃ priyam // SRS_32.135 //
children.translated_text: they will quickly attain awakening — those for whom this <s>sūtra</s> is dear. // SRS_32.135 //

children.text: na teṣāṃ kāṅkṣa vimatī sarvadharmeṣu bheṣyatī /
children.translated_text: Doubt and uncertainty shall not exist for them regarding all <s>dharmas</s>;

children.text: āsannā nirvṛtisteṣāṃ yeṣāṃ sūtramidaṃ priyam // SRS_32.136 //
children.translated_text: cessation is near for those for whom this <s>sūtra</s> is dear. // SRS_32.136 //

children.text: dṛṣṭastehi mahāvīro gṛdhrakūūṭe tathāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: They have seen the Great Hero, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s>;

children.text: sarve vyākṛtu buddhena drakṣyanti maitrakaṃ jinam // SRS_32.137 //
children.translated_text: all predicted by the <s>Buddha</s>, they shall see the Conqueror <s>Maitreya</s>. // SRS_32.137 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā maitreya saṃbuddhaṃ lapsyante kṣānti bhadrikām /
children.translated_text: Having seen the fully awakened <s>Maitreya</s>, they shall obtain the auspicious patient acceptance (<s>kṣānti</s>);

children.text: ye keci kṣayakālasminniha sūtre pratiṣṭhitāḥ // SRS_32.138 //
children.translated_text: all those who, in this time of decline, are established in this <s>sūtra</s>. // SRS_32.138 //

children.text: sthitāste bhūtakoṭīye bhūtakoṭiracintiyā /
children.translated_text: 'They stand at the limit of reality — the limit of reality is inconceivable;

children.text: acintiyāyāṃ koṭīye kāṅkṣā teṣāṃ na vidyate // SRS_32.139 //
children.translated_text: at that inconceivable limit, doubt does not exist for them. // SRS_32.139 //

children.text: na teṣāṃ vidyate kāṅkṣā aṇūmātrāpi sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Not even the slightest atom of doubt exists for them, in any way;

children.text: aṇūmātre prahīṇesmin bodhisteṣāṃ na durlabhā // SRS_32.140 //
children.translated_text: when even the atomic [doubt] is abandoned, <s>bodhi</s> is not hard for them to obtain. // SRS_32.140 //

children.text: caratāṃ duṣkaraṃ caiva kṣayakāle subhairave /
children.translated_text: 'For those practicing the difficult practice in the terrifying age of decline,

children.text: śikṣitva sūtraratne 'smin pratibhānasmi akṣayam // SRS_32.141 //
children.translated_text: having trained in this jewel of a <s>sūtra</s>, their eloquence becomes inexhaustible. // SRS_32.141 //

children.text: idaṃ sūtraṃ priyaṃ kṛtvā buddhānāṃ gañjarakṣakāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having held this <s>sūtra</s> dear, they are guardians of the <s>Buddhas</s>' treasury;

children.text: sarvabuddhāniyaṃ pūjā dharmapūjā acintiyā // SRS_32.142 //
children.translated_text: this is the worship of all <s>Buddhas</s> — an inconceivable worship through <s>dharma</s>! // SRS_32.142 //

children.text: na teṣāṃ durlabhaṃ jñānaṃ buddhajñānamacintiyam /
children.translated_text: 'The inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge is not hard for them to obtain;

children.text: dhārayiṣyantidaṃ sūtraṃ kṣayakālesmi dāruṇe // SRS_32.143 //
children.translated_text: they shall uphold this <s>sūtra</s> in this terrible age of decline! // SRS_32.143 //

children.text: yebhiśca pūrvabuddhānāmime sūtrānta dhāritāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Those by whom these <s>sūtrāntas</s> of former <s>Buddhas</s> were upheld —

children.text: teṣāṃ kāyagatā ete kṣayakāle pravartiṣu // SRS_32.144 //
children.translated_text: they shall appear embodied in the age of decline, to propagate [them]! // SRS_32.144 //

children.text: te te nādaṃ nadiṣyanti buddhānāṃ kṣetrakoṭiṣu /
children.translated_text: 'They shall roar their roar in <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Buddha</s>-fields,

children.text: saṃmukhaṃ lokanāthānāṃ śākyasiṃhasya yā carī // SRS_32.145 //
children.translated_text: in the presence of the Lords of the World — [proclaiming] the conduct of the Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>! // SRS_32.145 //

children.text: siṃhanādaṃ nadantaste buddhanādamacintiyam /
children.translated_text: 'Roaring the lion's roar, the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>'s roar,

children.text: anantapratibhānena vakṣyante bodhimuttamām // SRS_32.146 //
children.translated_text: with infinite eloquence they shall speak of the supreme <s>bodhi</s>. // SRS_32.146 //

children.text: (Vaidya 205)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 205)

children.text: te te vyākṛta buddhena ikṣvākukulasaṃbhavāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'They are predicted by the <s>Buddha</s>, born in the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> lineage —

children.text: ye rakṣiṣyantimāṃ bodhiṃ kṣayakāle mahābhaye // SRS_32.147 //
children.translated_text: those who shall protect this <s>bodhi</s> in the age of decline, the great terror! // SRS_32.147 //

children.text: te te rūpeṇa saṃpannā lakṣaṇehi vicitritāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'They shall be endowed with [beautiful] form, adorned with the marks;

children.text: vikurvamāṇā yāsyanti buddhakoṭīya vandakāḥ // SRS_32.148 //
children.translated_text: displaying miracles, they shall go to worship <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>! // SRS_32.148 //

children.text: māyopamehi puṣpehi hemavarṇanidarśanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'With illusion-like flowers, golden in appearance,

children.text: rūpyāmayehi puṣpehi vaidūryasphaṭikehi ca // SRS_32.149 //
children.translated_text: with silver flowers, and with <s>vaidūrya</s> (lapis) and crystal —

children.text: sarvāṇi ratnajātāni prādurbhontyeṣu pāṇiṣu /
children.translated_text: all kinds of jewels appear in their hands,

children.text: yairākiranti saṃbuddhān bodhimārgagaveṣakāḥ // SRS_32.150 //
children.translated_text: with which those seekers of the <s>bodhi</s>-path shower the Perfectly Awakened Ones! // SRS_32.150 //

children.text: citrā nānāvidhā pūjā vādyanirhārasaṃpadā /
children.translated_text: 'Variegated and manifold worship, with the perfection of musical performance,

children.text: niścarī romakūpebhyo yathā gaṅgāya vālikāḥ // SRS_32.151 //
children.translated_text: issues from their hair-pores — as many as the sands of the Ganges! // SRS_32.151 //

children.text: ye ca śṛṇvanti taṃ śabdaṃ sattvakoṭyo acintiyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And those inconceivable <s>koṭīs</s> of beings who hear that sound

children.text: bhavantyavinivartyāste buddhajñāne anuttare // SRS_32.152 //
children.translated_text: become irreversible in the unsurpassed <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge! // SRS_32.152 //

children.text: teṣāṃ ca buddhakoṭīnāṃ varṇaṃ bhāṣantyacintiyam /
children.translated_text: 'They speak the inconceivable praise of those <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>;

children.text: acintiyeṣu kṣetreṣu teṣāṃ śabdaḥ śruṇīyati // SRS_32.153 //
children.translated_text: their sound is heard in inconceivable [Buddha-]fields! // SRS_32.153 //

children.text: ye ca śṛṇvanti taṃ śabdaṃ teṣāṃ saṃjñā nirudhyate /
children.translated_text: 'And those who hear that sound — their perception ceases;

children.text: nirodhitāyāṃ saṃjñāyāṃ buddhān paśyantyanalpakān // SRS_32.154 //
children.translated_text: when perception has ceased, they behold innumerable <s>Buddhas</s>! // SRS_32.154 //

children.text: etādṛśena jñānena caritvā bodhicārikām /
children.translated_text: 'Having practiced the conduct of awakening with such knowledge,

children.text: kṛtvārthaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ bhavantyarthakarā jināḥ // SRS_32.155 //
children.translated_text: having accomplished the welfare of all beings, they become <s>Jinas</s>, workers for others' welfare! // SRS_32.155 //

children.text: guṇānuśaṃsā ityete yā labhante ha paṇḍitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'These are the benefits and advantages that the wise obtain;

children.text: anye aparimāṇāśca yairiyaṃ bodhi dhāritā // SRS_32.156 //
children.translated_text: and immeasurably more too — for those by whom this <s>bodhi</s> is upheld! // SRS_32.156 //

children.text: mātṛgrāmo 'pidaṃ sūtraṃ śrutvā gāthāpi dhārayet /
children.translated_text: 'Even a woman, having heard this <s>sūtra</s>, should uphold even a verse [of it];

children.text: vivartayitvā strībhāvaṃ sa bhaved dharmabhāṇakaḥ // SRS_32.157 //
children.translated_text: having turned away from womanhood, she shall become a preacher of the <s>dharma</s>! // SRS_32.157 //

children.text: na sā puno 'pi strībhāvamitaḥ paścād grahīṣyati /
children.translated_text: 'She shall never again, henceforth, take on the state of womanhood;

children.text: bhavet prāsādiko nityaṃ lakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtaḥ // SRS_32.158 //
children.translated_text: she shall always become gracious, adorned with the marks! // SRS_32.158 //

children.text: śreṣṭhe 'tha iha sūtrasmin guṇāḥ śreṣṭhāḥ prakāśitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In this foremost <s>sūtra</s>, the foremost qualities have been illuminated;

children.text: te 'sya sarve bhaviṣyanti kṣipraṃ bodhiṃ ca prāpsyate // SRS_32.159 //
children.translated_text: all of them shall be his, and he shall swiftly attain <s>bodhi</s>! // SRS_32.159 //

children.text: viśāradaśca so nityaṃ bhoti sarvāsu jātiṣu /
children.translated_text: 'And he is always confident in all his births,

children.text: dhārayitvā idaṃ sūtraṃ bodhisattvāna gocaram // SRS_32.160 //
children.translated_text: having upheld this <s>sūtra</s>, the domain of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>! // SRS_32.160 //

children.text: janako bodhisattvānāṃ samādhiḥ śānta bhāṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This peaceful <s>samādhi</s>, declared the progenitor of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> —

children.text: ya icched buddhituṃ bodhimidaṃ sūtraṃ pravartayet // SRS_32.161 //
children.translated_text: whoever wishes to awaken to <s>bodhi</s> should set this <s>sūtra</s> in motion! // SRS_32.161 //

children.text: (Vaidya 206)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 206)

children.text: āsannāste munīndrāṇāmāsannā vuddhabodhaye /
children.translated_text: 'They are near to the Lords of Sages, near to <s>Buddha-bodhi</s>;

children.text: lapsyanti nacireṇemāṃ bhūmiṃ śāntāṃ samāhitāḥ // SRS_32.162 //
children.translated_text: before long, they shall attain this peaceful, concentrated stage! // SRS_32.162 //

children.text: iha bodhīya te śūrā bodhisattvāḥ sthitāḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: 'Here those heroes, the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, always stand in <s>bodhi</s>;

children.text: paśyanti buddhakoṭīyo yathā gaṅgāya vālikāḥ // SRS_32.163 //
children.translated_text: they behold <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, as many as the sands of the Ganges! // SRS_32.163 //

children.text: rājā bhavitvā mahīpati cakravartī
children.translated_text: 'Having become a king, a sovereign, a universal monarch,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca buddhān virajān suśāntacittān /
children.translated_text: and having seen the dustless <s>Buddhas</s>, of well-tranquilized minds —

children.text: gāthāśataistāṃ staviṣyati lokanāthān
children.translated_text: he shall praise those Lords of the World with hundreds of verses,

children.text: sa labhitva śāntaṃ imu virajaṃ samādhim // SRS_32.164 //
children.translated_text: having obtained this dustless, peaceful <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_32.164 //

children.text: so pūja kṛtva atuliya nāyakānāṃ
children.translated_text: 'Having performed incomparable worship of the Leaders,

children.text: sumahāyaśānāṃ devanarottamānām /
children.translated_text: of great fame, the supreme among gods and men —

children.text: muktvā sa rājyaṃ yathariva kheṭapiṇḍaṃ
children.translated_text: having cast off his kingdom as if it were a lump of spittle,

children.text: śuddho viśuddhaścariṣyati brahmacaryam // SRS_32.165 //
children.translated_text: pure and purified, he shall practice the holy life! // SRS_32.165 //

children.text: sa pravrajitva jinavaraśāsanasmiṃ
children.translated_text: 'Having gone forth in the teaching of the best of <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: labdhvāpi caitaṃ viraju samādhi śāntam /
children.translated_text: and having obtained this dustless, peaceful <s>samādhi</s> —

children.text: kalyāṇavākyo madhuragiraḥ sa bhūtvā
children.translated_text: of auspicious speech, with sweet words,

children.text: adhiṣṭhānu dhīmān bhaviṣyati sūtrakoṭyāḥ // SRS_32.166 //
children.translated_text: the wise one shall become the foundation of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>sūtras</s>! // SRS_32.166 //

children.text: śūnyānimittaṃ paramapraṇītu śāntaṃ dharma praśāntaṃ cara nipuṇaṃ asaṅgam /
children.translated_text: 'Having practiced the supreme, refined, peaceful, tranquil, subtle, unattached <s>dharma</s> of emptiness and signlessness,

children.text: svabhāvaśūnyaṃ sada virajaṃ praśāntaṃ samādhiprāptyā bahu jani saṃprakāśayī // SRS_32.167 //
children.translated_text: empty by own-nature, always dustless and tranquil — through the attainment of <s>samādhi</s>, he shall illuminate [it] in many births! // SRS_32.167 //

children.text: gambhīrabuddhī satatamanantabuddhī vistīrṇabuddhī aparimitārthabuddhī /
children.translated_text: 'Of profound wisdom, constantly of infinite wisdom, of vast wisdom, of wisdom comprehending immeasurable meanings —

children.text: gambhīra śāntaṃ labhiya imaṃ samādhimālokaprāpto bhaviṣyati sarvalokaḥ // SRS_32.168 //
children.translated_text: having obtained this profound, peaceful <s>samādhi</s>, he shall become the one who brings light to the entire world! // SRS_32.168 //

children.text: śuciśca nityaṃ bhaviṣyati brahmacārī sa nirāmagandhaḥ satatamasaṃkiliṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He shall always be pure, a practitioner of the holy life, free from the odor [of defilement], constantly undefiled;

children.text: anyāṃśca tatra sthapiṣyati sattvakoṭayo labdhvā praśāntaṃ imu virajaṃ samādhim // SRS_32.169 //
children.translated_text: and he shall establish <s>koṭīs</s> of beings there too, having obtained this tranquil, dustless <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_32.169 //

children.text: sa sutīkṣṇaprajño bhaviṣyati śreṣṭhaprajñaḥ śrutisāgaro 'sau nityamanantabuddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He shall be of exceedingly sharp wisdom, of foremost wisdom, an ocean of learning, always of infinite understanding;

children.text: kalyāṇavākyo matikuśalo vidhijño dhāritva śāntiṃ imu virajaṃ samādhim // SRS_32.170 //
children.translated_text: of auspicious speech, skilled in thought, knowing the method — having upheld this dustless, peaceful <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_32.170 //

children.text: (Vaidya 207)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 207)

children.text: ye karmasthānā tathariva śilpasthānā bhaiṣajyasthānāstathariva auṣadhīnām /
children.translated_text: 'In the fields of <s>karma</s>, in the fields of arts, in the fields of medicine, and of healing herbs —

children.text: sarvatra dhīro bhaviṣyati pāraprāpto dhāritva sūtraṃ imu virajaṃ samādhim // SRS_32.171 //
children.translated_text: in all things the wise one shall have gone to the far shore — having upheld this dustless <s>sūtra-samādhi</s>! // SRS_32.171 //

children.text: kāvyeṣu śāstreṣu tathapi ca hāsyalāsye nṛtye 'tha gīte sukuśala pāraprāptaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In poetry, in treatises, in comedy and dance, in <s>nṛtya</s> (dramatic dance) and song — supremely skilled, gone to perfection;

children.text: ācāryu loke bhaviṣyati nityakālaṃ dhāritva śāntaṃ imu virajaṃ samādhim // SRS_32.172 //
children.translated_text: he shall be a teacher in the world at all times — having upheld this peaceful, dustless <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_32.172 //

children.text: parivāravān so bhaviṣyati nityakālaṃ sa abhedyapakṣaḥ sada sahitaḥ samagraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He shall always have a retinue, with an unbreakable faction, always united and complete,

children.text: caramāṇu śreṣṭhāṃ varāṃ śiva bodhicaryāṃ dhāritva sūtraṃ imu virajaṃ samādhim // SRS_32.173 //
children.translated_text: practicing the supreme, excellent, auspicious conduct of awakening — having upheld this dustless <s>sūtra-samādhi</s>! // SRS_32.173 //

children.text: śokātha śalyā tathariva cittapīḍā no tasya jātu bhaviṣyati paṇḍitasya /
children.translated_text: 'Grief, thorns [of sorrow], and mental anguish shall never arise for that wise one;

children.text: ārogyaprāpto bhaviṣyati sarvakālaṃ dhāritva śāntaṃ imu virajaṃ samādhim // SRS_32.174 //
children.translated_text: he shall be one who has attained health at all times — having upheld this peaceful, dustless <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_32.174 //

children.text: ye kāyaśūlāstathariva cittaśūlāḥ ye dantaśūlāstathapi ca śīrṣaśūlāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever bodily pains, mental pains, toothaches, and headaches there may be —

children.text: no tasya bhontī vyādhayu jīvaloke dhāritva śāntaṃ imu virajaṃ samādhim // SRS_32.175 //
children.translated_text: no diseases of the living world shall arise for him — having upheld this peaceful, dustless <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_32.175 //

children.text: yāvanta rogā bahuvidha martaloke ye kāyarogāstathariva cittarogāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever numerous diseases exist in the mortal world — diseases of body, diseases of mind —

children.text: te tasya rogāḥ satata na jātu bhonti dhāritva śāntaṃ imu virajaṃ samādhim // SRS_32.176 //
children.translated_text: those diseases shall never arise for him — having upheld this peaceful, dustless <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_32.176 //

children.text: cittasya vā ye bahuvidhu yatkileśāḥ kāye vāpi bahuvidha rogajātāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever numerous afflictions of the mind, and whatever numerous diseases born in the body —

children.text: te tasya nāstī bahuvidha saṃkileśā dhāritva śāntaṃ imu viraja samādhim // SRS_32.177 //
children.translated_text: those numerous defilements do not exist for him — having upheld this peaceful, dustless <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_32.177 //

children.text: yathantarīkṣaṃ gaganamanopaliptaṃ prakṛtiviśuddhaṃ vimala prabhāsvaraṃ ca /
