children.translated_text: 'Just as the sky, the firmament, is unstained, pure by nature, stainless, and radiant —

children.text: (Vaidya 208)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 208)

children.text: cittaṃ tathaiva bhavati viśuddha tasyo dhāritva śāntaṃ imu virajaṃ samādhim // SRS_32.178 //
children.translated_text: so too his mind becomes purified — having upheld this peaceful, dustless <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_32.178 //

children.text: candrasya ābhā tathariva sūryaābhā śuddhā agrāhyā bhavati prabhāsvarāśca /
children.translated_text: 'Just as the radiance of the moon and the radiance of the sun are pure, ungraspable, and luminous —

children.text: cittaṃ tathaiva bhavati prabhāsvaraṃ ca dhāritva śāntaṃ imu virajaṃ samādhim // SRS_32.179 //
children.translated_text: so too his mind becomes luminous — having upheld this peaceful, dustless <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_32.179 //

children.text: yatha antarīkṣaṃ na sukaru citraṇāya raṅgān gṛhītvā bahuvidha naikarūpān /
children.translated_text: 'Just as the sky cannot easily be painted upon, though one takes paints of various manifold colors —

children.text: cittaṃ tathaiva na sukaru citrituṃ sevetva śāntaṃ imu virajaṃ samādhim // SRS_32.180 //
children.translated_text: so too the mind cannot easily be stained — for one who cultivates this peaceful, dustless <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_32.180 //

children.text: vāto yathaiva caturdiśa vāyamāno asajjamāno vrajati diśaḥ samantāt /
children.translated_text: 'Just as the wind, blowing from the four directions, travels in all directions without attachment —

children.text: vātasamānā bhavati sa cittadhārā jagi so asakto vrajati anopaliptaḥ // SRS_32.181 //
children.translated_text: like the wind is his stream of mind — he moves through the world unattached, unstained! // SRS_32.181 //

children.text: jālena śakyaṃ gṛhṇitu vāyamānaḥ pāśena cāpī bandhitu śakya vātaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'One could catch the blowing wind in a net, or bind the wind with a rope —

children.text: no tasya cittaṃ sukaru vijānanāya bhāvetva śāntamimu virajaṃ samādhim // SRS_32.182 //
children.translated_text: but his mind cannot easily be known — for one who has cultivated this peaceful, dustless <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_32.182 //

children.text: pratibhāsu śakyaṃ jalagata gṛhṇanāya saṃprāptu toyaṃ tathapi ca tailapātre /
children.translated_text: 'One could grasp a reflection in water, or obtain water in an oil-pot —

children.text: no tasya cittaṃ sukaru vijānanāya bhāvetva śāntaṃ imu virajaṃ samādhim // SRS_32.183 //
children.translated_text: but his mind cannot easily be known — for one who has cultivated this peaceful, dustless <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_32.183 //

children.text: garjanti meghā vidyulatā carantā śakyaṃ grahītu pāṇina mānuṣeṇa /
children.translated_text: 'Clouds rumble, lightning flashes — one could grasp [lightning] with a human hand —

children.text: no tasya cittaṃ sukaru pramāṇu jñātuṃ bhāvetva śāntaṃ imu virajaṃ samādhim // SRS_32.184 //
children.translated_text: but his mind's measure cannot easily be known — for one who has cultivated this peaceful, dustless <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_32.184 //

children.text: sattvāna śakyaṃ rūtaravitaṃ grahītuṃ ye santi sattvā daśadiśi buddhakṣetra /
children.translated_text: 'One could grasp the cries and calls of beings — all beings in the ten directions of the <s>Buddha</s>-fields —

children.text: cittasya tasyo na sukaru jñātu koṭiṃ samādhilabdho yada bhavi bodhisattvaḥ // SRS_32.185 //
children.translated_text: but the limit of his mind cannot easily be known — when a <s>Bodhisattva</s> has attained the <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_32.185 //

children.text: (Vaidya 209)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 209)

children.text: so tāṃ labhitva virajaṃ samādhibhūmiṃ asaṃṃkiliṣṭo bhavati anopaliptaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having obtained that dustless ground of <s>samādhi</s>, he becomes undefiled and unstained;

children.text: no tasya bhūyo tribhavi niveśa jātu anena labdho bhavati samādhi śāntaḥ // SRS_32.196 //
children.translated_text: he shall never again have an abode in the three realms — by him this peaceful <s>samādhi</s> has been obtained! // SRS_32.196 //

children.text: no kāmalolo na ca puna rūpalolo na istrilolo na ca puna bhrāntacittaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Not lustful for sensual pleasures, not lustful for form, not lustful for women, not of confused mind —

children.text: śāntaḥ praśānto bhavati anopalipto yada bhoti labdho ayu virajaḥ samādhiḥ // SRS_32.187 //
children.translated_text: peaceful, tranquil, he becomes unstained — when this dustless <s>samādhi</s> has been obtained! // SRS_32.187 //

children.text: na putralolo na ca puna dhītalolo no bhāryalolo na ca parivāralolaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Not longing for sons, not longing for daughters, not longing for a wife, not longing for retinue —

children.text: suśāntacārī bhavati anopalipto yada bhoti labdho ayu virajaḥ samādhiḥ // SRS_32.188 //
children.translated_text: of well-tranquilized conduct, he becomes unstained — when this dustless <s>samādhi</s> has been obtained! // SRS_32.188 //

children.text: na hiraṇyalolo na ca punararthalolo na svargalolo dhanarataneṣvasaktaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Not longing for gold, not longing for possessions, not longing for heaven, unattached to wealth and jewels —

children.text: suviśuddhacitto bhavati sa nirvikalpaḥ samādhiprāpto ayu bhavatī viśeṣaḥ // SRS_32.189 //
children.translated_text: his mind becomes supremely purified, free from conceptual construction — one who has attained the <s>samādhi</s>, this becomes his distinction! // SRS_32.189 //

body.text:
na svargahetoścarati sa brahmacaryaṃ na svargalolo dadati sadā nu vijñaḥ /
saṃbodhikāmaḥ kuśalacariṃ carantaḥ | samādhiprāpto ayu bhavatī viśeṣaḥ // SRS_32.190 //
body.translated_text: 'He does not practice the holy life for the sake of heaven; the wise one does not give out of longing for heaven; practicing wholesome conduct, desiring <s>saṃbodhi</s> — one who has attained the <s>samādhi</s>, this becomes his distinction! // SRS_32.190 //

children.text: no rājyahetoścarati tapo vrataṃ vā naiśvaryamarthāstribhuvani prārthamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He does not practice austerities or vows for the sake of kingship, nor does he desire sovereignty, possessions, or power in the three worlds;

children.text: saṃbodhilolo bahujanahitāya niṣpādayī so imu virajaṃ samādhim // SRS_32.191 //
children.translated_text: longing for <s>saṃbodhi</s>, for the benefit of the many — he shall accomplish this dustless <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_32.191 //

children.text: no tasya rāgo janayati jātu pīḍāṃ yo na strīlolo so bhavati bhrāntacittaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Passion never generates affliction for him — one who is not lustful for women and whose mind is not confused —

children.text: tathāpi tena prakṛtiprajñāya rāgo labhitva etaṃ viraju samādhi śāntam // SRS_32.192 //
children.translated_text: for by his innate wisdom, passion [is overcome] — having obtained this dustless, peaceful <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_32.192 //

children.text: no tasya doṣo janayati jātu pīḍāṃ vyāpādu yeno pratighamatho kareyya /
children.translated_text: 'Hatred never generates affliction for him — whereby one might produce ill-will and enmity;

children.text: (Vaidya 210)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 210)

children.text: maitrāya teno nihata sa doṣadhātu pratilabhya etaṃ viraju samādhi śāntam // SRS_32.193 //
children.translated_text: through loving-kindness, that element of hatred has been destroyed by him — having obtained this dustless, peaceful <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_32.193 //

children.text: no tasya moho janayati jātu pīḍāṃ prajñāya teno nihata sa moha avidyā /
children.translated_text: 'Delusion never generates affliction for him — through wisdom, that delusion and ignorance have been destroyed by him;

children.text: taṃ jñānu labdhaṃ vitimiramaprameyaṃ samādhiprāpte imi guṇa aprameyāḥ // SRS_32.194 //
children.translated_text: that knowledge is obtained, dispelling darkness, immeasurable — for one who has attained the <s>samādhi</s>, these virtues are immeasurable! // SRS_32.194 //

children.text: aśubhāya rāgaḥ satata sunigṛhīto maitryāya doṣo nihatu sadā aśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'By the contemplation of the unbeautiful, passion is constantly well-restrained; by loving-kindness, hatred is always destroyed without remainder;

children.text: prajñāya moho vidhamiya kleśajālaṃ samādhiprāptaḥ pratapati sarvaloke // SRS_32.195 //
children.translated_text: by wisdom, having dispelled delusion and the net of afflictions — the one who has attained the <s>samādhi</s> blazes in the entire world! // SRS_32.195 //

children.text: no tasya middhaṃ janayati jātu pīḍāṃ subhāvitā se vividha utkileśāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Sloth never generates affliction for him — the various secondary afflictions are well-cultivated [i.e., well-overcome] by him —'

children.text: anopalipto bhavati ca vipramuktaḥ samādhiprāpte imi guṇa aprameyāḥ // SRS_32.196 //
children.translated_text: untainted and liberated — upon attaining the <s>samādhi</s>, these qualities are immeasurable. // SRS_32.196 //

children.text: no tasya moho janayati jātu pīḍāṃ tathā hi tyāge abhiratu nityakālam /
children.translated_text: "Delusion never generates affliction for him, for he always delights in renunciation;

children.text: sarvasvatyāgī bhavati sukhasya dātā ya imaṃ samādhiṃ dhārayati bodhisattvaḥ // SRS_32.197 //
children.translated_text: he becomes a relinquisher of all, a giver of happiness — the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_32.197 //

children.text: sthāmenupeto bhavati anopameyo sa balenupeto bhavati nityakālam /
children.translated_text: "He becomes endowed with incomparable stamina; he is always endowed with power;

children.text: no tasya loke bhavati samaḥ kadācid ya imaṃ samādhiṃ dhārayati bodhisattvaḥ // SRS_32.198 //
children.translated_text: there is never one equal to him in the world — the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who upholds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_32.198 //

children.text: yadāpi rājā sa bhavati cakravartīṃ manujānu loke upagata jambudvīpe /
children.translated_text: "When he becomes a <s>Cakravartin</s> king, arrived among men in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>,

children.text: tadāpi bhotī bahujanapūjanīyo viśeṣaprāpto matima viśiṣṭaprajñaḥ // SRS_32.199 //
children.translated_text: even then he is worthy of the worship of many people — one who has attained distinction, wise, of distinguished wisdom. // SRS_32.199 //

children.text: ye bhonti mukhyāḥ kularatanā viśiṣṭāḥ suprabhūtabhogā bahujanasvāpateyāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Those who are chief, distinguished jewels of families, of very abundant wealth, possessing the property of many people,

children.text: yatrāśva hastī rathavara yugyayānā hiraṇyasvarṇaṃ maṇīratanaṃ prabhūtam // SRS_32.200 //
children.translated_text: where there are horses, elephants, excellent chariots and vehicles, and abundant gold and jewel-gems — // SRS_32.200 //

children.text: (Vaidya 211)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 211)

children.text: ye śrāddha bhontī iha varabuddhajñāne te jambudvīpe kularatanābhiyuktāḥ /
children.translated_text: "those who have faith here in the excellent <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge — they are endowed with family jewels in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>;

children.text: tatropapannaḥ kularatane viśiṣṭe karoti so 'rthaṃ suvipula jñātisaṃghe // SRS_32.201 //
children.translated_text: born there in a distinguished family-jewel, he accomplishes vast welfare for the assembly of relatives. // SRS_32.201 //

children.text: aśrāddha ye vā iha kula jambudvipe śraddhāṃ sa teṣāṃ janayati apramattaḥ /
children.translated_text: "And those in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> who are without faith — he vigilantly generates faith in them;

children.text: yaṃ bodhicitte pratiṣṭhiti sattvakāye te buddha bhontī jinapravaraḥ svayaṃbhūḥ // SRS_32.202 //
children.translated_text: those whom he establishes in the thought of awakening among the body of beings — they become Buddhas, supreme self-arisen <s>Jinas</s>. // SRS_32.202 //

children.text: te ca spṛśitva atuliyamagrabodhiṃ cakraṃ pravartentyasadṛśa buddhakṣetre /
children.translated_text: "And having touched the incomparable, supreme awakening, they turn the wheel in incomparable <s>Buddha</s>-fields;

children.text: ye co vijānī imu tada dharmacakraṃ anutpattidharme nikhila te saṃpratiṣṭhī // SRS_32.203 //
children.translated_text: and those who then understand this <s>Dharma</s>-wheel — they are completely established in the patient acceptance of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s>. // SRS_32.203 //

children.text: subahukarāśco ami tada bodhisattvāḥ sattvāna bhonti satatu te pūjanīyāḥ /
children.translated_text: "And those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are then of great service; always worthy of worship by beings;

children.text: karonti te 'rthaṃ atuliya nityakālaṃ sattvāna cakṣurvitimiru te janenti // SRS_32.204 //
children.translated_text: they accomplish incomparable welfare always for beings; they generate the eye [of wisdom] that dispels darkness. // SRS_32.204 //

children.text: bahava śatasahasrāḥ sattvakoṭī anantā yeṣa kuśalamūlā bhonti tatra śruṇitvā /
children.translated_text: "Many hundreds of thousands — inconceivable <s>koṭis</s> of beings — whose roots of merit exist there, having heard,

children.text: te api pratilabhante uttamaṃ bodhicittaṃ yada jinu anuśāsī bodhisattvaṃ mahātmā // SRS_32.205 //
children.translated_text: they too attain the supreme thought of awakening — when the <s>Jina</s>, the great soul, instructs the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. // SRS_32.205 //

children.text: aśūnyakṣetrā pramudita bhonti nityaṃ nirupalepā ami tada buddha bhontī /
children.translated_text: "Their fields are never empty; they are always joyful; those Buddhas are then without defilement;

children.text: yatra sthihantī imi tada bodhisattvāḥ sattvānamartha aparimitaṃ karonti // SRS_32.206 //
children.translated_text: wherever those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are established, they accomplish immeasurable welfare for beings. // SRS_32.206 //

children.text: rakṣanti śīlaṃ asadṛśu brahmacaryaṃ bhāvī samādhī vipulamanantakalpān /
children.translated_text: "They guard morality — the incomparable holy life; they cultivate <s>samādhi</s>, vast, for incalculable <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: dhyāne vimokṣe suniśrita nityakālaṃ te bodhisattvā bhavi sada buddhaputrāḥ // SRS_32.207 //
children.translated_text: always well-established in <s>dhyāna</s> and liberations — those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are always sons of the <s>Buddha</s> in existence. // SRS_32.207 //

children.text: te ṛddhipādān satat niṣevamāṇā kṣetrāṇi gatvā bahu vividhānanantān /
children.translated_text: "They constantly cultivate the bases of <s>ṛddhi</s>; having gone to many various infinite fields,

children.text: (Vaidya 212)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 212)

children.text: śṛṇvanti dharmaṃ sugatavaraprabhāṣaṃ sarvaṃ ca gṛhṇī pratiṣṭhitu dhāraṇīye // SRS_32.208 //
children.translated_text: they hear the <s>Dharma</s> proclaimed by the supreme <s>Sugatas</s>; they grasp all of it and establish [themselves] in <s>dhāraṇī</s>. // SRS_32.208 //

children.text: prabhāṣi sūtrānaparimitānanantān ye dhāraṇīye pratiṣṭhitu bodhisattvāḥ /
children.translated_text: "They proclaim immeasurable, infinite <s>sūtras</s> — those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> established in <s>dhāraṇī</s>;

children.text: sattvāna arthaṃ aparimitaṃ karonti ye dhāraṇīye pratiṣṭhitu bodhisattvāḥ // SRS_32.209 //
children.translated_text: they accomplish immeasurable welfare for beings — those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> established in <s>dhāraṇī</s>. // SRS_32.209 //

children.text: cyutopapādaṃ jānāti sattvānāmāgatiṃ gatim /
children.translated_text: "He knows the death and rebirth of beings, their coming and going;

children.text: yādṛśaṃ taiḥ kṛtaṃ karma vipāko 'pi ca tādṛśaḥ // SRS_32.210 //
children.translated_text: whatever <s>karma</s> they have done, such is its corresponding fruit. // SRS_32.210 //

children.text: karmaṇo na ca saṃkrāntiraṇumātrāṇi labhyate /
children.translated_text: "Not even an atomic transfer of <s>karma</s> is found;

children.text: te 'pi teṣāṃ vijānanti bodhisattvā mahāyaśāḥ // SRS_32.211 //
children.translated_text: those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of great fame also know this [about beings]. // SRS_32.211 //

children.text: śūnyatā ca mahātmānāṃ vihāro bhoti uttamaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Emptiness is the supreme dwelling of those great beings;

children.text: sthāpayanti mahāyāne sattvakoṭīracintiyāḥ // SRS_32.212 //
children.translated_text: they establish inconceivable <s>koṭis</s> of beings in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. // SRS_32.212 //

children.text: na teṣāmovadantānāṃ sattvasaṃjñā pravartate /
children.translated_text: "When they instruct, the perception of 'being' does not operate in them;

children.text: apravṛttiṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ bodhisattvāḥ prakāśayī // SRS_32.213 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> illuminate the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s>. // SRS_32.213 //

children.text: na prakāśayatāṃ dharmāṇupalambhaḥ pravartate /
children.translated_text: "For those who illuminate <s>dharmas</s>, the apprehension [of real existence] does not operate;

children.text: śūnyāvihāriṇo bhonti dṛḍhajñāne pratiṣṭhitāḥ // SRS_32.214 //
children.translated_text: they dwell in emptiness, established in firm knowledge. // SRS_32.214 //

children.text: uddiśyemaṃ samādhiṃ ca vihāraṃ sarvaśāstunām /
children.translated_text: "Pointing to this <s>samādhi</s> — the dwelling of all Teachers —

children.text: na teṣāṃ vartate saṃjñā istrisaṃjñā svabhāvatā // SRS_32.215 //
children.translated_text: the perception does not operate in them; the perception of 'woman' has no inherent nature. // SRS_32.215 //

children.text: istrisaṃjñāṃ vibhāvitvā bodhimaṇḍe niṣīdati /
children.translated_text: "Having discerned the perception of 'woman' [as unreal], he sits at the seat of awakening;

children.text: bodhimaṇḍe niṣiditvā mārasaṃjñā nivartate // SRS_32.216 //
children.translated_text: having sat at the seat of awakening, the perception of '<s>Māra</s>' is turned back. // SRS_32.216 //

children.text: na cātra paśyate māraṃ mārasainyaṃ ca paṇḍitaḥ /
children.translated_text: "The wise one does not see <s>Māra</s> here, nor <s>Māra</s>'s army;

children.text: na ca paśyati mārasya tisro duhitaro 'pi saḥ // SRS_32.217 //
children.translated_text: nor does he see <s>Māra</s>'s three daughters. // SRS_32.217 //

children.text: bodhimaṇḍe niṣaṇṇasya sarvasaṃjñā prahīyate /
children.translated_text: "For one seated at the seat of awakening, all perceptions are abandoned;

children.text: saervasaṃjñāprahīṇasya sarvā kampati medinī // SRS_32.218 //
children.translated_text: when all perceptions are abandoned, the entire earth trembles. // SRS_32.218 //

children.text: sumeravaḥ samudrāśca yāva santi daśā diśe /
children.translated_text: "The <s>Sumerus</s> and the oceans — as many as there are in the ten directions —

children.text: taṃ ca sattvā vijānanti sarvadikṣu daśasvapi // SRS_32.219 //
children.translated_text: and beings know this [trembling] in all ten directions. // SRS_32.219 //

children.text: bodhisattvasya ṛddhyeyaṃ medinī saṃprakampitā /
children.translated_text: "By the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>ṛddhi</s>, the earth is shaken;

children.text: ṣaḍvikāraṃ tadā kāle budhyato bodhimuttamām // SRS_32.220 //
children.translated_text: in six ways at that time, as he awakens to the supreme <s>bodhi</s>. // SRS_32.220 //

children.text: yāvantaḥ saṃskṛtā dharmā ye ca dharmā asaṃskṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Whatever <s>dharmas</s> are conditioned, and whatever <s>dharmas</s> are unconditioned —

children.text: sarvāṃstān budhyate dharmān dharmaśabdena deśitān // SRS_32.221 //
children.translated_text: he awakens to all those <s>dharmas</s>, taught by the word '<s>dharma</s>.' // SRS_32.221 //

children.text: (Vaidya 213)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 213)

children.text: na cātra budhyate kaścit siṃhanādaśca vartate /
children.translated_text: "Yet no one awakens here — and the lion's roar occurs;

children.text: vartanīyaṃ vijānitvā bhoti buddhaḥ prabhākaraḥ // SRS_32.222 //
children.translated_text: knowing what is to be taught, he becomes a <s>Buddha</s>, a Light-Maker. // SRS_32.222 //

children.text: pratītya dharmā vartante utpadyante pratītya ca /
children.translated_text: "<s>Dharmas</s> arise dependently; they arise in dependence;

children.text: pratītyatāṃ yaddharmāṇāṃ sarve jānanti te viduḥ // SRS_32.223 //
children.translated_text: those wise ones who know the dependent nature of <s>dharmas</s> — they know all. // SRS_32.223 //

children.text: vidhijñāḥ sarvadharmeṣu śūnyatāyā gatiṃgatāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Knowers of method in all <s>dharmas</s>, having reached the course of emptiness,

children.text: gatiṃ ca te prajānanti sarvadharmagatiṃgatāḥ // SRS_32.224 //
children.translated_text: they know the course — having reached the course of all <s>dharmas</s>. // SRS_32.224 //

children.text: gatimetāṃ gaveṣitvā bodhisattvo na labhyate /
children.translated_text: "Having sought this course, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is not found [as a self];

children.text: yenaiṣā sarvabuddhānāṃ jñātā gatiracintiyā // SRS_32.225 //
children.translated_text: by this, the inconceivable course of all Buddhas is known. // SRS_32.225 //

children.text: sa tāṃ gatiṃ gato bhoti yaḥ sarvāṃ gati jānati /
children.translated_text: "He has gone to that course — he who knows all courses;

children.text: sarvasya māyā ucchinnā jñātvā saddharmalakṣaṇam // SRS_32.226 //
children.translated_text: all illusion is cut off, having known the characteristic of the true <s>Dharma</s>. // SRS_32.226 //

children.text: bodhimaṇḍe niṣīditvā siṃhanādaṃ nadī tathā /
children.translated_text: "Having sat at the seat of awakening, he roars the lion's roar;

children.text: vijñāpayī kṣetrakoṭīraprameyā acintiyāḥ // SRS_32.227 //
children.translated_text: he illuminates immeasurable, inconceivable <s>koṭis</s> of fields. // SRS_32.227 //

children.text: tāṃśca prakampayī sarvā buddhavīrā mahāyaśāḥ /
children.translated_text: "He causes them all to tremble — that <s>Buddha</s>-hero of great fame —

children.text: yatha vainayikān sattvān vinetī sattvasārathiḥ // SRS_32.228 //
children.translated_text: just as the tamer of beings tames those beings who are to be tamed. // SRS_32.228 //

children.text: spṛśitvā uttamāṃ bodhiṃ bodhimaṇḍāttu utthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Having touched the supreme awakening, having risen from the seat of awakening,

children.text: vineyān vinayet sattvānaprameyānacintiyān // SRS_32.229 //
children.translated_text: he would tame immeasurable, inconceivable beings who are to be tamed. // SRS_32.229 //

children.text: tato nirmiṇi saṃbuddho anantān buddhanirmitān /
children.translated_text: "Then the Perfectly Awakened One creates infinite <s>Buddha</s>-emanations;

children.text: kṣetrakoṭīsahasrāṇi gacchantī dharmadeśakāḥ // SRS_32.230 //
children.translated_text: they go to thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of fields — teachers of <s>Dharma</s>. // SRS_32.230 //

children.text: sthāpayantyagrabodhīye sattvakoṭīracintiyāḥ /
children.translated_text: "They establish inconceivable <s>koṭis</s> of beings in the supreme awakening;

children.text: deśayantyuttamaṃ dharmaṃ hitārthaṃ sarvaprāṇinām // SRS_32.231 //
children.translated_text: they teach the supreme <s>Dharma</s> for the benefit of all living beings. // SRS_32.231 //

children.text: īdṛśaṃ tanmahājñānaṃ buddhajñānamacintiyam /
children.translated_text: "Such is that great knowledge — inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge;

children.text: tasmājjanayatha cchandaṃ bodhicchandamanuttaram // SRS_32.232 //
children.translated_text: therefore generate zeal — the unsurpassed zeal for awakening! // SRS_32.232 //

children.text: janetha gauravaṃ buddhe dharme saṃghe guṇottame /
children.translated_text: "Generate respect for the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṅgha</s> of supreme qualities,

children.text: bodhisattvāna śūrāṇāṃ bodhimagryāṃ niṣevatām // SRS_32.233 //
children.translated_text: and for the heroic <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who cultivate the supreme awakening! // SRS_32.233 //

children.text: anolīnena cittena satkarotha atandritāḥ /
children.translated_text: "With an unshrunken mind, honor [them] unwearied;

children.text: bhaviṣyatha tato buddhā nacireṇa prabhākarāḥ // SRS_32.234 //
children.translated_text: you will thereafter quickly become Buddhas, Light-Makers! // SRS_32.234 //

children.text: ye ca kṣetrasahasreṣu bodhisattvā ihāgatāḥ /
children.translated_text: "And the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have come here from thousands of fields

children.text: paśyanti lokapradyotaṃ dharmaṃ deśentamuttamam // SRS_32.235 //
children.translated_text: behold the Illuminator of the World teaching the supreme <s>Dharma</s>. // SRS_32.235 //

children.text: okiranti mahāvīrā mahāratnehi nāyakam /
children.translated_text: "Those Great Heroes shower the Leader with great jewels

children.text: māndāravehi puṣpehi okirī bodhikāraṇāt // SRS_32.236 //
children.translated_text: and with <s>Māndārava</s> flowers — for the sake of awakening. // SRS_32.236 //

children.text: (Vaidya 214)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 214)

children.text: alaṃkarontidaṃ kṣetraṃ buddhakṣetramanuttaram /
children.translated_text: "They adorn this field — this unsurpassed <s>Buddha</s>-field;

children.text: ratnajālena cchādenti samantena diśo daśa // SRS_32.237 //
children.translated_text: they cover it with a jewel-net all around in the ten directions. // SRS_32.237 //

children.text: patākā avasaktāśca ucchritā dhvajakoṭayaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Pennants are hung and <s>koṭis</s> of banners raised;

children.text: alaṃkārairanantaiśca idaṃ kṣetramalaṃkṛtam // SRS_32.238 //
children.translated_text: with infinite ornaments, this field is adorned. // SRS_32.238 //

children.text: kūṭāgārāṃśca māpenti sarvaratnavicitritān /
children.translated_text: "They create pavilions inlaid with all jewels,

children.text: prāsādaharmyaniryūhānasaṃkhyeyān manoramān // SRS_32.239 //
children.translated_text: palaces, mansions, and balconies — innumerable and delightful. // SRS_32.239 //

children.text: vimānānyardhacadrāṃśca gavākṣān pañjarāṃstathā /
children.translated_text: "Celestial chariots, half-moons, windows, and lattices,

children.text: dhūpitā dhvajaghaṭikā nānāratnavicitritāḥ // SRS_32.240 //
children.translated_text: incensed banner-pots inlaid with various jewels. // SRS_32.240 //

children.text: dhūpyamānena gandhena abhrakūṭasamaṃ sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: "With the incense being burned, like a mass of clouds it fills [the sky];

children.text: kṣetrakoṭīsahasreṣu vāti gandho manoramaḥ // SRS_32.241 //
children.translated_text: in thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of fields, a delightful fragrance wafts. // SRS_32.241 //

children.text: te ca sarve spharitvāna gandhavarṣaṃ pravarṣiṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: "And all of them, having pervaded [space], rain down a rain of fragrance;

children.text: ye ca ghrāyanti taṃ gandhaṃ te buddhā bhonti nāyakāḥ // SRS_32.242 //
children.translated_text: those who smell that fragrance — they become Buddhas, Leaders. // SRS_32.242 //

children.text: rāgaśalyaṃ prahīṇaiṣāṃ doṣaśalyaṃ na vidyate /
children.translated_text: "The arrow of passion is abandoned in them; the arrow of hatred does not exist;

children.text: vidhvaṃsitaṃ mohajālaṃ tamaḥ sarvaṃ vigacchati // SRS_32.243 //
children.translated_text: the net of delusion is destroyed; all darkness departs. // SRS_32.243 //

children.text: ṛddhiṃ ca tatra sparśenti balabodhyaṅga indriyān /
children.translated_text: "And there they touch <s>ṛddhi</s>, the powers, awakening-factors, and faculties;

children.text: dhyānavimokṣān sparśenti bhonti co dakṣiṇārhāḥ // SRS_32.244 //
children.translated_text: they touch <s>dhyānas</s> and liberations; and they become worthy of offerings. // SRS_32.244 //

children.text: pañcakoṭīya prajñaptā vastrakoṭībhi saṃstṛtā /
children.translated_text: "Five <s>koṭis</s> [of seats] are prepared, covered with <s>koṭis</s> of fabrics,

children.text: saṃchannā ratnajālehi cchatrakoṭībhi citritāḥ // SRS_32.245 //
children.translated_text: canopied with jewel-nets, adorned with <s>koṭis</s> of parasols. // SRS_32.245 //

children.text: niṣaṇṇāstatra te śūrā bodhisattvāḥ samāgatāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Those heroes, the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have assembled, sit there;

children.text: lakṣaṇaiste virocante tathānuvyañjanairapi // SRS_32.246 //
children.translated_text: they shine with [major] marks and also with [minor] characteristics. // SRS_32.246 //

children.text: vṛkṣai ratnamayaiḥ sarvaṃ buddhakṣetramalaṃkṛtam /
children.translated_text: "With trees made of jewels, the entire <s>Buddha</s>-field is adorned;

children.text: nirmitāḥ puṣkariṇyaśca aṣṭāṅgajalapūritāḥ // SRS_32.247 //
children.translated_text: created lotus-ponds filled with water of eight qualities [appear]. // SRS_32.247 //

children.text: pānīyaṃ te tataḥ pītvā puṣkariṇītaṭe sthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Having drunk water from those [ponds], standing on the bank of the lotus-pool,

children.text: sarve tṛṣṇāṃ vinoditvā bhonti lokasya cetiyāḥ // SRS_32.248 //
children.translated_text: they all, having removed craving, become shrines for the world. // SRS_32.248 //

children.text: anyonyeṣu ca kṣetreṣu bodhisattvāḥ samāgatāḥ /
children.translated_text: "And in one another's fields, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> have assembled;

children.text: buddhasya varṇaṃ bhāṣante śākyasiṃhasya tāyinaḥ // SRS_32.249 //
children.translated_text: they speak the praise of the <s>Buddha</s>, the Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>, the Protector. // SRS_32.249 //

children.text: śṛṇvanti ye ca taṃ varṇaṃ te bhontī lokanāyakāḥ /
children.translated_text: "And those who hear that praise — they become World-Leaders;

children.text: acintyā anuśaṃsā me iha sūtre prakāśitāḥ // SRS_32.250 //
children.translated_text: the inconceivable benefits [of this text] have been proclaimed by me in this <s>sūtra</s>. // SRS_32.250 //

children.text: svarṇamayehi patrehi padmakoṭyo acintiyāḥ /
children.translated_text: "With golden petals, inconceivable <s>koṭis</s> of lotuses,

children.text: śuddhasyoragasārasya karṇikāstatra nirmitāḥ // SRS_32.251 //
children.translated_text: with seed-pods of pure <s>nāga</s>-essence are created there. // SRS_32.251 //

children.text: (Vaidya 215)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 215)

children.text: vaiḍūryasya ca daṇḍāni sphaṭikasya ca pañjarāḥ /
children.translated_text: "With stems of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> and lattices of crystal,

children.text: kesarā girigarbhasya māpitāstatra śobhanāḥ // SRS_32.252 //
children.translated_text: with filaments of mountain-crystal — beautifully fashioned there. // SRS_32.252 //

children.text: ye ca ghrāyanti taṃ gandhaṃ niścarantaṃ manoramam /
children.translated_text: "Those who smell the delightful fragrance issuing forth —

children.text: teṣāṃ sarve praśāmyanti vyādhayaḥ prītacetasām // SRS_32.253 //
children.translated_text: all their diseases are pacified; their minds are filled with joy. // SRS_32.253 //

children.text: rāgo dveṣaśca mohaśca aśeṣāstehi kṣīyate /
children.translated_text: "Passion, hatred, and delusion are completely exhausted in them;

children.text: trīn doṣān kṣapayitvā ca bhonti buddhā sukhaṃdadāḥ // SRS_32.254 //
children.translated_text: having destroyed the three faults, they become Buddhas, givers of happiness. // SRS_32.254 //

children.text: śabdastato niścarati buddhaśabdo hyacintiyaḥ /
children.translated_text: "From there issues forth a sound — the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-sound;

children.text: saddharmasaṃghaśabdaśca viniścarati sarvataḥ // SRS_32.255 //
children.translated_text: and the sound of the true <s>Dharma</s> and the <s>Saṅgha</s> issues forth everywhere. // SRS_32.255 //

children.text: śūnyatā animittasya svaro apraṇihitasya ca /
children.translated_text: "The sound of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness —

children.text: śrutvā taṃ sattvakoṭīyo bhontivaivartikā bahu // SRS_32.256 //
children.translated_text: hearing that, many <s>koṭis</s> of beings become non-retrogressing. // SRS_32.256 //

children.text: niścaraṃścaiva śabdo 'sau kṣetrakoṭīṣu gacchati /
children.translated_text: "And that issuing sound travels to <s>koṭis</s> of fields;

children.text: sthāpenti buddhajñānasmin sattvakoṭīracintiyāḥ // SRS_32.257 //
children.translated_text: they establish inconceivable <s>koṭis</s> of beings in <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. // SRS_32.257 //

children.text: śakuntā kalaviṅkāśca jīvaṃjīvakapakṣiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Birds, <s>kalaviṅkas</s>, and <s>jīvaṃjīvaka</s> birds —

children.text: te 'pi pravyāharī śabdaṃ buddhaśabdamanuttaram // SRS_32.258 //
children.translated_text: even they utter the sound — the unsurpassed <s>Buddha</s>-sound. // SRS_32.258 //

children.text: ratnāmayāśca te vṛkṣā iha kṣetrasmi nirmitāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Trees made of jewels are created here in this field;

children.text: viśiṣṭā darśanīyāśca maṇīvṛkṣā manoramā // SRS_32.259 //
children.translated_text: distinguished, beautiful to behold, gem-trees — delightful. // SRS_32.259 //

children.text: lambante teṣu vṛkṣeṣu sarvābharaṇaveṇayaḥ /
children.translated_text: "From those trees hang garlands of every ornament;

children.text: anubhāvena buddhasya iha kṣetrasmi nirmitāḥ // SRS_32.260 //
children.translated_text: by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, they are created here in this field. // SRS_32.260 //

children.text: na so 'sti keṣucid vyūhaḥ sarvakṣetreṣu sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: "There is no display in any other field whatsoever, in any direction,

children.text: yo neha dṛśyate kṣetre tadviśiṣṭatamastadā // SRS_32.261 //
children.translated_text: that is not seen here in this field — and here it is most distinguished. // SRS_32.261 //

children.text: peyālametadākhyātaṃ śākyasiṃhena tāyinā /
children.translated_text: "This has been declared in abbreviated form by the Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>, the Protector;

children.text: na te jñāne 'tra kāṅkṣati bodhisatvā mahāyaśāḥ // SRS_32.262 //
children.translated_text: those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of great fame do not doubt this knowledge. // SRS_32.262 //

children.text: koṭīya etāṃ budhyanti gatisteṣāmacintiyā /
children.translated_text: "They awaken to these <s>koṭis</s> [of truths]; their course is inconceivable. /

children.text: jñānena te vivardhante sāgaro vā sravantibhiḥ // SRS_32.263 //
children.translated_text: their knowledge grows, like the ocean [grows] with streams. // SRS_32.263 //

children.text: (Vaidya 216)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 216)

children.text: na teṣāṃ labhyate 'nto hi pibato vā mahodagheḥ /
children.translated_text: No end can be found for them — or for one who drinks from a great flood;

children.text: ākhyāto bodhisattvānāṃ nayo hyeṣa acintiyaḥ // SRS_32.264 //
children.translated_text: this inconceivable method has been declared for the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. // SRS_32.264 //

children.text: iha koṭayāṃ sthitāḥ śūrā bodhisattvā yaśasvinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, established at this limit, the heroic <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, the illustrious ones,

children.text: svarāṅgāni pramuñcanti yathā gaṅgāya vālikāḥ // SRS_32.265 //
children.translated_text: release their melodious sounds, like the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. // SRS_32.265 //

children.text: tataścintyaḥ svaro 'pyevaṃ bodhisattvo na manyate /
children.translated_text: Though even the sound may be conceived of thus, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not conceive;

children.text: manyanāyāṃ prahīṇāyāmāsanno bhoti bodhate // SRS_32.266 //
children.translated_text: when conceit has been abandoned, he is close to awakening. // SRS_32.266 //

children.text: na sa śīlaṃ vilumpeti api jīvitakāraṇāt /
children.translated_text: He does not transgress moral conduct, even for the sake of his life;

children.text: aviluptaḥ sa carati bodhisattvo dṛḍhavataḥ // SRS_32.267 //
children.translated_text: he walks untransgressed — the <s>Bodhisattva</s> of firm vows. // SRS_32.267 //

children.text: nāsau bhūyo vilupyeta kamasaṃjñāya sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: He would never again be transgressed, having abandoned all perception of sensual desire;

children.text: sarvasaṃjñāprahīṇasta aprameyāḥ samādhayaḥ // SRS_32.268 //
children.translated_text: all perceptions abandoned, his <s>samādhis</s> are immeasurable. // SRS_32.268 //

children.text: samāhitaḥ sa carati sajjate na samādhiṣu /
children.translated_text: He walks concentrated, yet does not cling to <s>samādhis</s>;

children.text: asaktaścāpramattaśca nāsau lokeṣu sajjate // SRS_32.269 //
children.translated_text: unattached and diligent, he does not cling to the worlds. // SRS_32.269 //

children.text: lokadhātūnatikramya sa gacchati sukhāvatīm /
children.translated_text: Transcending the world-realms, he goes to <s>Sukhāvatī</s>;

children.text: gataśca tatra saṃbuddhamamitābhaṃ sa paśyati // SRS_32.270 //
children.translated_text: having gone there, he sees the fully Awakened One, <s>Amitābha</s>. // SRS_32.270 //

children.text: bodhisattvāṃśca tān śūrān lakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtān /
children.translated_text: And those heroic <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, adorned with the marks,

children.text: pañcābhijñāpāramiṃ ca prāptā dhāraṇigocarāḥ // SRS_32.271 //
children.translated_text: who have attained the perfection of the five superknowledges and range in <s>dhāraṇī</s> — // SRS_32.271 //

children.text: gacchanti kṣetrakoṭīyo buddhānāṃ pādavandakāḥ /
children.translated_text: they go to <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, venerating the feet of the <s>Buddhas</s>;

children.text: obhāṣayanto gacchanti buddhakṣetrānacintiyān // SRS_32.272 //
children.translated_text: they go illuminating inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-fields. // SRS_32.272 //

children.text: sarvadoṣaprahīṇāśca sarvakleśaviśodhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: All faults abandoned, purified of all defilements,

children.text: sarvakleśasamucchinnā ekajātisthitā jināḥ // SRS_32.273 //
children.translated_text: all defilements cut off — Conquerors established in their last birth. // SRS_32.273 //

children.text: na co apāyān gacchanti tasmāt kṣetrāttu te narāḥ /
children.translated_text: They do not go to the lower realms from that <s>Buddha</s>-field;

children.text: sarve 'pāyā samucchinnāstasmin kṣetre aśeṣataḥ // SRS_32.274 //
children.translated_text: all lower realms are completely cut off in that field. // SRS_32.274 //

children.text: bodhitā buddhaśreṣṭhena amitābhena tāyinā /
children.translated_text: Awakened by the supreme <s>Buddha</s>, the protector <s>Amitābha</s> —

children.text: karotha mā tatra kāṅkṣāṃ gamiṣyatha sukhāvatīm // SRS_32.275 //
children.translated_text: do not doubt this! You shall go to <s>Sukhāvatī</s>! // SRS_32.275 //

children.text: yaḥ kṣetraśreṣṭhasya śruṇitva varṇaṃ
children.translated_text: Having heard the praise of the supreme <s>Buddha</s>-field,

children.text: cittaprasādaṃ pratilabhi mātṛgrāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: a woman who gains mental clarity,

children.text: sa kṣipra bhotī puruṣavaraḥ suvidvān
children.translated_text: she swiftly becomes an excellent man, learned,

children.text: ṛddhyā ca yāti kṣetrasahasrakoṭīḥ // SRS_32.276 //
children.translated_text: and by supernatural power travels to thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Buddha</s>-fields. // SRS_32.276 //

children.text: yāvanti pūjā bahuvidha aprameyā yā kṣetrakoṭīnayutayabiṃbareṣu /
children.translated_text: As many as the varied and immeasurable offerings in <s>koṭīs</s>, <s>nayutas</s>, and billions of <s>Buddha</s>-fields —

children.text: (Vaidya 217)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 217)

children.text: tāṃ pūja kṛtva puruṣavareṣu nityaṃ saṃkhyākalāpī na bhavati maitracittaḥ // SRS_32.277 //
children.translated_text: having made such offerings constantly to the supreme beings, they do not equal [even] a fraction of a loving mind. // SRS_32.277 //

children.text: śīlaṃ samādhiṃ satatu niṣevamāṇo dhyānān vimokṣāṃstathapi ca apramāṇān /
children.translated_text: Constantly practicing moral conduct and <s>samādhi</s>, as well as the <s>dhyānas</s>, liberations, and immeasurables,

children.text: śūnyānimittān satatu niṣevamāṇo nacireṇa so hi sugatu bhavati loke // SRS_32.278 //
children.translated_text: constantly practicing emptiness and signlessness — before long he becomes a <s>Sugata</s> in the world. // SRS_32.278 //

children.text: eṣā hi pūjā paramā viśiṣṭa mahyaṃ yaḥ śīlaskandhe pratiṣṭhitu bodhisattvo /
children.translated_text: This is the supreme and excellent worship for me — when a <s>Bodhisattva</s> is established in the aggregate of moral conduct;

children.text: sada sarvabuddhāstena supūjitā hi kṣayāntakāle yaḥ sthitu bodhicitte // SRS_32.279 //
children.translated_text: all <s>Buddhas</s> are always well-worshipped by one who abides in the thought of awakening at the time of the final end. // SRS_32.279 //

children.text: suparīnditāste buddhasahasrakoṭyo ye bodhisattvā imu kṣayi kāli ghore /
children.translated_text: Thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> are well-served by those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who, in this terrible age of decline,

children.text: rakṣanti dharmaṃ sugatavaropadiṣṭaṃ te mahya putrāścarimaka dharmapālāḥ // SRS_32.280 //
children.translated_text: guard the <s>dharma</s> taught by the supreme <s>Sugata</s> — they are my sons, the final protectors of the <s>dharma</s>. // SRS_32.280 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje sūtradhāraṇānuśaṃsāparivarto nāma dvātriṃśatitamaḥ || 32 ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the thirty-second chapter in the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, the chapter called "Benefits of Retaining the Sūtra" (<s>Sūtradhāraṇānuśaṃsāparivarta</s>).

body.text:
(Vaidya 218)
33 Kṣemadattaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 218) Chapter 33: The <s>Kṣemadattaparivarta</s> (Chapter on <s>Kṣemadatta</s>).

body.text:
atha khalu bhagavān punareva candraprabhaṃ kumārabhūtamāmantrayate sma - bhūtapūrvaṃ kumāra atīte 'dhvanyasaṃkhyeye kalpe asaṃkhyeyatare vipule apramāṇe acintye aparimite yadāsīt | tena kālena tena samayena ghoṣadatto nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān | sa khalu punaḥ kumāra ghoṣadattastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho aprameyānacintyānaparimāṇānasaṃkhyeyān sattvānāsravakṣayāyārhattve pratiṣṭhāpya parinirvāpya aprameyānasaṃkhyeyāṃśca sattvānanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhāvavinivartanīyatve pratiṣṭhāpya parinirvṛto 'bhūt | tena ca kumāra kālena tena samayena rājābhūcchrīghoṣo nāma | sa tasya tathāgatasya pūjārthaṃ tathāgatadhātugarbhāṇi caturaśītistūpakoṭisahasrāṇi kārayāmāsa | ekaikasmiṃśca stūpe caturaśīticaturaśītidīpārdhyakoṭīniyutasahasrāṇi pratiṣṭhāpayāmāsa | evaṃ vādyānāṃ tūryāṇāṃ puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākānām | ekaikatra ca stūpe caturaśīticaturaśītikoṭisahasrāṇi pratiṣṭhāpayāmāsa | ihi hi kumāra sa rājā śrīghoṣastathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā caturaśītyā bodhisattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahastrāṇāṃ mahāntaṃ bodhisattvasaṃnipātaṃ kārayitvā teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ sarvasukhopadhānena pūjāyāmudyukto 'bhūt | sarve ca te bodhisattvā mahāsattvā dharmabhāṇakā abhūvan anācchedyapratibhānāḥ samādhipratilabdhāḥ asaṅgadhāraṇīpratilabdhā bhūtaguṇadharmadeśakāḥ pariśuddhadharmadeśakāḥ bodhisattvavaśipāramiprāptāḥ | tena ca kumāra kālena tena samayena tatraiva parṣadi kṣemadatto nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'bhūcchiśurdaharaḥ kṛṣṇakeśaḥ prathamayauvanasamanvāgate bhadrake vayasi vartamānaḥ avikrīḍitāvī kāmeṣu kaumārabrahmacārī ekavarṣa upasaṃpadā | tena ca kumāra kālena tena ca samayena rāja śrīghoṣastaṃ mahāntaṃ bodhisattvamahāsattvagaṇamadhyeṣate sma yaduta ṣaṭpāramitāsaṃgītau | bodhisattvapiṭakamahādhāraṇyupāyakauśalyavaśivinayāsaṅgābhinirhārārthaṃ tān bodhisattvān mahāsattvānadhyeṣya rātrau saṃniṣaṇṇāyāṃ
tathāgatacaityasya purataḥ tatrānekāni dīpārdhyakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇi prajvālitāni | siktasaṃmṛṣṭaśodhitaśca maṇḍalamātraḥ kṛto 'bhūt puṣpābhikīrṇo nānāvicitraśayanāsanaprajñaptaḥ | rājāpi śrīghoṣaḥ sāntaḥpuragrāmanagarajanapadapāriṣadyaḥ sapauro niṣkrāntaḥ | vādyatūryatālāvacarapuṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākābhiḥ parigṛhītābhistathāgatacaityasya pūjāṃ kṛtvā sārdhamantaḥpūreṇa prāsādatalamabhirūḍho 'bhuddharmaśravaṇāya | mahatī ca devamānuṣikā pariṣat saṃnipatitā dharmaśravaṇārthikā | adrākṣīt kṣemadatto bodhisattvo mahāsatvastāni ca mahānti dīpārdhyakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi saṃprajvalitāni | avabhāsenaiva (Vaidya 219) sphuṭamabhūt | sadevamānuṣikāṃ ca janatāṃ dharmaśravaṇāya saṃnipatitāṃ viditvā tasyaitadabhūt - ahamapi mahāyānasaṃprasthitaḥ | yannvahamimaṃ samādhimākāṅkṣastathāgatapūjāṃ kuryām,yathārūpayā pūjayā sadevamānuṣāsuralokaścitrīkāraprāpto bhavedāttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto bhaveddharmālokaprāptaḥ | imāṃ ca sarvāṃ tathāgatapūjāmabhibhaveyaṃ yeyaṃ śrīghoṣeṇa rājñā kṛtā | rājā ca śrīghoṣaścitrīkāraprāpto bhavedāttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajātaḥ sāntaḥpuraparivāraḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One again addressed Prince <s>Candraprabha</s>: "Formerly, O Prince, in a past age, in an incalculable, even more incalculable, vast, immeasurable, inconceivable, and unlimited <s>kalpa</s> of the past, at that time, in that era, a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Ghoṣadatta</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, Blessed One. And, O Prince, that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ghoṣadatta</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, having established immeasurable, inconceivable, unlimited, and incalculable beings in <s>Arhatship</s> through the destruction of the <s>āsravas</s>, and having led them to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, and having established immeasurable and incalculable beings in the non-retrogression from unsurpassed perfect awakening, entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. At that time, in that era, O Prince, there was a king named <s>Śrīghoṣa</s>. He had eighty-four thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>stūpas</s> built, each containing relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, for the purpose of worship. In each <s>stūpa</s> he installed eighty-four times eighty-four thousand <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of lamp offerings. Likewise with musical instruments, cymbals, flowers, incense, fragrances, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and pennants — in each <s>stūpa</s> he installed eighty-four times eighty-four thousand <s>koṭīs</s>. Thus, O Prince, King <s>Śrīghoṣa</s>, having made offerings to the relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, convened a great assembly of eighty-four hundred thousand <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and was devoted to worshipping those <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> with every kind of comfort. All those <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> were <s>Dharma</s>-preachers, of unbreakable eloquence, who had attained <s>samādhi</s>, who had attained the unobstructed <s>dhāraṇī</s>, who taught the <s>dharma</s> of genuine qualities, who taught the purified <s>dharma</s>, who had reached the perfection of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mastery. At that time, in that era, O Prince, in that very assembly there was a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Kṣemadatta</s> — a youth, young, dark-haired, in the prime of good youth, who had not indulged in sensual pleasures, a celibate from youth, fully ordained at one year of age. At that time, in that era, O Prince, King <s>Śrīghoṣa</s> requested that great assembly of <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> for a recitation of the six <s>pāramitās</s> — for the purpose of mastering the <s>Bodhisattva-piṭaka</s>, the great <s>dhāraṇī</s>, skillful means, mastery, discipline, and unobstructed accomplishment. Having requested those <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s>, when night had fallen, before the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s shrine, many hundred thousand <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of lamp offerings were lit. A ground the size of a <s>maṇḍala</s> was sprinkled, swept, and cleaned, strewn with flowers, and furnished with various and colorful seats and beds. King <s>Śrīghoṣa</s> too, together with his inner palace, the people of the town, city, and countryside, and his attendants — the entire city — went forth. Having made offerings to the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s shrine with musical instruments, cymbals, drums, flowers, incense, fragrances, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and pennants, together with his inner palace he ascended the terrace of a mansion for hearing the <s>dharma</s>. And a great assembly of gods and humans gathered, intent on hearing the <s>dharma</s>. The <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Kṣemadatta</s> saw those many hundred thousand <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of lamp offerings blazing brightly. (Vaidya 219) It was illuminated by the radiance alone. And knowing that the assembly of gods and humans had gathered for hearing the <s>dharma</s>, this thought occurred to him: "I too have set out upon the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. What if I, aspiring to this <s>samādhi</s>, were to make an offering to the <s>Tathāgata</s> — such an offering that the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s> would be filled with wonder, uplifted in mind, joyful, endowed with delight and mental happiness, and attain the light of <s>dharma</s>? And I should surpass all this worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s> that King <s>Śrīghoṣa</s> has performed! And King <s>Śrīghoṣa</s>, together with his inner palace retinue, should be filled with wonder, uplifted in mind, joyful, endowed with delight and mental happiness!"

body.text:
atha khalu kṣemadatto bodhisattva evaṃcittaḥ prītisaumanasyajātastaṃ mahāntaṃ janakāyaṃ saṃnipatitaṃ viditvā dharmaśravaṇikānāṃ rātrau saṃniṣaṇṇāyāṃ tathāgatacaityasya purataḥ sthitvā dakṣiṇaṃ bāhuṃ cīvarapariveṣṭitaṃ kṛtvā tailaplutaṃ kṛtvā dīpayāmāsa | atha khalu kṣemadattasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyādhyāśayenānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ paryeṣamāṇasya tathā pradīpte dakṣiṇe pāṇau nābhūt cittasya mukhavarṇasya vā anyathātvam | atha khalu kumāraḥ samanantarapradīpte kṣemadattasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya pāṇau saṃprajvalite saṃjyotībhūte ekajvālāprāpte, atha khalu tasyāṃ velāyāṃ mahāpṛthivīcālaḥ prādurabhūt | tasya pāṇau dīpyamānasya prabhayā tānyanekāni dīpārdhyakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi dhyāmīkṛtānyabhūvan | sarvāsu ca dikṣu mahānavabhāso 'bhūt, yenāvabhāsena sarvā diśo 'vabhāsitāḥ samantāt sphuṭā abhūvan | sa prītisaumanasyajāta imaṃ sarvadharmasvabhāvasamatāvipañcitaṃ samādhiṃ valgunā manorameṇa svareṇa viśiṣṭayā vācānuprabaddhaiḥ padavyañjanairvistareṇa sarvaparṣadaṃ vijñāpayan saṃprakāśayati sma | tatra dvādaśa sahasrāṇi trāyatriṃśatkāyikānāṃ devānāṃ saṃnipatitāni dharmaśravaṇāya | te prītisaumanasyajātā vividhāṃ divyāṃ pūjāmakārṣuḥ, apsarogaṇāśca divyāḥ saṃgītīḥ prayojayāmāsuḥ | adrākṣīdrājā śrīghoṣaḥ upariṣṭāt prāsādatalagataḥ svajanapuraskṛtaḥ antaḥpuramadhyagato 'ṣṭāṅgapoṣadhasamādattaḥ kṣemadattaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ bāhunāvabhāsayantaṃ sarvāḥ prabhā abhibhūya divyayā atikrāntamānuṣikayāvabhāsitam | dṛṣṭvā ca punarasyaitadabhūt - abhijñāprāpto batāyaṃ kṣemadatto bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhaviṣyatīti | sa tīvraṃ prema ca prasādaṃ ca gauravaṃ ca cipasthāpya saparivāro mahākuśalamūlapuṇyaskandhopastabdhaḥ sārdhamaśītyāntaḥpurikābhistataḥ prāsādatalādātmānamutprākṣipat yadut kṣemadattasya bodhisattvasya darśanāya prītisaṃmodanāya | sa gauravanirjātena kuśalamūlena dṛṣṭa eva dharme saparivāro devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragaparigrahaṃ pratilabhate | sa devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragaparigṛhītaḥ
punareva rājā śrīghoṣaḥ saparivāraḥ paripūrṇāddhastaśatasahasrikāt prāsādāt patitaḥ | na cāsya kāyaviheṭhaścittaviheṭho vā avalīnatā vābhūt ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Kṣemadatta</s>, with such thoughts, filled with delight and mental happiness, knowing that the great assembly had gathered — those intent on hearing the <s>dharma</s> — when night had fallen, standing before the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s shrine, wrapping his right arm in his robe, soaking it with oil, he set it ablaze. Then, O Prince, for the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Kṣemadatta</s>, seeking unsurpassed perfect awakening with that resolve, when his right hand was thus lit, there was no change in his mind or in the expression of his face. Then, O Prince, the very moment the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Kṣemadatta</s>'s hand blazed, glowed, and became a single flame — at that very moment a great earthquake occurred. The radiance of his burning hand outshone those many hundred thousand <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of lamp offerings. And in all directions a great, unprecedented radiance arose, by which all directions were illuminated and filled on every side. Filled with delight and mental happiness, he fully elucidated to the entire assembly this <s>samādhi</s> that elaborates the equality of the own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s>, with a beautiful, delightful voice, in excellent speech, with connected words and syllables, in detail. Thereupon twelve thousand gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven gathered to hear the <s>dharma</s>. Filled with delight and mental happiness, they made various divine offerings, and hosts of <s>apsarases</s> performed divine concerts. King <s>Śrīghoṣa</s> saw from above, on the terrace of his mansion, surrounded by his own people and amid his inner palace, having taken the eight-limbed <s>poṣadha</s> vow, the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Kṣemadatta</s> illuminating with his arm, outshining all other lights, illuminated by a divine radiance surpassing the human. Having seen this, this thought occurred to him: "Surely this <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Kṣemadatta</s> must have attained the superknowledges!" Establishing intense affection, faith, and reverence, together with his retinue, supported by a great mass of merit from wholesome roots, together with eighty women of his inner palace, he leaped down from that terrace of the mansion — for the purpose of seeing the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Kṣemadatta</s> and rejoicing with him. By the wholesome roots born from his reverence, in that very existence, together with his retinue, he obtained the protection of gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s>. Protected by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s>, King <s>Śrīghoṣa</s> together with his retinue fell from the full height of a hundred-and-fifty-thousand-storied mansion. Yet he experienced no bodily harm, no mental distress, and no shrinking back.

body.text:
(Vaidya 220)
atha khalu rājā śrīghoṣaḥ ubhau bāhū pragṛhya mahatā janakāyena sārdhaṃ mahāntaṃ nirnādanirghoṣamākrandraṃ cākārṣīt yaduta kṣemadattasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bāhuṃ dahyamānaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃprajvalitam | sa rājā tena mahatā janakāyena sārdhaṃ prārodīdaśrūṇi pravartayamānaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 220) Then King <s>Śrīghoṣa</s>, raising both arms, together with the great assembly, let out a great wailing and crying — upon seeing the burning, blazing arm of the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Kṣemadatta</s>. The king, together with that great assembly, wept, shedding tears.

body.text: atha khalu kṣemadatto bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ rājānaṃ śrīghoṣamāmantrayate sma - kiṃ punasttvaṃ mahārāja anena mahatā janakāyena sārdhaṃ mahāntaṃ nirnādanirghoṣamākrandaṃ kurvan rodiṣi aśrūṇi ca pravartayasi? atha khalu rājā śrīghoṣaḥ kṣemadattaṃ bodhisattvaṃ gāthābhigītena prābhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Kṣemadatta</s> addressed King <s>Śrīghoṣa</s>: 'Why, O great king, together with this great multitude of people, making great wailing, outcry, and lamentation, do you weep and shed tears?' Then King <s>Śrīghoṣa</s> addressed the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Kṣemadatta</s> with verses:

children.text: kṣemadattaṃ mahāprājñaṃ paṇḍitaṃ dharmabhāṇakam /
children.translated_text: 'Knowing this <s>Kṣemadatta</s> — the greatly wise, the learned <s>Dharma</s>-preacher —

children.text: aṅgahīnaṃ viditvainaṃ jano 'yaṃ tena roditi // SRS_33.1 //
children.translated_text: to be deprived of a limb, this multitude weeps for him.' // SRS_33.1 //

children.text: etādṛśaṃ rūpamidaṃ tejorāśisamudgatam /
children.translated_text: 'Such is this form, arisen as a mass of splendor;

children.text: bāhuhīnaṃ viditvā hi bhūyo 'hamapi duḥkhitaḥ // SRS_33.2 //
children.translated_text: knowing it to be deprived of an arm, I too am greatly grieved.' // SRS_33.2 //

children.text: yastvayā dīpito bāhuḥ prabhā muktā diśo daśa /
children.translated_text: 'The arm that was set ablaze by you — radiance was released to the ten directions;

children.text: ime jihmīkṛtā dītā divyayā tvatprabhūtayā // SRS_33.3 //
children.translated_text: these [other] lights are put to shame by your divine radiance.' // SRS_33.3 //

children.text: prakampiteyaṃ pṛthivī cittaṃ te na ca līiyate /
children.translated_text: 'This earth trembled, yet your mind did not falter;

children.text: tata utpāditaṃ cittaṃ naiṣo avarakovidaḥ // SRS_33.4 //
children.translated_text: thereby [your] mind was aroused — this one is no novice in knowledge.' // SRS_33.4 //

children.text: hastaśatasahasrātaḥ prāsādāt patito hyaham /
children.translated_text: 'I fell from a palace a hundred thousand hands [in height],

children.text: sārdhamantaḥpureṇeha na ca me kāyu hiṃsitaḥ // SRS_33.5 //
children.translated_text: together with the inner palace [women] here, yet my body was not harmed.' // SRS_33.5 //

children.text: sādhu te jñānamāścaryaṃ sādhu cittamanuttaram /
children.translated_text: 'Excellent is your knowledge, wondrous! Excellent is your unsurpassed mind!

children.text: sādhu vīryaṃ ca svārabdhaṃ sādhuṃ cādhyāśayo mahān // SRS_33.6 //
children.translated_text: Excellent is the vigor well-commenced! Excellent is your great aspiration!' // SRS_33.6 //

children.text: yasya hastau vidahyante na jātvastīha iñjanā /
children.translated_text: 'One whose hands are burned yet there is never any trembling here —

children.text: prītiprāmodyajātaśca bhūyo dharmaṃ prabhāṣate // SRS_33.7 //
children.translated_text: filled with joy and gladness, he further proclaims the <s>Dharma</s>.' // SRS_33.7 //

children.text: pūrṇamāsyāṃ yathā candraḥ sūryo vāsau nabhastale /
children.translated_text: 'Like the moon at the full, or the sun in the vault of the sky,

children.text: sumerugirirājo vā evaṃ śobhasi māriṣa // SRS_33.8 //
children.translated_text: or the king of mountains <s>Sumeru</s> — thus you shine, O noble one.' // SRS_33.8 //

children.text: ahaṃ pi evaṃ praṇidhiṃ paripūreya paṇḍitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I too, as a wise one, having fulfilled such a vow,

children.text: kāye premaṃ jahitvāhaṃ kuryāmarthaṃ ca prāṇinām // SRS_33.9 //
children.translated_text: abandoning attachment to my body, shall accomplish the welfare of beings.' // SRS_33.9 //

children.text: dharmapremṇā ca hṛṣyāmi prīitirme 'tra acintiyā /
children.translated_text: 'I rejoice out of love for the <s>Dharma</s>; my delight herein is inconceivable;

children.text: yat puno aṅgahīno 'si tena me duḥkhamuttamam // SRS_33.10 //
children.translated_text: yet that you are deprived of a limb — thereby my grief is supreme.' // SRS_33.10 //

children.text: kṣemadatto hi rājānaṃ devanāgehi pūjitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Then <s>Kṣemadatta</s>, worshipped by gods and <s>Nāgas</s>,

children.text: anantapratibhānena imā gāthā abhāṣata // SRS_33.11 //
children.translated_text: with boundless eloquence, spoke these verses to the king:' // SRS_33.11 //

children.text: naivaṃ syādaṅgahīno 'sau yasya bāhurna vidyate /
children.translated_text: 'One is not truly deprived of a limb whose arm does not exist [physically];

children.text: sa tu devāṅgahīnaḥ syāda yasya śīlaṃ na vidyate // SRS_33.12 //
children.translated_text: rather, one is truly deprived of a limb whose morality does not exist.' // SRS_33.12 //

children.text: (Vaidya 221)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 221)

children.text: anena pūtikāyena pūjitā me tathāgatāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'With this putrid body, <s>Tathāgatas</s> have been worshipped by me —

children.text: acintiyā dakṣiṇīyāḥ sarvalokasya cetiyāḥ // SRS_33.13 //
children.translated_text: inconceivable worthy recipients, shrines for the entire world.' // SRS_33.13 //

children.text: anantā yāstrisāhasrā paripūritāḥ /
children.translated_text: '[If one filled] boundless three-thousand-fold [world systems],

children.text: pradadyāllokanāthebhyo buddhajñānagaveṣakaḥ // SRS_33.14 //
children.translated_text: and gave [them] to the Lords of the World, seeking <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge —' // SRS_33.14 //

children.text: astyeṣā laukikī pūjā anyā pūjā acintiyā /
children.translated_text: 'this is a worldly offering; another offering is inconceivable:

children.text: ye dharmān śūnyān jānanti tyajante kāyajīvitam // SRS_33.15 //
children.translated_text: those who know <s>dharmas</s> as empty and give up body and life.' // SRS_33.15 //

children.text: satyavākyaṃ kariṣyāmi mahārāja śṛṇohi me /
children.translated_text: 'I shall make a declaration of truth — O great king, listen to me!

children.text: yā ceyaṃ janatā sarvā imāṃ gāthāṃ vijānatha // SRS_33.16 //
children.translated_text: And all you people here, understand this verse!' // SRS_33.16 //

children.text: yena satyena buddho 'haṃ bheṣye lokasya cetiyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'By the truth that I shall become a <s>Buddha</s>, a shrine for the world —

children.text: tena satyena dharaṇī ṣaḍavikāraṃ prakampatu // SRS_33.17 //
children.translated_text: by that truth, may the earth tremble with six kinds of quaking!' // SRS_33.17 //

children.text: bhāṣitā va iyaṃ vācā dharaṇī ca prakampitā /
children.translated_text: 'No sooner was this utterance spoken than the earth trembled;

children.text: āścaryamadbhataprāptā devakoṭyaḥ praharṣitāḥ // SRS_33.18 //
children.translated_text: a wonder, a marvel was attained — <s>koṭīs</s> of gods were overjoyed.' // SRS_33.18 //

children.text: harṣitā devamanujā bodhicittamupādayuḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Gods and humans, filled with joy, generated <s>bodhicitta</s>;

children.text: prasthitā agrayānasminnaprameyā acintiyāḥ // SRS_33.19 //
children.translated_text: they set out in the foremost vehicle — immeasurable, inconceivable.' // SRS_33.19 //

children.text: yāttakānāṃ kṛto arthaḥ kṣemadattena bhikṣuṇā /
children.translated_text: 'Such was the welfare accomplished by the monk <s>Kṣemadatta</s>;

children.text: buddhānāṃ vartate jñānaṃ yatrākṣayamacintiyam // SRS_33.20 //
children.translated_text: the knowledge of <s>Buddhas</s> abides there — inexhaustible, inconceivable.' // SRS_33.20 //

children.text: yena satyena dharmo 'sau bāhurnāma na vidyate /
children.translated_text: 'By the truth that that <s>dharma</s> [holds] — an arm does not [truly] exist —

children.text: tena satyena me bāhurbhoti kṣipraṃ yathā purā // SRS_33.21 //
children.translated_text: by that truth, may my arm become swiftly as before!' // SRS_33.21 //

children.text: yena satyena dharmo 'sau kṣemadatto na vidyate /
children.translated_text: 'By the truth that that <s>dharma</s> [holds] — <s>Kṣemadatta</s> does not [truly] exist —

children.text: diśo daśa gaveṣadbhiḥ śunyatvānnopalabhyate // SRS_33.22 //
children.translated_text: sought in the ten directions, it cannot be found because of [its] emptiness.' // SRS_33.22 //

children.text: yo 'pi niścarate śabdastaṃ pu śūnyaṃ vijānatha /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever sound issues forth — know that too as empty;

children.text: pratiśrutkopamaḥ śabdo dharmānevaṃ vijānatha // SRS_33.23 //
children.translated_text: sound is like an echo — know <s>dharmas</s> thus.' // SRS_33.23 //

children.text: sadā viśārado bhoti śunyatāyāṃ gatiṃgataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'One who has reached the domain of emptiness is always confident;

children.text: tasya satyena vākyena sarvaloko na dahyate // SRS_33.24 //
children.translated_text: by the truth of his words, the entire world is not consumed [by fire].' // SRS_33.24 //

children.text: yāvantastribhave sattvā ye devā ye ca mānuṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'However many beings there are in the three realms of existence — those who are gods and those who are humans —

children.text: sarvajñatāyāstejena sarve bhonti samāhitāḥ // SRS_33.25 //
children.translated_text: by the splendor of omniscience, all of them become concentrated.' // SRS_33.25 //

children.text: yāvantyupadravāḥ kecid ye divyā ye ca mānuṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever calamities there are — those divine and those human —

children.text: avaivartikatejena sarve te bhonti nirvṛtāḥ // SRS_33.26 //
children.translated_text: by the splendor of irreversibility, all of them are pacified.' // SRS_33.26 //

children.text: bhāṣitāśca imā gāthā bāhuśca punarutthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'When these verses were spoken, the arm arose again;

children.text: kṣemadattasya kāyaśca lakṣaṇehi vicitritaḥ // SRS_33.27 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Kṣemadatta</s>'s body was adorned with the [major] marks.' // SRS_33.27 //

children.text: (Vaidya 222)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 222)

children.text: devakoṭīsahasrāṇi antarikṣe sthitāni ca /
children.translated_text: 'Thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of gods, standing in the sky,

children.text: mandārapuṣpaistaṃ bhikṣumokiranti ca tatkṣaṇam // SRS_33.28 //
children.translated_text: showered that monk with <s>Mandāra</s> flowers at that moment.' // SRS_33.28 //

children.text: amānuṣyehi puṣpehi jambudvīpo hyayaṃ sphuṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'With superhuman flowers, this <s>Jambudvīpa</s> was covered;

children.text: apsaraḥkoṭiniyutai saṃgītyaḥ saṃprayojitāḥ // SRS_33.29 //
children.translated_text: <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Apsarases</s> performed concerts.' // SRS_33.29 //

children.text: imaṃ nādaṃ nadantasya kṣemadattasya tatkṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: 'At that moment, when <s>Kṣemadatta</s> proclaimed this sound,

children.text: buddhakoṭīsahasrāṇi paśyantīdaṃ vikurvitam // SRS_33.30 //
children.translated_text: thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> beheld this miraculous feat.' // SRS_33.30 //

children.text: svakasvakeṣu kṣetreṣu ārocet sumahāyaśāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In their respective fields, those of great renown announced

children.text: bhikṣūṇāṃ bhikṣuṇīnāṃ ca upāsaka upāsikām // SRS_33.31 //
children.translated_text: to monks and nuns, to male and female lay followers:' // SRS_33.31 //

children.text: kṣemadatto hyasau bhikṣuḥ paṇḍitaḥ sumahābalaḥ /
children.translated_text: '"That monk <s>Kṣemadatta</s> is learned, of supremely great power —

children.text: yenāsau dīpito bāhurbuddhajñānasya kāraṇāt // SRS_33.32 //
children.translated_text: he who set ablaze his arm for the sake of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge."' // SRS_33.32 //

children.text: tena kṣetrasahasrāṇi yathā gaṅgāya vālikāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'By that [act], fields as many as the sands of the Ganges

children.text: obhāsitāḥ pradīpena kalpoddāha iva sthite // SRS_33.33 //
children.translated_text: were illuminated by [his] light, as if the conflagration at the end of a <s>kalpa</s> stood [blazing].' // SRS_33.33 //

children.text: puṣpacandanacūrṇaiśca sarvakṣetrāḥ sphuṭā abhūt /
children.translated_text: 'With flowers, sandalwood powders, all fields became covered;

children.text: yāvadbhūmimupādāya jānumātramabhūt sphuṭam // SRS_33.34 //
children.translated_text: from the ground up to the depth of a knee, [everything] was strewn.' // SRS_33.34 //

children.text: sarvaratnaiḥ sarvapuṣpairbuddhakṣetramabhūt sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: 'With all jewels and all flowers, the <s>Buddha</s>-field became covered;

children.text: kṣemadattasya pūjāyai nāgā varṣanti mauktikam // SRS_33.35 //
children.translated_text: for the worship of <s>Kṣemadatta</s>, the <s>Nāgas</s> rained pearls.' // SRS_33.35 //

children.text: sarvaratnāmayairvyūhairidaṃ kṣetramalaṃkṛtam /
children.translated_text: 'With arrays of all jewels, this field was adorned,

children.text: saṃstṛtaṃ ratnamuktābhioḥ kṣemadattasya pūjayā // SRS_33.36 //
children.translated_text: strewn with jewels and pearls, for the worship of <s>Kṣemadatta</s>.' // SRS_33.36 //

children.text: devā nāgāśca yakṣāśca kinnarāpsaramahoragāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Apsarases</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> —

children.text: prasthitā agrabodhīye yathā gaṅgāya vālikāḥ // SRS_33.37 //
children.translated_text: they set out for supreme awakening, as many as the sands of the Ganges.' // SRS_33.37 //

children.text: śākyasiṃho 'pi saṃbuddho gṛdhrakūṭasmi parvate /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Śākyasiṃha</s> too, the Perfectly Awakened One, on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> mountain,

children.text: purato bhikṣusaṃdhasya siṃhanādaṃ nadī jinaḥ // SRS_33.38 //
children.translated_text: before the assembly of monks, the <s>Jina</s> roared a lion's roar:' // SRS_33.38 //

children.text: kṣemadatto 'hamabhavaṃ śrīghoṣo 'pyajito 'bhavat /
children.translated_text: '"I was <s>Kṣemadatta</s>; <s>Śrīghoṣa</s> was <s>Ajita</s> (<s>Maitreya</s>);

children.text: kalpakoṭīsahasrāṇi caran saṃbodhicārikām // SRS_33.39 //
children.translated_text: for thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, [we were] practicing the conduct of awakening."' // SRS_33.39 //

children.text: sahadarśanena bhikṣusya kṣemadattasya tatkṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: 'At the very moment of seeing the monk <s>Kṣemadatta</s>,

children.text: acintyābhistadā strībhiḥ strībhāvo vinivartitaḥ // SRS_33.40 //
children.translated_text: by inconceivable women at that time, their female state was abandoned.' // SRS_33.40 //

children.text: vyākṛtāste narendreṇa nāsti teṣāṃ vinivartanā /
children.translated_text: 'They were predicted by the Lord of Men — there is no turning back for them;

children.text: svayaṃbhuvo bhaviṣyanti sarve lokavināyakāḥ // SRS_33.41 //
children.translated_text: they shall all become Self-Arisen Ones, Guides of the World.' // SRS_33.41 //

children.text: śrutvā sūtramidaṃ vidvān saṃlekhaguṇadarśanam /
children.translated_text: 'Having heard this <s>sūtra</s>, the wise one, seeing the qualities of austerity,

children.text: kāye prema na kurvīta iha dharme suśikṣitaḥ // SRS_33.42 //
children.translated_text: should not generate attachment to the body, being well-trained in this <s>Dharma</s>.' // SRS_33.42 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje kṣemadattaparivarto nāma trayastriṃśatitamaḥ || 33 ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the thirty-third chapter of the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, called the <s>Kṣemadatta</s> chapter.

body.text:
(Vaidya 223)
34 Jñānāvatīparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 223) Chapter 34: The <s>Jñānāvatī</s> chapter.

body.text: tatra bhagavān punarapi candraprabhaṃ kumārabhūtamāmantrayate sma - tasmāttarhi kumāra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena imaṃ samādhimākāṅkṣatā kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhukāmena kuśalamūle pratiṣṭhite dharmadānena vā āmiṣadānena vā yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | tena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena taddānaṃ catusṛbhi pariṇāmanābhiḥ pariṇāmayitavyam | katamābhiścatasṛbhiḥ? yaduta yairupāyakauśalyaistairbuddhairbhagavadbhiranuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirabhisaṃbuddhā, teṣāmupāyakauśalyānāṃ pratilambhāyedaṃ dānakuśalamūlamavaropayāmi | ayaṃ prathamaḥ pariṇāmaḥ | yebhyaḥ kalyāṇamitrebhyo 'ntikāttānyupāyakauśalyāni śṛṇuyāmudgṛhṇīyāṃ paryavāpnuyāṃ dhārayeyam, tairanuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirabhisaṃbudhyate | tairyaiḥ kalyāṇamitraiḥ sārdhaṃ samavadhānaṃ bhavet, evametaddānakuśalamūlamavaropayāmi | ayaṃ dvitīyaḥ pariṇāmaḥ | ye bhogapratilābhāḥ sarvalokopajīvyā bhaveyustairme bhogapratilābhaiḥ samavadhānaṃ bhavet, evamidaṃ kuśalamūlavaropayāmi | ayaṃ tṛtīyaḥ pariṇāmaḥ | ya ātmabhāvapratilābhaḥ dvābhyāmanugrahābhyāṃ sattvānanugṛhṇīyādāmiṣānugraheṇa ca dharmānugraheṇa ca, tasya me ātmabhāvasya pratilambho bhavet, evamidaṃ kuśalamūlavaropayāmi | ayaṃ caturthaḥ pariṇāmaḥ | ābhiḥ kumāra catasṛbhiḥ pariṇāmanābhirbodhisattvena mahāsattvena tāni kuśalamūlāni pariṇāmayitavyāni ||
body.translated_text: There the Blessed One again addressed the prince <s>Candraprabha</s>: 'Therefore, prince, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> who longs for this <s>samādhi</s> and wishes to quickly awaken to unsurpassed, perfect and complete awakening should exert himself in roots of merit through either the gift of <s>Dharma</s> or the gift of material things, whether as a householder or a renunciant. That <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> should dedicate that gift with four dedications. Which four? [1] "By whatever skillful means those Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> awakened to unsurpassed, perfect and complete awakening — for the attainment of those skillful means I plant this root of merit from giving." This is the first dedication. [2] "From whatever spiritual friends I might hear, grasp, master, and retain those skillful means, by which unsurpassed, perfect and complete awakening is awakened — that I might come together with such spiritual friends, thus I plant this root of merit from giving." This is the second dedication. [3] "Whatever attainments of wealth might become the livelihood of the entire world — that I might come together with such attainments of wealth, thus I plant this root of merit." This is the third dedication. [4] "Whatever attainment of a personal existence might benefit beings with two kinds of assistance — the assistance of material things and the assistance of <s>Dharma</s> — that I might obtain such a personal existence, thus I plant this root of merit." This is the fourth dedication. With these four dedications, prince, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> should dedicate those roots of merit.'

body.text: punaraparaṃ kumāra bodhisattvena mahāsattvenemaṃ samādhimākāṅkṣatā gṛhīṇā vā pravrajitena vā kṣipraṃ cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhukāmena śīlavanto guṇavantaḥ prajñāvanto bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sevitavyā bhajitavyāḥ paryupāsitavyā aśāṭhyena | yo 'sya samādherdhārako bhikṣurbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhavet,sa ca syādābādhiko bāḍhaglānaḥ, tena svamāṃsaśoṇiatenāpi sa bhikṣustasmādābādhād vyutthāpayitumutsoḍhavyaḥ | adhyāśayasaṃpannena kumāra bodhisattvena mahāsattvenemaṃ samādhimākāṅkṣata kṣipraṃ cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhukāmenāvikampamānena viśāradena svakaṃ māṃsaśoṇitamapi parityajya dharmabhāṇako bhikṣurābādhād vyutthāpayitavyaḥ | tadanenāpi te kumāra paryāyeṇaivaṃ veditavyam ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, prince, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> who longs for this <s>samādhi</s> and wishes to quickly awaken to unsurpassed, perfect and complete awakening — whether as a householder or a renunciant — should attend upon, associate with, and serve <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> who are endowed with morality, endowed with good qualities, and endowed with wisdom, without deceit. If there should be a monk who is a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, a holder of this <s>samādhi</s>, and he should be sick, gravely ill, that [aspirant] should strive to heal that monk from his illness even with his own flesh and blood. A <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> who is endowed with aspiration, who longs for this <s>samādhi</s>, who wishes to quickly awaken to unsurpassed, perfect and complete awakening — unwavering, confident — should heal the <s>Dharma</s>-preaching monk from his illness, even giving up his own flesh and blood. By this method too, prince, it should be understood thus.

body.text:
bhūtapūrvaṃ kumāra atīte 'dhvanyasaṃkhyeye kalpe asaṃkhyeyatare vipule apramāṇe yadāsīt tena kālena tena samayenācintyapraṇidhānaviśeṣasamudgatarājo nāma tathāgato 'han samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān | sa khalu punaḥ kumāra acintyapraṇidhānaviśeṣasamudgatarājastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho yasminneva divase 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhastatraiva divase parihate aprameyānasaṃkhyeyān buddhanirmitān nirmāya aparimāṇānāṃ ca sattvānāṃ vinayaṃ kṛtvā
(Vaidya 224) āsravakṣayāyārhattve pratiṣṭhāpya aparimāṇāṃśca sattvānanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhāvavinivartanīyatve pratiṣṭhāpya tatraiva divase parinirvṛto 'bhūt | tasya khalu punarbhagavataḥ parinirvṛtasya caturaśītiḥ varṣakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi saddharmo 'tiṣṭhat | tasya ca bhagavato 'cintyapraṇidhānaviśeṣasamudgatarājasya tathāgatasya śāsanāntardhānakālasamaye paścimāyāṃ pañcaśatyāṃ vartamānāyāṃ bahavo bhikṣavaḥ prādurbhūtā upalambhadṛṣṭayaḥ | teṣāmevaṃrūpāḥ sūtrāntā na rocante na cādhimucyante pratibādhante pratikṣipanti | īdṛśānāṃ ca sūtrāntadhārakāṇāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ pīḍāṃ kurvanto yāvajjīvitād vyavaropaṇamakārṣuḥ | tairabhisatkārādhyavasitairīdṛśasutrāntadhārakāṇāṃ bhikṣuṇāṃ sahasraṃ jīvitād vyavaropitamabhūt | tena ca punaḥ kumāra kālena tena samayena rājābhūd jñānabalo nāma jambudvīpeśvaraḥ saddharmaparigrāhakaḥ pūrvapraṇidhānasaṃpannaḥ | tena khalu punaḥ kumāra kālena tena samayena iha jambudvīpe eko bhikṣurdharmabhāṇako 'bhūt tasya samādherdhārako bhūtamatirnāmnā tasya rājñaḥ kulapraveśakaḥ kalyāṇamitro hitaiṣī anukampakaḥ arthakāmaḥ | sa cāsya rājā atṛpto darśanenābhīkṣṇapratikāṅkṣī cābhūddarśanena dharmasaṃkathanopasaṃkramaṇaparyupāsanaparipṛcchāgrahaṇadhāraṇavācanavijñāpanasamarthaḥ | sa khalu punardharmabhāṇako bhikṣuḥ sattvānāmīryācaryādhimuktidhātuvāsanākuśalo 'bhūt | sattvānāmindriyabalavīryavimātratājñānadhātuvāsanākuśalaḥ satyasaṃdhikuśalaḥ visaṃdhiprativacanakuśalaḥ arthaviniścayakuśalaḥ gambhīrapratibhānaḥ sattvānāṃ vinayavidhijñaḥ pūrvābhilāpī smitamukhaḥ apagatabhrūkuṭimukho mahadgatacittavihārī mahākarūṇābhiyuktaḥ anabhibhūtaḥ sarvaparapravādibhiḥ | tena ca kumāra kālena tena ca samayena rājño jñānabalasya duhitā dārikābhūt ṣoḍaśavarṣā jātyā abhirūpā prāsādikā darśanīyā paramayā śubhavarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgatā jñānāvatī nāma | tasyāḥ sa bhūtamatirbhikṣurācāryo 'bhūt kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu saṃdarśakaḥ samuttejakaḥ saṃpraharṣakaḥ samādāpakaḥ | tena ca kumāra kālena tena samayena tasya dharmabhāṇakasya
bhikṣormahākṛṣṇavaisarpaḥ ūrau prādurabhūt duścikitsyo durlabhabhaiṣajyaḥ | sa vaidyeḥ glānaḥ pratikṣipto 'bhūt ||
body.translated_text: 'Formerly, O prince, in the past, in an incalculable <s>kalpa</s>, more incalculable, vast, and immeasurable, at that time, at that occasion, a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Fully Awakened One named <s>Acintyapraṇidhānaviśeṣasamudgatarāja</s> (King Arisen through the Distinction of Inconceivable Vows) appeared in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, <s>Buddha</s>, Blessed One. Now, O prince, that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Acintyapraṇidhānaviśeṣasamudgatarāja</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Fully Awakened One — on the very day he awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening, on that very day, having created immeasurable and innumerable <s>Buddha</s>-emanations, having disciplined immeasurable beings, (Vaidya 224) having established them in <s>Arhatship</s> through the destruction of outflows, and having established immeasurable beings in non-retrogression from unsurpassed perfect awakening — on that very day he passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. After the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of that Blessed One, the true <s>Dharma</s> endured for eighty-four <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s>-hundred-thousands of years. And at the time of the disappearance of the teaching of that Blessed One <s>Acintyapraṇidhānaviśeṣasamudgatarāja</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, during the last five hundred [years], many monks appeared who held views of apprehension. Such <s>sūtras</s> did not please them, they had no faith in them, they obstructed and rejected them. Tormenting monks who upheld such <s>sūtras</s>, they deprived them of life.
