Driven by their hostility, they deprived a thousand monks who upheld such <s>sūtras</s> of their lives. Now, O prince, at that time, at that occasion, there was a king named <s>Jñānabala</s> (Power of Knowledge), lord of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, a protector of the true <s>Dharma</s>, endowed with former vows. Now, O prince, at that time, at that occasion, here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> there was a single <s>Dharma</s>-preaching monk, a holder of this <s>samādhi</s>, named <s>Bhūtamati</s> (True Intelligence), who had access to the king\'s household, a spiritual friend, benevolent, compassionate, seeking [others\'] welfare. The king was insatiable in seeing him and constantly wished to see him — capable of approaching for <s>Dharma</s>-discussion, attending, questioning, grasping, retaining, reciting, and understanding. Now, that <s>Dharma</s>-preaching monk was skilled in the conduct, behavior, dispositions, elements, and latent tendencies of beings; skilled in the faculties, powers, vigor, and the disparity of knowledge-elements and latent tendencies of beings; skilled in the bonds of truth; skilled in responses to objections; skilled in the ascertainment of meaning; of profound eloquence; knowing the methods of disciplining beings; speaking first, with a smiling face, free from frowning, dwelling with a lofty mind, devoted to great compassion, unconquered by all proponents of other doctrines. Now, O prince, at that time, at that occasion, King <s>Jñānabala</s> had a daughter, a girl of sixteen years, beautiful by birth, graceful, lovely, endowed with supreme excellence of beautiful complexion, named <s>Jñānavatī</s> (Possessing Knowledge). That monk <s>Bhūtamati</s> was her teacher, one who instructed, encouraged, gladdened, and exhorted her in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. Now, O prince, at that time, at that occasion, a great black spreading sore appeared on the thigh of that <s>Dharma</s>-preaching monk — difficult to cure, requiring rare medicine. He was given up by the physicians as incurable.' ||

body.text: atha khalu rājā sāntapuraḥ saputraḥ saduhitṛparivāraḥ taṃ bhikṣuṃ glānaṃ viditvā prārodīdaśrūṇi pravartayati sma sārdhamaśītyā strīsahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ paurairnāgaraiḥ sārdhaṃ rāṣṭreṇa naigamajānapadairgaṇakamahāmātraiḥ sārdhamamātyadauvārikapāriṣadyaiḥ | te sarve taṃ bhikṣuṃ glānaṃ viditvā prarodantaḥ aśraṇi pravartayāmāsuḥ - mā khalvayaṃ bhikṣuḥ kālaṃ kuryāditi | tena ca kumāra kālena tena samayena rājño jñānabalasyānyatarā devatā purāṇasālohitābhūdanubaddhā | sā tasya rājñaḥ svapnāntargatasyāpadarśayati sma - sacet mahārāja etasya bhikṣornavakenāsaṃkliṣṭena mānuṣyeṇa rudhireṇaiṣa kṛṣṇavaisarpa ālipyeta, navakaṃ cāsaṃkliṣṭaṃ mānuṣaṃ māsaṃ nānārasasaṃprayuktaṃ bhojanaṃ dīyeta, evameṣa bhikṣurasmādābādhād vyuttiṣṭheta | atha khalu rājā jñānabalastasyā rātryā atyayena tataḥ svapnāntarāt prativibuddho 'ntaḥpuramadhyagataḥ imāṃ svapnaprakṛtimantaḥpurāyārocayāmāsa - evaṃrūpaḥ svapno mayā dṛṣṭaḥ | iti hi kumāra tataḥ stryāgārāttataśca rājakulānna kācit strī utsahate tasya (Vaidya 225) bhikṣostadbhaiṣajyaṃ dātum | jñānāvatyapi rājaduhitā imamīdṛśameva svapnamadrākṣīt | dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ prativibuddhā antaḥpuramadhye imāmeva svapnaprakṛtiṃ mātṝṇāṃ parivārasya cārocayati sma | na ca kācidutsahate strī tasya bhikṣoretad bhaiṣajyaṃ dātum ||
body.translated_text: Then King [<s>Jñānabala</s>], together with his inner palace, together with his sons, surrounded by his daughters, wept and shed tears upon learning that the monk was ill — together with eighty thousand women, together with the townsfolk and citizens, together with the kingdom's merchants and villagers, accountants and ministers, together with the counselors, doorkeepers, and courtiers. All of them, upon learning that the monk was ill, wept and shed tears [saying]: 'May this monk not die!' Now, O prince, at that time, at that occasion, a certain deity who had been a blood-relative of King <s>Jñānabala</s> in a former life was attached [to him]. She appeared to the king while he was in a dream [and said]: 'If, O great king, this black spreading sore were anointed with fresh, undefiled human blood, and fresh, undefiled human flesh prepared with various flavors were given [as food] for a month, then this monk would recover from this illness.' Then King <s>Jñānabala</s>, having awakened from the dream after the passing of that night, went to the inner palace and announced this dream-vision to the inner palace [women]: 'Such a dream was seen by me.' Thus, O prince, from the women's quarters and from the royal household, no woman was willing to give that medicine to the monk. (Vaidya 225) Princess <s>Jñānavatī</s> also saw a dream of exactly this kind. Having seen it and awakened, she announced this same dream-vision to her mothers and attendants in the inner palace. But no woman was willing to give that medicine to the monk.

body.text: atha khalu jñānavatī rājaduhitā tuṣṭā udagrā āttamanaskā pramuditā prītisaumanasyajātā evaṃ vyavasāyamakārṣīt - yannvahametad bhaiṣajyaṃ svakāccharīrād yathopadiṣṭaṃ navaṃ rudhiraṃ navaṃ ca māṃsaṃ dadyām | ahameveha rājakule sarvadaharā ca sarvataruṇī ca asaṃkliṣṭakāyavāṅbhanaskarmā ca | asaṃkliṣṭaṃ jñānameṣāmi asaṃkliṣṭasya dharmabhāṇakasya svaśarīrāda rudhiraṃ ca māṃsaṃ copanāmayiṣyāmi | apyeva nāmaiṣa bhikṣurasmādābādhād vyuttiṣṭheta | atha khalu sā jñānavatī rājaduhitā svakamāvāsaṃ gatvā tīkṣṇaṃ śastraṃ gṛhītvā dharmāntargatena mānasena svakamūrumāṃsaṃ chittvā nānārasasaṃprayuktaṃ praṇītamabhisaṃskṛtya lohitaṃ ca pragṛhya taṃ cācāryaṃ praveśya rājño jñānabalasya purato niṣadya lohitena taṃ visarpamālepayitvā tena ca svabhisaṃskṛtena bhojanena saṃtarpayati | atha khalu sa bhikṣurajānannaparibudhyamānaḥ apariśaṅkamānastadbhaktaṃ paribhuktavān | samanantaraparibhukte ca tasminnāhāre tasya bhikṣoḥ sarvāstā vedanā pratiprasrabdhāḥ, sarvaśca vyādhirapagataḥ | tena vigataparidāhena sarvasukhasamarpitena tathā dharmo deśito yathā tato 'ntaḥpurāttataśca nagarajanapadarāṣṭrasaṃnipātād dvādaśānāṃ prāṇisahasrāṇāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpannāni ||
body.translated_text: Then Princess <s>Jñānavatī</s>, delighted, elated, joyful, glad, filled with rapture and happiness, formed this resolution: 'Let me give this medicine from my own body — fresh blood and fresh flesh, as prescribed. I am the youngest and most youthful in this royal household, of undefiled actions of body, speech, and mind. I shall attain undefiled knowledge and offer blood and flesh from my own body to the undefiled <s>Dharma</s>-preacher. May this monk recover from this illness!' Then Princess <s>Jñānavatī</s>, having gone to her own quarters, taking a sharp blade, with her mind absorbed in the <s>Dharma</s>, cut the flesh from her own thigh, prepared it exquisitely with various flavors, collected the blood, brought it to her teacher, and sitting before King <s>Jñānabala</s>, anointed the spreading sore with the blood and nourished [the monk] with that prepared food. Then that monk, unknowing, unaware, unsuspecting, ate that food. Immediately upon eating that meal, all the painful feelings of that monk subsided, and the entire disease departed. Free from fever and endowed with complete comfort, he taught the <s>Dharma</s> in such a way that from the inner palace and from the assembly of the city, countryside, and kingdom, the minds of twelve thousand beings were directed toward unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: atha khalu rājā jñānabalaḥ svakāṃ duhitaraṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Jñānabala</s> addressed his own daughter with verses:

children.text: kutastvayā śoṇitu labdhu dārike kuto idaṃ āhṛtu māṃsa mānuṣam /
children.translated_text: 'Where did you obtain the blood, O girl? From where was this human flesh brought?

children.text: āhāru yaḥ sādhitu te 'dya dhīte yeno sukhīyaṃ kṛtu dharmabhāṇakaḥ // SRS_34.1 //
children.translated_text: The food that was prepared by you today, O wise one, by which the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher was made well — // SRS_34.1 //

children.text: hato hyayaṃ vātha mṛto 'tha labdho yat sādhitaṃ nānarasehi vyañjanam /
children.translated_text: was someone killed, or did someone die, or was [the flesh] obtained, that a dish was prepared with various flavors?

children.text: kutaśca te śoṇitu labdhu dārike yeno ayaṃ mocitu vyādhi pāpakaḥ // SRS_34.2 //
children.translated_text: From where did you obtain the blood, O girl, by which this terrible disease was cured?' // SRS_34.2 //

children.text: pituḥ śruṇitvā vacanaṃ ca dārikā jñānāvatī tasya idaṃ bravīti /
children.translated_text: Having heard her father's words, the girl <s>Jñānavatī</s> said this to him,

children.text: alīnacittā ca giraṃ prabhāṣate śṛṇuṣva tātā yadahaṃ bravīmi te // SRS_34.3 //
children.translated_text: speaking with undaunted mind: 'Listen, father, to what I say to you: // SRS_34.3 //

children.text: dṛṣṭastāta mayā svapno devatāyā nidarśitaḥ /
children.translated_text: "A dream was seen by me, father, shown by a deity;

children.text: śṛṇuṣva me bhūmipate bhūtamarthaṃ vijānatha // SRS_34.4 //
children.translated_text: listen, O lord of the earth, understand the true matter! // SRS_34.4 //

children.text: (Vaidya 226)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 226)

children.text: sā devatā mamāvicanmānuṣaṃ māṃsaśoṇitam /
children.translated_text: That deity told me: human flesh and blood —

children.text: yo dadyādasya bhikṣusya vyādhermucyet sa pāpakāt // SRS_34.5 //
children.translated_text: whoever would give it to this monk, he would be freed from the terrible disease. // SRS_34.5 //

children.text: mayā cotthāya śayyātaḥ praviśyāntaḥpuraṃ nṛpa /
children.translated_text: And having risen from my bed, entering the inner palace, O king,

children.text: svapnastadāyamākhyāto jyeṣṭhikānāṃ hi mātṛṇām // SRS_34.6 //
children.translated_text: I then told this dream to my elder mothers. // SRS_34.6 //

children.text: ceṭikānāṃ mayākhyātaṃ kā śaktā kartumīdṛśam /
children.translated_text: I told the maidservants too — who is able to do such a thing?

children.text: mānuṣaṃ śoṇitaṃ māṃsaṃ rasasiddhaṃ susaṃskṛtam // SRS_34.7 //
children.translated_text: [To give] human blood and flesh, well-prepared with flavors, properly cooked — // SRS_34.7 //

children.text: bhojanaṃ ca pradātavyaṃ śoṇitena ca lepanam /
children.translated_text: food must be given and the sore anointed with blood;

children.text: kṛṣṇavaisarpato eṣa kathaṃ bhikṣurvimucyate // SRS_34.8 //
children.translated_text: how else will this monk be freed from the black spreading sore? // SRS_34.8 //

children.text: yadi kriyā na kriyate kṣiprametena vyādhinā /
children.translated_text: If this treatment is not performed, quickly by this disease

children.text: kālaṃ kuryādayaṃ bhikṣurbhaiṣajyena vineti vā // SRS_34.9 //
children.translated_text: this monk will die, or [suffer] without medicine. // SRS_34.9 //

children.text: tribhave ko na sattvastyājayet svamāṃsaśoṇitam /
children.translated_text: Who in the three realms of existence would not sacrifice their own flesh and blood?

children.text: imaṃ dṛṣṭvā na ko vidvān kuryāt kāyasmi niśrayam // SRS_34.10 //
children.translated_text: What wise person, seeing this, would not take refuge in [sacrificing] the body? // SRS_34.10 //

children.text: antaḥpurasyo prativedayāmyahaṃ na eka nārīpi bhaṇāti dāsye /
children.translated_text: I announced to the inner palace — not a single woman said 'I will give';

children.text: priyaśca me bhikṣuḥ priyaśca ātmā bodhyarthu tyaktaṃ maya māṃsaśoṇitam // SRS_34.11 //
children.translated_text: dear to me is this monk, and dear to me is my self — for the sake of awakening I sacrificed my flesh and blood. // SRS_34.11 //

children.text: teṣāṃ na kāyesmi ca bhakti niśritā premāpi naivātmani cāṇumātram /
children.translated_text: They have no devotion regarding the body, nor even the slightest love for the self;

children.text: tyaktvāpi cātmānu na bhoti durmanāḥ ye bodhi prārthenti śivāmaśokām // SRS_34.12 //
children.translated_text: even having sacrificed their selves, they are not dejected — those who aspire to auspicious, sorrowless awakening. // SRS_34.12 //

children.text: antaḥpuraṃ tataḥ śrutvā sarvaṃ tadvismitaṃ abhūt /
children.translated_text: The inner palace, having heard this, was entirely amazed;

children.text: na cātrotsahate kācidenāṃ yojayituṃ kriyām // SRS_34.13 //
children.translated_text: but no one there was willing to undertake this act. // SRS_34.13 //

children.text: tato me nāmitaṃ cittaṃ bhikṣordāsyāmi bhojanam /
children.translated_text: Then my mind was inclined: 'I shall give food to the monk,

children.text: svāni māṃsānyahaṃ chittvā śoṇitena ca lepanam // SRS_34.14 //
children.translated_text: cutting my own flesh, and anointing [the sore] with blood.' // SRS_34.14 //

children.text: svakamūruṃ mayā chittvā gṛhītaṃ māṃsaśoṇitam /
children.translated_text: I cut my own thigh and collected the flesh and blood;

children.text: māṃsapeśī mayā pakvā nānārasasusaṃskṛtā // SRS_34.15 //
children.translated_text: a piece of flesh was cooked by me, well-prepared with various flavors. // SRS_34.15 //

children.text: bhikṣostasyāturasyāhaṃ dāsyāmi pituragrataḥ /
children.translated_text: To that ailing monk, I gave, before my father,

children.text: bhojanaṃ mānuṣaṃ māṃsaṃ śoṇitena ca lepanam // SRS_34.16 //
children.translated_text: food of human flesh, and anointed [the sore] with blood. // SRS_34.16 //

children.text: śṛṇohi mahyaṃ vacanaṃ narādhipā manuṣyamāṃsasmi avidyamāne /
children.translated_text: Hear my words, O lord of men — since no human flesh was available elsewhere,

children.text: (Vaidya 227)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 227)

children.text: chittvā svamāṃsāni mayoruto nṛpā sādhetva dattānima dharmabhāṇake // SRS_34.17 //
children.translated_text: cutting my own flesh from the thigh, O king, I prepared it and gave it to this <s>Dharma</s>-preacher." // SRS_34.17 //

children.text: eṣo mayānuttarabodhi arthe svakātta kāyātta kṛto mahārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: "For the sake of unsurpassed awakening, from my own body, I performed this great deed;

children.text: bhikṣuśca muktaḥ kṛtu nirvikāro mayā ca puṇyaṃ kṛtamaprameyam // SRS_34.18 //
children.translated_text: the monk is freed and made well, and immeasurable merit has been made by me. // SRS_34.18 //"

children.text: rājāpyavocadduhitāṃ kathaṃ te chidyanti kāyāttu svakāttu māṃse /
children.translated_text: The king too said to his daughter: 'How is it that flesh is cut from your own body?

children.text: bhaiṣajyayoge kriyamāṇi dārike mā te abhūd duḥkha śarīravedanā // SRS_34.19 //
children.translated_text: When such a medicinal treatment is performed, O girl, did you not have painful bodily feeling?' // SRS_34.19 //

children.text: sa rājadhītā matimān viśāradā tamālapī rāja śṛṇu narādhipā /
children.translated_text: That wise and confident princess said to the king: 'Listen, O lord of men!

children.text: śrutvā ca tatra pratipadya yoniśo acintiyaḥ karmavipāku tādṛśaḥ // SRS_34.20 //
children.translated_text: Having heard, reflect upon it properly — such is the inconceivable ripening of <s>karma</s>: // SRS_34.20 //

children.text: pāpena karmeṇa kṛtena tātā niraye 'pi sattvā prapacanti dāruṇe /
children.translated_text: "By evil <s>karma</s> that has been done, father, beings fall into terrible hells,

children.text: nirmāṃsa bhūtvā ca samāṃsa bhonti paśyetu karmāṇa phalaṃ acintiyam // SRS_34.21 //
children.translated_text: and having become fleshless, they become fleshed again — behold the inconceivable fruit of <s>karma</s>! // SRS_34.21 //

children.text: pāpena karmeṇa nirmāṃsaśoṇitāḥ kṣaṇena co bhonti samāṃsaśoṇitāḥ /
children.translated_text: By evil <s>karma</s>, [beings become] fleshless and bloodless, and in an instant they become fleshed and blooded again;

children.text: kiṃ vā punā tat kuśalena karmaṇā adhimuktito jāyati māṃsaśoṇitam // SRS_34.22 //
children.translated_text: how much more so through wholesome <s>karma</s> — from [right] intention, flesh and blood are born! // SRS_34.22 //

children.text: chidyanti māṃse na mamāsi vedanā āhāri me śoṇitu nāsti iñjanā /
children.translated_text: My flesh is cut yet I feel no pain; my blood is drawn yet there is no disturbance;

children.text: na dharmakāyasya vraṇo na chidraṃ yadi sarvu chidyeyu mama svamāṃsam // SRS_34.23 //
children.translated_text: There is no wound nor fissure in the <s>Dharmakāya</s> — even if all my own flesh were cut away! // SRS_34.23 //

children.text: prītiṃ mayā dharmi parāṃ janitvā chittvā pradattaṃ svakamūrumāṃsam /
children.translated_text: Having generated the highest joy in the <s>Dharma</s>, I cut and gave my own thigh-flesh;

children.text: na co mamā tāta vraṇena duḥkhaṃ jānāmi kāyo yathapūrvamāsīt // SRS_34.24 //
children.translated_text: and there was no suffering for me, father, from the wound — I know [my] body to be as it was before. // SRS_34.24 //

children.text: (Vaidya 228)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 228)

children.text: audumbaraṃ puṣpu yathaiva tātā bahukalpakoṭīṣu kadāci dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: Just as the <s>udumbara</s> flower, father, is seen once in many <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: emeva etādṛśa dharmabhāṇako kadāci dṛśyantiha jambudvīpe // SRS_34.25 //
children.translated_text: even so such a <s>Dharma</s>-preacher is seen but rarely here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. // SRS_34.25 //

children.text: yathaiva jāmbūnada niṣku bhāsate paśyanta sattvā na vitṛptimenti /
children.translated_text: Just as a <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold ornament shines, and beings looking upon it are never sated,

children.text: emeva etādṛśa dharmabhāṇakān dṛṣṭvā na tṛpyantiha devamānuṣāḥ // SRS_34.26 //
children.translated_text: even so, having seen such <s>Dharma</s>-preachers, gods and humans here are never sated. // SRS_34.26 //

children.text: pītvā yathācchaṃ salilaṃ janasya tṛṣābhibhūtasya tṛṣā vigacchati /
children.translated_text: Just as when a person overcome by thirst drinks clear water, [his] thirst departs,

children.text: emeva ete vidu dharmabhāṇakā dharmāmṛtaistṛṣṇa vinenti prāṇinām // SRS_34.27 //
children.translated_text: even so these wise <s>Dharma</s>-preachers remove the craving of living beings with the nectar of <s>Dharma</s>. // SRS_34.27 //

children.text: sutyaktametanmaya māṃsaśoṇitaṃ yaddattu bhikṣusya gilānakasya /
children.translated_text: Well-relinquished by me was that flesh and blood which was given to the sick <s>bhikṣu</s>;

children.text: visarpu śāntaśca sa dharmabhāṇake kṛtaṃ mayā gauravu buddhavarṇitam // SRS_34.28 //
children.translated_text: the spreading disease was calmed in that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher — I performed the reverence praised by the <s>Buddha</s>. // SRS_34.28 //

children.text: cāritravantasya bahuśrutasya imaṃ samādhīvaradhārakasya /
children.translated_text: For one of virtuous conduct, of great learning, who upholds this supreme <s>samādhi</s> —

children.text: yanme tu tyaktaṃ svakamātmamāṃsameteṣa dharmāṇa bhaveyya lābhinī // SRS_34.29 //
children.translated_text: that I relinquished my own bodily flesh — may I become a receiver of these <s>dharmas</s>! // SRS_34.29 //

children.text: yathaiva gandhaḥ surabhī manoramaḥ kālānusārī śubha candanasya /
children.translated_text: Just as the fragrance of excellent sandalwood, sweet-smelling and delightful, following the breeze,

children.text: pravāti gandho daśasu diśāsu emeva gandhopama dharmabhāṇakāḥ // SRS_34.30 //
children.translated_text: wafts in the ten directions — even so <s>Dharma</s>-preachers are like fragrance. // SRS_34.30 //

children.text: yathaiva merurdiśatāsu dṛśyate samantaprāsādiku darśanīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Meru</s> is seen in [all] directions, beautiful as a palace on every side,

children.text: avabhāsayanto diśatāsu rocate tathaiva merūpama dharmabhāṇakāḥ // SRS_34.31 //
children.translated_text: illuminating and shining in [all] directions — even so <s>Dharma</s>-preachers are like <s>Meru</s>. // SRS_34.31 //

children.text: yathaiva stūpaṃ patamānu kaścid vyutthāpayet saṃskari paṇḍito naraḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a wise, skilled person would restore a <s>stūpa</s> that was falling down,

children.text: yastatra stūpe 'pi prasādu kuryād vyutthāpito yena sa tasya hetuḥ // SRS_34.32 //
children.translated_text: and whoever generates faith in that <s>stūpa</s> — the one who restored it is the cause of that [merit]. // SRS_34.32 //

children.text: (Vaidya 229)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 229)

children.text: emevayaṃ dharmastūpo gilānako vimocito lohitalepanena /
children.translated_text: Even so, this sick one — a <s>Dharma</s>-<s>stūpa</s> — was rescued by [the application of] blood,

children.text: svakena māṃsena ca dharmagauravād dīpo mayā dīpitu jambudvīpe // SRS_34.33 //
children.translated_text: and by my own flesh, out of reverence for the <s>Dharma</s> — a lamp was lit by me in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. // SRS_34.33 //

children.text: eṣo 'kariṣyad yadi bhikṣu kālaṃ samādhiśabdo 'piha jambudvīpe /
children.translated_text: If this <s>bhikṣu</s> had died, the very sound of '<s>samādhi</s>' here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>

children.text: niruddhu sattvāna sadābhaviṣyat cikitsite 'smin sa samādhi labdhaḥ // SRS_34.34 //
children.translated_text: would have been extinguished for beings forever — but having been healed, he attained the <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_34.34 //

children.text: sarvasya lokasya paritrāṇu bhikṣurandhasya lokasya ca cakṣudāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: This <s>bhikṣu</s> is the protector of the entire world and the giver of sight to the blind world;

children.text: rāgasya doṣasya mohasya caiva cikitsako 'yaṃ mama vaidyarājaḥ // SRS_34.35 //
children.translated_text: he is the physician of passion, hatred, and delusion — this one is my king of physicians. // SRS_34.35 //

children.text: mahadgate citti sadā pratiṣṭhitaḥ pramāṇu caryāya na tasya labhyate /
children.translated_text: His mind is always established in the great vehicle; no measure of his conduct can be found;

children.text: suviniścitārtheṣu padeṣu śikṣito anābhibhūtaśca parapravādibhiḥ // SRS_34.36 //
children.translated_text: trained in words of well-ascertained meaning, unconquered by opponents. // SRS_34.36 //

children.text: na mahya bhūyo vinipātato bhayaṃ strītvaṃ punarme na ca bhūyu bheṣyati /
children.translated_text: For me there is no more fear of the lower realms, and womanhood shall never again be mine,

children.text: sahasrakalpāna ca koṭiyo bhuyo kṛtvā paraṃ gauravu dharmabhāṇake // SRS_34.37 //
children.translated_text: having performed supreme reverence to the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher for thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s> more. // SRS_34.37 //

children.text: yo buddhakṣetrān yatha gaṅgavālikāḥ ratanāna pūrṇān dadi nāyakānām /
children.translated_text: One who gives <s>Buddha</s>-fields as [numerous as] the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, filled with jewels, to the Guides,

children.text: yaścaiva pādāṅgulimeka dadyādidaṃ tataḥ puṇyu viśiṣyate param // SRS_34.38 //
children.translated_text: and one who gives even a single toe — this merit is superior to that. // SRS_34.38 //

children.text: sā dārikā kālamitaśca kṛtvā adrākṣi buddhāna sahasrakoṭyaḥ /
children.translated_text: That girl, after dying, beheld thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>;

children.text: sarveṣa co śāsani pravrajitvā imaṃ varaṃ śāntu samādhi deśayī // SRS_34.39 //
children.translated_text: and having gone forth in the teachings of all of them, she taught this supreme, peaceful <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_34.39 //

children.text: sarveṣa teṣāṃ dvipadottamānāṃ parinirvṛtānāṃ caramismi kāle /
children.translated_text: In the final period of all those supreme among bipeds who had entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: (Vaidya 230)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 230)

children.text: pravrajyalābhinyabhu nityakālamasaṃkiliṣṭāḥ sugatāna putrakāḥ // SRS_34.40 //
children.translated_text: she always obtained the going-forth — undefiled sons of the <s>Sugatas</s>. // SRS_34.40 //

children.text: dīpaprabhasyātha tathāgatasya caritva sā śāsani brahmacaryam /
children.translated_text: Having practiced the holy life in the teaching of <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dīpaprabha</s>,

children.text: strībhāvu tasmin vinivartayitvā abhūṣi bhikṣustada dharmabhāṇakaḥ // SRS_34.41 //
children.translated_text: having turned away from womanhood in that [teaching], she became a <s>bhikṣu</s>, a <s>Dharma</s>-preacher. // SRS_34.41 //

children.text: maitreya jñānaṃbalu so narendraḥ saddharmaparigrāhaku nityakālam /
children.translated_text: O <s>Maitreya</s>, that king, <s>Jñānabala</s>, was always a guardian of the True <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: dīpaṃkaro 'sau abhūddharmabhāṇako ahaṃ ca āsaṃ tada rājadhītā // SRS_34.42 //
children.translated_text: he was the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, and I was then the king's daughter. // SRS_34.42 //

children.text: svakena māṃsena ca śoṇitena co upasthito me tada dharmabhāṇakaḥ /
children.translated_text: With my own flesh and blood, I attended to that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher;

children.text: śāṭhyaṃ ca sarvaṃ parivarjayitvā imaṃ samādhiṃ pratikāṅkṣatā tadā // SRS_34.43 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned all deceit, aspiring to this <s>samādhi</s> at that time. // SRS_34.43 //

children.text: yebhī tadā roditu bhikṣu dṛṣṭvā gilānakaṃ pīḍitu vedanābhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who wept upon seeing the sick <s>bhikṣu</s>, afflicted and tormented by painful sensations —

children.text: avivartikāste sada sarvi bhūvan na jātu yātā vinipātabhūmim // SRS_34.44 //
children.translated_text: they all became irreversible forever, never going to the realms of misfortune. // SRS_34.44 //

children.text: nābhūṣi teṣāṃ sada akṣirogo na śīrṣarogo na ca karṇarogaḥ /
children.translated_text: There was never any eye disease for them, no head disease, no ear disease,

children.text: na ghrāṇarogo na ca jihvarogo na ca dantaśūlaṃ na kadācidāsīt // SRS_34.45 //
children.translated_text: no nose disease, no tongue disease, and never any toothache. // SRS_34.45 //

children.text: samantaprāsādiku bhonti nityaṃ śirīya tejena jvalantakāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: They are always beautiful as palaces on every side, their bodies blazing with glory and splendor,

children.text: dvātriṃśaketuśatapuṇyalakṣaṇā upasthito yaistada bhikṣu glānakaḥ // SRS_34.46 //
children.translated_text: endowed with the thirty-two marks of a hundred [types of] merit — those who attended to the sick <s>bhikṣu</s>. // SRS_34.46 //

children.text: (Vaidya 231)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 231)

children.text: mahyaṃ ca te śāsani pravrajitvā pralujyamānānimu buddhabodhim /
children.translated_text: Having gone forth in my teaching and [advancing toward] this <s>Buddha</s>-awakening as it disintegrates,

children.text: dhāritva te gañju tathāgatānāṃ drakṣyanti buddhāna sahasrakoṭiyo // SRS_34.47 //
children.translated_text: having upheld the treasury of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, they shall behold thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>. // SRS_34.47 //

children.text: susaṃgṛhītvānima buddhabodhiṃ dhāretva nityaṃ ca hi gauraveṇa /
children.translated_text: Having well-grasped this <s>Buddha</s>-awakening and upheld it always with reverence,

children.text: te arthu kṛtvā vipulaṃ prajānāṃ drakṣyanti akṣobhya narāṇamuttamam // SRS_34.48 //
children.translated_text: having accomplished vast benefit for beings, they shall behold <s>Akṣobhya</s>, supreme among humans. // SRS_34.48 //

children.text: śrutvā ca te carya niruttarāmimāṃ lapsyanti prītiṃ cariyāṃ nirāmiṣām /
children.translated_text: Having heard this unsurpassed conduct, they shall attain joy and the conduct free from worldly gain;

children.text: śrutvā ca te ātmana pūrvacaryāṃ kāhinti buddhāna udārapūjām // SRS_34.49 //
children.translated_text: having heard their own former conduct, they shall make magnificent offerings to the <s>Buddhas</s>. // SRS_34.49 //

children.text: dṛṣṭā ca bhikṣūn vidu śīlavanto niḥśāṭhiyeno sada sevitavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having seen wise <s>bhikṣus</s> of virtuous conduct, one should always serve them without deceit;

children.text: akhilaṃ ca doṣaṃ ca vivarjayitvā seveta bhikṣuṃ tada dharmabhāṇakāḥ // SRS_34.50 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned all faults and defects, one should serve the <s>bhikṣu</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher. // SRS_34.50 //

children.text: āghātu krodhaṃ ca vivarjayitvā pūjetha putrān mama dharmaśāsane /
children.translated_text: Having abandoned hostility and anger, one should worship [my] sons in the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching;

children.text: mā andhabhūtā bahukalpakoṭiyo vinipātaprāptāśca bhaveta duḥkhitāḥ // SRS_34.51 //
children.translated_text: do not become blind for many <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, fallen into misfortune and suffering! // SRS_34.51 //

children.text: na śīlu trāyeta śrataṃ ca tasya na dhyānu trāyenna araṇyavāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: Neither moral conduct nor learning protects him, neither <s>dhyāna</s> nor forest-dwelling protects him,

children.text: tadā nu trāyenna ca buddhapūjā vyāpādu kṛtvāna paraspareṇa // SRS_34.52 //
children.translated_text: nor does <s>Buddha</s>-worship protect him — when one has acted with hostility toward others. // SRS_34.52 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje jñānāvatīparivartaścatustriṃśatitamaḥ || 34 ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the thirty-fourth chapter in the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, the <s>Jñānavatīparivarta</s> (Chapter on <s>Jñānavatī</s>). || 34 ||

body.text:
(Vaidya 232)
35 Supuṣpacandraparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 232) Chapter 35: The <s>Supuṣpacandraparivarta</s> (Chapter on <s>Supuṣpacandra</s>).

body.text:
atha khalvāyuṣmānānanda utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat - pṛccheyamahaṃ bhagavantaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ kaṃcideva pradeśaṃ sacenme bhagavānavakāśaṃ kuryāt praṣṭavyapraśnavyākaraṇāya | evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandametadavocat - tena hyānanda svake āsane niṣadya pṛccha tvaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ yad yadevākāṅkṣasi, ahaṃ te tasya tasya praśnasya vyākaraṇena cittamārādhayiṣye | evamukte āyuṣmānānando bhagavantametadavocat - kṛtāvakāśo 'smi bhagavan, kṛtāvakāśo 'smi sugata praśnavyākaraṇāya | atha khalvāyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ purataḥ āsane niṣadya bhagavantametadavocat - ko nu bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo yadiha ekatyā bodhisattvā bodhisattvacārikāṃ caramāṇā hastacchedān pādacchedān karṇacchedānakṣyutpāṭanāni aṅgottamāṅgacchedān nigacchanti pratyaṅgacchedāṃśca? vividhāni duḥkhāni pratyanubhavanti? no ca hīyante?na ca parikṣīyante 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ? evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandametadavocat - sacet tvamānanda jānīyā yāni me duḥkhāni pratyanubhūtāni imāmanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ samudānayitum, etadapi te ca pratibhāyāt | kiṃ punaryattathāgataṃ paripraṣṭavyaṃ manyathāḥ | tad yathāpi nāma ānanda iha kāścideva puruṣaḥ adhastāt pādatalamupādāya yāvanmūrdhakādādīpto bhavet prajvalitaḥ ekajvālībhūtaḥ, taṃ kaścideva puruṣa upasaṃkramya evaṃ vadet - ehi tvaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa anirvāpitenātmabhāvena pañcabhiḥ kāmaguṇaiḥ samarpitaḥ samanvaṅgībhūtaḥ krīḍasva ramasva paricārayasveti | tat kiṃ manyase ānanda api tu sa puruṣaḥ anirvāpitenātmabhāvena pañcabhiḥ kāmaguṇaiḥ samarpitaḥ samanvaṅgībhūtaḥ krīḍeta rameta paricārayeta? ānanda āha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan | bhagavānāha - krīḍetānanda sa puruṣo rameta paricārayeta parikalpamupādāyānirvāpitenātmabhāvena pañcabhiḥ kāmaguṇaiḥ samarpitaḥ samanvaṅgībhūtaḥ | na tveva tathāgatasya pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacārikāṃ caramāṇasya sattvāṃstribhirupāyairduḥkhitān dṛṣṭvā daridrānnābhūt sukhaṃ
vā saumanasyaṃ vā cittapraharṣo vā | ye ānanda bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacārikāṃ caramāṇā akhaṇḍaśīlā bhavanti achidraśīlāḥ akalmāṣaśīlā aśabalaśīlāḥ aparāmṛṣṭaśīlāḥ acalitaśīlāḥ, alulitaśīlā akopyaśīlāḥ, nottānaśīlāḥ,na paradarśanaśīlāḥ na visaṃvādaśīlāḥ, ṛjuśīlāḥ yathāpratijñāśīlāḥ sattvānugrahaśīlāḥ | evaṃrūpeṇa śīlena samanvāgatā bhavanti, te ānanda bodhisattvā mahāsattvā anantāṃ bodhisattvacārikāṃ caramāṇā na hastacchedena parihāṇiṃ nigacchanti | na pādacchedena parihāṇiṃ nigacchanti | na karṇanāsācchedena parihāṇiṃ nigacchanti | (Vaidya 233) na netrotpāṭanaśīrṣacchedena parihāṇiṃ nigacchanti | nāṅgapratyaṅgacchedena parihāṇiṃ nigacchanti | na ca vividhāni duḥkhāni pratyanubhavanti | kṣipraṃ cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyante ||
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, and joining his palms toward the Blessed One, addressed the Blessed One thus: "I would ask the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, about a certain matter, if the Blessed One would grant me the opportunity to ask a question and receive an answer." Thus addressed, the Blessed One said to the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, sit in your own seat and ask the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, whatever you wish. I shall satisfy your mind with an answer to each question." Thus addressed, the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said to the Blessed One: "I have been granted the opportunity, Blessed One; I have been granted the opportunity, <s>Sugata</s>, to ask and receive an answer." Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, sitting before the Blessed One in his seat, addressed the Blessed One thus: "What, Blessed One, is the cause, what is the condition, that here certain <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, while practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-career, undergo the cutting of hands, cutting of feet, cutting of ears, gouging out of eyes, cutting of head and limbs, and cutting of secondary limbs? They experience various sufferings, yet do not decline and are not diminished from unsurpassed perfect awakening?" Thus addressed, the Blessed One said to the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "If you, <s>Ānanda</s>, were to know the sufferings I experienced in order to accomplish this unsurpassed perfect awakening, this too would occur to you — how much more so what you think to ask the <s>Tathāgata</s>! Suppose, <s>Ānanda</s>, some person were ablaze from the soles of his feet up to the crown of his head — burning, flaming, become a single blaze. And suppose someone were to approach that person and say: 'Come, good sir, while your body is still unextinguished, enjoy, delight, and amuse yourself, endowed with and possessed of the five strands of sensual pleasure!' What do you think, <s>Ānanda</s> — would that person, with his body still unextinguished, enjoy, delight, and amuse himself, endowed with and possessed of the five strands of sensual pleasure?" <s>Ānanda</s> said: "Certainly not, Blessed One!" The Blessed One said: "That person, <s>Ānanda</s>, might conceivably enjoy, delight, and amuse himself, endowed with and possessed of the five strands of sensual pleasure while his body is still unextinguished. But never did the <s>Tathāgata</s>, formerly while practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-career, upon seeing beings suffering in the three ways — impoverished — experience any pleasure, ease, or mental delight. Those <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, who while formerly practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-career possess unbroken moral conduct, unfissured moral conduct, unspotted moral conduct, unmottled moral conduct, uncorrupted moral conduct, unshaken moral conduct, undisturbed moral conduct, inviolable moral conduct, not superficial moral conduct, not for display to others moral conduct, not deceptive moral conduct — straight moral conduct, conduct true to their vow, conduct for the benefit of beings — endowed with such moral conduct, those <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, while practicing the infinite <s>Bodhisattva</s>-career, do not undergo decline through the cutting of hands, do not undergo decline through the cutting of feet, do not undergo decline through the cutting of ears and nose, (Vaidya 233) do not undergo decline through the gouging of eyes or cutting of the head, do not undergo decline through the cutting of limbs and secondary limbs, nor do they experience various sufferings — and they swiftly attain unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text:
bhūtapūrvamānanda atīte 'dhvanyasaṃkhyeyakalpairasaṃkhyeyatarairvipulairapramāṇairacintyairatulyairamāpyairaparimāṇairyadāsīt | tena kālena tena samayena ratnapadmacandraviśuddhābhyudgatarājo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān | tena khalu punarānanda samayena tasya bhagavato ratnapadmacandraviśuddhābhyudgatarājñastathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya navatikalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyāyuṣpramāṇamabhūt | sarvatra ca divase navatikalpakoṭīsahasrāṇi sattvānāmavaivartikatāyāṃ buddhadharmeṣu pratiṣṭhāpayati sma | tena khalu punarānanda samayena tasya bhagavato ratnapadmacandraviśuddhābhyudgatarājñastathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya parinirvṛtasya caramikāyāṃ pañcāśati saddharmāntardhānakālasamaye saddharmavipralope vartamāne ime evaṃrūpāḥ sūtrāntā bahujanajugupsitā bahujanavivarjitā bahujanaviruddhā mahājanotsṛṣṭāścābhūvan | mahābhayabhairavakāle vartamāne mahopadrave ativṛṣṭikālasamaye anāvṛṣṭikālasamaye vartamāne vyālakālasamaye vartamāne vidyutkāntārakalpasamaye durbhikṣakālasamaye mithyādṛṣṭikālasamaye asamyagdṛṣṭikālasamaye tīrthikamantraparyeṣṭikālasamaye buddhabodheḥ pralujyamānakālasamaye vartamāne sapta bodhisattvasahasrāṇi grāmanagaranigamarā rājadhānījanapadebhyo nirvāsitāni samantabhadraṃ nāma vanakhaṇḍaṃ tadupaniśritya viharanti sma sārdhaṃ supuṣpacandreṇa dharmabhāṇakena, yasteṣāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ dhāraṇīdharmapayāya deśayati sma | sa khalu punā rājā supuṣpacandro dharmabhāṇaka eko rahogataḥ pratisaṃlīno divyena cakṣuṣā atikrāntamānuṣeṇa paśyati sma - bahvīrbodhisattvakoṭiravaruptakuśalamūlā anyonyebhyo buddhakṣetrebhyaḥ ihopapannāḥ | sacette labheran dhāraṇīdharmaparyāyaśravaṇāya, na nivarterannanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ | atha na labheran dhāraṇīdharmaparyāyaśravaṇāya, vivarterannanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ | atha khalu supuṣpacandro dharmabhāṇakaḥ smṛtaḥ saṃprajānaṃstataḥ samādhervyutthāya yenāsau mahān bodhisattvagaṇastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ upasaṃkramya taṃ mahāntaṃ bodhisattvagaṇametadavocat
- gamiṣyāmaḥ kulaputrāḥ | grāmanagaranigamarāṣṭarājadhānīravataritvā sattvebhyo dharmaṃ deśayiṣyāmaḥ | atha khalu sa mahān bodhisattvagaṇaḥ supuṣpacandraṃ dharmabhāṇakametadavocat - nāsmākamabhipretaṃ yadāyuṣmānito vanaṣaṇḍād grāmanagaranigamarāṣṭrarājadhānīravataret | tatkasya hetoḥ? bahvayo 'bhimānikā bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikāḥ| saddharmapratikṣepakālaśca vartate | tamāyuṣmantaṃ jīvitādvayavaropayiṣyanti | āyuṣmāṃścātīva prāsādiko 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prathamayauvanasamanvāgato bhadrake vayasi vartate | sa dhautakāñcanahāṭakacchaviḥ (Vaidya 234) śaṅkhakundenduvarṇayorṇayā pratimaṇḍito 'pi śobhitalalāṭo nīlakuñcitakeśoṇīṣaśca | mā te rājaputrā vā anye vā tatpratimā īrṣyāmātsaryopahacetaso jīvitādvayavaropayiṣyanti | atha khalu supuṣpacandro dharmabhāṇakastaṃ bodhisattvagaṇametadavocat - sacenme ātmā ārakṣyo bhavet, na mayā atītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ śāsane ārakṣā kṛtā bhavet | tasyāṃ ca velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Formerly, <s>Ānanda</s>, in a past age, in incalculable, even more incalculable, vast, immeasurable, inconceivable, incomparable, unfathomable, and unlimited <s>kalpas</s> of the past — at that time, in that era, a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Ratnapadmacandraviśuddhābhyudgatarāja</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, Blessed One. At that time, <s>Ānanda</s>, the lifespan of that Blessed One, <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnapadmacandraviśuddhābhyudgatarāja</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, was ninety thousand <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>. And every single day he established ninety thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of beings in non-retrogression from the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. At that time, <s>Ānanda</s>, after that Blessed One, <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnapadmacandraviśuddhābhyudgatarāja</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, had entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, in the final period, at the time of the disappearance of the true <s>dharma</s> during the fiftieth [period], when the corruption of the true <s>dharma</s> was underway, these kinds of <s>sūtras</s> became despised by many people, shunned by many people, opposed by many people, and cast away by the masses. When a time of great terror and dread prevailed, a time of great calamity, a time of excessive rain, a time of drought, a time of wild beasts, a time like a wilderness of lightning, a time of famine, a time of wrong views, a time of incorrect views, a time of seeking the spells of <s>tīrthikas</s>, a time when the awakening of the <s>Buddha</s> was crumbling — seven thousand <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, exiled from villages, cities, towns, royal capitals, and provinces, took up residence in a forest grove called <s>Samantabhadra</s>, together with the <s>dharma</s>-preacher <s>Supuṣpacandra</s>, who taught those monks the <s>dhāraṇī-dharma</s> discourse. That <s>dharma</s>-preacher, King <s>Supuṣpacandra</s>, alone in seclusion, in meditative absorption, saw with the divine eye surpassing the human: "Many <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, whose wholesome roots have been planted, have been reborn here from other <s>Buddha</s>-fields. If they could obtain the hearing of the <s>dhāraṇī-dharma</s> discourse, they would not regress from unsurpassed perfect awakening. But if they cannot obtain the hearing of the <s>dhāraṇī-dharma</s> discourse, they will regress from unsurpassed perfect awakening." Then the <s>dharma</s>-preacher <s>Supuṣpacandra</s>, mindful and clearly knowing, arose from that <s>samādhi</s> and approached that great assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Having approached, he said to that great assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: "Let us go, sons of good family! Having entered villages, cities, towns, kingdoms, and royal capitals, let us teach the <s>dharma</s> to beings!" Then that great assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> said to the <s>dharma</s>-preacher <s>Supuṣpacandra</s>: "It is not our wish that the Venerable One should leave this forest grove and enter villages, cities, towns, kingdoms, and royal capitals. For what reason? There are many conceited monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen. The time of rejection of the true <s>dharma</s> prevails. They will deprive the Venerable One of his life! Moreover, the Venerable One is exceedingly handsome, well-formed, and beautiful, in the prime of good youth. He is of complexion like pure refined gold, (Vaidya 234) adorned with a tuft of hair between his brows of the color of conch, jasmine, and moon, with a beautiful forehead, and with curling blue-black hair on his crown. Lest princes or others of similar [beauty], their minds seized by jealousy and envy, deprive you of your life!" Then the <s>dharma</s>-preacher <s>Supuṣpacandra</s> said to that assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: "If my own self were to be protected, then I would not have made a protection in the teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, of the past, future, and present." And at that time he spoke these verses:

children.text: na ātmasaṃjñāya vasitva jātu śakyaṃ ihā śāsani rakṣa kurvaṇā /
children.translated_text: "One who abides in the perception of self can never guard the teaching here;

children.text: mahāvitānā sugatāna bodhiḥ prakāśanā paścimi kāli dāruṇe // SRS_35.1 //
children.translated_text: the awakening of the <s>Sugatas</s> is a great canopy — illuminating it in the terrible latter age! // SRS_35.1 //

children.text: yo ātmasaṃjñā prajahitva sarvaśaḥ sattvānimān pudgalavādaniśritān /
children.translated_text: One who abandons all self-perception, regarding these beings attached to the doctrine of a person (<s>pudgalavāda</s>),

children.text: rūpāṇi śabdāṃśca rasāṃśca gandhān spraṣṭavyu varjeti sa rakṣi śāsanam // SRS_35.2 //
children.translated_text: and avoids forms, sounds, tastes, smells, and tactile objects — he guards the teaching! // SRS_35.2 //

children.text: buddhāna koṭīnayutānyupasthihedannena pānena prasannacittaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having served <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> with food and drink, with a clear mind,

children.text: chatraiḥ patākābhi dīpakriyābhiḥ kalpāna koṭī yatha gaṅgavālikāḥ // SRS_35.3 //
children.translated_text: with parasols, banners, and lamp offerings, for <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s> like the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> — // SRS_35.3 //

children.text: yaścaiva saddharma pralujyamāne nirudhyamāne sugatāna śāsane /
children.translated_text: yet one who, when the true <s>dharma</s> is crumbling, when the teaching of the <s>Sugatas</s> is ceasing,

children.text: rātriṃdivaṃ eka careyya śiṣyān idaṃ tataḥ puṇyu viśiṣṭu bhoti // SRS_35.4 //
children.translated_text: wanders alone day and night as a student — this merit is more excellent than that! // SRS_35.4 //

children.text: ye dāni teṣāṃ puruṣarṣabhāṇāṃ saddharmi lujyanti upekṣi bhāvayī /
children.translated_text: Those who now, when the true <s>dharma</s> of those bulls among men is crumbling, cultivate indifference —

children.text: na tairjinā satkṛta bhonti kecit na co kṛtaṃ gauravu nāyakeṣu // SRS_35.5 //
children.translated_text: by them no Conqueror has been honored; they have shown no reverence to the Guides! // SRS_35.5 //

children.text: yuṣme bhotha sukhī svakārthu kuruthā gopāyathā
children.translated_text: May you be happy! Accomplish your own aims! Guard

children.text: ātmanaṃ yuṣme bhotha ihāpramatta vinaye maitrīvihārī sadā /
children.translated_text: yourselves! May you be diligent here, in discipline, always dwelling in loving-kindness!

children.text: śīlaṃ rakṣatha ujjvalaṃ aśabalaṃ śuddhaṃ śuci nirmalaṃ
children.translated_text: Guard moral conduct — bright, spotless, pure, clean, stainless —

children.text: yehī rakṣitu śīlu bhoti amalaṃ buddhebhi saṃvarṇitam // SRS_35.6 //
children.translated_text: that stainless moral conduct which has been praised by the <s>Buddhas</s> as guarding! // SRS_35.6 //

body.text: (Vaidya 235)

children.text: yehī satkṛtu bhonti sarvi sugatā yāvanta pūrve abhūt
children.translated_text: By which all <s>Sugatas</s>, as many as existed before, are honored —

children.text: tehi trāyitu bhonti sarvajanatā yā bodhisaṃprasthitā /
children.translated_text: by that, all people who have set out for awakening are protected!

children.text: tehī uddharitāḥ bhavanti narakā sattvā bahū pāpakāḥ
children.translated_text: By that, many sinful beings are raised up from the hells —

children.text: yehī rakṣitu bhonti śīlu amalaṃ buddhaiḥ praśastaṃ purā // SRS_35.7 //
children.translated_text: by that stainless moral conduct which was formerly praised by the <s>Buddhas</s>! // SRS_35.7 //

body.translated_text: (Vaidya 235)

children.text: dānaṃ detha viśiṣṭa dharmaratanaṃ kṣāntiṃ sadā rakṣathāraṇyaṃ cāśrayathā samādhikuśalā bhāvetha co mārdavam /
children.translated_text: Give the gift of the excellent jewel of <s>dharma</s>! Always guard <s>kṣānti</s> (patience)! Resort to the forest! Skilled in <s>samādhi</s>, cultivate gentleness!

children.text: mā co vigraha sarvathā vicarathā śiṣṭāṃ śivāṃ cārikāṃ
children.translated_text: Do not engage in contention at all! Walk the virtuous and auspicious path!

children.text: gacchāmo vayu rājadhāni nagaraṃ sattvāna trāṇārthikāḥ // SRS_35.8 //
children.translated_text: Let us go, friends, to the royal capital city, wishing to protect beings! // SRS_35.8 //

children.text: tasminnotaratī mahāmatidhare sattvāgrasāre ṛṣau
children.translated_text: When that great sage, the foremost of beings, the <s>ṛṣi</s>, was about to depart,

children.text: vartentī imi aśrukāḥ sukaruṇaṃ pādehi anye patī /
children.translated_text: they shed tears with great compassion, others falling at his feet, crying out in anguish:

children.text: mā hī otarahī mahāmati vidu prekṣa vane pādapān
children.translated_text: "O great sage, O wise one, do not depart! Behold the trees in the forest —

children.text: mañjugandha manoramān surucirānātmāna trāṇātmakaḥ // SRS_35.9 //
children.translated_text: of sweet fragrance, delightful, most beautiful — protect yourself, O self-protector! // SRS_35.9 //

children.text: te 'pī pūrva vināyakā daśabalāḥ śāntendriyāḥ sūratāḥ
children.translated_text: "Those former Guides too, the Ten-Powered Ones, with senses calmed and gentle,

children.text: gatvā kānani śailaśṛṅgaśikhare bodhādhigamyāṃ varām /
children.translated_text: going to forests and mountain peaks and ridges, attained the supreme awakening!

children.text: śreṣṭhāṃ cārika bodhihetu caritāste puṇyajñānāṃ varāḥ
children.translated_text: The most excellent conduct for the cause of awakening they practiced — supreme in merit and knowledge —

children.text: teṣāṃ śikṣihi kānane nivasato mā gaccha tvaṃ suvrata // SRS_35.10 //
children.translated_text: train in their [example], dwelling in the forest! Do not go, O one of good vows! // SRS_35.10 //

children.text: gātraṃ citritu lakṣaṇaiḥ suruciraiḥ keśāśca nīlāstavā
children.translated_text: "Your body is adorned with beautiful marks, and your hair is dark blue;

children.text: varṇaḥ kāñcanasaṃnibhaprabhakaro obhāsate medinīm /
children.translated_text: your complexion, like golden radiance, illuminates the earth!

children.text: ūrṇā te bhramukhāntare surucirā śaṅkhanikāśaprabhā
children.translated_text: The <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft of hair) between your brows is beautiful, with radiance like a conch —

children.text: mā te īrṣyu janitva kāyu vikirī rājānurāje tathā // SRS_35.11 //
children.translated_text: lest princes or those like them, generating jealousy, destroy your body! // SRS_35.11 //"

body.text: atha khalvānanda supuṣpacandro dharmabhāṇakastaṃ bodhisattvagaṇaṃ gāthayābhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then, <s>Ānanda</s>, the <s>dharma</s>-preacher <s>Supuṣpacandra</s> addressed that assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in verse:

children.text: yāvantaḥ parimeṇa āsi sugatāḥ sarvajña kṣīṇāsravāḥ
children.translated_text: "As many <s>Sugatas</s> as existed in the past, omniscient, with defilements destroyed —

children.text: sarve te 'tha kariṃsu loki tribhave bodhādhigamyāṃ varām /
children.translated_text: all of them performed in this world, in the three realms, the supreme awakening conduct!

children.text: śreṣṭhāṃ cārika bodhihetu caritāste puṇyajñānāṃ varāḥ
children.translated_text: The most excellent conduct for the cause of awakening they practiced — supreme in merit and knowledge —

children.text: teṣāṃ śikṣaya bodhisatva niyutā sattvāna trāṇārthikaḥ // SRS_35.12 //
children.translated_text: train in their [example], O <s>Bodhisattvas</s> by the <s>niyutas</s>, wishing to protect beings! // SRS_35.12 //

children.text: sarve kṛtva pradakṣiṇaṃ ṛṣividuṃ pādāni vanditvanā
children.translated_text: All circumambulated the wise <s>ṛṣi</s> and venerated his feet;

children.text: ghoraṃ āśvasato svananti karuṇaṃ krandanta ārtasvaram /
children.translated_text: consoling him in the dreadful [hour], they cried out pitifully, weeping in anguished voices.

children.text: anye chinna prapāta medini patī mūrcchitva sālo yathā
children.translated_text: Others, their legs giving way, fell to the ground, fainting like <s>śāla</s> trees —

children.text: no cā te parivarti puṇyanicitaḥ sattvārthakāmo ṛṣiḥ // SRS_35.13 //
children.translated_text: but that <s>ṛṣi</s>, rich in merit, desiring the welfare of beings, did not turn back. // SRS_35.13 //

body.text:
pātraṃ cīvaru gṛhya prasthitu ṛṣī siṃho yathā kesarī
no cāsyo guṇadoṣa tatra akarī dharmasvabhāve sthitaḥ /

children.text: (Vaidya 236)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 236)

children.text: ghane kānani asmi loki vasataḥ sattvā apāye pati
children.translated_text: "While we dwell in the dense forest, in this world, beings fall into misfortune —"

children.text: so 'bhūttaṃ nagaraṃ gamī puravaraṃ sattvānaṃ trāṇārthikaḥ // SRS_35.14 //
children.translated_text: so he went to that city, the excellent town, wishing to protect beings. // SRS_35.14 //

body.translated_text: Taking his bowl and robe, the <s>ṛṣi</s> set forth like a lion, a maned lion; he made no distinction of virtue or fault therein, established in the own-nature of <s>dharma</s>.

body.text:
atha khalu supuṣpacandro dharmabhāṇako grāmanagaranigamarāṣṭarājadhānīravataritvā sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati sma | tena pūrvāhṇe avataritvā sattvānāṃ navanavati prāṇikoṭyaḥ avaivartiṃkatāyāṃ sthāpitāḥ anuttarāyāḥ samyaksaḥbodhau | na ca tāḥ ratnāvatīḥ rājadhānīmanuprāptaḥ | so 'nupūrveṇa tāḥ ratnāvatīḥ rājadhānīmanuprāptaḥ | sa tasyāḥ ratnāvatyāḥ rājadhānyāmupasaḥkramitvā anyatarasmin plakṣasālamūle vyahārṣīt | sa tasyā rātryā atyayena tāḥ ratnāvatīḥ rājadhānīḥ prāviśat | praviśya ṣaṭatriḥśatprāṇikoṭīravaivartikatve sthāpayati buddhadharmeṣu | na ca tāvad bhaktakṛtyamakārṣīt | sa bhaktacchedacchinno ratnāvatyā rājadhānyā niṣkramya yena bhagavato nakhastūpastenopasaḥkramya āsthitaka eva rātriḥdivamatināmayati sma | sa tasyā rātryā atyayena dvitīye prāgbhakte ratnāvatīḥ rājadhānīḥ praviśya trayoviḥśatiprāṇikoṭīravaivartikabuddhadharmeṣu pratiṣṭhāpayati sma | na ca tāvad bhaktakṛtyamakārṣīt | sa dvitīyabhaktacchedacchinno ratnāvatyā rājadhānyā niṣkramya yena bhagavato nakhastūpastenopasaḥkramya utthitaka eva rātriḥdivamatināmayati sma | sa tasyāḥ rātryāmatītāyāḥ trirātrabhaktacchedacchinno ratnāvatīḥ rājadhānīḥ praviśya navanavatiprāṇikoṭīśatasahasrāṇyavaivartikabuddhadharmeṣu pratiṣṭhāpayati sma | na ca tāvad bhaktakṛtyamakārṣīt | sa trirātrabhaktacchedacchinno ratnāvatyā rājadhānyā niṣkramya yena bhagavato nakhastūpastenopasaḥkramya utthitaka eva tṛtīyaḥ rātriḥdivamatināmayati sma | sa tasyā rātryā atyayena caturthe prāgbhakte ratnāvatīḥ rājadhānīḥ praviśya navanavatiprāṇiśatasahasrāṇyavaivartikabuddhadharmeṣu pratiṣṭhāpayati | sa caturdivasabhaktacchedacchinno ratnāvatyā rājadhānyā niṣkramya yena bhagavato nakhastūpastenopasaḥkramya utthitaka eva rātriḥdivamatināmayati sma | sa tasyā rātryā atyayena pañcame divase ratnāvatīḥ rājadhānīḥ praviśya rājño 'ntaḥpuraḥ prāviśat | pravisya cāśītiḥ strīsahasrāṇyavaivartikatve 'nuttarāyāḥ samaksaḥbodhau pratiṣṭhāpayati sma | tasmācca nagarāt sarvasattvānavaivartikatāyāḥ sthāpayati buddhadharmeṣu | sa tasyā rātryā atyayena ṣaṣṭhe prāgbhakte ratnāvatīḥ rājadhānīḥ praviśya sahasraḥ
rājaputrāṇāmavaivartikatve sthāpayati sma anuttarāyāḥ samyaksaḥbodhau | na ca tāvad bhaktasya kṛtyaḥ karoti sma | sa ṣaṣṭhe bhaktacchedacchinno ratnāvatyā rājadhānyā niṣkramya yena bhagavato nakhastūpastenopasaḥkramya rātriḥdivamatināmayati sma | sa tasya rātryā atyayena saptame purobhakte ratnāvatīḥ rājadhānīḥ praviśyādrākṣīcchūradattaḥ rājānamudyānamabhiniṣkramantaḥ suvarṇamayena rathena rūpyamayaiḥ pakṣabhiruragasāracandanamayyā īṣayā vaidūryamayaiścakraiḥ ucchritacchatradhvajasamalaḥkṛtena īṣāpaṭṭāvanaddhena dūṣyapaṭṭasaḥchāditena (Vaidya 237) yatrāṣṭau śatāni kumārīṇāḥ ratnasūtraparigṛhītānām, yāstaḥ rathaḥ vāhayanti abhirūpāḥ prāsādikā darśanīyāḥ paramayā śubhravarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgatāḥ pritikārye audvilyakārye bālānāḥ na piṇḍatānām | caturaśītikṣatriyamahāśālakulasahasrāṇi pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddhānyabhūvan | caturaśītibrāhmaṇamahāśālasahasrāṇi caturaśītigṛhapatimahāśālasahasrāṇi pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nubaddhānyabhūvan | pañca ca duhitṛśatāni ratnamayīśibikābhirūḍhāḥ purato niryānti sma | tāḥ sahadarśanenaiva tasya bhikṣoravaivartikā abhūvannanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaḥbodhau | aṣṭaḥaḥṭiścāntaḥpurikāśatasahasrāṇi sahadarśanenaiva tasya bhikḥuravaivartikānyabhūvannanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaḥbodhau | sa ca mahājanakāyo maṇikuṇḍalānyapanīya pādukāścāpanīya ekāḥsaḥ cīvaraḥ prāvṛtya dakḥiṇaḥ jānumaṇḍalaḥ pṛthivyāḥ pratiḥṭhāpya yena sa bhikḥustenāñjaliḥ praṇamya namasyamānaḥ sthito 'bhūt | atha khalu tā api kumārthaḥ pūrvakaiḥ kuśalamūlaiḥ saḥcoditāḥ samānāstābhyaḥ śibikābhyo 'vataritvā ekāḥsaḥ cīvaraḥ prāvṛtya dakḥiṇaḥ jānumaṇḍalaḥ pṛthivyāḥ pratiḥṭhāpya yena sa bhi stenāñjāla praṇamya gāthābhiradhyabhāḥanta -
body.translated_text: Then the Dharma-preacher <s>Supuṣpacandra</s>, having descended into villages, towns, market-towns, kingdoms, and royal capitals, taught the <s>Dharma</s> to beings. Having descended in the morning, he established ninety-nine <s>koṭīs</s> of living beings in irreversibility toward unsurpassed, perfect awakening. And he had not yet reached the royal capital <s>Ratnāvatī</s>. Gradually he reached that royal capital <s>Ratnāvatī</s>. Having approached that royal capital <s>Ratnāvatī</s>, he rested at the foot of a certain <s>plakṣa</s>-<s>śāla</s> tree. When that night had passed, he entered that royal capital <s>Ratnāvatī</s>. Upon entering, he established thirty-six <s>koṭīs</s> of living beings in irreversibility toward <s>Buddha</s>-qualities. And he had not yet taken his meal. Having gone without food, he departed from the royal capital <s>Ratnāvatī</s> and approached the fingernail <s>stūpa</s> of the Blessed One, where he passed the night and day standing. When that night had passed, on the second morning he entered the royal capital <s>Ratnāvatī</s> and established twenty-three <s>koṭīs</s> of living beings in irreversibility toward <s>Buddha</s>-qualities. And he had not yet taken his meal. Having gone without food for a second time, he departed from the royal capital <s>Ratnāvatī</s> and approached the fingernail <s>stūpa</s> of the Blessed One, where he passed the night and day standing. When that night had passed, having gone without food for three nights, he entered the royal capital <s>Ratnāvatī</s> and established ninety-nine hundred thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of living beings in irreversibility toward <s>Buddha</s>-qualities. And he had not yet taken his meal. Having gone without food for three nights, he departed from the royal capital <s>Ratnāvatī</s> and approached the fingernail <s>stūpa</s> of the Blessed One, where he passed the third night and day standing. When that night had passed, on the fourth morning he entered the royal capital <s>Ratnāvatī</s> and established ninety-nine hundred thousand living beings in irreversibility toward <s>Buddha</s>-qualities. Having gone without food for four days, he departed from the royal capital <s>Ratnāvatī</s> and approached the fingernail <s>stūpa</s> of the Blessed One, where he passed the night and day standing. When that night had passed, on the fifth day he entered the royal capital <s>Ratnāvatī</s> and entered the inner palace of the king. Upon entering, he established eighty thousand women in irreversibility toward unsurpassed, perfect awakening. And he established all beings from that city in irreversibility toward <s>Buddha</s>-qualities. When that night had passed, on the sixth morning he entered the royal capital <s>Ratnāvatī</s> and established a thousand princes in irreversibility toward unsurpassed, perfect awakening. And he had not yet taken his meal. Having gone without food for six days, he departed from the royal capital <s>Ratnāvatī</s> and approached the fingernail <s>stūpa</s> of the Blessed One, where he passed the night and day. When that night had passed, on the seventh morning, having entered the royal capital <s>Ratnāvatī</s>, <s>Śūradatta</s> saw the king setting out for the garden in a golden chariot with silver wings, a shaft of serpent-sandalwood, wheels of <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, adorned with raised parasols and banners, bound with cloth on the shaft-seat, covered with silk fabrics — (<s>Vaidya</s> 237) wherein eight hundred maidens, garlanded with jeweled strings, drew that chariot — beautiful, lovely, fair to behold, endowed with supreme radiance of fair complexion — causing delight and joy, youthful, not yet old. Eighty-four thousand families of <s>Kṣatriya</s> great nobles followed behind. Eighty-four thousand <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> great nobles, eighty-four thousand householder great nobles followed behind. And five hundred daughters, mounted on jeweled palanquins, came forth in front. Those [women], at the very sight of that monk, became irreversible toward unsurpassed, perfect awakening. And eighty-eight hundred thousand women of the inner palace, at the very sight of that monk, became irreversible toward unsurpassed, perfect awakening. And that great crowd, removing their jeweled earrings and taking off their sandals, wrapping their upper garments over one shoulder, placing their right knees on the ground, joining their palms toward that monk, stood bowing in reverence. Then those princesses too, impelled by their previous roots of merit, descended from their palanquins, wrapped their upper garments over one shoulder, placed their right knees on the ground, and joining their palms toward that monk, praised him with verses —

children.text: avabhāsitamadyaivaṃ raviṇeva samantataḥ /
children.translated_text: Today [the city] is illuminated on all sides, as if by the sun,

children.text: bhikṣuṇā praviśantena janakāyaśca dhiṣṭhitaḥ // SRS_35.15 //
children.translated_text: by the monk entering, and the crowd is inspired. // SRS_35.15 //

children.text: rāgadoṣāḥ samucchinnā mohāśca vidhamīkṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: Passion and hatred are cut off, and delusion is dispelled;

children.text: krodho doṣaśca īrṣyā ca sarvaṃ chinnaṃ tadantaram // SRS_35.16 //
children.translated_text: anger, malice, and envy — all are severed at that moment. // SRS_35.16 //

children.text: na rājaṃ prekṣate kaścinnaṃ caivamanuyātyasau /
children.translated_text: No one looks at the king, nor does anyone follow him —

children.text: yo rājñaḥ śūradattasya parivāraḥ sutādikaḥ // SRS_35.17 //
children.translated_text: the retinue, sons, and others of King <s>Śūradatta</s>. // SRS_35.17 //

children.text: pūrṇamāsyāṃ yathā candro nakṣatraparivāritaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as on the full moon night, the moon is surrounded by stars,

children.text: evaṃ sa śobhate bhikṣū rājaputrapuraskṛtaḥ // SRS_35.18 //
children.translated_text: so that monk shines, attended by princes. // SRS_35.18 //

children.text: svarṇabimbaṃ yathā citraṃ kuśalebhiḥ sucitritam /
children.translated_text: Like a golden image, beautifully painted by skilled artists,

children.text: puṣpitaḥ sālarājo vā emeva bhikṣu śobhate // SRS_35.19 //
children.translated_text: or like the king of <s>śāla</s> trees in bloom — even so that monk shines. // SRS_35.19 //

children.text: śakraśca devendra mahānubhāvaḥ sahasranetrādhipatiḥ puraṃdaraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of gods, of great power, the thousand-eyed lord, destroyer of cities,

children.text: sumerumūrdhni tridaśāna īśvaro emeva bhikṣuḥ praviśatu śobhate 'yam // SRS_35.20 //
children.translated_text: the lord of the thirty [gods] on the summit of <s>Sumeru</s> — even so this monk entering shines. // SRS_35.20 //

children.text: brahmeva manye pratiṣṭhitu brahmaloke sunirmito vādhipati devaputraḥ /
children.translated_text: Like <s>Brahmā</s>, I think, established in the <s>Brahma</s>-world, or <s>Sunirmita</s>, the lord, a son of the gods,

children.text: suyāmu devo yathariva kāmadhātau emeva bhikṣuḥ praviśatu śobhate 'yam // SRS_35.21 //
children.translated_text: or <s>Suyāma</s>, the god, as if in the realm of desire — even so this monk entering shines. // SRS_35.21 //

children.text: (Vaidya 238)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 238)

children.text: sūryo vā manye pratapati antarīkṣe sahasraraśmirvidhamiya andhakāram /
children.translated_text: Or like the sun, I think, blazing in the sky, the thousand-rayed one dispelling darkness,

children.text: obhāsayanto samu diśatā samantād emeva bhikṣuḥ praviśatu śobhate 'yam // SRS_35.22 //
children.translated_text: illuminating all the directions entirely — even so this monk entering shines. // SRS_35.22 //

children.text: dānaṃ daditvā suvipula nantakalpān rakṣitva śīlaṃ aśabalu nityakālam /
children.translated_text: Having given vast generosity for endless <s>kalpas</s>, having guarded morality, unstained, at all times,

children.text: bhāvetva kṣāntimasadṛśa sarvaloke so lakṣaṇebhiḥ parivṛtu eva śobhī // SRS_35.23 //
children.translated_text: having cultivated patience unequaled in all the world — he shines, surrounded by the [major] marks. // SRS_35.23 //

children.text: janayitva vīryaṃ ariyajanapraśastaṃ sevitva dhyānā caturi alīnacittaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having generated vigor praised by noble people, having practiced the four <s>dhyānas</s> with undistracted mind,

children.text: utpādya prajñāṃ nihaniya kleśajālaṃ tenaiṣa bhikṣuḥ pratapati sarvaloke // SRS_35.24 //
children.translated_text: having produced wisdom, destroying the net of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) — therefore this monk blazes throughout all the world. // SRS_35.24 //

children.text: ye buddhavīrā asadṛśa sattvasārāḥ samatīta śūrā vikiriya dharmaśreṣṭhān /
children.translated_text: Those <s>Buddha</s>-heroes, incomparable, the essence of beings, who have passed beyond, brave ones, scattering the best of <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: ye 'nāgate 'dhve tathariva pratyutpanne tenaiṣa putro vaśagānu dharmarājñaḥ // SRS_35.25 //
children.translated_text: those in the future age and likewise in the present — therefore this one is a son under the authority of the <s>Dharma</s>-king. // SRS_35.25 //

children.text: mā te anityaṃ bhavatu kadāci bhikṣo yadrapataivaṃ pratapasi sarvaloke /
children.translated_text: May impermanence never befall you, O monk, you who blaze thus throughout all the world;

children.text: saṃpaśya tejo surucira śabdaghoṣo rājāna tejo na tapati suṣṭhu bhūyaḥ // SRS_35.26 //
children.translated_text: behold this radiance, beautiful, of resounding fame — the king's radiance no longer shines so greatly. // SRS_35.26 //

children.text: dharmo yathāyaṃ adhigatu ātmanā te buddhānujñāto vicarasi sarvaloke /
children.translated_text: This <s>Dharma</s>, as you have attained it yourself, authorized by the <s>Buddha</s>, you wander throughout all the world;

children.text: emeva sarve vijahita istribhāvaṃ sarve 'pi yāmo yathariva eṣa bhikṣuḥ // SRS_35.27 //
children.translated_text: even so, may we all abandon the female state — may we all go forth just like this monk. // SRS_35.27 //

children.text: te añjalīyo daśanakha kṛtva sarve bhāṣitva gāthāḥ kṣipiṃsu pilandhanāni /
children.translated_text: All of them, making <s>añjali</s> (joined palms) with ten fingers, having spoken these verses, cast down their ornaments,

children.text: sauvarṇamālā tathapi ca muktahārānavataṃsakāni tathapi ca karṇaniṣkān // SRS_35.28 //
children.translated_text: golden garlands and also pearl necklaces, head-wreaths and also ear-ornaments. // SRS_35.28 //

body.text:
rājā vai yatha cakravarti balavān sarvān vipaśyī mahī
putrasaṃjña upasthapeti vicaran dvīpāni catvārime /

children.text: (Vaidya 239)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 239)

children.text: śreṣṭhī kṣatriya brāhmaṇāṃ gṛhapatī ye koṭṭarājā svakā
children.translated_text: nobles, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, householders, and vassal kings —

children.text: no teṣāmatireku sneha janayī sarveṣu premaṃ samam // SRS_35.29 //
children.translated_text: he does not generate excessive affection for any of them, [but] equal love for all. // SRS_35.29 //

body.translated_text: Just as a powerful universal monarch (<s>cakravartin</s>), seeing all, establishes the perception of sonship in the people while traversing these four continents,

children.text: evaṃ śikṣita dhāraṇīvaśagato bhikṣū ayaṃ sūrato
children.translated_text: So too, this gentle monk, trained, master of <s>dhāraṇī</s>,

children.text: bodhyaṅgā bala indriyān bibhajati mārgaṃ ca aṣṭāṅgikam /
children.translated_text: distributes the limbs of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), the powers, the faculties, and the eightfold path.

children.text: candro vā yatha rātriye pratapati tārāgaṇairmadhyago
children.translated_text: Like the moon blazing in the night amid the host of stars,

children.text: sūryaśco yatha maṇḍalaṃ pratapate vairocanastejavān // SRS_35.30 //
children.translated_text: or like the sun, <s>Vairocana</s>, powerful in radiance, blazing in its orb. // SRS_35.30 //

children.text: sarvān buddhānnamasyāmo daśabalān śāntendriyān sūratān
children.translated_text: We pay homage to all the <s>Buddhas</s>, possessors of the ten powers, with calmed faculties, gentle,

children.text: yeṣāṃ varṇanu kaścidutsahi naro kalpāśataiḥ kṣepitum /
children.translated_text: whose praise no person could exhaust even in hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>.

children.text: kalpā koṭisahasra bhāṣitu bahūn no ced guṇā kṣepituṃ
children.translated_text: Though one spoke for thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, one could not exhaust the qualities,

children.text: no co varṇa kṣipeya lokapravare ekasya romasya hi // SRS_35.31 //
children.translated_text: nor could one exhaust the praise of even a single hair-pore of the best in the world. // SRS_35.31 //

children.text: yeno cakra pravartitaṃ asadṛśaṃ jñānopadaṃ deśitaṃ
children.translated_text: By whom the incomparable wheel was turned, the teaching of knowledge was proclaimed,

children.text: nipuṇaṃ dharma prabhāṣitasya virajaṃ no cāsya dṛśyaṃ kvacit /
children.translated_text: the subtle <s>Dharma</s> was spoken — stainless, not visible anywhere.

children.text: śramaṇābrāhmaṇadevānāga asuraurmāraiḥ sabrahmādibhir
children.translated_text: By <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Māras</s>, and those including <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: no śakto guṇaārṇavaḥ prakathituṃ buddhasya sarvajñinaḥ // SRS_35.32 //
children.translated_text: the ocean of qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>, the Omniscient One, cannot be recounted. // SRS_35.32 //

body.text:
vandāmo jinavaidyarājamasamaṃ yasyedṛśā aurasāḥ
bhāṣitvā imi gātha sarvi muditā rājñaḥ kumāryastadā /

children.text: svarṇaṃ kāñcanacūrṇakāṃśca prakirī cailāni ca prastarī
children.translated_text: scattered gold, gold-dust, and spread garments,

children.text: cūḍānāṃ ca maṇīn sahārarucirā koṭīśatāmūlikā
children.translated_text: jewels from their diadems along with beautiful pearl necklaces, and hundreds of <s>koṭīs</s> of root-gems,

children.text: taṃ bhikṣuṃ abhichādayitva muditā bodhāya saṃprasthitāḥ // SRS_35.33 //
children.translated_text: and having covered that monk [with offerings], delighted, they set out for awakening. // SRS_35.33 //

body.translated_text: We pay homage to the <s>Jina</s>, the incomparable Physician-King, whose sons are such [as this]!' Having spoken these verses, the princesses of the king, all delighted,

body.text: atha khalu rājñaḥ śūradattasyaitadabhavat - vipratipannaṃ batedamantaḥpuraṃ janakāyaśca vyutthitaḥ | sa ca jano maṇikuṇḍalānyapanīya ekāṃsaṃ cīvaramāvṛtya dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena sa bhikṣustenāñjaliṃ praṇamya namasyati sma | sa ca rājā śūradattastāvat prāsādiko 'bhūt tāvaddarśanīyo na ca tāvadabhirūpo yāvadabhirūpaḥ sa bhikṣuḥ | sa rājyahetoruttrasto 'bhūt | rūpakāyapariniṣpattiṃ ca tasya bhikṣodṛṣṭvā atīva roṣamakārṣīt | tasya ca bhikṣo rājamārgasthasya rājñaścakṣurbhyāṃ praviṣṭaḥ | tasyaitadabhavat - saṃraktacittenaitena bhikṣuṇā mamāntaḥpuraḥ dṛṣṭam | akṣibhyāṃ cānena saṃketaḥ kṛtaḥ | tasyaitadabhavat - ka idānīmimaṃ bhikṣuṃ jīvitād vyavaropayiṣyatīti | atha rājñaḥ śūradattasyaḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ putrasahasramanubaddhamabhūt | sa tānāmantrayati sma - vyavaropayadhvaṃ kumārā etaṃ bhikṣuṃ jīvitāditi ||
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śūradatta</s> thought: 'This inner palace has gone astray, and the crowd has risen up!' And that crowd, removing their jeweled earrings, wrapping their upper garments over one shoulder, placing their right knees on the ground, joining their palms toward that monk, were bowing in reverence. Now King <s>Śūradatta</s> was handsome and fair to behold, but not as beautiful as that monk. He became alarmed for his kingdom. And seeing the perfection of that monk's physical form, he became exceedingly enraged. And that monk, standing on the royal road, entered the king's field of vision. He thought: 'This monk, with lustful mind, has looked upon my inner palace. And with his eyes he has made a signal.' He thought: 'Who now will deprive this monk of life?' Now behind King <s>Śūradatta</s>, a thousand sons followed. He addressed them: 'Put this monk to death, princes!'

body.text:
(Vaidya 240)
atha khalu te kumārā rājñaḥ śūradattasya prativahanti sma tasya bhikṣoḥ kṛtaśaḥ | tasyaitadabhavat - putrā api me ājñāṃ na kurvanti | eka evāhaṃ sthāpitaḥ advitīyaḥ | ka idānīmimaṃ bhikṣuṃ jīvitādvayavaropayiṣyati? atha rājñaḥ śūradattasya nandiko nāma vadhyaghātako 'bhūt caṇḍaḥ sāhasiko raudraḥ | atha rājā śūradattastuṣṭa udagraḥ āttamanāḥ evaṃ cintayāmāsa - ayaṃ nandika etaṃ bhikṣuṃ jīvitādvayavaropayiṣyati | atha khalu nandiko vadhyaghātako yena rājā śūradattastenopasaṃkrāmat | atha khalu rājā śūradattastamāha - śakṣyasi tvaṃ nandika etaṃ bhikṣuṃ jīvitādvayavaropayitum? mahāntaṃ te 'bhicchādaṃ dāsyāmi | nandika āha - suṣṭhu deva, yathājñāpayasi | adyainaṃ bhikṣuṃ jīvitādvayavaropayiṣyāmi | tena hi nandika yasyedānīṃ kālaṃ manyase | tīkṣṇamasiṃ gṛhītvā etaṃ bhikṣorhastapādaṃ chinda | karṇanāsāṃ chinda | anena me saṃraktacittenāntaḥpuraṃ prekṣitam | ato 'sya saṃdaṃśenākṣiṇī utpāṭaya | atha nandikena vadhyaghātakena tasyāmena velāyāṃ tīkṣṇamasiṃ gṛhītvā bhikṣohastapādāśchinnā akṣiṇī cotpāṭite | tato 'sau mahān janakāyo rudan krandan paridevamānaḥ punarapi ratnāvatīṃ rājadhānīṃ praviṣṭaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 240) Then those princes refused King <s>Śūradatta</s>'s repeated [commands] regarding that monk. He thought: 'Even my sons do not obey my command. I alone am left, without a second. Who now will deprive this monk of life?' Now King <s>Śūradatta</s> had an executioner named <s>Nandika</s> — cruel, violent, and fierce. Then King <s>Śūradatta</s>, delighted, elated, and joyful, thought thus: 'This <s>Nandika</s> will deprive that monk of life.' Then the executioner <s>Nandika</s> approached King <s>Śūradatta</s>. Then King <s>Śūradatta</s> said to him: 'Are you able, <s>Nandika</s>, to deprive this monk of life? I shall give you a great reward.' <s>Nandika</s> said: 'Very well, Your Majesty, as you command. Today I shall deprive this monk of life.' 'Then, <s>Nandika</s>, whenever you think it is time — taking a sharp sword, cut off this monk's hands and feet! Cut off his ears and nose! He looked upon my inner palace with a passionate mind — therefore, with pincers, gouge out his eyes!' Then the executioner <s>Nandika</s>, at that very moment, taking a sharp sword, cut off the monk's hands and feet, and gouged out his eyes. Then that great multitude of people, weeping, wailing, and lamenting, entered again into the royal capital <s>Ratnavatī</s>.

body.text: atha khalu rājā śūradattaḥ saptāhasyātyayādudyānagato na ramate na krīḍati na paricārayati | sa udyānānnivṛttaḥ saptāhasyātyayena ratnāvatīṃ rājadhānīṃ prāviśat | so 'drākṣīttaṃ bhikṣuṃ rājamārge choritaṃ saptāhamṛtakaṃ avivarṇaśarīram | tasyaitadabhūt - yathāyaṃ bhikṣuravivarṇaśarīraḥ, niḥsaṃśayameṣa bhikṣuravaivartiko bhaviṣyatyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | pāpaṃ mayā karma kṛtaṃ mahānagarakasaṃvartanīyam | kṣiprameva mayā mahāniraye pratipattavyaṃ bhaviṣyati | tasyaivaṃ cintayataḥ uparyantarīkṣe caturaśītibhirdevaputrasahasrairekarutasvaraghoṣaśabdamudīritam - evametanmahārāja yathā vadasi | avaivartika eṣa bhikṣuranuttarḥyḥṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | tasya tḥvad bhūyasyḥ mḥtrayḥ bhayaṃ ca trḥsaṃ ca stambhitatvaṃ ca romaharṣaścotpanno vipratisḥraścḥbhūt | atha rḥjḥ śūradatto duḥkhito durmanḥ vipratisḥrī tasyḥṃ velḥyḥmimḥ gḥthḥ abhḥṣata -
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śūradatta</s>, after the passing of seven days, went to his pleasure garden but did not enjoy himself, did not play, did not take amusement. Having returned from the garden after seven days, he entered the royal capital <s>Ratnavatī</s>. He saw that monk cast aside on the royal highway — seven days dead, yet with body unaltered in color. He thought: 'Since this monk's body is unaltered in color, without doubt this monk must be irreversible from unsurpassed, perfect and complete awakening. Evil <s>karma</s> has been done by me, leading to rebirth in the great <s>Avīci</s> hell. Quickly I shall have to fall into the great hell.' While he was thinking thus, eighty-four thousand <s>devaputras</s> in the sky above uttered a sound with a single voice: 'It is just so, O great king, as you say! This monk is irreversible from unsurpassed, perfect and complete awakening.' Thereupon, even greater dread, terror, stupefaction, and hair-raising arose in him, and he was filled with remorse. Then King <s>Śūradatta</s>, grieved, dejected, and remorseful, at that moment spoke these verses:

children.text: rājyaṃ tyajiṣye tathapi ca rājadhānīṃ hiraṇya suvarṇaṃ tatha maṇimukta ratnān /
children.translated_text: 'I shall give up my kingdom and also my royal capital, gold, silver, gems, pearls, and jewels;

children.text: ghāteyamātmā svaya śastra gṛhya nihīnakarmāsmiha bālabuddhiḥ // SRS_35.34 //
children.translated_text: I shall slay myself, taking up a weapon — I am of base deeds, of foolish intellect here.' // SRS_35.34 //

children.text: supuṣpacandro 'yamiha bhikṣurāsīd dvātriṃśatā kavacitu lakṣaṇebhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'That monk <s>Supuṣpacandra</s> was here, armored with the thirty-two marks;

children.text: obhāsayanto praviśati rājadhānīṃ nakṣatrarājo yathariva pūrṇamāsyām // SRS_35.35 //
children.translated_text: illuminating [everything], he entered the royal capital, like the king of stars (the moon) at the full.' // SRS_35.35 //

children.text: (Vaidya 241)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 241)

children.text: ahaṃ ca hīnaḥ pralulitu kāmabhoge nārīgaṇenā pramuditu niṣkramāmi /
children.translated_text: 'And I, base, wallowing in sensual enjoyments, went forth rejoicing with a troop of women,

children.text: rathābhirūḍhaḥ parivṛtu kṣatriyebhiḥ ayaṃ ca etī surabhi sunetra bhikṣuḥ // SRS_35.36 //
children.translated_text: mounted on a chariot, surrounded by <s>Kṣatriyas</s> — and this monk <s>Surabhi Sunetra</s> came along.' // SRS_35.36 //

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭva bhikṣuṃ pramuditu nārisaṃgho sauvarṇamālānavasiri premajātā /
children.translated_text: 'Seeing that monk, the troop of women rejoiced; casting golden garlands, filled with love,

children.text: sarve gṛhītvā daśanakhu añjalīyo gāthābhigītaistamabhistaviṃsu bhikṣum // SRS_35.37 //
children.translated_text: all of them, joining their palms with ten nails, praised that monk with verses.' // SRS_35.37 //

children.text: te gītaśabdāḥ praśamita sarvi rājñaḥ sa rathābhirūḍhaḥ parivṛtu kṣatriyebhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Those songs were all silenced by the king; mounted on a chariot, surrounded by <s>Kṣatriyas</s>,

children.text: ayaṃ ca etī surabhi sunetro bhikṣurmahānubhāvaḥ sugatavarasya putraḥ // SRS_35.38 //
children.translated_text: this monk <s>Surabhi Sunetra</s> of great power came along — a son of the best of <s>Sugatas</s>.' // SRS_35.38 //

children.text: mama caiva cittaṃ parama nihīnu māsīdīrṣyāṃ ca krodhaṃ ca tatra janemi mūḍhaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And my mind became supremely base; deluded, I generated jealousy and anger there,

children.text: muditaṃ viditva suvipula nārisaṃgho ālokya bhikṣuṃ praviśatu rājadhānim // SRS_35.39 //
children.translated_text: knowing the vast troop of women to be delighted upon seeing the monk entering the royal capital.' // SRS_35.39 //

children.text: atighorarūpā ahu giri bhāṣi tatra putrasahasraṃ bhaṇami tatkṣaṇasmin /
children.translated_text: 'Of supremely terrible form, I, the mountain [of anger], spoke there; at that instant I addressed a thousand sons:

children.text: gatvāna bhikṣuṃ prakuruta khaṇḍakhaṇḍāmeṣo hi mahyaṃ parama amitra ghoraḥ // SRS_35.40 //
