children.translated_text: "Go and cut this monk to pieces — he is my supreme, terrible enemy!"' // SRS_35.40 //

children.text: te kumāra sarve paramasuśīlavanto svahitaiṣicittā abhirata yena bhikṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Those princes, all of supreme good morality, desiring their own welfare, went to where the monk was;

children.text: āṇatti devā na kariya evarūpā śokābhibhūto ahamabhu tasmi kāle // SRS_35.41 //
children.translated_text: [they said:] "Lord, do not perform such a command!" — I was overcome by grief at that time.' // SRS_35.41 //

children.text: imu bhikṣu dṛṣṭvā parama suśīlavantaṃ maitryā upetaṃ pitaramiva pravṛttam /
children.translated_text: 'Seeing this monk of supreme good morality, endowed with loving-kindness, acting like a father —

children.text: sudṛṣṭacitto avasari ghātanārthaṃ patito avīcau ahu paścakāle // SRS_35.42 //
children.translated_text: yet with corrupted mind I set upon him for slaughter — I fell into <s>Avīci</s> in the afterlife.' // SRS_35.42 //

children.text: yannandiko 'yaṃ iha sthitu rājamārge atiraudrakarmā dukhakaru mānuṣāṇām /
children.translated_text: 'That this <s>Nandika</s> stands here on the royal highway — of supremely cruel deeds, a maker of suffering for humans —

children.text: (Vaidya 242)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 242)

children.text: āṇatti tenā mama kṛta evarūpā mālāguṇo vā ayamiha chinna bhikṣuḥ // SRS_35.43 //
children.translated_text: by him, at my command, this was done — this monk was cut like a garland.' // SRS_35.43 //

children.text: samantabhadre vanavari premaṇīye dvijābhikīrṇe kusumitamañjugandhe /
children.translated_text: 'In the lovely, delightful forest park <s>Samantabhadra</s>, frequented by birds, fragrant with blossoming flowers —

children.text: so cāpi anyaḥ suvipula bhikṣusaṃgho mātrā vihīno yathariva ekaputrakaḥ // SRS_35.44 //
children.translated_text: there too the vast assembly of monks [grieves], deprived of their mother, like an only child [left alone].' // SRS_35.44 //

children.text: uttiṣṭha bhikṣo prativasa kānanasmin kṛto te arthaḥ suvipula mānuṣāṇām /
children.translated_text: 'Arise, O monk! Dwell again in this forest; the welfare of vast [numbers of] humans has been accomplished by you;

children.text: yadrājadhānīmimu tada āgato 'si eṣyanti bhikṣu sukaruṇa krandamānāḥ // SRS_35.45 //
children.translated_text: since you came to this royal capital, monks will come, crying with compassion.' // SRS_35.45 //

children.text: puṣpadhvajāni ima kṛta dakṣiṇenā vāmena anye surucira darśanīyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'These flower-banners were made on the right side, and others — splendid, beautiful — on the left;

children.text: prajñapta mārgaḥ sphuṭa kṛta cīvarebhi uttiṣṭha bhikṣo pratibhaṇa dharma śreṣṭham // SRS_35.46 //
children.translated_text: a path is prepared, fully spread with robes — arise, O monk, proclaim the supreme <s>Dharma</s>!' // SRS_35.46 //

children.text: cirapraviṣṭo tuhu iha rājadhānyāmeṣyanti bhikṣu sukaruṇu krandamānāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'You entered this royal capital long ago; monks will come, crying with compassion;

children.text: mā antarāyo bhava siya jīvitasya pralopakāle jinavaraśāsanasmin // SRS_35.47 //
children.translated_text: let there not be an obstacle to [your] life — in this time of destruction, in the teaching of the best of <s>Jinas</s>.' // SRS_35.47 //

children.text: yathaiva kaścita puruṣa mahānubhāvo dikṣu vidikṣu satatu vighuṣṭaśabdaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Just as a certain man of great power, whose fame resounds constantly in the directions and intermediate directions,

children.text: mahāprapātaṃ prapatati vasuṃdharāyāṃ sarvābhibhūya tribhavamimaṃ samantāt // SRS_35.48 //
children.translated_text: falls into a great precipice upon the earth, overwhelming the entire three realms all around —' // SRS_35.48 //

children.text: emeva bhikṣuriha patito dharaṇyāṃ surūparūpo bhūṣitu lakṣaṇairvaraiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'even so this monk has fallen on the earth — of beautiful form, adorned with the excellent marks,

children.text: adoṣaduṣṭo maya kṛta pāpabuddhinā supuṣpacandro tiṣṭhati khaṇḍakhaṇḍaḥ // SRS_35.49 //
children.translated_text: faultless, [yet] made [to suffer] by me of evil intellect — <s>Supuṣpacandra</s> lies [here] cut to pieces.' // SRS_35.49 //

children.text: bhikṣu iho duḥkhahata sarva eva aprītijātāstathapi ca śalyacittāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The monks here are all stricken with grief, joyless, and with minds pierced as by a dart;

children.text: (Vaidya 243)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 243)

children.text: bheṣyanti kṣipraṃ dṛṣṭvimu dharmabhāṇakaṃ supuṣpacandraṃ hatu patitaṃ pṛthivyām // SRS_35.50 //
children.translated_text: they will be [even more distressed] quickly upon seeing this <s>Dharma</s>-preacher <s>Supuṣpacandra</s>, slain, fallen upon the earth.' // SRS_35.50 //

children.text: supuṣpacandro yathariva śailarājo dvātriṃśatībhiḥ kavacitu lakṣaṇebhiḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Supuṣpacandra</s>, like the king of mountains, armored with the thirty-two marks —

children.text: mālāguṇeva pramadagaṇena gṛhya kṣaṇe vikīrṇaṃ kṛtu khaṇḍakhaṇḍam // SRS_35.51 //
children.translated_text: seized like a garland by the troop of women, in an instant made cut to pieces.' // SRS_35.51 //

children.text: kṛtasmi karmaṃ parama sughorarūpam avīci gamiṣye yamaviṣayamanātho /
children.translated_text: 'I have done supremely terrible <s>karma</s>; I shall go to <s>Avīci</s>, to the realm of <s>Yama</s>, without a protector;

children.text: buddhāna bheṣye parama sudūradūre sa bhikṣuḥ kṛtu iha khaṇḍakhaṇḍam // SRS_35.52 //
children.translated_text: I shall be supremely far from <s>Buddhas</s> — having caused this monk to be cut to pieces here.' // SRS_35.52 //

children.text: na putra trāṇa na pi mama jñātisaṃgho no cāsya mānyā na ca bhaṭapādamūlikāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Neither sons are a refuge, nor my retinue of relatives, nor his honored ones, nor foot-soldiers;

children.text: meṣyanti trāṇaṃ narakagatasya mahyaṃ svayaṃ karitva parama nihīnakarma // SRS_35.53 //
children.translated_text: they will not come as a refuge for me gone to hell — I who have done this supremely base deed myself.' // SRS_35.53 //

children.text: ye 'tīta buddhāstathapi ca ye anāgatāstiṣṭhanti ye co daśasu diśāsu kecit /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever <s>Buddhas</s> of the past and those of the future, and whatever [<s>Buddhas</s>] abide in the ten directions —

children.text: te sārthavāhā daśabalā niṣkileśāḥ śaraṇaṃ upaimī vajraghana ātmabhāvān // SRS_35.54 //
children.translated_text: those caravan-leaders, the ten-powered, free from defilements — I go to them for refuge, with a diamond-firm resolve.' // SRS_35.54 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvān bhikṣuṃ kṛtu iha khaṇḍakhaṇḍaṃ krośaḥ pramuktaḥ sukaruṇa devatābhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Seeing the monk made cut to pieces here, a compassionate cry was released by the deities;

children.text: gatvāna te ārocayi bhikṣusaṃghe supuṣpacandro itu iha rājyadhānyām // SRS_35.55 //
children.translated_text: having gone, they announced to the assembly of monks: "<s>Supuṣpacandra</s> is [slain] here in the royal capital!"' // SRS_35.55 //

children.text: yo 'sau vidu paṇḍitu dharmabhāṇako mahānubhāvo diśividiśāsu ghuṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He who is learned, wise, a <s>Dharma</s>-preacher, of great power, whose fame resounds in the directions and intermediate directions —

children.text: so bodhisattvo pratiṣṭhitu dhāraṇīye supuṣpacandro hatu iha rājadhānyām // SRS_35.56 //
children.translated_text: that <s>Bodhisattva</s>, established in <s>dhāraṇī</s>, <s>Supuṣpacandra</s>, has been slain here in the royal capital.' // SRS_35.56 //

children.text: yo deti dānaṃ vividhamanantakalpān yo śīla rakṣatyaśabalamasaṃpravedhim /
children.translated_text: 'He who gives various gifts for boundless <s>kalpas</s>, who guards morality unblemished and unwavering,

children.text: yo bhāvi kṣāntīmasadṛśa sarvaloke supuṣpacandro hatu iha rājadhānyām // SRS_35.57 //
children.translated_text: who cultivates patience unequaled in all the world — <s>Supuṣpacandra</s> has been slain here in the royal capital.' // SRS_35.57 //

children.text: (Vaidya 244)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 244)

children.text: yo vīryavantaḥ satatamanantakalpān yo dhyānu dhyāyī caturi alīnacitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He who is vigorous constantly for boundless <s>kalpas</s>, who meditates in the four <s>dhyānas</s> with unlax mind,

children.text: yaḥ prajña bhāveti kileśaghātakīṃ supuṣpacandro hatu iha rājadhāniye // SRS_35.58 //
children.translated_text: who cultivates wisdom that destroys the defilements — <s>Supuṣpacandra</s> has been slain here in the royal capital.' // SRS_35.58 //

children.text: yaḥ kāyapremaṃ vijahitva sarvaśo ' napekṣa bhūtvā tatha jīvitāto /
children.translated_text: 'He who has abandoned all attachment to the body, having become indifferent even to life,

children.text: samantabhadrādvanatotaritvā supuṣpacandro hatu iha rājadhāniye // SRS_35.59 //
children.translated_text: having descended from the forest park <s>Samantabhadra</s> — <s>Supuṣpacandra</s> has been slain here in the royal capital.' // SRS_35.59 //

children.text: te rājadhānīṃ praviśitva sūratā ārtasvaraṃ krandiṣu ghorarūpam /
children.translated_text: 'Those [monks], entering the royal capital, gentle, uttered piteous, terrible cries;

children.text: dṛṣṭvān bhikṣuṃ kṛtu iha khaṇḍakhaṇḍaṃ mūrcchitva sarve prapatita te dharaṇyām // SRS_35.60 //
children.translated_text: seeing the monk cut to pieces here, all of them fainted and fell upon the earth.' // SRS_35.60 //

children.text: rājāna taṃ so avaciṣu bhikṣusaṃgho kimāparāddhaṃ tava deva bhikṣuṇā /
children.translated_text: 'The assembly of monks addressed that king: "What offence did this monk commit against you, Your Majesty —

children.text: acchidaśīlena susaṃvṛtena yaḥ pūrvajātiṃ smarate acintiyām // SRS_35.61 //
children.translated_text: one of unbroken morality, well-restrained, who remembers inconceivable former lives?"' // SRS_35.61 //

children.text: eṣo vaśī dhāraṇijñānapārago eṣa prajānātiha śūnya saṃskṛtam /
children.translated_text: '"He is self-mastered, who has reached the far shore of <s>dhāraṇī</s>-knowledge; he knows the conditioned as empty here;

children.text: eṣo 'nimittaṃ jagato nidarśayī praṇidhānasaṃjñāṃ iti sarva varjayī // SRS_35.62 //
children.translated_text: he demonstrates the signless to the world; he has abandoned all notions of vows [as ultimate]."' // SRS_35.62 //

children.text: eṣo muñci manojña ghoṣa ruciraṃ śāntendriyaḥ sūrato
children.translated_text: '"He releases a sweet, delightful, and beautiful voice; of peaceful faculties, gentle;

children.text: eṣo pūrvanivāsapāramigato lokasya abhyudgataḥ /
children.translated_text: he has gone to the far shore of recollecting past lives; he is exalted above the world;

children.text: eṣo buddha svayaṃbhu jñānavṛṣayo lokasya citrīkṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: he is a self-arisen <s>Buddha</s>, a bull of knowledge; he has amazed the world;

children.text: śuddhā cakṣuṣa prekṣiṣū vitimiro atyarthamaitrīkṛpaḥ // SRS_35.63 //
children.translated_text: with pure eye, they behold him, free from darkness — of supremely great loving-kindness and compassion."' // SRS_35.63 //

children.text: kāmā hīna jaghanya duḥkhajananāḥ svargasya nirnāśakāḥ
children.translated_text: '"Sensual pleasures are base, low, generators of suffering, destroyers of heaven;

children.text: kāmān sevatu bhonti śrotravikalāḥ prajñāvihīnā narāḥ /
children.translated_text: by indulging in pleasures, men become deaf and devoid of wisdom;

children.text: kāmān sevatu andhu bhoti manujo mātāpita ghātayī
children.translated_text: by indulging in pleasures, a man becomes blind, a slayer of mother and father;

children.text: kāmān sevatu śīlavantu vadhayī tasmādvivarjennaro // SRS_35.64 //
children.translated_text: by indulging in pleasures, one slays the virtuous — therefore a man should avoid [them]."' // SRS_35.64 //

body.text: (Vaidya 245)

children.text: kāmān sevatu rāja pārthivavarā varjetva ṛddhimimāṃ
children.translated_text: '"By indulging in pleasures, kings, the best of rulers, having abandoned this prosperity,

children.text: ghorān gacchati karkaśān dukhakarānnarakān bhayānantakān /
children.translated_text: go to terrible, harsh, suffering-producing hells, fearsome, endless;

children.text: pāpaṃ karma karoti īdṛśa viduṃ bhikṣuṃ vadhetī sadā
children.translated_text: one who performs evil <s>karma</s> — who always slays such a learned monk —

children.text: tasmāt pāpu vivarjitavyu vividhaṃ yo icchi bodhiṃ śivām // SRS_35.65 //
children.translated_text: therefore various evils should be avoided by one who desires auspicious awakening."' // SRS_35.65 //

body.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 245)

children.text: rūpāṇi śabdān rasa tatha gandha śreṣṭhān spraṣṭavyadharmān tyajati alīnacittaḥ /
children.translated_text: '"Forms, sounds, tastes, and smells — the finest objects of touch — he abandons with unlax mind,

children.text: kāyaṃ viditva yathariva māya tucchaṃ cakṣuṃ ca śrotraṃ tathariva ghrāṇa jihvam // SRS_35.66 //
children.translated_text: knowing the body to be like an illusion, hollow — and the eye, ear, likewise nose and tongue."' // SRS_35.66 //

children.text: dāne śikṣitu śīli apratisamaḥ kṣāntiṃ ca vīryaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: '"Trained in giving, of morality without equal, and patience and vigor likewise;

children.text: dhyānaṃ sevatu prajñapāramigataḥ sattvāna arthakaraḥ /
children.translated_text: cultivating <s>dhyāna</s>, gone to the perfection of wisdom, accomplishing the welfare of beings —

children.text: lokaḥ sarvu sadevakaḥ samanujaḥ prekṣanti maitryā jinaṃ
children.translated_text: the entire world with its gods and humans beholds the <s>Jina</s> with loving-kindness;

children.text: teno cakṣu mahāndhakāragahane budhyanti bodhiṃ śivām // SRS_35.67 //
children.translated_text: by that eye, in the great darkness of the abyss, they awaken to auspicious awakening."' // SRS_35.67 //

children.text: hastī aśvarathāṃstyajanti muditā aṅgālamañcāṃstathā
children.translated_text: '"They give up elephants, horses, chariots, and also palanquins and couches,

children.text: śibikāṃ dollikayugyayānavṛṣabhān grāmāṇi rāṣṭrāṇi ca /
children.translated_text: litters, swings, yokes, vehicles, bulls, villages, and kingdoms;

children.text: nagaraṃ rājya tyajitva svarṇasphaṭikāṃ rūpyaṃ pravālāṃstathā
children.translated_text: having given up cities, kingdoms, gold, crystal, silver, and corals likewise —

children.text: bhāryāpriyaputradhīrasvaśirāstyajitvā bodhiprasthitāḥ // SRS_35.68 //
children.translated_text: wives, dear sons, and steadfastly their own heads — they set out for awakening."' // SRS_35.68 //

children.text: pūjāṃ co atulāṃ karonti muditāḥ puṣpebhi gandhebhi co
children.translated_text: '"And they make incomparable worship, joyful, with flowers and incenses,

children.text: gṛhya cchatradhvajā patāka vividhā saṃgītibhāṇḍāni ca /
children.translated_text: taking up parasols, banners, pennants of various kinds, and musical instruments;

children.text: no cāpī abhinandiṣu bhavagatiṃ jñātvāna śūnyān bhavān
children.translated_text: yet they do not delight in the states of [worldly] existence, having known existences as empty —

children.text: teno lakṣaṇacitritā daśabalā bhāsanti sarvā diśaḥ // SRS_35.69 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, adorned with marks, the Ten-Powered Ones shine in all directions. // SRS_35.69 //

children.text: na kāmadhātau na ca rūpadhātāvārūpyadhātau ca na te niviṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: Not established in the desire-realm, nor in the form-realm, nor in the formless realm —

children.text: traidhātukaṃ nābhiniviṣṭadharmā ye bodhisattvāḥ pratiṣṭhitu dhāraṇīye // SRS_35.70 //
children.translated_text: not established in the phenomena of the three realms — those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> established in the <s>dhāraṇī</s>! // SRS_35.70 //

children.text: no ātmasaṃjñā na ca puna sattvasaṃjñā no jīvasaṃjñā pudgalasaṃjña nāpi /
children.translated_text: No perception of self, nor perception of a being, no perception of a living soul, nor perception of a person —

children.text: nityaṃ carantā aśabalu brahmacaryaṃ ye bodhisattvāḥ pratiṣṭhitu dhāraṇīye // SRS_35.71 //
children.translated_text: always practicing the spotless holy life — those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> established in the <s>dhāraṇī</s>! // SRS_35.71 //

children.text: na bhāvasaṃjñā na ca punarabhāvasaṃjñā na kṣemasaṃjñā na punarakṣemasaṃjñā /
children.translated_text: No perception of existence, nor perception of non-existence, no perception of security, nor perception of insecurity,

children.text: (Vaidya 246)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 246)

children.text: no saukhyasaṃjñā na punarasaukhyasaṃjñā ye bodhisattvāḥ pratiṣṭhitu dhāraṇīye // SRS_35.72 //
children.translated_text: no perception of happiness, nor perception of unhappiness — those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> established in the <s>dhāraṇī</s>! // SRS_35.72 //

children.text: no astisaṃjñā na punarnāstisaṃjñā no istrisaṃjñā na punaḥ puruṣasaṃjñā /
children.translated_text: No perception of 'it exists,' nor perception of 'it does not exist,' no perception of woman, nor perception of man,

children.text: na grāmasaṃjñā na ca nagareṣu saṃjñā no rāṣṭrasaṃjñā na pi nigameṣu saṃjñā // SRS_35.73 //
children.translated_text: no perception of village, nor perception of cities, no perception of kingdom, nor perception of towns. // SRS_35.73 //

children.text: no rāgasaṃjñā na puna virāgasaṃjñā no doṣasaṃjñā na punaradoṣasaṃjñā /
children.translated_text: No perception of passion, nor perception of dispassion, no perception of hatred, nor perception of non-hatred,

children.text: no mohasaṃjñā na punaramohasaṃjñā ye bodhisattvāḥ pratiṣṭhitu dhāraṇīye // SRS_35.74 //
children.translated_text: no perception of delusion, nor perception of non-delusion — those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> established in the <s>dhāraṇī</s>! // SRS_35.74 //

children.text: no indriyebhirna puna te balebhirbodhyaṅgadhyāne na ca puna te niviṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: Not established in the faculties, nor in the powers, nor in the factors of awakening and <s>dhyānas</s> —

children.text: traidhātuke te pravijahi doṣa sarva ye bodhisattvāḥ pratiṣṭhitu dhāraṇīye // SRS_35.75 //
children.translated_text: they have abandoned all faults in the three realms — those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> established in the <s>dhāraṇī</s>! // SRS_35.75 //

children.text: no rāgaraktā na ca puna doṣaduṣṭā no mohamūḍhā aśaṭha bhavanti nityam /
children.translated_text: Not stained by passion, nor corrupted by hatred, nor deluded by delusion — always sincere;

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca buddhā daśabala satkaronti no cāpi svargaṃ matidhara prārthayanti // SRS_35.76 //
children.translated_text: having seen the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Ten-Powered Ones, they honor them, yet those wise ones do not seek heaven. // SRS_35.76 //

children.text: teṣāṃ śrutvā parata viśiṣṭadharmaṃ no bhuya tasmin bhavati kadāci kāṅkṣā /
children.translated_text: Having heard from others the distinguished <s>Dharma</s>, no doubt ever arises in them regarding it;

children.text: tailasya pātraṃ yathariva accha śuddhaṃ chedācchedaṃ paramata tebhi jñātam // SRS_35.77 //
children.translated_text: like a vessel of oil, clear and pure — the cutting of [all] cutting has been known by them from the ultimate. // SRS_35.77 //

children.text: snehaṃ kurvatu jāyate anunayaḥ so 'pī kileśo mahān
children.translated_text: When one makes attachment, affection arises — that too is a great defilement;

children.text: doṣaṃ kurvatu jāyate 'sya pratigho vairaṃ bhayaṃ pāpakam /
children.translated_text: when one makes hostility, aversion arises in him — enmity, fear, and evil.

children.text: dvāvetau vijahitvanā matigharā bodhāya ye prasthitāḥ
children.translated_text: Having abandoned these two, those wise ones who have set out for awakening —

children.text: te bhontīha nararṣabhā daśabalā loke samabhyudgatāḥ // SRS_35.78 //
children.translated_text: they become here the bulls among men, the Ten-Powered Ones, arisen in the world. // SRS_35.78 //

body.text:
adhyātmaṃ prajahitva bāhyamapi co dharmasvabhāve sthitāḥ
śīlaskandhu viśodhito aśabalo akhaṇḍa acchidritaḥ /

children.text: (Vaidya 247)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 247)

children.text: no vā teṣu kadāci śīla śabalaṃ no cāpi kalmāṣatā
children.translated_text: never for them is morality spotted, nor is there mottledness —

children.text: dvāvetau parivarjiyā matidharā budhyanti bodhiṃ śivām // SRS_35.79 //
children.translated_text: having avoided these two, the wise ones awaken to auspicious awakening. // SRS_35.79 //

body.translated_text: Having abandoned the internal and external, established in the own-nature of <s>dharma</s>, the aggregate of morality is purified — spotless, unbroken, unfissured;

children.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: ahaṃ sa pūrve caramāṇu cārikāṃ rājā abhūvaṃ tada śūradattaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I formerly, while wandering on my journey, was a king then, named <s>Śūradatta</s>;

children.text: ratanāvatī nāma sa rājadhānī udyānabhūmiryatu niṣkramāmi // SRS_35.80 //
children.translated_text: my royal capital was named <s>Ratanāvatī</s> — from its garden-ground I went forth. // SRS_35.80 //

children.text: rathābhirūḍhastada dṛṣṭva bhikṣuṃ samantaprāsādiku darśanīyam /
children.translated_text: Mounted on a chariot, I then saw a monk — splendid on all sides, beautiful to behold,

children.text: dvātriṃśatā kavacitu lakṣaṇebhirobhāsayantaṃ daśa diśatā samantāt // SRS_35.81 //
children.translated_text: armored with the thirty-two marks, illuminating the ten directions all around. // SRS_35.81 //

children.text: supuṣpacandro diśatā suviśruto hitānukampī karuṇāvihārī /
children.translated_text: <s>Supuṣpacandra</s>, renowned in the directions, benevolent, compassionate, dwelling in compassion,

children.text: sattvānukampī nagaraṃ praviṣṭaḥ śirīya tejena ca śobhamānaḥ // SRS_35.82 //
children.translated_text: compassionate toward beings, had entered the city — shining with glory and splendor. // SRS_35.82 //

children.text: ahaṃ ca rūpeṇa tādṛśo 'bhavaṃ mātsaryamutpannu subhairavaṃ me /
children.translated_text: And I was of such appearance — terrible jealousy arose in me;

children.text: kāmeṣu gṛddho grathitaśca rājye mā eṣa rājyānmama cyāvayeta // SRS_35.83 //
children.translated_text: greedy for pleasures, bound to kingship: "May he not dislodge me from my kingdom!" // SRS_35.83 //

children.text: putrāṇa saṃpūrṇa sahasra mahyaṃ rathānurūḍhā anuyānti pṛṣṭhataḥ /
children.translated_text: I had a full thousand sons, mounted on chariots, following behind,

children.text: vicitramukuṭābharaṇā vibhūṣitā yatha devaputrāstridaśendra yānti // SRS_35.84 //
children.translated_text: adorned with various crowns and ornaments, like the sons of gods going to <s>Tridaśendra</s> (<s>Indra</s>). // SRS_35.84 //

children.text: duhitṝṇa tasmin śata pañca mahyaṃ maṇipādukārūḍha sudarśanīyāḥ /
children.translated_text: I had five hundred daughters there, standing on jeweled sandals, beautiful to see,

children.text: ābaddhamukuṭābharaṇā vibhūṣitāste hemajālai rathu te vahanti // SRS_35.85 //
children.translated_text: adorned with bound crowns and ornaments — those golden-netted chariots carried them. // SRS_35.85 //

children.text: strīṇāṃ sahasrāṇi aśīti mahyaṃ prāsādikāḥ sarva sudarśanīyāḥ /
children.translated_text: I had eighty thousand women, all graceful, all beautiful to see,

children.text: (Vaidya 248)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 248)

children.text: rathādhirūḍhāḥ samudīkṣya bhikṣuṃ prāsādikaṃ merumivodgataśriyam // SRS_35.86 //
children.translated_text: mounted on chariots, they beheld the monk — graceful, of glory risen like <s>Meru</s>. // SRS_35.86 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca tāsāṃ pitṛsaṃjña jātā utpāditaṃ citta varāgrabodhaye /
children.translated_text: Having seen [him], the perception of a father arose in them; they directed their minds toward supreme awakening;

children.text: samādayitvā tada brahmacaryaṃ kṣipiṃsu tānābharaṇān manoramān // SRS_35.87 //
children.translated_text: having undertaken the holy life, they cast away those delightful ornaments. // SRS_35.87 //

children.text: īrṣyā mamotpanna abhūṣi tatkṣaṇaṃ vyāpādadoṣaśca khilaṃ cā dāruṇam /
children.translated_text: Jealousy arose in me at that very instant — hostility, hatred, and cruel obstinacy;

children.text: aiśvaryamattaśca vadāmi putrān ghāteya bhikṣuṃ sthitu yaḥ purastāt // SRS_35.88 //
children.translated_text: intoxicated with sovereignty, I said to my sons: "Kill the monk who stands before us!" // SRS_35.88 //

children.text: śrutvātha te mahya kumāra vākyaṃ suduḥkhitā durmanaso abhūvan /
children.translated_text: Having heard my words, the princes were deeply distressed and dejected:

children.text: mā eva pravyāhara tāta vācaṃ na ghātayāmo vaya bhikṣumīdṛśam // SRS_35.89 //
children.translated_text: "Do not utter such a word, father! We shall not kill a monk like this! // SRS_35.89 //

children.text: yadyaṅgamaṅgātu śarīra chidyet kalpāna koṭyo yatha gaṅgavālukāḥ /
children.translated_text: Even if limb by limb our bodies were cut for <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> like the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: na tveva bhikṣuṃ vaya hiṃsayema tathāhi bodhāya utpannu cittam // SRS_35.90 //
children.translated_text: we would never harm a monk — for our minds have been directed toward awakening!" // SRS_35.90 //

children.text: śrutvātha rājā tada putravāsyaṃ bhṛtyaṃ bhaṇī roṣitu vadhyaghātakam /
children.translated_text: Having heard his sons' words, the king then spoke angrily to a servant, an executioner:

children.text: ānetha śīghraṃ imu bhikṣu ghātayī sthitu yaḥ purastāpi antaḥpurasya // SRS_35.91 //
children.translated_text: "Bring [him] quickly! Kill this monk who stands here before the inner palace!" // SRS_35.91 //

children.text: athāgamī paści sa vadhyaghātako sa raudracitto va su nandināmā /
children.translated_text: Then that executioner came forward — of cruel mind, named <s>Sunandī</s>;

children.text: asiṃ gṛhītvāna sa tailapāyitaṃ yeno kṛto bhikṣuṇa aṣṭakhaṇḍaḥ // SRS_35.92 //
children.translated_text: having seized an oil-anointed sword, he cut the monk into eight pieces. // SRS_35.92 //

children.text: kṛtvā tvakarmeti sughorarūpaṃ niryātu udyānu gatā kṣaṇena /
children.translated_text: Having done that deed of terrible appearance, [the king] went out to the garden and was gone in a moment;

children.text: (Vaidya 249)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 249)

children.text: na tasya krīḍā na ratī ca jāyate smaritva bhikṣuṃ tada puṣpacandram // SRS_35.93 //
children.translated_text: no pleasure or delight arose in him, remembering the monk <s>Puṣpacandra</s>. // SRS_35.93 //

children.text: sa śīghraśīghraṃ tvaramāṇarūpaḥ tataḥ praviṣṭaḥ svaku rājadhānīm /
children.translated_text: Very quickly, in great haste, he then entered his own capital city;

children.text: rathābhirūḍho gatu taṃ pradeśaṃ yasmin kṛto bhikṣu sa aṣṭakhaṇḍam // SRS_35.94 //
children.translated_text: mounting a chariot, he went to that place where the monk had been cut into eight pieces. // SRS_35.94 //

children.text: aśrauṣi so ghoṣamathāntarīkṣād bahūn devānayutāna krandatām /
children.translated_text: He heard a sound from the sky — of many <s>nayutas</s> of gods wailing:

children.text: kalirāja pāpaṃ subahu tvayā kṛtaṃ cyuto gamiṣyasyasukhaṃ avīcim // SRS_35.95 //
children.translated_text: "O wicked king, much evil has been done by you! Fallen, you shall go to the misery of <s>Avīci</s>!" // SRS_35.95 //

children.text: śrutvāna rājā marutāna ghoṣaṃ suduḥkhito durmanu trastacittaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard the cry of the gods, the king was deeply distressed, dejected, with trembling mind:

children.text: bahū mayā dāruṇa pāpakaṃ kṛtaṃ yeno mayā ghātitu puṣpacandraḥ // SRS_35.96 //
children.translated_text: "Much terrible evil has been done by me, by which <s>Puṣpacandra</s> has been killed by me! // SRS_35.96 //

children.text: yaḥ putru buddhāna nararṣabhāṇāṃ anantajñānīna tathāgatānām /
children.translated_text: He who was a son of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the bulls among men, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> of infinite knowledge —

children.text: guptendriyaḥ sūratu śāntamānasaḥ so 'pī mayā ghātitu kāmakāraṇāt // SRS_35.97 //
children.translated_text: of guarded senses, heroic, of peaceful mind — he too was killed by me on account of desire! // SRS_35.97 //

children.text: yo dharmu dhāreti tathāgatānāṃ saddharmakośaṃ kṣayi vartamāne /
children.translated_text: He who upheld the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the treasury of the true <s>Dharma</s>, in a time of decline,

children.text: jñānapradīpaṃ kari sarvaloke kaṣṭaṃ sa me ghātitu kāmakāraṇāt // SRS_35.98 //
children.translated_text: who made a lamp of knowledge for the entire world — alas, he was killed by me on account of desire! // SRS_35.98 //

children.text: yo dharma pravyāharatī prajānāṃ gambhīra śāntaṃ nipuṇaṃ sudurdṛśam /
children.translated_text: He who proclaimed the <s>Dharma</s> to beings — profound, peaceful, subtle, hard to see,

children.text: yo bodhimaṇḍasya varasya deśakaḥ so 'yaṃ mayā ghātitu kāmakāraṇāt // SRS_35.99 //
children.translated_text: he who was the teacher of the supreme seat of awakening — he was killed by me on account of desire! // SRS_35.99 //

children.text: yo dharmakośaṃdharu nāyakānāmandhasya lokasya pradīpabhūtaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who upheld the <s>Dharma</s>-treasury of the Guides, who was a lamp for the blind world,

children.text: (Vaidya 250)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 250)

children.text: yo dhāraṇī dhārayi sūtrarājaṃ sa kiṃ mayā ghātitu kāmakāraṇāt // SRS_35.100 //
children.translated_text: who held the <s>dhāraṇī</s>, the king of <s>sūtras</s> — why was he killed by me on account of desire? // SRS_35.100 //

children.text: asaṃkiliṣṭaḥ suviśuddhajñānī śāntaḥ praśāntaḥ satataṃ samāhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Undefiled, of purified knowledge, calm, tranquil, constantly concentrated —

children.text: kāmāndhabhūtena mayādya ghātito yenātikaṣṭaṃ nirayaṃ gamiṣye // SRS_35.101 //
children.translated_text: he was killed today by me, blinded by desire — by which I shall go to the most terrible hell! // SRS_35.101 //

children.text: ye 'tīta buddhāpyatha ye anāgatā ye cāpi tiṣṭhanti narottamā jināḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddhas</s> of the past, those yet to come, and those who now abide, the supreme among men, the Conquerors —

children.text: anantavarṇān guṇasāgaropamān upaimi sarvān śaraṇaṃ kṛtāñjaliḥ // SRS_35.102 //
children.translated_text: of infinite virtues, ocean-like in qualities — I go to all of them for refuge, with joined palms! // SRS_35.102 //

children.text: ghorān gamiṣye nirayāṃścyutasya trātā na tatra pratividyate mama /
children.translated_text: I shall go to terrible hells upon death — no protector is found for me there;

children.text: karmaṃ hyaniṣṭaṃ hi kṛtaṃ mayādya yad ghātito 'yaṃ maya dharmabhāṇakaḥ // SRS_35.103 //
children.translated_text: for an unwholesome deed has been done by me today — that this <s>Dharma</s>-preacher was killed by me! // SRS_35.103 //

children.text: dhik pāpacittaṃ vyasanasya kartṛ dhig rājabhāvaṃ madagarvitānām /
children.translated_text: Shame on the evil mind, the maker of ruin! Shame on the state of being a king, intoxicated with pride!

children.text: ekaḥ prayāsyāmi vihāya sarvaṃ sāraṃ na me kiṃcidito gṛhītam // SRS_35.104 //
children.translated_text: I shall depart alone, having left everything — nothing of essence has been taken by me from here! // SRS_35.104 //

children.text: viśuddhadharmo gatadoṣamohaḥ priyaṃvadaḥ kāruṇiko jitātmā /
children.translated_text: Of purified <s>Dharma</s>, free from hatred and delusion, speaking kindly, compassionate, self-conquered,

children.text: adūṣakaḥ sarvajanaikabandhuḥ kasmāddhato me varapuṣpacandraḥ // SRS_35.105 //
children.translated_text: blameless, the sole friend of all people — why was my noble <s>Puṣpacandra</s> killed? // SRS_35.105 //

children.text: hā suvratā kṣāntitapodhanāḍhyā hā rūpadākṣiṇyaguṇairupetā /
children.translated_text: Alas, O one of good vows, rich in patience and austerity! Alas, endowed with beauty, grace, and virtue!

children.text: hā niṣkuhā śrīghana niṣprapañcā kuha prayāto 'si vihāya mā tvam // SRS_35.106 //
children.translated_text: Alas, O guileless one, mass of glory, free from proliferation — where have you gone, leaving me? // SRS_35.106 //

children.text: adyāvagacchāmi maharṣivākyaṃ kāmā hyanityā vadhakāḥ prajānām /
children.translated_text: Now I understand the words of the great sages — desires are impermanent, the slayers of beings;

children.text: manojvarā durgatihetavaśca tasmāt prahāsye eta kāmacaryām // SRS_35.107 //
children.translated_text: they are fevers of the mind and causes of lower rebirths — therefore I shall abandon this life of desire! // SRS_35.107 //

body.text: (Vaidya 251)

children.text: yāsye ghoramahaṃ hyavīcinirayaṃ trāṇaṃ na me vidyate
children.translated_text: I shall go to the terrible <s>Avīci</s> hell — no protection is found for me;

children.text: pāpaṃ karma kṛtaṃ hyaniṣṭamasukhaṃ bhikṣurmayā ghātitaḥ /
children.translated_text: evil, unwholesome, miserable <s>karma</s> has been done — a monk was killed by me!

children.text: muktvā rājya hu brahmacaryaparamaḥ pūjāṃ kariṣye varāṃ
children.translated_text: Having abandoned kingship, devoted to the supreme holy life, I shall perform excellent worship —

children.text: puṣpairgandhavilepanaiḥ suruciraiḥ stūpaṃ kariṣyāmyaham // SRS_35.108 //
children.translated_text: with flowers, fragrances, and ointments most beautiful, I shall build a <s>stūpa</s>! // SRS_35.108 //

body.translated_text: (Vaidya 251)

children.text: putrāśco duhitṝḥ striyo gṛhapatī ye cā amātyā mama
children.translated_text: My sons and daughters, wives and householders, and whatever counselors I have,

children.text: śreṣṭhī naigama kṣatriyā bahuvidhāḥ sarveṣa bhāṣāmyaham /
children.translated_text: merchants, townsfolk, warriors of many kinds — to all of them I say:

children.text: agaruṃ padmaku candanaṃ suruciraṃ gandhāśca ye śobhanāḥ
children.translated_text: Aloe-wood, lotus-bark, sandalwood most beautiful, and whatever fragrances are excellent —

children.text: śīghraṃ kurvatha mañjugarbhaśibikāṃ yadbhikṣu dhmāpīyatu // SRS_35.109 //
children.translated_text: quickly build a beautiful bier with a precious casket, so that the monk may be cremated!" // SRS_35.109 //

children.text: śrutvā pārthivavākya sarvanagaraṃ gandhāṃ haritvā varāṃ
children.translated_text: Having heard the king's words, the entire city brought the finest fragrances;

children.text: citikāṃ kṛtva manojñagandha rucirāmāropya bhikṣuṃ tahim /
children.translated_text: having built a pyre, fragrant and beautiful, they placed the monk upon it.

children.text: agaruṃ padmaku candanaṃ satagaraṃ spṛkkāṃ tathā pāṭalāṃ
children.translated_text: Aloe-wood, lotus-bark, sandalwood, <s>tagara</s>, <s>spṛkkā</s>, and <s>pāṭalā</s> —

children.text: puṣpairmālyavilepanena ruciraistailena prajvālayī // SRS_35.110 //
children.translated_text: with flowers, garlands, ointments most beautiful, and oil, [the king] set it ablaze. // SRS_35.110 //

children.text: droṇyāṃ tasya kṛtaṃ śarīramabhavad yā māpitā bhikṣubhis
children.translated_text: The body was [collected] in a <s>droṇa</s> (reliquary vessel) that was built by the monks;

children.text: teṣāṃ stūpu karitva rāja avacī pūjāsya kāmāmyaham /
children.translated_text: having made a <s>stūpa</s> for them, the king said: 'I wish to worship it!'

children.text: puṣpaṃ mālya vilepanaṃ ca grahiya cchatrān patākāṃ dhvajāṃs
children.translated_text: Taking flowers, garlands, and ointments, parasols, banners, and flags —

children.text: tasmiṃstūryasahasrakoṭinayutāṃ vādāpayī pārthivaḥ // SRS_35.111 //
children.translated_text: at that [<s>stūpa</s>] the king had thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of musical instruments played. // SRS_35.111 //

children.text: traikālyaṃ divase vrajī mahipati bhikṣusya stūpaṃ tadā
children.translated_text: Three times daily the king went to the <s>stūpa</s> of the monk;

children.text: triṣvapyadhvasu deśayī purīmakaṃ yatkiṃci pāpaṃ kṛtam /
children.translated_text: in all three times he confessed whatever evil had been done formerly.

children.text: varṣā koṭisahasra pañcanavatiṃ taṃ kṣepayī duṣkṛtaṃ
children.translated_text: For ninety-five thousand <s>koṭis</s> of years he expiated that misdeed,

children.text: śīlaṃ paści akhaṇḍa rakṣitu varaṃ śuddhaṃ śucī nirmalam // SRS_35.112 //
children.translated_text: and afterward he guarded unbroken, supreme, pure, clean, stainless morality. // SRS_35.112 //

children.text: varṣā koṭisahasra pañcanavatiṃ poṣī tadā poṣadhaṃ
children.translated_text: For ninety-five thousand <s>koṭis</s> of years he kept the <s>poṣadha</s> (observance day);

children.text: bhinne co tada ātmabhāvi patito ghorāmavīciṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: but when his body broke, he fell again into the terrible <s>Avīci</s> [hell].

children.text: kṛtvā nirghṛṇa karma vedayi dukhaṃ kāmaṃnidānaṃ bahu
children.translated_text: Having done merciless <s>karma</s>, he experienced great suffering caused by desire;

children.text: buddhā koṭisahasra pañcanavatiṃ vīrāgitā ye mayā // SRS_35.113 //
children.translated_text: ninety-five thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, those heroes, were passed by me. // SRS_35.113 //

children.text: varṣā koṭisahasra pañcanavatī andho 'hamāsaṃ tadā
children.translated_text: For ninety-five thousand <s>koṭis</s> of years I was then blind;

children.text: dvāṣaṣṭī pi ca kalpa koṭinayutā netrā mi bhinnā purā /
children.translated_text: for sixty-two <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, my eyes were formerly destroyed.

children.text: naikā kalpasahasra koṭinayutāmutpāṭya cakṣurhṛtaṃ
children.translated_text: For many thousands of <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, my eyes were plucked out and taken;

children.text: hastā cchinna anantakalpanayutān pādāśca karṇāḥ śirāḥ // SRS_35.114 //
children.translated_text: hands were cut for innumerable <s>kalpa</s>-<s>nayutas</s>, and feet, ears, and heads. // SRS_35.114 //

children.text: mānuṣye sati kalpakoṭinayutānanyāsu vā jātiṣu
children.translated_text: In the human state for <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, and in other births too,

children.text: duḥkhā vedana vedayāmi ca ciraṃ saṃsāraduḥkhārditaḥ /
children.translated_text: I experienced painful feelings for a long time, tormented by the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: kṛtvā pāpaku karma duḥkhanubhavī saṃsāramāṇaściraṃ
children.translated_text: Having done evil <s>karma</s>, experiencing suffering, wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s> for a long time —

children.text: tasmāt pāpu na kuryu adhvi tribhave yo bodhimicchecchivām // SRS_35.115 //
children.translated_text: therefore one should not do evil in the three realms of existence, if one desires auspicious awakening! // SRS_35.115 //

children.text: (Vaidya 252)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 252)

children.text: deśetva karmaṃ purimaku rājaśreṣṭho nāsau vimucyī purimaku duṣkṛtātaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having confessed his former <s>karma</s>, that excellent king was not freed from the former misdeed;

children.text: kṛtvā ca karmaṃ purimaku ghorarupaṃ sa ca cyavitva gacchennirayamavīci ghoram // SRS_35.116 //
children.translated_text: having done that former <s>karma</s> of terrible form, he, dying, went to the terrible <s>Avīci</s> hell. // SRS_35.116 //

children.text: hastā vicchinnāstathapi ca pāda karṇa nāsā vicchinnā bahuvidha nantakalpān /
children.translated_text: Hands were cut off, and also feet, ears, and nose were cut off in many ways for innumerable <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: netrā ca mahyaṃ balaśo hṛtā kṣipitvā utkṣipta daṇḍairvicaratu cārikāyām // SRS_35.117 //
children.translated_text: and my eyes were forcibly torn out; cast out, struck with sticks, I wandered on the path. // SRS_35.117 //

children.text: tyaktvā svakāye śira kara bodhihetoḥ putrāśca dārānnayana tathātmamāṃsam /
children.translated_text: Having given up his own body — head, hands — for the sake of awakening, sons and wife, eyes, and even his own flesh,

children.text: hastāṃśca pādān parityaji hṛṣṭacitto no ca kṣapemī purimaku pāpakarma // SRS_35.118 //
children.translated_text: having renounced hands and feet with a joyful mind — yet I did not exhaust my former evil <s>karma</s>! // SRS_35.118 //

children.text: rājā abhūvaṃ tada ahu śūradatto te putra mahyaṃ carimaka dharmapālāḥ /
children.translated_text: "I was the king then; I was <s>Śūradatta</s>. Those [mentioned] are my sons, the final protectors of the <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: padmottaro 'yaṃ āsi supuṣpacandro vasunandi āsīddaśabalu śāntirājaḥ // SRS_35.119 //
children.translated_text: This <s>Padmottara</s> was <s>Supuṣpacandra</s>; <s>Vasunandi</s> was the Ten-Powered One, <s>Śāntirāja</s>. // SRS_35.119 //

children.text: si nārisaṃgho suvipula kṣatriyāśco gṛhapatī ye balapati ye camātyāḥ /
children.translated_text: That group of women, the vast <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, the householders, the generals, and the ministers,

children.text: śreṣṭhī tathaiva naigama kodṛrājā sarve 'pyabhūṣī daśabala niṣkileśāḥ // SRS_35.120 //
children.translated_text: the merchants, likewise the guild-leaders and the prince — all became Ten-Powered Ones, free from defilements! // SRS_35.120 //

children.text: kumāra evācaritamanantakalpaṃ dṛṣṭvān buddhān dhutaguṇa niṣkileśāḥ /
children.translated_text: O Prince, such was the conduct practiced for infinite <s>kalpas</s>, having seen the <s>Buddhas</s>, [devoted to] ascetic qualities, free from defilements;

children.text: te te mi duḥkhā tada anubhūtapūrvā carantu śreṣṭhāṃ ima bodhicaryām // SRS_35.121 //
children.translated_text: those various sufferings I formerly experienced — [therefore] practice this most excellent conduct for awakening! // SRS_35.121 //

children.text: yo bodhisattvaḥ pratiṣṭhita dhāraṇīye maitrāvihārī acalitu aprakampī /
children.translated_text: A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is established in the <s>dhāraṇī</s>, who dwells in loving-kindness, immovable and unshakeable,

children.text: (Vaidya 253)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 253)

children.text: nāsau kadācid vrajati apāyabhūmiṃ pūjetva buddhān dhutaguṇa niṣkileśān // SRS_35.122 //
children.translated_text: he never goes to the realm of misfortune, having worshipped the <s>Buddhas</s>, [devoted to] ascetic qualities, free from defilements. // SRS_35.122 //

children.text: yo icchi buddho kathamiha dharmasvāmī dvātriṃśatībhiḥ kavacitu lakṣaṇebhiḥ /
children.translated_text: One who wishes to become a <s>Buddha</s>, a Lord of <s>Dharma</s> here, armored with the thirty-two marks,

children.text: so śīlarakṣī aśabala apravedhā deśeti dharmaṃ pratiṣṭhitu dhāraṇīye // SRS_35.123 //
children.translated_text: he should guard moral conduct — spotless and unwavering — and teach the <s>dharma</s>, established in the <s>dhāraṇī</s>. // SRS_35.123 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje supuṣpacandraparivartaḥ pañcatriṃśatitaḥ || 35 ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the thirty-fifth chapter in the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, the <s>Supuṣpacandraparivarta</s> (Chapter on <s>Supuṣpacandra</s>).

body.text:
(Vaidya 254)
36 Śīlaskandhanirdeśaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 254) Chapter 36: The <s>Śīlaskandhanirdeśaparivarta</s> (Chapter on the Exposition of the Aggregate of Moral Conduct).

body.text: tasmāttarhi kumāra ya ākāṅkṣedbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ kimityahaṃ sukhamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyamiti, tena kumāra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena śīlaskandhe supratiṣṭhitena bhavitavyam, sarvabodhisattveṣu ca śāstṛpremasaṃjñā upasthāpayitavyā ||
body.translated_text: "Therefore, O Prince, a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> who desires: 'How may I comfortably attain unsurpassed perfect awakening?' — that <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s>, O Prince, should be well-established in the aggregate of moral conduct, and should cultivate the perception of the Teacher with affection toward all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>."

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One at that time spoke these verses:

children.text: yaḥ śīlaskandhe pratiṣṭhitu bodhisattvo hitaiṣicitto vicarati cārikāyām /
children.translated_text: "A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is established in the aggregate of moral conduct and wanders on the path with a mind wishing well-being —

children.text: kṣipraṃ sa gatvā abhiratibuddhakṣetraṃ kṣāntiṃṃ labhitvā bhaviṣyati dharmarājaḥ // SRS_36.1 //
children.translated_text: swiftly going to the <s>Abhirati</s> <s>Buddha</s>-field, having obtained <s>kṣānti</s> (patient acceptance), he will become a <s>Dharma</s>-King. // SRS_36.1 //

children.text: tasmāt samagrā bhavatha aduṣṭacittāḥ sarve ca bhogā satata manāpakārī /
children.translated_text: Therefore be harmonious, with uncorrupted minds, and may all possessions always be shared amicably;

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca buddhān śirighana aprameyān bodhiṃ spṛśitvā bhaviṣyatha dharmasvāmī // SRS_36.2 //
children.translated_text: having seen the <s>Buddhas</s>, dense as a mountain, immeasurable — touching <s>bodhi</s>, you will become Lords of <s>Dharma</s>! // SRS_36.2 //

children.text: tasmācchruṇitvā ima vara ānuśaṃsān dṛṣṭā ca bhikṣūn parama suśīlavantā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, having heard these supreme benefits, and having seen monks of most excellent moral conduct,

children.text: niḥśāṭhiyeno vidu sada sevitavyāḥ samādhiptāptā bhaviṣyatha nocireṇa // SRS_36.3 //
children.translated_text: without guile, the wise should always be attended — and you will attain the <s>samādhi</s> before long! // SRS_36.3 //

children.text: sacennidhānāparimitāpramāṇa pūrṇā bhaveyu maṇiratanebhi saptaiḥ /
children.translated_text: If infinite, immeasurable treasuries

children.text: tathaiva bhūyo ratanavarāṇa pūrṇāḥ kṣetrā bhaveyurvālikagaṅgatulyāḥ // SRS_36.4 //
children.translated_text: were filled with the seven kinds of jewels, and likewise further <s>Buddha</s>-fields, equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, were filled with the best jewels, // SRS_36.4 //

children.text: dānādhimukto bhaviya sa bodhisattva ekaika rātriṃdivamiha dānu dadyāt /
children.translated_text: and a <s>Bodhisattva</s> devoted to giving were to give that gift each day and night,

children.text: evaṃ dadan so bahuvidha kalpakoṭīḥ no viṣṭhitaḥ syād vālika gaṅgatulyāḥ // SRS_36.5 //
children.translated_text: and thus giving for many <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, he would not be established [in merit] — // SRS_36.5 //

children.text: yaśco samādhiṃ imumiha bodhisattvo śrutvāna dhāreta sugatavarāṇa gañjam /
children.translated_text: yet a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who, having heard this <s>samādhi</s>, retains the treasury of the supreme <s>Sugatas</s> —

children.text: yaḥ puṇyaskandho bhavati gṛhītu teno tat sarvadānaṃ kalamapi nānubhoti // SRS_36.6 //
children.translated_text: the mass of merit that arises from retaining it — all that giving does not equal even a fraction of it! // SRS_36.6 //

children.text: (Vaidya 255)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 255)

children.text: eṣo varo anupama puṇyaskandho jñānasya kośa aparimitākaropama /
children.translated_text: This is the supreme, incomparable mass of merit — a treasure of knowledge, like an unlimited mine;

children.text: śrāddho naro yo imu ānulomikaṃ dhāreyya agraṃ imu virajaṃ samādhim // SRS_36.7 //
children.translated_text: a faithful person who retains this conforming, supreme, dustless <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_36.7 //

children.text: dhāreyya eta viraja samādhi śānta mahādhano bhavati sa bodhisattvaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who retains this dustless, peaceful <s>samādhi</s> — that <s>Bodhisattva</s> becomes greatly wealthy;

children.text: mahāsamudro bahuvidharatanasya ākaro na tasya puṇyasya pramāṇamasti // SRS_36.8 //
children.translated_text: the great ocean, a mine of various jewels — yet there is no measure for his merit! // SRS_36.8 //

children.text: varehi dharmehi acintiyehi saṃbṛhito vuccati bodhisattvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Augmented with supreme, inconceivable <s>dharmas</s>, he is called a <s>Bodhisattva</s>;

children.text: na tasya bodhāya kadāci saṃśayo ya uddiśeyāti imaḥ samādhim // SRS_36.9 //
children.translated_text: there is never any doubt about his awakening — for one who expounds this <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_36.9 //

children.text: saṃsthāpya lokācariyaṃ vināyakaṃ buddhaṃ mahākāruṇikaṃ svayaṃbhuvam /
children.translated_text: Having established the world's teacher, the Guide, the <s>Buddha</s>, the greatly compassionate, the Self-arisen —

children.text: yaḥ puṇyaskandhena vareṇupeto acintiyo yasya pramāṇu nāsti // SRS_36.10 //
children.translated_text: he who is endowed with the supreme mass of merit — his [merit] is inconceivable, without measure. // SRS_36.10 //

children.text: na uttaro tasya ca sattva kaścit mahāsahasrāya kadāci vidyate /
children.translated_text: No being superior to him exists anywhere in the great trichiliocosm,

children.text: yaḥ puṇyaskandhena samo bhaveta jñānena vāsādṛśācintiyena // SRS_36.11 //
children.translated_text: who could equal him in mass of merit or in inconceivable knowledge. // SRS_36.11 //

children.text: anyatra yaḥ śrutva samādhimetaṃ dhāreyya vāceyya paryāpuṇeyyā /
children.translated_text: Except one who, having heard this <s>samādhi</s>, retains it, recites it, and masters it,

children.text: paryeṣamāṇo 'tula budhabodhiṃ na tasya jñānena samo bhaveta // SRS_36.12 //
children.translated_text: seeking the incomparable awakening of the <s>Buddha</s> — no one could equal him in knowledge. // SRS_36.12 //

children.text: sacet kumārā siya ayu dharmarūpa yaḥ puṇyaskandho upacitu tena bhoti /
children.translated_text: If, O Princes, life were to take the form of <s>dharma</s>, the mass of merit accumulated by one

children.text: dhāratu vācetu imaṃ samādhiṃ na so viceyyā iha pṛthulokadhātuṣu // SRS_36.13 //
children.translated_text: who retains and recites this <s>samādhi</s> — it could not be exhausted in these vast world-realms! // SRS_36.13 //

children.text: tasmāt kumāreha ya bodhisattvo ākāṅkṣate pūjitu sarvabuddhān /
children.translated_text: Therefore, O Prince, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> here who desires to worship all the <s>Buddhas</s>,

children.text: (Vaidya 256)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 256)

children.text: asaṅganirdeśapadārthakovido atīta utpanna tathāgatāṃśca dhāretu vācetu imaṃ samādhim // SRS_36.14 //
children.translated_text: skilled in the meaning of the teaching of non-attachment, regarding the <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the past and present — let him retain and recite this <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_36.14 //

children.text: eṣā hi sā bodhi tathāgatānāṃ śraddhehi mahyaṃ vacanaṃ kumārāḥ /
children.translated_text: This indeed is the <s>bodhi</s> of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> — believe my words, O Princes!

children.text: na bhāṣate vācamṛṣāṃ tathāgato na hīdṛśāḥ sattva mṛṣāṃ vadanti // SRS_36.15 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s> does not speak a false word; beings such as these do not speak falsehood! // SRS_36.15 //

children.text: yasmin mayā śodhitu ātmagrāho itaḥ pure kalpaśatānacintiyān /
children.translated_text: In which I purified the grasping of self, from before this, for inconceivable hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: śreṣṭhā carantena pi bodhicārikāṃ paryeṣamāṇena imāṃ samādhim // SRS_36.16 //
children.translated_text: practicing the most excellent conduct for awakening, seeking this <s>samādhi</s> — // SRS_36.16 //

children.text: tasmādimaṃ śrutva atha dharmagañjaṃ yaḥ sūtrakoṭīnayutāna āgamaḥ /
children.translated_text: therefore, having heard this treasure of <s>dharma</s>, which is the source of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>sūtras</s>,

children.text: yaḥ puṇyaskandho vipulo acintiyo yeno laghuṃ budhyati buddhajñānam // SRS_36.17 //
children.translated_text: the mass of merit is vast and inconceivable — by which one swiftly awakens to <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. // SRS_36.17 //

children.text: sarveṣa sūtrāṇidamagrasūtramacintiyasyo kuśalasya ākaram /
children.translated_text: Of all <s>sūtras</s>, this is the foremost <s>sūtra</s>, the mine of inconceivable wholesome [merit];

children.text: paryantu dharmāṇa na teṣa labhyate yāṃ so sadā nirdiśate viśāradaḥ // SRS_36.18 //
children.translated_text: no limit of the <s>dharmas</s> can be found therein — which that confident one always teaches! // SRS_36.18 //

children.text: chinditva bhinditva mahāsahasraṃ śakyaṃ gaṇetuṃ paramāṇusaṃcayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having broken and shattered the great trichiliocosm, it would be possible to count the accumulation of atoms;

children.text: na tveva te sūtraśatā acintiyān pramātu yaṃ bhāṣati so aviṣṭhitaḥ // SRS_36.19 //
children.translated_text: but the inconceivable hundreds of <s>sūtras</s> that he speaks, the unswerving one — their measure cannot be taken! // SRS_36.19 //

children.text: āśvāsa praśvāsa gaṇetu śakyaṃ sarveṣa sattvāniha buddhakṣetre /
children.translated_text: It would be possible to count the inhalations and exhalations of all beings in this <s>Buddha</s>-field;

children.text: paryantu sūtrāṇa na teṣa śakyaṃ yān bhāṣate so 'tra samādhiye sthitaḥ // SRS_36.20 //
children.translated_text: but the limit of the <s>sūtras</s> cannot be known — which he speaks while established in this <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_36.20 //

children.text: buddhāna kṣetrā yatha gaṅgavālikā ye teṣa sattvā gati teṣūpapannāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Buddha</s>-fields like the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> — the beings born in those destinies therein —

children.text: gaṇetu te śakyamathāpi cintituṃ na teṣa sūtrāṇa ya nityu bhāṣate // SRS_36.21 //
children.translated_text: they could be counted, even conceived of — but not the <s>sūtras</s> that he constantly speaks! // SRS_36.21 //

children.text: (Vaidya 257)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 257)

children.text: gaṇetu śakyamita kalpakoṭibhiḥ mahāsamudreṣviha yātti vālikāḥ /
children.translated_text: It would be possible to count, over <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, the grains of sand in the great oceans,

children.text: nadīṣu kuṇḍeṣu hradeṣu tadvad ananta sūtrānta sa yat prabhāṣate // SRS_36.22 //
children.translated_text: in rivers, pools, and lakes likewise — but the endless <s>sūtras</s> he proclaims [cannot be counted]! // SRS_36.22 //

children.text: śakyaṃ gaṇetuṃ bahukalpakoṭiṣu ya āpaskandhaḥ sada tatra tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: It would be possible to count, over many <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, the mass of water that always remains therein;

children.text: śatāya bhinnāya vālāgrakoṭiyo svarāṅga teṣāṃ na tu śakyu sarvaśaḥ // SRS_36.23 //
children.translated_text: divided into hundreds of tips of split hairs — but their melodious sounds cannot be [counted] at all! // SRS_36.23 //

children.text: śakyaṃ gaṇetuṃ bahukalpakoṭibhirye sattva āsan purimeṇa tatra /
children.translated_text: It would be possible to count, over many <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, the beings that existed before therein;

children.text: ya ātmabhāve vinibaddhasārā na teṣa sūtrāntanirhāra jānitum // SRS_36.24 //
children.translated_text: those bound in essence to [the cycle of] self-existence — but the production of his <s>sūtras</s> cannot be known! // SRS_36.24 //

children.text: gaṇetu śakyaṃ ruta sarvaprāṇināṃ ye santi sattvā daśasu diśāsu /
children.translated_text: It would be possible to count the sounds of all living beings in the ten directions;

children.text: na śakyu sūtrānta gaṇetu tasya yad bhāṣate 'sau satatamaviṣṭhitaḥ // SRS_36.25 //
children.translated_text: but the <s>sūtras</s> of that one who constantly speaks without ceasing cannot be counted! // SRS_36.25 //

children.text: sarveṣa dharmāṇa nideśu jānati niruktinirdeśapadārthakovidaḥ /
children.translated_text: He knows the exposition of all <s>dharmas</s>, skilled in etymology, exposition, and meaning of words;

children.text: viniścaye bhūtanayeṣu śikṣito viśālabuddhiḥ sada harṣaprajñaḥ // SRS_36.26 //
children.translated_text: trained in the method of truth in discernment — of vast intellect, always joyful in wisdom! // SRS_36.26 //

children.text: abhinnabuddhirvipulārthacintī acintya cinteti sadā prajānati /
children.translated_text: Of unbroken intellect, contemplating vast meaning, he always comprehends the inconceivable contemplation;

children.text: ghoṣasvabhāvaṃ pṛthu sarva jānatī śabdāṃśca tān nirdiśato na sajjati // SRS_36.27 //
children.translated_text: he knows the own-nature of sound extensively and all — and teaching those sounds, he does not cling! // SRS_36.27 //

children.text: asakta so vuccati dharmabhāṇako na sajjate sarvajagasya bhāṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: He is called an unattached <s>dharma</s>-preacher; he does not cling while teaching the entire world;

children.text: praśnāna nirdeśapadehi kovidaḥ tathāhi teno paramārthu jñātaḥ // SRS_36.28 //
children.translated_text: skilled in the words of exposition of questions — for thus he has known the ultimate truth! // SRS_36.28 //

children.text: ekasya sūtrasyupadeśakoṭiyo acintiyāṃ niordiśato na sajjati /
children.translated_text: The inconceivable <s>koṭīs</s> of teachings of a single <s>sūtra</s> — expounding them, he does not cling;

children.text: (Vaidya 258)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 258)

children.text: asaṅganirdeśapadārthakovido bhāṣantu so parṣagato na sajjate // SRS_36.29 //
children.translated_text: skilled in the meaning of the words of the teaching of non-attachment — speaking in the assembly, he does not cling! // SRS_36.29 //

children.text: yaḥ susthito bhoti iho samādhiye sa bodhisattvo bhavatī akampiyaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who is well-established here in this <s>samādhi</s>, that <s>Bodhisattva</s> becomes unshakeable;

children.text: dharme balādhānaviśeṣaprāptaḥ karoti so 'rthaṃ bahuprāṇakoṭinām // SRS_36.30 //
children.translated_text: having attained the distinction of the power of <s>dharma</s>, he accomplishes the welfare of many <s>koṭīs</s> of beings! // SRS_36.30 //

children.text: yathaiva meruracalo akampiyaḥ sarvehi vātehi na śakya kampitum /
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Meru</s> is immovable and unshakeable, unable to be shaken by any winds,

children.text: tathaiva bhikṣurvidu dharmabhāṇakaṃ kampetu śakyaṃ na parapravādibhiḥ // SRS_36.31 //
children.translated_text: so too a wise monk, a <s>dharma</s>-preacher — cannot be shaken by opposing disputants! // SRS_36.31 //

children.text: mahāsahasreṣviha lokadhātuṣu ye parvatā ukta akampanīyāḥ /
children.translated_text: In this great trichiliocosm, the mountains that are called unshakeable —

children.text: te śakya vātena prakampanāya na tveva dharme sthitu śūnyi bhikṣuḥ // SRS_36.32 //
children.translated_text: they can be shaken by the wind, but not the monk established in the <s>dharma</s> of emptiness! // SRS_32.32 //

children.text: ya śūnyatāyāṃ satataṃ prayukto buddhāna eṣo niyataṃ vihāraḥ /
children.translated_text: One who is constantly devoted to emptiness — this is assuredly the dwelling-place of the <s>Buddhas</s>;

children.text: prajānatī niścitu dharma śūnyāṃ sa sarvavādībhi na śakyu kṣobhitum // SRS_36.33 //
children.translated_text: he who certainly knows the <s>dharma</s> as empty — he cannot be disturbed by any disputant! // SRS_36.33 //

children.text: akampiyo bhoti parapravādibhiḥ savapravādehi anābhibhūtaḥ /
children.translated_text: He is unshakeable by opposing disputants, unconquered by their own doctrines,

children.text: anābhibhūtaśca aninditaśca imumuddiśitvāna samādhi śāntam // SRS_36.34 //
children.translated_text: both unconquered and blameless — having expounded this peaceful <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_36.34 //

children.text: gatiṃ gato bhoti sa śunyatāyāṃ sarveṣu dharmeṣu na kāṅkṣate 'sau /
children.translated_text: He has gone to the course of emptiness; in all <s>dharmas</s> he does not doubt;

children.text: anantajñāne sada supratiṣṭhito imumuddiśitvāna samādhi śāntam // SRS_36.35 //
children.translated_text: always well-established in infinite knowledge — having expounded this peaceful <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_36.35 //

children.text: balāni bodhyaṅga na tasya durlabhā pratisaṃvido ṛddhividhī acintiyā /
children.translated_text: The powers and factors of awakening are not hard for him to obtain; the analytical knowledges and inconceivable supernatural powers —

children.text: abhijña no tasya bhavanti durlabhā dhāretva vācetva ima samādhim // SRS_36.36 //
children.translated_text: the superknowledges are not hard for him to obtain — having retained and recited this <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_36.36 //

children.text: (Vaidya 259)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 259)

children.text: bhavābhivṛttasya na tasya durlabhaṃ anantajñānena jināna darśanam /
children.translated_text: For one who has transcended existence, the seeing of the Conquerors through infinite knowledge is not hard to obtain;

children.text: saṃbuddha koṭīnayutānacintiyān so drakṣyate etu samādhi dhārayan // SRS_36.37 //
children.translated_text: he will see inconceivable <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of fully Awakened Ones — by retaining this <s>samādhi</s>! // SRS_36.37 //

children.text: sarveṣa co teṣa jināna antike sa śroṣyate etu samādhi śāntam /
children.translated_text: In the presence of all those Conquerors, he will hear this peaceful <s>samādhi</s>;

children.text: vareṇa jñānena upetu bheṣyatī pratisaṃvidāsu vaśa pāramiṃ gataḥ // SRS_36.38 //
children.translated_text: endowed with supreme knowledge, he will become fearless, having reached the perfection of mastery in the analytical knowledges! // SRS_36.38 //

children.text: saced bhavenmaṇiratanāna pūrṇā mahāsahasrā iya lokadhātuḥ /
children.translated_text: If this great trichiliocosm, this world-realm, were filled with jewels and gems,

children.text: ye divya śreṣṭhā maṇiratanāḥ pradhānā heṣṭaṃ upādāya bhavāgru yāvat // SRS_36.39 //
children.translated_text: the finest divine and supreme jewels — from the lowest level up to the highest existence, // SRS_36.39 //

children.text: yāvanta kṣetrā bahuvidha te anantā jāmbūnadāsaṃstṛta pūrṇa sarve /
children.translated_text: as many varied and infinite <s>Buddha</s>-fields — all covered and filled with <s>jāmbūnada</s> (fine gold),

children.text: dānaṃ dade jinavareṣu sarvaṃ bhūmītalādupari bhavāgra yāvat // SRS_36.40 //
children.translated_text: were one to give all of this as a gift to the supreme Conquerors — from the surface of the earth up to the highest existence, // SRS_36.40 //

children.text: yāvanti santi bahu vividhā hi sattvā dānaṃ dadeyurvividhamanantakalpān /
children.translated_text: as many varied beings as there are — were they to give varied gifts for infinite <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: buddhāna dadyuḥ satatamaviṣṭhihanto bodhyarthiko co daditu dānaskandham // SRS_36.41 //
children.translated_text: were they to give constantly to the <s>Buddhas</s> without ceasing — the mass of giving for the sake of awakening — // SRS_36.41 //

children.text: yaścaiva bhikṣurabhiratu śūnyatāyāṃ buddhānnamasye daśanakhaprāñjalīyo /
children.translated_text: yet a monk who delights in emptiness, who worships the <s>Buddhas</s> with palms joined at ten nails —

children.text: na sa dānaskandhaḥ purimaku yāti saṃkhyāṃ yaḥ śūnyatāyāmabhiratu bodhisattvaḥ // SRS_36.42 //
children.translated_text: that prior mass of giving does not equal [even] a fraction — for a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who delights in emptiness! // SRS_36.42 //

children.text: taṃ co labhitvā sa hi naru puṇyavanto dānaṃ dadeti vipulu janetva śraddhām /
children.translated_text: And having obtained that, the person rich in merit gives generously, having generated vast faith,

children.text: paryeṣamāṇo atuliya buddhabodhiṃ aupamyametaṃ kṛtu puruṣottamena // SRS_36.43 //
children.translated_text: seeking the incomparable awakening of the <s>Buddha</s> — this comparison was made by the Supreme Person! // SRS_36.43 //

children.text: yaśco samādhimimu varu śreṣṭha gṛhṇeccatuṣpadāṃ gātha sa tuṣṭacittaḥ /
children.translated_text: And one who grasps this supreme and excellent <s>samādhi</s>, [even] a four-line verse, with a satisfied mind —

children.text: yaḥ puṇyaskandho upacitu tena bhoti tat sarvadānaṃ śatimakalā nu bhoti // SRS_36.44 //
children.translated_text: the mass of merit accumulated by him — all that giving does not equal even a hundredth fraction of it! // SRS_36.44 //

children.text: (Vaidya 260)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 260)

children.text: na tāva śīghraṃ pratilabhi buddhajñānaṃ dānaṃ dadet so hitakaru bodhisattvaḥ /
children.translated_text: A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who acts for the benefit [of beings] does not so swiftly attain <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge by giving gifts

children.text: aśrutva etaṃ viraju samādhi śāntaṃ yatha śrutva śīghraṃ labhati sa buddhajñānam // SRS_36.45 //
children.translated_text: without hearing this dustless, peaceful <s>samādhi</s>, as he swiftly attains <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge upon hearing it. // SRS_36.45 //

children.text: yaśco labhitvā imu vara śāntabhūmiṃ śrutasya gotraṃ imu virajaṃ samādhim /
children.translated_text: And one who, having attained this supreme peaceful stage, the dustless <s>samādhi</s> of the lineage of learning,

children.text: puryāpuṇeyyā pramuditu bodhisattvaḥ sa śīghrametaṃ pratilabhi buddhajñānam // SRS_36.46 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Bodhisattva</s> rejoices with fulfillment — he swiftly attains this <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. // SRS_36.46 //

children.text: yo 'pī nidhānaṃ pratilabhi evarūpaṃ kṣetrānanantān yathariva gaṅgavālikāḥ /
children.translated_text: One who obtains such a treasure — fields as innumerable as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: te co bhaveyurmaṇiratanāna pūrṇā divyāna co tathapi ca mānuṣāṇām // SRS_36.47 //
children.translated_text: and those were to be filled with jewels and precious things, both divine and human — // SRS_36.47 //

children.text: durdharṣu so bhoti prebhūtakośo mahādhano dhanaratanenupetaḥ /
children.translated_text: he becomes invincible, of abundant treasury, possessing great wealth and jewels;

children.text: yo bodhisattvo labhati imaṃ samādhiṃ paryāpuṇantaḥ satatamatṛptu bhoti // SRS_36.48 //
children.translated_text: [yet] the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who attains this <s>samādhi</s>, while mastering it, remains ever unsated. // SRS_36.48 //

children.text: rājyaṃ labhitvā paramasamṛddha sphītaṃ na tena tuṣṭo bhavati kadāci vijñaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having attained a supremely prosperous and flourishing kingdom, a wise one is never content with that;

children.text: yathā labhitvā imu virajaṃ samādhiṃ tuṣṭo udagro bhavati sa bodhisattvaḥ // SRS_36.49 //
children.translated_text: but having attained this dustless <s>samādhi</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> becomes content and elated. // SRS_36.49 //

children.text: te te dharmadharā bhavanti satataṃ buddhāna sarvajñināṃ
children.translated_text: They are always bearers of the <s>Dharma</s> of the omniscient <s>Buddhas</s>,

children.text: dhārentī varadharmanetri vipulāṃ kṣīṇāntakāle tathā /
children.translated_text: upholding the vast, excellent <s>Dharma</s>-eye likewise at the time of the final end;

children.text: dharmakośadharā mahāmatidharāḥ sarvajñagañjaṃdharāḥ
children.translated_text: bearers of the <s>Dharma</s>-treasury, bearers of great wisdom, bearers of the treasury of omniscience —

children.text: te te sattva sahasrakoṭiniyutāṃstoṣanti dharmasvaraiḥ // SRS_36.50 //
children.translated_text: they satisfy thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of beings with the sounds of <s>Dharma</s>! // SRS_36.50 //

children.text: te te śīladhanenupeta matimān śikṣādhanāḍhyā narāḥ
children.translated_text: They are endowed with the wealth of moral conduct, wise, people rich in the wealth of training;

children.text: te te śīlavrate sthitā abhiratā dharmadrumasyāṅkurāḥ /
children.translated_text: they stand firm in moral observances, delighting [therein] — sprouts of the tree of <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: te te raktakaṣāyacīvaradharā naiṣkramyatuṣṭāḥ sadā
children.translated_text: they wear red-dyed robes, always content with renunciation;

children.text: te te sattvahitāya apratisamāḥ sarvajñatāṃ prasthitāḥ // SRS_36.51 //
children.translated_text: they are without equal for the benefit of beings, set out for omniscience! // SRS_36.51 //

children.text: te te dānta sudānta sattvadamakā damathenupetāḥ sadā
children.translated_text: They are tamed, well-tamed, tamers of beings, always endowed with the taming method;

children.text: te te śānta suśāntatāmanugatāḥ śāntapraśāntendriyāḥ /
children.translated_text: they are peaceful, having followed the state of supreme peace, with senses calmed and tranquil;

children.text: te te supta prasupta sattva satataṃ dharmasvanairbodhayī
children.translated_text: they constantly awaken sleeping, deeply slumbering beings with the sounds of <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: bodhitvā varaśreṣṭha dharmaratanaiḥ sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayī // SRS_36.52 //
children.translated_text: and having awakened them, establish beings in the supreme, excellent jewel of <s>Dharma</s>! // SRS_36.52 //

body.text: (Vaidya 261)

children.text: te te dānapatī bhavanti satataṃ sada muktatyāgī vidu
children.translated_text: They are always lords of giving, ever wise with open-handed liberality;

children.text: te te matsariyairna saṃvasi mahātyāge ramante sadā /
children.translated_text: they do not associate with miserliness, always delighting in great generosity;

children.text: te te sattva daridra dṛṣṭva dukhitān bhogehi saṃtarpayī
children.translated_text: seeing impoverished beings in distress, they satisfy them with possessions;

children.text: te te sattvahite sukhāya satataṃ sarvajñatāṃ prasthitāḥ // SRS_36.53 //
children.translated_text: they are always set out for omniscience, for the benefit and happiness of beings! // SRS_36.53 //

body.translated_text: (Vaidya 261)

children.text: te te āhani dharmabheri vipulāṃ jñāne sadā śikṣitāḥ
children.translated_text: They beat the great drum of <s>Dharma</s> daily, always trained in knowledge;

children.text: chindantī jana sarva saṃśayalatāṃ jñāne sadā prasthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: cutting the creeper of doubt in all people, always set out for knowledge;

children.text: te te suśruta dharmadhāri virajā sūtrāntakoṭīśatān
children.translated_text: they are well-learned, bearers of the <s>Dharma</s>, dustless, [having mastered] hundreds of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>sūtrāntas</s> —

children.text: parṣāyāṃ sthita āsane matidharāḥ pravyāharī paṇḍitāḥ // SRS_36.54 //
children.translated_text: wise bearers of wisdom, standing in the assembly on their seats, they discourse as scholars. // SRS_36.54 //

children.text: te te bhonti bahuśrutāḥ śrutidharāḥ saṃbuddhadharmaṃdharāḥ
children.translated_text: They are of great learning, bearers of what has been heard, bearers of the <s>Dharma</s> of the Perfectly Awakened Ones;

children.text: kośān dharmamayān dharanti munināṃ dharmānnidhāne ratāḥ /
children.translated_text: they bear the treasuries made of <s>Dharma</s> of the sages, delighting in the store of <s>dharmas</s>;

children.text: te te bhonti viśālaprajña vipulāṃ prīitiṃ janenti sadā
children.translated_text: they are of vast wisdom, always generating abundant joy,

children.text: deśentā varadharma śānta nipuṇaṃ nairyāṇikaṃ durdṛśam // SRS_36.55 //
children.translated_text: teaching the excellent, peaceful, subtle <s>Dharma</s>, leading to liberation, difficult to see. // SRS_36.55 //

children.text: te te dharmamadharmajñeya matimān dharme sthitāḥ sūratāḥ
children.translated_text: They are wise, knowing <s>dharma</s> from non-<s>dharma</s>, heroes established in the <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: dharmarājyi praśāsi apratisamā varadharmacārī sadā /
children.translated_text: they rule in the kingdom of <s>Dharma</s>, without equal, always practicing the excellent <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: te te bhonti viśiṣṭadharmagurukā gurugaurave ca sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: they revere the excellent <s>Dharma</s> as most eminent, established in reverence for teachers;

children.text: dharme nagavare sthitā matidharā dharmadhvajocchrāyikāḥ // SRS_36.56 //
children.translated_text: established on the mountain-peak of <s>Dharma</s>, bearers of wisdom, raisers of the banner of <s>Dharma</s>! // SRS_36.56 //

children.text: te te matta pramatta sattva satataṃ dṛṣṭvā pramāde sthitān
children.translated_text: Seeing intoxicated, heedless beings constantly established in negligence,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā caiva pranaṣṭa utpathagatān saṃsāramārge sthitān /
children.translated_text: and seeing those who are lost, gone astray, established on the path of <s>saṃsāra</s> —

children.text: teṣū maitra janitvudāra karuṇā muditāpyupekṣā sthitā
children.translated_text: having generated noble loving-kindness toward them, with great compassion, joy, and equanimity established,

children.text: teṣāṃ mārgavaraṃ pradarśayi śivamaṣṭāṅgikaṃ durdṛśam // SRS_36.57 //
children.translated_text: they show them the excellent, auspicious, eightfold path, difficult to see. // SRS_36.57 //

children.text: te tu nāva karitva dharma sudṛḍhāṃ dhārenti sattvān bahūn
children.translated_text: Having made the <s>Dharma</s> into a sturdy boat, they carry many beings

children.text: udyantān mahārṇaveṣu patitān saṃsārasrotogatān /
children.translated_text: who are striving [yet] fallen into the great oceans, gone with the current of <s>saṃsāra</s>;

children.text: bodhyaṅgā bala indriyaiḥ kavacitāḥ saddharmanāvāruhāḥ
children.translated_text: armored with the factors of awakening, powers, and faculties, mounted on the boat of the true <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: tīre pārami kṣema nityamabhaye sthāpenti sattvān sadā // SRS_36.58 //
children.translated_text: they always establish beings on the shore of the <s>pāramitās</s>, secure and ever fearless. // SRS_36.58 //

children.text: te te vaidyavarā vrateṣu caritā vaidyottamā vedakā
children.translated_text: They are the best of physicians, practiced in observances, supreme physicians and healers,

children.text: vidyājñānavimuktipāragamitā saddharmabhaiṣajyadāḥ /
children.translated_text: having reached the far shore of knowledge, wisdom, and liberation, giving the medicine of the true <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: dṛṣṭvā sattva gilāna nekavividhai rogaiḥ samabhyāhatān
children.translated_text: seeing sick beings afflicted by many and various diseases,

children.text: teṣāṃ dharmavirecanaṃ dadati taddharmaiścikitsanti tān // SRS_36.59 //
children.translated_text: they give them the purgative of <s>Dharma</s> and treat them with <s>dharmas</s>. // SRS_36.59 //

children.text: te te vādi apavādimathanā lokendra vāgīśvarāḥ
children.translated_text: They are speakers, crushers of opponents, lords of speech among world-leaders;

children.text: sarvajñeyaprabhaṃkarā matidharā varajñānabhūmisthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: illuminators of all that is to be known, bearers of wisdom, established on the stage of supreme knowledge;

children.text: śūra jñānabalā balapramathanāḥ saṃvarṇitā jñānibhiḥ
children.translated_text: heroes of knowledge-power, crushers of [hostile] forces, praised by the wise;

children.text: jñāneno bahusattvakoṭiniyutāṃstoṣyanti dharme sthitāḥ // SRS_36.60 //
children.translated_text: established in <s>Dharma</s>, they shall satisfy thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of beings through knowledge. // SRS_36.60 //

body.text: (Vaidya 262)

children.text: te te 'dhipati sārthavāha vipadaḥ sattvāna trāṇārthikāḥ
children.translated_text: They are sovereigns, caravan-leaders in dangers, seeking the protection of beings;

children.text: dṛṣṭvā sattva pramūḍha mārgaratane sada mārapāśe sthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: seeing beings deluded on the jeweled path, always standing in <s>Māra</s>'s snare —

children.text: teṣāṃ mārgavaraṃ prakāśayi śivaṃ kṣemaṃ sadā nirvṛtī
children.translated_text: they illuminate for them the excellent, auspicious, secure path, always [leading to] <s>nirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: yena jñānapathena nenti kuśalān bahusattvakoṭīśatān // SRS_36.61 //
children.translated_text: by which path of knowledge they lead hundreds of <s>koṭīs</s> of wholesome beings. // SRS_36.61 //

body.translated_text: (Vaidya 262)

children.text: te te lenu bhavanti trāṇu śaraṇaṃ cakṣuḥ pradīpaṃkarāḥ
children.translated_text: They are a shelter, a protection, a refuge, sight, and lamp-makers;

children.text: bhītānāmabhayapradāśca satataṃ trastāna cāśvāsakāḥ /
children.translated_text: always givers of fearlessness to the frightened and consolers of the terrified;

children.text: te 'tiduḥkhita sattva jñātva paramān jātyandhabhūtānimān
children.translated_text: knowing those exceedingly suffering beings, the supremely blind from birth —

children.text: dharmāloku karonti dharmaratane bhūtanaye śikṣitāḥ // SRS_36.62 //
children.translated_text: trained in the true method of the jewel of <s>Dharma</s>, they create the light of <s>Dharma</s>. // SRS_36.62 //

children.text: ye ye śilpavarā jage bahukarāḥ sattvāna arthāvahā
children.translated_text: Whatever excellent arts exist in the world, of many kinds, bringing benefit to beings —

children.text: yebhiḥ sattva sadā bhavanti sukhitāḥ śilpeṣu saṃśikṣitāḥ /
children.translated_text: by which beings are always made happy, trained in [those] arts;

children.text: śikṣāpāramitāṃ gatāḥ sukuśalā āścaryaprāptādbhutā
children.translated_text: having reached the perfection of training, supremely skillful, having attained the marvelous and wondrous —

children.text: ye bodhīnabhiprasthitā matidharā lokasya cakṣurdadāḥ // SRS_36.63 //
children.translated_text: those who have set out for awakening, bearers of wisdom, give sight to the world. // SRS_36.63 //

children.text: no te tṛpta kadācidapratisamā varabuddhadharmaśrutāḥ
children.translated_text: They are never sated, without equal, having heard the excellent <s>Buddha-dharma</s>,

children.text: śīlakṣāntisamādhipāragamitā gambhīradharmaśrutāḥ /
children.translated_text: having reached the far shore of moral conduct, patience, <s>samādhi</s>, having heard the profound <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: no tṛptāśca pareṣu dharmaratanaṃ te deśayantaḥ śivaṃ
children.translated_text: nor are they sated when teaching others the auspicious jewel of <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: mokṣopāyu pravarṣamāṇu varṣaṃ dharmairnarāṃstarpayī // SRS_36.64 //
children.translated_text: raining down the rain of the means of liberation, satisfying people with <s>dharmas</s>. // SRS_36.64 //

children.text: yāvanto bahu sattva teṣupagatā dharmārthikāḥ paṇḍitāḥ
children.translated_text: As many wise beings as approach them, desiring the <s>Dharma</s>, [saying:]

children.text: śroṣyāmo varadharmaśreṣṭharatanaṃ mārgaṃ ṛjuṃ añjasam /
children.translated_text: 'We shall hear the excellent, supreme jewel of <s>Dharma</s>, the straight and direct path!' —

children.text: teṣāṃ chindiṣu saṃśayān matiadharā dharmeṇa saṃtoṣayī
children.translated_text: they cut their doubts, bearers of the highest wisdom, satisfying them with the <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: śīlakṣāntisamādhipāramigatā jānanta sattvaśayān // SRS_36.65 //
children.translated_text: having reached the perfection of moral conduct, patience, and <s>samādhi</s>, knowing the dispositions of beings. // SRS_36.65 //

children.text: jñānī jñānavarāgra pāramigatāḥ sattvāśaye kovidāḥ
