children.translated_text: Wise, having reached the highest and foremost perfection of knowledge, skilled in the dispositions of beings,

children.text: jānantaḥ parasattvacittacaritaṃ yeṣāṃ kathā yādṛśī /
children.translated_text: knowing the mental conduct of other beings — whatever discourse is [appropriate] for each —

children.text: ye ye jñānakathāya sattvanayutā varadharmacakṣurlabhāḥ
children.translated_text: whatever <s>nayutas</s> of beings obtain the excellent eye of <s>Dharma</s> through discourse on knowledge,

children.text: te te jñānaviśeṣapāramigatā mārgopadeśaṃkarāḥ // SRS_36.66 //
children.translated_text: having reached the perfection of distinguished knowledge, they give instruction on the path. // SRS_36.66 //

children.text: mārā koṭisahasra teṣa viduṣāṃ cittaṃ pi no jāniṣu
children.translated_text: Thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Māras</s> cannot know the mind of those wise ones,

children.text: ākāśe yatha pakṣiṇāṃ padagatiṃ jñātuṃ na śakyā kvacit /
children.translated_text: just as the track of birds in the sky can never be known anywhere;

children.text: śāntā dānta praśānta jñānavaśino āryasmi jñāne sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: peaceful, tamed, supremely tranquil, masters of knowledge, established in noble knowledge —

children.text: sarvān māra nihatya śūra vṛṣabhā budhyanti bodhiṃ śivām // SRS_36.67 //
children.translated_text: having defeated all <s>Māras</s>, heroic bulls, they awaken to the auspicious awakening! // SRS_36.67 //

body.text:
ṛddhipāramiprāpta bhonti satataṃ gacchanti kṣetrān śatān
paśyanti bahubuddhakoṭiniyutān gaṅgā yathā vālikāḥ /

children.text: (Vaidya 263)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 263)

children.text: cakṣusteṣa na sajjate daśadiśe paśyanti rūpān bahu
children.translated_text: their eye is unattached in the ten directions, they behold many forms;

children.text: ye co sattva daśaddiśe bhavasthitāḥ sarveṣa te nāyakāḥ // SRS_36.68 //
children.translated_text: whatever beings are established in existence in the ten directions — they are the guides of them all. // SRS_36.68 //

body.translated_text: Having always attained the perfection of supernatural power, they go to hundreds of fields and behold many <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, as [numerous as] the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>;

children.text: te tasyo bhaṇi ānuśaṃsa sakalāṃ kalpāna koṭīśatān
children.translated_text: Were one to speak of the complete benefits of that [<s>samādhi</s>] for hundreds of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: no co pūrvacarīya varṇa kṣapaye pratibhānato bhāṣato /
children.translated_text: one could not exhaust the description of [their] former conduct, speaking with eloquence;

children.text: buddhānāṃ dhanamakṣayaṃ suvipulaṃ jñānasya co sāgaraṃ
children.translated_text: the inexhaustible, vast wealth of the <s>Buddhas</s>, and the ocean of knowledge —

children.text: yo etaṃ virajaṃ samādhimatulaṃ dhāreya kaścinnaraḥ // SRS_36.69 //
children.translated_text: [all this belongs to] whatever person upholds this dustless, incomparable <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_36.69 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje śīlaskandhanirdeśaparivartaḥ ṣaṭtriṃśatitamaḥ || 36 ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the thirty-sixth chapter in the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, the <s>Śīlaskandhanirdeśaparivarta</s> (Chapter on the Exposition of the Aggregate of Moral Conduct). || 36 ||

body.text:
(Vaidya 264)
37 Yaśaḥprabhaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 264) Chapter 37: The <s>Yaśaḥprabhaparivarta</s> (Chapter on <s>Yaśaḥprabha</s>).

body.text: tatra bhagavān punarapi candraprabhaṃ kumārabhūtamāmantrayate sma - tasmāttarhi kumāra bodhisattvena mahāsattvenemāṃścāparimāṇānāścaryādbhutān bodhisattvadharmānākāṅkṣatā kṣipraṃ cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhukāmenāyaṃ sarvadharmasvabhāvasamatāvipañcitaḥ samādhiḥ śrotavya udgrahītavyaḥ paryavāptavyo dhārayitavyo vācayitavyaḥ pravartayitavyaḥ uddeṣṭavyaḥ svādhyātavyo 'raṇābhāvanayā bhāvayitavyo bahulīkartavyaḥ parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayitavyaḥ | kṣāntibalaṃ cānena bhāvayitavyam | kṣāntirāsevayitavyā bhāvayitavyā bahulīkartavyā | dharmārthikena ca bhavitavyaṃ dharmakāmena dharmapratigrāhakena dharmānudharmapratipannena | buddhapūjābhiyuktena bhavitavyam | tena triṣu sthāneṣvabhiyogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | katameṣu triṣu? yaduta kleśakṣayāya puṇyabalādhipataye buddhajñānamākāṅkṣatā kuśalamūlānyavaropayitavyāni no tu khalu lokasukhasparśābhikāṅkṣiṇā | eṣu triṣu sthāneṣvabhiyogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: There the Blessed One again addressed Prince <s>Candraprabha</s>: "Therefore, O Prince, a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> who aspires to these immeasurable, marvelous, and wondrous <s>Bodhisattva-dharmas</s>, who wishes to swiftly attain unsurpassed perfect awakening, should hear this <s>samādhi</s> that elaborates the equality of the own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s>, should grasp it, master it, retain it, recite it, propagate it, expound it, study it, cultivate it through the practice of forest solitude, make it abundant, and explain it in detail to others. He should cultivate the power of patience; patience should be resorted to, cultivated, and made abundant. He should be one who desires the <s>Dharma</s>, loves the <s>Dharma</s>, receives the <s>Dharma</s>, practices the <s>Dharma</s> in conformity with the <s>Dharma</s>. He should be devoted to <s>Buddha</s>-worship. He should exert effort in three areas. Which three? Namely: desiring the destruction of defilements, the supremacy of merit-power, and <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, he should plant wholesome roots — but not out of desire for worldly happiness. In these three areas, effort should be exerted."

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāṃ candraprabhasya kumārabhūtasya tamevārthamudyotayamāna imameva pūrvayogakathānirdeśaṃ gāthābhigītena saṃprakāśayati sma -
body.translated_text: Then at that time, the Blessed One, illuminating that very meaning for Prince <s>Candraprabha</s>, elucidated this very narrative of a former connection (<s>pūrvayoga</s>) in verse:

children.text: hanta śṛṇotha mametu kumārā kalpasahasra yathā caritā me /
children.translated_text: "Come, listen to me, O princes — how my conduct was for thousands of <s>kalpas</s>!

children.text: pūjita buddhasahasraśatāni eṣatu eti samādhi praṇītam // SRS_37.1 //
children.translated_text: I worshipped hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s> — this excellent <s>samādhi</s> is thus! // SRS_37.1 //

children.text: kalpa acintiya evamatītāḥ kṣetraśateṣu ye vālika asti /
children.translated_text: Inconceivable <s>kalpas</s> thus passed — [as many as] the grains of sand in hundreds of fields;

children.text: eṣa nidarśanu kīrtitu bhotī yaṃ jinu āsi gaṇeśvaranāmā // SRS_37.2 //
children.translated_text: this illustration is proclaimed — there was a <s>Jina</s> named <s>Gaṇeśvara</s>. // SRS_37.2 //

children.text: ṣaṣṭiranūnaka koṭisahasrāṇyāsi gaṇottamu tasya jinastha /
children.translated_text: No less than sixty thousand <s>koṭīs</s> were the supreme assembly of that <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: sarvi anāsravi kṣīṇakileśā aṣṭavimokṣapratiṣṭhita dhyāyī // SRS_37.3 //
children.translated_text: all without <s>āsravas</s>, defilements destroyed, meditators established in the eight liberations. // SRS_37.3 //

children.text: tatra ca kāli iyamapi sarvā kṣema subhikṣa anākula āsīt /
children.translated_text: And at that time, this entire [land] was secure, well-provisioned, and untroubled;

children.text: saukhyasamarpita sarvamanuṣyāḥ prīṇita mānuṣakebhi sukhebhiḥ // SRS_37.4 //
children.translated_text: all human beings were endowed with happiness, delighted by human pleasures. // SRS_37.4 //

children.text: (Vaidya 265)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 265)

children.text: puṇyabalena ca sarva upetā darśaniyāstatha premaṇiyāśca /
children.translated_text: All endowed with the power of merit, beautiful and lovable,

children.text: āḍhya mahādhana sarva samṛddhā divyasukhena samarpitagātrāḥ // SRS_37.5 //
children.translated_text: wealthy, of great riches, all prosperous, their bodies endowed with divine happiness. // SRS_37.5 //

children.text: sūratu suvrata mandakileśāḥ kṣāntibalābhiratā abhirūpāḥ /
children.translated_text: Of good conduct and good vows, with slight defilements, delighting in the power of patience, of beautiful form,

children.text: devapureṣu yathā maruputrāḥ śīlaguṇopagatā matimantaḥ // SRS_37.6 //
children.translated_text: like the sons of <s>Maruts</s> in divine cities — endowed with the virtues of moral conduct, wise. // SRS_37.6 //

children.text: tatra ca kāli mahīpatirāsīd rājasuto varapuṣpasunāmā /
children.translated_text: At that time there was a prince, a king's son, named <s>Varapuṣpa</s>;

children.text: tasya ca putra anūnakamāsan pañcaśatā smṛtimanmatimantaḥ // SRS_37.7 //
children.translated_text: his sons were no fewer than five hundred — mindful and wise. // SRS_37.7 //

children.text: tena ca rājasutena jinasyo ṣaṣṭi udyānasahasraśatāni /
children.translated_text: By that prince, to the <s>Jina</s>, sixty hundred thousand pleasure-gardens,

children.text: puṣpaphalapratimaṇḍita sarve tasya niryātita kāruṇikasya // SRS_37.8 //
children.translated_text: all adorned with flowers and fruits, were given over to the Compassionate One. // SRS_37.8 //

children.text: vicitra udyāna sahasraśatā caṃkramaśayyaniṣadyasahasraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Varied hundreds of thousands of pleasure-gardens, with thousands of walking-paths, beds, and seats,

children.text: cīvarakoṭisahasraśatebhiḥ saṃstṛta caṃkramaṇāśca niṣadyāḥ // SRS_37.9 //
children.translated_text: with hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of robes — walking-paths and seats were spread [therewith]. // SRS_37.9 //

children.text: evamanekaprakārasahasrā yāttaka śrāmaṇakāḥ paribhogāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, with many and various thousands — whatever requisites there are for renunciants —

children.text: rājasutena prasannamanenā tasya upasthāpitāḥ sugatasya // SRS_37.10 //
children.translated_text: by the prince with a clear mind, the <s>Sugata</s> was served. // SRS_37.10 //

children.text: so daśasu śubhakarmapatheṣu rāja pratiṣṭhita sādhūjanenā /
children.translated_text: That king, established in the ten wholesome courses of action by virtuous people,

children.text: prāṇasahasraśatānayutebhirgacchi puraskṛtu nāyaku draṣṭam // SRS_37.11 //
children.translated_text: went, accompanied by hundreds of thousands of <s>nayutas</s> of living beings, to see the Guide, going before him. // SRS_37.11 //

children.text: puṣpavilepanadhūpa gṛhītvā chatrapatākadhvajāṃstatha vādyān /
children.translated_text: Taking flowers, ointments, and incense, as well as parasols, banners, flags, and music,

children.text: (Vaidya 266)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 266)

children.text: pūja karitva sa tasya jinasya prāñjalikaḥ purata sthita āsīt // SRS_37.12 //
children.translated_text: having made worship to that <s>Jina</s>, he stood before him with palms joined. // SRS_37.12 //

children.text: tuṣṭa abhūttada bhikṣusahasrā devamanuṣyatha yakṣasurāśca /
children.translated_text: Then thousands of monks, gods, humans, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Asuras</s> were delighted:

children.text: vyākaru kiṃ nu jino imu pūjāṃ sādhu kiṃ vakṣyati dharmu narendraḥ // SRS_37.13 //
children.translated_text: 'Will the <s>Jina</s> give a prediction for this worship? Will the Lord of Men speak well the <s>Dharma</s>?' // SRS_37.13 //

children.text: tasya ca āśaya jñātva svayaṃbhū rājasutasya niruttaru cittam /
children.translated_text: The Self-Arisen One, knowing the disposition of that prince — his unsurpassed mind,

children.text: pāragato abhimuktipadeṣu tasyima deśayi śānta samādhim // SRS_37.14 //
children.translated_text: having gone beyond, [established] in the stages of liberation — taught him this peaceful <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_37.14 //

children.text: yāva pramukta girā sugatenā kampita medini savanaṣaṇḍā /
children.translated_text: As soon as the <s>Sugata</s> released this utterance, the earth trembled with its groves,

children.text: puṣpa pravarṣi tadā gaganātaḥ padmaśatāpi ca udgata bhūmau // SRS_37.15 //
children.translated_text: flowers rained from the sky, and hundreds of lotuses arose from the ground. // SRS_37.15 //

children.text: vyākari nāyaku āśayu jñātvā arthapadeṣu suśikṣita śāstā /
children.translated_text: The Guide gave a prediction, knowing his disposition; the Teacher, well-trained in doctrinal points,

children.text: deśayi śānta samādhi narendrastatrimi arthapadāni śṛṇotha // SRS_37.16 //
children.translated_text: taught the peaceful <s>samādhi</s> to the lord of men — hear these doctrinal points here. // SRS_37.16 //

children.text: sarvi bhavā abhavāḥ parikalpāstuccha marīcisamā yatha māyāḥ /
children.translated_text: All existences are non-existences, mere conceptualizations — empty, like a mirage, like an illusion,

children.text: vidyatameghasamāścala śūnyāḥ sarvi nirātma nisattva nijīvāḥ // SRS_37.17 //
children.translated_text: like a flash of lightning, a cloud — transient, empty; all are without self, without being, without life. // SRS_37.17 //

children.text: āditu śūnya anāgata dharmā nāgata asthita sthānavimuktāḥ /
children.translated_text: From the very beginning empty, future <s>dharmas</s> have not come, have not abided, are free from abiding;

children.text: nityamasāraka māyasvabhāvāḥ śuddha viśuddha nabhopama sarve // SRS_37.18 //
children.translated_text: always insubstantial, of the nature of illusion — pure, utterly pure, all like space. // SRS_37.18 //

children.text: naiva ca nīla na pita na śvetā nāmatu riktaku ghoṣasvabhāvāḥ /
children.translated_text: Neither blue, nor yellow, nor white — named [yet] hollow, of the nature of mere sound;

children.text: cittavivikta acittasvabhāvāḥ sarvarūtāpagatāḥ kṣaṇikatvāt // SRS_37.19 //
children.translated_text: the mind is isolated, of the nature of non-mind; all utterances are departed, because of momentariness. // SRS_37.19 //

children.text: bhāṣatu akṣaru saṃkramu nāsti no pi abhāṣatu saṃkaru bhoti /
children.translated_text: Though spoken, there is no transference of syllables; nor does transference occur when unspoken.

children.text: (Vaidya 267)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 267)

children.text: nāpi ca akṣara deśa vrajantī no punarakṣaru krānti kutaścit // SRS_37.20 //
children.translated_text: Nor does a syllable go to any place; nor again does a syllable come from anywhere. // SRS_37.20 //

children.text: akṣara akṣaya kṣīṇa niruddhā bhāṣatato va abhāṣatato vā /
children.translated_text: Syllables are inexhaustible, exhausted, ceased — whether from speaking or not speaking;

children.text: nityamimakṣara akṣaya uktā yaḥ parijānati so 'kṣayu bhoti // SRS_37.21 //
children.translated_text: always these syllables are declared inexhaustible — one who fully comprehends this becomes inexhaustible. // SRS_37.21 //

body.text:
buddhasahasraśatā ya atītā dharmasahasraśatāni bhaṇitvā /
naiva ca dharmu na cākṣara kṣīṇā | nāsti samutpatti tena akṣīṇā // SRS_37.22 //
body.translated_text: Hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s> who have passed, having spoken hundreds of thousands of teachings — neither the <s>Dharma</s> nor the syllables are exhausted; there is no arising, therefore they are inexhaustible. // SRS_37.22 //

children.text: yena prajānati akṣayadharmān nityu prajānati akṣayadharmān /
children.translated_text: One who comprehends the inexhaustible <s>dharmas</s> always comprehends the inexhaustible <s>dharmas</s>;

children.text: sutrasahasraśatāni bhaṇitvā sarvi anakṣara jānati dharmān // SRS_37.23 //
children.translated_text: having spoken hundreds of thousands of <s>sūtras</s>, he knows all <s>dharmas</s> as without syllables. // SRS_37.23 //

children.text: yaṃ ca prabhāṣati dharma jinasyo taṃ ca na manyati so 'kṣayatāye /
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>Dharma</s> the <s>Jina</s> proclaims, he does not conceive of that as inexhaustibility;

children.text: ādi nirātmani ye tvimi dharmā tāṃśca prabhāṣati no ca kṣapeti // SRS_37.24 //
children.translated_text: these <s>dharmas</s> which from the beginning are without self — those he proclaims, yet does not diminish them. // SRS_37.24 //

children.text: sarvagiraḥ sa prabhāṣati vijño no ca girāya harīyati cittam /
children.translated_text: The wise one speaks all words, yet his mind is not carried away by words;

children.text: sarvagiro girighoṣanikāśo tena na sajjati jātu girāye // SRS_37.25 //
children.translated_text: all words are like a mountain echo — therefore he is never attached to words. // SRS_37.25 //

children.text: yāya girāya sa kīrtitu dharmaḥ sā gira tatkṣaṇi sarva niruddhā /
children.translated_text: By whatever word the <s>Dharma</s> was proclaimed, that word ceases entirely at that very moment;

children.text: yādṛśu lakṣaṇu tasya girāye sarvimi dharma tallakṣaṇaprāptāḥ // SRS_37.26 //
children.translated_text: whatever is the characteristic of that word — all these <s>dharmas</s> have attained that [same] characteristic. // SRS_37.26 //

children.text: sarvimi dharma alakṣa vilakṣā sarvi alakṣaṇa lakṣaṇaśuddhāḥ /
children.translated_text: All these <s>dharmas</s> are sign-less, free from signs; all are without marks, purified in their marklessness;

children.text: nitya vivikta viśuddha nabho vā saṃkhya samāsatu te na upenti // SRS_37.27 //
children.translated_text: always isolated, pure, like space — they do not submit to enumeration or summary. // SRS_37.27 //

children.text: saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛta sarvi viviktā nāsti vikalpana teṣamṛṣīṇām /
children.translated_text: The conditioned and unconditioned are all isolated; there is no conceptualization for those sages.

children.text: (Vaidya 268)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 268)

children.text: sarvagatīṣu asaṃskṛta prāptā dṛṣṭigatehi sadaiva viviktāḥ // SRS_37.28 //
children.translated_text: In all destinies, having attained the unconditioned, they are always isolated from views and theories. // SRS_37.28 //

children.text: nityamarakta aduṣṭa amūḍhāstasya svabhāva samāhitacittāḥ /
children.translated_text: Always without passion, without hatred, without delusion — their minds concentrated in that [<s>dharma</s>-]nature;

children.text: eṣa samādhibalī balavanto yo imu jānati īdṛśa dharmān // SRS_37.29 //
children.translated_text: this is the power of <s>samādhi</s>, the powerful one — he who knows <s>dharmas</s> of such a nature. // SRS_37.29 //

children.text: śailaguhāgiridurganadīṣu yadva pratiśrutka jāyi pratītya /
children.translated_text: In mountain caves, gorges, ravines, and rivers — whatever echo arises from conditions,

children.text: evimu saṃskṛti sarvi vijāne māyamarīcisamaṃ jagu sarvam // SRS_37.30 //
children.translated_text: know all conditioned existence thus — the entire world is like an illusion and a mirage. // SRS_37.30 //

children.text: prajñabalaṃ guṇa dharmagatānāṃ jñānabalena abhijña ṛṣīṇām /
children.translated_text: The power of wisdom, the qualities of those who have entered the <s>Dharma</s>, by the power of knowledge, the <s>abhijñā</s> (higher knowledges) of sages,

children.text: vāca upāyakuśalya niruktā yatra prakāśitu śānta samādhiḥ // SRS_37.31 //
children.translated_text: words spoken with skill in means and etymology — where this peaceful <s>samādhi</s> is illuminated. // SRS_37.31 //

children.text: kalpitu vuccati kalpanamātraṃ antu na labhyati saṃsaramāṇe /
children.translated_text: What is conceptualized is called mere conceptualization; no end can be found in <s>saṃsāra</s>;

children.text: koṭi alakṣaṇa yā puri āsīdapi anāgati pratyayatāye // SRS_37.32 //
children.translated_text: the limit is mark-less, which was formerly [unknown] — and also in the future, through conditionality. // SRS_37.32 //

children.text: karma kriyāya ca vartati evaṃ hīna utkṛṣṭatayā samudenti /
children.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> proceeds through action in just this way — arising in inferior and superior forms;

children.text: vivikta dharma sadā prakṛtīye śūnya nirātma vijānatha sarvān // SRS_37.33 //
children.translated_text: know all <s>dharmas</s> as always isolated in their nature, empty, without self. // SRS_37.33 //

children.text: saṃvṛti bhāṣitu dharma jinenāsaṃskṛtasaṃskṛta paśyatha evam /
children.translated_text: The <s>Dharma</s> was spoken by the <s>Jina</s> as conventional truth — see the unconditioned and conditioned thus:

children.text: nāstiha bhūtatu ātma naro vā etaku lakṣaṇa sarvajagasya // SRS_37.34 //
children.translated_text: there exists in truth neither a self nor a person — such is the characteristic of the entire world. // SRS_37.34 //

children.text: kṛṣṇāśubha ca na naśyati karma ātmana kṛtva ca vedayitavyam /
children.translated_text: Dark, unwholesome <s>karma</s> does not perish; having created it oneself, it must be experienced;

children.text: no puna saṃkrama karmaphalasya no ca ahetuka pratyanubhonti // SRS_37.35 //
children.translated_text: there is no transference of the fruit of <s>karma</s>, nor do [beings] experience it without a cause. // SRS_37.35 //

children.text: (Vaidya 269)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 269)

children.text: sarvi bhavā alikā vaśikāśco riktaku tuccha phenasamāśca /
children.translated_text: All existences are false and illusory — hollow, empty, like foam;

children.text: māyamarīcisamāḥ sada śunyā deśitu śabditu te ca viviktāḥ // SRS_37.36 //
children.translated_text: always empty like an illusion and a mirage — those that are taught and proclaimed are [also] isolated. // SRS_37.36 //

children.text: evaṃ vijānatu manyana nāstī śīlavu bhotī aniśritacittaḥ /
children.translated_text: For one who knows thus, there is no conceit; he becomes possessed of morality, with unattached mind;

children.text: kṣāntibalena na kalpayi kiṃci eva carantu samāhitu bhoti // SRS_37.37 //
children.translated_text: by the power of patience he does not conceptualize anything — practicing thus, he becomes concentrated. // SRS_37.37 //

children.text: yāttaka dharma vijāni sa rājā tāttaka deśita tena jinena /
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>Dharma</s> that king understood, that much was taught to him by the <s>Jina</s>;

children.text: śrutva nṛpo imu dharma jinasyo saparivāru samādadi śikṣām // SRS_37.38 //
children.translated_text: having heard this <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Jina</s>, the lord of men with his retinue undertook the training. // SRS_37.38 //

children.text: rājasuto imu śrutva samādhiṃ āttamanā mudito bhaṇi vācam /
children.translated_text: The prince, having heard this <s>samādhi</s>, delighted and joyful, spoke these words:

children.text: suṣṭhu subhāṣitu eṣa samādhī eṣa tavā caraṇeṣu patāmi // SRS_37.39 //
children.translated_text: 'Excellent! Well-spoken is this <s>samādhi</s>! I fall at your feet!' // SRS_37.39 //

children.text: tatra ca prāṇisahasra aśītiḥ śrutvimu dharmasvabhāva praṇītam /
children.translated_text: There, eighty thousand beings, having heard this excellent explanation of the nature of <s>dharmas</s> —

children.text: bhūtu ayaṃ paramārtha nirdeśo te anutpattika kṣānti labhiṃsu // SRS_37.40 //
children.translated_text: this being an exposition of ultimate truth — they attained the <s>anutpattikadharma-kṣānti</s> (acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas). // SRS_37.40 //

children.text: nāsti upādu nirodhu narasyo evimi dharma sadā viviktāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'There is no arising or cessation for a person' — thus these <s>dharmas</s> are always isolated;

children.text: eva prajānatu no parihāṇi rāja labhī anutpattika kṣāntim // SRS_37.41 //
children.translated_text: for one who comprehends thus, there is no decline — the king attained the <s>anutpattikadharma-kṣānti</s>. // SRS_37.41 //

children.text: rāja tadā vijahitvana rājyaṃ pravraji śāsani tasya jinasya /
children.translated_text: The king then, abandoning his kingdom, went forth in the teaching of that <s>Jina</s>;

children.text: te 'pyanu pravrajitāḥ suta rājñaḥ pañcaśatāni anūnaka sarve // SRS_37.42 //
children.translated_text: after him, the sons of the king also went forth — five hundred, all without exception. // SRS_37.42 //

children.text: pravrajito yada rāja saputro anya tadā bahuprāṇisahasrāḥ /
children.translated_text: When the king went forth with his sons, then many other thousands of beings

children.text: pravrajitāḥ sugatasya samīpe dharma gaveṣiyu tasya jinasya // SRS_37.43 //
children.translated_text: went forth in the presence of the <s>Sugata</s>, seeking the <s>Dharma</s> of that <s>Jina</s>. // SRS_37.43 //

children.text: (Vaidya 270)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 270)

children.text: viṃśativarṣaśatān paripūrṇān dharma prakāśitu tena jinenā /
children.translated_text: For a full two thousand years, the <s>Dharma</s> was illuminated by that <s>Jina</s>;

children.text: rāja saputraku tena janenā viṃśativarṣaśatā cari dharmam // SRS_37.44 //
children.translated_text: the king with his sons and that people practiced the <s>Dharma</s> for two thousand years. // SRS_37.44 //

children.text: atha apareṇa punaḥ samayena so 'pi jinaḥ parinirvṛtu āsīt /
children.translated_text: Then at another time, that <s>Jina</s> too entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s>;

children.text: ye jinaśrāvaka te 'pi atītāḥ so 'pi ca dharmu parittaku āsīt // SRS_37.45 //
children.translated_text: those who were the <s>Jina</s>'s disciples also passed away, and that <s>Dharma</s> too became diminished. // SRS_37.45 //

body.text:
tasya ca rājina putra abhūṣī puṇyamatī sada śrāddhu prasannaḥ /
tasya ca bhikṣu kulopagu āsīt | so imu deśayi śānta samādhim // SRS_37.46 //
body.translated_text: The king had a son, <s>Puṇyamati</s>, always faithful and devoted, and there was a monk who frequented his family — he taught this peaceful <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_37.46 //

children.text: so akhilo madhuro ca abhūṣī satkṛtu prāṇisahasraśatebhiḥ /
children.translated_text: He was sincere and sweet-natured, honored by hundreds of thousands of beings;

children.text: devata koṭiśatānyanubaddhā varṇa bhaṇanti kulān praviśitvā // SRS_37.47 //
children.translated_text: hundreds of <s>koṭīs</s> of deities followed him, proclaiming his virtues when he entered households. // SRS_37.47 //

children.text: sa smṛtimān matimān gatimāṃśco suvratu sūratu śīlarataśca /
children.translated_text: He was mindful, wise, eloquent, well-disciplined, gentle, delighting in morality,

children.text: susvaru aparuṣa so madhuraśco dhātuṣu jñānavaśī varaprāptaḥ // SRS_37.48 //
children.translated_text: sweet-voiced, mild, agreeable — a master of knowledge in the elements, having attained the best. // SRS_37.48 //

children.text: cīvarakoṭiśatāna ca lābhī āsi sa bhikṣu yaśaḥprabhu nāmnā /
children.translated_text: He obtained hundreds of <s>koṭīs</s> of robes — that monk was named <s>Yaśaḥprabha</s>;

children.text: tasya ca puṇyabalaṃ asahantā bhikṣusahasra tadā jani īrṣām // SRS_37.49 //
children.translated_text: unable to bear his power of merit, thousands of monks then generated envy. // SRS_37.49 //

children.text: puṇyabalena ca rūpabalena jñānabalena ca ṛddhibalena /
children.translated_text: By the power of merit, the power of beauty, the power of knowledge, the power of <s>ṛddhi</s>,

children.text: śīlabalena samādhibaleno dharmabalena samudgata bhikṣuḥ // SRS_37.50 //
children.translated_text: the power of morality, the power of <s>samādhi</s>, the power of <s>Dharma</s> — that monk was exalted. // SRS_37.50 //

children.text: hṛṣṭamanaśca priyaśca janasyo bhikṣu upāsakabhikṣuṇikānām /
children.translated_text: He was joyful in mind and dear to the people — to monks, lay followers, and nuns;

children.text: (Vaidya 271)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 271)

children.text: ye jinaśāsani sattva prasannāsteṣamabhīpsita pūjaniyāśca // SRS_37.51 //
children.translated_text: those beings who were devoted to the <s>Jina</s>'s teaching — for them he was desired and worthy of worship. // SRS_37.51 //

children.text: yaśca sa rājinu putru abhūṣī puṇyamatī sada śrāddhu prasannaḥ /
children.translated_text: The king's son, <s>Puṇyamati</s>, always faithful and devoted,

children.text: jñātva praduṣṭamanān bahubhikṣūṃ rakṣa sa kārayi ācariyasya // SRS_37.52 //
children.translated_text: knowing that many monks had corrupt minds, arranged protection for his teacher. // SRS_37.52 //

children.text: pañcahi prāṇisahasraśatehī varmita khaḍgagadāyudhakehi /
children.translated_text: With five hundred thousand beings, armed with armor, swords, and maces,

children.text: tehi sadā parivārita bhikṣu bhāṣati bhūtacarīmaparyantām // SRS_37.53 //
children.translated_text: always surrounded by them, the monk proclaimed the limitless conduct of truth. // SRS_37.53 //

children.text: so pariṣāya prabhāṣati dharmaṃ śūnya nirātma nirjīvimi dharmāḥ /
children.translated_text: He proclaimed the <s>Dharma</s> to the assembly: 'These <s>dharmas</s> are empty, without self, without life;

children.text: ye upalambhika ātmaniviṣṭāsteṣa na rocati yaṃ bhaṇi bhikṣuḥ // SRS_37.54 //
children.translated_text: those who are attached to self-grasping — for them what the monk speaks is not pleasing.' // SRS_37.54 //

children.text: utthitu bhikṣava śastra gṛhītvā yeṣa na rocati śūnyata śāntā /
children.translated_text: The monks rose up, seizing weapons — those for whom peaceful emptiness was not pleasing:

children.text: eṣa adharma prabhāṣati bhikṣuḥ etu hanitva bhaviṣyati puṇyam // SRS_37.55 //
children.translated_text: 'This monk proclaims non-<s>Dharma</s>! Come, having killed him, there will be merit!' // SRS_37.55 //

children.text: dṛṣṭva ca śastra na bhāyati bhikṣuḥ śūnyaka dharmamanusmaramāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing the weapons, the monk was not afraid, recollecting the empty nature of <s>dharmas</s>:

children.text: nāstiha sattva naro vāpahatyai kuḍyasamā imi riktaka dharmāḥ // SRS_37.56 //
children.translated_text: 'There is here no being or person to be slain — these <s>dharmas</s> are hollow like a wall.' // SRS_37.56 //

children.text: bhikṣu karoti sa añjali mūrdhnā bhāṣati vāca namo 'stu jinānām /
children.translated_text: The monk made <s>añjali</s> at his head and spoke: 'Homage to the <s>Jinas</s>!

children.text: yena satyenimi śūnyaka dharmā bhontimi śastra māndāravapuṣpāḥ // SRS_37.57 //
children.translated_text: By the truth that these <s>dharmas</s> are empty — may these weapons become <s>Māndārava</s> flowers!' // SRS_37.57 //

children.text: śīlavratopagatasya munisyo bhāṣitamātra ananyathavākye /
children.translated_text: For that sage who had undertaken morality and vows, by the mere utterance of his truthful words,

children.text: kampita medini savanaṣaṇḍā śastra te jāta māndāravapuṣpāḥ // SRS_37.58 //
children.translated_text: the earth trembled with its groves, and those weapons became <s>Māndārava</s> flowers! // SRS_37.58 //

children.text: (Vaidya 272)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 272)

children.text: bhikṣu abhūttada maṃkuśarīrā ye upalambhika śastragṛhītāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the monks became limp in body — those who had grasped weapons with attachment to [the view of] apprehension;

children.text: bhūyu ya śakyupasaṃkramaṇāye trasya abhūt sumahādbhutajātāḥ // SRS_37.59 //
children.translated_text: that they were still able to approach — they became greatly terrified, astonished. // SRS_37.59 //

children.text: ye puna śrāddha prasanna munīndre yeṣiha rocati śunyata śāntā /
children.translated_text: But those who had faith and devotion in the Lord of Sages, those for whom peaceful emptiness was pleasing —

children.text: tehi huṃkārasahasra karitvā dūṣyaśatairabhichādita bhikṣuḥ // SRS_37.60 //
children.translated_text: they, making thousands of exclamations of wonder, covered the monk with hundreds of silk garments. // SRS_37.60 //

children.text: bhikṣu janitvana maitra sa teṣu sarvajanasya purasta bhaṇāti /
children.translated_text: The monk, generating <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) toward them, proclaimed before all people:

children.text: ye mayi sattva pradoṣa karontī teṣa kṛte na hu bodhi carāmi // SRS_37.61 //
children.translated_text: 'Those beings who generate hostility toward me — it is for their sake that I practice the awakening conduct.' // SRS_37.61 //

children.text: tena ca varṣa aśītiranūnā bhāṣita śūnyata koṣu jinānām /
children.translated_text: For a full eighty years, he proclaimed emptiness in the treasury of the <s>Jinas</s>;

children.text: bhikṣusahasra pratyarthika āsan ye ca nivārita rājasutena // SRS_37.62 //
children.translated_text: thousands of monks were adversaries, yet they were restrained by the king's son. // SRS_37.62 //

children.text: so 'pi tadā paribhūt abhūṣī tasya ca bhikṣu parīttaku āsan /
children.translated_text: He too was reviled at that time, and that monk had few [followers];

children.text: vācamaniṣṭa tadā śruṇamānaḥ kṣāntibalā cyuta no ca kadācit // SRS_37.63 //
children.translated_text: hearing unpleasant words, he never once fell from the power of patience. // SRS_37.63 //

children.text: so 'pareṇa ca punaḥ samayena prāṇiśatāna karī mahadartham /
children.translated_text: Then at another time, he performed great benefit for hundreds of beings,

children.text: śīlamakhilamanusmaramāṇaḥ puṇyamatisya tadā bhaṇi vācam // SRS_37.64 //
children.translated_text: recollecting his unblemished morality — <s>Puṇyamati</s> then spoke these words. // SRS_37.64 //

children.text: tatra sa gauravu kṛtva udāraṃ puṇyamatī avacī tada bhikṣum /
children.translated_text: There, having shown great respect, <s>Puṇyamati</s> then said to the monk:

children.text: mā mama kinacidācariyasyo cetasi kiṃci kṛtaṃ amanāpam // SRS_37.65 //
children.translated_text: 'May my teacher not have anything unpleasant done to his mind by me!' // SRS_37.65 //

children.text: so avacī śṛṇu rājakumārā kṣāntibalena samudgata buddhāḥ /
children.translated_text: He replied: 'Listen, prince! <s>Buddhas</s> arise through the power of patience;

children.text: (Vaidya 273)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 273)

children.text: yena mi bhāṣita vācamaniṣṭāstasyimi antiki maitra udārā // SRS_37.66 //
children.translated_text: toward those who have spoken unpleasant words to me — for them I have great loving-kindness.' // SRS_37.66 //

children.text: yena sa kalpasahasraśatāni kṣānti niṣevita pūrvabhaveṣu /
children.translated_text: For hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, he cultivated patience in former existences;

children.text: so ahu bhikṣu yaśaḥprabhu āsaṃ śākyamunirbhagavān bhaṇi vācam // SRS_37.67 //
children.translated_text: 'I was that monk <s>Yaśaḥprabha</s>' — the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> spoke these words. // SRS_37.67 //

children.text: yena yaśaḥprabhu rakṣitu bhikṣuḥ puṇyamatī tada rājinu putraḥ /
children.translated_text: The one who was <s>Puṇyamati</s>, the king's son, who protected the monk <s>Yaśaḥprabha</s> —

children.text: jātisahasra mamāsi sahāyaḥ so maya vyākṛtu maitraku buddhaḥ // SRS_37.68 //
children.translated_text: for thousands of births he was my companion; he was predicted by me as the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Maitreya</s>. // SRS_37.68 //

children.text: yena gaṇeśvara pūjitu śāstā yena tu kārita śreṣṭha vihārāḥ /
children.translated_text: The one by whom the Teacher, Lord of the Assembly, was worshipped, by whom excellent <s>vihāras</s> were built —

children.text: pūrvamasau varapuṣpasunāmā so padumotturu āsi munīndraḥ // SRS_37.69 //
children.translated_text: he was formerly the <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Varapuṣpa</s> (Excellent Flower); he was the supreme lotus among Lords of Sages. // SRS_37.69 //

children.text: eva mayā bahukalpa anantā dhārayitāmimu dharma jinānām /
children.translated_text: Thus for endless many <s>kalpas</s>, I have upheld this <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Jinas</s>;

children.text: kṣāntibalaṃ samudānita pūrve śratva kumāra mamā anuśikṣāḥ // SRS_37.70 //
children.translated_text: the power of patience was accumulated in the past — having heard, O prince, follow my example! // SRS_37.70 //

children.text: nirvṛtimapyatha bheṣyati evaṃ paścimi kāli saddharmavilope /
children.translated_text: and he too shall attain <s>nirvāṇa</s> — thus in the final age, when the true <s>Dharma</s> is disappearing,

children.text: bhikṣu va tīrthamateṣvabhiyuktā te mama dharma pratikṣipi śāntam // SRS_37.71 //
children.translated_text: monks devoted to the doctrines of <s>tīrthikas</s> shall reject my peaceful <s>Dharma</s>.' // SRS_37.71 //

children.text: unnata uddhata duṣṭa pragalbhā pāpasahāyaka bhojanalubdhāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Conceited, proud, corrupt, bold, having evil companions, greedy for food,

children.text: cīvarapātraratāḥ paṭalubdhāḥ lābhasaṃniśrita te kṣipi dharmam // SRS_37.72 //
children.translated_text: delighting in robes and bowls, greedy for cloth, relying on gain — they shall reject the <s>Dharma</s>.' // SRS_37.72 //

children.text: duṣtapraduṣṭamanā akṛtajñā hīnakuleṣu daridrakuleṣu /
children.translated_text: 'Of corrupt and thoroughly corrupt minds, ungrateful, gone forth in my teaching

children.text: pravrajitā iha śāsani mahyaṃ te 'pi pratikṣipi śāntamu dharmam // SRS_37.73 //
children.translated_text: from low families and destitute families — they too shall reject the peaceful <s>Dharma</s>.' // SRS_37.73 //

children.text: (Vaidya 274)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 274)

children.text: māramatena ca mohita sattvā rāgavaśānugatābhiniviṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Beings deluded by <s>Māra</s>'s doctrine, subject to the power of passion, attached,

children.text: mohavaśena tu mohita bālā yeṣa na rocati śūnyata śāntā // SRS_37.74 //
children.translated_text: fools deluded by the power of delusion — for them, peaceful emptiness is not pleasing.' // SRS_37.74 //

children.text: bhikṣu ca bhikṣuṇikā gṛhiṇaśco grāhita mohita pāpamatībhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Monks, nuns, and householders, seized and deluded by those of evil views —

children.text: teṣa vaśānugatā sada bhūtvā paścimi kāli pratikṣipi bodhim // SRS_37.75 //
children.translated_text: having come under their power always, in the final age they shall reject awakening.' // SRS_37.75 //

children.text: śrutva kumāra imā mama vācaṃ bhikṣu araṇyakule vasi nityam /
children.translated_text: 'Having heard these words of mine, O prince — monks who dwell always in forest clans,

children.text: yeṣiya rocati śūnyata śāntā tairayu dhāritu dharmu jinānām // SRS_37.76 //
children.translated_text: those for whom peaceful emptiness is pleasing — by them shall the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Jinas</s> be upheld.' // SRS_37.76 //

children.text: pravraji te mama śāsani caritva bhikṣu upasaṃpadapoṣadhakarmam /
children.translated_text: 'Those who go forth in my teaching, who practice the monk's ordination and <s>poṣadha</s> rites,

children.text: bhuñjimu piṇḍamasaktā aduṣṭā ye imu dhārayiṣyanti samādhim // SRS_37.77 //
children.translated_text: who eat alms-food without attachment, without corruption — they shall uphold this <s>samādhi</s>.' // SRS_37.77 //

children.text: jīvita kāya apekṣi prahāyā śūnyata bhāvayathā supraśāntām /
children.translated_text: 'Having abandoned concern for life and body, cultivate supremely peaceful emptiness;

children.text: yuktaprayuktamanā ca bhavitvā seva araṇya sadā mṛgabhūtāḥ // SRS_37.78 //
children.translated_text: with minds engaged and applied, serve the forest always, like wild deer.' // SRS_37.78 //

children.text: nitya karotha ca pūja jinānāṃ chatradhvajarddhiyamālyavihāraiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Always perform worship of the <s>Jinas</s> with parasols, banners, prosperity, garlands, and monasteries;

children.text: cetiya pūjayathā pratimānāṃ kṣipra labhiṣyatha etu samādhim // SRS_37.79 //
children.translated_text: worship the shrines and images — quickly you shall obtain this <s>samādhi</s>.' // SRS_37.79 //

children.text: stūpa karāpayathā sugatānāṃ hemavibhūṣita rūpiyaliptān /
children.translated_text: 'Have <s>stūpas</s> of the <s>Sugatas</s> built, adorned with gold, anointed with silver;

children.text: pratima suniṣṭhita ratnavicitrā bodhinidhānu janitvana cittam // SRS_37.80 //
children.translated_text: images well-fashioned, variegated with jewels — having generated the mind set upon awakening.' // SRS_37.80 //

children.text: yāvati pūja jagesmi praṇītā divyatha mānuṣikā ramaṇīyā /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever worship in the world is excellent — divine or human, delightful —

children.text: (Vaidya 275)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 275)

children.text: sarva gaveṣiya buddha mahethā bodhinidhānu karitva pratijñām // SRS_37.81 //
children.translated_text: seek all of it for the great <s>Buddhas</s>, having made the vow set upon awakening.' // SRS_37.81 //

children.text: dharmata paśyatha sarvi narendrān yāvata santi daśa diśi loke /
children.translated_text: 'See all Lords of Men through <s>dharmatā</s> — however many there are in the world in the ten directions;

children.text: dṛśyati nirvṛti sarvajinānāṃ dharmatayā sthita saṃmukha buddhāḥ // SRS_37.82 //
children.translated_text: the <s>nirvāṇa</s> of all <s>Jinas</s> is seen [thus] — through <s>dharmatā</s>, the <s>Buddhas</s> stand face-to-face.' // SRS_37.82 //

children.text: bhotha ca sarviṣu tyāgādhimuktāḥ śīlaviśuddhagatā sthiracittāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Be devoted to renunciation in all things, of morality purified, of firm mind,

children.text: kṣāntiratāḥ sada maitraratāśco sarvi prajānatha śūnyaka dharmān // SRS_37.83 //
children.translated_text: always delighting in patience and loving-kindness — know all <s>dharmas</s> as empty.' // SRS_37.83 //

children.text: vīryu janetha alīna adīnāḥ dhyānaratāḥ pravivekaratāśca /
children.translated_text: 'Generate vigor, without laxity or depression; delight in <s>dhyāna</s> and delight in seclusion;

children.text: prajña prajānatha prajñaviśuddhiṃ bheṣyatha kāruṇikā nacireṇa // SRS_37.84 //
children.translated_text: know wisdom through purity of wisdom — you shall become compassionate ones before long.' // SRS_37.84 //

children.text: rāgu śametha sadā aśubhā ye doṣu nigṛhṇatha kṣāntibalena /
children.translated_text: 'Always pacify passion through the impure [contemplations]; restrain hatred by the power of patience;

children.text: mohu nigṛhṇatha prajñabalenā prāpsyatha bodhi jinānu praśastām // SRS_37.85 //
children.translated_text: restrain delusion by the power of wisdom — you shall attain the awakening of the <s>Jinas</s>, which is praised.' // SRS_37.85 //

children.text: kāyu vibhāvayathā yathā phenaṃ duḥkhamasāraku pūtidurgandham /
children.translated_text: 'Contemplate the body as foam — suffering, insubstantial, putrid, foul-smelling;

children.text: skandha prajānatha riktaka sarvāṃllapsyatha jñānamanuttaru kṣipram // SRS_37.86 //
children.translated_text: know all the <s>skandhas</s> as hollow — you shall obtain unsurpassed knowledge quickly.' // SRS_37.86 //

children.text: dṛṣṭi ma gṛhṇatha pāpika jātu ātma ayaṃ puruṣo atha jīvaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Never grasp at evil views — [that there is] a self, a person, or a living being;

children.text: sarvi prajānatha śūnyaka dharmān kṣipra spṛśiṣyatha uttamabodhim // SRS_37.87 //
children.translated_text: know all <s>dharmas</s> as empty — quickly you shall touch the supreme awakening.' // SRS_37.87 //

children.text: lābha ma kurvatha gṛddho kadācit mā paritapyatha piṇḍalamabdhvā /
children.translated_text: 'Never be greedy for gain; do not be distressed at not obtaining alms-food;

children.text: nindita śaṃsita mā khu calethā merusamāśca akampiya bhothā // SRS_37.88 //
children.translated_text: do not waver at blame or praise — be unshakeable like <s>Meru</s>.' // SRS_37.88 //

children.text: (Vaidya 276)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 276)

children.text: dharma gaveṣatha gauravajātāḥ śratva tadāpi ca tatpara bhotha /
children.translated_text: 'Seek the <s>Dharma</s> with reverence; having heard, be devoted to it;

children.text: tiṣṭhata gocari sarvajinānāṃ yāsyatha kṣipra sukhāvatikṣetram // SRS_37.89 //
children.translated_text: stand in the domain of all <s>Jinas</s> — you shall go quickly to the <s>Sukhāvatī</s> field.' // SRS_37.89 //

children.text: sarvajage samacitta bhavitvā apriya mā priya citta karotha /
children.translated_text: 'Having an equal mind toward all the world, do not make the mind [favor] the unpleasant or the pleasant;

children.text: mā na gaveṣatha lābhu yaśo vā kṣipra bhaviṣyatha buddha munīndrāḥ // SRS_37.90 //
children.translated_text: do not seek gain or fame — quickly you shall become <s>Buddhas</s>, lords of sages.' // SRS_37.90 //

children.text: buddhaguṇāṃśca prabhāṣatha nityaṃ bhūtaguṇehi niruktipadehi /
children.translated_text: 'Always proclaim the qualities of <s>Buddhas</s>, with true qualities, in clear expressions;

children.text: yān guṇa śrutviha sattva prasannāḥ buddhaguṇeṣu spṛhāṃ janayeyuḥ // SRS_37.91 //
children.translated_text: those qualities which, having heard, beings become faithful — may they generate aspiration for the qualities of <s>Buddhas</s>.' // SRS_37.91 //

children.text: nitya sagaurava cācariyeṣu mātu pitustatha sarvajagasmin /
children.translated_text: 'Always [be] with reverence toward teachers, toward mother and father, and toward all the world;

children.text: mā puna mānavaśānuga bhothā lapsyatha lakṣaṇa triṃśa duve ca // SRS_37.92 //
children.translated_text: do not be under the power of pride — you shall obtain the thirty-two marks.' // SRS_37.92 //

children.text: saṃgaṇikāṃ vijahitva aśeṣāṃ nityu vivekaratāpi ca bhotha /
children.translated_text: 'Having abandoned group-living entirely, always be ones who delight in seclusion;

children.text: sūrata nityupaśobhana śāntā ātmahitāḥ parasattvahitāśca // SRS_37.93 //
children.translated_text: gentle, always resplendent, peaceful — seeking one's own welfare and the welfare of other beings.' // SRS_37.93 //

children.text: maitri niṣevi tathā karuṇāṃ co muditapekṣaratāḥ sada bhotha /
children.translated_text: 'Cultivate loving-kindness and compassion likewise; always be ones who delight in joy and equanimity;

children.text: śāstuḥ praśāsanu paśyatha nityaṃ bheṣyatha kṣipra hitaṃkaru loke // SRS_37.94 //
children.translated_text: always behold the teaching of the Teacher — you shall quickly become benefactors of the world.' // SRS_37.94 //

children.text: pāpaka mitra ma jātu bhajetha sevatha mitra ye bhonti udārāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Never associate with evil friends; serve friends who are noble —

children.text: yeṣiha rocati śūnyata śāntā ye abhiprasthitā uttamabodhim // SRS_37.95 //
children.translated_text: those for whom peaceful emptiness is pleasing, who have set out for the supreme awakening.' // SRS_37.95 //

children.text: śrāvakabhūmi ma śikṣatha jātu mā ca spṛheṣyatha tatra carīye /
children.translated_text: 'Never train in the <s>Śrāvaka</s> stage; do not aspire to that practice;

children.text: (Vaidya 277)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 277)

children.text: cittu ma riñcatha buddhaguṇeṣu kṣipra bhaviṣyatha buddha jinendrāḥ // SRS_37.96 //
children.translated_text: do not abandon the mind set on <s>Buddha</s>-qualities — quickly you shall become <s>Buddhas</s>, lords of <s>Jinas</s>.' // SRS_37.96 //

children.text: satya giraṃ sada bhāṣatha śuddhāṃ mā mṛṣa bhāṣatha mā paruṣāṃ ca /
children.translated_text: 'Always speak truthful, pure words; do not speak falsely, nor harshly;

children.text: nitya priyaṃ madhuraṃ ca bhaṇethā lapsyatha vāca lokācariyāṇām // SRS_37.97 //
children.translated_text: always speak what is pleasing and sweet — you shall obtain the speech of World-Teachers.' // SRS_37.97 //

children.text: kāyi anarthika jīvita bhothā mātma utkarṣaka mā parapaṃsī /
children.translated_text: 'Be indifferent toward the body and life; do not exalt yourself, do not disparage others;

children.text: ātmaguṇān samudānayamānāḥ paracariyāsu upekṣaka bhotha // SRS_37.98 //
children.translated_text: while accumulating your own good qualities, be equanimous toward the conduct of others.' // SRS_37.98 //

children.text: śūnyavimokṣaratāḥ sada bhothā mā praṇidhāna karotha gatīṣu /
children.translated_text: 'Always be ones who delight in the liberation of emptiness; do not make aspirations [directed] toward [worldly] destinies;

children.text: sarvanimitta vivarjya aśeṣāṃ bhotha sadā animittavihārī // SRS_37.99 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned all signs without remainder, always be ones who dwell in the signless.' // SRS_37.99 //

children.text: anta vivarjayathā sadakālaṃ śāśvatucchedasthitā ma bhavātha /
children.translated_text: 'Always abandon the extremes; do not stand in eternalism or annihilationism;

children.text: pratyayatā sada budhyata sarvaṃ eva bhaviṣyatha yādṛśa śāstā // SRS_37.100 //
children.translated_text: always awaken all [things] through conditionality — thus you shall become like the Teacher.' // SRS_37.100 //

children.text: kāmaratīṣu ratiṃ vijahitvā doṣakhilāṃśca malān vijahitvā /
children.translated_text: 'Having abandoned delight in sensual pleasures, having abandoned the defects, hostilities, and stains,

children.text: mohatamo vijahitvase sarvaṃ śāntaratā narasiṃha bhavātha // SRS_37.101 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned all the darkness of delusion — become ones who delight in peace, O lions among men.' // SRS_37.101 //

children.text: nityamanitya ca paśyatha nityaṃ sarvabhavā sukhaduḥkha vimucya /
children.translated_text: 'Always see the impermanent as impermanent; released from the suffering and happiness of all existences,

children.text: aśubhamanātmata ātmaśubheṣu bhāvayamānu bhaveya naredraḥ // SRS_37.102 //
children.translated_text: contemplating the impure and non-self in what [appears as] self and pure — one would become a lord of men.' // SRS_37.102 //

children.text: lokapradīpakarebhi jinebhiryeṣiha yoniśo dharma sunīta /
children.translated_text: 'By those who have properly guided [themselves in] the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Jinas</s>, the world-illuminators —

children.text: tairiha mārabalāni hanitvā prāptamanuttarabodhirudārā // SRS_37.103 //
children.translated_text: by them, having destroyed <s>Māra</s>'s armies here, the unsurpassed, noble awakening has been attained.' // SRS_37.103 //

children.text: (Vaidya 278)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 278)

children.text: yāttaka bhāṣita eti guṇā me ye ca prakāśita doṣaśatā me /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever qualities of mine have been spoken, and whatever hundreds of faults have been revealed by me —

children.text: doṣa vivarjiya śikṣa guṇeṣu bheṣyasi buddhu tadeha kumāra // SRS_37.104 //
children.translated_text: avoiding faults and training in qualities, you shall become a <s>Buddha</s> here, O prince.' // SRS_37.104 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje yaśaḥprabhaparivartaḥ saptatriṃśatitamaḥ || 37 ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the thirty-seventh chapter of the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, called the <s>Yaśaḥprabha</s> (Splendor of Fame) chapter.

body.text:
(Vaidya 279)
38 Kāyavāṅmanaḥsaṃvaraparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s> 279) Chapter 38: The <s>Kāyavāṅmanaḥsaṃvara</s> (Restraint of Body, Speech, and Mind) chapter.

body.text: tasmāttarhi kumāra kāyasaṃvarasaṃvṛto bhaviṣyāmītyevaṃ tvayā kumāra śikṣitavyam | tatra kumāra katamaḥ kāyasaṃvaraḥ? yena kāyasaṃvareṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvadharmeṣvasaṅgajñānaṃ pratilabhate, ayamucyate kumāra kāyasaṃvara iti | yena kāyasaṃvareṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāni pratilabhate, ayamucyate - - - - - - iti | yena - - - - - - mahāsattvo daśa tathāgatabalāni catvāri vaiśāradyāni aṣṭādaśāveṇikān buddhadharmān pratilabhate, ayamucyate - - - - iti | yena - - - - mahāsattvastrīṇi vimokṣamukhāni pratilabhate | katamāni trīṇi? yaduta śūnyatāmanimittamapraṇihitam | imāni trīṇi vimokṣamukhāni, ayamucyate - - - - iti | yena - - - - mahāsattvaścaturo brāhmān vihārān pratilabhate | katamāṃścaturaḥ ?yaduta maitrīṃ karuṇāṃ muditāmupekṣāṃ imāṃścaturo brāhmān vihārān, ayamucyate - - - - iti | yena - - - - mahāsattvaścatasraḥ pratisaṃvidaḥ pratilabhate | katamāścatasraḥ? yaduta arthapratisaṃvit dharmapratisaṃvit niruktipratisaṃvit pratibhānapratisaṃvit | imāścatasraḥ pratisaṃvidaḥ, ayamucyate - - - - iti | yena mahāsattvaḥ saptatriṃśadbodhipakṣān dharmān pratilabhate | katamān saptatriṃśat?yaduta catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni | catvāri samyakprahāṇāni | catura ṛddhipādān | pañcendriyāṇi | pañca balāni | sapta bodhyaṅgāni | āryāṣṭāṅgakaṃ mārgam | imān saptatriṃśadbodhipakṣān dharmān pratilabhate | ayamucyate - - - - iti | yena - - - - mahāsattvo mahākaruṇāvihāraṃ pratilabhate | mahopekṣāvihāraṃ pratilabhate, kṣemāṃśca vitarkān pratilabhate | pravivekāṃśca dharmān pratilabhate | ayamucyate kāyasaṃvara iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, prince, you should train thus: "I shall be one restrained by bodily restraint." And what, prince, is bodily restraint? That bodily restraint endowed with which a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> obtains unobstructed knowledge regarding all <s>dharmas</s> — this, prince, is called bodily restraint. That bodily restraint endowed with which a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> obtains the thirty-two marks of a great man — this is called [bodily restraint]. That [bodily restraint] endowed with which a <s>Mahāsattva</s> obtains the ten powers of a <s>Tathāgata</s>, the four confidences, and the eighteen unique <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> — this is called [bodily restraint]. That [bodily restraint] endowed with which a <s>Mahāsattva</s> obtains the three gates of liberation — which three? Namely: emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness — these three gates of liberation; this is called [bodily restraint]. That [bodily restraint] endowed with which a <s>Mahāsattva</s> obtains the four <s>Brahmā</s>-abodes — which four? Namely: loving-kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity — these four <s>Brahmā</s>-abodes; this is called [bodily restraint]. That [bodily restraint] endowed with which a <s>Mahāsattva</s> obtains the four analytical knowledges — which four? Namely: analytical knowledge of meaning, analytical knowledge of <s>dharma</s>, analytical knowledge of etymology, and analytical knowledge of eloquence — these four analytical knowledges; this is called [bodily restraint]. That [bodily restraint] endowed with which a <s>Mahāsattva</s> obtains the thirty-seven factors of awakening — which thirty-seven? Namely: the four establishments of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of supernatural power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the noble eightfold path — these thirty-seven factors of awakening [he obtains]; this is called [bodily restraint]. That [bodily restraint] endowed with which a <s>Mahāsattva</s> obtains the abode of great compassion, obtains the abode of great equanimity, obtains beneficial thoughts, and obtains <s>dharmas</s> of seclusion — this is called bodily restraint.'

body.text: punaraparaṃ kumāra yena kāyasaṃvareṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prāṇātipātāt prativirato bhavati | adattādānāt abrahmacaryānmṛṣāvādāt piśunavacanāt paruṣavacanāt saṃbhinnapralāpāt abhidhyāyādū vyāpādanmithyādṛṣṭeḥ prativirato bhavati | tulākūṭānmānakūṭātkāṃsyakūṭāt karṣaṇabandhanarodhanatāḍanacchedanabhedanaviparāmoṣālokasāhasebhyaḥ prativarato bhavati | na hastalolaḥ na pādalolo hastapādasaṃyataḥ| tasya sarvaṃ kāyavāṅbhanodauṣṭhulyaṃ prahīṇaṃ bhavatyucchinnamūlaṃ tālāmastakavadāyatyāmanutpādadharmi | ayamucyate kumāra kāyasaṃvara iti | tadanenāpi te kumāra paryāyeṇaivaṃ veditavyam ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, prince, that bodily restraint endowed with which a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> abstains from taking life, from taking what is not given, from unchastity, from false speech, from divisive speech, from harsh speech, from idle chatter, from covetousness, from ill-will, and from wrong views; [endowed with which] he abstains from fraud in weighing, fraud in measuring, fraud in alloys, from seizing, binding, imprisoning, striking, cutting, piercing, and robbery by force; [endowed with which] he is not restless with hands, not restless with feet, restrained in hands and feet — all his bodily and vocal offensiveness has been abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm-tree stump, so that it does not arise in the future, its nature being non-production — this, prince, is called bodily restraint. By this method too, prince, it should be understood thus.

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ kumāra atīte 'dhvanyasaṃkhyeye kalpe asaṃkhyeyatare vipule apramāṇe acintye aparimāṇe yadāsīt | tena kālena tena samayena jñānaprabhāso nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka (Vaidya 280) udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān | tena khalu punaḥ kumāra kālena tena samayena tasya bhagavato jñānaprabhāsasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya ṣaṣṭivarṣakoṭyaḥ āyuṣpramāṇamabhūt | ṣaṣṭirarhatkoṭyaḥ śrāvakasaṃgho 'bhūt | aprameyāśca bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ saddharmaparigrāhakā abhūvan ||
body.translated_text: In the past, prince, in a bygone era, in an incalculable, even more incalculable, vast, immeasurable, inconceivable, illimitable <s>kalpa</s>, there arose in the world a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Jñānaprabhāsa</s> (<s>Vaidya</s> 280) — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, a knower of the world, unsurpassed, a tamer of men to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. At that time, prince, the lifespan of that Blessed <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jñānaprabhāsa</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, was sixty <s>koṭis</s> of years. His <s>Śrāvaka</s> <s>Saṃgha</s> comprised sixty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Arhats</s>. And there were immeasurable <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> who were upholders of the true <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: tena ca kumāra kālena tena samayena rājābhūdviśeṣacintī nāma | atha khalu rājā viśeṣacintī aśītyā prāṇikoṭibhiḥ sārdhaṃ tathāgatamupasaṃkrāntaḥ| upsaṃkramya tasya tathāgatasya pādau śirasābhivandya bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtyaikānte nyaṣīdat | ekāntaniṣaṇṇaśca rājā viśeṣacintī taṃ tathāgataṃ paryupāste | atha khalu kumāra jñānaprabhāsastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho rājño viśeṣacintinaḥ saparivārasyādhyāśayaṃ viditvā ito dharmaparyāyādimaṃ kāyasaṃvarasamādhimukhapraveśaṃ gāthābhigītena deśayati -
body.translated_text: Now, O prince, at that time, at that occasion, there was a king named <s>Viśeṣacintī</s> (Distinguished Thought). Then King <s>Viśeṣacintī</s>, together with eighty <s>koṭis</s> of beings, approached the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Having approached, having venerated the feet of that <s>Tathāgata</s> with his head, having circumambulated the Blessed One three times, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, King <s>Viśeṣacintī</s> attended upon that <s>Tathāgata</s>. Then, O prince, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jñānaprabhāsa</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Fully Awakened One, knowing the disposition of King <s>Viśeṣacintī</s> together with his retinue, taught from this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse the entry into the <s>samādhi</s>-gate of <s>kāyasaṃvara</s> (bodily restraint), in verses:

children.text: yathāntarīkṣaṃ gaganaṃ viśuddhamatyantaśuddhaṃ prakṛtiprabhāsvaram /
children.translated_text: 'Just as the sky, the firmament, is pure — utterly pure, luminous by nature —

children.text: emeva śuddho ayu kāyasaṃvaro na śakyu ghoṣeṇa kadāci deśitum // SRS_38.1 //
children.translated_text: even so is this <s>kāyasaṃvara</s> (bodily restraint) pure; it can never be taught by sound. // SRS_38.1 //

children.text: viviktu śūnyo ayu kāyasaṃvaro etādṛśe te ubhi kāyalakṣaṇe /
children.translated_text: Secluded and empty is this <s>kāyasaṃvara</s>; such are the two marks of the body —

children.text: alakṣaṇāste yatha antarīkṣaṃ tallakṣaṇo deśitu kāyasaṃvaraḥ // SRS_38.2 //
children.translated_text: they are markless, like the sky; with such marks is <s>kāyasaṃvara</s> taught. // SRS_38.2 //

children.text: yo jānatī saṃvaramevalakṣaṇaṃ na tasya jātu bhavatī nasaṃvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: One who knows this restraint as markless — for him, non-restraint never occurs;

children.text: ye cāpravṛttāḥ kṛtu teṣa gocaro anāsravasyo upapatti nāsti // SRS_38.3 //
children.translated_text: and those who are non-active — their domain is made; there is no rebirth for one free from outflows. // SRS_38.3 //

children.text: na śakyu kāmān pratisevamānai rūpeṣu bhogeṣu jahitva tṛṣṇām /
children.translated_text: For those who indulge in sensual pleasures, who have not abandoned craving for forms and enjoyments,

children.text: bhaveṣu doṣānavijānamānairna śakyu jñātumayu kāyasaṃvaraḥ // SRS_38.4 //
children.translated_text: who do not understand the faults in [states of] existence — this <s>kāyasaṃvara</s> cannot be known. // SRS_38.4 //

children.text: anāsravaṃ saṃvaru yaḥ prajānate na tasya bhotī upapatti jātu /
children.translated_text: One who understands restraint as free from outflows — for him rebirth never occurs;

children.text: arhantadharmā ima evarūpāḥ na sukaraṃ jānitu tīrthikebhiḥ // SRS_38.5 //
children.translated_text: such are the qualities of an <s>Arhat</s> — they are not easy to know by <s>tīrthikas</s>. // SRS_38.5 //

children.text: (Vaidya 281)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 281)

children.text: ye sarvatraidhātuki trastamānasā na kāmabhogeṣu spṛhāṃ janenti /
children.translated_text: Those whose minds are alarmed regarding the entire triple world, who do not generate desire for sensual enjoyments,

children.text: rājyena bhogaiśca na jātu arthikā jñāsyanti te īdṛśa kāyasaṃvaraḥ // SRS_38.6 //
children.translated_text: who are never interested in kingship or possessions — they shall know such <s>kāyasaṃvara</s>. // SRS_38.6 //

children.text: artho ayaṃ vuccati kāyasaṃvaro arthaśca śabdena na śakyu deśitum /
children.translated_text: This meaning is called <s>kāyasaṃvara</s>; and the meaning cannot be taught by words;

children.text: yo jānatī īdṛśu dharmanetrīṃ sa saṃvare 'smin bhavati pratiṣṭhitaḥ // SRS_38.7 //
children.translated_text: one who knows such a guide to <s>Dharma</s> — he is established in this restraint. // SRS_38.7 //

children.text: arthe prayuktāna mayārthu deśito ye arthanetrīparatā vicakṣaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: To those devoted to meaning, meaning has been taught by me; those who are wise, devoted to the guide of meaning,

children.text: anarthu varjenti ya arthayuktā te saṃvare 'smin satataṃ pratiṣṭhitāḥ // SRS_38.8 //
children.translated_text: who avoid what is not meaning while devoted to meaning — they are constantly established in this restraint. // SRS_38.8 //

children.text: artho ya ukto hi jināna śāsane kathaṃ sa artho bhavatī vijānato /
children.translated_text: The meaning that has been spoken in the teaching of the Conquerors — how does that meaning become [known] to one who understands?

children.text: yo arthanetrīya svabhāvu jānati pratiṣṭhitaḥ socyati kāyasaṃvare // SRS_38.9 //
children.translated_text: One who knows the own-nature of the guide to meaning — he is said to be established in <s>kāyasaṃvara</s>. // SRS_38.9 //

children.text: yenānimittaṃ bhavatī vijānitaṃ nairātmyataḥ śūnyatu tucchato vā /
children.translated_text: By whom the signless has been understood — through selflessness, emptiness, or voidness —

children.text: na tasya jātū bhavati nasaṃvarastathāhi so śikṣitu bhūtaniścaye // SRS_38.10 //
children.translated_text: for him non-restraint never occurs; thus he is trained in the ascertainment of reality. // SRS_38.10 //

body.text:
bhāvānabhāvāniti yaḥ prajānati sa sarvabhāveṣu na jātu sajjate /
yaḥ sarvabhāveṣu na jātu sajjate | sa ānimittaṃ spṛśatī samādhim // SRS_38.11 //
body.translated_text: One who understands existence and non-existence is never attached to any state of being; one who is never attached to any state of being — he touches the signless <s>samādhi</s>. // SRS_38.11 //

children.text: vijñāta yeneha nirātmadharmāḥ svabhāvaśūnyāḥ prakṛtiprabhāsvarāḥ /
children.translated_text: By whom selfless <s>dharmas</s> have been understood here — empty of own-nature, luminous by nature —

children.text: na tasya jātu bhavatī asaṃvarastathāhi so śikṣitu bhūtaniścaye // SRS_38.12 //
children.translated_text: for him non-restraint never occurs; thus he is trained in the ascertainment of reality. // SRS_38.12 //

children.text: yo jānatī śūnyata pañcaskandhān viditva nairātmasvabhāvaśūnyān /
children.translated_text: One who knows the five <s>skandhas</s> as empty, having understood them as empty of own-nature and selfless —

children.text: (Vaidya 282)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 282)

children.text: na tasya jātu bhavatī asaṃvaro yat karma kāyena samācareta // SRS_38.13 //
children.translated_text: for him non-restraint never occurs regarding whatever action he performs with the body. // SRS_38.13 //

children.text: nimittagrāhisya asaṃvṛtasya ya ātmasaṃjñāya sadā pratiṣṭhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: For one who grasps at signs, who is unrestrained, who is always established in the perception of self,

children.text: rūpeṣu āsvādagatasya jantunaḥ prakupyate rāga asaṃvṛtasya // SRS_38.14 //
children.translated_text: for that being who has resorted to relishing forms — passion arises in the unrestrained one. // SRS_38.14 //

children.text: ye bhūtakoṭīya bhavanti śikṣitā gatiṃgatāḥ sūrata śūnyatāyām /
children.translated_text: Those who are trained in the limit of reality, who have reached the course of emptiness, heroic —

children.text: na teṣa rāgaḥ puna jātu kupyate asaṃvaro yena vrajeta durgatim // SRS_38.15 //
children.translated_text: for them passion never arises again, the non-restraint by which one goes to lower rebirths. // SRS_38.15 //

children.text: na śakyu kampetu yathā sumeru acāliyaḥ sarvapipīlikairmahān /
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Sumeru</s> cannot be shaken — immovable, great — by all the ants,

children.text: tathā vidū bhūtanayeṣu śikṣito rūpehi divyairapi so na kampate // SRS_38.16 //
children.translated_text: so too the wise one trained in the way of reality is not shaken even by divine forms. // SRS_38.16 //

children.text: śakyeta raṅgairgaganaṃ vicitrituṃ śakyeta cākāśa gṛhītu pāṇinā /
children.translated_text: One might paint the sky with colors; one might seize space with one's hand —

children.text: na tveva śakyaṃ sa vicālanāya rāgeṇa doṣeṇa na ca mārakoṭibhiḥ // SRS_38.17 //
children.translated_text: but one cannot shake him — neither by passion, nor hatred, nor by <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Māras</s>. // SRS_38.17 //

children.text: pratiśrukā śakyu gṛhītu kenacicchilā plavedapyudakasya madhye /
children.translated_text: An echo might be seized by someone; a rock might float in the middle of water —

children.text: draṣṭuṃ na śakyaṃ tviha tasya āśayā yaḥ śikṣito īdṛśi kāyasaṃvare // SRS_38.18 //
children.translated_text: but the intention of one trained in such <s>kāyasaṃvara</s> cannot be seen. // SRS_38.18 //

children.text: yāvanta śabdāḥ pṛthu sarvaloke gṛhṇitva peḍāgata śakya kartum /
children.translated_text: However many sounds there are widely in the entire world — one might seize them and put them in a box —

children.text: na tasya śakyaṃ sthitirasthitirvā vijānituṃ yaḥ sthitu kāyasaṃvare // SRS_38.19 //
children.translated_text: but the stability or instability of one established in <s>kāyasaṃvara</s> cannot be known. // SRS_38.19 //

children.text: śakyaṃ prabhā gṛhṇitu sūryamaṇḍalāt pragarjato meghatu vidyuto vā /
children.translated_text: One might seize the radiance from the disc of the sun, from the rumbling cloud, or from lightning —

children.text: na tasya kāyasya svabhāva jñātuṃ yaḥ śikṣitaḥ syādiha kāyasaṃvare // SRS_38.20 //
children.translated_text: but the own-nature of the body of one trained in <s>kāyasaṃvara</s> here cannot be known. // SRS_38.20 //

children.text: jālena pāśena ca śakyu bandhituṃ caturdiśaṃ vāyati vātamaṇḍalī /
children.translated_text: With a net or a snare one might bind the circle of wind blowing in the four directions —

children.text: (Vaidya 283)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 283)

children.text: na śakyamājānitu tasya kāyaḥ pratiṣṭhito yo iha kāyasaṃvare // SRS_38.21 //
children.translated_text: but the body of one established in <s>kāyasaṃvara</s> here cannot be known. // SRS_38.21 //

children.text: agocaro 'sāviha sarvaprāṇināṃ yatra sthito yo vidu cittasaṃyame /
children.translated_text: This is beyond the domain of all beings — where the wise one stands, established in mind-restraint;

children.text: yatra sthito gocari kāyasaṃvare na lipyate khamiva sa lokadharmaiḥ // SRS_38.22 //
children.translated_text: where he stands in the domain of <s>kāyasaṃvara</s>, he is not stained by worldly conditions, like the sky. // SRS_38.22 //

children.text: śakyaṃ padaṃ paśyitu sarvaprāṇināṃ name carantāna pṛthak caturdiśam /
children.translated_text: One might see the tracks of all beings, of fish swimming separately in the four directions —

children.text: na tasya kāyasya na cittagocaro pramāṇu jñātumiha śakya kenacit // SRS_38.23 //
children.translated_text: but the measure of his body and his mind's domain cannot be known by anyone here. // SRS_38.23 //

children.text: evaṃ sthitasyo iha kāyasaṃvare sarve na bhonti vividhāḥ kileśāḥ /
children.translated_text: For one thus established in <s>kāyasaṃvara</s>, the various defilements do not exist;

children.text: prahīṇa tasyeha upakileśāstathā hyasau śikṣitu kāyasaṃvare // SRS_38.24 //
children.translated_text: the secondary defilements are abandoned for him — thus he is trained in <s>kāyasaṃvara</s>. // SRS_38.24 //

children.text: na tasya agniḥ kramate na śastraṃ tathāpi agrāhyu sa tasya kāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Neither fire nor weapons approach him; that body of his is ungraspable;

children.text: śantapraśānte sthitu so samādhau tathā hyasau śikṣitu kāyasaṃvare // SRS_38.25 //
children.translated_text: he stands in calm, tranquil <s>samādhi</s> — thus he is trained in <s>kāyasaṃvara</s>. // SRS_38.25 //

children.text: evaṃ sthitasyo na bhayaṃ na trāso na kṣobhu cittasyu na cerṣyu jāyate /
children.translated_text: For one thus established, there is no fear, no terror, no agitation of mind, and no jealousy arises;

children.text: muktaḥ sa sarvebhirupadravebhiryaḥ śikṣito tādṛśa kāyasaṃvare // SRS_38.26 //
children.translated_text: he is freed from all misfortunes — one who is trained in such <s>kāyasaṃvara</s>. // SRS_38.26 //

children.text: viṣasya śastrasya na jātu bhāyati na cāgnimadhye na jalasya madhye /
children.translated_text: He never fears poison or weapons, nor in the midst of fire, nor in the midst of water;

children.text: sarvehi muktaḥ sa upadravehi ya śikṣito īdṛśa kāyasaṃvare // SRS_38.27 //
children.translated_text: he is freed from all misfortunes — one trained in such <s>kāyasaṃvara</s>. // SRS_38.27 //

children.text: caurāṇa dhūrtāna ca pāpakāriṇāmāśīviṣāmadhyagato na bhāyate /
children.translated_text: In the midst of thieves, rogues, and evildoers, among poisonous serpents, he does not fear;

children.text: tathā hi tasyo vigatātmasaṃjñā saṃjñāvimuktasya bhayaṃ na bhoti // SRS_38.28 //
children.translated_text: for the perception of self has departed from him — for one freed from perception, there is no fear. // SRS_38.28 //

children.text: bhayairvimuktasya na trāsu jāyate asaṃtrasantasya na bhoti iñjanā /
children.translated_text: For one freed from fears, no terror arises; for one unalarmed, there is no disturbance;

children.text: (Vaidya 284)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 284)

children.text: aniñjamānasya kuto 'sti trāso na mārakoṭībhi sa śakyu kampitum // SRS_38.29 //
children.translated_text: for one undisturbed, how can there be terror? He cannot be shaken by <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Māras</s>. // SRS_38.29 //

children.text: ācakṣito deśitu saṃprakāśito yo bodhisattvasya hitāya saṃvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: This restraint has been declared, taught, and illuminated for the benefit of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>;

children.text: yaḥ śikṣate īdṛśa kāyasaṃvare so bhoti no kampiyu mārakoṭibhiḥ // SRS_38.30 //
children.translated_text: one who trains in such <s>kāyasaṃvara</s> — he shall not be shaken by <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Māras</s>. // SRS_38.30 //

children.text: sarveṣu dharmeṣu asaṃjñajñānaṃ pūrṇā aśītiranuvyañjanāni /
children.translated_text: Knowledge without perception regarding all <s>dharmas</s>; the eighty minor marks are complete;

children.text: dvātriṃśa co lakṣaṇa cittaśuddhā na durlabhā bhonti sthitasya saṃvare // SRS_38.31 //
children.translated_text: the thirty-two marks and purity of mind — these are not hard to obtain for one established in restraint. // SRS_38.31 //

children.text: ya icchate budhyitu buddhadharmān acintiyān yeṣa pramāṇu nāsti /
children.translated_text: One who wishes to awaken to the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> — inconceivable, of which no measure exists —

children.text: sa śikṣitu īdṛśuḥ kāyasaṃvare bhaviṣyate cetiyu sarvaloke // SRS_38.32 //
children.translated_text: he should train in such <s>kāyasaṃvara</s>; he will become a reliquary (<s>caitya</s>) for the entire world. // SRS_38.32 //

children.text: ya icchate dharmamimaṃ maharṣiṇāṃ daśo balān buddhabalānacintiyān /
children.translated_text: One who wishes [to attain] this <s>Dharma</s> of the great sages — the ten powers, the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-powers —

children.text: sa śikṣitu īdṛśa kāyasaṃvare yaḥ śikṣitastasya balā na durlabhāḥ // SRS_38.33 //
children.translated_text: he should train in such <s>kāyasaṃvara</s>; for one thus trained, the powers are not hard to obtain. // SRS_38.33 //

children.text: ye cāpi aṣṭādaśa buddhadharmā āveṇikā yeṣu jinā pratiṣṭhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: And the eighteen exclusive <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> in which the Conquerors are established —

children.text: te cāpi tasyo na bhavanti durlabhā yaḥ śikṣate īdṛśa kāyasaṃvare // SRS_38.34 //
children.translated_text: those too are not hard to obtain for one who trains in such <s>kāyasaṃvara</s>. // SRS_38.34 //

children.text: ye sapta bodhyaṅga mahāmaharṣiṇāṃ pratisaṃvidaśco tatha ṛddhipādāḥ /
children.translated_text: The seven factors of awakening of the great sages, the analytical knowledges, and the bases of miraculous power —

children.text: te cāpi tasyo na bhavanti durlabhā yaḥ śikṣate īdṛśa kāyasaṃvare // SRS_38.35 //
children.translated_text: those too are not hard to obtain for one who trains in such <s>kāyasaṃvara</s>. // SRS_38.35 //

children.text: brahmāvihārāścaturaśca dhyānā vimokṣadvārāstraya saṃprakāśitāḥ /
children.translated_text: The four <s>Brahmā</s>-dwellings and four <s>dhyānas</s>, the three gates of liberation have been proclaimed;

children.text: kṣemā vitarkā atha prāvivekyā na durlabhā bhonti sthitasya saṃvare // SRS_38.36 //
children.translated_text: secure deliberations and solitary [thoughts] — these are not hard to obtain for one established in restraint. // SRS_38.36 //

children.text: karuṇāvihārī tathupekṣalābhī tatha īryacaryāmiha maitrivarām /
children.translated_text: Dwelling in compassion, and likewise obtaining equanimity, and here the supreme conduct of loving-kindness,

children.text: (Vaidya 285)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 285)

children.text: hitacittu bhoti ca sa sarvajage yaḥ kāyasaṃvari sthito bhavati // SRS_38.37 //
children.translated_text: his mind is benevolent toward the entire world — for one established in <s>kāyasaṃvara</s>. // SRS_38.37 //

children.text: smṛtī upasthāna prahāṇa samyak pañcendriyāḥ pañca balā maharṣiṇām /
children.translated_text: The foundations of mindfulness, right efforts, the five faculties, the five powers of the great sages,

children.text: āścarya aṣṭāṅgiku mārgaśreṣṭho na durlabho śikṣitu kāyasaṃvare // SRS_38.38 //
children.translated_text: the wondrous, supreme eightfold path — these are not hard to obtain for one trained in <s>kāyasaṃvara</s>. // SRS_38.38 //

children.text: ye cāpi anye vara buddhadharmā acintiyā yeṣa pramāṇu nāsti /
children.translated_text: And whatever other supreme <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> there are — inconceivable, of which no measure exists —

children.text: te tasya sarve na bhavanti durlabhā yaḥ śikṣate īdṛśa kāyasaṃvare // SRS_38.39 //
children.translated_text: all of those are not hard to obtain for one who trains in such <s>kāyasaṃvara</s>. // SRS_38.39 //

children.text: śrutvā iho īdṛśa kāyasaṃvare viśeṣaprāpto abhu rājaputraḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard such [teaching on] <s>kāyasaṃvara</s> here, the prince attained distinction;

children.text: tuṣṭo udagro atulāya prītiyā sa pravrajī tasya jinasya śāsane // SRS_38.40 //
children.translated_text: delighted, elated, with incomparable joy, he went forth in the teaching of that Conqueror. // SRS_38.40 //

children.text: sa pravrajitvā daśa varṣakoṭīracārṣi śuddhaṃ vara brahmacaryam /
children.translated_text: Having gone forth, for ten <s>koṭis</s> of years he practiced the pure, supreme holy life,

children.text: bhāvetva brāhmān caturo vihārānarthāya lokasya sadevakasya // SRS_38.41 //
children.translated_text: having cultivated the four <s>Brahmā</s>-dwellings for the benefit of the world with its gods. // SRS_38.41 //

children.text: subhāvitā brahmavihāra kṛtvā adrākṣi buddhāna aśītikoṭiyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having well-cultivated the <s>Brahmā</s>-dwellings, he beheld eighty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>;

children.text: tatottare yāttika gaṅgavālikā idaṃ caraṃ so vara brahmacaryam // SRS_38.42 //
children.translated_text: and beyond those, as many as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> — while practicing this supreme holy life. // SRS_38.42 //

children.text: sarveṣa co śāsani pravrajitvā acārṣi śuddhaṃ vara brahmacaryam /
children.translated_text: Having gone forth in the teaching of all of them, he practiced the pure, supreme holy life;

children.text: bhikṣu abhūṣī vara dharmabhāṇako bahuśrutaśco pratibhānavāṃśca // SRS_38.43 //
children.translated_text: he became a monk, a supreme <s>Dharma</s>-preacher, of great learning and endowed with eloquence. // SRS_38.43 //

body.text:
akhaṇḍaśīlaśca acchidraśīlo viśuddhaśīlo akalmāṣaśīlaḥ /
ārye ca śīle sa anāsrave sthitaḥ | prajānamāno imu kāyasaṃvaram // SRS_38.44 //
body.translated_text: Of unbroken morality, unfissured morality, purified morality, unmottled morality, established in noble morality free from outflows — knowing this <s>kāyasaṃvara</s>. // SRS_38.44 //

children.text: (Vaidya 286)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 286)

children.text: siyā kumārā tava anya sāsīd viśeṣacintī tada rājakuñjaraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Perhaps, O prince, you might think that <s>Viśeṣacintī</s>, that bull among kings, was someone else —

children.text: na eva draṣṭavyamihānyu so 'bhūttadāhamāsaṃ caramāṇu cārikām // SRS_38.45 //
children.translated_text: it should not be seen thus; it was I, at that time wandering on my journey. // SRS_38.45 //

children.text: tasmāt kumārā mama śikṣamāṇā pratiṣṭhihesī iha kāyasaṃvare /
children.translated_text: Therefore, O prince, training under me, become established in this <s>kāyasaṃvara</s>;

children.text: anyeṣa co deśaya prāṇakoṭināṃ nacireṇa tvaṃ bheṣyasi yādṛśo 'ham // SRS_38.46 //
children.translated_text: and teach it to <s>koṭis</s> of other beings too — before long you shall become such as I am. // SRS_38.46 //
