body.text: tasmāttarhi kumāra pariśuddhakāyasamācāro bhaviṣyāmītyevaṃ tvayā kumāra śikṣitavyam | tat kasya hetoḥ? pariśuddhakāyasamācāro hi kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na nirayebhyo bibheti | na tiryagyonerna yamalokānna sarvadurgatibhyo bibheti | nodakād bibheti | na śastrato na siṃhebhyo na vyāghrebhyo na ṛkṣebhyo na hastibhyo narṣabhebhyo na manuṣyebhyo bibheti | pariśuddhakāyasamācāraḥ kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ imamapi trisāhasraṃ mahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātuṃ karatale kṛtvā tālamātraṃ dvitālamātraṃ tritālamātraṃ catustālamātraṃ pañcatālamātraṃ ṣaṭtālamātraṃ saptatālamātramutkṣipet | yāvantaṃ vā punarākāṅkṣettāvantamevotkṣipet ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, O prince, you should train thus: "I shall be one of purified bodily conduct." For what reason? Because, O prince, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> of purified bodily conduct does not fear the hells; does not fear the animal realm, the world of <s>Yama</s>, or any lower realm; does not fear water, nor weapons, nor lions, nor tigers, nor bears, nor elephants, nor bulls, nor humans. A <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> of purified bodily conduct, O prince, can take this trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātu</s>) in the palm of his hand and toss it up one palm-tree height, two palm-tree heights, three, four, five, six, or seven palm-tree heights; and for however long he wishes, he can toss it up just so far.

body.text: punaraparaṃ pariśuddhakāyasamācāraḥ kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattva ṛddhiprātihārye paramapāramiprāpto bhavati | sa ṛddhipādavipākaviśuddhaḥ puṇyaparigṛhīto vivekaviviktaḥ sarvatrānugata etatsamādhipratilabdhaḥ anāsravapuṇyapariniṣpannaḥ sarvalokadhātāvapratihatacakṣuḥ evaṃrūpaiḥ ṛddhipratihāryaiḥ samanvāgato bhavati | tatra katamā ṛddhiḥ? yayā ṛddhayā prārthanāsamṛddhipariniṣpattiḥ | iyamucyate ṛddhiriti | tatra katamad ṛddhiprātihāryam? yayā ṛddhayā samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattva anekavidhānṛddhiviṣayān pratyunubhavati | eko 'pi bhūtvā bahudhā bhavati, bahudhāpi bhūtvaiko bhavati | avirbhāvaṃ tirobhāvamapi pratyanubhavati | tiraḥkuḍyaṃ tiraḥprākāraḥ tiraḥparvatamapyasajjamāno gacchati | ākāśe 'pi kramate tadyathāpi nāma pakṣī śakuniḥ | pṛthivyāmapyunmajjananimajjanaṃ karoti tadyathāpi nāmodake | udake 'pyabhidyamāno gacchati tadyathāpi nāma pṛthivyām | dhūmāyatyapi prajvalatyapi tadyathāpi nāma mahānagniskandhaḥ | imāvapi candrasūryāvevaṃmaharddhikāvevaṃmahānubhāvau evaṃmahaujaskau pāṇinā parāmṛśati parimārjati | ākāṅkṣamāṇo yāvad brahmalokādapi sattvān kāyena vaśe vartayati ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O Prince, the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> of purified bodily conduct attains the supreme perfection in the miracle of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhiprātihārya</s>). Purified through the fruition of the bases of supernatural power, supported by merit, secluded in solitude, pervading everywhere, having attained this <s>samādhi</s>, perfected in merit free from <s>āsravas</s>, with unobstructed vision throughout all world-realms — he is endowed with such supernatural miracles. And what is supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>)? That supernatural power by which [there is] the fulfillment of aspirations and accomplishments — this is called supernatural power. And what is the miracle of supernatural power? That supernatural power endowed with which a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> experiences many kinds of supernatural domains: having been one, he becomes many; having been many, he becomes one. He experiences appearing and disappearing. He passes unimpeded through walls, through ramparts, through mountains. He walks through the sky, just like a winged bird. He dives in and out of the earth, just as in water. He passes through water without breaking it, just as on earth. He smokes and blazes, just like a great mass of fire. He touches and strokes with his hand even these sun and moon — so mighty, so powerful, so majestic. If he wishes, he exercises mastery over beings with his body even up to the <s>Brahma</s>-world.

body.text:
(Vaidya 287)
atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 287) Then at that time, the Blessed One spoke these verses:

children.text: pṛthivīya unmajja nimajja gacchatī abhidyamāno udake 'pi gacchati /
children.translated_text: He dives in and out of the earth, passes through water without breaking it;

children.text: pakṣī yathā gaganatalena gacchatī dhūmāyate prajvalate ca ṛddhiyā // SRS_38.47 //
children.translated_text: like a bird, he goes through the vault of the sky — he smokes and blazes through supernatural power. // SRS_38.47 //

children.text: yathāntarīkṣasmi na vāyu sajjate gacchanti cāsmiṃ bahavo 'bhrakūṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as wind is unattached in the atmosphere, yet many cloud-masses move through it,

children.text: tathaiva yogī gaganena gacchatī asajjamāno yatha vātameghaḥ // SRS_38.48 //
children.translated_text: even so the <s>yogin</s> goes through the sky, unattached like the wind and clouds. // SRS_38.48 //

children.text: yathā niṣaṇṇo vidu yogi bhotī parimārjate pāṇina candrasūryau /
children.translated_text: Just as a wise <s>yogin</s>, seated [in meditation], strokes the sun and moon with his hand —

children.text: āsanna so jānati brahmalokaṃ brahmāṇa koṭīna sa dharma deśayī // SRS_38.49 //
children.translated_text: he knows the <s>Brahma</s>-world as near, and teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Brahmās</s>. // SRS_38.49 //

children.text: yadā ca ākāṅkṣati dharma bhāṣituṃ mahātrisāhasra sa vijñapeti /
children.translated_text: And when he wishes to speak the <s>Dharma</s>, he makes the great trichiliocosm aware;

children.text: ākāṅkṣamāṇo bahukṣetrakoṭiṣu deśeti dharma bahusattvakoṭinām // SRS_38.50 //
children.translated_text: when he wishes, in many <s>koṭīs</s> of fields, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to many <s>koṭīs</s> of beings. // SRS_38.50 //

body.text: tasmāttarhi kumāra pariśuddhakāyasamudācāro bhaviṣyāmītyevaṃ tvayā kumāra śikṣitavyam | tat kasya hetoḥ? pariśuddhakāyasamudācāro hi kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvo divyena śrotradhātunā atikrāntamānuṣakeṇa śabdān śṛṇoti divyān mānuṣyakāṃśca | nairayikānāmapi tiryagyonigatānāmapi yāmalaukikānāmapi | ye dūre antike vā devānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ vā dūrāvacarāṇāṃ vā antikāvacarāṇāṃ vā ||
body.translated_text: "Therefore, O Prince, you should train thus: 'I shall be one of purified bodily conduct.' For what reason? Because, O Prince, a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> of purified bodily conduct hears sounds with the divine ear-element, surpassing the human — both divine and human sounds, as well as those of hell-beings, those reborn in the animal realm, and those of <s>Yama</s>'s world — whether far or near, of gods or humans, whether ranging far or ranging near."

body.text: tasmāttarhi kumāra pariśuddhakāyasamudācāro bhaviṣyāmītyevaṃ tvayā kumāra śikṣitavyam | tat kasya hetoḥ? pariśuddhakāyasamudācāro hi kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ parasattvānāṃ parapudgalānāṃ cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkacaritāni yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti | sarāgaṃ cittaṃ sarāgaṃ cittamiti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti | vītarāgaṃ cittaṃ vītarāgaṃ cittamiti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti | peyālaṃ | sadoṣaṃ (Vaidya 288) vītadoṣaṃ samohaṃ vītamohaṃ sopādānamanupādānaṃ saṃkṣiptaṃ vikṣiptaṃ viparītamaviparītaṃ sakleśaṃ niṣkleśaṃ mahadgatamamahadgataṃ prabhāsvaramaprabhāsvaraṃ sapramāṇamapramāṇaṃ sottaramanuttaraṃ samāhitamasamāhitaṃ vimuktamavimuktaṃ - - - - sāṅgaṇaṃ cittaṃ sāṅgaṇaṃ cittamiti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti | anaṅgaṇaṃ cittamanaṅgaṇaṃ cittamiti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti | iti hi sarvasattvānāṃ parapudgalānāṃ cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti ||
body.translated_text: "Therefore, O Prince, you should train thus: 'I shall be one of purified bodily conduct.' For what reason? Because, O Prince, a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> of purified bodily conduct knows as they truly are, with his own mind, the mental deliberations and conduct of other beings and other persons. He knows as it truly is: 'A mind with passion is a mind with passion.' He knows as it truly is: 'A mind free from passion is a mind free from passion.' [Abbreviation.] With hatred, (Vaidya 288) free from hatred; with delusion, free from delusion; with clinging, without clinging; contracted, distracted; perverted, unperverted; defiled, undefiled; lofty, not lofty; luminous, not luminous; limited, unlimited; surpassed, unsurpassed; concentrated, unconcentrated; liberated, unliberated — — — — he knows as it truly is: 'A mind with blemish is a mind with blemish.' He knows as it truly is: 'A mind without blemish is a mind without blemish.' Thus he knows as they truly are, with his own mind, the mental deliberations of all beings and other persons."

body.text: pariśuddhakāyasamudācāraḥ kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sākāraṃ soddeśamanekavidhaṃ pūrvenivāsamanusmarati | ekāmapi jātimanusmarati | dve tisraḥ pañca daśa viṃśatiḥ triṃśat catvāriṃśat pañcāśat jātiaśatamapyanusmarati | jātisahasrapyanusmarati | jātiśatasahasramapi yāvadanekānyapi kalpakoṭinayutaśatasahasrāṇyanusmarati | saṃvartakalpamapyanusmarati vivartakalpamapi | yāvadanekānapi saṃvartavivartakalpānanusmarati | kalpamapyanusmarati kalpaśatamapi kalpasahasramapi kalpaśatasahasramapi, yāvadanekānyapi kalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇyanusmarati | yāvat pūrvāntakoṭīmapyanusmarati | amutrāhamāsamevaṃnāmā evaṃgotra evaṃjātya evaṃvarṇa evamāhāra evamājīva evamāyuṣpramāṇa evaṃcirasthitika evaṃsukhaduḥkhapratisaṃvedī | tataścyutaḥ amutropapannaḥ | so 'haṃ tataścyuta ihāsmyupapanna iti | sākāraṃ sanimittaṃ soddeśamanekavidhaṃ pūrvenivāsamanusmarati ||
body.translated_text: "The <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> of purified bodily conduct recollects in detail, with its features and descriptions, many kinds of former dwellings (<s>pūrvenivāsa</s>). He recollects one birth; he recollects two, three, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty births; he recollects a hundred births; he recollects a thousand births; he recollects a hundred thousand births; he recollects up to many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>; he recollects <s>kalpas</s> of dissolution; he recollects <s>kalpas</s> of evolution; he recollects up to many <s>kalpas</s> of dissolution and evolution; he recollects one <s>kalpa</s>, a hundred <s>kalpas</s>, a thousand <s>kalpas</s>, a hundred thousand <s>kalpas</s>, up to many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>; he recollects up to the very beginning-point of the past: 'There I was, of such a name, such a clan, such a birth, such a complexion, such food, such livelihood, such a lifespan, of such longevity, experiencing such pleasure and suffering. Having passed away from there, I was reborn there. Having passed away from there, I was reborn here.' Thus he recollects in detail, with its features, marks, and descriptions, many kinds of former dwellings."

body.text: pariśuddhakāyasamudācāraḥ kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvo divyena cakṣuṣā viśuddhenātikrāntamānuṣakeṇa sarvān paśyati cyavamānānupapadyamānān suvarṇān durvarṇān sugatān durgatān hīnān praṇītān sugatimapi gacchato durgatimapi gacchato yathākarmopagān sattvān yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti ime bata sattvāḥ kāyaduścaritena samanvāgatā vāgaduścaritena samanvāgatā manoduścaritena samanvāgatā āryāṇāmapavādakā mithyādṛṣṭikā mithyādṛṣṭikarmasamādānahetoḥ kāyasya bhedāt paraṃ maraṇādapāyaṃ durgatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayeṣu upapannāḥ | ime punarbata sattvāḥ kāyasucaritena samanvāgatā vākasucaritena samanvāgatā manaḥsucaritena samanvāgatā āryāṇāmanapavādakāḥ samyagdṛṣṭirmasamādānahetoḥ kāyasya bhedāt paraṃ maraṇāt sugatau svargaloke deveṣūpapannāḥ | iti hi devyena cakṣuṣā viśuddhenātikrāntamānuṣakeṇa sattvān paśyati cyavamānānupapadyamānān suvarṇān durvarṇān hīnān praṇītān sugatimapi gacchato durgatimapi gacchato yathākarmopagān sattvān yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti ||
body.translated_text: "The <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> of purified bodily conduct, with the divine eye — purified, surpassing the human — sees all beings passing away and being reborn: fair-complexioned and foul-complexioned, in good states and bad states, inferior and superior, going to good destinations and going to bad destinations. He knows as they truly are the beings who have gone according to their <s>karma</s>: 'Alas, these beings, endowed with misconduct of body, endowed with misconduct of speech, endowed with misconduct of mind, revilers of noble ones, holding wrong views, undertaking actions based on wrong views — upon the dissolution of the body, after death, they have been reborn in the lower realm, in a bad destination, in a state of ruin, in the hells. But alas, these beings, endowed with good conduct of body, endowed with good conduct of speech, endowed with good conduct of mind, not revilers of noble ones, holding right views, undertaking actions based on right views — upon the dissolution of the body, after death, they have been reborn in a good destination, in the heavenly world, among the gods.' Thus with the divine eye — purified, surpassing the human — he sees beings passing away and being reborn: fair-complexioned and foul-complexioned, inferior and superior, going to good destinations and going to bad destinations. He knows as they truly are the beings who have gone according to their <s>karma</s>."

body.text: pariśuddhakāyasamudācāraḥ kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ ekakṣaṇasamāyuktayā prajñayā yat kiṃcijjñātavyamadhimoktavyaṃ vikurvitavyaṃ tatsarvaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti śṛṇoti paśyate budhyate ||
body.translated_text: "The <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> of purified bodily conduct, with wisdom conjoined in a single instant, knows as it truly is whatever is to be known, whatever is to be resolved, and whatever is to be magically created — he hears it, sees it, and understands it."

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then at that time the Blessed One spoke these verses:

children.text: abhijñākramanirdiṣṭo bodhisattvāna tāyinām /
children.translated_text: "The course of the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) has been taught for the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, the Protectors;

children.text: samādhīya sthihitvāna bodhisattvo 'dhigacchati // SRS_38.51 //
children.translated_text: having been established in this <s>samādhi</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> attains [them]. // SRS_38.51 //

children.text: (Vaidya 289)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 289)

children.text: śrotraṃ ca te viśodhenti divyaṃ śrotramacintiyam /
children.translated_text: They purify the ear — the divine ear, inconceivable —

children.text: yena śṛṇvanti te dharmān sarvabuddhehi bhāṣitān // SRS_38.52 //
children.translated_text: by which they hear the <s>dharmas</s> spoken by all the <s>Buddhas</s>. // SRS_38.52 //

children.text: sarāgamasarāgaṃ vā sadoṣaṃ vītadoṣakam /
children.translated_text: Whether with passion or free from passion, with hatred or free from hatred,

children.text: samohaṃ vītamohaṃ vā cittaṃ jānanti prāṇinām // SRS_38.53 //
children.translated_text: with delusion or free from delusion — they know the minds of living beings. // SRS_38.53 //

children.text: pūrvenivāsaṃ jānanti yatra te uṣitāḥ purā /
children.translated_text: They know [their] former dwellings, where they dwelt before,

children.text: kalpakoṭīsahasrāṇi saṅgasteṣāṃ na vidyate // SRS_38.54 //
children.translated_text: for thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s> — yet for them there is no attachment. // SRS_38.54 //

children.text: cakṣuśca te viśodhenti divyaṃ cakṣuranuttaram /
children.translated_text: They purify the eye — the divine eye, unsurpassed —

children.text: anupaśyanti te sattvāṃścyavato 'pyupapadyataḥ // SRS_38.55 //
children.translated_text: they behold beings passing away and also being reborn. // SRS_38.55 //

children.text: ekakṣaṇasamāyuktaprajñayā sarvajātiṣu /
children.translated_text: With wisdom conjoined in a single instant, in all births,

children.text: yat kiṃcidiha jñātavyaṃ dharmāṇāṃ bhūtalakṣaṇam // SRS_38.56 //
children.translated_text: whatever is to be known here — the true characteristic of <s>dharmas</s> — // SRS_38.56 //

body.text: tatra bhagavān punarapi candraprabhaṃ kumārabhūtamāmantrayate sma - tasmāttarhi kumāra vāksaṃvarasaṃvṛto bhaviṣyāmītyevaṃ bodhisattvena mahāsattvena śikṣitavyam | tatra kumāra katamo vāksaṃvaraḥ? yena vāksaṃvareṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ ṣaṣṭyākārasamanvāgatamasaṅgabuddhasvaraghoṣamacityaṃ pratilabhate | ayamucyate kumāra vāksaṃvaraḥ | yena vāksaṃvareṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ ādeyavākyatāṃ pratilabhate | ayamucyate kumāra vāksaṃvaraḥ | yena vāksaṃvareṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāni pratilabhate | daśa tathāgatabalāni, catvāri tathāgatavaiśāradhyāni, aṣṭādaśāveṇikān buddhadharmān pratilabhate | ayamucyate kumāra vāksaṃvaraḥ | yena vāksaṃvareṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvastrīṇi vimokṣamukhāni pratilabhate, caturo brahmavihārān pratilabhate | ayamucyate kumāra vāksaṃvaraḥ | yena vāksaṃvareṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaścatvāri smṛtyupasthānāni pratilabhate | catvāri samyakprahāṇāni, catura ṛddhipādān, pañcendriyāṇi,pañca balāni,sapta bodhyaṅgāni, āryāṣṭāṅgaṃ mārgaṃ pratilabhate | ayamucyate kumāra vāksaṃvaraḥ | yena vāksaṃvareṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo mahākaruṇāvihāraṃ pratilabhate, mahopekṣāvihāraṃ pratilabhate, kṣemāṃśca vitarkān pratilabhate, pravivekāṃśca vitarkān pratilabhate | ayamucyate kumāra vāksaṃvara iti ||
body.translated_text: There the Blessed One again addressed Prince <s>Candraprabha</s>: "Therefore, O Prince, a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> should train thus: 'I shall be one restrained in speech (<s>vāksaṃvara</s>).' And what, O Prince, is restraint of speech? That restraint of speech endowed with which a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> attains the inconceivable, unattached voice-sound of a <s>Buddha</s>, endowed with sixty qualities — this is called, O Prince, restraint of speech. That restraint of speech endowed with which a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> attains persuasive speech — this is called, O Prince, restraint of speech. That restraint of speech endowed with which a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> attains the thirty-two marks of a great person, the ten powers of a <s>Tathāgata</s>, the four fearlessnesses of a <s>Tathāgata</s>, and the eighteen distinctive qualities of a <s>Buddha</s> — this is called, O Prince, restraint of speech. That restraint of speech endowed with which a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> attains the three gates of liberation and the four <s>brahmavihāras</s> (divine abidings) — this is called, O Prince, restraint of speech. That restraint of speech endowed with which a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> attains the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right exertions, the four bases of supernatural power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the noble eightfold path — this is called, O Prince, restraint of speech. That restraint of speech endowed with which a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> attains the abiding in great compassion, the abiding in great equanimity, and attains secure thoughts and thoughts of seclusion — this is called, O Prince, restraint of speech."

body.text: punaraparaṃ kumāra vāksaṃvara ucyate - yena vāksaṃvareṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo mṛṣāvādāt prativirato bhavati | paiśunyāt pāruṣyāt saṃbhinnapralāpāt prativirato bhavati | mātāpitṛṇāmācāryāṇāṃ cāntike asabhyāṃ vācaṃ na niścārayati | yā api tadanyā doṣopasaṃhitā vācastābhyo bodhisattvaḥ prativirato bhavati | tāśca vācaḥ pratiśrutkopamā avatarati | svapnopamā nirmitopamā marīcyupamāḥ pratiśrutkopamāḥ pratibhāsopamā māyopamā avatarati | sa tāmevaṃbhūtāṃ vācaṃ nopalabhate, na kalpayati,na manyate,nāvalambate, nābhiniviśate | ayamucyate kumāra (Vaidya 290) vāksaṃvaraḥ | pariśuddhavāksaṃvaro hi kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvāpāyebhyo na bibheti | sarvabuddhadharmān pratilabhate | sarvabuddharddhi sarvābhijñāṃ pratilabhate ||
body.translated_text: "Furthermore, O Prince, restraint of speech is said [to be this]: that restraint of speech endowed with which a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> refrains from false speech, refrains from slander, harsh speech, and idle chatter. He does not utter unseemly words in the presence of his mother, father, and teachers. Whatever other words connected with faults there may be — the <s>Bodhisattva</s> refrains from those too. He understands those words as like an echo, like a dream, like a magical creation, like a mirage, like an echo, like a reflection, like an illusion. He does not apprehend such speech, does not conceptualize it, does not imagine it, does not cling to it, does not settle upon it. This is called, O Prince, (Vaidya 290) restraint of speech. For, O Prince, a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> of purified speech-restraint does not fear any of the lower realms, attains all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, attains all the supernatural powers and superknowledges of a <s>Buddha</s>."

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then at that time the Blessed One spoke these verses:

children.text: yeneha vāksaṃvaraṇenupeto labhatyavaśaṃ sa hi bodhisattvaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Endowed with such restraint of speech here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> attains mastery;

children.text: sarveṣu dharmeṣu asaṅgajñānamayaṃ hi so ucyati vācasaṃvaraḥ // SRS_38.57 //
children.translated_text: in all <s>dharmas</s>, unattached knowledge — this is called restraint of speech. // SRS_38.57 //

children.text: yeneha vāksaṃvaraṇena dhīrā labhanti dvātriṃśati lakṣaṇāni /
children.translated_text: By which restraint of speech here, the steadfast ones attain the thirty-two marks —

children.text: daśo balāveṇikabuddhadharmānayaṃ hi so ucyati vācasaṃvaraḥ // SRS_38.58 //
children.translated_text: the ten powers and the distinctive <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> — this is called the restraint of speech. // SRS_38.58 //

children.text: yenaha vāksaṃvaraṇena dhīmān prāpnoti sarvānima buddhadharmān /
children.translated_text: By which restraint of speech the wise one obtains all these <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>,

children.text: ye pūrvamasmin parikīrtitā me ayaṃ hi so ucyati vācasaṃvaraḥ // SRS_38.59 //
children.translated_text: which were formerly proclaimed by me — this is called the restraint of speech. // SRS_38.59 //

children.text: yeneha vācāvaraṇena dhīmān labhedvihārān pratisaṃvidaśca /
children.translated_text: By which restraint of speech the wise one obtains the [meditative] abodes and the analytical knowledges,

children.text: atyadbhutān dharma acintiyāṃśca ayaṃ hi so ucyati vācasaṃvaraḥ // SRS_38.60 //
children.translated_text: and most wondrous, inconceivable <s>dharmas</s> — this is called the restraint of speech. // SRS_38.60 //

children.text: yeneha vācāvaraṇena dhīmān smṛtyupasthānāni samyakprahāṇā /
children.translated_text: By which restraint of speech the wise one [obtains] the foundations of mindfulness and the right strivings,

children.text: tatharddhipādān bala indriyāṇi labhatyayaṃ socyati vācasaṃvaraḥ // SRS_38.61 //
children.translated_text: and likewise the bases of supernatural power, the powers, and the faculties — this is called the restraint of speech. // SRS_38.61 //

children.text: yeneha vāksaṃvaraṇena dhīmān mahā upekṣāṃ labhate viśāradaḥ /
children.translated_text: By which restraint of speech the wise one obtains the great equanimity, becoming confident,

children.text: mahākṛpāṃ śuddhavihāratāṃ ca ayaṃ hi so ucyati vācasaṃvaraḥ // SRS_38.62 //
children.translated_text: and the great compassion and the purified abiding — this is called the restraint of speech. // SRS_38.62 //

children.text: yeneha vāksaṃvaraṇena dhīmān kṣemān vitarkāṃllabhate viśuddhān /
children.translated_text: By which restraint of speech the wise one obtains peaceful and purified thoughts,

children.text: (Vaidya 291)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 291)

children.text: tathā vitarkān pravivekaśāntānayaṃ hi so ucyati vācasaṃvaraḥ // SRS_38.63 //
children.translated_text: and likewise thoughts of seclusion and tranquility — this is called the restraint of speech. // SRS_38.63 //

children.text: yeneha vāksaṃvaraṇena dhīmān mṛṣā na bhāṣī piśunāśca vācaḥ /
children.translated_text: By which restraint of speech the wise one does not speak falsehood or slanderous words,

children.text: saṃbhinnapralāpaṃ paruṣāṃ ca vācaṃ ayaṃ khu so ucyati vācasaṃvaraḥ // SRS_38.64 //
children.translated_text: nor frivolous talk or harsh speech — this indeed is called the restraint of speech. // SRS_38.64 //

children.text: yeneha vāksaṃvaraṇena dhīmān saddharmakṣepaṃ na karoti jātu /
children.translated_text: By which restraint of speech the wise one never rejects the true <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: na buddhasaṃghaṃ ca abhyācakṣeta ayaṃ kho so ucyati vācasaṃvaraḥ // SRS_38.65 //
children.translated_text: nor slanders the <s>Buddha</s> or the <s>Saṃgha</s> — this indeed is called the restraint of speech. // SRS_38.65 //

children.text: yeneha vāksaṃvaraṇena dhīmān mātāpitṛṣvācariyānamantike /
children.translated_text: By which restraint of speech the wise one, in the presence of mother, father, and teachers,

children.text: asatyavācaṃ purato na bhāṣī ayaṃ khu so ucyati vācasaṃvaraḥ // SRS_38.66 //
children.translated_text: does not speak untruthful words before them — this indeed is called the restraint of speech. // SRS_38.66 //

children.text: yeneha vāksaṃvaraṇena dhīmān yā anyavāco iha doṣasaṃhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: By which restraint of speech the wise one, from whatever other words are faulty,

children.text: tābhyo 'pyaśeṣaṃ virataḥ sa bhoti ayaṃ khu so ucyati vācasaṃvaraḥ // SRS_38.67 //
children.translated_text: abstains completely from all of them — this indeed is called the restraint of speech. // SRS_38.67 //

children.text: yeneha vāksaṃvaraṇena dhīmān pratiśrutkasaṃnibhatāṃ pi vācam /
children.translated_text: By which restraint of speech the wise one, even speech that is like an echo,

children.text: supinopamāmo tarate viśārado ayaṃ khu so ucyati vācasaṃvaraḥ // SRS_38.68 //
children.translated_text: and like a dream — the confident one transcends — this indeed is called the restraint of speech. // SRS_38.68 //

children.text: nirātmanirjīvanirīhatāṃ cā pratītyutpannāṃ supinopamāṃ mṛṣā /
children.translated_text: Without self, without soul, without agent, dependently arisen, like a dream, false —

children.text: yadeva vācottari bodhisattvo ayaṃ khu so ucyati vācasaṃvaraḥ // SRS_38.69 //
children.translated_text: when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> thus transcends speech — this indeed is called the restraint of speech. // SRS_38.69 //

children.text: nirodhasatyaṃ supinaṃ yathaiva svapnasvabhāvā atha nirvṛtiṃ ca /
children.translated_text: The truth of cessation is just like a dream; <s>nirvāṇa</s> too is of dream-nature —

children.text: yadeva vācottari bodhisattvo ayaṃ khu so ucyati vācasaṃvaraḥ // SRS_38.70 //
children.translated_text: when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> thus transcends speech — this indeed is called the restraint of speech. // SRS_38.70 //

children.text: (Vaidya 292)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 292)

children.text: no cāpi vācaṃ labhate sa kāṃcinna kalpayī nāpi ca manyate saḥ /
children.translated_text: He does not find any speech, nor does he construct, nor does he conceive;

children.text: nālambate nābhiniveśa jātū ayaṃ khu so ucyati vācasaṃvaraḥ // SRS_38.71 //
children.translated_text: he does not grasp, nor does he settle into fixation — this indeed is called the restraint of speech. // SRS_38.71 //

body.text: tatra bhagavān punarapi candraprabhaṃ kumārabhūtamāmantrayate sma - tasmāttarhi kumāra manaḥsaṃvarasaṃvṛto bhaviṣyāmītyevaṃ bodhisattvena mahāsattvena śikṣitavyam | tatra kumāra katamo manaḥsaṃvaraḥ? yena manaḥsaṃvareṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo vajropamaṃ samādhiṃ pratilabhate | ayamucyate kumāra manaḥsaṃvaraḥ | yena manaḥsaṃvareṇa samanvāgato bodhisatvo mahāsattvo jvalanāntarābhāṃ nāma raśmiṃ pratilabhate | ayamucyate manaḥsaṃvaraḥ | yena manaḥsaṃvareṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'ṣṭāṅgopetasvaraghoṣasaṃpadaṃ pratilabhate | ayamucyate manaḥsaṃvaraḥ | yena manaḥsaṃvareṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāni pratilabhate | daśa tathāgatabalāni, catvāri vaiśāradyāni catasraḥ pratisaṃvidaḥ, aṣṭādaśāveṇikāṃśca buddhadharmān pratilabhate | ayamucyate manaḥsaṃvaraḥ | yena manaḥsaṃvareṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ trīṇi vimokṣamukhāni pratilabhate | śūnyatāmanimittamapraṇihitaṃ vimokṣamukhaṃ pratilabhate | ayamucyate manaḥsaṃvaraḥ | yena manaḥsaṃvareṇaḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaścaturo brahmavihārān pratilabhate | mahāmaitrīṃ mahākaruṇāṃ mahāmuditāṃ mahopekṣāṃ pratilabhate | ayamucyate manaḥsaṃvaraḥ | yena manaḥsaṃvareṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaścatvāri smṛtyupasthānāni pratilabhate | catvāri samyakprahāṇāni, catura ṛddhipādān, pañcendriyāṇi,pañca balāni,sapta bodhyaṅgāni, āryāṣṭāṅgaṃ mārgaṃ pratilabhate | ayamucyate manaḥsaṃvaraḥ | yena manaḥsaṃvareṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo mahākaruṇāvihāraṃ pratilabhate | mahopekṣāvihāraṃ pratilabhate | kṣemāṃśca vitarkān pratilabhate | pravivekāṃśca vitarkān pratilabhate | hitaiṣitāṃ ca īryāṃ ca caryāṃ ca pratilabhate | ayamucyate manaḥsaṃvaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: There the Blessed One again addressed Prince <s>Candraprabha</s>: "Therefore, O Prince, a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> should train thus: 'I shall be restrained in the restraint of mind.' What, O Prince, is the restraint of mind? The restraint of mind by which a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> attains the <s>vajra</s>-like <s>samādhi</s> — this, O Prince, is called the restraint of mind. The restraint of mind by which a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> attains the ray called 'radiance-within-blazing' — this is called the restraint of mind. The restraint of mind by which a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> attains the endowment of vocal sounds possessing eight qualities — this is called the restraint of mind. The restraint of mind by which a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> attains the thirty-two marks of a great person, the ten powers of a <s>Tathāgata</s>, the four confidences, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen distinctive <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> — this is called the restraint of mind. The restraint of mind by which a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> attains the three doors of liberation — the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness doors of liberation — this is called the restraint of mind. The restraint of mind by which a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> attains the four <s>brahmavihāras</s> (divine abidings) — great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity — this is called the restraint of mind. The restraint of mind by which a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> attains the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right strivings, the four bases of supernatural power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the noble eightfold path — this is called the restraint of mind. The restraint of mind by which a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> attains the abiding in great compassion, the abiding in great equanimity, peaceful thoughts, thoughts of seclusion, and the aspiration, conduct, and practice of benevolence — this is called the restraint of mind."

body.text: punaraparaṃ kumāra manaḥsaṃvara ucyate - yena manaḥsaṃvareṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo mithyādṛṣṭiprahāṇāya mithyādṛṣṭyā sārdhaṃ na saṃvasati | abhidhyāprahāṇāya anabhidhyālurbhavati | vyāpādaprahāṇāya vyāpādena sārdhaṃ na saṃvasati | kausīdyaprahāṇāya kusīdena sārdhaṃ na saṃvasati | guruṇāmantike mātāpitrorācāryāṃṇāṃ cāntike śāṭhyacittaṃ notpādayati | rāgadveṣamohacittaṃ notpādayati | na ca taiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃvasati | bodhicittaṃ notsṛjati | adhyāśayacittaṃ ca notsṛjati | ye cānye doṣopasaṃhitā manaḥsaṃkalpāstebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ prativirato bhavati | na ca taiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃvasati | ayamucyate manaḥsaṃvara | tacca mano māyopamamityavatarati | svapnopamamapi marīcyupamamapi | nirmitopamamiti pratibhāsopamamityavatarati | na kutaścidāgamanato 'vatarati | svapnopamaṃ sukhamavatarati | svapnopamamanityato 'vatarati | svapnopamaṃ nirjīvato 'vatarati | (Vaidya 293) svapnopamaṃ śūnyato 'vatarati | tacca nopalabhate na kalpayati na manyate nāvalambate nābhiniviśate | ayamucyate kumāra manaḥsaṃvaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: "Furthermore, O Prince, the restraint of mind is this: the restraint of mind by which a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s>, for the abandonment of wrong views, does not dwell together with wrong views; for the abandonment of covetousness, becomes free from covetousness; for the abandonment of ill-will, does not dwell together with ill-will; for the abandonment of laziness, does not dwell together with laziness; does not generate a mind of guile in the presence of his elders — his mother, father, and teachers; does not generate a mind of passion, hatred, or delusion; does not dwell together with them; does not abandon the thought of awakening; does not abandon the mind of aspiration; and abstains from all other mental intentions that are faulty — does not dwell together with them. This is called the restraint of mind. And he comprehends that mind as being like an illusion, like a dream, like a mirage, like a magical creation, like a reflection. He comprehends it as not coming from anywhere. He comprehends happiness as like a dream. He comprehends impermanence as like a dream. He comprehends it as like a dream in being without life. (Vaidya 293) He comprehends it as like a dream in being empty. And he does not find it, does not construct, does not conceive, does not grasp, and does not settle into fixation. This, O Prince, is called the restraint of mind."

body.text: pariśuddhamanaḥsamudācāro hi kumāra bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvākṣaṇāṃśca varjayati | acintyāṃśca sarvabuddhadharmān pratilabhate | sarvabuddhebhyaśca sarvabuddhābhijñāṃ akopyāṃ ca cetovimuktiṃ pratilabhate | ayamucyate manaḥsaṃvaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: "A <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> whose mental conduct is purified, O Prince, avoids all the unfavorable conditions and attains all the inconceivable <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. From all <s>Buddhas</s> he attains the complete <s>Buddha</s>-superknowledge and the unshakeable liberation of mind. This is called the restraint of mind."

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One at that time spoke these verses:

children.text: śṛṇotha sarvi avikṣiptamanā mama bhāṣato manaḥsaṃvaraṇam /
children.translated_text: "Listen, all of you, with undistracted minds, as I speak of the restraint of mind!

children.text: śrutvā ca tatra pratiapadyathā me yadīcchathā laghu viśodhanatām // SRS_38.72 //
children.translated_text: And having heard, practice it — if you wish for swift purification! // SRS_38.72 //

children.text: manaḥsaṃvareṇa labhi yena vidu parama praśānta vipulānacalān /
children.translated_text: By the restraint of mind, by which the wise one attains the supreme, peaceful, vast, and immovable —

children.text: jinadharmacintiya tathādbhutatāṃ manaḥsaṃvarucyati viśuddha ayam // SRS_38.73 //
children.translated_text: the inconceivable and wondrous <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> — this is called the purified restraint of mind. // SRS_38.73 //

children.text: manaḥsaṃvareṇa labhi yena vidu cetovimuktimacalāṃ satatam /
children.translated_text: By the restraint of mind, by which the wise one attains the constant and unshakeable liberation of mind,

children.text: vajropamaṃ tatha samādhivaraṃ manaḥsaṃvarūcyati hi śreṣṭha ayam // SRS_38.74 //
children.translated_text: and the supreme <s>vajra</s>-like <s>samādhi</s> — this is called the most excellent restraint of mind. // SRS_38.74 //

children.text: niṣpādayatyapi ca yena vidu upacāraraśmiṃ vipulārthakarīm /
children.translated_text: By which the wise one accomplishes the "radiance" ray, productive of vast benefit,

children.text: āryāṣṭāṅgupetaśvara yena labhī manaḥsaṃvarūcyati viśuddha ayam // SRS_38.75 //
children.translated_text: and by which he attains the sounds endowed with the noble eightfold [qualities] — this is called the purified restraint of mind. // SRS_38.75 //

children.text: manaḥsaṃvareṇa vidu yena varāṃ dvātriṃśalakṣaṇa laghū labhate /
children.translated_text: By the restraint of mind, by which the wise one swiftly attains the supreme thirty-two marks,

children.text: yaśa co balānyakhilabuddhaguṇān manaḥsaṃvaraḥ kathitu śreṣṭha ayam // SRS_38.76 //
children.translated_text: and fame, and the powers, and all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities — this supreme restraint of mind has been declared. // SRS_38.76 //

children.text: manasaṃvareṇa labhi yena vidu pratisaṃvidastatha viśāradatām /
children.translated_text: By the restraint of mind, by which the wise one attains the analytical knowledges and likewise confidence,

children.text: paramādbhutān guṇa acintya tathā manaḥsaṃvaraḥ kathitu śreṣṭhu ayam // SRS_38.77 //
children.translated_text: and supreme wondrous, inconceivable qualities — this supreme restraint of mind has been declared. // SRS_38.77 //

children.text: (Vaidya 294)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 294)

children.text: manaḥsaṃvareṇa labhi yena vidu smṛtyupasthāna catu ṛddhipādān /
children.translated_text: By the restraint of mind, by which the wise one [attains] the four foundations of mindfulness and the four bases of supernatural power,

children.text: samyakprahāṇa bala indriya co manaḥsaṃvara kathitu śreṣṭha ayam // SRS_38.78 //
children.translated_text: the right strivings, the powers, and the faculties — this supreme restraint of mind has been declared. // SRS_38.78 //

children.text: manaḥsaṃvareṇa laghu yena vidu bodhyaṅga sapta labhate vimalān /
children.translated_text: By the restraint of mind, by which the wise one swiftly attains the seven stainless factors of awakening,

children.text: aṣṭāṅgikaṃ ca tatha mārgavaraṃ manaḥsaṃvaraḥ kathitu śreṣṭha ayam // SRS_38.79 //
children.translated_text: and likewise the supreme noble eightfold path — this supreme restraint of mind has been declared. // SRS_38.79 //

children.text: manaḥsaṃvareṇa labhi yena vidu mahupekṣatāviharaṇaṃ pravaram /
children.translated_text: By the restraint of mind, by which the wise one [attains] the supreme abiding in great equanimity,

children.text: karuṇāvihārimamalaṃ ca paraṃ manaḥsaṃvaraḥ kathitu śreṣṭha ayam // SRS_38.80 //
children.translated_text: and the stainless, supreme abiding in compassion — this supreme restraint of mind has been declared. // SRS_38.80 //

children.text: manaḥsaṃvareṇa labhi yena śivān kṣemān vitarka vidu śuddha sadā /
children.translated_text: By the restraint of mind, by which the wise one [attains] auspicious, peaceful, and always pure thoughts,

children.text: labhate guṇāḍhyu pravivekakathāṃ manaḥsaṃvaraḥ kathitu śreṣṭha ayam // SRS_38.81 //
children.translated_text: and attains the discourse of seclusion, rich in qualities — this supreme restraint of mind has been declared. // SRS_38.81 //

children.text: manasaṃvareṇa vidu yena yuto mithyākudṛṣṭyā saha na vasati /
children.translated_text: By the restraint of mind, by which the wise one endowed [therewith] does not dwell together with wrong and evil views,

children.text: vyāpādābhidhyā na ca saṃjanayī manaḥsaṃvaraḥ kathitu śreṣṭha ayam // SRS_38.82 //
children.translated_text: and does not generate ill-will or covetousness — this supreme restraint of mind has been declared. // SRS_38.82 //

children.text: manaḥsaṃvareṇa vidu yena yutaḥ kuhanāṃ karoti na muhūrtamapi /
children.translated_text: By the restraint of mind, by which the wise one endowed [therewith] does not engage in hypocrisy even for a moment,

children.text: gurūṇāṃ ca śāṭhiyu na saṃjanayī manaḥsaṃvaraḥ kathitu śreṣṭha ayam // SRS_38.83 //
children.translated_text: and does not generate guile toward his elders — this supreme restraint of mind has been declared. // SRS_38.83 //

children.text: manaḥsaṃvareṇa vidu yena yuto rāgatha dveṣa na janeti manaḥ /
children.translated_text: By the restraint of mind, by which the wise one endowed [therewith] does not generate a mind of passion or hatred,

children.text: tatha mohacittu na janeti kvacit manaḥsaṃvaraḥ kathitu śreṣṭhu ayam // SRS_38.84 //
children.translated_text: nor generates a mind of delusion anywhere — this supreme restraint of mind has been declared. // SRS_38.84 //

children.text: manaḥsaṃvareṇa vidu yena yuto bodhāya citta na viniḥsṛjatī /
children.translated_text: By the restraint of mind, by which the wise one endowed [therewith] does not abandon the thought of awakening,

children.text: adhyāśayaṃ ca na vikopayatī manaḥsaṃvaraḥ kathitu śreṣṭha ayam // SRS_38.85 //
children.translated_text: and does not corrupt his aspiration — this supreme restraint of mind has been declared. // SRS_38.85 //

children.text: (Vaidya 295)
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 295)

children.text: manaḥsaṃvareṇa vidu yena yuto ye cānya doṣa vividhā manasaḥ /
children.translated_text: By the restraint of mind, by which the wise one endowed [therewith], whatever other various faults of mind —

children.text: sarvebhi sārdha na ca saṃvasatī manaḥsaṃvaraḥ kathitu śreṣṭhu ayam // SRS_38.86 //
children.translated_text: he does not dwell together with any of them — this supreme restraint of mind has been declared. // SRS_38.86 //

children.text: māyopamaṃ ca mana otaratī supinopamaṃ tatha marīcisamam /
children.translated_text: And he comprehends the mind as like an illusion, like a dream, like a mirage,

children.text: pratibhāsalakṣaṇamatho satataṃ manaḥsaṃvaraḥ kathitu śreṣṭhu ayam // SRS_38.87 //
children.translated_text: with the characteristic of a reflection constantly — this supreme restraint of mind has been declared. // SRS_38.87 //

children.text: supimopamaṃ ca sukhamotaratī tathanitya śūnyata aśāśvatataḥ /
children.translated_text: He comprehends happiness as like a dream, impermanent, empty, and non-eternal;

children.text: mana eva otarati yena vidu manasaṃvaraḥ kathitu śreṣṭhu ayam // SRS_38.88 //
children.translated_text: by which the wise one comprehends the mind itself — this supreme restraint of mind has been declared. // SRS_38.88 //

children.text: nirjīvamotarati niḥsattva mano utpannu pratyayata cakrasamam /
children.translated_text: He comprehends [the mind as] without life, without a being, arisen from conditions, like a wheel;

children.text: na kutaścidāgatu na cāpi gataṃ manasaṃvaraḥ kathitu śreṣṭha ayam // SRS_38.89 //
children.translated_text: not coming from anywhere, nor going anywhere — this supreme restraint of mind has been declared. // SRS_38.89 //

children.text: na ca tanmanye upalabhāti kvaci na ca kalpayatyatha na manyatyasau /
children.translated_text: He does not find or obtain that mind anywhere; nor does he construct, nor does he conceive;

children.text: nālambhate viniviśati na co manasaṃvaraḥ kathitu śreṣṭhu ayam // SRS_38.90 //
children.translated_text: he does not grasp, nor does he settle into fixation — this supreme restraint of mind has been declared. // SRS_38.90 //

children.text: paramārthasatya supinena samaṃ nirvāṇa svapnasamamotarati /
children.translated_text: The ultimate truth is the same as a dream; he comprehends <s>nirvāṇa</s> as equal to a dream;

children.text: mana evamotarati yena vidu manasaṃvaraḥ kathitu śreṣṭha ayam // SRS_38.91 //
children.translated_text: by which the wise one thus comprehends the mind — this supreme restraint of mind has been declared. // SRS_38.91 //

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje kāyavāṅbhanaḥsaṃvaraparivartaḥ aṣṭatriṃśatitamaḥ || 38 ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the thirty-eighth chapter in the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>, the <s>Kāyavāṅmanaḥsaṃvaraparivarta</s> (Chapter on the Restraint of Body, Speech, and Mind).

body.text:
(Vaidya 296)
39 Padatriśatanirdeśaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 296) Chapter 39: The <s>Padatriśatanirdeśaparivarta</s> (Chapter on the Exposition of the Three Hundred Words).

body.text: tatra kumāra katamā karmaviśuddhiḥ? yadidaṃ svapnopamaṃ tribhavaṃ dṛṣṭvā tatra virāgatāmutpādayati | iyamucyate karmaviśuddhiḥ || tatra katama ālambanasamatikramaḥ? yadidaṃ māyopamatāṃ skandhadhātvāyatanānāṃ buddhā teṣāṃ vyavasargaḥ | ayamucyate ālambanasamatikramaḥ || tatra katamā skandhaparijñā? yadidaṃ marīcyupamatāṃ skandhānāmavatarati || tatra katamā dhātusamatā? yadidaṃ nirmitopamānāṃ dhātūnāṃ pratinisargaḥ || tatra katama āyatanāprakarṣaḥ? yadidaṃ pratibhāsopamānāmāyatanānāṃ pratinisargaḥ || - - - - tṛṣṇāprahāṇam? yadidaṃ sarvadharmāṇāmanālambanatā || - - - - anutpādasākṣātkriyā? yadidaṃ sarvadharmāṇāmanupalabdhiḥ || - - - - kriyāvatāraḥ? yadidaṃ vīryasamutthitasya duḥkhasya vipraṇāśaḥ || - - - - hetudīpanā? yadidaṃ pratiśrutkopamānāṃ skandhānāmabhinirvṛttiḥ || - - - - phalāvipraṇāśaḥ? yadidaṃ svapnopamasya karmaphalasyāvipraṇāśaḥ || - - - - dharmadarśanam? yadidaṃ sarvadharmāṇāmapaśyanatā || - - - - mārgabhāvanā? yadidaṃ sarvadharmāṇāmanupalabdhibhāvanā || - - - - tathāgatasamavadhānam? yadidaṃ sarvabuddhānāṃ śikṣāpratipattiḥ || - - - - tīkṣṇaprajñatā? yadidaṃ sarvadharmāṇāmanutpattikakḥāntiḥ || - - - - sattvānupraveśajñānam? yadidaṃ indriyaparāparajñatājñānam ||
body.translated_text: There, prince, what is purification of <s>karma</s>? It is this: seeing the three realms of existence as dream-like, one generates dispassion toward them. This is called purification of <s>karma</s>. There, what is transcendence of the object of support? It is this: understanding the illusion-like nature of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), the <s>Buddhas</s> [teach] their relinquishment. This is called transcendence of the object of support. There, what is full comprehension of the <s>skandhas</s>? It is this: one enters into [the understanding that] the <s>skandhas</s> are like a mirage. There, what is equality of the <s>dhātus</s>? It is this: the relinquishment of the <s>dhātus</s> as being like magical creations. There, what is non-extension of the <s>āyatanas</s>? It is this: the relinquishment of the <s>āyatanas</s> as being like reflections. [There, what is] abandonment of craving? It is this: the absence of an object of support for all <s>dharmas</s>. [There, what is] direct realization of non-arising? It is this: the non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s>. [There, what is] entry into action? It is this: the destruction of suffering that arises from vigor. [There, what is] illumination of causes? It is this: the production of <s>skandhas</s> that are like an echo. [There, what is] non-destruction of the fruit? It is this: the non-destruction of the fruit of <s>karma</s> that is like a dream. [There, what is] seeing the <s>Dharma</s>? It is this: the non-seeing of all <s>dharmas</s>. [There, what is] cultivation of the path? It is this: the cultivation of the non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s>. [There, what is] <s>Tathāgata</s>-mindfulness? It is this: the practice of the training of all <s>Buddhas</s>. [There, what is] sharp wisdom? It is this: the acceptance of the non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpattikadharma-kṣānti</s>). [There, what is] knowledge of entry into [the minds of] beings? It is this: the knowledge of the superiority and inferiority of faculties.

body.text: tatra katamad dharmajñānam? yadidaṃ sarvadharmāṇāmanupalabdhiḥ || - - - - pratisaṃvidāvatārajñānam? yadidaṃ yathābhūtadharmanayapraveśaḥ || - - - - akṣaraprabhedajñānam? yadidaṃ trimantraprayogajñānam, ākārānākārajñānam || - - - - vastusamatikramaḥ? yadidaṃ avastubudhyanā || - - - - ghoṣaparijñā? yadidaṃ pratiśrutkopamāvatārajñḥnam || - - - - prḥmodyapratilḥbhaḥ? yadidaṃ sarvadharmḥṇḥmanupalabdhiḥ, saṃsḥrḥt duḥkhasya utsargo bhḥrḥvaharaṇam || - - - - dharmaprītyanubhavanatḥ? yadidaṃ avavḥdasaṃtoṣaṇḥnutsargasvayḥnḥnuśaṃsḥpaśyanḥ || - - - - ḥrjavatḥ? yadidaṃ ḥryasatyaprativedhaḥ || - - - - rijukatḥ? yadidaṃ īryḥpathasyḥkalpanatḥ || - - - - apagatabhṛkuṭitḥ? yadidaṃ doṣaprahḥṇam || - - - - sauśīlyatḥ? yadidaṃ sukhasaṃvḥsatḥ || - - - - mḥdhuryatḥ? yadidaṃ pareṣu hitavastutḥṃ || - - - - pūrvḥlḥpitḥ? yadidaṃ ehisvḥgatavacanatḥ laghūtthḥnatḥ || - - - - gurugauravatḥ? yadidaṃ gurūṇḥmantike bhayaṃ ca kalyḥṇamitratḥ ca || - - - - guruśuśrūṣḥ? yadidaṃ guruṇḥmupasthḥnḥvasthḥnaparicaryḥ || - - - - upapattisaṃtuṣṭiḥ? yadidaṃ sarvopapattiṣvanḥsvḥdanatḥ | - - - - śukladharmḥtṛptatḥ? yadidaṃ śukladharmḥṇḥṃ paryeṣṭiḥ kiṃkuśalamḥrgaṇatḥ ca ||
body.translated_text: There, what is knowledge of <s>dharmas</s>? It is this: the non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s>. [There, what is] knowledge of entry into the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>)? It is this: entry into the method of <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are. [There, what is] knowledge of the analysis of syllables? It is this: knowledge of the application of the three <s>mantras</s>, knowledge of form and formlessness. [There, what is] transcendence of substance? It is this: awakening to substancelessness. [There, what is] full comprehension of sound? It is this: knowledge of entry into [understanding sounds as] echo-like. [There, what is] attainment of joy? It is this: the non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s>, the letting go of the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>, the removal of the burden. [There, what is] experience of delight in the <s>Dharma</s>? It is this: seeing the benefits of contentment with poor [robes], relinquishment, and solitary dwelling. [There, what is] sincerity? It is this: penetration of the noble truths. [There, what is] straightforwardness? It is this: non-conceptualization of deportment. [There, what is] absence of a furrowed brow? It is this: abandonment of faults. [There, what is] good character? It is this: being easy to live with. [There, what is] sweetness? It is this: being beneficial in substance toward others. [There, what is] greeting first? It is this: saying 'Come, welcome!' and rising promptly. [There, what is] reverence toward teachers? It is this: fear and spiritual friendship in the presence of teachers. [There, what is] obedience to teachers? It is this: attending upon, remaining near, and serving teachers. [There, what is] contentment with [any] rebirth? It is this: not relishing any [particular] rebirth. [There, what is] insatiability for wholesome <s>dharmas</s>? It is this: the seeking of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> and the search for what is skillful.

body.text:
tatra katamā ājīvapariśuddhiḥ? yadidaṃ itaretarasaṃtuṣṭitā akūhaṇatā anaiṣikatā, lābhena lābhācikīrṣaṇatā ca|| - - - - araṇyavāsānutsargaḥ? yadidaṃ anikṣiptadhuratā kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu (Vaidya 297) prāntaśayyāsanābhiratirvanagahanagiridurgaguhākandareṣvabhiratiḥ dharmaprītyanubhavanatā ca | asaṃsargaḥ gṛhipravrajitairabhisatkāraślokenānadhyavasānatā tṛṣṇāprahāṇadhyānaprītyanubhavanatā ca | ayamucyate 'raṇyavāsānutsargaḥ || tatra - - - - bhūmyavasthānajñānam? yadidaṃ śrāvakabhūmiphalavyavasthānajñānaṃ pratyekabuddhabhūmivyavasthānajñānaṃ bodhisattvabhūmivyavasthānajñānaṃ ca | tatra - - - - smṛtyuvipraṇāśaḥ? yadidaṃ anityaduḥkhaśūnyānātmamanasikāraḥ || tatra - - - - skandhakauśalyajñānam? yadidaṃ skandhadhātvāyatanaprabhedajñānaṃ ca tatra cānupalabdhiḥ || tatra - - - - abhijñāsākṣātkriyā? yadidaṃ caturṇāmṛddhipādānāṃ pratilambhaḥ ṛddhivikurvaṇatā ca || tatra - - - - kleśāpakarṣaḥ? yadidaṃ rāgadveṣamohaprahāṇam || tatra - - - - vāsanānusaṃghisamuddhātajñānam? yadida pūrvabālacarivijugupsanatā śrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmyaspṛhaṇatā ca || tatra - - - - viśeṣagāmitā? yadidaṃ buddhavaiśāradyapratisaṃvidāṃ niṣpādanatā || tatra - - - - bhāvanābhiniṣyandaḥ? yadidaṃ anunayapratighaprahāṇam || tatra - - - - āpattikauśalyam? yadidaṃ prātimokṣavinayasaṃvaraḥ || - - - - paryutthānaviṣkambhaṇam? yadidaṃ atyayadeśanā āyatisaṃvaraścākuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām || - - - - anunayaprahāṇam? yadidaṃ traidhātukabhavatṛṣṇālatāsamuddhāto 'samutpannānāṃ cākuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmanutpādanatā, utpannānāṃ ca kuśalamūlānāṃ dharmāṇāmavipraṇāśaḥ | - - - - bhavasamatikramaḥ? yadidaṃ traidhātukānupalabdhiḥ, amanasikāratā ca || - - - - jātismaratā? yadidaṃ pūrvenivāsajñānam || - - - - karmavipākaniṣkāṅkṣaṇatā? yadidaṃ ucchedaśāśvatavivarjanatā || tatra - - - - dharmacintā? yadidaṃ yathābhūtacintā || tatra - - - - śrutaparyeṣṭiḥ? yadidaṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhapiṭakasya bodhisattvapiṭakasya ca ādhāraṇatā bhāvanatā ca || - - - - jñānatīkṣṇatā? yadidaṃ svapnopamamanutpādajñānam || - - - - jñānatṛṣṇā? yadidaṃ jñānaparyeṣṭiḥ || - - - - jñānāvabodhaḥ? yadidaṃ anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhyabhiniṣpādanatā
ca || - - - - ājāneyabhūmiḥ? yadidaṃ bodhisattvaśikṣāsthānam || - - - - śailopamatā? yadidaṃ bodhicittasyānutsargaḥ? - - - - akampanatā? yadidaṃ kleśairasaṃhāryatā || - - - - acalanatā? yadidaṃ sarvanimittānāmamanasikāraḥ || - - - - avaivartyalakṣaṇam? yadidaṃ ṣaṭpāramitānāmakhaṇḍanatā, anyalokadhātusthitānāṃ buddhānāmabhīkṣṇadarśanatā ca || - - - - kuśaladharmābhisaṃpat? yadidaṃ āsannībhāvo 'nuttarāyāḥ samaksaṃbodheḥ || - - - - pāpakarmajugupsanatā? yadidaṃ āyatisaṃvaratā cānutpādaśca pāpasya || - - - - kleśānāmasamudācāraḥ? yadidaṃ avidyāyā bhavatṛṣṇāyāśca krodhasya cānutpādanatā || - - - - śikṣāyā aparityāgaḥ? yadidaṃ karmavipākapattīyanatā buddhagauravatā ca || - - - - samādhivyavasthānam? yadidaṃ cittacaitasikānāṃ dharmāṇāmanutpādāvyayakauśalyaṃ cittaikāgratā ca || - - - - sattvāśayajñānam? yadidaṃ indriyaparāparajñatājñānam || - - - - upapattiviśeṣajñānam? yadidaṃ pañcānāṃ gatīnāṃ vyavasthānajñānam || - - - - jñānānantatā? yadidaṃ laukikalokottareṣu śilpeṣvanābhogajñānam || - - - - vacanapratisaṃghijñānam? yadidaṃ tathāgatasaṃghābhāṣyānubudhyanatā || - - - - gṛhāvāsaparityāgaḥ? yadidaṃ kāyacittavivekābhiniṣkramaḥ || - - - - traidhātuke 'nabhiratiḥ? yadidaṃ traidhātukayathābhūtadarśanatā || - - - - cittasyānavalīnatā? yadidaṃ cittasyāparityāgaḥ samāpadyamānāparityāgaśca || (Vaidya 298) - - - - dharmeṣvabhiniveśaḥ? yadidaṃ sarvasnehaprahāṇam || - - - - dharmaparigrahaḥ? yadidaṃ buddhabodhyārakṣā, eṣāṃ caiva sūtrāntānāṃ pratīcchanatā || - - - - dharmaguptiḥ? yadidaṃ saddharmapratikṣepakāṇāṃ sahadharmeṇa nigrahaḥ || - - - - karmavipākapattiyanatā? yadidaṃ lajjayā pāpakāt karmaṇo viratiḥ, kuśaladharmaparyeṣṭau cābhiyogaḥ || - - - - vinayakauśalyam? yadidaṃ prakṛtyāyapattyanāpattibudhyanatā || - - - - adhikaraṇavyupaśamaḥ? yadidaṃ gaṇavivarjanatā || - - - - avigraho 'vivādaḥ? yadidaṃ laukikakathānirarthikatā || - - - - kṣāntibhūmiḥ? yadidaṃ kāyacittapīḍādhivāsanatā || - - - - kṣāntisamādānam? yadidaṃ parato duruktānāṃ vacanapathānāmadhyupekṣā kṣāntyakhaṇḍanatā ca || - - - - dharmapravicayaḥ? yadidaṃ skandhadhātvāyatanānāṃ prabhedaḥ saṃkleśavyavadānapakṣasya
ca prabhedasteṣāṃ cānupalabdhiḥ || - - - - dharmaviniścayakauśalyam? yadidaṃ sarvadharmāṇāmanabhilāpaḥ || - - - - dharmapadaprabhedjñānam? yadidaṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ vyavasthānanistīraṇatā || - - - - dharmapadanirhārakauśalyam? yadidaṃ yathābhūtānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ nirdeśaḥ || - - - - arthānarthasaṃbhedanirhārakauśalyajñānam? yadidaṃ dharmaprakṛtyanutkṣepāprakṣepaḥ || - - - - pūrvāntajñānam? yadidaṃ hetujñānam || - - - - aparāntajñānam? yadidaṃ pratyayajñānam || - - - - trimaṇḍalapariśuddhijñānam? yadidaṃ atītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ dharmāṇāmanupalabdhiḥ, amanasikāritā ca || - - - - cittāvasthānam? yadidaṃ cittānupalabdhiḥ || - - - - kāyavyavasthānam? yadidaṃ kāyagatānusmṛtiḥ ||.... īryāpathalakṣaṇam? yeyamāryadharmāsaṃbhrāntatā | - - - - īryāpathasyāvikopanatā? yadidaṃ pracchannakalyāṇatā ||.... īryāpathasyāvikalpanatā? yadidaṃ vigatapāpecchatā || - - - - indriyaprāsādikatā? yadidaṃ dharmagatamanasikāratā yuktabhāṇitā kālajñatā yathābhūtānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ bhūtaprakāśanatā || .... lokajñatā? yadidaṃ atikramamasaṃprajānatā ||....muktatyāgitā? yadidaṃ satāṃ vastūnāmagrahaṇatā, amātsaryatā ca ||.... pratatapāṇitā? yadidaṃ saṃvibhāvaśīlatā ||.... agṛhītacittatā? yadidaṃ śraddhānāvilatā ||....vyapatrāpitā? yadidaṃ amukharatā ||....hriyāpaṇata || yadidaṃ anabhimukhatā ||.... akuśalacittajugupsanatā? yadidaṃ bāladharmabudhyanatā taiścāsamavadhānam ||.... dhūtānavasṛjanatā? yadidaṃ dṛḍhasamādānatā ||.... cāritrasamavadhānatā? yadidaṃ caryāpathakramasaṃjānanatā ||.... prītisamudācāraḥ? yadidaṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmanuśaṃsācittatā ||.... gurūṇāmāsanapratyutthānam? yadidaṃ nihatamānatā, anālasyatā cā ||.... mānasya nigrahaḥ? yadidaṃ ātmano 'nupalabdhiranālambanatā ca ||.... cittasya saṃgrahaḥ? yadidaṃ śukladharmāṇāmavipraṇāśajñānam |....cittotsāhanatā? yadidaṃ vīryaphalāvipraṇāśajñānam ||.... arthapratisaṃvijjñānam? yadidaṃ yathābhūtasatyaprativedhajñānam ||.... jñānānubodhaḥ? yadidaṃ laukikalokottarāṇāṃ dharmāṇāmanubudhyanatā ||.... ajñānavigamaḥ? yadidaṃ yathābhūtānāṃ dharmāṇāmadhyāropavigamaḥ ||.... cittapraveśajñānam? yadidaṃ utpādavyayajñānam ||.... āhāranirhārakauśalyajñānam?
yadidaṃ tīkṣṇaprajñatā ||.... rutaravitajñānam? yadidaṃ yathābhūtadharmaprakāśanatā ||....vyavasthānajñānam? yadidaṃ yathābhūtasyāvatārajñānam ||....arthaviniścayaḥ? yadidaṃ saṃskāraskandhocchedaḥ ||....arthānarthavivarjanatā? (Vaidya 299) yadidaṃ bhavasamatikramaḥ, pareṣāṃ ca bhavasamatikramaṇāvatāraṇatā ca ||.... satpuruṣāśrayaḥ? yadidaṃ buddhāvirahitatā ||....satpuruṣasamavadhānam? yadidaṃ buddhabodhisattvapratyekabuddhaśrāvakasevanatā ||.... asatpuruṣavarjanatā? yadidaṃ upalambhikānāṃ kusīdānāṃ ca vivarjanatā ||.... dhyānābhiratiḥ? yadidaṃ kāmakaṇṭakavivarjanatā, dhyānānāmanutsarjanatā, prītyavijahatā ca ||.... dhyāneṣvanadhyavasānam? yadidaṃ traidhātukasamatikramaṇacchandaḥ satvaparipācanācchandaḥ uttariprajñāvabhāsacchandaśca ||....abhijñāvikurvaṇatā? yadidaṃ pañcasvabhijñāsu sthitvā durvijñeyānāṃ buddhadharmāṇāṃ parebhyaḥ saṃprakāśanatā ||.... nāmasaṃketaḥ? yadidaṃ apariniṣpannānāṃ nāmnāmanubudhyanatā ||.... prajñaptivyavahāraḥ? yadidaṃ lokavyavahāraḥ ||....prajñaptisamuddhātaḥ? yadidaṃ pravyāhārajñānam ||....saṃsāranivṛttiḥ? yadidaṃ saṃsāradoṣapratyavekṣā ||.... lābhānarthikatā? yadidaṃ bhūtālpecchatā ||.... lābhasatkārānādeyatā? yadidaṃ anutkaṇṭhatā ca viagatapāpecchatā ca ||.... avarṇairamaṅkubhāvatā? yadidaṃ skandhadhātuparīkṣājñānam ||.... bhūtānāṃ varṇānāmanadhivāsanatā? yadidaṃ praticchannakalyāṇatā ca lābhasatkārasya cāntarāyabudhyanatā || ....satkāreṣūpekṣā? yadidaṃ karmavipākabudhyanatā ||.... asatkāreṣvamaṅkubhāvatā? yadidaṃ yogasyānutsarjanatā ||.... nindāyāmakupyanatā? yadidaṃ laukikadharmapratyavekṣā ||.... praśaṃsāyāmupekṣā? yadidaṃ kalyāṇadharmaparyeṣṭiniṣkramaṇam ||.... alābhe 'līnatā? yadidaṃ svayaṃkṛtānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ pratyavekṣaṇatā |.... gṛhībhiḥ sārdhamasaṃstavaḥ? yadidaṃ āmiṣakiṃcidvivarjanatā || .... pravrajitaiḥ sārdhamasaṃstavaḥ? yadidaṃ ayuktavivarjanatā ca yuktaparyeṣaṇatā ca ||....agocaravivarjanatā? yadidaṃ pañcānāṃ nivaraṇānāṃ prahāṇam ||.... gocarapracāraḥ? yadidaṃ smṛtyupasthānānāṃ bhāvanā ||....ācārasaṃpad? yadidaṃ parānurakṣā ||....ācāravivarjanatā? yadidaṃ ātmanaḥ
kalyāṇadharmānurakṣaṇatā ||.... kulānāmadūṣaṇatā? yadidaṃ jñātravivarjanatā ||.... śāsanarakṣāḥ? yadidaṃ dharmaparyeṣṭisamādānatā dharmānudharmapratipattiśca || ....alpabhāṣyatā? yadidaṃ śamathapratilambhaḥ ||.... mārdavatā? yadidaṃ vipaśyanāpratilambhaḥ ||....prativacanakauśalyam? yadidaṃ uttarapratyuttarajñānam ||.... pratyarthikanigrahaḥ? yadidaṃ yathābhūtānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ prakāśanatā vyavasthāpanatā ca, upālambhānigrahaśca ||....kālapratikramaḥ? yadidaṃ kālajñatā ||.... pṛthagjaneṣvaviśvāsaḥ? yadidaṃ bāladharmadoṣadarśitā ||....duḥkhitānāmaparibhavaḥ? yadidaṃ sarvasattveṣu samacittatā ||.... duḥkhitānāṃ dhanānuprayacchanatā? yadidaṃ lokāmiṣadānam ||.... daridrāṇāmanavasādanam? yadidaṃ pareṣāmantike kṛpābuddhitā ||.... duḥśīlānāmanukampanā? yadidaṃ pareṣāmāpatteruddharaṇatā ca śīlapratiṣṭhāpanatā ca || ....hitavastutā? yadidaṃ pareṣāmupakārakaraṇatā ||....kṛpābuddhitā? yadidaṃ sattvānāmanāgataduḥkhapaśyanatā ||.... dharmānugrahaḥ? yadidaṃ pareṣāṃ yathābhūtadharmāvataraṇatā ||.... āmiṣaparityāgaḥ? yadidaṃ skandhaparityāgaḥ, pareṣāṃ cāmiṣānugrahaḥ ||.... asaṃnicayasthānam? yadidaṃ āmiṣajugupsanatā ārakṣādoṣadarśanatā ca ||.... śīlapraśaṃsā? yadidaṃ śīlaphalānubodhaḥ || (Vaidya 300) .... dauḥśīlyajugupsanatā? yadidaṃ dauḥśīlyadoṣabuddhyanatā ||.... śīlavatāmakampyasevanatā? yadidaṃ śīlavatsu durlabhasaṃjñājñānam ||....sarvāstiparityāgitā? yadidaṃ kalyāṇāśayatā ||....adhyāśayanimantraṇatā? yadidaṃ pareṣāṃ sukhārthikatā ||....yathoktakāritā? yadidaṃ kalyāṇāśayasaṃpat ||.... abhīkṣṇaparyupāsanatā? yadidaṃ kuśalagaveṣaṇaparipṛcchanatā ||....prītyanubhavanatā? yadidaṃ adhigamajñānaṃ cāgamajñānaṃ ca |.... dṛṣṭāntajñānam? yadidaṃ upamājñānamavavādajñānaṃ ca ||.... pūrvayogakauśalyam? yadidaṃ jātyanusmaraṇatā śrutabahulatā ca ||....kuśalamūlapūrvaṃgamatā? yadidaṃ bodhau tīvracchandatā ca pareṣāṃ samutsāhanatā ca || .... upāyakauśalyam? yadidaṃ pratideśanānumodanādhyeṣaṇā kuśalānāṃ ca pariṇāmanākauśalyam || ....nimittaprahāṇam? yadidaṃ svapnopamānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ budhyanatā ca vastuvibhāvanatā
ca |.... saṃjñāvivartaḥ? yadidaṃ viparyāsotsargaḥ ||.... vastulakṣaṇatā? yadidaṃ alakṣaṇajñānam ||.... sūtrāntābhinirhārakauśalyam? yadidaṃ yathābhūtānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ kuśalākuśalānāṃ upamāvadānaiḥ saṃprakāśanatā ||.... satyaviniścayaḥ? yadidaṃ vijñānanirodho nāmarūpānutpattiśca ||.... vimuktisākṣātkriyā? yadidaṃ vajropamasamādheracalanatā aprakupyanatā ca ||.... ekapravyāhāraḥ? yadidaṃ tīrthyāyatanavijugupsanatā cānutpattikajñānatā ca ||.... vaiśāradyapratilambhaḥ? yadidaṃ buddhadharmāvabudhyanatā ||.... śīlādhiṣṭhānatā? yadidaṃ kāyasaṃvaraḥ prātimokṣasaṃvaraśca ||.... samāpattyavatāraḥ? yadidaṃ traidhātukavairāgyatā ||.... prajñāpratilābhaḥ? yadidaṃ sāmarthyajñānaṃ cānupalabdhiśca ||.... ekārāmatā? yadidaṃ saṃgaṇikādoṣavivarjanatā ca śukladharmānutsṛjanatā ||.... alpajñātrasaṃtuṣṭiḥ? yadidaṃ itaretarasaṃtuṣṭiḥ ||.... cittasyānāvilatā? yadidaṃ nivaraṇānāṃ viṣkambhaṇatā ||.... dṛṣṭikṛtānāṃ vivarjanatā? yadidaṃ upalambhadṛṣṭivivarjanatā ||.... dhāraṇīpratilambhaḥ? yadidaṃ yathādṛṣṭānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ yathābhūtāsaṅgasaṃprakāśanatā || ....jñānāvatāraḥ? yadidaṃ prakṛtipraveśaḥ ||.... sthānam? yadidaṃ śīlasthānam ||....avasthānam? yadidaṃ cittāvasthānam ||.... pratiṣṭhānam? yadidaṃ śraddhāpratiṣṭhānam ||.... pratipattiḥ? yadidaṃ mārgapratipattiḥ ||.... hetuḥ? yadidaṃ avidyā hetuḥ saṃsārasya ||.... yuktiḥ? yadidaṃ vidyā yuktirmokṣasya ||....nayaḥ?
