(Vaidya 301) yadidaṃ mithyāmāno yoginām ||.... bodhisattvaiḥ parigṛhītāḥ? yadidaṃ durlabhatā ca mahābhaiṣajyatā ca ||.... daśabalairanubaddham? yadidaṃ kṛcchrayogena ||.... devaiḥ pujanīyam? yadidaṃ sarvasukhāhārakamupādāya ||.... brahmaṇā vandanīyam? yadidaṃ sarvamokṣāhārakayogena |.... nāgairnamasyanīyam? yadidaṃ sarvavāsanāsamutyāgatāmupādāya ||....yakṣairanumodanīyam? yadidaṃ sarvadurgatīnāṃ mārgacchedanatāmupādāya ||....kinnaraiḥ stavanīyam? yadidaṃ sarvamokṣaprāmodyāharaṇatāmupādāya? mahoragaiḥ praśaṃsanīyam? yadidaṃ saṃsārocchedanatāmupādāya ||.... bodhisattvairbhāvayitavyam? yadidaṃ sarvajñānāhārikamupādāya ||.... paṇḍitaiḥ paryavāptavyam? yadidaṃ avaivartyabhūmyāhāritrakamupādāya ||....dhanamanuttaram? yadidaṃ devamānuṣikāyāḥ prajāyāḥ saṃpatterāhātitrakaṃ copādāya mokṣāhāritrakamupādāya ||.... dānaṃ nirāmiṣam? yadidaṃ sarvakleśaccheditrakatāmupādāya ||.... bhaiṣajyaṃ glānānām? yadidaṃ rāgadveṣamohapraśamanatāmupādāya ||.... kośo jñānasya? yadidaṃ bhāvanāmupādāya ||.... akṣayatā pratibhānasya? yadidaṃ yathābhūtajñānadarśanatāmupādāya ||.... vigamaḥ śokasya? yadidaṃ nirarthakaḥ vyādhiduḥkhabudhyanāvataraṇatāmupādāya nairātmyaduḥkhaprajānanatāmupādāya ||.... parijñā traidhātukasya? yadidaṃ svapnamāyābudhyanatāmupādāya ||.... nāvaḥ pāramitānām? yadidaṃ adhyāaśayena parinirvātukāmānāmanityaduḥkhaśūnyatābhāvanatāmupādāya ||.... nauroghamadhyagatānām? yadidaṃ nirvāṇasyāhārakatāmupādāya ||.... kīrtiryaśaskāmānām? yadidaṃ vipuladharmāhārakatāmupādāya ||.... varṇo buddhānām? yadidaṃ anantaguṇabhaiṣajyadānapatimupādāya ||.... yaśastathāgatānām? yadidaṃ sarvaguṇasukhamokṣadānapatimupādāya ||.... stavo daśabalānām? yadidaṃ durlabhadharmaratnadānapatimupādāya ||.... guṇā bodhisattvānām?
yadidaṃ dharmaśikṣitatāmupādāya ||.... upekṣā kāruṇikānām? yadidaṃ kṛtabuddhakṛtyakaraṇīyatāmupādāya ||.... maitryā doṣapraśamanam? yadidaṃ pratighapratipakṣatāmupādāya ||....śvāso mahāyānikānām? yadidaṃ sarvabuddhadharmābhiprāyapāripūritrakamupādāya ||.... pratipattiḥ siṃhanādanādinām? yadidaṃ agradharmaśreṣṭhadharmāhāritrakamupādāya ||.... mārgo buddhajñānasya? yadidaṃ sarvakuśaladharmāhāritrakamupādāya || .... mudrā sarvadharmāṇām? yadidaṃ pārādapāramavabudhyanatāmupādāya ||.... asaṃhāryatā sarvajñānasya? yadidaṃ sarvākuśaladharmaprahāṇāya ca saṃvartate sarvakuśaladharmāhāraṇatāyai ca sarvasattvamokṣāharaṇatāyai saṃvartate ||....udyānaṃ bodhisattvānām? yadidaṃ sarvaprītiprāmodyātmasukhena sarvasattvasukhāharaṇatāmupādāya || ....vidrāpaṇaṃ mārasainyānām? yadidaṃ sarvabalāhāritrakamupādāya sarvakleśaśamanaṃ copādāya || ....vidyā kṣemagāminām yadidaṃ sarvopadravakṣayāya saṃvartate ||.... arthaḥ siddhānām? yadidaṃ sarvadharmasaṃpattyāhāritrakamupādāya ||.... paritrāṇamamitramadhyagatānām? yadidaṃ sarvopalambhikānāṃ mithyādṛṣṭikānāṃ parājayatāyai saṃvartate || ....sahadharmeṇa tīrthikānāṃ nigrahaḥ? yadidaṃ sahadharmeṇa tīrthikānāṃ nigrahamupādāya ||....satyākāro vaiśāradyānām? yadidaṃ sarvadharmākoṭitapratyākoṭitakṣematāmupādāya ||.... bhūtaparyeṣṭirbalānām? yadidaṃ aviparītayogena ||.... pūrvanimittamaṣṭādaśānāmāveṇikānāṃ buddhadharmāṇām? yadidaṃ sarvaśukladharmāharaṇatāmupādāya || (Vaidya 302).... alaṃkāraḥ? yadidaṃ dvātriṃśatāṃ mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇānāmāhārakamupādāya ||.... ratirmokṣakāmānām? yadidaṃ ādimadhyaparyavasānakalyāṇatāmupādāya ||.... prītirjyeṣṭhaputrāṇām? yadidaṃ paitṛkaṃ dhanaṃ buddhadhanānubhāvāhārakamupādāya ||.... pāripūrirbuddhajñānasya? yadidaṃ sarvaśukladharmānurakṣaṇatāmupādāya sarvaśukladharmānanyapoṣaṇāharaṇatāmupādāya ||....abhūmiḥ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānām? yadidaṃ udārāprameyabuddhadharmāhārakamupādāya ||.... saṃviśuddhiścittasya? yadidaṃ sarvamalaprahāṇāya saṃvartate ||.... pariśuddhiḥ kāyasya? yadidaṃ sarvaglānipraśamanatāmupādāya
||.... pariniṣpattiḥ vimokṣamukhānām? yadidaṃ anityaduḥkhaśūnyānātmaśāntapratyavekṣaṇatāmupādāya || ....asaṃkliṣṭatā rāgeṇa? yadidaṃ amṛtapadāhārikamupādāya ||.... vigamo doṣasya? yadidaṃ mahāmaitryāhārikamupādāya ||.... abhūmirmohasya? yadidaṃ bhūtadharmālokāhārakamupādāya ||.... āgamaḥ saṃjñānasya? yadidaṃ sarvalaukikalokottarakāyajñānasyotpādamupādāya ||.... utpādo vidyāyāḥ? yadidaṃ sarvayoniśomanasikāraharaṇatāmupādāya ||.... prahāṇamavidyāyāḥ? yadidaṃ sarvayoniśomanasikāravigamāya saṃvartate ||.... tṛptirvimuktisārāṇām? yadidaṃ āryamāhātmyāharaṇatāmupādāya ||.... tuṣṭiḥ samādhisārāṇām? yadidaṃ sarvasukhacittaikāgrāharaṇatāmupādāya ||.... cakṣurdraṣṭukāmānām? yadidaṃ ahaṃpaśyitāmupādāya ||.... abhijñā vikurvitukāmānām? yadidaṃ anāvaraṇatāmupādāya kāmanīyadharmatāṃ copādāya ||.... ṛddhirabhibhavitukāmānām? yadidaṃ sarvadharmavikalpitajñānānāvaraṇatāmupādāya ||.... dhāraṇī śrutārthikānām? yadidaṃ sarvadharmanirvāṇasamatāmupādāya ||.... smṛterasaṃpramoṣaḥ? yadidaṃ nirvāṇālambanaprakṛtivyupaśamatāmupādāya ||.... adhiṣṭhānaṃ buddhānām? yadidaṃ anantāharaṇatāmupādāya ||.... upāyakauśalyaṃ nāthānām? yadidaṃ sarvasukhakṣemagamanatāmupādāya ||.... sūkṣmama? yadidaṃ nirvāṇālambanavyupaśamatāmupādāya ||.... durvijñeyam? yadidaṃ duḥkhapratijñānatāmupādāya ||.... durājānatānabhiyuktaiḥ? yadidaṃ apratilabdhapūrvatāmupādāya ||.... vivarto 'kṣarāṇām? yadidaṃ sarvavākyakathānupalabdhitāmupādāya ||.... durvijñeyo ghoṣeṇa? yadidaṃ sarvadharmācintyatāmupādāya ||.... ajñātaṃ vijñaiḥ? yadidaṃ ratnamahārthikatāmupādāya ||.... jñānaṃ surataiḥ? yadidaṃ satkārājānatāmupādāya ||.... vibuddhamalpecchaiḥ? yadidaṃ satkārājānatāmupādāya ||.... udgṛhītamāravdhavīyaiḥ? yadidaṃ anikṣiptadhuratāmupādāya ||.... dhāritaṃ smṛtimadbhiḥ? yadidaṃ kṛtāvipraṇāśatāmupādāya ||.... kṣayo duḥkhasya? yadidaṃ rāgadveṣamohasaṃvartanatāmupādāya ||.... anutpādaḥ sarvadharmāṇām? yadidaṃ sarvavijñānanirodhatāmupādāya ||.... ekanayanirdeśaḥ || yadidaṃ sarvabhavagaticyutyupapattyāyatanānāṃ sarvadharmāḥ svapnopamā
iti sarvadharmānutpādyatāmupādāya? ayameṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ padaśatānāṃ nirdeśo draṣṭavyaḥ | ayaṃ sa ucyate kumāra sarvadharmasvabhāvasamatāvipañcito nāma samādhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: And what is purification of livelihood? Namely: contentment with whatever [one receives], non-deceitfulness, non-scheming, and not wishing to obtain gain through gain. [What is] non-abandonment of forest-dwelling? Namely: not laying down one's burden regarding wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, (<s>Vaidya</s> 297) delight in remote resting-places and seats, delight in forests, thickets, mountain-fastnesses, and caves, and experiencing the joy of <s>Dharma</s>. Non-association [means] not settling into honor and praise with householders and renunciants, and experiencing the joy of <s>dhyāna</s> through the abandonment of craving. This is called non-abandonment of forest-dwelling. [What is] knowledge of the stages of the [Bodhisattva] grounds? Namely: knowledge of the stage-results of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> ground, knowledge of the stage of the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> ground, and knowledge of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> ground. [What is] non-loss of mindfulness? Namely: attention to impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self. [What is] knowledge of skill in the <s>skandhas</s>? Namely: knowledge of the divisions of <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, and <s>āyatanas</s>, and non-apprehension therein. [What is] direct realization of superknowledges? Namely: obtaining the four bases of miraculous power and displaying miraculous transformations. [What is] removal of defilements? Namely: abandonment of passion, hatred, and delusion. [What is] knowledge of uprooting residual tendencies? Namely: disgust at one's former foolish conduct and non-aspiration for the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> grounds. [What is] progressive advancement? Namely: accomplishment of the <s>Buddha</s>'s confidences and analytical knowledges. [What is] the outflow of cultivation? Namely: abandonment of attachment and aversion. [What is] skill in transgressions? Namely: the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> restraint of the <s>Vinaya</s>. [What is] suppression of secondary defilements? Namely: confession of transgressions and future restraint from unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>. [What is] abandonment of attachment? Namely: uprooting the creeper of craving for existence in the three realms, non-arising of unarisen unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, and non-loss of arisen roots of merit. [What is] transcendence of existence? Namely: non-apprehension of the three realms and non-attention [to them]. [What is] recollection of births? Namely: knowledge of former abodes. [What is] freedom from doubt regarding the ripening of <s>karma</s>? Namely: avoidance of [the views of] annihilation and eternalism. [What is] contemplation of <s>Dharma</s>? Namely: contemplation in accordance with reality. [What is] pursuit of learning? Namely: upholding and cultivating both the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-<s>Pratyekabuddha</s> collection and the <s>Bodhisattva</s> collection. [What is] sharpness of knowledge? Namely: knowledge of non-arising, dream-like [in nature]. [What is] thirst for knowledge? Namely: pursuit of knowledge. [What is] awakening of knowledge? Namely: accomplishment of unsurpassed, perfect and complete awakening. [What is] the ground of the thoroughbred? Namely: the training-ground of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. [What is] mountain-likeness? Namely: non-abandonment of <s>bodhicitta</s>. [What is] unshakeability? Namely: not being carried away by defilements. [What is] immovability? Namely: non-attention to all signs. [What is] the mark of irreversibility? Namely: non-breaking of the six <s>pāramitās</s> and frequent seeing of <s>Buddhas</s> abiding in other world-systems. [What is] accomplishment of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>? Namely: nearness to unsurpassed, perfect and complete awakening. [What is] disgust at evil <s>karma</s>? Namely: future restraint and non-arising of evil. [What is] non-occurrence of defilements? Namely: non-arising of ignorance, craving for existence, and anger. [What is] non-abandonment of the training? Namely: conviction in the ripening of <s>karma</s> and reverence for the <s>Buddha</s>. [What is] establishment in <s>samādhi</s>? Namely: skill in the non-arising and non-perishing of <s>dharmas</s> of mind and mental factors, and one-pointedness of mind. [What is] knowledge of beings' dispositions? Namely: knowledge of the superiority and inferiority of faculties. [What is] knowledge of distinctions of rebirth? Namely: knowledge of the arrangement of the five destinies. [What is] infinitude of knowledge? Namely: effortless knowledge of worldly and supramundane arts. [What is] knowledge of rejoinder to speech? Namely: understanding the words spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s assembly. [What is] renunciation of household life? Namely: departure into seclusion of body and mind. [What is] non-delight in the three realms? Namely: seeing the three realms as they truly are. [What is] non-sinking of mind? Namely: non-abandonment of the mind and non-abandonment while entering attainments. (<s>Vaidya</s> 298) [What is] non-attachment to <s>dharmas</s>? Namely: abandonment of all affection. [What is] embracing the <s>Dharma</s>? Namely: guarding <s>Buddha</s>-awakening and accepting these very <s>sūtras</s>. [What is] protection of <s>Dharma</s>? Namely: subduing those who reject the true <s>Dharma</s> by means of the true <s>Dharma</s>. [What is] conviction in the ripening of <s>karma</s>? Namely: abstention from evil <s>karma</s> through shame, and exertion in pursuit of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. [What is] skill in the <s>Vinaya</s>? Namely: understanding natural and prescribed transgressions. [What is] settling of disputes? Namely: avoiding groups. [What is] non-contention and non-disputation? Namely: non-interest in worldly talk. [What is] the ground of patience? Namely: endurance of physical and mental affliction. [What is] undertaking patience? Namely: forbearance toward harsh words from others and non-breaking of patience. [What is] investigation of <s>dharmas</s>? Namely: analysis of <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, and <s>āyatanas</s>, and of the factors of defilement and purification, and their non-apprehension. [What is] skill in determining <s>dharmas</s>? Namely: the inexpressibility of all <s>dharmas</s>. [What is] knowledge of the analysis of <s>Dharma</s>-terms? Namely: settling and determining all <s>dharmas</s>. [What is] skill in drawing out <s>Dharma</s>-terms? Namely: teaching <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are. [What is] skill in knowledge of distinguishing meaning and non-meaning? Namely: neither elevating nor deprecating the nature of <s>dharmas</s>. [What is] knowledge of the prior end? Namely: knowledge of causes. [What is] knowledge of the posterior end? Namely: knowledge of conditions. [What is] knowledge of the purity of the three spheres? Namely: non-apprehension of <s>dharmas</s> of the past, future, and present, and non-attention [to them]. [What is] stability of mind? Namely: non-apprehension of mind. [What is] stability of body? Namely: mindfulness directed to the body. [What is] the characteristic of deportment? Namely: not being confused regarding noble <s>dharmas</s>. [What is] non-disruption of deportment? Namely: concealing one's good qualities. [What is] non-discrimination of deportment? Namely: absence of evil desires. [What is] serenity of the faculties? Namely: mental attention directed to the <s>Dharma</s>, speaking at the right time, knowing the proper occasion, and illuminating <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are. [What is] knowledge of the world? Namely: awareness of transgressions. [What is] liberated generosity? Namely: non-grasping at real things and non-miserliness. [What is] open-handedness? Namely: the disposition to share. [What is] unattached mind? Namely: unpolluted faith. [What is] conscience? Namely: non-loquaciousness. [What is] sense of shame? Namely: not being brazen. [What is] disgust at unwholesome mental states? Namely: understanding the <s>dharmas</s> of fools and not coming together with them. [What is] non-abandonment of the ascetic practices? Namely: firm undertaking. [What is] conformity to conduct? Namely: knowing the sequence of the paths of conduct. [What is] arising of joy? Namely: mental orientation toward the benefits of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. [What is] rising from one's seat for elders? Namely: humility and non-laziness. [What is] restraint of pride? Namely: non-apprehension of self and non-grasping. [What is] gathering the mind? Namely: knowledge of non-loss of bright <s>dharmas</s>. [What is] mental exertion? Namely: knowledge of not losing the fruit of vigor. [What is] knowledge of analytical knowledge of meaning? Namely: knowledge of penetrating the truths as they truly are. [What is] awakening of knowledge? Namely: understanding worldly and supramundane <s>dharmas</s>. [What is] departure of ignorance? Namely: departure of superimposition upon <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are. [What is] knowledge of entry into the mind? Namely: knowledge of arising and perishing. [What is] skill in knowledge of drawing out nutriment? Namely: sharpness of wisdom. [What is] knowledge of words and sounds? Namely: illuminating <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are. [What is] knowledge of arrangement? Namely: knowledge of entry as it truly is. [What is] determination of meaning? Namely: cutting off the <s>saṃskāra</s> aggregate. [What is] avoiding meaning and non-meaning? (<s>Vaidya</s> 299) Namely: transcendence of existence and causing others to enter into the transcendence of existence. [What is] reliance on true persons? Namely: never being separated from <s>Buddhas</s>. [What is] association with true persons? Namely: attending upon <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Śrāvakas</s>. [What is] avoidance of false persons? Namely: avoiding the lazy and those who hold views of real existence. [What is] delight in <s>dhyāna</s>? Namely: avoiding the thorns of sensual desire, non-abandonment of <s>dhyānas</s>, and not forsaking joy. [What is] non-settling in <s>dhyānas</s>? Namely: desire to transcend the three realms, desire to ripen beings, and desire for the light of higher wisdom. [What is] display of superknowledges? Namely: standing in the five superknowledges and illuminating the hard-to-know <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> to others. [What is] conventional designation? Namely: understanding names as not ultimately established. [What is] conventional usage? Namely: worldly usage. [What is] transcendence of designation? Namely: knowledge of utterance. [What is] turning away from <s>saṃsāra</s>? Namely: reflecting on the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s>. [What is] non-interest in gain? Namely: genuine contentment with few desires. [What is] not accepting gain and honor? Namely: non-anxiety and absence of evil desires. [What is] not being dismayed by blame? Namely: knowledge of examining the <s>skandhas</s> and <s>dhātus</s>. [What is] not being elated by true praise? Namely: concealing one's good qualities and understanding gain and honor as obstacles. [What is] equanimity toward honor? Namely: understanding the ripening of <s>karma</s>. [What is] not being dismayed by dishonor? Namely: non-abandonment of one's practice. [What is] not being angry at blame? Namely: reflecting on worldly <s>dharmas</s> [as impermanent]. [What is] equanimity toward praise? Namely: departing into the pursuit of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. [What is] non-depression at non-gain? Namely: reflecting on one's self-made <s>dharmas</s>. [What is] non-intimacy with householders? Namely: avoiding whatever is motivated by material gain. [What is] non-intimacy with renunciants? Namely: avoiding the improper and pursuing the proper. [What is] avoiding wrong resorts? Namely: abandonment of the five hindrances. [What is] walking in [right] resort? Namely: cultivation of the foundations of mindfulness. [What is] accomplishment of [good] conduct? Namely: care for others. [What is] avoidance of [bad] conduct? Namely: guarding one's own wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. [What is] not corrupting families? Namely: not avoiding relatives [out of wrong motivation]. [What is] guarding the teaching? Namely: undertaking the pursuit of <s>Dharma</s> and practicing in accordance with <s>Dharma</s>. [What is] speaking little? Namely: attainment of <s>śamatha</s>. [What is] gentleness? Namely: attainment of <s>vipaśyanā</s>. [What is] skill in reply? Namely: knowledge of answer and counter-answer. [What is] subduing opponents? Namely: illuminating, establishing, and refuting <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are. [What is] proper timing? Namely: knowing the [right] occasion. [What is] distrust of ordinary persons? Namely: seeing the faults of foolish <s>dharmas</s>. [What is] not disdaining the suffering? Namely: equal-mindedness toward all beings. [What is] giving wealth to the suffering? Namely: giving worldly material gifts. [What is] not despising the destitute? Namely: having compassionate thought toward others. [What is] compassion for the immoral? Namely: rescuing others from transgressions and establishing them in morality. [What is] speaking beneficial things? Namely: doing service to others. [What is] compassionate thought? Namely: seeing beings' future suffering. [What is] <s>Dharma</s>-assistance? Namely: causing others to enter <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are. [What is] renunciation of material things? Namely: renunciation of the <s>skandhas</s> and materially assisting others. [What is] non-accumulation? Namely: disgust at material things and seeing the faults of guarding [possessions]. [What is] praise of morality? Namely: understanding the fruits of morality. (<s>Vaidya</s> 300) [What is] disgust at immorality? Namely: understanding the faults of immorality. [What is] unshakeable attendance on the virtuous? Namely: knowledge of the rarity of the virtuous. [What is] giving up all possessions? Namely: a wholesome disposition. [What is] invitation through aspiration? Namely: desiring the happiness of others. [What is] doing as one says? Namely: accomplishment of wholesome aspiration. [What is] frequent attendance? Namely: inquiring into and asking about wholesome [qualities]. [What is] experiencing joy? Namely: knowledge of realization and knowledge of scripture. [What is] knowledge of similes? Namely: knowledge of analogy and knowledge of admonition. [What is] skill in former connections? Namely: recollection of births and abundance of learning. [What is] precedence of roots of merit? Namely: intense desire for awakening and encouraging others. [What is] skill in means? Namely: confession, rejoicing, supplication, and skill in dedicating wholesome [merit]. [What is] abandonment of signs? Namely: understanding <s>dharmas</s> as dream-like and analyzing things. [What is] reversal of perception? Namely: giving up distortions. [What is] seeing the characteristics of things? Namely: knowledge of the markless. [What is] skill in drawing out <s>sūtras</s>? Namely: illuminating <s>dharmas</s> — wholesome and unwholesome as they truly are — through similes and <s>avadānas</s>. [What is] determination of truth? Namely: cessation of consciousness and non-arising of name-and-form. [What is] direct realization of liberation? Namely: immovability and imperturbability of the <s>vajra</s>-like <s>samādhi</s>. [What is] single proclamation? Namely: disgust at the bases of <s>tīrthikas</s> and knowledge of non-arising. [What is] attainment of confidence? Namely: understanding the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. [What is] establishment in morality? Namely: bodily restraint and <s>Prātimokṣa</s> restraint. [What is] entry into attainment? Namely: dispassion toward the three realms. [What is] attainment of wisdom? Namely: knowledge of capability and non-apprehension. [What is] delight in solitude? Namely: avoiding the faults of groups and not abandoning bright <s>dharmas</s>. [What is] contentment with few acquaintances? Namely: contentment with whatever [one has]. [What is] non-turbidity of mind? Namely: suppression of the hindrances. [What is] avoidance of views? Namely: avoiding views of real existence. [What is] attainment of <s>dhāraṇī</s>? Namely: illuminating without attachment the <s>dharmas</s> one has seen as they truly are. [What is] entry into knowledge? Namely: entry into the [dharmas'] own-nature. [What is] foundation? Namely: the foundation of morality. [What is] position? Namely: the position of the mind. [What is] establishment? Namely: the establishment of faith. [What is] practice? Namely: practice of the path. [What is] cause? Namely: ignorance is the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>. [What is] method? Namely: knowledge is the method of liberation. [What is] guidance? Namely: abandonment of craving. [What is] gate? Namely: abandonment of faults. [What is] path? Namely: knowledge of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self. [What is] ground? Namely: the ten grounds of non-aspiration. [What is] departure from birth? Namely: cutting off birth. [What is] ground of knowledge? Namely: non-confusion. [What is] abandonment of ignorance? Namely: abandonment of delusion. [What is] establishment in knowledge? Namely: non-establishment. [What is] ground of yogic practice? Namely: cultivation of the thirty-seven factors of awakening. [What is] domain of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>? Namely: the six <s>pāramitās</s>. [What is] attendance on true persons? Namely: devotion to <s>Buddhas</s>. [What is] avoidance of false persons? Namely: avoiding <s>tīrthikas</s> who hold views of real existence. [What is] declared by <s>Tathāgatas</s>? Namely: liberation through natural knowledge while standing in the <s>Buddha</s>-powers. [What is] the <s>Buddha</s>-ground? Namely: obtaining all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. [What is] approved by the wise? Namely: approved by the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Śrāvakas</s> of past, future, and present. [What is] rejected by fools? Namely: hard to know for all fools. [What is] hard to know for <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>? Namely: the inconceivability of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. [What is] not the ground of <s>tīrthikas</s>? (<s>Vaidya</s> 301) Namely: the false pride of [non-Buddhist] yogins. [What is] embraced by <s>Bodhisattvas</s>? Namely: its rarity and its being a great medicine. [What is] pursued by the Ten-Powered? Namely: through effortful practice. [What is] to be worshipped by gods? Namely: insofar as it brings about all happiness. [What is] to be honored by <s>Brahmā</s>? Namely: insofar as it brings about all liberation. [What is] to be revered by <s>Nāgas</s>? Namely: insofar as it brings about complete departure from all residual tendencies. [What is] to be rejoiced in by <s>Yakṣas</s>? Namely: insofar as it cuts off the path to all lower rebirths. [What is] to be praised by <s>Kinnaras</s>? Namely: insofar as it brings about the joy of all liberation. [What is] to be extolled by <s>Mahoragas</s>? Namely: insofar as it cuts off <s>saṃsāra</s>. [What is] to be cultivated by <s>Bodhisattvas</s>? Namely: insofar as it brings about all knowledge. [What is] to be mastered by the wise? Namely: insofar as it brings about the ground of irreversibility. [What is] unsurpassed wealth? Namely: insofar as it brings about the prosperity of divine and human beings, and insofar as it brings about liberation. [What is] immaterial giving? Namely: insofar as it cuts off all defilements. [What is] medicine for the sick? Namely: insofar as it pacifies passion, hatred, and delusion. [What is] the treasury of knowledge? Namely: insofar as it brings about cultivation. [What is] inexhaustibility of eloquence? Namely: insofar as it brings about seeing knowledge as it truly is. [What is] departure of grief? Namely: insofar as it brings about understanding that disease-suffering is meaningless and understanding the suffering of non-self. [What is] full comprehension of the three realms? Namely: insofar as it brings about understanding [all] as dream and illusion. [What is] the boat of the <s>pāramitās</s>? Namely: insofar as it brings about, for those wishing to attain <s>nirvāṇa</s> through aspiration, the cultivation of impermanence-suffering-emptiness. [What is] a vessel [for those] in the midst of the flood? Namely: insofar as it brings about <s>nirvāṇa</s>. [What is] fame for those desiring renown? Namely: insofar as it brings about vast <s>Dharma</s>. [What is] praise of <s>Buddhas</s>? Namely: insofar as [one becomes] a lord of giving the medicine of infinite qualities. [What is] fame of <s>Tathāgatas</s>? Namely: insofar as [one becomes] a lord of giving the happiness and liberation of all qualities. [What is] eulogy of the Ten-Powered? Namely: insofar as [one becomes] a lord of giving the rare jewel of <s>Dharma</s>. [What is] qualities of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>? Namely: insofar as [one is] trained in <s>Dharma</s>. [What is] equanimity of the compassionate? Namely: insofar as [one has] accomplished what is to be done as a <s>Buddha</s>-deed. [What is] pacification of faults through loving-kindness? Namely: insofar as [it is] the antidote to aversion. [What is] the breath of <s>Mahāyāna</s> practitioners? Namely: insofar as it fulfills the intention of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. [What is] the practice of those who roar the lion's roar? Namely: insofar as it brings about the foremost and supreme <s>Dharma</s>. [What is] the path to <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge? Namely: insofar as it brings about all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. [What is] the seal of all <s>dharmas</s>? Namely: insofar as it brings about understanding of this shore and the other shore. [What is] indefeasibility of all knowledge? Namely: insofar as it conduces to the abandonment of all unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, to the bringing about of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, and to the bringing about of the liberation of all beings. [What is] the pleasure-garden of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>? Namely: insofar as, through the bliss of all joy, gladness, and personal happiness, it brings about the happiness of all beings. [What is] the routing of <s>Māra</s>'s armies? Namely: insofar as it brings about all powers and pacifies all defilements. [What is] the knowledge of those going to safety? Namely: insofar as it conduces to the destruction of all calamities. [What is] the goal of the accomplished? Namely: insofar as it brings about the attainment of all <s>dharmas</s>. [What is] protection for those in the midst of enemies? Namely: insofar as it conduces to the defeat of all who hold views of real existence and wrong views. [What is] subduing <s>tīrthikas</s> by the true <s>Dharma</s>? Namely: insofar as it subdues <s>tīrthikas</s> by the true <s>Dharma</s>. [What is] the mode of truth of the confidences? Namely: insofar as it brings about safety [when] all <s>dharmas</s> are probed and counter-probed. [What is] true pursuit of the powers? Namely: through correct practice. [What is] the precursory sign of the eighteen unique <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>? Namely: insofar as it brings about all bright <s>dharmas</s>. (<s>Vaidya</s> 302) [What is] ornament? Namely: insofar as it brings about the thirty-two marks of a great man. [What is] the delight of those desiring liberation? Namely: insofar as it brings about goodness at beginning, middle, and end. [What is] the joy of eldest sons? Namely: insofar as it brings about [access to] the paternal wealth — the power of <s>Buddha</s>-wealth. [What is] the fulfillment of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge? Namely: insofar as it brings about guarding all bright <s>dharmas</s> and sustaining them through no other nourishment. [What is] not the ground of all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>? Namely: insofar as it brings about the noble, immeasurable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. [What is] purification of mind? Namely: insofar as it conduces to the abandonment of all stains. [What is] purification of body? Namely: insofar as it brings about the pacification of all illness. [What is] perfection of the gates of liberation? Namely: insofar as it brings about the contemplation of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, non-self, and peace. [What is] non-defilement by passion? Namely: insofar as it brings about the deathless state. [What is] departure of hatred? Namely: insofar as it brings about great loving-kindness. [What is] not the ground of delusion? Namely: insofar as it brings about the light of true <s>dharmas</s>. [What is] the coming of discernment? Namely: insofar as it brings about the arising of all worldly and supramundane bodily knowledge. [What is] the arising of knowledge? Namely: insofar as it brings about all proper attention. [What is] the abandonment of ignorance? Namely: insofar as it conduces to the departure of all improper attention. [What is] satisfaction of those whose essence is liberation? Namely: insofar as it brings about the greatness of the Noble Ones. [What is] contentment of those whose essence is <s>samādhi</s>? Namely: insofar as it brings about all happiness and one-pointedness of mind. [What is] the eye of those wishing to see? Namely: insofar as it brings about [the state of] 'I see.' [What is] superknowledge for those wishing to display miracles? Namely: insofar as it brings about unobstructedness and the quality of being pleasing. [What is] miraculous power for those wishing to overpower? Namely: insofar as it brings about unobstructed knowledge of the analysis of all <s>dharmas</s>. [What is] <s>dhāraṇī</s> for those seeking what they have heard? Namely: insofar as it brings about the equality of all <s>dharmas</s> with <s>nirvāṇa</s>. [What is] non-loss of mindfulness? Namely: insofar as it brings about the natural pacification that takes <s>nirvāṇa</s> as its object. [What is] empowerment of <s>Buddhas</s>? Namely: insofar as it brings about the infinite. [What is] skill in means of the Protectors? Namely: insofar as it brings about going to all happiness and safety. [What is] subtlety? Namely: insofar as it brings about the pacification that takes <s>nirvāṇa</s> as its object. [What is] hard to know? Namely: insofar as it brings about the understanding of suffering. [What is] hard to understand by the unapplied? Namely: insofar as it brings about what has not been attained before. [What is] the reversal of syllables? Namely: insofar as it brings about the non-apprehension of all speech and talk. [What is] hard to know by sound? Namely: insofar as it brings about the inconceivability of all <s>dharmas</s>. [What is] unknown to the learned? Namely: insofar as it brings about seeking the great treasure. [What is] knowledge of the gentle? Namely: insofar as it brings about understanding of honor. [What is] awakened to by those of few desires? Namely: insofar as it brings about understanding of honor. [What is] taken up by those of aroused vigor? Namely: insofar as it brings about not laying down one's burden. [What is] retained by the mindful? Namely: insofar as it brings about non-loss of what has been done. [What is] destruction of suffering? Namely: insofar as it brings about [the end of] passion, hatred, and delusion. [What is] non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s>? Namely: insofar as it brings about the cessation of all consciousness. [What is] the teaching of the single guide? Namely: insofar as it brings about — taking 'all <s>dharmas</s> are dream-like' and 'all <s>dharmas</s> are non-arising,' together with [understanding] all the realms of existence, the destinies, death and rebirth, and sense-fields — [the understanding that all is non-arising]. This exposition of these three hundred terms should be seen thus. This, O prince, is called the <s>samādhi</s> that elaborates the equality of the own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: iti śrīsamādhirāje ekonacatvāriṃśatitamaḥ parivartaḥ || 39 ||
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the thirty-ninth chapter in the glorious <s>Samādhirāja</s>. || 39 ||

body.text:
(Vaidya 303)
40 Parīndanāparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 303) Chapter 40: The <s>Parīndanāparivarta</s> (Chapter on Entrustment).

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: vipulā buddhadharmā hi vipulo deśito nayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Vast are the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>; vast is the method taught;

children.text: vipulaṃ dharma deśitvā vipulāṃllabhate guṇān // SRS_40.1 //
children.translated_text: having taught the vast <s>Dharma</s>, one obtains vast virtues. // SRS_40.1 //

children.text: yathā vipulamākāśamevaṃ dharmāṇa lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Just as space is vast, such is the mark of <s>dharmas</s>;

children.text: ratnāni vipulānyatra tasmādvaipulyamucyate // SRS_40.2 //
children.translated_text: jewels are vast therein — therefore it is called "<s>vaipulya</s>" (the vast). // SRS_40.2 //

children.text: vipulā cari sattvānāṃ vipulā teṣu deśitā /
children.translated_text: Vast is the conduct regarding beings; vast is what is taught concerning them;

children.text: vipulo āgamo yasya tasmādvaipulyamucyate // SRS_40.3 //
children.translated_text: vast is the scripture of one [who knows this] — therefore it is called "<s>vaipulya</s>." // SRS_40.3 //'

body.text: asmin khalu punaḥ sarvadharmasvabhāvasamatāvipañcitasamādhinirdeśe dharmaparyāye bhāṣyamāṇe aprameyaiḥ sattvairanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpāditāni, aprameyāśca sattvā avaivartikā abhūvannanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | aprameyāṇāṃ ca sattvānāṃ pratyekabodhau ciattamutpannam | aprameyāṇāṃ ca sattvānāmarhattvaphalasākṣātkriyāyāṃ cittānyutpannāni | ayaṃ ca trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātuḥ ṣaḍavikāraṃ kampitaḥ prakampitaḥ saṃprakampitaḥ | calitaḥ pracalitaḥ saṃpracalitaḥ | vedhitaḥ pravedhitaḥ | saṃpravedhitaḥ | kṣumitaḥ prakṣubhitaḥ saṃprakṣubhitaḥ | raṇitaḥ praraṇitaḥ saṃpraraṇitaḥ | garjitaḥ pragarjitaḥ saṃpragarjitaḥ | pūrvā digavanamati paścimā digunnamati | paścimā digavanamati pūrvā digunnamati| uttarā digunnamati dakṣiṇā digavanamati | uttarā digavanamati dakṣiṇā digunnamati | antādavanamati madhyādunnamati | madhyādavanamati antādunnamati | aprameyasya cāvabhāsasya loke prādurbhāvo 'bhūt | mahacca divyagandhavarṣamabhiprāvarṣat | devatāśca mahāntaṃ divyaṃ puṣpavarṣamutsṛjanti sma | divyāni ca tūryaśatasahasrāṇyuparyantarīkṣe bhrāmayanti | evaṃ ca vācamabhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: When this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, the exposition of the <s>samādhi</s> that elaborates the equality of the own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s>, was being spoken, immeasurable beings directed their minds toward unsurpassed perfect awakening, and immeasurable beings became non-retrogressing from unsurpassed perfect awakening. The minds of immeasurable beings were directed toward <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-awakening. The minds of immeasurable beings were directed toward the realization of the fruit of <s>Arhatship</s>. And this trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātu</s>) trembled in six ways: it quaked, greatly quaked, and quaked all around; it shook, greatly shook, and shook all around; it trembled, greatly trembled, and trembled all around; it rumbled, greatly rumbled, and rumbled all around; it roared, greatly roared, and roared all around; it thundered, greatly thundered, and thundered all around. The eastern direction sank and the western direction rose; the western direction sank and the eastern direction rose; the northern direction rose and the southern direction sank; the northern direction sank and the southern direction rose; the edges sank and the center rose; the center sank and the edges rose. An immeasurable radiance appeared in the world. A great rain of divine fragrances fell. The gods released a great rain of divine flowers. And hundreds of thousands of divine musical instruments resounded in the sky above. And they spoke these words:

body.text: sulabdhā lābhāsteṣāṃ sattvānāṃ ya imaṃ mahākaruṇāvatāradharmaparyāyaṃ śroṣyanti | bahubuddhaparyupāsitāste sattvā bhaviṣyanti ya imaṃ sarvadharmasvabhāvasamatāvipañcitasamādhiṃ punaḥ punaḥ śroṣyanti, śrutvā ca likhiṣyanti udgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti araṇābhāvanayā bhāvayiṣyanti, bahulīkariṣyanti, parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyanti | sarvasatvānāṃ te dakṣiṇīyā bhaviṣyanti ||
body.translated_text: 'Well-gained are the gains of those beings who will hear this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse called the Descent of Great Compassion (<s>Mahākaruṇāvatāra</s>). Those beings will have attended upon many <s>Buddhas</s> who will hear again and again this <s>samādhi</s> that elaborates the equality of the own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s>, and having heard it, will write it, take it up, retain it, master it, cultivate it through the practice of forest solitude, make it abundant, and illuminate it in detail to others. They will be worthy of offerings from all beings.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate sma - udgṛhvīṣva tvamānanda imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ dhāraya vācaya paryavāpnuhi, pareṣāṃ ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśaya | atha khalvāyuṣmānānado bhagavantametadavocat - ko nāmāyaṃ bhagavan dharmaparyāyaḥ, kathaṃ caina dhārayāmi? bhagavānāha - mahākaruṇāvatāro nāmānanda idaṃ sūtraṃ dhāraya | sarvadharmasamatāvipañcito nāma samādhiriti dhāraya | ānanda āha - udgṛhīto me bhagavannayaṃ dharmaparyāya iti ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Take up, <s>Ānanda</s>, this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse; retain it, recite it, master it, and illuminate it in detail to others.' Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said to the Blessed One: 'What, Blessed One, is the name of this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, and how shall I retain it?' The Blessed One said: 'This <s>sūtra</s> is called the Descent of Great Compassion (<s>Mahākaruṇāvatāra</s>), <s>Ānanda</s> — retain it thus. It is a <s>samādhi</s> called the Elaboration of the Equality of the Nature of All <s>Dharmas</s> (<s>Sarvadharmasamatāvipañcita</s>) — retain it thus.' <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'I have taken up this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, Blessed One.'

body.text: (Vaidya 304) idamavocad bhagavān | āttamanāścandraprabhaḥ kumārabhūta āyuṣmāṃścānandaḥ tāścatasraḥ parṣado bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikāḥ aneke ca śuddhāvāsakāyikā devaputrāḥ sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvaśca loko bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandanniti ||
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 304) Thus spoke the Blessed One. Delighted, Prince <s>Candraprabha</s>, the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, and the four assemblies — monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen — and many <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> gods, and the world with its gods, humans, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s>, rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One.

body.text: ityāryasarvadharmasvabhāvasamatāvipañcitāt samādheryathālabdhaṃ samādhirājaṃ nāma mahāyānasūtraṃ parivarto nāma catvāriṃśatitamaṃ samāptam || 40 ||
body.translated_text: Thus, from the noble <s>Samādhi</s> that Elaborates the Equality of the Own-Nature of All <s>Dharmas</s> (<s>Sarvadharmasvabhāvasamatāvipañcita</s>), the <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtra</s> called the <s>Samādhirāja</s> (King of <s>Samādhis</s>), the fortieth chapter named [Entrustment] is completed. || 40 ||

children.text: ye dharmā hetuprabhavā hetusteṣāṃ tathāgato hyavadat |
children.translated_text: Those <s>dharmas</s> which arise from causes — the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared their cause;

children.text: teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha evaṃ vādī mahāśramaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and that which is their cessation — thus has spoken the Great Ascetic.
